full:
PHARMACY - chel. Chelidonium majus. Greater celandine. N. O. Papaveracae. Cheli- doniae. Tincture of entire fresh plant, at time of flowering. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Arthritis. Backaches. Bilious. Bronchitis. Cancer. Chest, disorders. Chorea. Colic. Constipation. Coughs. Diabetes mellitus. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Eczema. Gallbladder,pains. Gallstones. Gonorrhea. Headaches. Hemoptysis. Hemor- rhoids.Hepatitis. Hydrocele. Hypoglycemia. Indigestion. Influenza. Intercostal, neuralgia. Jaundice. Lachrymal, fistula. Laryngismus. Leucorrhea. Liver, disorders. Liver, pains. Lung disorders. Morning, sickness. Nausea. Neonatal, jaundice. Nephritis. Neuralgias. Nosebleed. Pleurodynia. Pneumonia. Rheumatism. Scald-head. Stiff-neck. Taste, altered, Tumors. Vertigo. Vomiting. Warts. Whooping, cough. Worms. Yawning.

HERBAL - Chelidonium is a poppy and therefore allied to Op. and Sang, with which it has many features in common. Closely allied to Lyc., when Lyc. seems indicated but fails to act, Chel. should be considered. The juice of Chel. causes vesication when applied to the skin. The juice is yellow, like bile. Probably based on the “signature” of the bile-like juice, it was recommended as a remedy for jaundice by Galen and Dioscorides. Given on the broad ground of organ-therapy in tinctures, material or semi-material doses, it has achieved notable results in cases of liver disease. An extract used locally in cancer cases has gained a reputation in the old school. Chelidonium works very well in tincture for a weak liver with low blood sugar, morning fatigue, and a craving for sweets (also Card-m.).

HOMEOPATHIC - Chelidonium acts upon the liver, spleen, kidneys, portal system, right side of abdomen and right lower lung. Predominantly a right sided remedy (Sang., Lyc.), with right infrascapular pain and the action on the liver. Also an action on the cecum, right ovary and on the base of the right lung. A major liver remedy, covering many of the direct reflex symptoms of diseased conditions of that organ. Keynote a continued, bruised, sharp, aching pain at the inferior angle of the right scapula. Jaundice. Yellowness and bilious disturbances. Bilious complications during pregnancy, lung disorders. Paralytic drawing and lameness in single parts. Neuralgia over the right eye and in right malar bone. Headaches over the right eye, “bilious headaches,” with a bad taste in the mouth and a yellow tongue, irritable, may vomit bile. Arthritis associated with liver problems. Great lethargy and indisposition to make any effort. Horror of motion. Feels tired on little exertion. Serous effusions. Hydrocele. Stitching pains. Heavy, stiff, sore, paralyzed, dislocated or broken feeling. Numbness. Ailments brought on or renewed by change of weather. MIND - Despondent. Restless, hence agile. Anxiety as if she had committed a crime. Sudden anxiety, with strong palpitations. Fear of going crazy. Fear he has ruined his health. Fear of her condition being observed. Delusions that he has an incurable disease. Restlessness, constantly moves from place to place. Bilious temperament. Forceful, very obstinate. Cross, and irritable. Domineering and sceptical, not impressed by authority. Irritable, upset easily. Desires to beat children. Vexed about every trifle and violent attacks of passionate outbursts of temper. Loses control, when she gets out of bed, couldn't explain why. Feels like crying with ill humor or without any reason. Thinks she must die. Sudden excitement with confusion of intellect at night. Talked incoherently during fit of anxiety. Inclination to weep. Weeping when carried. Confusion at night on waking. Stupid feeling on looking intently. Aversion to mental exertion or conversation. Great absence of mind, forgets what she wants to do or has done. Imagines she can't think and will lose her reason. Forgetful of shaving or dressing. Unconsciousness, better rubbing soles of feet.

Head - Headache better after eating. Headache extends backwards. Occiput feels heavy as lead, icy coldness of occiput from nape of neck. Nausea and bilious vomiting with sick headaches. Heavy, lethargic, drowsiness, very marked with general numbness. Right-sided headaches down behind ears and shoulder blade. Neuralgia over right eye, right cheekbone and right ear with excessive lachrymation, preceded by pain in liver. Pressing headache. Pressure in brain, with burning over eyebrows. Outward pressing, in forehead. Cranium feels too small. Congestion to cerebellum. Falling out of hair. Scalp on crown painful. Severe itching on occiput. Heart - Angina pectoris. Violent palpita tion with tightness in chest. Periodic palpitations. Lancinating pain in heart. Stitches in cardiac region, must breathe short, followed by strong palpitations and anxiety. Periodic palpitations. Beating of heart so strong that clothing is lifted from chest. Pulse slow, small and quick. Pulse full and hard.

Eyes - Aching in eyeballs, worse moving eyes. Dirty yellow color of whites. Burning and shooting pain in eyes. Burning in lids. Soreness of eyes, worse looking up. Tears Chelidonium majus fairly gush out. Orbits as if bruised on moving eyes. Orbital neuralgia of right eye with profuse lachrymation, pupils contracted, relieved by pressure. Lachrymation, when looking intently, with pain in eyes or from tickling in larynx. Mucus in eyes. Could not open eyes with prosopalgia. Agglutination of lids in morning. Thick, yellow mucus discharge from eyes. Fistula lachrymalis. Hordeolum. Photophobia. Lens uniformly grey.

Ears - Coldness or burning of ears. One ear cold, the other warm. Itching in right concha. Hearing lost, during cough. Deafness with liver disorders. Neuralgic pains in and around ears. Long-continued stitch in right external ear, passing off gradually. Sticking in ears. Sensation in both the ears, as if wind were rushing out or something crawling out. Loss of hearing during cough. Ears feel stopped. Loud distant roaring. Sounds as from a distant storm of wind. Humming. Ringing in left ear while walking.

Nose - Flapping of ala nasi (Lyc.). Red. Obstruction with liver complaints. Tip of nose swollen and red. Dryness. Delusions of smell. Soreness of nostrils and flow of water from nose, with eruption like measles. Fluent coryza with sneezing. Thick blood in mucus in morning when blowing nose. Itching of nose and tip of nose.

Face - Dark red or sallow, sunken. Face red and swollen. Dry lips. Lips burning, dry, chapped, scabby. Yellow face, worse nose and cheeks. Itching of whole face and forehead. Wilted skin. Right cheekbone feels as if swollen with tearing pain. Flushes of heat. Nodular eruptions. Violent tearing pains. Acne. Red pimples on different parts of face. Inflamed pimples on chin and cheeks. Itching herpes, mostly on chin. Facial erysipelas. Lower jaw drops.

Mouth - Burning pain in mouth. Mucus in mouth and tough mucus saliva. Salivation with nausea, giddiness. Bitter, pasty taste. Bad odor from mouth. Taste acid, insipid, metallic. Bitter water collects in mouth. Mucus flies from mouth when coughing. Oozing of blood from mucus membranes of mouth.

Throat - Hoarseness in afternoon. Choking during bilious eructations. Choking, worse breathing, as from hasty swallowing or as if too large a morsel had been swallowed. Spasm of glottis on expiration, with cough. Pressure or heat in trachea. Pressure in larynx as if air could not pass through. Severe tickling in larynx. Irritation to cough in trachea. Shooting and burning pain in throat and larynx. Pricking pain in larynx, rendering loud speaking impossible. Left sided goiter. Tonsils ache. Shooting in tonsils. Venereal ulcers in throat.

Stomach - Eructations, tasting like juniper berries. Constant eructation of wind. Heartburn with eructations. Anxiety and oppression at stomach. Pain through stomach to back and right shoulder blade. Pressure in pit on stooping. Gastric pains, gnawing scraping better eating. Nausea, vomiting, better very hot water. Nausea and vomiting, with feeling of heat in stom- Chelidonium majus ach, spreading over whole body. Nausea and bilious vomiting with sick headaches. Nausea and vomiting in pregnancy. Sensations of heat or coldness in stomach. As if a plug in stomach. Qualmishness better belching. Vomiting of tough, acid or greenish mucus.

Abdomen - Sensation of fullness. Abdominal pains better wine. Rumbling followed by diarrhea. Fatty liver with icterus. Epigastric region tender. Constriction across abdomen, as if by a string. Distention. Ascites with yellow palms. Burning pain in bowels. Sensation as if an animal wriggling in epigastrium. Navel drawn in during colic. Severe pain around umbilical region. Painful pressure over umbilicus. Numbness in muscles of hepatic region. Pinching and cutting pains in bowels, with rumbling and gurgling. Pain and rumbling in cecal region. Pot-belly, with worms. Swelling and ulceration of inguinal glands.

Rectum - Constipation. Alternation of diarrhea and constipation. Chronic diarrhea with liver affection. Diarrhea without pain, without urging. Crawling anditching in rectum. Burning and itching of anus (Rat., Sulph.). Burning and cutting pain in rectum. Frequent discharge of flatus. Fermentation and sluggish bowels. Sensation as if anus were contracted, alternating with itching, during stool. Round worms.

Stool - Fluid feces, often escape unexpectedly. Stools, hard, round balls like sheep's dung. Stools bright yellow, pasty, claycolored. Stools float in water. Stools like rice-water, tinged yellow. Deficiency of biliary coloring matter in stools. Yellow watery stool containing flakes of mucus.

Male - Acne on genitals. Eczema rubrum on scrotum. Frequent erections, even during day. Pain in glans. Itching, creeping on scrotum and glans. Drawing pains in spermatic cords, testicles. Hydrocele. Redness, heat and swelling of scrotum. Painful swelling of right testicle. Gonorrhea and secondary syphilis, with ulcer- ated buboes.

Female - Menses, too late and too profuse. Menses too long duration. Irregular menses, with profuse flow. Acrid leucorrhea. Leucorrhea, white, stains linen yellow. Burning in vagina, recurs at the same hour during day. Longing for unusual articles of food during pregnancy. Breast milk diminished. Food - Loss of appetite, with disgust and nausea. Loss of appetite, with great emaciation. Nausea, better drinking milk. Itching better eating. Aversion to meat, coffee. Aversion to cheese, spinach. Generally better after eating. Hypoglycemia. Generally better from hot drinks. Desire for very hot drinks. Desire cheese, strange things during pregnancy. Prefers hot food and drink. Fond of vinegar or sour wine. Craves milk, piquant or hot food and drinks. Bitter taste when not eating or drinking. Cold drinks disagree. Thirstlessness.

Chest - Skin yellow on throat and chest. Pain in right side of chest and shoulder with difficult respiration. Constriction of chest. Oppression on inspiration after dinner. As if a tight girdle around chest, hindering breathing. Deep seated pain or nail sensation, deep in right chest. Pain in lower right ribs, worse bending towards left side. Stitches under left clavicle and in region of right breast. Pains in right side of chest and shoulder, with difficult respiration. Intercostal neuralgia. Constitutions - Bilious constitutions.

Back - Aching soreness in all vertebrae, worse motion and pressure on spinous processes. Burning pain in back. Fixed pain under inner and lower angle of the right scapula, which may extend into chest and stomach, causing nausea or vomiting. Pain beneath right scapula, worse inspiration and motion of right arm. Pain from neck to temple (right). Pressing pain in vertebrae, worse bending backwards and forwards. Occiput heavy with pain in right side of back. Pain in nape. Stiffness in back between shoulders. Stiff neck, head drawn to left. As if a string around the neck. Cervico-brachial neuralgia. Pain at lower angle of left scapula. Shivering running down back.

Limbs - Whole flesh sore to touch. Limbs feel paralyzed. Heavy feeling in lower limbs. Rheumatic pain in hips and thighs. Paresis of lower limbs with rigidity of muscles. Burning and stiffness in right knee, worse moving. Intolerable pains in heels, as if pinched by too narrow a shoe, worse right. Ankles stiff. Feels paralyzed. One foot cold, other hot. Pain in arms, shoulders, hands, fingertips. Icy coldness of fingertips, wrists sore, tearing in metacarpal bones. Edematous swelling of limbs. Edema around ankles and feet. Wandering pains in joints.

Sleep - Lethargic. Drowsy and chilly. Sleepiness without being able to sleep. Falls asleep while speaking. Vnrefresh- ing sleep. Frequent yawning, drowsy and sleepy during day. Can’t sleep because of numbness and coldness of limbs. Sleeplessness during headache. Wakes up repeatedly, feels wretchedly. Dreams of bodies, corpses and funerals. Confused dreams. Vivid dreams about business matters, causes unrefreshing sleep. Unremembered dreams.

Skin - Burning pain like nettles, preceding an eruption like measles. Dry heat of skin, itches, yellow. Wilted, wrinkled skin. Skin cool and dry. Skin cool and rough. Sallow, cold, clammy. Jaundice. Yellow-grey color of skin. Neonatal jaundice (Phos., Cham., Chin.).Itching as in jaundice. Painful red pimples and pustules. Itching, better eating. Old, spreading, offensive ulcers. Sallow, cold, clammy. Veins swollen. Red, ring-shaped, confluent spots, skin seems mottled. Scabs, exuding moisture and scaling off.

Modalities - Better after dinner, eating. Better lying on abdomen. Better pressure. Better bending backward. Better hot bath. Better hot food. Better milk. Worse from motion. Worse looking up. Worse cough. Worse touch. Worse right side. Worse change of weather. Worse northeast wind. Worse 4 a.m. and 4 p.m. Worse very early in morning.

Teeth - Gums pale and bleed easily. Drawing or tearing pains, better warmth, worse at night in bed. Drawing pain in upper incisors. Drawing pain, through middle incisors of lowerjaw. Toothache, chiefly in whole left cheek, worse at night. Pressure or transient pain in teeth.

Tongue - Tongue pale, moist, whitish. Tongue dried up, brown, cracked. Tongue yellow with imprint of teeth, large and flabby (Merc., Hydr.). Narrow, pointed tongue. Tongue red on edges and tip. Tongue red and sore, with raised papillae. Vertigo - Vertigo with liver disturbance. Vertigo with inclination to fall forward. Vertigo, felt in vertex, worse closing eyes with bilious vomiting and pain in liver. Vertigo, worse rising from bed or sitting. Vertigo on closing eyes, as if turning in a circle. Vertigo with shivering over upper part of body. Vision - Blackish-grey specks before eyes. Misty appearance. Amaurosis from rheumatic troubles, also after suppression of ringworm. Muscae volitantes. Dazzling spots. Blinding spot, lachrymation when looking at it. Dim vision. Diplopia. Sparks, during headache. Flickering, brilliant specks. Candlelight seems very small. Blackness, with sensation of fainting. When reading or writing, letters run together and seem blurred. COMMENTS - Chelidonium is a major liver remedy and is also a venous medicine. According to Rademacher, Chel. acts on the center of the liver. Neonatal jaundice remedy (Phos., Cham., Chin.). Yellow tongue, yellow skin, yellow eyes. Hepatitis (Phos.). Yellowness of the skin, ulceration. Prominent paralytic symptoms. Chills or creeps accompany the headache or the jaundice. Constipation with clay-colored stools or diarrhea with bright yellow stools. Nausea during pregnancy with desire for food, better by drinking milk. Desire for hot food and drinks, only water almost boiling will stay on stomach. “Aversion to cheese” in many gastric conditions. Eating ameliorates. Desire to lie down after a meal. Great debility and drowsiness after eating and on waking. Aversion to move, feels tired on least exertion. Sleepiness and yawning (Op.). Better hot baths. Worse 4:00 pm or 4:00 am (Lyc.). The dirty yellow complexion produced by Chel. along with other signs of cachexia, strongly suggests cancer. The action of Sang., its relative, in breast cancer is well known. Additionally, Op., in addition to its narcotic influence, is believed by Snow to have a retarding effect on cancerous growth. Pneumonia with bilious symptoms. Fanlike movement of alae nasi in chest disorders (Lyc.). Numerous cases of pneumonia of right lung have been cured when associated with hepatic derangement, distressing pain under right scapula. Hepatization of upper half of right lung. Bry. is very similar to Chel. in pneumonia but the pains go continually to the back in Chel. and esp. to the right scapula. Rattling in lungs, worse changing position after waking. Frequently useful in bronchitis of children, with dusky red face, oppressed breathing. Strong action in the respiratory sphere. Characteristic cough is caused by a sensation of “dust” in the air passages. St. Clair Smith related a case of a young woman, who had for several weeks a dry, racking, fatiguing cough night and day, worse at night, no expectoration and no pain. She looked completely worn out. The cough was excited by a sensation as if throat and larynx were full of dust. Chel. 3c, a powder every two hours, was given. She only took three when the “dust” left the throat, and with it the cough, and never returned. Carleton Smith cured a “Dry cough through day with pain and stitches right side, severe hoarseness 5 p.m., voice scarcely audible.” C. M. Foss recorded a typical Chel. case simulating cancer. A man, 45, had catarrh of the nose and, at the same time of the stomach. He had been told he had stomach cancer. Tenderness over stomach with sinking, gone feeling, at times reaching a state of painful anguish. Sickness at stomach. All symptoms better by eating. Chel. 6x cured at once. Teste, who proved Chel., placed it at the head of a group which includes Caps, and Viol-o. He mentioned the analogy between the juice of Chel. and the: juice of Garcinia morella, and Gamb. Both are bright yellow and change to orange and brown on drying. Some authorities have recommended Chel. juice as a substitute for Gamb. as a hydragogue cathartic. Its ancient external uses ranged from an application in eye disorders to chronic ulcers and warts. In Teste's proving he emphasized a dull and heavy, deep-seated pain in whole right side of chest and right shoulder, at 1:30 p.m., without cough, but with embarrassed respirations. This pain, which is at times accompanied by dull beatings in the chest, does not allow him to draw a long breath, it is not perceptibly aggravated by the motions of the arm. The pain is particularly felt in the axilla and under the shoulder blade. A sort of numbness of the muscles in the region of the liver and in the right side of the neck, face and head. Apprehension of threatening pneumonia. Great anxiety. Constant desire to stir and change one's position. “Extremely profuse emission of a whitish and foaming urine.” “2 p.m.: drowsiness which is so marked, even in the open air, that she is near falling asleep while walking, lasts half an hour.” A large field in rheumatic disorders. Edema, heat, tenderness and stiffness are the leading indications. A baby girl had rheumatism of both ankles for a week, when it settled in the right one, which became greatly swollen, very tender, painful and hot. Constipated for two months previously, whitish stools. Chel. improved in twelve hours and cured entirely in a week. In another case of acute rheumatism of feet and ankles, supervening on a slow, remittent fever, Chel. cured after the failure of Rhus-t. and Bry. The patient was a girl of six. Both ankles were affected, feet much swollen and extended. The slightest movement or touch extorted screams. The only relief was constant bathing with hot water. W. A. Burr cured a case of right sciatic rheumatism of ten years' history in a very corpulent woman, age 55. In her case, there were aggravations coming on in the afternoon and evening of each day and lasting into the middle of the night. During the paroxysms, the outer ankle’ and lower leg became cyanotic, swelling around ankle, constriction above, great sensitiveness to touch and motion. Very nervous during the spells. Great external sensitiveness, aversion to touch and worse from it. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Aeon., Cham., acids, wine and coffee, Camph. It is antidote to: Bry. Compare: (1) In pain below angle of scapula, Jug-c., Chenop. - Lower than angle and nearer spine), Ran-b. (edge of left, through to chest, Lob-c. - inside edge right scapula, Ang. - Cutting from just beneath right scapula to breast, near nipple. (2) Nux-v., Sulph., Bry., Lyc., Op., Podo., Sang., Ars. (3) Chel. - Spasm of smooth muscle everywhere intestinal colic, uterine colic, bronchial spasm, tachycardia. (4) Boldoa fragrans. (5) Elemuy Gauterusa - Stone in kidneys and bladder, grain doses of powdered bark in water or 5 drops of tincture. Pellagra. (6) Ip., Led., Sulph. (7) Kah-c. -pneumonia in later stages, copious exudation into lungs, rattling with cough, worse 2-3 a.m. (8) Colch. -nausea with desire for food. (9) Aeon., Ars., Bell., Calc., Caps., Chin., Gamb., Graph., Ign., Nit-ac., Nux-v., Phos., Podo., Puls., Rhus, Sep., Spig., Sulph., Viol-o. Complementary: Bry. is adose analog in many symptoms—yellow tongue, swelling of liver. Ars., Ip., Lyc., Sulph. often completes its work. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Liver - Liver pains going backward. Pains fixed at angle of right scapula. Liver enlarged, tender. Hypoglycemia. Jaundice due to hepatic and gallbladder obstruction. Jaundice, sometimes with clear urine, tongue white, stools dark, offensive urine. Gallbladder colic. Gallstones (Berb.). Pressive pain in region of liver. Dull throbbing pain in region of liver. Lungs - Nightly attacks of asthma with sense of constriction in chest. Dyspnea, worse urinating. Very quick and short inspirations. Pressive pain on deep inspiration. Hemoptysis. Copious, mucus, in morning. Respiratory symptoms with liver symptoms. Bronchial pneumonia. Bilious pneumonia. Blood-streaked phlegm, or brownish-bloody sputum. Right sided pneumonia. Small lumps of mucus fly from mouth when coughing. In left lung soreness like a wound, by deep breathing, coughing and sneezing.

Kidneys - Kidneys are sensitive to pressure, even of clothing. Spasmodic pain in right kidney and liver. Violent paroxysms of pain in kidneys, with intense headache, vertigo and syncope. Violent pain in direction of ureters, preceding passing of turbid urine. Urine copious. Profuse, foaming, yellow urine, dark turbid, like beer (Chen- a.). Urine stains the diaper dark yellow. Urine yellow as gold. Urine smells acid or ammoniacal. Urine has a resinous odour. Diabetes mellitus. Urine red, cloudy, with chalky sediment.

Bladder - Frequent urging. Catarrh of bladder, with sexual excitation. Discharge of pus from urethra. Strangury, lasting all day, with scanty urination. Dragging pain in bladder, with spasmodic trembling pains in inguinal region. Stabbing pain in region of bladder. Cutting pain in urethra on urinating and continuing after urinating. Burning pain in urethra on urinating.

Cough - Short, exhausting. Violent cough with pain behind sternum, at night. Cough with constant tickling in larynx. Cough with painful contraction of abdomen. Racking cough as in tuberculosis, with copious mucus expectoration. Cough, as from dust with much rattling, but little expectoration or it flies from mouth. Whooping cough, spasmodic cough, loose, rattling, expectoration difficult.

Perspiration - Sweaty with aversion to uncover and without relief. Sweat during sleep, after midnight, from slight exertion. Sweats from slight exertion. Awakes in morning perspiring, after many unremembered dreams. Watery, sour-smelling sweat. Copious sweat, in evening.

Temperature - General lack of vital heat, coldness of limbs. Chill and coldness of whole body. Chilliness, with cold feet, in morning on waking. Y awning and shivering before attack of neuralgia. V iolent fit of shivering daily. Fluctuating temperature. High fever. Burning heat spreads from hands over the body.

HERBAL…
full:
PHARMACY - chelo. Chelone glabra. Snakehead. Balmony. Turtle-head. N. O. Scrofularia- ceae. Tincture of the whole plant Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Cachexia. Debility. Dumb-ague. Dyspepsia. Jaundice. Liver, disorders. Malaise. Quinine. Worms.

HERBAL - Chelo, has been used by old-school practitioners andherbalists as aliver and worm remedy. Burnett used it as an organ-remedy in liver disorders.

HOMEOPATHIC - Burnett's indications are “pain or soreness of the left lobe of the liver and extending downwards.” Chelo, acts in a line between the hilus of the liver and the fundus of the uterus. Liver disorders with pain or soreness of the left lobe of the liver, extending downwards. Soreness of external parts, as if skin were off, debility. Dyspepsia with hepatic torpor. Jaundice. Round and thread worms. Dumb ague. Malaise, following intermittents. COMMENTS - According to some observers it antidotes the quinine cachexia and is a remedy for “dumb- ague,” i.e., ill-defined paroxysms of aching and fever following severe malarial fevers. “Soreness of external parts, as if the skin were off, especially about elbow,” has been confirmed as an indication. Hale noted “debility from loss of tone of digestive organs or liver or from exhausting diseases.” One to five-drop doses of the tincture have been given. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Chin., Chenop., Cina, Helon., Hydr. (2) Card-m. - left lobe of liver. (3) Scrofularias, Grat., Dig., Tab., Scroph-n. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Chenopodium Anthelminticum
author: Murphy
constitution: Aphasia. Asthma. Cerebral deafness. Convulsions. Deafness. Dropsy. Ear, disorders. Epilepsy. Headaches. Hemicrania. Hemiplegia. Hookworm. Leucorrhea. Meniere's, disease. Menses, suppressed. Otitis, media. Paralysis. Roundworm. Scapula, pain. Strokes. Tinnitus. Tonsillitis. Vertigo. Worms.
keynote: PHARMACY - chen-a. Chenopodium anthelminticum. Jerusalem oak. Chenopodium ambrosioides. Wormseed. N. O. Chenopo- diacae. North America. Central America. Tincture of fresh plant. Solution of seed oil. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies. Oil of Chen-a. for…
full:
PHARMACY - chen-a. Chenopodium anthelminticum. Jerusalem oak. Chenopodium ambrosioides. Wormseed. N. O. Chenopo- diacae. North America. Central America. Tincture of fresh plant. Solution of seed oil. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies. Oil of Chen-a. for hookworm.

CLINICAL - Aphasia. Asthma. Cerebral deafness. Convulsions. Deafness. Dropsy. Ear, disorders. Epilepsy. Headaches. Hemicrania. Hemiplegia. Hookworm. Leucorrhea. Meniere's, disease. Menses, suppressed. Otitis, media. Paralysis. Roundworm. Scapula, pain. Strokes. Tinnitus. Tonsillitis. Vertigo. Worms.

HERBAL - Oil of Chenopodium has been used for hookworm and roundworm. HOMEOPATinC - Several cases of poisoning have been reported in which all the symptoms of a stroke and the consequent right hemiplegia with aphasia were reproduced. Stertorous breathing with the very peculiar rattle as of a ball rolling loose in the trachea. Heavy breathing with flapping of cheeks. Vanishing of sight and roaring in ears with (right) hemicrania. Roaring in ears as of cannons going off, ringing, deafness. Meniere's disease. Affections of auditory nerves (Nat-sal.). Serous or bloody effusions in the labyrinth. Chronic otitis media. Buzzing noises. Absent or deficient bone conduction. A consciousness of the ear. Hearing better for shrill, high-pitched sounds than for low ones. Deafness progressivefor human voice but great sensitiveness to sound as of a passing vehicle or to distant sounds. Aural vertigo. Sudden vertigo. Characteristic dull pain below the angle of right scapula and nearer the spine than the similar pain of Chel. Chenopodii glauci aphis has a similar pain below angle of left scapula. Paralysis with spasms of forearms and hand in flexion contraction of limbs. Right sided convulsion and paralysis. Staggering gait. Pains through heart, under right scapula and in right shoulder. Sub-acute and chronic enlargement of tonsils in pale, scrofulous children. Caseous deposits with painful inflammation of tonsils. Rough, furry feeling in throat. Stertorous breathing (Op.). Fever after a fright. Jaundiced. Urine, profuse, foamy, yellow, burning. Menses suppressed, leucorrhea instead. MIND - Constantly repeats an action. Weeping mood. Insensible, convulsed, foaming at mouth. Loss of memory of attack after it is over. Weeping mood, suppressed menses. Forgetful of words while speaking. Uses wrong words. Aphasia.

Head - Pain in whole right side of head, with roaring in ears, dim sight or complete loss of vision. Dull, pressive pain in vertex extending through head.

Eyes - Impaired movement of right eyeball, loss of sensitiveness. Vanishing of sight.

Ears - Torpor of auditory nerve. Hearing is better for the high-pitched sounds. Comparative deafness to sound of voice, but great sensitiveness to sound as of passing vehicles and also a shrinking from low tones. Buzzing in ears. Roaring in ears as of cannons, deafness. Tinnitus synchronous with heartbeats.

Face - Flapping cheeks with stertorous breathing.

Throat - Enlargement of the tonsils. Chronically enlarged tonsils, caseous deposits. Furry feeling in throat. Vertigo - Aural vertigo. Vertigo with transient vanishing of sight. COMMENTS - Complete aphasia in a patient who took 1 1/2 oz. of worm-seed oil and 30 drops of turpentine. Five days from taking the dose he died in profound coma with high temperature. “Whatever he did he would keep repeating. When the doctor entered he arose and shook him heartily by the hand, and then sat down. In about a minute he arose, solemnly came forward and again shook hands. This he repeated twenty times in as many minutes. He then went through the performance of washing his hands in an empty basin and repeated this many times.” In poisoning cases, there was hemiplegia with contractions of limbs and certain epileptic seizures. When given as a vermifuge it frequently produces progressive and long- lasting deafness. The peculiar deafness corresponds nearly to the “cerebral deafness” described by Cooper in which the watch- hearing is good while the voice-hearing is bad or absent. Linnell cured with it two cases in which there was deafness to voice-hearing but sensitiveness to other sounds. In one case there was implication of left labyrinth with slight chronic otitis media of both ears, deafness in the left ear several years, no tinnitus, consciousness of the ear, sensitive to musical sounds, deaf for watch and voice, hearing diminished. Linnell also cured a roaring tinnitus synchronous with heart. Sensitiveness to cold. Hearing better for high- pitched than low-pitched sounds. Allen reported three cases of poisoning in which there was insensibility, convulsions, and foaming at the mouth. All remembrance of taking the poison was lost upon recovery. Deep, heavy, stertorous breathing accompanied by a very peculiar rattle, as if there were a ball rolling loose in the trachea. Any attempt to swallow threatened instant suffocation. Pulse small, weak, frequent and feeble. Eyes insensible to light or external objects. Convulsive movements of right half of body. Limbs cold. In one case, a patient took 1.5 oz. of worm-seed oil and 30 drops of turpentine. It produced disagreeable belchings and nausea. Staggering like a drunken man. Deafness to the sound of the voice, but exquisite sensi- tiveness to the sound of passing vehicles, they sounded like cannons in his ears, also annoying buzzing. In smoking, he would scarcely light his cigar before he would lay it down again and take a fresh one, arguing perversion of taste. By afternoon the mantelpiece was strewn with cigars only partly used. No disposition to engage in conversation. Aphasia, he clearly wanted his attendant to get or do something but could not make him understand. The attendant wrote, “Don’t understand,” showed it to him and gave him, paper and pencil. After great efforts he wrote distinctly words with no meaning. The voice and hearing became progressively worse but he heard the tea-bell three stories below, promptly and to the astonishment of the family, got up and walked deliberately into the dining-room. He did not seem to know his accustomed seat and sat in the wrong place. During the afternoon became completely aphasic. Finding himself unable to express his ideas, this seemed to amuse him much and he laughed heartily. Whatever he did he would keep repeating. When the doctor entered he arose and shook him heartily by the hand and then sat down. In about a minute he arose, solemnly came forward and again shook hands. This he repeated twenty times in as many minutes. He then went through the performance of washing his hands in an empty basin and repeated this many times. Sitting at tea, he ate with apparent relish, taking singly tea and bread. While grasping a piece of bread, there was a distinct spasm of right forearm and hand, fingers firmly clenched, hand forcibly flexed on forearm. Assisted to his room, his walk was entirely natural, when put to bed showed some resistance, striking at the doctor. He at once commenced to groan, tossed from side to side of the bed, suggesting abdominal distress. Soon became unconscious, right arm paralyzed, dragging helplessly. The next day, continued impairment of motion and sensation right side, right eyeball insensitive to touch. During the third day, there was frequent twitching and stiffness of the right limbs, culminating in a one-side convulsion during the early morning of the fourth day. At noon on the third day, copious involuntary urination in bed. This continued to the end, except when drawn off. In the afternoon, heavy breathing and the flapping cheeks of a stroke appeared. Constant regurgitation of yellow frothy material from mouth, smelling of worm-seed, as also did the perspiration. This material was at times so profuse as to embarrass respiration. During one of the attacks of dyspnea and while in drenching sweat, which suggested dissolution, he was gently turned in bed, immediately a general convulsion set in, markedly opisthotonic, lasting ten minutes, despite the use of chloroform. By this time jaundice appeared, having been only noticed the day before. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aphis, Chel., Chen-v. (2) In strokes and puffing respiration, Chin., Op., Lyc. (3)In deafness, Chin., Chin-s., Chin-sal. and Salicylates in general. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Perversion of taste. Disagreeable belchings, nausea. Constant, profuse regurgitation of yellow, frothy material smelling of worm-seed.

Female - Menses is suppressed, has leucorrhea instead, with rough, furry feeling in throat.

Chest - Pains through heart, under right scapula and in right shoulder. Pain throughout right chest, beginning at attachment of 6th rib to its cartilage and extending to front of right scapula.

Back - Intense pain between angle of right shoulder blade near spine and through the chest. Pain beneath point of right scapula, with giddiness in forehead, ringing in ears and pale face.

Limbs - Hemiplegia with contraction of limbs. Frequent twitching and stiffness of right limbs. Paralysis and spasm of right forearm and hand in flexion. Lungs - Stertorous breathing with flapping cheeks. Dyspnea, peculiar rattle as of a ball rolling loose in trachea. Respiration embarrassed by a quantity of yellow frothy material which was constantly regurgitated.

Skin - Jaundice.

Kidneys - Slight pain in region of kidneys. Involuntary urination. Copious, yellow, foaming urine with acrid sensation in urethra. Yellowish sediment (Chel.).

PHARMACY - chen-v. Chenopodium vulvaria. Stinking goosefoot. Stinkender Gânsefuss. Chenopodium olidum. N. O. Chenopodiacae. Europe. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

HOMEOPATHIC - Chen-v. has an odor of decaying fish and contains Trimethylamine. It constantly gives off ammonia. Chen-v. seemed to affect the left side more than the right in provings. Pain in middle of back on right side of spinal column (Chen-a.), increasing gradually to a pressing wedge-like pain, beneath right scapula, worse when sitting. Pain spine of left scapula. Pressure on the left side of the head. Restlessness caused by pricking pains. Constipation with external hemorrhoids. Nocturnal cold saliva, cooling sensation in abdomen. Modalities - Sitting aggravates the pain in back, better by bending backwards. Walking aggravates sharp pains in spleen and pain in right knee. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Am-c., Trimeth., Chen-a., Aphis. REFERENCES Clarke

full:
PHARMACY - cher-p-b. Cherry plum. Prunus cerasifera. Twigs of flowers are picked and boiled for half an hour. The boiled water i s strained and used as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle, (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.

HOMEOPATHIC - The remedy Cherry Plum belongs to the group For Those who have Fear, as classified by Bach. Further remedies in this group are Rck-r-b., Mimul-b., Asp-b., and Rd-ch-b. Cher-p-b. can help people suffering from diseases of the nervous system to find added peace in mind and body (Rck-r-b.). Extreme nervousness with a threatened nervous breakdown (Rck-r-b, Verv-b.). Nervous twitches, grimaces, and gestures are common in severe cases. The body expresses the mental struggle taking place within. The remedy is of service in tic disorders, elimination disorders and sexual disorders (Cer-b.). Mounting tension can release suddenly in unpredictable outbursts of violence. Physical concomitant symptoms related to speech problems. Phobias of all kind (Mimul-b, Rck-r-b.). Fear of sudden physical or mental failure, as in stammering, or in diseases such as epilepsy or repeated fainting. Fear of losing control over one's faculties, one feels helpless in the face of overwhelming stress. Severe pain, when one feels almost unable to bear the strain and torture, when the mind is at the verge of breaking down. During drug rehabilitation, physical and emotional cravings can be reduced. In some cases, unbearable pain can lead to homicide or suicide. MIND - The mind is over-strained and out of balance, after prolonged mental effort leading to failing nerve power and exhaustion. Delu- Cherry plum sions andpsychotic states when the boundaries of consciousness are disintegrating and the mind becomes subjected to unconscious and primordial forces. Nervousness, shyness and stage fright. Great anguish and distress, with intense fear of losing control. Fear that all balance will be lost and the impulsive, unwanted thoughts will win. Thrill or excitement from doing forbidden things. Problems in regard to impulses (Imp-b., Holly-b, Verv-b.). Obsessive-compulsive, perfectionist orritualistic behavior, with the intention to avoid succumbing to the dreaded impulses. Impulses dictating to carry out certain acts, dangerous to oneself or others, or socially unfit. Crimes and suicides. REFERENCES - Bach.

This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.

HOMEOPATHIC - Chestnut Bud, with Clem- b., Honey-b„ Wld-r-b.,Oliv-b. and Wh-ch-b., belongs to Bach's group of Not Sufficient Interest in Present Circumstances. These remedies help those not fully engaged in the here and now. Impulsive physical conduct and some degree of hyperactivity or restlessness can be concomitant physical features. One may bring the self and others in danger through recklessness, or disregard important physical needs. Developmental problems, attentiondeficit and hyperactivity disorder and disruptive behaviors. Ch-bd-b. helps the mind to settle into restful concentration and retain the learning material. Personality disorders marked by a refusal to change and acquire empathy for others, such as in antisocial, criminal and personality disorders (Vine-b.). MIND - Restless and impulsive, easily distracted. Absent-minded, not set on learning in the factual and moral sense. Jumps from topic to topic, goes superficially through a text, rushes ahead impatiently. Learned material is not contained very well, although capacity for memory is usually present. Inappropriate laughing or gliding over reprimands. Do not learn readily from their experiences, are often heedless or careless. Easily carried by positive as well as negative emotions. Unreasonable, easily swayed, naive. Emotionally unstable, impulsive. Defiant and somewhat lacking in integrity or depth. People not willing to obey laws and adjust to anormal socialization process. REFERENCES Bach.

full:
PHARMACY - chic-b. Chicory. Cichorium intybus. The flowers are picked, floated in a bowl of water and let sit in the sun for several hours. The strained water is used as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle, (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.

HOMEOPATHIC - Chicory belongs to the group of Over-care for Others' Welfare, as classified by Bach. The other remedies in this group are Rck-w-b., Beech-b., Vine-b., Verv-b. This group deals with mental, emotional imbalances in regard to caring for or controlling others. The inactive Chic-b. type may show an unspoken need to be loved. (Scler-b.). Self-pity, prone to pout or look hurt and withdrawn. Overly controlling and service- oriented, while suppressing hostile emotions and demanding attention when sick. Self-protective with an anxious attempt to hold in emotions. Ulcer patients, if prone to tyrannical outbursts, yet falling ill whenever affection is withdrawn. Anorexia, vomiting, nausea, bulimia and over-eating, in an effort to draw attention and love. Bronchial asthma, with difficulty in expiring, can rest on emotional hurt and self-pity. Diseases of soft tissue, rheumatism andrheumatoid arthritis of a psychosomatic origin. Hypochondriasis, pain disorders. Chronic constipation. MIND - Bent on taking care of others according to one's own design or idea, may be interpreted as being too forceful or unnecessary. Self-pity, a sense of not being appreciated for one's efforts. Fairly rigid opinions and ways of working with others. Conviction that one's perceptions and opinions are correct and one assumes the right to enforce them on others. Tendency to be overly careful with details, one's daily duties and cleanliness. Possessiveness of people, as well as of goods. Preoccupation with pain without physical findings. Personality disorders, based on attention seeking within the sexual sphere. Feigning sickness in order to gain attention (Ch-bd-b„ Heath-b.). Eating disorders (Crb- a-b.. Must-b.). Hysterical neurosis, when the body expresses through illness the unvoiced need for attention and love. Need to be the center of attention and be appreciated. Self-pity, sullenness and pouting, if affectionate attention is not offered. Annoyance and persisted self-pity if consoled, as if to arouse even more sympathy in the other. Manipulation, power play, pretense, threat, possessiveness, or feigning of sickness in order to convey that they feel hurt, offended, or overlooked. May reject being consoled, which increases their self-pity and may create further alienation in others. REFERENCES - Bach.

Stricture. Syphilis. Toothaches. Tumors. Ulcers, malignant. Urinary disorders. Whitlow.

HERBAL - Chim. is a medicine used by many North American Indians for gravel and urinary disorders. It has also been used as a vulnerary. Among the herbalists it is used as an alternative in skin affections, e.g., acne, herpes, eczema in enlarged lymphatic glands injoint rheumatism. It is said by them to act mainly as an eliminative through the bowels and kidneys. They use it in cases of chyliferous urine, cystitis, strangury, smarting, burning pains on urination, turbid urine and frequent urination and diabetes.

HOMEOPATHIC - Chim. acts principally on the kidneys and bladder, producing gravel in kidneys and acute and chronic catarrh in the bladder (cystitis). Scanty urine loaded with ropy, muco-purulent sediment. Calculus. Hepatic and kidney dropsies. Passive kidney, uterine and intestinal hemorrhages. Leucorrhea. Gonorrhea. Chim. also acts on the prostate and liver. Prostatic enlargement. Prostatic irritation. Catarrhal states with mucus, pus and blood, offensive or not. Affects lymphatic and mesenteric glands and female breasts. Plethoric young women with dysuria. Women with large breasts. Chronic alcoholics. Incipient and progressive cataracts.

Head - Pain in left frontal protuberance. Halo about the light. Itching of eyelids. Stabbing pain in the left eye with lachrymation. Tinea capitis.

Eyes - Halo around the light. Stabbing pain in the left eye with lachrymation.

Face - Flushing of cheeks with some general heat and quickened pulse.

Mouth - Jaws feel stiff, cannot close mouth at night, sleeps with the mouth open. Vesicular ulcers in mouth.

Throat - Palate sore, very sensitive to warm drink or food. Rawness of upper and back part of palate.

Abdomen - Aching pain below right hypochondrium while writing. Organic disease of the liver with ascites. Ascites. Scrofulous mesenteric gland.

Rectum - Sticking pain in left side rectum. deep in. Inclination to stool, either ineffectual or attended with great pain. Bloody mucus stools. Griping after stool. Diarrhea. Obstinate constipation, with hemorrhoids. Worms.

Male - Acute prostatitis with retention and dysuria and feeling of a ball in perineum, as if sitting on aball (Cann-i.). Gonorrhea and prostatitis. Smarting in urethra from neck of bladder to meatus, excessive itching. Gonorrhea, gleet, syphilis, prostatorrhea. Loss of prostatic fluid. Prostatic enlargement and irritation. Atrophy of testicles.

Female - Labia inflamed, swollen. Pain in vagina. Hot flashes. Prolapsed uterus or vagina. Leucorrhea.

Back - Sensation in region of kidneys, as if something were fluttering within. Breasts - Suppression of milk. Rapid atrophy of breasts. Scirrhus tumors. Painful tumor of breasts, not ulcerated, with undue secretion of milk. Painful breast tumor in young unmarried women. Women with very large breasts and tumor in the breast gland with sharp pain through it. Constitutions - Suited to cachectic, scrofulous individuals and broken-down constitutions. Abdominal and kidney dropsies in broken-drown constitutions and intemperate subjects. Women with large breasts or plethoric women with dysuria.

Limbs - Feeling of a band above left knee. Acute rheumatism of shoulder. Pain in right arm, about upper half of biceps and shoulder joint. Fistulous ulcer on right forearm, with stinging and crawling. Paronychia.

Skin - Scrofulous ulcers. Glandular enlargements. Redness, vesication or desquamation. Eruption of dark red spots without sensation. Malignant ulcers. Scarlet fever.

Modalities - Better from walking. Worse in damp weather, washing in cold water, sitting on cold stones orpavements, beginning urination, and on left side.

Teeth - Toothache, as if being gently pulled, worse after eating or from exertion, better by cold water.

Tongue - Tongue smarting, sore. Full of vesicles, great thirst and desire to cool the tongue. Tongue is furred, more towards root, no appetite. COMMENTS-Chim. has been proved by Jean G. Bute and H. P.Gatchell. Itcauses flushing of cheeks with some general heat and accelerated pulse. Increase of appetite. Worse in cold damp weather, after washing in cold water, from sitting on a cold, wet stone. Acute rheumatism of shoulder. Edema of arms (right). Inward trembling without mental disturbance. Cannot close jaws at night jaws feel stiff, sleeps with mouth open. Toothache worse after eating and from exertion, better by cold water. Palate sore, very sensitive to warm drink or food, rawness of upper and back part of palate. Inflammation of liver with ascites, abdominal and kidney dropsies. Enlarged mesenteric glands. Gallstone colic. Particularly indicated for kidney and liver problems in conjunction (Berb., Lyc.). Constant pain in region of kidneys, as if something fluttering in kidney region, first one side, then the other. Obstinate constipation and hemorrhoids. Deep-seated shooting pain in the left side of anus. “Sensation of swelling in perineum on sitting, as if a ball was pressing against it.” Pressing fullness in region of bladder. Bladder tenesmus, strangury. Constant desire to urinate, must rise several times in the night. Great quantities of thick, ropy mucus in urine. Blood in urine. Smarting pain, painful irritation from neck of bladder, whole length of urethra to meatus. Prostatic disorders. Loss of prostatic fluid. Bruised pain in testicle, with stricture. Leucorrhea. Rapid atrophy of breasts ortumors. In homeopathic practice, Coburn reported the cures in several cases. The first concerned a case of stricture in a man, 30. He had dysuria, severe pain, scalding and burning. At times urine voided in a large gush, at others in thready stream and towards the end, drained off drop by drop. Merc-c. and Canth. had temporarily relieved. Coburn also noted a case of prostatitis after sitting on cold stone. There was pain and a sensation as if he had bruised one of the testicles. The third case Coburn recorded concerned a case of breast cancer in a 21 year old patient. Tumor in left breast, hard, movable, sharp pains at site. For four months, under Arn., Ars., Cic., Thuj., the tumor increased, skin became contracted, nipple drawn in. In eight months, it broke out into an irregular ulceration with lacerated edges, fetid discharge. Axillary glands swollen. Chim. 1c in 10 drops doses, every four hours was given and the same locally applied. The pains diminished. Swelling decreased, and in six months the patient was well. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Chim-m. - intense gnawing hunger, burning fever, sensation of swelling in arm pits. (2) Uva., Ledum, Epigea. (3) Apoc. - dropsy, Agnus - gonorrhea, breast-feeding, Con., Coff. - toothache better by cold water. (4) Rhod., Kahn., Uva., Sabal. (5) In pterygium Calc., Zinc. Ball in perineum, Cann-i. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Kidneys - Acute inflammation of the urinary tract. Nephritis. Suppressed urine in infants. Urging to urinate. Urine turbid offensive, containing ropy or bloody mucus and depositing a copious sediment. Burning and scalding during urination and straining afterwards. Must strain before flow comes. Scanty urine. Fluttering in region of kidney. Cystitis. Bladder tenesmus, worse sitting, better walking. Cannot pass urine without standing with feet apart and body inclined forwards. Clots of blood pass with urine. Sugar in urine.

Temperature - Hectic fever and night sweats. Flushing of checks with general heat.

HOMEOPATHIC - China boliviana has the main features of Chin, off., but some are peculiar and deserve separate mention. Chin-b. was proved by Modiedo. Chin-b. has ulceration of commissures of mouth. Cough with dagger-like pains in base Of right lung. Rigidity of nape of neck. Hands red hot or cold and sticky. Sticky sweat about the anus. Flatulence. Disturbed and dream-filled sleep. Sensitiveness to touch. MIND - Gloom alternating with serenity. Alternation of bad and good humor. Fits of rage, blasphemes. Cowardice.

Head - Headache in morning on awaking, leaves during the day or lasts all day and leaves during sleep.

Eyes - Violent pains like a stab in left eyes, followed by itching and tears.

Ears - Detonation as of a cannon in right ear. Ringing, humming, whistling sounds.

Face - Aphthae on inner surface of lips, ulceration of commissures. Food - Hunger or lack of appetite, repugnance to meat. After eating, feels a weight in stomach. Cold, sneezing, sleepy and desire to sleep in evening.

Mouth - Mouth bitter in morning on waking. Nose - Much sneezing on awaking with smell of fresh pus. Sensation of incipient cold with tight feeling and pain in throat. Violent cold in head. Mucus from posterior sinuses.

Stomach - Much gas rises from stomach. Throat - Constriction and burning in throat. Vertigo - Vertigo as after a drunken fit, voracious appetite. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Abdomen - Pain in both hypochondria and under ribs on waking in the morning. Pain in splenic region.

Rectum - Biting in anus as from worms, excoriated sensation. Viscous sweat on anus.

Male - Pollutions exceedingly weakening. Excoriation on inner and lower part of prepuce. Gleet and ulceration of prepuce.

Back - Nape of neck rigid, cannot turn head to right, any sudden movement causes a snap or crack. Wry- neck. Pain in left shoulder, left buttock and also in right hip bone on sitting up in bed.

Limbs - Legs and feet icy cold, as if blown on by wintry wind. Painful corns. Lungs - Cough with pain in right lung, as from a dagger buried there, at times makes breathing laborious, burning in eyes, limbs cold. Unbearable pain in right lung, extends to region of liver, sensitive to touch.

Sleep - Dreams of the sea, of fishes, swimming, bathing. Dreams of journeys by land and sea, Dreams of vomiting of worms.
