author: Murphy
keynote:
PHARMACY - culx. Culex musca. Mosquito. N. O. Culicide. Insecta. Tincture. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Cramps. Edema. Flatus. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - Kent wrote “When this remedy is needed your patient will present to you a picture of something on fire, he burns…
full:
PHARMACY - culx. Culex musca. Mosquito. N. O. Culicide. Insecta. Tincture. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Cramps. Edema. Flatus. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - Kent wrote “When this remedy is needed your patient will present to you a picture of something on fire, he burns like something he would like to mention and perhaps does mention the place, the itching and burning are present every where in this remedy, he mbs and scratches wherever the eruptions appears.” Edematous swelling. Sensation as of cold air blowing through a hole in clothes on the chest or back. Strange feeling of having been poisoned. Menses stain indelibly. Generally a right-sided remedy. Sharp, stinging pains all over the body like needles, lightning-like. Pain, itching, burning, worse in a warm room and better in the open air. Pains darting here and there, aggravated by light pressure and ameliorated by hard pressure. Griping pain down over hips, then into the womb. Vertigo on blowing the nose. Tired and weak. Can scarcely move, cannot walk straight, with soreness and aching all over the body. Nervous, finds it impossible to keep still, almost constant motion of the hands and feet (Zinc.). MINI) - Busy scratching to relieve the itching, and walking to relieve the restlessness, any interruption makes him impatient and ready to quarrel. Anxiety and fear of death. Poor memory and a disinclination for all work.

Head - Dull, frontal headache, begins on waking at 5 a.m. and passes away after lying awake for a while. Headache, worse from the least motion. Headache followed by intense vertigo in the afternoon, located in a spot over the right eye. Head pains go from the cerebellum to the forehead or right temple. Boring pains in the temples, several times a day. Pain comes and goes across the forehead just above the eyes. Rending pain in back of the eyeballs. Itching and stinging of the scalp.

Eyes - Inflamed eyeballs. Stye-like ulceration. Rending pains in the eyeballs, could not keep his eyes open, yet it pained to keep them shut. Eyes feel tired. Feeling of fullness in the right eye, extending to the parotid gland, to the sub-lingual, and finally involves the right side of the face and head. Margins of the lids are sore and crusted over. Inflammation of the lids, worse in the morning with a discharge of sticky fluid.

Ears - Swelling of the parotid glands and soreness on pressure, pain as if he were going to have mumps. Sharp pains in both ears followed by sticky, watery discharge.

Nose - Itching, stinging and tickling. Rubs and scratches because his nose itches inside and out, but rubbing increased burning. Shining redness on top of nose. Nose is swollen. Eruptions contain a clear colorless fluid. Nosebleed, morning and night on blowing the nose. Head feels stuffed. Ineffectual desire to sneeze. Watery discharge with bloody scabs on the inside, dry or moist and bloody. Copious discharge, greenish or light- colored.

Face - Swollen sub-maxillary gland, tender on pressure. Eruption on the face and between the eyes, contains a colorless fluid, with swelling and puffiness underthe eyes. Heat and redness of the right side of the face, with a sore bruised feeling.

Mouth - Dryness and burning. Constant wetting of the lips. Saliva leaves the lips sticky. Whitish saliva, leaves a bad taste in the mouth in the morning. Sickish taste as if he had been drinking warm mineral water. Periodical attacks of salivation, at night the pillow is wet and the daytime the saliva accumulates and causes continued swallowing (Merc.). Foul breath, seemed as if he could smell it himself.

Throat - Burning and dryness of the throat. Soreness in throat and in the posterior sinuses on swallowing solids or fluids. The right side of the throat is always sore. Hoarseness, could scarcely speak a word, in the morning.

Stomach - Increased appetite. Undigested food sours in the stomach.

Abdomen - Cramps in the abdomen during stool, with rumbling and the passing of much offensive flatus. Colicky pairs come on about 10 a.m. and last from one to three hours. Blotcheson the abdomen the size of a twenty-five cent piece. Itching, burning, with little pimples on the blotches.

Rectum - Usual desire for morning stool is absent. Stool is scanty, lumpy and expelled with effort. First part of the stool is hard and scratches the anus, followed by a soft stool. After stool, sensation that he has not finished so he sits and strains until blood comes (Merc.). Itching and burning of the anus, scalding hot and raw as from a bite.

Male - Burning of the glans penis. Strong smelling discharge from the glans. Itching of the scrotum from swollen, burning spots, like bee stings. Rubbing aggravates itching, stinging, and burning.

Female - Menses, too soon, with a profuse dark clotted flow. Violent pains in the uterus, compelling her to go to bed. Itching and burning in vagina, so intense that she feels as if she could tear it to pieces, can return at intervals for years. Food - Ravenous appetite, feels faint if supper is late. Especially hungry and faint in the morning, cannot wait for breakfast to be prepared.

Chest - Cutting pains in the right pectoral muscles. Right side of the neck is swollen.

Back - Dull pain in the right side in the region of the kidney, extending up the back to the occiput.

Limbs - Hands and fingers are hot and burning, as if frozen with severe pain. As if he must tear the flesh for relief while the back of the hands felt cold and benumbed. Right hand is cold, left hand is warm. Lower limbs feel heavy apd restless. Feet are tired all day. Soles tender while walking. Intense itching on the tops of the feet. Lungs - Oppression and anxiety in the chest. Apex of the right lung sore, aggravated by deep breathing or raising the right arm. Deep sighing breathing, with constant desire for a deep breath. Constant desire to sneeze and cough. On rising, hawking and coughing dark green scabs and strings of tough mucus tinged with dark blood. Cough caused by burning in the chest. Whistling, strangling, choking cough, with red face and water running from the eyes. Dry hacking cough with the feeling as if he would vomit. Small amount of yellowish white expectoration.

Sleep - Restless, unrefreshing sleep, much tossing about. Dreams of quarrels, fights and of the dead. Heat of the bed causes him to waken frequently, must rise early in the morning to move around for relief.

Skin - Tormented by itching, burning, heat. Must scratch to relieve the constant itching, but aggravates. No comfort in or out of bed.

Tongue - Tongue is coated white, dry, swollen. thick on waking. Edge of the tongue is covered with a double row of small, painful vesicles. Tongue numb, with ulceration at the tip following scarlet fever. COMMENTS - Culex was proved by Kent, but the only verification Clarke found was of the symptom “vertigo every time he blows his nose.” W. P. Wesselheft cured a man, 40, stout, thick-set, light brunette, who had swelling on upper jaw over first right tricuspid. Slight redness of cheek. Abscess threatened with paroxysmal throbbing, dull pain better by warm applications. This came on after exposure to wet weather. Merc, and Rhus-t. did no good. The patient then said that whenever he blew his nose he had vertigo with a sense of fullness in the ears. Culx. promptly relieved the pain and in forty-eight hours the swelling had gone. RELATIONS - Compare: Apis. REFERENCES - Clarke. Kent.

Temperature - Hot flushes as if a chill would follow, followed by warm, sticky, strong smelling perspiration.

full:
PHARMACY - cund. Cundurango. Condor plant. Condurango. Gonolobus cundurango. Marsdenia cundurango. N. O. Asclepiadacae. Ecuador. South America. Tincture and trituration of the dried bark of the stem. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anus, cracks. Breast, tumors. Cancer. Cracks. Eczema. Epithelioma. Fistula. Headaches. Locomotor, ataxia. Lupus. Rodent, ulcer. Smallpox. Stomach, cancer. Stomach, disorders. Syphilis. Tumors. Ulcers. Varicose, ulcers.

HOMEOPATHIC - The Condor plant was first introduced into medicine as a cancer remedy by Dr. Bliss of Washington. Cundurango belongs to the Milk-weed family and is thus related to Asclepias Syriaca and Tuberosa and also to Calotropis. Cancer, especially for those originating in epithelial structures. Scirrhus cancers. Cancer of the breasts with retraction of the Cundurango nipples and sharp pains emanating from the tumor over the whole breast. Jagged ulcers of the tongue. Tumors, strictures of the esophagus. Cancer of the stomach with constant burning and vomiting, food seems to stick behind the sternum. Allays the stomach pain accompanying cancer of stomach. Stimulates the digestive functions and thus improves the general health. Modifies secretions of digestive glands. Chronic stomach catarrh. Cutting, stinging, burning, tingling, constrictive and piercing pains. Cracks at muco-cutaneous orifices and warty excrescences. Painful cracks in corner of mouth. Blotches. Eczema, pimples, pustules. Indolent ulcers. Varicose ulcers. Lupus. Syphilitic affections. The active principle (Condurangin) produces locomotor ataxia. This remedy is worth trying when other seemingly indicated remedies fail to effect the disease. MIND - Depressed, miserable. Irritable.

Head - Severe dull headache all day. Violent pain in left temple, cutting in left temple and through ball of left eye. Sensation as if forehead were broad and high, as if left half were bigger than right. Left half feels heavy, right half feels clear. Cundurango

Eyes - Flat epithelioma on lower eyelid. Appearance of objects before eyes.

Nose - Much glairy mucus from nose, alternating with unusual dryness. Stiffness in nose. Pressive full feeling in bridge. Flat epithelioma left side of nose. Nasal sound to voice.

Face - Deep crack in corner in corner of mouth, warty growths occupying edges. Ulcer on chin, right side perforating to gums.

Mouth - Slight pain in left half of tongue. Small, painful pustule on right side of tip of tongue, on upper surface towards edge. Cracks at angles of mouth. Tongue cancer.

Throat - Aching in throat, extending to stomach with great burning in stomach. Persistent sore throat, with burning, aching and a husky feeling which causes a dry, hacking cough. Vertigo - Great dizziness on stooping, or turning head. COMMENTS - Burnett, who proved it and whose symptoms were of a severe nature, observed that it produced “a painful crack in the right corner of the mouth.” These cracks were produced in several patients who were taking the drug and Burnett cured similar cracks with it. He regarded them as a keynote indication and has cured patients of tumors, some undoubtedly cancerous, who had that symptom as a concomitant. Cundurango Clotar Muller cured with Cund. several cases of old, obstinate, foul-smelling, ichorous ulcers. Carcinoma of the lips, an unclean and sinus ulcer. Dudgeon recorded a cure with Cund. first dilution of an undoubted case of cancer of left breast in a women of sixty-nine. The nipple was so retracted as to be invisible. A hard tumor the size of an egg on the outer side of the nipple was the center of sharp pains radiating from it, the whole breast was very tender to touch. The tumor increased steadily under Hydr. and Phyt. and was only checked temporarily by Con. Under Cund., it entirely disappeared. Burnett considered it to have a strong affinity for the tongue. He cured a jagged ulcer of the tongue (doubtful whether cancerous or syphilitic), where the tongue and lips were red. One prover had a slight creeping pain along the periosteum of the right humerus and Clarke observed “a creeping sensation up the back and headache in right temple” in a patient taking it in the lx tincture. An old-school authority, Dr. Guyvenot, credits Condurango with causing a “veritable locomotor ataxia.” It appears late and he thinks it is due to the formation of some toxic substance by the splitting up of the alkaloid in the organism. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aster. Con., Hydr., Ars. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Anorexia. Painful disorders of the stomach, ulceration. Stomach cancer. Vomiting of food with indurations and constant burning pain. Stricture of esophagus with burning pains behind sternum, where food seems to stick.

Abdomen - Pain in right hypochondrium.

Rectum - Constipation. Cracks at anus, terrible pains when bowels are moved.

Chest - Cancer-like ulcers on false ribs, as large as hand. Constitutions - Cancerous diathesis. Broken-down constitution. In Burnett's opinion, it is anti-psoric.

Heart - Constrictive pain. Sharp, distinct pain in heart on rising in morning, followed by passage of flatus.

Back - Dull, heavy, continuing pain in left scapula. Breasts - Tumor of breast on either side. Cracked, painful, suppurating nipples. Retraction of the nipples. Hard, painful swellings around nipple, ranging in size from pigeon's to hen's egg. Axillary glands swollen, emaciation.

Limbs - Soreness all over body like rheumatism, worse through left shoulder and under left scapula (burning). Cracks on hips and in bends of knees.

Skin - Fissures form about the muco-cutaneous outlets. Epithelioma of lips or anus. Ulcerative stage of carcinoma when fissures form. Some small congenital warty excrescences enlarge and look fresh. Blotches, pimples and boils.

Kidneys - Incontinence of urine. Urine scanty, high-colored, loaded with phosphates.

full:
PHARMACY - cuph. Cuphea viscosissima. Flux-weed. Lythrum petiolatum. Waxweed. Red pennyroyal. N. O. Lythraceae. Decoction or tincture of fresh plants collected in July or August. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acidity. Cholera infantum. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Fever. Sleeplessness. Tenesmus. Vomiting.

HERBAL - Cuphea viscosissima is a popular remedy in some parts of the U.S. for summer diarrhea and dysentery, as one of its names, Cuphea viscosissima “Flux weed,” would imply. The entire plant has a clammy, sticky feel. It contains a large percentage of tannic acid and seems to possess decidedly tonic properties, as children rally rapidly under its use.

HOMEOPATHIC - Vomiting of undigested food. Cholera infantum, much acidity. Frequent green, watery, acid stools. Tenesmus and great pain. Obstinate constipation. High fever, restlessness and sleeplessness. COMMENTS - Cuphea viscosissima was first introduced to homeopathic practice by Dr. A. Roth of Frederick, Maryland, who was induced to try it in his practice by a female patient. His experience was confirmed by S. G. A. Brown. Dr. Roth gave from 5 to 10-drop doses, according to age. He considered in to have “tonic” properties. Roth found it to be highly successful in two chief forms, but useless in diarrhea from cold. The first form consists of cases arising from acidity of milk or food. There is vomiting of undigested food or curdled milk with frequent green, watery, acid stools, varying in number from five to thirty a day. Children are fretful and feverish, can retain nothing on stomach, food seems to pass right through the child. In the second form, stools are decidedly dysenteric, small frequent, bloody with tenesmus and great pain, high fever, restlessness and sleeplessness. Brown said “If you have a child that is fretful and feverish, vomits curdled milk from a hyperacidity of the stomach, has frequent green, watery, acid stools or even if the stools are dysenteric with great tenesmus and colic, high fever and restlessness, give Cuphea.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aeth. (2) Coto Bark - intestinal catarrh, chronic, copious, exhausting diarrhea and dysentery, colliquitine sweats of tuberculosis and chronic diarrhea. (3) Typha latifolia, Cat-tail flag - diarrhea, dysentery, summer complaint of children. Tincture and first potency. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke.

HOMEOPATHIC - Cupre-1. has been proved in a fragmentary way by Burnett, who had to relinquish the proving on account of the “terrible pains it caused in the stomach.” Burnett concluded from his experience that the action of Cupre-1. is like that of Thuj. He successfully used it as a variant of that remedy and of Sabin, in the cure of tumors like cocks-comb growth in the mouth, lipoma of the thigh, and keloids. REFERENCES - Clarke.

PHARMACY - cupr-acet. Cuprum aceticum. Copper acetate. Verdigris. Solutions.Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.

Measles. Paralyzes. Psoriasis. Scarlatina. Smallpox. Strabismus. Stroke. Tapeworm. Uremia. Vertigo. Whooping cough.

HOMEOPATHIC - Burnett cured with Cupr-acet. a case of left-sided brow ague of many years' standing. He used Rademacher's Tincture of Copper. The pain was described as boring, screwing and was spoken of by the patient as “awful.” Burnett was unable to say whether the cure was strictly homeopathic or whether the Cuprum acted on the basis of the Paracelsus's Universalia, of which it is one. Cupr-acet. produces the leading features of Cupr., including cramps, griping pains, spasms, paralytic disorders and convulsions. Attacks come on suddenly and periodically. Protracted labor. Facial neuralgia in cheekbone, upper jaw and behind the ear better by chewing, pressure and hot applications. Chorea, periodical with melancholy and dread of society. In epilepsy, aura begins in the knee and ascends to hypogastrium. Chronic psoriasis and leprous-like eruption over whole body in spots of various sizes without itching. It corresponds to the results of repelled eruptions. Hay fever with burning excoriation. Paroxysmal cough with tough, tenacious mucus and fear of suffocation. Constitutions - Suited to the carbo-nitrog- enous constitution.

Head - Neuralgia with heaviness of head, burning, stinging and stitching in temples and forehead. Violent throbbing and sharp pains in forehead. Left-sided brow ague. Brain seems void. Inclined to gape and cry. Loses consciousness, headreels when in large room. Constant protrusion and retraction of tongue (Lach.). Lungs - Spasmodic constriction of the chest. Violent spasmodic cough. Short, difficult respiration. Dyspnea. Attacks of angina pectoris coming on when excited.

Face - Collapsed, hippocratic. Facial neuralgiain cheekbone, upper jaw and behind right ear. Better by chewing, pressure and external warmth.

Stomach - Violent spasmodic pains in stomach and abdomen. Vomiting. Violent tenesmus. Slimy brown diarrhea. Cholera. Vertigo - Head reels when in a high-ceilinged room. COMMENTS - A man, 50, was cured with Cupr-acet. 5c trituration, of a tonic spasm of the toes of the right foot, very painful, lasting for hours, brought on by friction, standing on cold floors, etc. There was no traceable cause and no other derangement of health. Complete cure in five days after months of previous suffering. Petroz recommended its use in smallpox and verified his induction in practice. As pointed outby General Phelps, the “Crimson Cross Ointment” which was used successfully by Fielden in the Gloucester epidemic of smallpox owes its virtue to the Cupr-acet. which it contains. In epilepsy, the aura begins in the knees and ascends to hypogastrium, when patient becomes insensible. The symptoms are worse by heat and motion. The patient frequently changes posture. RELATIONS - Acts similarly to Cupr. but is more violent in action. In poisoning cases it is Antidoted by: sugar or white of egg, given freely. Homeopathic antidotes: Bell., Chin., Con., Cic., Dulc., Hep., Ip., Merc., Nux-v.

Skin - Leprous-like eruption over whole body in spots of various sizes, without itching.

Modalities - Better chewing. Better pressure. Better night. Better lying on affected side and warmth. Worse from heat. Worse motion. Worse emotions. Worse touch.

Compare - (l)Calc., Gels, -overworked brain. (2) Cic. and Solanaceae - mental symptoms. (3) Zinc. - hydrocephalus and convulsions from suppressed exanthems. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Paralysis, left sided. Ulcers. Uremia. Uterine, neuralgia. Vomiting. Cuprum arsenicosum HOMEOPATHIC - Cupr-ar. combines the characters of its two metallic components. J. N. Majumdar noted the great characteristic of Cupr-ar. in choleraic conditions after B. L. Bhaduri pointed it out to him. Majumdar noted “icy-coldness of the whole body with cramps and an obstinate hiccough.” Various intestinal affections. Cholera morbus and infantum. Rice water stools. Entero-colitis, diarrhea and dysentery. Gastro-intestinal disturbances of influenza or typhoid. Inflammation of the digestive tract with violent colic, vomiting, diarrhea and uremia, with obstinate hiccough and icy cold body. Deficient kidney action. Urine of garlicky odor. Uremic convulsions, headache, vertigo and unconscious conditions resulting from brain edema. Uremic convulsions preceded by gastro-intestinal symptoms. Nephritis ofpregnancy. Awful distress in epigastric region, burning along esophagus and in urethra. Numbness, creeping, itching and chilly sensations. Intense neuralgic pains in abdomen. Visceral neuralgia, sharp shooting abdominal pains. Painful neuroses, enteroptosis. Violent cramps in chest, fingers, calves toes etc. Delirium and tremor cordis. Leg cramps, better pressing foot on the floor. Numb paralyzed feeling in the legs. Trembling of the whole body when attempting to walk. Chorea after fright. Bronchial asthma and with emphysema. Chlorosis. Weak heart. Purulent endocarditis (Royal). Cold, clammy intermittent sweat. Abdomen - Gastro-enteritis. Violent abdominal pain. Rumbling and sharp, cutting pain.

Mouth - Tongue thickly coated, dirty brown, white, metallic taste, thirst. Dry mouth.

Rectum - Rice water stools. Cholera infantum, cholera (Verat., Camph.). Rumbling and sharp, cutting pain. Dark liquid stools. Diarrhea in tuberculosis.

Heart - Cardiac rhythm and force altered due to defective elimination.

Back - Persistent lameness. Pain in lumbar region, lower left shoulder blade, chest tight.

Limbs - Cramps in calves of legs, worse after midnight, only relieved by getting out of bed and standing. Gangrene ulcers. Male - Perspiration of scrotum is constantly damp and moist. Boils on scrotum. Purulent discharge of a white color from urethra, tingling and burning in urethra. Pain in prostate, pains in penis.

Skin - Icy cold sweat and skin even when dry. Cold, clammy perspiration of an intermittent nature. Acne, pustules on face and in the genital region, ulcers look like chancre. Gangrene, carbuncles. COMMENTS - Salzer showed that “cold, clammy perspiration of intermittent nature” is unique and characteristic. He found it most valuable in the collapse stage of cholera, where intermittent cold, clammy sweat was noted. The skin is very sensitive to touch and pressure worse all symptoms. Weakness and restlessness. Periodicity in the symptoms. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ars. and Cupr. preparations (2) Aeon., Cimic. - angina pectoris, numbness of left side of body, paresis of left arm. (3) Merc-c. - diarrhea and tenesmus. (3) Iris-v. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Modalities - Better rest and worse motion, but stiffness of back and tingling of hands are better from motion. Damp weather causes neuralgia of abdomen.

Kidneys - Diabetes. Kidney inefficiency and uremia. Garlic odor of urine. Urine of high specific gravity increased, acetones and diacetic acid.

Psoriasis. Ringworm. Sleeplessness. Spasms. Spinal irritation. Tapeworms. Ulcers. Whooping cough. Worms. Yellow fever.

HOMEOPATHIC - Metallic copper is one of the most important remedies where the diseased conditions “appear” on account of the non-appearance or suppressions of eruptions and the discharges. Skin eruptions and foot-sweat. Effects of suppression of eruptions, exanthems and foot-sweat, whether these effects are internal pains or spasms or oppression of the brain and mental disturbance. Affects the nerves of the cerebro-spinal axis and muscles, causing spasmodic effects, convulsions and cramps of violent form. Cramps in toes, fingers, calves where the muscles are knotted, better stretching. Cramps beginning in fingers and toes, violent, contractive and intermitting pain. Cramps may occur in the chest (angina pectoris), behind the sternum. Cramps in the limbs in elderly people, particularly leg cramps (Calc., Mag-p., acutely). Cramps before sex, preventing sex, in the calves, soles and feet. Spasms with blue face and clenched thumbs. Jerking during sleep. Restless tossing all night. Stupor with jerking of muscles. Paralysis of isolated muscles. Chorea from fright, periodical. Chorea from suppressed eruptions. Convulsions of children during dentition, children lie on abdomen and jerk the buttock up. Convulsions are tonic or clonic. With convulsions, the eyes roll upward, out, or inward (Aeth.). Convulsions start in the knees, toes, or fingers and radiate over the whole body with piercing ties. Twisting of the head to one side. Trismus followed by headache. Spasmodic laughter. Shivering. Deathly exhaustion with cold perspiration. Epilepsy, at night, during menses. Violent epilepsy, legs may shoot out and lock in spasm. Epilepsy after suppressed eruptions, especially on the head (Zinc). Epilepsy after fright. In epilepsy, aura begins at knees, ascends to hypogastrium, then unconsciousness, foaming and falling. The patient falls with a shriek, passes urine and feces. Headache follows after spasms or a group of symptoms. Followed by the appearance as if the patient were dead or in a state of ecstasy. Pains like knife-thrusts, worse on least motion, that take away the breath. Patient thinks that he must die if they last. The thrusts go through to the back from the umbilicus. Pains worse touch and motion. Pressive pains, as from a blow being broken, racking darts through the whole body. Cholera (Verat., Camph.). Gushing watery stools, with blue, cold extremities and jerking and cramping. Tape- worms. Complaints from scarlet fever, including excessive vomiting, stupor, and convulsions. Nausea. Meningitis. Chlorosis. Hypersensitive, every drug overacts without curing. Easy relapses. Symptoms disposed to appear periodically and in groups. Complaints begin in left side (Lach.). MIND - Nervous. Uneasy. Fixed ideas, malicious and morose. Sullen, tricky, alternating yielding and head- strong. Imitates, mimics. Speaks in a whisper because of pain. Uses words not intended. Sense of losing consciousness. Attacks of rage, wants to bite the bystanders. Mania, bites, beats, tears the things. Delirium, cold sweat. Piercing shrieks. Weeps violently. Convulsive laughter. Fearful. Confusion, afraid of everybody who approaches him. Loquacious, then melancholy with fear of death. Fear of society, shuns everybody. Abdomen - Tense, hot and tender to touch. Neuralgia of abdominal viscera. Spasmodic movements of abdominal muscles. Frightful colic with contraction of the abdomen. Better pressure, worse raising arms. Intussusception, with fecal vomiting.

Head - Meningitis, cannot hold head erect or bores into the pillow. Pulls her hair. Shakes the head from side to side. Strange tingling, crawling in the vertex (suppressed menses). Headache after epilepsy. Sensation as if water were poured over the head with headache. Empty feeling with pain. Purple, red swelling of head with convulsions. Bruised pain in brain and eyes on turning them.

Eyes - Aching over eyes. Fixed, staring, sunken, glistening, turned upwards. Eyeballs rotate quickly behind closed lids or roll from side to side. Bruised pain in the orbits, worse moving the eyes. Lids spasmodically closed, twitching of lids (left). Photophobia.

Nose - Stoppage of the nose. Sensation of violent congestion of blood to nose (Meli.). Violent, fluent coryza.

Face - Distorted,pale bluish, livid, sunken, pinched. Icy cold. Lips blue. Chewing motion of the lower jaw. Lockjaw. Contraction of jaws with foam at mouth.

Mouth - Strong metallic, slimy taste with flow of saliva. Froth from mouth. Grinds the teeth. Food tastes like clear water. Stammering speech, loss of speech. Paralysis of tongue. Firmly closed or open with tongue darting in and out like a snake in convulsions.

Throat - Swelling of the glands of the neck. Spasms of throat. Unable to talk on account of spasms of throat. Dryness of the throat, with thirst. Inflammation of the pharynx. Audible sound of drinking (gurgling), while swallowing it. Intermittent aphonia in professional singers. Vertigo - Giddiness accompanies many ailments, head falls forward on chest. Vertigo with internal tremors, head sinks forwards on the chest, better stool, lying down, worse looking up. COMMENTS - Metallic copper is an anti-psoric remedy, working from within outwards. It is one of the most important remedies that relieve states arising from the “striking inward’’ of diseases or the failure of eruptions or discharge to appear. Suppressed discharges that lead to spasms and convulsions. Relieve internal spasms which renders it appropriate to the collapse stage of cholera (Sulph.). Aprophylactic either when worn next the skin or when taken internally. Maliciousness and a desire to injure. Screaming with cerebral or mental symptoms. Loquaciousness. Violent head pains that are worse over the left eye. Brain seems paralyzed. Over-sensitiveness of the skin, especially in the region of the stomach and fourth and fifth dorsal vertebrae. Cramps, spasms, twitches, and convulsions. Twitches of little muscles spread into the major muscles and can ultimately go into aconvulsion. Face will turn blue, fingers and toes cramp, thumb will go into the hand and lock. B ack arches, neck goes back. Drawing in the fingers. Sudden and severe flexion and extension of the limbs. Cramps and convulsions in meningitis, cholera, whooping cough and spasmatic asthma. Spasms of the stomach that lead to nausea and vomiting. Severe spasms after a vexation or a fright (Op.). Vomiting, hiccoughs and spasms better by drinking cold water. Whooping cough. Violent, spasmodic coughing, worse cold air (Rumx.). Wheezing and spasm. Spasmodic breathing with rattling in the chest. Asthma with bluish lips and spasms and constriction of the chest. Constriction pains with stress of asthma (Cact.). Constriction below the xiphoid process. Feels as if stuck with the knife from the xiphoid to the back. Cramps at puberty, better bathing in Cuprum metallicum cold water. Convulsions during menses. Dysmenorrhea associated with cramps in the fingers, severe cramps and spasms In the uterus. Labor pains are so severe they start convulsing. Or they feel the labor pains and their hands and feet start cramping up or spasms outside the uterus. Sudden blindness during labor. Senile gangrene with the toes and fingers due to poor circulation, with cramps and spasms in the fingers and toes (Ars., Sec., Agar.). Chlorosis from abuse of iron. J. C. McLaren noted “Cramps or spasms beginning in hands and feet, extending to belly.” Guernsey said that “a slimy metallic taste in the mouth” is one of the strongest indications for Cupr. (Rhus-t.). Paralysis of the tongue, stammering (Caust., Merc.). Grinds teeth at night. Thirst for cold drinks and ameliorated by cold drinks. Worse inhaling cold air. Mackechnie made a brilliant cure of psoriasis in a young girl with Cupr. The leading features of its symptomatology are cramps, convulsions, violent spasms, coming on from disappearance of pains, discharges, eruptions, mental derangement. Patient screams with suppression of menses. Tonic spasms of thumbs. Eyeballs turn up. Opisthotonos. Tonic and clonic spasms. Convulsions during pregnancy. Puerperal convulsions which begin in the fingers or toes and spread all over the body. Can also have a great restlessness between the attacks, either filling up the entire interval or only a part of the time. Mossa regarded Cupr. as one of the remedies for the effects of fright, and relates the case of a girl who after a fright was affected by involuntary motions of left arm and leg developing into pronounced general chorea. Cupr. brought about slow but decided recovery. Another girl, 12, who had recovered from whooping cough got a kind of chorea from repeated frights on seeing an epileptic. To the muscular movements was added silly behavior including a heavy tongue, slow speech and unwieldy gait. Frightened at night. Greediness in eating and drinking. Ign., Stram., Sulph., did little good. She became ill-natured. Cupr. every four days cured completely in three months. Mackechnie reported the case of a boy who became epileptic after being locked up in school. Very great improvementfollowed the administration of Cupr. Schwencke cured a case of epilepsy of forty years' standing with Cupr. 6c after Bell, and Hyos. had done little good. The patient was a man aged 45. The fits began suddenly towards morning with chewing motion of lower jaw, gnashing of teeth, becomes upright and rigid in bed, shrieks, limbs convulsed. After giving way to violent anger, attacks become more severe, arms and legs were thrown outwards and trunk arched upward. Cupr. was given. For a time the attacks continued, but gradually improvement set in and in less than three months they ceased altogether. The “anger” in this case and the “ill-humor” in Mossa's are noteworthy as maliciousness is an indication for Cupr. In a second case cured by Schwencke, that of a man, 38, epileptic seven years, a pressive headache preceded the attacks, ascending from nape to forehead, then there was profuse salivation, head turned to left, eyes closed tongue in active motion in open mouth, trunk arched upward, slight spasms of right arm outward. After the attack, there was a dullness in the head and a feeling in the body as if beaten. Cupr. first removed the fits and then the dullness of the head. RELATIONS -Antidotes: Bell., Hep., Camph. Copper is found in Dulc., Staph., Con. and some other plants. Also in the king-crab, Limulus. Compare: ( 1 ) Cupr-s. Cupr-cyan. - meningitis basilaris. (2) Cholas terrapina- cramps in calves and feet, rheumatism with cramp-like pains, Plb.. Nux-v, Verat. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Painful crampy pressure in epigastrium, worse touch and movement. Lies on stomach and jerks the buttocks up (colic, convulsions). Whendrinking, thefluid descends with gurgling sound (Laur.). As if something bitter were in stomach. Hiccough, before vomiting, convulsions, spasms or asthma. Pronounced nausea. Periodical attacks of vomiting. Vomiting, violent tormenting with agonizing colic, diarrhea, shrieks or convulsions, better cold drinks. Vomits always on waking up in morning, on least motion.

Rectum - Cholera with cramps in abdomen and calves. Cholera, summer diarrhea in children. Diarrhea, profuse, spurting out of green water. Black, painful, bloody with tenesmus and weakness. Constipation with great heat of body. Round, tapeworms or threadworms.

Male - Cramps in calves prevents sex. especially in old or nervous young men.

Female - Menses too late, protracted. Menses absent due to suppression of foot sweat. Violent cramps in abdomen extending into the chest before or during menses, or from suppressions of the menses ,or from suppressed foot sweats (Sil.). Convulsions before menses. Puerperal convulsions with open mouth and opisthotonos. After- pains. especially in women who had borne many children. Ebullition of blood, and palpitations. Chlorosis. Food - Desire for cold drinks, which ameliorate. Milk causes belching. Food tastes sweetish, or metallic, acid, or salt, watery. Desire for cold food in preference to hot.

Chest - Spasm and constriction of chest. Painful constriction of the chest (lower). Loud rattling in chest. Round balls moving to and fro under the ribs, better tight clothing and lying quiet. Constitutions - Suited to fair-haired people. Carbo-nitrogenoid constitution. Women who have borne many children (after-pains).

Heart - Palpitations, precordial anxiety and pain. Palpitations before menses. Fatty degeneration (Phos.). Angina pectoris with asthmatic symptoms and cramps. Slow pulse or hard, full and quick.

Back - Paralysis of all the muscles up to the neck. Sensation of heaviness in the axillary glands. Swelling of the glands of the neck. Hyperesthesia of spinal column. Backache top of sacrum. Causations - Ailments from emotions, anger, fright, suppressions, loss of sleep, mentally and bodily over- work. Chorea from fright. Getting wet causes epileptic attacks.

Limbs - Cramps in calves, soles, and palms. Jerking, twitching of muscles in hands and feet. Clonic spasms, beginning in fingers and toes. Clenching of thumbs in palms. Joints contracted. Great weariness of limbs. Knees double up involuntary when walking, bringing him down. Ankles painfully heavy. Ankylosis of shoulder joint. Coldness of hands. Epilepsy, aura begins in knees, feel as if broken.

Sleep - Lethargic sleep. Profound sleep, with shocks in the body and starting in the limbs. Constant rumbling in abdomen during sleep.

Skin - Bluish, marbled skin. Suppressed or undeveloped eruptions. Severe itching without eruptions. Chronic psoriasis. Ulcers, itching spots and pimples at the folds of joints. Yellow scaly eruptions (bend of elbow). Leprosy.

Modalities - Better during perspiration. Better drinking cold water. Better being mesmerized. Better laying hand on affected part. Better pressure over heart. Headache better wrapping head. Worse from emotions, anger, fright. Worse loss of sleep. Worse suppression. Worse bodily and mental over work. Worse from motion. Worse raising arms. Worse touch. Worse pressure. Worse before menses. Worse evening and night. Worse cold air, cold wind. Worse hot weather. Worse at new moon.

Liver - Cirrhosis of liver. Lungs - Dyspnea with epigastric uneasiness. Dyspnea, cannot bear anything near the mouth, worse coughing, laughing, bending backwards, before the menses. Hoarseness, worse breathing cold air. Cough in violent paroxysms, coughs herself out of breath, better cold drinks, worse deep breathing, bending backwards with cramps, lachrymation. Cough has a gurgling sound. Suffocative attacks, worse 3 a.m. (Am-c.). Trembling after coughing. Whooping cough, better swallowing water with vomiting, spasms and purple face. Asthma, hiccough before, alternating with spasmodic vomiting. Angina with asthmatic symptoms and cramps.

Kidneys - Suppression of urine in cholera, uremia. Urgent desire to urinate with scanty emission. Frequent emission of fetid, viscid urine. Passes clear, watery urine during or after spasms. B urning shootings in the urethra, during and subsequent to the emission of urine. Bedwetting.

Temperature - Chilly. Icy coldness of skin. Sweat, cold, clammy, at night, sour smelling after convulsions.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sulphate of Copper is a well-known emetic and caustic. It is a well- known application in allopathic practice for stimulating flabby granulations and it has cured itching eruptions and manifestations of syphilis. Pains better rest. Cupr-s. causes forcible vomiting and much nausea. Burning at vertex. Paleness of face or jaundiced appearance, pale skin generally. Tongue and lips bluish. Granular eyelids. Catarrhal and purulent conjuncti- vitis. Incessant, spasmodic cough, worse at night. Diarrhea. Enlarged liver. J. D. Tyrrell mentioned the case of a woman who could not use Cupr-s. for “stamping” fancy work because it “made her face hurt and swell so she could scarcely see and her lips became everted, turned inside out, she said.” RELATIONS - Antidotedby: Milk, eggs, pure yellow prussiate of potash. Compare: ( 1 ) Kali- bi. - cough and Merc. REFERENCES Clarke.

CLINICAL - Cancer. Catalepsy. Cirrhosis. Corns. Coughs. Debility. Diabetes. Dysmenorrhea. Dyspnea. Ear, disorders. Eczema. Emphysema. Epilepsy. Facial, paralysis. Faintness. Headache. Leprosy. Liver, spots. Locomotor, ataxia. Nervous, debility. Neuralgias. Otitis. Ozaena. Paralysis. Ptosis. Rabies. Reflexes, weak. Scrofula, disorders. Tetanus. Tuberculosis. Ulcerations. Uterus, disorders. Vaginitis. Whooping cough.

HOMEOPATHIC - An arrow poison used by South American Indians, Curare affects the muscles and brain. It is a muscular poison, causing paralysis of muscles without impairing the sensations and consciousness. Muscular paralysis without impairing any sensation or consciousness. It causes death by paralysis of the respiratory muscles. Reflex action is diminished or abolished. In many ways, its action is opposite that of Nux-v. Paralysis, facial, mouth, threatening respiration. Catalepsy. Trismus. Nervous debility. Sensation as if the brain were full of fluid. As of a heavy weight hung to the limbs. Weakness, heaviness, numbness, numbness with tingling. Piercing, sharp pains. Throbbing pains. Debility of the aged (Bar-c.) and from loss of fluids. Glycosuria with motor paralysis. Diabetes mellitus. Decreases the output of adrenalin. Vomiting of bile in cirrhosis of liver. Fetid discharges. Leprosy. Many symptoms appear on right side. MIND - Indecision, no longer wishes to think or act for herself. Inability to think or study, forgetful, stupid, sleepy, indolent. Excited, hurried feeling. Depressed, desire to be alone. Abdomen - Weary ache from throat to left hip. Neuralgic pain in hypogastrium with pressure in vagina. Pain in groin low down with heaviness in limbs while walking. Bowels feel sore and bruised.

Head - Head drawn backward. Rush of blood to head. Brain feels full of fluid. Head confused, great weight in vertex. Head beats like a hammer, with vomiting of bile. Nervous headache. Sharp pains all over head. Falling out of hair.

Eyes - Sharp, stitching pains over right eye. Ptosis of right side. Heavy eyes, lids can hardly be kept open. Eyes haggard, sunken. Feel as if full of sticks. Red, hot, sensitive to light. Black spots before vision, especially worse from reading.

Ears - Otitis interna, driving crazy. Noises, unbearable earache. Purulent discharge. Swelling of lobes of ear. Sharp pains start from ears, extending down to legs.

Nose - Nasal catarrh. Ozaena, fetid lumps of pus. Tubercles on nose.

Face - Facial and mouth paralysis. Paralysis of muscles of expression. Aching right side of face. Tongue and mouth drawn. Red face.

Mouth - Mouth dry. Tongue and mouth drawn to right. Tongue coated. On waking, tongue yellowish at base, papillae raised, light pink anteriorly, yellow-white, bitter or bloody taste.

Throat - Burning heat in throat with sensation of distention. Vertigo - Instant giddiness, falling in swoon while standing or walking. Dizzy when looking at near objects or at water. COMMENTS - Causes death by paralysis of the respiratory muscles. Reflex action is diminished or abolished (opp. Nux-v.). Catalepsy, immobility with fixed gaze on waking. Indicated by debility short of paralysis, the debility of the aged and nervous, and debility from the loss of fluids. Fetid odor of secretions and discharges. It favors the formation of corns. Its relation to hydrophobia and tetanus is probably antipathic. Used allopathically in tetanus treatments. A cure of a pseudo-hypertrophic paralysis by the 200c was recorded. Two cases of diabetes in middle-aged men have been cured by Burkhardt with Cur. 4c. Diabetes mellitus. Grimmer noted that it is useful for cancer with weakness and a tendency to faint, extreme debility, difficult breathing, vertigo with fainting. States of catalepsy, worse by exercise, walking, etc., worse in dampness. Cold air, cold weather, worse 2 a.m. and 2 p.m. to 3 p.m. RELATIONS - Antidote to: Strychnia and to the poison of rabies. In cases of poisoning artificial respiration must be resorted to. Bromine and Chlorine antidote its effects. If the poisoning is due to a punctured wound, rubbing in tobacco or salt will neutralize it. Compare: (1) Cystisin - motor paralysis. (2) Con., Caust., Crot-h., Nux-v. (3) Aran. - fever worse in damp weather. (4) Ferr. - hammering pains in head. (5) Crot-h. - blows in region of cerebellum. (6) In yellow-brown spots on skin, Sep., Lyc., Nux-v., Sulph. Compatible: After Arn. (paralysis from injury) after Bell, (paralysis after nosebleed). Follows well: in debility of the aged: Bar-c. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Empty, gone feeling in stomach. Sharp pain in pit of stomach, followed by nausea. Shooting in stomach. Heartburn, pain and distention after eating ever so little. Chill after eating. Nausea in morning after eating. Vomits green bile all night. Frequent and annoying hiccoughs.

Rectum - Extreme watery diarrhea. Diarrhea with constant urging, fetid, thin mush-like feces. Excessive pain in hemorrhoids.

Female - Menses too early. During menses, colic, headache and kidney pain. Dysmenorrhea. Leucorrhea, thick, purulent offensive, in clots. Bearing-down, dragging, tired, in all pelvic organs. Vaginitis. Griping in right ovary. Ulcerations of os uteri, scirrhus. Aversion to sex. Food - Thirst and great hunger with fever. Sudden hunger almost to faintness. Better after first mouthful of food. Aversion to bread. Great thirst especially evening and night. Craves acids.

Chest - Sore to pressure or touch. Constitutions - Suited to scrofulous children, producing scrofulous eruptions on skin, eczema, especially of face and behind ears, and yellow brown liver-spots.

Heart - Precordial pain, anguish with palpitations and stinging pains in heart.

Back - Tired pain up and down spine. Stiffness in neck, head drawn back. Stiffness of muscles or right neck and shoulder. Dull, tired ache in shoulders and across back, numb. Chills running up back and all over body.

Limbs - Paralysis of limbs, burning with heat and chills. Aching in all the limbs and body. Numbness and tingling. Debility, paralysis. Catalepsy. Reflexes lessened or abolished. Arms weak, heavy. Cannot lift the fingers. Weakness of hands and fingers in pianists. Legs tremble, give way in walking. Favors development of corns. Lungs - Severe pains in lungs, especially left. Shortness of breath. Threatened paralysis of the respiration on falling asleep. Very distressing dyspnea. Dyspnea, stitching pains right side. Dyspnea, worse ascending. Short, dry, hacking cough, provokes vomiting, followed by fainting. Dry cough with soreness of chest walls. Cough, worse breathing cold air, laughing, moving, eating. Cough troublesome in morning.

Sleep - Drowsy, cannot keep awake. Nights restless, always desiring to put feet out of bed, especially towards morning.

Skin - Leprosy. Dirty-looking skin. Itching, with hunger. Eczema. Liver-spots. Boils. Tubercles on nose. Blood oozes through.

Modalities - Worse from motion. Worse walking. Worse ascending, 2 a.m. and 2 p.m. to 3 p.m. Worse from dampness. Worse cold weather, cold wind. Worse change of weather.

Kidneys - Digging, crampy pain in kidneys, dry mouth, great thirst. Urine copious, urgent, bladder feels distended. Clear and frequent urine. Sugar in urine, great emaciation (acute diabetes).

Temperature - Chill, creeping up back without thirst. Body blue, and yet fever. Heat worse at night and in open air. Sweat with every exertion. Sweat, cold and bloody, especially at nights.

PHARMACY - cure. Curcuma longa. Turmeric. Curcuma rotunda. Southern Asia. N. 0. Zingiberaceae. Rhizome. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Atherosclerosis. Cancer. Gastritis. Indigestion. Liver, problems. Osteoarthritis. Parasites. Skin, diseases. Stomach, disorders. Uveitis. Worms. Wounds.

HERBAL - Turmeric (Curcuma longa), a flowering plant in the ginger family, is widely used as a food coloring and is one of the principal ingredients in curry powder. Turmeric is fragrant and has a bitter, somewhat sharp taste. The aboveground and underground roots, or rhizomes, are used in medicinal and food preparations. These are generally boiled and then dried, turning into the familiar yellow powder. Curcumin from turmeric, as well as other substances in this herb, have antioxidant properties. Turmeric has long been used in both Ayurvedic and Chinese medicine as an antiinflammatory, to treat digestive disorders and liver problems, and for the treatment of skin diseases and wound healing. Curcumin has been shown, to stimulate the production of bile and to facilitate the emptying of the gallbladder. It has also demonstrated a protective effect on the liver, anti-tumor action, and ability to reduce inflammation and fight certain infections. Turmeric is for a variety of digestive disorders. Curcumin, for example, one of the active ingredients in turmeric, induces the flow of bile, which helps break down fats. Stomach upset, gas, abdominal cramps. Extracts of turmeric root can reduced secretion of acid from the stomach and protected against injuries such as inflammation along the stomach (gastritis) or intestinal walls and ulcers from certain medications, stress, or alcohol. Because of its ability to reduce inflammation, turmeric may help relieve the symptoms of osteoarthritis. Early studies suggest that turmeric may prove helpful in preventing the build up of atherosclerosis (blockage of arteries that can eventually cause a heart attack or stroke) in one of two ways. Turmeric may also prevent platelet build up along the walls of an injured blood vessel. Platelets collecting at the site of a damaged blood vessel cause blood clots to form and blockage of the artery as well. Curcumin has potential in the treatment of various forms of cancer, including prostate, breast, skin, and colon. Roundworms and Intestinal worms. Turmeric, may reduce the destructive activity of parasites or roundworms. Turmeric's volatile oil functions as an external antibiotic, preventing bacterial infection in wounds. Turmeric applied to wounds hastens the healing process. Inflammation of the uvea, and the retina. The uvea contains many of the blood vessels that nourish the eye. Inflammation of this area, therefore, can affect the cornea, the retina, the sclera, and other important parts of the eye. REFERENCES - Potter.

name: Cyclamen Europaeum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from moistening diseased parts, bathing. Better rubbing parts. Better moving about, walking. Better warm room. Better during menstrual flow. Better weeping. Better lemonade. Worse cold, cold water. Worse open air. Worse night, evenings. Worse eating at night. Worse standing. Worse sitting, rest. Worse fats. Menstrual flow worse sitting. Worse drawing shoulders forward or backward..

full:
PHARMACY - cycl. Cyclamen europaeum. Sow-bread. N. O. Primulacae. Tincture of the root gathered in spring. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anemia. Bone, pain. Chlorosis. Coryza. Diplopia. Dyspepsia. Enteralgia. Eye, disorders. Headaches. Heel. pain. Hiccoughs. Menstruation, disorders. Menopause. Pregnancy. Prostatitis. Rheumatism. Sleepiness. Strabismus. Thirstless. Urethritis. Vertigo. Weaning, complaints. Writer's spasm.

HOMEOPATHIC - Cyclamen has a traditional reputation as a remedy for disorders of the uterus and appendages. Later provings affirmed this reputation. Large doses produce violent purging and vomiting, disturbed digestion with very salty saliva. Cycl. is in many ways similar to Puls., from which it differs mainly in having no relief from open air and in hot having thirstless- ness as so frequent an accompaniment of other conditions. Anemic and chlorotic conditions. Affections of uterus. Gastro-intestinal and genitourinary tracts affected inducing secondary anemia and various reflexes. Cough, at night while asleep without waking, especially in children (Cham., Nit-ac.). Sleepiness, morose and lassitude. MIND - Dull, sleepy and morose. Depression, with weeping desire to be alone. Silent weeping. Grieves, sadness as if he had committed a bad act or not done his duty. Self-reproaches. Terrors of conscience. Tearful and broods over imaginary grief. Ajoyous feeling alternating with irritability. Hallucinations as if two persons were lying in her bed. The room seems too small. Thinks she is alone and persecuted.

Head - Prolonged migraine. One-sided headache. Headaches in morning with flickering before eyes, better cold water. Pain in left temple. Brain as if wrapped up in a cloth. As if brain wobbled about while walking, menses absent or scanty. Frequent sneezing with itching in ears.

Eyes - Disturbance of vision, associated with gastric disturbances. Dim vision with headache, worse on waking with spots before eyes. Diplopia. Flickering of various colors. Hemiopia. Sees countless stars. Fluttering, glittering orblack spots. Squint, especially connected with menstrual irregularities. Convergent squint after convulsions, left eye drawn inwards. Face - Pale, anemic. Upper lip, as if numb or indurated.

Ears - Itching in the ears with increased wax. Drawing in the ears. Diminution of hearing, as if the ears were stopped.

Nose - Fluent coryza, with sneezing. Sneezing with itching in the ear. Loss of smell.

Mouth - Taste lost or salty, which is communicated to all food. Saliva salty. Tongue loaded with a white coating. Fine stitches on the surface of the tongue. Burning on the tip of the tongue. Dryness of the lips, without thirst.

Stomach - Satiety after a few mouthfuls, loathing and nausea from the least food afterwards. Nausea felt in throat. Salty taste, hiccough-like eructation, worse fat food. Hiccough, worse pregnancy, with yawning. Vomiting of pregnancy.

Abdomen - Fullness and pressure. Uneasiness in the abdomen with nausea. Painful on the slightest touch. Sudden attacks of griping, with pinching. Borborygmi in the abdomen, immediately after a meal. Running in bowels as if something alive.

Rectum - Drawing pressure in the anus. Pain about anus and perineum, as if a spot were suppurating, when walking or sitting. Pressure in the rectum. Discharge of blood from the rectum. Evacuations hard and frequent. Diarrhea after every cup of coffee.

Male - Prepuce and corona glandis feel sore after slight rubbing. Stitches and pressure in prostate with urging to stool and urination.

Female - Menses changeable, profuse, black, membranous, clotted too early, with labor-like pains from back to pubes. The flow is less when moving about. Dysmenorrhea. Menstrual irregularities with megrim and blindness or fiery spots before eyes. Suppression of menses after excessive dancing or being over heated. Leucorrhea with retarded or scanty menses. Hiccough during pregnancy. Post-partum hemorrhage with colicky bearing-down pains with relief after gush of blood. Food - Desire for lemonade, sardines, inedible things. Aversion to bread, butter, fat, beer. Disgust for meat, especially pork. Loss of appetite after taking beef tea or a cup of tea. No thirst all day.

Heart - Pressure on the heart, as from congestion of blood. Sensible palpitations of the heart, stitches in the region of the heart. Frequent palpitations from suppressed menses.

Back - Excoriation in the nape of the neck. Aching, with paralytic weakness, or traction in the nape of the neck and in the neck. Dull stitches in the region of the kidney, worse when drawing a long breath. Breasts - Air seems to stream from the nipples. Milk in virgin breast or nonpregnant women. Swelling of breast with milky secretion after menses. Causations - Ill effects of inward grief and terror of conscience. Constitutions - Suited to the blonde leuco-phlegmatic subjects with chlorotic conditions, disinclined for labor and easily fatigued. Special senses enfeebled or their functions suspended.

Limbs - Pains in parts where bones lie near the surface. Pains in periosteum. Shooting pains in the loins. Weakness of knees. Burning, sore heels, better walking, worse sitting, standing. Chilblains. Cramp-like slow contractions of the right thumb and index finger, they have to be extended by force. Writer's spasms. Lungs - Scraping and dryness in the pharynx, causing a suffocative cough. Coughing without waking.

Sleep - Great inclination to lie down, and to sleep. Nightmares when falling to sleep. Unrefreshing sleep, with terrible, frightful, lascivious dreams.

Skin - Gnawing itching in several parts of the skin. Itching, in the evening in bed. Acne in young women. Pruritus better scratching and appearance of menses, worse at night in bed.

Modalities - Better from moistening diseased parts, bathing. Better rubbing parts. Better moving about, walking. Better warm room. Better during menstrual flow. Better weeping. Better lemonade. Worse cold, cold water. Worse open air. Worse night, evenings. Worse eating at night. Worse standing. Worse sitting, rest. Worse fats. Menstrual flow worse sitting. Worse drawing shoulders forward or backward.

Kidneys - Frequent desire to urinate with abundant emission of whitish urine. Shootings in the urethra, followed by a sudden discharge of a dark red urine. Urine profuse, watery and frequent.

Temperature - Attacks of chilliness in the morning or evening. During the evening, chill and great sensitiveness to cold air or to being uncovered. Chilly all over, not better by covers. Febrile shivering and cold, followed by heat. Offensive sweat. Throat - When reading aloud the voice is weak. The tonsils and palate are shriveled and white. Dryness in the throat. Burning and scraping in throat. Sensation of painful constriction in the throat. Nausea in throat. Vertigo - Vertigo, objects turn in circles or look pale, worse open air, better in a room and sitting. COMMENTS - Debility, torpidity of mind and body. Dullness of senses. Flickering before the eyes, squint, especially in connection with menstrual irregularities or fevers. After convulsions, convergent squint, lefteye drawn inwards. Amblyopia, diplopia, hemiopia. Digestive disturbances. Saliva has a salty taste, which is communicated to all food eaten. After eating but little, satiety, aversion to food with nausea in palate and thirst. Aversion to bread, butter, meat, fat, beer and ordinary food. Craving for lemonade, sardines, inedible things. Frequent vomiting in morning. Prostatic troubles with stitches and pressure, urging to stool and urination. Menstruation too early, with some relief of melancholy mood and heaviness of feet. Scanty or suppressed menstruation with headache and vertigo. During pregnancy, hiccough, loathing and nausea in mouth and throat, complaints after weaning. Pressing, drawing or tearing pains at parts where bones lie near surface. Chilliness. Itching leaving a numb sensation. Chilblains, itching and pricking, worse at night in bed. Eidherr of Vienna gave the best account of this remedy. He noted the more copious menstruation, more frequent, tooearly, with severe abdominal pains. Accompanied with labor-like pains, flow is excessive, black and lumpy. Commencement of menses after protracted cessation. Eidherr's clinical experience illustrates in a remarkable way Cycl.'s sphere of action. In one i nstance a higher potency of the same remedy antidoted this effect. He found the remedy especially suited to blonde leuco- phlegmatic subjects. The “Sleepiness, morose and lassitude.” and also the vertigo noted by Hahnemann, are prominent in many of Eidherr's cases. J. K., 24, blonde, pale delicate skin, pale lips and gums, had menstruated normally until 22, when she got wet at a picnic just as menstruation was starting. It stopped at once and did not reappear until ten months later after vigorous use of all kinds of domestic remedies. The periods were then accompanied by terrible abdominal, labor-like pains, lasting eleven hours. Menses recurred every two or four months, always with the pains, starting from sacrum, extending along both sides of abdomen to pelvis. They were periodical, every one, two or five minutes during which time there was no flow, the blood appearing after these attacks was somewhat watery. Other symptoms included slightly edematous eyelids, pressing pain in the forehead and vertigo frequently changing into syncope. Chilliness of the whole body. Disturbed, unrefreshing sleep interspersed with terrible dreams. Continued loathing for meat. Longing for salt fish. Frequent vomiting in morning. After partial relief from Puls., Cycl. made a complete cure. The ocular symptoms which developed were remarkable. The vertigo and headache were untouched by Puls., but quickly subsided under Cycl. 15x. On their disappearance she saw fiery flames dancing before her eyes, on awakening at night and in the morning she saw everything double. And she had the hallucination as if two persons lay in her bed and that the body of the other overlapped hers by half. Cycl. was discontinued and in two days her sight was normal. Anna F., 20, blonde, menstruated since her tenth year. In her seventeenth year she suffered from chlorosis, ever since, menstruation was regular, but lasting only one or two days in a moderate degree. Troubled at other times by vertigo and pressing pain in forehead and temples, which attacks were ameliorated by foot baths with ashes. Appetite poor, little thirst, stool regular, sleeps too long, always sleepy, dejected mood, morose. All movements, as well as speech, were languid, palpitation. Puls, made no change, Cycl. 3x quickly improved the headache, vertigo and spirits. After three days, sight became obscured and there was glimmering before eyes. A case of hemicrania was cured with Cycl. Theresa F., 37., had menstruated sparingly and irregularly (often at two or three months' intervals). For four years suffered from violent headache affecting right side of head and face, coming every 8-14 days, spells lasting 12-36 hours. During menstruation, the attacks were extra severe. Patient was emaciated, skin, gums and lips pale. Right eye closed owing to cramps in eyelids. When forcibly opened, a stream of hot tears gushed out, otherwise the eye was normal. Under Cycl. 3c the symptoms diminished, but there appeared “glittering sparks before the eyes” and these remained after all symptoms of headache had gone. Cycl. was given persistently, the periods became regular and rather copious, and the headaches entirely ceased. Another case (in a wet-nurse who had just weaned her baby) presented unceasing, violent, stitching pain in temporal region extending to vertex. Throbbing temporal arteries. Bell, diminished the pain, but vertigo came on. Under Cycl. 3x, the headache and vertigo disappeared altogether, but the patient complained of her sight having become so weak that she did not dare to walk alone. This passed off when the medicine was discon- tinued and her headache did not recur. Cycl. cured aboy of violent squinting. Six months before, he had a fall from a table, convulsion followed and after the second attack the squinting came on. Am. was given and the convulsions did not recur, but the squinting remained. Cycl. 15x was given and after a few weeks the squint entirely disappeared. Wurmb cured a case of squint in a coachman with Cycl. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Coff., Puls. The modalities of Cycl. are in general opposite to those of Puls., the menstrual flow of Cycl. is more profuse while at rest with Puls, the opposite is the case. Compare: (1) Puls., Ign., Ambr. (2) Ferr. and Chin, resemble it in chlorosis. (3) Crocus and Thuj. in sensation of something alive in abdomen. (4) Am-m. - menses worse at night. (5) Iris-v. and Kali-bi. (migraine with scintillations, headache worse as sight returns, Kali-bi. (6) Coc-c. - leucorrhea worse sitting better walking, Cycl. menses worse sitting better walking. (7)Rhus-t. (enter- algia). Gels, and Seneg. (diplopia), Am. (falls), Bar-c., Calc., Canth. (chilly and fever), Cocc. (8) In speedy satiety. Lyc., Nux-v., Sep. (9) In prostatitis and urethritis, Lith-c., Dig., Sei., Caust., Lyc., Apisin squint. Alum., sudden vanishing of sight with menses, Sep., Puls. (Puls, scanty, Cycl. profuse and dark). ( 10) nausea in throat, Sep. Berb.. pain in heels on standing. Desire for lemonade. Bell., Sabin. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

full:
PHARMACY - cyn-d. Cynodon dactylon. Doorba. Grantha doorba bhargavi. N. O. Graminaceae. A grass from India. Tincture of the whole fresh plant Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Anasarca. Cholera. Conjunctivitis. Diarrhea, summer. Dysentery. Flatulence. Headaches. Hematuria. Scabies. Ulcerative, colitis.

HERBAL - The Cynodon dactylon grows throughout India, and is used in some of the religious ceremonies of the country. Popularly known as doorba, the Sanskrit name for this plant is grantha doorba bhargavi. It is an elegant perennial plant that flowers throughout the whole year. The freshly extracted juice of the grass is useful for hematuria, vomiting and as an application for conjunctivitis. A decoction of the plant is used as a diuretic and can be useful for dropsy and anasarca. Chakradatta mentioned it as being an excellent remedy for scabies and amenorrhea.

HOMEOPATHIC - Jugal Kishore carried out a homeopathic proving on three provers, two men and one woman. The potencies used were the mother tincture, 6x and 200c. The stock of Cyn-d. was supplied by the Hahnemann Publishing Co. of Calcutta. General weakness, more marked in the hands, with difficulty in writing. General lassitude, laziness, aversion to work. The least physical effort causes pain all over. Mental work causes frontal headaches. Aversion to noise, but desires jolly company. Elective action on the gastro-intestinal passages and urinary system. Flatulence and abdominal cramps. Stools irritating with acrid odor and noisy expulsion. Urgent need to stool. Urethral pain after urination. Pain in the upper or lower limbs, ameliorated by a tight bandage or by walking. Heat in the soles of the feet with the need to take the feet out from beneath the covers. MIND - Irritable, quarrelsome, flies into a rage. Angry without cause. Aversion to noise and does not want to be spoken to. Desire jolly company.

Head - Forehead hot and heavy. Pain on the right side of the head and in very localized areas of the body. Headache after mental exertion or anger.

Eyes - Conjunctivitis. Conjunctiva are painfully sensitive. Swelling of the upper right eyelid, worse in the morning. Eyelids stuck together in the morning. Pain in the eyes in morning after a bath or washing the face. Food - Loss of appetite, which returns on eating.

Mouth - Increased salivation with insipid taste. Loss of sense of taste. Dryness of the palate, cannot take sour or spicy food, better by taking something cold. Red patch on the palate and small red granules in the pharynx.

Stomach - Sensation of heaviness in the stomach after lunch.

Abdomen - Flatulence and abdominal distention after 4 p.m. Cramping abdominal pains, with an urge to go to stool. Pain in the right hypochondrium, which disappears after resting. Heaviness around the umbilicus. Impression of a ball below and around the umbilicus.

Rectum - Urgent need to go to stool when rising with a feeling of colic. Urgent need to go to stool continues during the day. Stools hard, difficult to evacuate. Stools semi-solid, then soft with irritating mucus. Stools, irritating, yellow and soft. Offensive, acrid stools with noisy expulsion. Much gas passed with stools.

Limbs - Sudden, shooting pain in the back of the left forearm Feeling of great weakness in the forearms and hands. Aggravation from typewriting. Pain in the upper part of the body, especially in the back. Pain and restlessness in the legs when lying down at night, better by rising from the bed or by tight bandaging. Sensation of heat in the soles of the feet, desire to put the feet outside the covers.

Sleep - Sleepiness after meals. Heavy sleep. Sleep disturbed by pains in the legs.

Modalities - Better from heat, eating. Worse in the afternoon, evening. Worse from physical or mental exertion. Worse predominantly on the right side.

Kidneys - Involuntary urination while sneezing. Frequent and copious urination. Urethral pain after urination with feeling of not having finished.

Temperature - Feverish, needs to cover himself. Sensation of heat in tips of toes. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Podo. - Diarrhea in the morning, fetid stools, expelled in a rush, tenesmus general weakness, rumbling and feeling of emptiness in the abdomen. (2) Verat. - Copious diarrhea, abdominal colic, extreme weakness with cold sweating. (3) Aloe - Abdominal distention, hot stomach, heavy with expulsion of burning irritating gases. Diarrhea after resting, urgent need to go to stool. Involuntary passing of stools when urinating or when expelling wind. REFERENCES - Julian.

constitution: Brain, disorders. Chorea. Con- vulsions. Debility. Delirium, tremens. Ecstasy. Epilepsy. Insomnia. Mental, despondency. Nervous, debility. Nervousness. Neuralgias. Post-influenzal, debility. Rhus, poisoning. Sleeplessness. Spermatorrhea. Styes.

full:
PHARMACY - cypr. Cypripedium pubescens. Yellow lady's slipper. N. O. Orchidaceae. Tincture and infusions of fresh root gathered in autumn. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Brain, disorders. Chorea. Con- vulsions. Debility. Delirium, tremens. Ecstasy. Epilepsy. Insomnia. Mental, despondency. Nervous, debility. Nervousness. Neuralgias. Post-influenzal, debility. Rhus, poisoning. Sleeplessness. Spermatorrhea. Styes.

HERBAL - Lady’s slipper has great repute as a “nervine” among eclectics and in domestic practice. It ranks with Scut, and Valer. Hale noted a strong infusion causes exhilaration followed by calmness and is much resorted to by women whose nerves are shattered by long illness or excessive indulgence in greentea or coffee.

HOMEOPATHIC - Indicated in the brainhyperesthesia of children who wake in the night lively and full of play. Epilepsy from reflex irritation. Trembling and twitching of limbs. Nervousness in children from teething and intestinal troubles. Debility after gout. The skin symptoms correspond to those of Rhus-t. poisoning, for which it has been found an efficient antidote. MIND - Sleeplessness and agitation. Irascibility. Throws emotional fits. Hysterical symptoms. Ecstasy, preliminary to incipient brain disorder. Indifference. Constitutions - Suited to nervous disorders from mental over-excitement or reflex nervous excitement. Nervous weakness after influenza.

Head - Child cries out at night, is wakeful and begins to laugh and play. Brain hypersensitivity in young children often the result of over stimulation of brain. Hydrocephaloid symptoms, result of long, exhausting diarrhea, sleeplessness. Headaches of elderly people and during menopausal.

Eyes - Stye on right lower lid.

Male - Spermatorrhea with great nervous prostration and dejection of spirits.

Female - Amenorrhea with hysteria. Great nervous debility and despondency. Irritable vagina, hysterical symptoms, sleeplessness and agitation.

Sleep - Sleeplessness with desire to talk. A constant crowding of pleasant ideas with restlessness of body. Ecstasy, children awaken in night from sleep “wide-awake,” unnaturally playful, with no desire to go to sleep again. Vertigo - Vertigo followed by heaviness and dragging of left foot. RELATIONS - Antidote to: Rhus poisoning. Compare: (1) Aven., Kali-br., Scut., Valer., Ign. (2) Skin relations: Grind., Anae. (3) Ambra. Coca, Guar., Thea, Zinc. (4) In ecstasy, Coffea. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - cyt-1. Cystisus laburnum. Laburnum anagyroides. Cystisus aubour. N. O. Leguminose. Tincture or trituration of seeds. Tincture of fresh bark. The tincture is prepared from the essences ofthe flowers and young leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abdominal typhus. Angina, pectoris. Convulsions. Cramps. Cyanosis. Diarrhea. Dyspepsia. Eyes, disorders. Heart, anomalies. Heat-stroke. Hydrocephalus. Hypertension. Influenza. Meningitis. Migraines. Morning sickness. Motion sickness. Nausea. Raynaud's disease. Spasms. Sunstroke. Thyroid disorders. Typhoid. Vertigo. Vomiting, pregnancy. Writer's cramp.

HOMEOPATHIC - The proving was done by Joseph Schier in 1900-1901 on sixteen pro vers using the low potencies and the mother tincture. J. Mezger made a clinical re-proving with it. Cystisus Laburnum, or wild laburnum, is a member of the leguminosae family. Cystisus Aubour is a shrub or small tree, growing naturally or cultivated as an ornamental plant with trifoliate leaves. It has pale, yellow flowers which hang in clusters with long pods and which are hairy when yellow. All parts of this well-known ornamental tree are poisonous, especially the flowers and seeds, owing to the presence of cytisin. This oxygenated, unsaturated alkaloid is toxic to the glands, which it first arouses and then paralyzes. It causes convulsions and can lead to death by asphyxia. The toxicity of cytisin is allied to that of nicotine. Knowledge of it is derived chiefly from the accidental poisoning of children who have eaten the pea-like seeds and pods. A typical case can be seen in that of W. G., et. 10, who ate eight to ten seeds. Five or ten minutes later, began to sweat, but soon became cold and shivering, skin pale, pulse scarcely perceptible, general collapse. Pupils dilated. Drowsy and giddy, without pain. Emetics and brandy were given, but after an hour of this there was no improvement. An enema of hot, strong coffee was then given, the patient was wrapped in blankets and hot bottles applied. The collapse then gradually passed off. Cyt-1. acts on the central and sympathetic nervous system causing cramping spasmodic conditions. Hyperesthesia of the peripheral nerves. Cerebral shock. Epidemic cerebral and spinal meningitis. Migraine. Nausea, pallor, cold sweating. Vertigo. Face pale. Dryness of the mouth tongue and throat. Sunstroke. Heatstroke. Travel sickness (air, sea and car). MIND - Intense uneasiness, anguish. Depressive and irritable condition. Maniacal depressive conditions. Oppression. Insomnia. Sleepiness to the point of being in a stupor. Comatose condition.

Head - Neuralgic pains in the head of a migraine type. Pulsating headaches. Pressing frontal pain. Pricking pain in the left temple.

Eyes - Pupils dilated.

Nose - Nosebleeds.

Mouth - Dryness of mouth, tongue and back of throat. Burning, mouth and pharynx.

Throat - Feeling of constriction in the throat. Tickling sensation in the throat with the need to clear it. Vertigo - Vertigo and absent feeling. Constant vertigo, even while lying, if she attempted to sit upright, she immediately fell back again. COMMENTS - In one case of poisoning by Cyt-1., the head was hot and rigidly thrown back. Muscular twitchings about the face. Convulsions, insensibility, drowsiness and mental indifference. Two boys who were poisoned by the root of an old tree had very strange waving motions of the arms and convulsive drawing up of the legs, first one leg then the other. Pupils equally dilated. A boy who ate the green twigs of Cyt-1. was seized with vomiting, pain in the stomach and collapse, there was no diarrhea but tenesmus and erections. After a few hours he passed 300 grams of grass-green urine, after which he felt better. Soon after passing, the urine assumed a natural color. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Coffee and stimulants, hot and cold douches to chest. Compare: (1) Nux-v. (2) Gels. - better by copious urination. (3) Tab. - Prostration, nausea, vomiting, general coldness and cold sweating, vertigo and pallor. (4) Verat. - State of discomfort, collapse, coldness of the limbs, cyanosis, prostration, vomiting, cold sweating and tiring diarrhea. (5) Bapt. - Intense nervous depression, extreme agitation, impression that the body is double, sensation of breaking in the bones, putrid breath, fetid diarrhea. REFERENCES - Clarke. Julian.

Stomach - Gastric heaviness, burning pains in the stomach. Acrid dyspepsia. Nausea with vertigo and vomiting.

Abdomen - Chronic gastro-duodenitis. Spasmodic colon afflictions. Mesenteric irritation.

Rectum - Diarrhea with painful abdominal colic, intestinal rumbling and anal tenesmus. Cholera-type diarrhea.

Male - Strong erections.

Female - Dysmenorrhea. Menopausal complaints. Copious leucorrhea.

Chest - Angina pectoris. Feeling of tightness in the chest.

Heart - Hypertensive attack with state of collapse, pale, livid face and cold sweating. Palpitations with accelerated pulse. Arterial pulsation in all limbs. Rhythmic anomalies. Raynaud's disease.

Back - Muscular cramps. Drawing pains starting at the nape of the neck, spreading towards the occiput.

Limbs - Weakness and numbness of the limbs. Sensation of breaking in all the limbs. Stiffness and drawing pains in the limbs. Muscular cramps. Lungs - Respiration rapid at first, then slower and difficult. Wheezing respiration. Whooping cough.

Sleep - Insomnia with delirium. Worrying dreams.

Skin - Skin cold, cold sweating. Cyanosis. Pruritus. Vésicules around the cheek.

Modalities - Better after passing wind, after going to stool. Worse from the cold. Worse in the afternoon, evening. Worse predominantly on the left side.

Temperature - Discomfort, accompanied by a feeling of coldness.

name: Damiana Aphrodisiaca
author: Murphy
constitution: Amenorrhea. Chronic, fatigue. Dysmenorrhea. Gonorrhea. Headaches. Infertility. Impotence. Incontinence. Leucorrhea. Migraines. Prostate, disorders. Sexual, weakness. Spinal, injury. Spermatorrhea. Syphilis. Urinary, disorders.
keynote:
PHARMACY - dam. Damiana aphrodisiaca. Tumeraaphrodisiaca. N. O. Turneraceae. Tincture of fresh plant. Tincture of dried leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Chronic, fatigue. Dysmenorrhea. Gonorrhea. Headaches. Infertility. Impotence.…
full:
PHARMACY - dam. Damiana aphrodisiaca. Tumeraaphrodisiaca. N. O. Turneraceae. Tincture of fresh plant. Tincture of dried leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Chronic, fatigue. Dysmenorrhea. Gonorrhea. Headaches. Infertility. Impotence. Incontinence. Leucorrhea. Migraines. Prostate, disorders. Sexual, weakness. Spinal, injury. Spermatorrhea. Syphilis. Urinary, disorders.

HERBAL - Damiana is the local name of the herb Tumera aphrodisiaca. It has long been a domestic medicine in Mexico, where it is used to “invigorate the system.” Indians discovered that a decoction of it was a great invigorator after wearisome journeys and dispels fatigue. They also found in it a remedy for the inability to exercise the reproductive functions in both sexes.

Head - Headaches, migraines.

Male - Prostate disorders. Spermatorrhea. Gonorrhea. Syphilis. Impotence. Sexual weakness. COMMENTS - Hale collected a great deal of experience concerning this remedy from old-school sources, showing its power over the genito-urinary system. Douglass reported three cases of incontinence of urine, including the case of a man, age 63, who had dribbling of urine day and night for four years. He was given Dam. 2x in water, four times a day, and was cured in two months. History of curing cases of severe migraines. One or two doses given within an hour would cause the headache to cease and induced sleep, from which the patient woke free from headache and with good appetite. Spinal injury from a fall. Sexual excess. Syphilis or gonorrhea. Amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea and leucorrhea. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Impotence, injuries, over-exertion, fatigue, Bell-p., Arn., Agn. (2) Prostatic affections, Sabal., Solid. (3) Migraines, Bry., Epipheg. REFERENCES - Clarke. Murphy.

Female - Dysmenorrhea. Amenorrhea. Leucorrhea. Sexual weakness. Infertility.

Back - Spinal injury.

Bladder - Urinary disorders. Incontinence.
