CLINICAL - Aneurysm. Aortitis. Asthma. Bladder, disorders. Bronchitis. Cachexia. Coryza. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Dyspepsia. Dysuria. Fistulae. Gonorrhea. Gout. Influenza Intermittent, fever. Kidney, disease. Migraines. Nephritis. Ophthalmia. Quinine, cachexia. Rheumatism. Spleen, affection. Strychnine, poisoning. Syphilis. Toxemia. Tumors. Typhoid. Urethra, stricture. Urethral, caruncle. Varicose, ulcers. Worms.

HERBAL - Eucalyptus, the gum-tree, is a native of Australia. It was transplanted to marshy districts in mild climates on account of its capability of absorbing water and its alleged power of destroying malarial poisons. Eucal. became well-known during the influenza epidemic as a prophylactic and disinfectant. Eucalyptus is a powerful antiseptic and disinfectant. Merrel noted that the volatile oil possesses in common with other terpenes, the property of converting water in the presence of air and sunlight into hydrogen peroxide or to convert oxygen into ozone. Used locally in catarrhal affections, especially when of a suppurating or putrid nature. Enlarged, ulcerated tonsils and inflamed throat. Use the tincture locally as a gargle.

HOMEOPATHIC - Eucal. affects the mucus membranes, producing profuse acrid and foul catarrhal discharges, with aching, stiffness and weariness, as from taking cold. Marked effects on catarrhal processes, malaria and intestinal disturbances. Relapsing or intermittent fevers. Typhoid fever. Malaria. Useful in convalescence from intermittents. Odorous sweat. Influenza (Gels.), said to be a preventive for influenza. Coryza, headache of a dull, congestive character, sore throat. Hemorrhages internally and locally (Ham.). Exhausted with toxemia and hemorrhage. Sticking, jerking pains at night. Remarkable bodily exhaustion, no desire for any motion, unable to do any real mental work, study, etc. Rheumatism. Atonic dyspepsia, gastric and intestinal catarrh. Indigestion with excessive development of fetid gas and fever. Slow digestion. A gastro-intestinal irritant with pain in stomach and upper intestines several hours after eating. Diuresis and increase of urea. MIND- Mental exhilaration. Exhilaration with feeling of buoyancy and increased strength. Desire for exercise, to move about. Intoxication followed by mental depression and exhaustion. Dull and drowsy.

Head - Cerebral congestion with much excitement. Dull and congestive headache. Migraine. Sick headache. Nervous headache, and other pains in head, not exactly periodical. Headache in anemic persons. Eucal. relieves the pain and causes sleep.

Eyes - Eyes hot, burning, smarting. Eyes smart and burn. Catarrhal ophthalmia. Eyelids heavy. Gonorrheal ophthalmia. Dim vision.

Ears - Tinnitus. Ringing in ears.

Nose - Coryza, sore throat. Stuffed-up sensation . Thin, watery coryza, nose does not stop running. Chronic catarrhal, purulent and fetid discharge. Ethmoid and frontal sinus involved. Tension across the nose, tightness across the bridge.

Face - Flushed, congested face.

Mouth - Aphthae. Mouth burns. Mouth feels full. Relaxed aphthous condition. Excessive secretion of saliva. Slightly burning taste extending into throat and esophagus with thirst. Tongue pasty.

Throat - Aphthous condition of throat with burning. Burns, feels full. Excessive secretions of saliva. Constant sensation of phlegm in throat. Enlarged, ulcerated tonsils and inflamed throat. Vertigo - Vertigo during all stages of intermittent fever. COMMENTS - Vascular conditions including a distinct beating in stomach region, accompanying a sense of emptiness, one prover referred this to the abdominal aorta. V ascular tumors of the female urethra. Glandular enlargements and nodular swellings over joints. Marked periodicity. Most pains occur at night. It has an intoxicating effect and produces adesire forexercise. Discharges show a tendency to foulness, high temperature, accelerated but not strong pulse. Largely used for bronchitis and bronchial asthma. It cured a tumor, the size of a filbert with stabbing pains below left nipple. C. E. Fischer cured many case of dysentery with it. Dr. Arthur Dalzell related two striking cases of bronchial asthma promptly relieved with five-drop doses of Oil of Eucalyptus given in a tablespoonful of water. The dose was given last thing at night. It also relieved the dyspnea in a case of mitral insufficiency. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Eucalyptus tereti- coris - menstrual cough and prostration. (2) Eucalyptol - depresses temperature of healthy body more than Quinine, acts on kidneys like Ter., Anae., Hydr., Kali-s. Eucalyptus neutralizes ill effectsofStry. (3) Angophora, Red Gum - dysentery, pains, tenesmus, better lying flat on face, obstinate constipation. Eucalyptus rostrata, Kino. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Hot, burning sensation in stomach. Strong smelling, burning eructations. Slow difficult and painful digestion with much fetid gas. Pain in epigastrium and upper abdomen ameliorated by food. Beating and emptiness with pulsation in epigastric arteries. Throbbing in stomach. Fullness, pressure and weight in stomach. Malignant disease of stomach with vomiting of blood and sour fluid. Cancer. Nausea and vomiting with chill.

Abdomen - Gastrointestinal derangements with sleeplessness and restlessness. Burning in epigastrium and umbilical regions. As if a weight in bowels. Sharp aching in the hypogastrium, worse after dinner. Flatulent distention. Spleen hard and contracted. Breasts - Swellings in different parts of body, one below nipple in right side, size of filbert with stabbing, darting pains.

Rectum - Dysentery with rectal heat, tenesmus, hemorrhage. Typhoid diarrhea. Aching pains in bowels with feeling of impending diarrhea. Acute diarrhea. Chronic diarrhea, mucus and bloody. Stools thin, watery, preceded by sharp pains. Fetor of stools and flatus. Condition of mucus membrane favoring worms. Sensations - Burning pains and sensations predominate, but also pricking, stabbing, and sharp aching.

Male - Increased sexual appetite. Subacute and chronic gonorrhea. Recent chancres.

Female - Acrid, fetid leucorrhea. Ulcer around orifice of urethra. Vasculartumors of urethra. Food - Increased appetite, tormenting thirst.

Heart - Painful palpitation. Strong beating of abdominal aorta. Aneurysms pressing on vagus nerve. Sudden flushing of face with much flatulence, in women at menopause.

Limbs - Rheumatic pains, worse at night, walking orcarrying anything. Stiff, weary sensation. Pricking sensation, followed by painful aching. Nodular swellings over metacarpal and metatarsal joints. Lungs - Asthma with great dyspnea and palpitations. Breathing is quickened. Cardiac asthma. Moist asthma. Bronchial asthma. Bronchitis in elderly, feeble pesons. Bronchorrhea (Bals-p.). Fetid form of bronchitis, bronchial dilatation and emphysema. Irritativecough. Coughs of influenza. Profuse expectoration of offensive muco-pus. Expectoration is white, thick with frothy mucus. Whooping cough in rickety children.

Skin - Glandular enlargements and nodular swelling over joints. Foul and indolent ulcers. Herpetic eruptions.

Modalities - Worse periodically. Worse night.

Kidneys - Suppurative inflammation of kidneys. A cute nephritis, complications from influenza. Urethral caruncle. Bladder feels loss of expulsive force. Catarrh of bladder. Spasmodic stricture, gonorrhea. Burning and tenesmus. Diuresis. Hematuria. Urine contains pus and is deficient in urea. Urine has the odor of violets.

Temperature - Chill, then nausea and vomiting. Fever with aching. Continued and typhoid fevers. Scarlet fever.

author: Murphy

full:
PHARMACY - eug. Eugenia jambosa. Rose- apple. Jambosa vulgaris. Eugenia vulgaris. Malabar, Plum-tree. N. O. Myrtacae. A tree native to the tropics, never without flower or fruit. Tincture of fresh seeds. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne rosacea. Catarrhal, fever. Catarrhs. Comedones. Constipation. Coryza. Cough. Cramps. Diarrhea. Diplopia. Hernia. Hiccough. Impotence. Influenza. Nausea. Otitis. Pimples. Throat, sore.

HOMEOPATHIC - Eug. like Eucal., produces a state of intoxication similar to alcohol. Talkative, but indolent. Excitement soon changing to depression. Characteristic better after urination,becomes more cheerful, exhilarated, but passing into gloominess again soon after. Nausea, better from smoking. Acne rosacea. Acne, simple and indurated. Comedones. The pimples are painful for Some distance around. Sufferings occur especially in the evening and at night. An old wound from a thrust became painful again. Rheumatic pain wanders from place to place with catarrh. MIND - Quite talkative but indolent. Prefers to do nothing but smoke all day. Remarkably changed, mentally, after urination. Sadness better urination, but soon everything became gloomy again. Constant desire to sit alone and reflect. Everything seems wrong. Nothing seems right. Restlessness, constantly changing positions. Forgets all his business. Delusion, all things seem beautiful after urination.

Head - Headache as if a board were lying on right side. Dullness and slight sticking pain. Pressive, pinching pain, in small spot deep in forehead. Pressive pinching pain, on vertex. Neuralgia in left forehead over eye. Headache in evening nausea, vomiting. Nocturnal headache, with burning in eyes, great thirst and much urination.

Eyes - Eyes look sleepy and drunken. Burning pain, in the afternoon. Suddenly biting in the eyes as from pepper. Needle-like stitches in inner canthus right eye. Hot lachrymation. Lachrymation with burning and gnawing pains. Whirling before right eye.

Ears - Catarrhal otitis.

Nose - Mucus goes from nose into throat. Perspiration - Sweats when walking. Rectum - Cramp or pinching pains in rectum. Constipation. Urging to stool and colic. Tenesmus, urging to stool. Loose evacuation, followed by vomiting. Hemorrhoids bleed copiously for days with great relief of mind and body. Scanty evacuation of stool, the consistence of pap and sandy, spurting and fetid. Very scanty, pasty, gritty stool. Scanty, hard stool after much pressing, followed by spasmodic closure of anus. Offensive, sputtering stool, without much urging. Sensations - Headache as if a heavy board were lying on right side. As of cramp in orifice of stomach, as if a ten-pound weight were hanging on rectum and as if everything below would fall out.

Face - Pimples on the face with painful sensibility of their circumferences. Food - Appetite increased. Great thirst. Great desire to smoke tobacco (Calad., Daph.). Agreeable taste, of tobacco, of food and drink when smoking.

Mouth - Abundant accumulation of frothy and viscid saliva in the mouth, especially before a meal and when talking.

Throat - At night, violent thirst from dryness low down in throat, so that he did not feel the drink, which also did not better the dryness. Pain in small spot in region of left corner of hyoid bone. Inflamed throat (in catarrhal fever). Vertigo - Whirling in head while sitting. Vertigo after rising from lying down. Vertigo caused by rush of blood to head. Dizzy and nauseated, in evening. COMMENTS - Effects the eyes and vision. Darkness and double vision, on looking intently double vision disappears. Whirling before right eye as if it would become dark. Whirling in the head while sitting, houses at a distance seem to turn bottom upwards. Inflamed eyes. As though fire came out of eyes and tears ran out in streams in evening and night. Worse by sun, causes eyes to fill with water. Burning worse by closing eyes, prevents sleeping at night. Burning not better from cold water. Pain in small of back and calves. Aching in sacrum and knees. Sticking pain in back as if something were sticking in spine, better by bending back. Rheumatic pain wanders from place to place with catarrh. An old wound from a thrust became painful again. Skin disease, worse during menses. Open air causes much exhaustion, yawning while walking in morning. RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Coffee, by smoking tobacco. Compare: (1) Myrtus chekan - chronic bronchitis. (2) Ant-t., Berb-a. (3)Eucal. a myrtaceous tree in catarrhal conditions, Laur. and drugs containing Hydrocyanic acid, Puls. - fugitive rheumatic pains. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Heartburn at night. Cramp in orifice of stomach, causing nausea. Contractive, pinching sensation deep in stomach. Sensation as of cramp in orifice of stomach, which results in nausea. Nausea rising up from end of esophagus.

Abdomen - Flatulence, rumbling in bowels. Colic, with labor-like pains, pressing downward, much urging to stool and to urinate. Burning pain in abdomen. Drawing about navel. Inguinal hernia from a fall.

Male - Impotence. Emission of semen too slow or entirely wanting during sex. Perspiration and thirst after sex.

Back - Burning, itching in a small spot on back, worse after scratching. Sticking pains in back. Pain in small of back and in calves. Aching in sacrum and knees.

Limbs - Nightly cramps in soles of feet (Calc., Cupr.. Mag-p.). Fissures between toes. Skin recedes from the nails, forming pus. Cramp-like and paralytic pains in the tibia and in the heels. Hot hands. Lungs - Catarrh with much mucus and rheumatic pains. Rattling in lungs. Moist cough without yellowish, bloody expectoration in the evening and at night.

Sleep - Profound sleep. Stupefying sleep, even at noon with confused dreams. Yawning while walking in open air. Difficult waking.

Skin - Acne rosacea. Acne, simple and indurated. Comedones. Desquamation and suppuration of the skin around the nail of the thumb. Skin cracks about toes.

Kidneys - Burning during urination. Frequent urination at night. Shuddering or sudden increase of brightness and of light before the eyes after urinating. Deepcolored urine.

Temperature - Shiverings run over him after urination. Coldness, as if the body were naked. Perspiration in the morning with burning thirst. Hot hands. Fever, heat before midnight with little thirst and much sweat.

PHARMACY - euonin. Euonyminum. A concentrated extract, so-called active principle from the bark of Euonymus Americana, E. atropurpúrea and other American species of Euonymus. Celastraceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Bright's disease.…
full:
PHARMACY - euonin. Euonyminum. A concentrated extract, so-called active principle from the bark of Euonymus Americana, E. atropurpúrea and other American species of Euonymus. Celastraceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Bright's disease. Cholera. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Dysentery. Gallstones. Indigestion. Liver, disorders. Nausea.

HOMEOPATHIC - Euonyminum is largely used by herbalists in cases of constipation, indigestion, and torpid liver. It has not been proved, but Hale quoted the following account of its effects, which do not seem to differ much from Euon. “In very large doses, it proves a drastic cathartic, its operation being attended with a death-like nausea, excessive tormina and cold sweats. The dejections from the bowels are profuse, violent and accompanied by much flatus.” COMMENTS - Lutze recorded a case of albuminuria of pregnancy with dropsy cured with the 1 x, and also a case of albuminuria and dropsy in a young man of seventeen. This patient had eczema and was cured by Lutze with Ars. 200c. Later he got a chill from standing in the water fishing. He suffered from malaise and finally dropsy developed. Euonyminum After a week of treatment, he was indifferent, drowsy, sleeping most of the day and night, sometimes with heavy breathing. Anasarca general, chiefly in face and limbs. Pulse full, slow, 50 to 60. Occasionally dull frontal or occipital headache, face sallow, sclerotics yellow, temperature 102 to 103. Urine scanty, 1,017 (later 1,009), containing large quantities of albumen, epithelial casts and granular debris, no bile or chlorides. Stool grayish. He had no pains or subjective symptoms. There were all the evidences of a fully- developed case of acute Bright's disease. He was given Euonymus lx, 2 grains in half a tumbler of water, a spoonful every hour. In three days there was evident improvement. The treatment was continued for a month, when he was nearly well, the cure being completed with Puls., Calc., Sulph. at long intervals. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

PHARMACY - euon-a. Euonymus atropurpúrea. Burning bush. Wahoo. N. O. Celastra- ceae. Tincture of fresh bark and root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Bilious fever. Biliousness. Cholera morbus. Constipation. Diarrhea. Gallstones. Gout. Heart, weakness. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Levitation. Liver disorders. Rheumatism. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - Euon-a„ like Euonin. and Euon., is a favorite liver remedy among herbalists. It has not been proved, but clinical experience shows that its action is very like that of its botanical relatives. Migraines. Headache, mental disturbances and much distress in hepatic and kidney region. Bilious headache, coated tongue, bad taste, constipation. Passive congestion and torpor of liver. Chronic catarrhal disorders of stomach and intestines. Profuse stools, varying or of several colors. Albuminuria. Chronic rheumatism and gout. Weak heart. MIND - Mental confusion. Loss of memory, Euonymus atropurpúrea unable to recall familiar names. Despondent, irritable.

Head - Bilious headaches, pressure over brows, compressing eyes. Heavy frontal headache. Sore, tired feeling, bruised feel ing of scalp. Pain overright eye extending back through the head.

Mouth - Dry, pasty taste.

Stomach - Thirsty. Feels full and uncomfortable. Vertigo - Vertigo, obscure vision and gastric derangement, associated with albuminuria. Vertigo in forehead, as if drawn up and pitched forward. COMMENTS - A woman who tasted the juice of the bark related her experience to Hale: “I felt immediately a sick weakening feeling all through the nervous system, dull, heavy pain through upper portion of head together with enlarged blurred feeling. I seemed so drawn up from the floor, that is seemed difficult to place my foot down when walking with sufficient firmness to stand up, a tipping over sensation when sitting and walking.” She also had a deathly sickness at her stomach with perspiration and heat in her face, in alternation with chills in the back and back part of the arms. Some of the symptoms returned the next day, but were dissipated by vinegar, which must be looked upon as its antidote. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Euonymus Euro- poea. Spindle-tree - liverdisorders, biliousness, lumbago, gastric derangements with albuminuria. (2) Cutting pains in malar bones tongue, penis up to bladder, Podo. (3) Am-pic., Chel., Euonymin lx trituration, albuminuria. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Abdomen - Flatus and pain. Pain about umbilical region, navel.

Rectum - Anus very sore and burning. Constipation with hemorrhoids and severe backache. Diarrhea, stools variable and profuse, bloody.

Back - Crawling in back. Dull pain between shoulders and about kidney and splenic region, pain in lumbar region better lying down. Constitutions - Brunettes more easily affected.

Limbs - Aching in all joints, especially ankles. Feet feel swollen and tired.

Modalities - Better from cool air. Better pressure. Worse from eating. Worse evening.

Liver - Liver engorged. Gallstones.

Kidneys - Urine scanty, high-colored. Acid ity increased. Urine poured out rapidly.

PHARMACY - euon. Euonymus europaea. Spindle-tree. N. O. Celastraceae. Trituration of dried seeds. Tincture of fresh seeds. Historical dose: Trimration and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Backaches.BiZioMS. Cholera. Collapse. Constipation. Convulsions. Diarrhea. Gallstones. Gastric, derangements. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Liver, disorders. Lumbago. Pusmles. Vertigo.

HERBAL - The Celastraceae, to which Euonymus belongs, are closely related to the Rhamnacae which include the well-known purgative Cascara sagrada.

HOMEOPATHIC - Euon. has been used successfully in cases of engorgement of the liver, biliousness, headache, coated tongue, bad taste, and constipation. Passive constipation with hemorrhoids or severe pain in back like lumbago. Diarrhea, profuse stool, variable in color. Gastric derangements with albuminuria, headache, weakness, vertigo and obscuration of sight. Liver disorders, biliousness, lumbago. COMMENTS - Allen recalls the effects ofEuon- yminum in a case of poisoning with the seeds. “A man, forty- three took eighteen seeds one morning and as many the following evening. He was seized with frightful abdominal pain and profuse diarrhea, eventually bloody. “He was not seen until the evening, when he was in a state of profound collapse with involuntary evacuations of blood and mucus. On lifting him up tetanic convulsions were induced which immediately preceded death.” In its proving, cutting, sticking and drawing pains predominated. The left side is more affected than the right. Cutting pains in the malar bones in the tongue. Cutting in the penis extends up to the bladder. Pains compel lying down and are then relieved or reappear in other parts. Violent shivering chill over whole body. Pains in chest, head and abdomen, worse after eating. Tingling in the skin which provokes scratching, followed by a burning sensation. Eruption of small dry pustules. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Podo., Rham., Iris. Euon. atrop. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Eupatorium Aromaticum
author: Murphy
constitution: Ague. Aphthae. Chorea. Gravel. Hysteria. Neurasthenia. Sore, nipples. Stomatitis. Vomiting.
keynote: PHARMACY - eup-a. Eupatorium aromaticum. White snake-root. Eupatorium urticifolium. Deer-wort. Pool- root. N. O. Composite. Found in low woods from Massachusetts to Louisiana. Flowers are white and aromatic. Tincture of root. Historical dose: Tincture and all…
full:
PHARMACY - eup-a. Eupatorium aromaticum. White snake-root. Eupatorium urticifolium. Deer-wort. Pool- root. N. O. Composite. Found in low woods from Massachusetts to Louisiana. Flowers are white and aromatic. Tincture of root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Ague. Aphthae. Chorea. Gravel. Hysteria. Neurasthenia. Sore, nipples. Stomatitis. Vomiting.

HERBAL - Eupatorium aromaticum, when chewed, produces in the mouth a warm, aromatic, pungent sensation and is regarded as a “warm, stimulating tonic.” Hale quoted herbal authorities as commending this plant in “aphthous stomatitis” in women and children. Also for burning in the stomach with “nursing sore mouth,” before and after confinement. Locally it is useful as a mouthwash. Eup-a. is a “nervine,” like Scutellaria and Cypripedium for “restlessness and morbid watchfulness, morbid irritability of the nervous system, tremors, chorea and hysteria.” Like Eup-pur., it has been used for gravel. The Native Americans used it as a cure for ague.

HOMEOPATHIC - Eup-a. is doubly indicated where nervous weakness and aphthous disease are combined. Nervous weakness, restlessness and morbid watchfulness. Hysteria and chorea. Low fevers with extreme restlessness. Aphthous disease. Sore nipples. Sore mouth in infants. Vomiting of bile, pain in stomach, headache and fever. COMMENTS - In a case of sore mouth in a man, 57, recorded by P. S. Duff, Eup-a. caused soon “a general aggravation like a cold or catarrh, annoyed by pain in left shoulder, posterior scapular region, pulse 94 unnatural, tight in left bronchia, felt ill, dull and oppressed.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lapsana communis - useful in sore nipples andhemorrhoids. (2) Hyos., Passi., Hydrin-mur. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

author: Murphy

Worse periodically. Worse every third or fourth day. Worse lying on part. Worse morning. Worse at 7a.m. to 9 a.m. Worse coughing. Worse motion. Worse smell or sight of food..

PHARMACY - eup-per. Eupatorium perfolia- tum. Bone-set. Thoroughwort. N. O. Composite. Tincture of whole plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anus, herpes. Back. pain. Bilious, fevet.Bones,pains. Cachexia. Chills. Cough. Dengue, fever. Diarrhea. Fractures. Fever. Gout. Headaches. Hiccoughs. Hoarseness. Indigestion. Influenza. Intermittent, fever. Jaundice. Liver, pain. Malaria. Measles. Mouth, cracks. Nausea. Ophthalmia. Relapsing, fever. Remittent fever. Rheumatism. Ringworm. Spotted fever. Syphilitic pains. Thirst. Vomiting. Wounds.

HERBAL - Eupatorium perfoliatum is an herbal remedy recommended by Dioscorides for ill- conditioned ulcers, dysentery, stings of reptiles, chronic fevers and obstructed livers. It is known as “Boneset” from the prompt manner in which it relieves pain in limbs and muscles that accompanies some forms of febrile disease like malaria and influenza. Eup-per. is a boon in miasmatic districts, along rivers and marshes. Clarke found Eupper. most useful in epidemic influenza.

HOMEOPATHIC - Characteristic violent aching, bone-breaking pains. Bone pains, general soreness and fevers. Distressing bone pains and muscle pains, with malarial fevers and influenza. Dengue fever. Colds. Conditions where there is a great deal of bone pain. Muscles of chest, back and limbs feel bruised, sore aching. Inability to lie on the left side. Sluggishness of all organs and functions. Weakness. Acts upon the gastro-hepatic organs and bronchial mucus membrane. Bilious effects. Restless, chilly and nauseated. Cachexia from old chronic, bilious intermittents. Useful in old broken down constitutions of inebriate. Marked periodicity (Ars., Chin., Cedr.), changing periodicity, chill in the morning one day, in the evening the next. MIND - Feels at night as if going out of his mind. Anxiety, despondency. Very restless, cannot keep still, though wishes to. Sadness during heat. Moaning during chill. Moans with aching pains.

Head - Head pains alternating with gouty pains. Occipital pain after lying down with sense of weight. Headache with soreness internally. Throbbing, sore pain. Sensation as of a metal cap on head. Top and back of head with painful. Headaches with soreness of eyeballs. Headaches better by vomiting of bile, by conversation. Sick headaches every third and seventh day. Headaches with influenza. Lifts head with hands during headache. Headache and nausea every other morning, when awaking. Violent headache, comes on before the chill and lasts through all the stages, worse during the sweat.

Eyes - Eyes glistened. Yellow eyes. Painful soreness of eyeballs, lids. Sore aching eyeballs with headache. Great aversion to light. Intense, darting pain through eyes, as from needles. Increased lachrymation, during cough. Redness of margins of lids. Glutinous secretion from meibomian glands.

Ears - Buzzing in ears with heat on vertex. Could hear everything while seemingly in profound sleep, but couldn't speak.

Nose - Coryza with sneezing, with aching in the bones. Sneezing with influenza. Nose very dry and stopped up.

Face - Sudden, severe contraction of muscles of right cheek. Yellow face. Sallow, sickly in intermittent fever. Pale face, during catarrhs. Flushed face during cough or fever.

Mouth - Taste bitter. Breath smells moldy, sourish. Paleness of the mucus membrane of the mouth. Cracks in corners of mouth. Soreness of the corners of the mouth. Tongue yellow, covered with white fur.

Throat - Hoarseness, worse morning. Hoarseness and cough, with soreness in chest; must support it. Soreness in trachea and bronchia. Fauces sore, dryness of throat. Throat dry, at times becomes hoarse and loses her voice. Vertigo - Vertigo, sensation of falling to left, worse lying on right side, better vomiting. Early in morning whirling around in brain as if he had been whirled in cool screen: repeated after a short cessation. COMMENTS - Characteristic soreness, painful aching in the bones. Bruised feeling, especially in old injuries. Useful for residual bone pain, after the flu. Aching in limbs, throughout the body. Parietal protuberances, sore with pain. Pains come and go quickly (Bell., Coloc., Mag-p.). Pain and extreme tenderness of left glutei muscles. Aching in the right scapula (similar to Chel.,Phos., Gels.). Aright-sided remedy, difficult to lie on the left side (Phos. ). Swelling of the limbs. Headaches with internal soreness. Migraine headaches, severe pain at the base of the brain. Congestive headache (Bell.). Headache with nausea and vomiting. Sleepiness and yawning. Dizzy with a tendency to fall to the left. Influenza, periodic flus (Bry., Ip., Nux-v., Ars.). Winter colds, with sneezing in the back of the head. Bursting, severe headaches and a thirst for cold water (Bry., Oscilloc. has the headache and bone pains). Eyeballs are sore and achy. Dizziness (Gels.). Runny nose (All-c.). High fever, alternates with chills. High fever with bone ache (Merc.. Aur.). Bilious fevers. Edema with intermittent fever or malaria. Yellow fever. History of malaria. Periodic attacks of fever, colds, infection. High fever with increased aching, followed by scanty or profuse sweat. All pains better with sweat except headaches, which are worse. Headache is better rising up. Prostration. Chilliness predominates, wants to be covered, better in the house, worse in open air. Chills with a shudder down the back. Chills begin in the small of the back with aching in the limbs as though every bone in the body were being broken. Difficulty getting comfortable because of a bruised feeling, restless (Ars.). Prominent catarrhal symptoms. Sore throat, hoarseness in the morning. Hoarseness with aching soreness of the trachea. Hoarse, rough, dry, hacking cough with scraping in bronchia. Desire for something cold to relieve the throat. Sternal pains, especially when coughing. Bruised feeling with cough, desire to hold the chest (Bry.). Cough with extreme soreness down trachea. Painful cough. Nocturnal, loose cough. Cough better by getting on hands and knees, kneeling with face towards pillow, worse lying on back. W. P. Defriez reported a case in which, every winter for several years, the patient had been annoyed by a dry, hacking cough with paroxysms lasting some time, only relieved by getting on hands and knees. Eup-per. cured. Cough arising from irritation of the liver. Bilious vomiting and diarrhea, bilious sick headaches. Liver pain, soreness, may desire to rub the liver which is enlarged and tender. Hepatitis. Jaundice, clay-colored, white stools. Bile in the urine, mahogany colored urine. Gout. Bitter, bile taste in the mouth. Intense thirst, but drinking cold water causes shuddering and vomiting of bile. Eating causes violent, distressing pains which are relieved only by vomiting. Can be disgusted by food, nausea from smelling food (Colch.). RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bry., Sep., Nairn., Chel. (2) Nyctanthes arbor-tristis - bilious fever insatiable thirst, bitter vomiting at close of chill, also constipation of children. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Tight clothing is oppressive. Hiccoughs. Indigestion from alcohol of old people. Great thirst for cold water, but after drinking shuddering and vomiting of bile. Distressing pain in the stomach not better until all is vomited. Indigestion consequent on the use of alcoholic drinks. Nausea from smell or sight of food. Nausea, vomiting of bile at close of chill or hot stage, throbbing headache. Vomits water or food that has been taken. Vomiting and purging of bile of green liquid several quarts at a time. Vomiting preceded by thirst.

Abdomen - Abdomen distension and tympanitic. Avoids tight clothing. Colicky pains in upper abdomen with headache and other pains. Cramps. Griping pain worse after stool, with tenesmus. Tightness in left hypochondrium.

Rectum - Cramps. Constipated with sore liver. Stools, frequent, whitish, green, watery. Constipation with catarrh. Purging stools with smarting and heat in anus. Morning diarrhea.

Male - Itching of the groin. Herpes on scrotum and thighs.

Female - Itching of the mons veneries. Herpes on thighs. Food - Canine hunger during or before ague. Anorexia of alcoholics. Food has no taste. Thirst for cold water, before and during chill. Great thirst for cold water, but after drinking shuddering and vomiting of bile. Craving for ice cream. Desire for acid drinks.

Chest - Great oppression of chest. Raw, hot, sore chest and bronchi. Muscles of chest are sore, worse from inspiration. Soreness in chest, can't twist when standing, sitting or lying. Pain and soreness behind sternum. Constitutions - Worn-out constitutions from inebriety.

Heart - Pressure as if heart is in too small a space. Pain, soreness in cardiac region, worse by least motion or turning body around.

Back - Backache before and during chill. Chill spreads from back. Pain in back of neck and between the shoulders. Intense backache. Pain as if beaten, pain ascends. Aching pain in back. Beating pain in nape and occiput, better after rising. Trembling in back during fever. Weakness in small of back. Deep-seated pains in loins, with soreness from motion. Trembling in back during fever. Breasts - Aching, under left breast, can't lie on left side. Pain through right nipple, when breathing. Causations - Ill effects of the ice-house.

Limbs - Boneaches with influenza. Swellings of limbs with the debility. Aching in bones with soreness of flesh. Painful gouty nodes, associated with headache. Bone aches with fever and chills. Gouty soreness and inflamed nodosities of joints, associated with headache. Dropsy of legs, feet and ankles. Aching in arms and wrists. Bruised pain in calves. Swelling of left great toe.

Sleep - Stretching and yawning, before chill. Sleepiness with difficult breathing. Has to lie with head high. Headache on awaking.

Skin - Jaundice. Skin pale and sensitive during fever. Eruptions develop late, especially in measles. Ringworm. Her- pectic eruptions.

Modalities - Better by conversation. Better by getting on hands and knees. Better vomiting bile. Better lying on face. Better sweating. Worse from cold air. Worse night. Worse periodically. Worse every third or fourth day. Worse lying on part. Worse morning. Worse at 7a.m. to 9 a.m. Worse coughing. Worse motion. Worse smell or sight of food.

Liver - Liver problems on the use of alcoholic drinks. Soreness and sharp pains in region of liver on moving or coughing. Lungs - Dyspnea, must lie with head and shoulders high. Difficulty of breathing, with perspiration, anxious countenance, sleeplessness. Sharp pain through right lung on deep inspiration, at night, disturbed breathing frightens him.

Kidneys - Dark-colored, clearurine. Watery urine, during intermittents. Urine profuse, pale, with gout. Urine alternately profuse and scanty. Dark-brown, scanty urine, depositing a whitish, clay-like sediment.

Cough - Hoarseness and cough with soreness in chest, must support it. Cough after eruptive stage of measles. Cough preceding or following measles. Cough with influenza. Chronic, loose cough, chest sore, worse at night. Cough better getting on hands and knees. Cough lying on back. Loose cough, at night. Cough from laryngeal tickling. Cough with soreness and heat in bronchi, flushed face, tearful eyes. Hectic cough from suppressed intermittent fever. Cough worse from 2 a.m. to 4 a.m.

Perspiration - Coldness during night sweats. Sweat, relieves all the symptoms except the headache. Sweat scanty. Skin bathed in sweat. Sweats at night, with chilliness. Sweats from moving oruncov- ering. Profuse sweat at night in old cases of intermittent fever. Copious sweats, in rheumatism.

Temperature - Chill preceded by thirst, with great soreness and aching of bones. Pain all over, in the bones as if broken, before the chill. Chill between 7 a.m. and 9 a.m. At the conclusion of the chill, vomiting of bile or after every draft. Thirst continues during the chill and heat. Influenza with weak pulse, prostration, bones sore. Influenza in inebriates and with old people. Great weakness and prostration during the fever. Burning heat. Intermittent fever paroxysm generally commences in the morning.

Hysteria. Impo- tence. Indigestion. Infertility. Intermittent fever. Leucorrhea. Miscarriages. Kidney colic. Metritis. Nausea. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Stones. Strangury. Throat, sore. Urine, retention. Vomiting.

full:
PHARMACY - eup-pur. Eupatorium purpureum. Gravel root. Queen of the meadow. Joe Pye weed. Trumpet weed. N. O. Composite. Tincture of the root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Bedwetting. Bladder, irritable. Chills. Cystitis. Diabetes, insipidus. Dropsy. Dyspnea. Dysuria. Enlarged, prostate. Fever. Gravel. Headache. Hematuria. Homesickness. Hysteria. Impo- tence. Indigestion. Infertility. Intermittent fever. Leucorrhea. Miscarriages. Kidney colic. Metritis. Nausea. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Stones. Strangury. Throat, sore. Urine, retention. Vomiting.

HERBAL - The common name, “gravel root,” indicates the traditional use of the drug and in the hands of the eclectics it has well in cases of irritable bladder, diabetes insipidus, incontinence of urine, and kidney stones. Hale mentioned that impotency has been cured in the male and infertility and uterine atony in the female. It is similar in action to Cimic. and Helon. here.

HOMEOPATHIC - Eup-pur. was well proved by a Mrs. Dresser; she experienced a feeling of homesickness even when living in her own house. Distressing dyspnea from dropsy. Kidney dropsy. Albuminuria, diabetes, strangury, irritable bladder. Cystitis in pregnant women from riding over rough roads. Enlarged prostate. Impotency and infertility. Bone pains, nausea and vomiting accompany fever. Sweat is slight. Restless tossing, moaning, unable to lie down. General soreness (Eup-pur.). Chills and pains run upwards, beginning in the back, with shaking and comparatively little coldness. MIND - Homesick, even though at home and among family. Sighing. Depressed and sleepy. Hysterical, low- spirited state. Great fear of sickness. Talkative, exclamations. Stupid, dull mind. Delusions of sight and hearing. Delusion that heels were crowding through boots. Delusion so marked that she felt compelled to look and see if it was really the case.

Head - Sick headache beginning in morning, worse afternoon and evening, worse in cold air. Left sided headache with vertigo, as if falling to the left side. Pain from left shoulder to occiput.

Eyes - Staring. Red and swollen, with headache. Lachrymation.

Ears - Ears feel full. Illusions of hearing. Crackling, worse on swallowing.

Nose - Coryza. Hoarseness. Hacking cough, in evening. Cough with soreness and heat in bronchi.

Face - Face flushed. Lips blue.

Mouth - Tongue furred, brown along center. Tongue, prickling and stinging in tip, on back. Numbness of tongue. Saliva abundant.

Throat - Choking fullness, must swallow often. Burning, as if had swallowed some hot substance, most at back of throat, worse swallowing. Pain left side of throat, causing pain on swallowing, before chill. Fluttering in throat pit. Vertigo - Light headed, dizzy, as if flying round and round. Vertigo as if falling towards left side. Vertigo worse morning. Vertigo with illusions of sight and hearing. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Senec., Cann-s., Helon., Ph-ac, Triticum, Epigea. (2) Apoc. - dropsy., Apis., Cann-s., Canth., Cop., For., Hydre., Mit., Senec., (3) Vespa- kidney symptoms. (4) Caps.. Ph-ac. in homesickness. (5) Eup-per., Colch. - nausea at smell of food. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Wants lemonade or cold drinks during chill. Much wind in stomach, belch- ings almost constant. Nausea at smell or sight of food or cooking. Great nausea ht no vomiting, with chill. Vomiting with fever with sick headache. Griping, crampy pain.

Abdomen - Pain and soreness of abdomen, much worse left side. Hypogastric region swollen and hot. Rumbling, rolling and twisting pain in bowels. Severe colic after voiding urine.

Rectum - Bilious diarrhea. Pressure and weight on rectum. Feeling as if bowels must be moved immediately, without being able to do so. Bowels loose, during ague.

Male - Impotency from exhaustion or abuse.

Female - Profuse leucorrhea, caused by exhaustion and chronic metritis. Numbness, worse in groin. External genitals, vulva feels as though wet. Quick jerking pain in left ovary. Tense, cutting pain above left ovary. Sterility from ovarian atony. Threatened miscarriages. Habitual miscarriage at third or fourth month. Inefficient labor- pains. Food - No appetite. Loss of appetite during fever, desire to eat immediately after. Desire for warm drinks. Desires lemonade. Desires cold drinks during chill. Thirst during chill and heat. Thirst before chill, none during. Thirst with dropsy. Longing for hot drinks.

Chest - Grating sensation in chest at every deep inspiration.

Heart - Violent palpitations. Fluttering in heart and throat. Pulse accelerated and full.

Back - Weight and heaviness in back and Joins. Cutting pain in neck running from left shoulder to occiput. Between shoulder-blades chilly feeling. Pains running upward from sacrum into kidneys from left side of back and hip. Distressing pain in lumbar region before chill.

Limbs - Tired, weak, uneasiness in limbs with numbness and gnawing pains. Rheumatic pains shifting from place to place, always from below upward. Soreness of bones, aching of limbs as if bones were broken. Pains come and go suddenly, very restless, but not better by motion. Pains in arms and legs before chill, limbs cold during fever. Neuralgia of right shoulder or right knee, passing over to left. Lungs - Dyspnea with dropsy. Sighing every few minutes. Strong desire to inflate the lungs, which she continued to do from time to time without noticing particularly that she was doing so.

Sleep - Y awning, gaping andsighing. Sleepy and depressed. Sleep restless and mind disturbed, frightful dreams.

Skin - Skin hot and dry with fever, hot to touch in face.

Modalities - Worse from motion. Worse left side. Changing position ever so little causes chilliness down back. Sensation as if falling to left side (Eup-per.).

Kidneys - Nephritis, with severe pain in back, after taking cold. Chronic nephritis. Deep, dull pain in kidneys. Cutting pains. Diabetes insipidus. Dysuria. Insufficient flow, milky. Urine smells sweet. Urinary Eupatorium purpureum stream smaller. Hematuria. Incontinence of urine, in children. Frequent effort with passage of but a few drops of urine. Weak, tired and faint after urinary symptoms. Kidney and bladder stones.

Bladder - Cystitis in pregnant women on riding on rough roads. Bladder irritability in women. Strangury. Burning in bladder and urethra on urinating. Constant desire, even after frequent urination, the bladder feels full. Soreness and pain in bladder. Smarting and burning pain very intense in bladder and urethra. Cutting, aching pain in bladder, with constant desire to urinate.

Cough - Hacking cough in evening. Cough with soreness and heat in bronchia. Dry, hacking cough in spells. Cough before attack of intermittent fever. Cough continuing throughout paroxysm.

Perspiration - Sweats about forehead. Sweats on upper portion of body.

Temperature - No thirst during chill, but much frontal ache. Chill commences in back. Violent shaking with comparatively little coldness. Fever with protracted bone pains, nausea and vomiting, followed by slight sweat, mostly about forehead and head.

CLINICAL - Antrum, pain. Anus, spasms, prolapse. Debility. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Hemorrhoids. Skin, eruptions. Smell, illusion. Spleen disorders. Throat, soreness.

HOMEOPATHIC - Produces irritation and burning sensations of the intestinal tract with vomiting and diarrhea. Dark brown, watery, mucus stools, sometimes mixed with solid feces. Sometimes offensive with blood, mostly in afternoon. Diarrhea, stools difficult with painful anal spasm. If stool lasts two or three days there is prolapse returning very gradually, if replaced within half an hour the bowel generally prolapses again. If the diarrhea lasts longer, external hemorrhoids appear, not returning with the prolapse. Rheumatic pains come on when heated. Malaise, tired weak feeling during and after walking. Restlessness all night, turning about half awake and half asleep. Pain in antrum. Sense of taste blunted. Cold water relieves burning in back of throat (Caps., burning worse from cold water). Skin disorders. Symptoms go from right to left.

Stomach - Nausea, worse moving about indoors, better sitting still, from supper. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Abdomen - Tightness, stitch in region of spleen. Sensation as if a long worm writhing in region of transverse colon or duodenum. Throbbing in groins.

Rectum - Feeling or action of the liver, followed by griping and passing of offensive flatus. Offensive diarrhea, followed by slight prolapse rendering sitting uneasy, going off gradually. Stool difficult from painful spasm of anus, continued after the evacuation. Sensations - Illusion of smell, “odor of mice.” Seething sensation in the head and thigh.

Stool - Dark brown, watery, mucus stool, sometimes mixed with solid feces, sometimes offensive. Feces small, lumpy, slimy with prolapse, though there had been no straining. Diarrhea returns at lengthened intervals.

Modalities - Better after eating. Worse evening. Worse from walking.

Liver - Severe stitches in liver, when walking up a hill. Lungs - Heat in chest, radiating from stomach. Feeling as if lungs remained partly inflated. Hoarseness.

CLINICAL - Cholera. Cholera, infantum. Cholerine. Dehydration. Diarrhea. Gastritis. Nausea. Seasickness. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Euph-c. is a diaphoretic, expectorant and cathartic of the old school. It produces gastro- enteric disturbances like other Euphorbias, but with peculiarities especially in the sequence and character of the vomit. Deadly nausea, sudden and powerful vomiting of food in stomach. Vomits large quantities of water mixed with mucus, then of clear fluid like rice-water. Copious watery evacuations of the bowels. Gastro-enteric disturbances with great anxiety, deadly prostration and cold sweat. Attacks recur after short intermissions. Dehydration. Feeling of clawing in stomach, cold sweat (Verat.). COMMENTS -Grimmerremarked “Euphorbia tends to particularly affect the gastrointestinal tract, copious vomiting, rice water stools, cold sweat, prostration, wants to die, intermittent attacks.” REFERENCES - Clarke. Grimmer.

HOMEOPATHIC - The fresh, milky juice is exceedingly acrid when applied to the skin and the…
full:
PHARMACY - euph-1. Euphorbia lathyris. Caper spurge. N. O. Euphorbiacae. A tincture of the whole plant is made. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Cholera. Diarrhea. Dysentery.

HOMEOPATHIC - The fresh, milky juice is exceedingly acrid when applied to the skin and the fruit is highly purgative and poisonous. The juice causes redness, itching, pimples, sometimes gangrene. Poisoning from the seeds produces symptoms including retching, vomiting, and bloody stools with brilliant eyes, flushed face. The abdomen is drawn inward. The whole body is stiff and icy cold. Uneasiness. The symptoms point to its use in erysipelas, poison oak, etc. Rheumatic pains during rest. Paralytic weakness in joints. MIND - Delirium and hallucinations. Stupor, coma.

Eyes - Almost closed from edema of eyelids.

Nose - End of nose very much inflamed externally. Very sensitive and edematous mucus membranes with ulceration.

Face - At first ruddy glow on cheeks, afterwards death-like pallor. Cold perspiration in beads on forehead. Red, puffed face and in spots suppurating. Erythema, beginning on face, gradually extending into the hair parts and then spreading over whole body. Glossy eruption, rough edematous with burning and smarting, aggravated by touch and cold air, ameliorated by close room and sweet-oil applications. Bran-like desquamation. Stinging, smarting and burning of face when touched. Sensation of cobwebs.

Mouth - Tongue coated, slimy, acrid taste. Breath cold, musty odor.

Stomach - Nausea and vomiting of copious, clear water intermingled with white, gelatinous lumps.

Rectum - Drastic purgation from large doses, mild laxative condition from smaller doses, followed several weeks afterwards by obstinate constipation. Stools of white, transparent, gelatinous mucus, later mingled with blood.

Male - Inflammation of scrotum, resulting in deep acrid ulcers with intense itching and burning, worse touching the parts, or from washing.

Heart - Weak and fluttering.

Sleep - Restlessness at night. Sleep disturbed, anxious dreams.

Skin - Erythema, beginning on uncovered parts and face, and spreading over whole body, glossy, rough, edematous with burning and smarting. Fine bran-like desquamation following in the wake of the erythema. Eruption rough, scaly, smarting and burning, when scratched forms deep, ragged ulcers. Ulcerated skin remains red.

Modalities - Better close room. Better sweet-oil application. Worse touch. Worse cold air.

Kidneys - Copious flow of urine. Lungs - Labored breathing. Cold breath, musty odor. Cough, first hacking, as from inhalation of sulphur, later on, regular paroxysms like whooping cough. Cough ending in diarrhea and vomiting, with sleepiness between each paroxysm.

Pulse - 120 beats, full, bounding, somewhat irregular.

Temperature - Body bathed in profuse perspiration, standing out like beads on forehead. Cold, clammy perspiration on forehead. Temperature increased. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Rhus-t. - skin symptoms. Verat. - vomiting, purging, cough and coma. REFERENCES Clarke.

HOMEOPATHIC - The application of the juice and leaves sets up intense and painful inflammation, erysipelatous, phlegmonous, pustular with intense burning pain. COMMENTS - In one of the cases observed, the juice of the stem was applied to an inflamed gum. In another, a boy applied the leaves as a poultice to a black eye. Burnett produced a sore throat in himself by chewing the herb. He cured with the 3x a case of simple sore throat with swelling and painful swallowing. REFERENCES Clarke.

HOMEOPATHIC - In the Medical Press of May 3,…
full:
PHARMACY - euph-pi. Euphorbia pilulifera. Euphorbia hirta. N. O. Euphorbiacae. Tincture. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Bronchitis. Dyspnea. Gonorrhea. Hay fever. Leucorrhea. Sunstroke. Traumatism. Urethritis.

HOMEOPATHIC - In the Medical Press of May 3, 1893, Dr. George Foy gave an account of this medicine. Gray, in 1817, mentioned it as a remedy for syphilis and for venomous bites. In gonorrhea, when there are intense pains at each urination, burning pains which oblige the patient to sit down or to keep quiet, and violent desire to pass water (Cann-s., Canth.). Humid asthma with prostration and restlessness. Hemorrhages caused by sunstroke or traumatism. None of the irritant effects common to most of the Euphorbias were produced, but there was a powerful action on the heart. First, an alarmingly quick pulse, and then a sudden chill. Cardiac dyspnea, hay fever and bronchitis. Urethritis with intense pain on urinating and much urging. Acrid leucorrhea, worse least movement. It has been used by the old-school practitioners in asthma, hay asthma and bronchitis, chiefly in considerable doses. COMMENTS - In the Universal Homeopathic Annual, Dr. Cartier gave this account: “Euphorbia pilulifera has given excellent results in cases of acrid leucorrhea, aggravated by the least motion, especially useful forpale, delicate and sensitive women” (Facaranda). REFERENCES Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - euph-po. Euphorbia poly carpa. Golondrina. Euphorbiagolondrina. N. O. Euphorbiacae. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Snakebites.

HOMEOPATHIC - An antidote to snake poison, its use also renders the body immune to the influence of the snake venom and thus acts as a prophylactic. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cedrón., The Euphorbias. (2) Euphorbia prostata - Used by Indians as an infallible remedy against bites of poisonous insects and snakes, especially the rattle-snake. (3) Plumeria celinus Tincture internally and locally every 15 minutes for snake poisoning, (Dr. Correa). (4) Micania guacho, a Brazilian snake cure. (5) Selaginella - Macerate in milk, locally and internally for bites of snakes and spiders. lodium, tincture for rattle snake bites externally and one drop doses every 10 minutes. (6) Gymnema sylvestre will abolish the taste of bitter things, sense of taste altered, powdered root for snakebite, (7) Sisyrinchium - Ten to fifteen drop doses of tincture for rattlesnake bites. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Influenza. Peritonitis. Sciatica. Syphilis. Teeth, disorders. Toothaches. Ulcers. Vision, disorders. Warts. Writer's cramp.

HOMEOPATHIC - Euph. is an irritant to the skin and mucus membranes, causing much secretion with a sense of dryness. Terrible burning pains, as if a live coal were on or in the part. Burning pain in bones. Burning pain in internal parts. Burning pains of cancer. Pains in limbs and paralytic weakness in joints. Rheumatic pains of a tearing, pressing, and stinging character, but only during rest. Slow inflammations. Blisters. Gangrene of old persons. Everything appears larger than it really is. Convulsions with loss of consciousness. Congestion of blood to head. MIND - Acute mania with symptoms of violent cerebral congestion. Melancholy. Anxiety and apprehension. Starting at night while lying awake in bed. Wants to be by himself and in silence. Quiet, reflective mood. Inclination to work. Temporary attacks of madness. Delusion he sees the same man walking after him that he sees walking before him. Insists upon saying his prayers at the tail of his horse. Everything seems larger than it really is. Abdomen - Excessive colic and tympanites. Spasmodic, flatulent colic. Burning like fire in abdomen and stomach. Griping through whole intestinal canal, followed by thin stool, with burning itching about rectum. Much rumbling, followed by emission of flatus. Anxious sore aching in lower abdomen. Sunken. Feels hollow.

Head - Stupefying frontal headache. Constrictive headache in occiput. Violent, pressive headache. Erysipelas of head and face, with digging, boring and gnawing pains. Sore pain as if beaten, in occiput, worse morning. Bruised pain in head, in occiput and forehead.

Eyes - Pale-red inflammation of eyelids with nightly agglutination. Swelling of lids. Heaviness of upper lids. Biting in eyes, with lachrymation. Great dryness in eyes with profuse discharge. Eyes inflamed and agglutinated in morning. Intolerance of light. Chronic ophthalmia. Eyelids itch severely, are wet and agglutinated. Purulent discharge.

Ears - Ringing in ears, also when sneezing. Roaring at night. Buzzing in right ear, can't sleep at night.

Nose - Nasal itching with mucus secretions from naso-phary nx. Much abortive sneezing. Coryza with swelling. Acrid ozaena. Violent, fluent coryza, with burning and cough. Coryza with watery discharge from eyes and nose.

Face - Red swelling of cheeks. Burning in cheek, worse left. Eyes inflamed and agglutinated in morning. Erysipelas. Yellow blisters. Food - Great hunger. Thirst for cold drinks.

Mouth - Dryness of mouth without thirst. Mouth feels coated with rancid grease. Profuse saliva. Saliva tastes salty. Mouth feels coated with rancid grease. Flat taste in mouth, after breakfast. White coated tongue. Much tenacious mucus in mouth, after midday sleep. Salivation preceded by shivering. Teeth as if screwed together, brittle, crumbling, decay.

Throat - Burning as from hot coal in throat with pain and anxiety. Scraping and rawness in throat. Burning in throat and stomach as if flame were rushing out. Burning pains with pain and anxiety. Vertigo - Violent vertigo, when standing. Vertigo walking in open air. Vision - Diplopia. Dim or feeble vision. Cataract. Lens milk white. Sees better on a dark day. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Op., large quantities of lemon juice. It antidotes: Ars., Nux-v. v.

Stomach - Burning like fire in stomach and abdomen. Inflammation of stomach. Eructations. Frequent hiccough. Erysipelatous gastritis. Profuse empty eructations. As if stomach were hanging loose. Nausea with shuddering. Vomiting with diarrhea. Waterbrash.

Rectum - Burning, sore, around anus. Constipation from inactivity of bowels, hard stool, difficult to pass. Griping pain followed by thin stool. Violent burning itching of rectum. Profuse diarrhea and vomiting. Diarrhea with tenesmus, burn- ing at anus and soreness in abdomen. Stools like glue, painful and flatulent, preceded by itching of rectum. Stool first thin, then knotty. Stools fermented, profuse, clay.

Chest - Burning and sharp pains in left side of chest, during rest, better motion. Stitch-like pressure upon sternum while sitting and standing. Warm feeling in chest, as if hot food had been swallowed. As if left lobe of lung was adhering. Heaviness in pectoral muscles, when turning body to right side.

Heart - Irregular, hurried pulse.

Back - Coccyx sensitive to touch. Pain in coccyx, worse on rising from sitting, worse after stool. Feeling of pressure in muscles of back. Sensation in lumbar region or joints, as if paralyzed.

Limbs - Paralytic pains. Hip-joint as if sprained. Pain in hip joint and coccyx. Paralytic tightness in shoulder joint, mornings, from moving arm. Cramp in muscles of right hand when writing. Paralytic pain in wrist on moving it. Great weakness of legs. Cold sweat on legs in morning. Burning, at night in bones of hip and thigh. Numbness of feet when sitting. Sciatica. Lungs - Breathing oppressed as if chest were not wide enough. Violent, fluent coryza with burning and cough. Spasmodic, dry cough, day and night with asthma. Constant cough with stitches from pit of stomach to sides of chest. Croup, dry, hollow, cough. Warm feeling in chest, as if hot food had been swallowed.

Sleep - Sleepiness during day. Sleeplessness with tremulous tossing about before midnight, roaring in ears, unable to close eyes. Sudden starting up as from an electric shock at night, while lying awake in bed. Anxious, vivid dreams at night, causing him to cry out, whereupon he awakes.

Skin - Erysipelatous inflammation, especially of the cheek. Biting, stinging, red, swollen. Vesicular erysipelas. Pustules, vesicles filled with yellow lymph or liquid. Carbuncle. Old, torpid, indolent ulcers with biting, sharp pain. Gangrene (Echi., Sec.). Ulcerating carcinoma and epithelioma of the skin. As if thin cord lay under skin.

Modalities - Better from application of oil. Better cold application. Better motion. Worse from sitting. Worse rest. Worse beginning of motion. Worse mercury. Worse touch.

Compare - (1) Euphorbia marginata, Snow on the mountain - Honey from the flowers is poisonous, detected by the hot, acrid taste. The milky juice produces skin symptoms like Rhus-t. (2) Psoralea - A Columbian plant - pains of cancer, ulcers. Leucorrhea fetid. Pruritus. Uterine tumors. (3) Crot-t., Jatr. (4) Colch., Elat., Ant-t., Verat. (5) Euphorbiacious plants Acai., Crot-t., Jatr., Mancin., Mercurialis., Ricinus, Yucca fil. It follows: Graph., Lach., Puls., Sep., Sulph. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Temperature - Chilliness and shivering over whole body, in morning. Chilliness while walking in open air. Shivering over back with gio wing cheeks and cold hands. Constant chilliness with constant sweat. Coldness of body with internal burning heat. Great heat. Fever with aversion to be dressed, clothing feels too heavy. Heat only on head. High fever.

author: Murphy

Worse from sunlight. Worse room, indoor. Worse evening. Worse after sleep. Lying down aggravates coryza, better cough. Cold air and wind causes lachrymation. Walking in open air causes yawning..
