PHARMACY - ip. Ipecacuanha. Ipec root. Cephaelis ipecacuanha. Psychotria ipecacuanha. Uragoga ipecacuanha. N. O. Rubiaceae. Tincture and trituration of the dried root. Historical dose: Trituration, tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anemia. Anorexia. Asthma. Bronchitis.…
full:
PHARMACY - ip. Ipecacuanha. Ipec root. Cephaelis ipecacuanha. Psychotria ipecacuanha. Uragoga ipecacuanha. N. O. Rubiaceae. Tincture and trituration of the dried root. Historical dose: Trituration, tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anemia. Anorexia. Asthma. Bronchitis. Catarrh. Chills. Cholera. Cholera, infantum. Colic. Convulsions. Coughs. Cramps. Cyanosis. Deafness. Diarrhea. Drug, addictions. Drug, poisoning. Dys- pepsia. Dyspnea. Dysentery. Enteric, fever. Eyes, disorders. Fever. Food, poisoning. Gallstone, colic. Gastric, ulcer. Gastritis. Gastroenteritis. Hematemesis. Hemorrhages. Hemorrhoids.Hemoptysis. Hysteria. Indigestion. Intermittent, fever. Menstruation, disorders. Migraine. Miscarriage. Morning, sickness. Nausea. Nosebleeds. Opium, habit. Opisthotonos. Pityriasis. Pneumonia. Poisonings. Pregnancy, disorders. Remittent, fever. Salivation. Spasms. Stomach, disorders. Tetanus. Toothache. Tuberculosis. Uterine, hemorrhage. Vomiting. Whooping, cough. Worm fever. Yellow fever.

HERBAL - Ipecac is likely to be of help wherever ailments are associated with the presence of constant nausea. Ipecacuanha wine has a well-known emetic effect. Mixed with oil, powdered ipecac has been used to vesicate the skin and, diluted, the tincture is used for the bites of insects, bee and wasp-stings. In material doses, it produces violent irritation of the skin and, between the acts of vomiting, an uncontrollable desire to scratch.

HOMEOPATHIC - Persistent nausea and vomiting. Profuse salivation with nausea. Constant desire to vomit. Disgust for food, empty vomiting, vomiting of bile or blood. Not better by vomiting. Immediately after vomiting, instead of relief, there is the desire to vomit again. Characteristic feeling “as if the stomach were hanging down relaxed.” Tongue is clean, or not very dirty. Affinity for the pneumo-gastric nerve, producing gastro-intestinal disturbances and respiratory disorders with continuous nausea. Nausea and shortness of breath usually accompany most of the complaints. Bright red, gushing hemorrhages with nausea. Discharges are foamy and profuse. Spasmodic disorders. Opisthotonos and emprosthotonos. Body rigid, stretched out, followed by spasmodic jerking of arms towards each other. Awkward, stumbles against everything. Tetanic spasms from swallowing tobacco. Infantile convulsions. Convulsions in whooping cough from suppressed exanthema from indigestible food. Oversensitive to heat and cold. Faints suddenly in summer or hot room. Morphine or heroin addiction (Aven.). Especially indicated in fat children and adults, who are feeble and catch cold in relaxing atmosphere, warm, moist weather. MIND - Mental depression. Sad, morose. Dejected mood. Peevish, irritable, scornful mood. Impatient, fretful. Full of desires, but do not know what they want. Hard to please. Holds everything in contempt. Disgust with everything. Haughty. Censorious, critical. Intolerance of noise. Wrapped in thought, taciturn. Moaning and sighing with the fever. Anxiety during fever. Restlessness during the fever. Awkward and stumbles against everything. Shrieking before convulsions. Child cries and screams violently and incessantly. Delusion he is unfortunate. Hypochondriasis. Disposition to slander. Ailments from anger, mortification, vexation and reserved displeasure. Irascible, restless, angry in suddenly appearing spells.

Head - Cold sweat on forehead. Heat and throbbing in head, with red cheeks. Aching pain, pressure in forehead. Throbbing in forehead. Migraine or gastric headaches with nausea and vomiting. Headaches with nosebleed. Headache as if brain compressed. Bones of skull feel crushed or bruised. Pain, bruised feeling in brain. Pain in occiput, worse vomiting during chill. Shooting pain in vertex. Pain in the occiput and the neck. Headache over left eye. Pain extends to teeth and root of tongue. Stinging pain with heaviness of head. Hydrocephaloid, fontanels open.

Eyes - Inflamed, red eyes. Red circle around cornea. Yellow sclera. Dilated pupils. Eyes fixed and turned to right. Conjunctivitis. Ulcers of cornea or conjunctiva. Pustular inflammation of cornea and conjunctiva. Cornea dim. Profuse, gushing lachrymation with nausea. Shooting pains through the eyeball. Twitching of eyelids. Lids red and swollen after catching cold. Eyes tire from near vision. Cannot move eyes without nausea. Nausea from looking at moving objects. Photophobia without redness of eyes. Light, candlelight aggravates.

Ears - Cannot endure the least noise. Coldness and chilliness of the ears, during the fever.

Nose - Nosebleed, bright red blood. Nosebleed during cough, headache, every time the patient takes cold. Coryza with stoppage of nose and nausea. Discharge of thin mucus with cough and expectoration. Sneezing. Itching of nose. Loss Ipecacuanha of smell.

Face - Puffed or sunken. One side of face hot, the other cold. Pale, blue about the eyes or lips, white linea nasalis. Redness of the skin around the mouth. Lips blue during chill. Lips covered with small aphthae and eruptions. Rash in the face. Pityriasis. Periodical orbital neuralgias with some lachrymation, photophobia and smarting eyelids. Convulsive startings of the muscles of the face.

Mouth - Mouth moist with much saliva. Saliva increased. Earthy, bitter, sweetish, bloody taste. Smarting pain in mouth and on tongue. Child thrusts its fists into the mouth and screams during dentition.

Throat - Sore throat, as from swelling of the pharynx. Difficult swallowing, as from paralysis of the tongue and of the gullet. Fauces, stinging, rough, sore, and dry. Pressure in throat with pains in diaphragm. Deep red color of tonsils and pharynx. Tickling in upper part of larynx. Croup. Gagging and choking. Spasms of vocal cords. Spasm of glottis, with Ipecacuanha blueness of face and coldness of limbs. Spasmodic contractive sensation in the throat. Hoarseness, especially at end of a cold. Complete aphonia. Voice hollow.

Stomach - Stomach feels relaxed, as if hanging down. Sinking sensation in stomach. Pressing pain in stomach. Indescribable pain and sick feeling in stomach. Violent clutching and cramping pains. Attacks of cramps. Dyspepsia. Gastritis, inveterate cases, not even a drop of water will stay down, continuous gagging. Gastroenteritis. Eructations with rumbling in abdomen. Hiccoughs. Food poisoning. Loss of appetite and frequent nausea. Horrid nausea, not better vomiting. Nausea, copious salivation, violent itching in the skin and empty risings. Constant nausea and vomiting with pale, twitching of face. Incessant retching with vomiting of watery fluids andcutting pain in belly. Vomits blood, bile, food, mucus. grass-green mucus, black matter like pitch. Hematemesis of children. Bilious vomiting. Vomiting with thirst, sweat, and bad breath. Nausea and vomiting with menses, cramps, during pregnancy. Nausea from smell of food, from looking at moving objects, from slightest motion or cough. Retching, especially after drinking anything cold or after smoking. Constant nausea and retching of hysterical women. Vomiting of infants at the breast. Morning vomiting in weakly persons who are affected by worms. Stools - Mucus fetid diarrhea, worse at night. Stools, brown, grass or yellow green, lemon colored. Stools, painless, fermented frothy or bloody, slimy, pitch-like. Stools covered with red, bloody mucus, or lumps of mucus. Stools like frothy molasses with griping at navel. Stools spurting out with much flatus. Stools very offensive, putrid smelling.

Abdomen - Cramps with nausea and vomiting. Flatulent colic with frequent loose stools. Colic of children with diarrhea, restlessness, screaming and tossing about. Cold drinks or ice cream causes colic. Abdominal colic after sour or unripe fruit, beer, etc. Clawing pains as from a hand clawing intestines. Cutting pain worse around the navel. Inguinal hernia. Griping, drawing or cutting pain about the navel. Pinching pain. Sharp pain from navel to uterus. Diaphragm, as if pressed between two stones.

Rectum - Rectal pain so great that it nauseates. Itching at anus. Hemorrhoids bleeding very profusely. Diarrhea after overloading stomach with sweets or fat pastry. Diarrhea from taking cold, due to chill or from emotions. Amoebic dysentery with tenesmus, while straining. Dysentery with head hot and cold legs. Cholera infantum. Beginning cholera infantum, with nausea, vomiting, colic, diarrhea. Autumn diarrhea. Diarrhea of teething children, yellow, white or green discharges. Worm and parasites.

Female - Menses too early and too profuse. Menses with cramps and constant nausea. Scanty menses with great weakness. Menses return every two weeks. Prolapsed uterus worse during menses. Great debility and leucorrhea during intervals of menses. Uterine hemorrhages, profuse, bright red, steady flow or gushing with nausea and gasping with each gush of blood. Pain from navel to uterus. Cutting pain in uterus from left to right. Dragging sensation towards uterus and anus. Nausea and vomiting during pregnancy. Threatened miscarriage, often with sharp or pinching pain around umbilicus. Hemorrhage following labor or after miscarriage. Hemorrhage from placenta previa. Arterial bleeding from partial separation of placenta. Laborpains spasmodic, cutting across from left to right with nausea and clutching about navel. Labor pains running downward. Food - General loss of appetite as from weakness of stomach. Great disgust and loathing of any sort offood. No appetite, earthy taste, stomach feels relaxed, nausea. Nausea from smell of food. Violent hunger when nausea is over. Thirstlessness. No thirst during chill, but much thirst all through fever. Stomach disordered by rich food, pork, pastry, fruits, candy, ice cream. Food poisoning. Desires or adverse to sweets and dainty things. Worse cold drinks, black coffee, sour beer, smoking tobacco. Worse from fats, ice cream, pastry, pork, unripe fruit, salads. Cold drinks or ice-cream causes colic. Cold water worsens spasmodic cough.

Chest - Constant constriction in chest and larynx, worse least motion. Chest seems full of phlegm, but does not yield to coughing. Constitutions - Suited to stout persons of lax tissue, to fair people, to women and children, to emphysematous persons, to persons who have a history of nosebleed or other blood loss. Indicated in fat children and adults who are feeble and catch cold in warm wet weather.

Heart - Pain in heart, followed by dryness of mouth and great thirst. Pulse large and soft. Pulse accelerated but weak, sometimes imperceptible.

Back - Tetanic spasms of back which bends the back backwards or forwards. Pain in back, during urination. Shooting from kidney region into thighs. Cramps between scapulae during motion. Causations - Ill effects of vexation, reserved displeasure. Injuries, loss of blood, suppressed eruptions. Morphine, opium and heroin addictions. Quinine. Foodpoison- ing. Indigestible food, rich food, pork, pastry, fruits, candy, ice cream.

Limbs - Pains in limbs during chill. Numbness, as if joints had gone to sleep. Shocks in limbs on falling asleep. Body stretched stiff, followed by spasmodic jerking of arms towards each other. Pains as if bruised in all the bones and joints. Femur as if dislocated on sitting down. Cold hands and feet. Coldness of one hand, other is hot. Lungs - Cyanosis. Dyspnea with constant constriction in chest. Attacks of difficult shortness of breathing. Gasps for air at open window. Difficult expiration. Sighing. Shortness of breath as from inhaling dust. Suffocative attacks from foreign substance in wind pipe. Threatened suffocation from accumulation of mucus. Asthma with skin disease. Humid asthma from damp or sudden changes in weather. Spasmodic asthma after suppressed eruptions. Croup. Bronchopneumonia. Pneumonia. Bubbling rales. Loose, coarse rattle in chest without expectoration. Suffocative cough, child becomes stiff and blue in the face. Continued sneezing, coryza, wheezing cough. Bleeding from lungs with nausea, feeling of constriction, rattling cough. Hemoptysis from slightest exertion (Mill.).

Sleep - Sleeplessness. Shocks in all limbs on going to sleep (Ign.). Restless, unrefreshing sleep. Eyes half open during sleep with moaning and groaning. Starting during sleep. Loss of sleep that causes nausea and fatigue. Frightful dreams, with frequent starts and terror during sleep. Yawning and stretching.

Skin - Pale, lax. Miliary rash. Erysipelas. Itching, unchanged by scratching. Itching with nausea, scratches until he vomits. Suppressed rash or eruptions. Delayed eruption in scarlatina. Rash in lying-in women. Herpetic eruptions.

Modalities - Better from open air, rest, pressure, closing eyes, cold drinks. Worse from drugs, morphine. Worse after overeating, vomiting, lying down, motion. Worse from mixed or rich foods, ice cream, pork, veal, candy, fruits, berries, raisins, salads, lemon peel. Worse cold, winter, dry weather, warmth, damp, external heat, periodically. Catarrh, asthma andchill are worse in warm, moist wind. Summer heat or hot room causes fainting.

Compare - ( 1 ) Lob., Emetin., Ars., Tab., Cham., Puls., Ant-t., Squil, Conv. - colic and diarrhea. (2) In asthma, Lob., Blatta. (3) Typh. - dysentery, diarrhea and summer complaint. (4) Euph-hy. - very similar to Ipecac. Irritation of the respiratory and gastro-intestinal tracts and female organs. (5) Lip. - persistent dry. hard, bronchial cough-asthmaand chronic bronchitis. Complementary: Cupr., Am. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Teeth - Teeth chatter, with chill. Toothache, with a jerk radiating to temples, better while eating. Toothache in a hollow tooth as if it would be torn out.

Tongue - Tongue clean, not coated.Tongue. dry, yellow, white, pale. Red, pointed tongue. Tongue coated in middle, edges red. Flat taste, with white, thickly coated tongue. Smarting pain on tongue. Vertigo - Vertigo with tottering and staggering. Vertigo when walking, when turning around, during pregnancy. Vision - Obscuration of vision. State of vision constantly changing. Blue and red halo around light. Optical illusions in bright colors. Spasm of accommodation from weakness of ciliary muscle. COMMENTS - The stomach disgust of the remedy is depicted on the countenance, which expresses nausea. Sickly, disgusted appearance. The corners of the mouth are drawn down. Blue rings around the eyes. Deathly nausea (Tab.). Constant nausea, not ameliorated by vomiting. Can vomit blood. Salivation and vomiting of white, stringy mucus. Vomiting can lead to shudders with a chill, severe spasms, convulsions. Can be sleepy after vomiting. Desire for fresh air, thirstless while nauseas (Puls.).Any condition with concomitant nausea and vomiting. Vomiting after pregnancy. Sensation as if the stomach is hanging down (Sep.). Corresponding mental state, “moroseness and contempt for everything,” “disdainful humor.” Irritability in adults, crying and screaminginchildren. Restless and exhausted (Ars.). Disgust. Sensitiveness (Chin.), over sensitive to heat and cold. Better by touch. Exhaustion and an achy, bruised feeling. Sore pain in the shoulder blades. Bone pains in the head and elsewhere. Pains as if bones were all tom to pieces. Keynote cutting pains in the left side of the abdomen over to the right. Peripheral neuritis. Generally a left sided remedy. Intermittent headaches. Migraine headaches. Bruised feeling, severe prostration. Headache “as if bruised, all through the bones of the head and down into the root of the tongue.” Pain extending to roots of teeth. Headache with nausea. Gastric headache, originating in the stomach, nausea precedes the headache and persists throughout. Desire to lie perfectly still. Meningitis with vomiting and a high fever. Tetanus, lockjaw with severe spasms and retching. Marked periodic action. Intermittent fevers (Eup-per.). Characteristic nausea through all the stages. Stages can be completely mixed up, short chill, followed by long fever. Can have a pain in the upper back between the shoulder blades with fever (Gel. has a chill). Violent dyspnea with wheezing and great weight and anxiety about the précordia. Threatened suffocation from accumulation of mucus. Loss of breath, pale, stiff and blue. Strangling with gagging and vomiting of mucus, bleeding from nose or mouth. Coughing up mucus, gagging. Must stand by the window to get oxygen. Worse damp weather and changes in weather. Pneumonia and bronchitis with severe shortness of breath with rattling mucus (Ant-t.). For bronchitis in infants with coarse rattling in the chest. Concomitant respiratory and gastric symptoms. For emphysema in theelderly. Suffocative respiration (Spong.), but wet. Asthma with a breathless feeling, nausea and vomiting, with thick, yellow mucus (Lob., Ars., Ant-t., Ant-c.). Dry, spasmodic, constricted, asthmatic cough. Whooping cough. Characteristic spasmodic rigidity in whooping cough. Sub-acute inflammation of the cornea with intense pain. Pustular conjunctivitis, especially in children. Inflammation with tearing pain and gushing of tears. Photophobia. Violent neuralgia of eyeballs, shooting in the head with gushes of tears, nausea, etc. Hemorrhage with bright, red blood (Phos.). Gushing blood, with sinking feeling and nausea (Ferr. is weak and flushed with gushing). Nosebleeds with a sensation of nausea and sinking, or nosebleeds from coughing and sneezing attacks. Uterine hemorrhage. Threatened miscarriage, with a sharp pain around the umbilicus, running downward to the uterus. Miscarriage due to spasmodic vomiting. Spotting blood before contractions. Hemorrhage after childbirth with bright red blood, nausea, disgust and weakness. Metrorrhagia after confinement with a low pulse, nausea. Steady flow of bright red blood, which may soak through the bed to the floor or may run over the foot of the bed. Constant nausea and discharge of blood before the proper period. Menstrual cramps with nausea and vomiting, must lie still in bed. Copious menses. Bloody diarrhea associated with nausea and vomiting. Constant urge to stool, tenesmus. Stools can be bloody, burning, offensive, watery. Severe colic that is associated with dysentery. Suppressed skin eruptions that go to the stomach and bowels and cause severe colic. Stomach symptoms worse from ice cream, pork, and rich, fatty foods (Puls.). Bad taste in the mouth. The thought, smell or idea of food causes patient to gag and choke. Anorexia. Heroin withdrawal symptoms. J. R. Haynes used Ip. as an antidote to the opium and morphine addiction. He gave five drops of Ip. tincture for every grain of morphine, or its equivalent in heroin or opium, which the patient has been accustomed to take. Jahr recommended that in all cases of intermittents in which no other remedy is particularly indicated Ip. should be given. It will either cure the case or bring out more indications for another remedy. Clarke frequently found this advice useful. As most intermittents have been treated with quinine, it is thought the antidotal properties of Ip. may have good effects. Allen noted that Ip. dilutions have helped granulations of the eyelids. Cooper cured an immense uterine fibroid with persistent painful irritation of the skin. There was constant retching and vomiting, made worse by eating. Vaginal irritation with thick leucorrhea and a feeling of desperation. Dr. Nancy T. Williams cured several cases of gallstone colic on the symptom “external chilliness with internal heat,” with Ip. 6c. The relief was prompt and lasting. Dr. Edwin Muskett noted its specific use for malignant pustule and anthrax, used locally and internally. Hahnemann considered it a short-acting medicine. RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Am., Ars., Chin., Copperfumes. Dulc., Ferr., Laur., Op.. Sul-ac., Tab., Ant-t.

Kidneys - Shooting pain from kidney, down the thighs to the knees. Ineffectual urging to urinate. Burning in urethra during urination. Red, scanty urine. Urine turbid, with red sediment. Hematuria with nausea and cutting in abdomen and urethra, with oppression in chest and short breath.

Cough - Suffocative, paroxysmal cough. Cough incessant and violent with every breath. Cough with nausea and vomiting, or vomiting without nausea. Dry cough caused by tickling in upper part of lar- ynx. Dry, spasmodic cough, after coryza. Cough producing sonorous and bubbling rales. Suffocative, strangling cough with much mucus accumulated in bronchia. Henjoptysis. Cough with spitting of blood, worse from least effort. Cough during fever. Whooping cough with nosebleed and bleeding from mouth. Child becomes stiff and blue or red in face, stiffens out with cough. Cough in teething children. Dry, spasmodic coughs of elderly persons, coming on in fits.

Perspiration - Cold, clammy. Hands and feet drip cold sweat. Very profuse sweats, mostly during night. Sweats with redness of one cheek and paleness of the other. Hot sweats, sudden attacks in room. Sour sweat with turbid urine. Sweat stains yellow. Profuse perspiration after quinine.

Temperature - Chill alternating with heat. Short chill with long heat. Internal chill, with external heat. Chill and much heat, nausea, vomiting, and dyspnea. Chill with nausea, vomiting, great lassitude, weariness, oppression of the chest. Chills, up and down back. Coldness of upper part of body. Anxious dry heat in evening. Heat with or without thirst. Fever with nausea and vomiting. Catarrhal or gastric fevers. Intermittent fever, irregularcases after quinine. Infantile remittent fever. Suppressed of mixed intermittents, nausea in all stages. Relapses with improper diet.

name: Ipomoea Purpurea
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from lying down. Worse in the morning, at night, from fatty foods..
constitution: Anorexia. Backache. Bilious, vomiting. Catatonia.Cholecystitis. Delirium. Epilepsy. Fever. Flatulence. Headache. Insomnia. Jaundice. Kidney, colic. Kidney, disorders. Worms.
keynote:
PHARMACY - ipom. Ipomoea purpurea. Morning glory. Convolvulus duartinus. Bind-weed. N. O. Convulvulaceae, family. The mother tincture is prepared from the dried bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anorexia. Backache. Bilious, vomiting.…
full:
PHARMACY - ipom. Ipomoea purpurea. Morning glory. Convolvulus duartinus. Bind-weed. N. O. Convulvulaceae, family. The mother tincture is prepared from the dried bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anorexia. Backache. Bilious, vomiting. Catatonia.Cholecystitis. Delirium. Epilepsy. Fever. Flatulence. Headache. Insomnia. Jaundice. Kidney, colic. Kidney, disorders. Worms.

HOMEOPATHIC - Ipomoea is used solely as a drastic purgative in allopathic medicine; not one homeopathic treatise mentions it as a remedy for constipation. Castro carried out a proving in 1940, using the potencies lx, 2x, 3x, at the rate of 1-200 drops per day in progressive doses. Symptoms included fever, agitation and mental confusion. Delirium with hallucinations, excitability, and mumbling. Predominant irritation of the brain. Epilepsy. Catatonia. Insomnia and delirious dreams. Neuromuscular and arthritic pains. Aching in top of right shoulder, in small of back Ipomoea purpurea and limbs. Pain in left lumbar muscles on stooping. Kidney disorders with pain in back. Kidney colic. Much abdominal flatulence. Bilious vomiting. MIND - Desire for solitude. Sadness, tears, hypersensitive to noise. Intense anxiety with palpitations. Prostration. Loss of memory. Delirious dreams. Nocturnal terror in children, especially in the worm-ridden.

Head - Great heaviness of head. Headache first in right, then in left temple. Headache with a unilateral perspiration. Itching of scalp.

Eyes - Smarting pain in eyes. Itching of internal canthus of left eye. Pupils dilated. Food - Anorexia. Aggravated by and aversion to fatty foods, meat and milk.

Ears - Buzzing noise in ears.

Nose - Smarting and dryness in nostrils. Purulent discharge from nose. Very acute sense of smell.

Mouth - Mouth discolored, with a bad taste. Feeling of swallowing his tongue.

Throat - Pain in left tonsil. Throat dry, constant need to swallow, but swallowing difficult. Vertigo - Vertigo with nausea, ameliorated by lying down. RELATIONS - Compare: (1 ) Cresol. (2) Stram. - hallucinations, delirium with talkativeness. (3) Hyos. - delirium, strips himself. (4) Agar. - muscular jerks in the lower limbs. (5) Nux- v. - abdominal distention, neuromuscular over excitability. REFERENCES - Boericke. Julian.

Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Hiccoughs, thirsty for cold water. Yellow-green vomiting.

Abdomen - Abdomen distended. Sharp cutting pain in abdomen above umbilicus. Rumbling and grumbling in epigastric region and lower bowels. Rumbling of flatus with pain in the colon. Sensation of heat in the epigastrium before passing stools. Cholecystitis. Biliary sycosis syndrome.

Rectum - Rectal tenesmus. Stools soft, orange-yellow in color.

Chest - Thoracic spasms. Feeling of laryngeal and pectoral constriction. Constitutions - Suited to neuro-bilious, hypersensitive types, prone to epileptiform fits. Useful for phospho- fluoric types, syphilitic.

Heart - Palpitations with anxiety and hysterical spasms. Pulse accelerated with extra systole.

Back - Heaviness of the back and neck, aggravated at night, on going to bed. Pain, aching in lumbar region. Pain in first dorsal vertebrae. Itching over left scapula.

Limbs - Limbs cold, sweating, heavy. Joints painful. Muscular spasms with fatigue. Pain in the left lumbar muscles on bending down. Aching in top of right shoulder. Pain in left shoulder and arm. Lungs - Irregular breathing. Disposition to cough with sneezing.

Sleep - Nocturnal aggravation, forcing him to get up.

Skin - Skin discolored, yellow, dry, despite cold sweating. Viral jaundice.

Modalities - Better from lying down. Worse in the morning, at night, from fatty foods.

Kidneys - Severe pain in left kidney with nausea and occasional vomiting. Kidney pain spreading towards the left ureter. Kidney stones. Kidney disorders or gravel with pain in back. Kidney colic, predominantly on the left side.

Temperature - Chilliness alternating with backache. Flushes of heat, followed by copious sweat. General fever with total insomnia, cold sweats and contracture of the jaw muscles.

name: Iridium Metallicum
author: Murphy
constitution: Abscesses. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Axilla, abscess. Bronchitis. Cancer. Cerebral, hemorrhage. Cramps. Eczema. Epilepsy. Exhaustion. Gout. Headache. Heart, disorders. Hemiplegia. Lupus. Multiple sclerosis. Nephritis. Neuralgias. Numbness. Paralysis. Parkinson's disease. Rheumatism. Septicemia. Spinal, paresis. Trembling. Urticaria. Uterine, tumors. Weakness.
keynote:
PHARMACY - irid. Iridiummetallicum. Iridium metal. At. Wt. 193.10. Trituration. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscesses. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Axilla, abscess. Bronchitis. Cancer. Cerebral, hemorrhage. Cramps. Eczema. Epilepsy. Exhaustion. Gout.…
full:
PHARMACY - irid. Iridiummetallicum. Iridium metal. At. Wt. 193.10. Trituration. Historical dose: Trituration and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscesses. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Axilla, abscess. Bronchitis. Cancer. Cerebral, hemorrhage. Cramps. Eczema. Epilepsy. Exhaustion. Gout. Headache. Heart, disorders. Hemiplegia. Lupus. Multiple sclerosis. Nephritis. Neuralgias. Numbness. Paralysis. Parkinson's disease. Rheumatism. Septicemia. Spinal, paresis. Trembling. Urticaria. Uterine, tumors. Weakness.

HOMEOPATHIC - Iridium is a rare metal of the platinum group, found in platinum ore. It is one of the heaviest known substances. It shares with Osm., Pall, and Plat, a place in the treatment of rheumatism and gout. Boring, contracting pains. Sensations of being swollen, blown up, heavy, full. Shocks and twitching. Epilepsy, clonic, tonic, tetanic. Spinal paresis. Numbness and paralysis. Trembling. Parkinson's disease. Multiple sclerosis. Lupus. Anemia with decreased red corpuscles. Exhaustion after disease. Weakness, nervousness and restlessness. Weakness after influenza. Cerebral hemorrhage. Congestion of blood. Affections of bones, necrosis and inflammation. Abscesses. Septicemia. Intestinal putrefaction. Trypanosoma infections. Glands swollen, inflamed, indurated. Problems with testes and ovaries, inflammations, cancer, cryptorchism. Uterine tumors. Sterility, amenorrhea, metrorrhagia. Nephritis of pregnancy. Children who are puny, weak- limbs and grow too fast. MIND - Facilitates mental labor. Forgetful. Difficult concentration. Sensation as if mind were void. Confusion, loses his way in well-known streets. Feeling of self confidence. Anxiety on waking, as if something bad is going to happen. Clinging to persons. Bites nails. Averse to being disturbed. Irritability from noise. Weeping after anger. Sadness, better walking in open air.

Head - Right side of scalp sensitive. “Wooden” feeling in right side of head. Heaviness of head like liquid lead. Swashing sensation. Numbness in occiput. Pains in middle of occipital bone. Open air and noise seem to bruise the head. Pain, like cold metal pressing across forehead. Neuralgia of head especially temples, drives one crazy.

Eyes - Eyes red, heavy. Eye inflammations. Itching in morning on waking. Desire to close the eyes. Feeling as if eyes were being affected from below upward. Ingrown eyelashes. Far sighted. Visual disturbances.

Ears - Feeling of numbness in ears and throughout the body lasting a short time. Heat of ears when lying down. Sounds seem distant.

Nose - Posterior sinuses feel raw inflamed. Bridge of nose painful, feels too narrow. Profuse, watery coryza, better indoors. Ozaena. Profuse, thick, yellowish discharge. Vision - Colors look brighter. Everything looks golden. Zigzags, in shape of circle. COMMENTS - A. J. Tafel took 20 grains of the 3c trituration. He experienced a number of symptoms, all within two hours of taking the dose. Prominent among them were a sensation of numbness in ears and throughout the body. A feeling as if they eyes were being affected from below upward. A feeling as of a triangle in face, the based formed by the two malar bones, the apex in the vertex. Cramp-like contractions in the right calf. The majority of symptoms appeared on the left side. Laboucher said it is “admirable in all cases of anemia.” He claimed it was better than Chin, for the aged and persons exhausted by disease, for puny, weak-limbed children and for those who grow too fast. He mentioned a particular alternation of symptoms or reaction. Painful weakness of lower limbs and kidney region, followed by a favorable reaction, self confidence and facilitated mental labor. Laboucher gave Irid. in the 4c potency, Pall, in the 3c, Plat, in 2c and Osm. in the 1c. He said Irid. is superior to Pall., Plat, and to Osm. in uterine tumors. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Plat, Pall., Osm.. (2) In uterine diseases, Aur. and Aur-mur. (3) In exhaustion after disease, Chin. Irid-m. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Face - Face swollen. Sensation of swelling in morning on rising. Sensation of elongation of left side of face. Numbness of lips. Stinging pain in the left malar bone. Pain, pressure in right malar bone. Animated expression.

Mouth - Increased saliva, with sensation in malar bones, which is more perceptible on left side. One-sided white discoloration of tongue.

Stomach - Cramps in stomach.

Abdomen - Dragging pain as if menses would come in abdomen.

Female - Swelling of ovaries without dropsy. Corroding and suppurating ulcers of uterus, bluish patches on uterus. Uterine tumors with suppuration. Sterility. Amenorrhea, metrorrhagia. Food - Desire for carbonated drinks. Aversion to brown bread. Worse from cold drinks, oranges.

Chest - Sensation of iron band around chest.

Heart - High blood pressure. Heart weakness, infarction. Heart failure, pain. Pulse, too fast, too slow, full, weak, irregular. Sensation as if an iron rod is standing straight in the heart region.

Back - Spinal paresis, especially for the aged and after disease. Weariness in back and limbs. Weakness of cervical region, as if it could not support weight of head. Breasts - Piercing, gnawing pains in breasts.

Limbs - Neuralgia of the limbs. Dislocated feeling in left hip joint and dull pain toward left gluteal region. Pressing in groin and left thigh. Tension in both thighs, especially left. Achilles tendon painful, aggravated by walking. Achilles tendon torn from jumping. Lungs - Difficulty breathing deeply. Short of breath, aggravated from climbing the stairs. Hoarse cough, worse talking. Profuse, thick, yellowish discharge. Chronic laryngeal catarrh.

Kidneys - Weakness in kidney region. Nephritis during pregnancy.

HOMEOPATHIC - Irid-m. produces salivation and stiffness of the jaws followed by head and nervous symptoms. Congestion of sinuses and bronchials. Headache worse right side, heavy feeling as of liquid lead. Dragging pain in lower back. REFERENCES - Boericke.

HOMEOPATHIC - Iris-fl. gives an odor of violets to the…
full:
PHARMACY - iris-fl. Iris florentina. Orris root. White flag. N. O. Iridaceae. Tincture of fresh rhizome. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Convulsions. Delirium. Diarrhea. Headache. Hemiplegia (r.).

HOMEOPATHIC - Iris-fl. gives an odor of violets to the breath and communicates to vinegar a flavor of raspberries, hence is used in the manufacture of raspberry vinegar. Powdered orris root has been used as an application to the hair and in some young girls has produced violent symptoms. Headaches and giddiness occurred on waking in the morning. Complete paralysis of the right side. In one case, convulsions and delirium from which complete recovery did not take place for three months. 1ELATIONS - Compare: (1) Verat., Sabad., Iris. REFERENCES Clarke.

full:
FARMACY - iris-foe. Iris foetidissima. N. O. Iridaceae. Tincture of root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Headaches. Hernia.

HOMEOPATHIC - Iris-foe. was proved under 3erridge's direction. One prover, Dr. Crocker, :hewed a piece of the root, another took the tincture, one experienced symptoms from potentizing the drug and later the 14c dilution. The rest took very high potencies. The prover who chewed the root experienced a burning feeling in mouth and fauces extending to stomach, not relieved by cold water or anything else. A number of pains were felt in the head. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) The arums and the other irises. REFERENCES-Clarke.

name: Iris Tenax
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Sweet oil and camphor ameliorates burning in mouth and throat. Worse by sucking in cold air, (burning in mouth and throat). Hot applications aggravates pain in bowels. Cup of tea aggravates vomiting. Worse on waking. COMMENTS - Dr. Wigg, age 44, took 5 drops to lx of the strong tincture. A female prover took repeated doses of Iris-t. 2x and 3x. The order in which the symptoms occurred in Dr. Wigg's case is roughly as follows: In the first fifteen minutes, there was burning in the mouth and throat. This passed off in the night, but was intensified by each fresh dose. After the second dose, taken early the next morning, the burning was reproduced, followed two hours later by dry mouth and absence of saliva. This was followed by a mental gloom and homesick feeling, increasing towards midnight. Headache in temples. Itching and burning of the scalp. Toothache. Sinking, all gone feeling. Abdominal pains, diarrhea. Desperate exhaustion compelling him to keep in bed. Hard chill followed by rise of temperature. Wigg noticed the all-gone feeling particularly on standing up, on walking in the morning. Cold water did not improve the burning in mouth and throat. A cold pillow improved pain in the temples. The acute pains in the bowels passed off in the night, but for fourteen days there was a tender spot over the ileo-cecal region and the bowels did not act normally for ten days. In the female prover, it produced a strange sensation in her mind: she though some of her friends had died, the next day she was unusually cheerful. The most remarkable symptoms were the “fearful pain in the ileo-cecal region and the hard chill at 2 p.m.” These indications led to the cure in the two following cases: The first case concerned Miss A., a schoolteacher, who had for several years a pain beginning in right eye, extending to the right half of her head. When the pain was most severe, she vomited a quantity of green bile. When she did not vomit she had nausea and chill between 2 and 3 p.m. The pain passed off in sleep at night. It always began on Saturday, before rising. Iris-t. 30x every six hours commencing on Friday morning, was given and quickly cured after Iris., Aloe, Cimic. and Kali-bi. had failed to give much relief. The relief from Iris-t. was so marked the patient thought she had received morphine. The second case concerned Mr. E., who drank a large quantity of buttermilk while in a state of perspiration after walking thirty miles over a mountainous country in August. Four hours after, he was taken with fearful pain in ileo-cecal region. This caused a deathly sensation at his epigastrium. Finally he vomited much dark green bile without relief. An old school doctor was called in and diagnosed obstruction with probable death in four days. He lingered three weeks and was brought home to Portland where Dr. Wigg saw him and diagnosed typhilitis, badly treated. Pressure on the ileo-cecal region caused the death like sensation at stomach pit. Pain continued until he vomited a cupful of dark green bile. He was somewhat constipated. Under Iris-t. 15x every three hours he commenced to improve at once and in two weeks was back at his business. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Effect on cecal region - Am., Ars., Lach., Sil. (2) Headache - Gels., Grat., Iris., Kali-bi., Ign. (3) Burning not worse by cold, Caps. (4) Homesickness - Caps., Ph-ac. REFERENCES - Clarke..

Pain in one tooth only. Itching and burning of scalp without eruption. Chill at 2 p.m. Painful spot in ileo-cecal region. Bilious vomiting, burning sensations (Iris.). Deathly sensation at point of stomach. Appendicitis. Gloomy, cast- down, homesick feeling. MIND - Gloomy, cast-down, homesick feeling.

Abdomen - Appendicitis. Pain in ileo-cecal region. Pains from adhesions after surgery.

author: Murphy

keynote:
PHARMACY - iris. Iris versicolor. Blue flag. Iris hexona. N. O. Iridaceae. Tincture of fresh root collected in early spring or autumn. Trituration of the resinoid. Irin or Irisin. Historical dose: Trituration, tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Cholera. Colic. Diabetes.…
full:
PHARMACY - iris. Iris versicolor. Blue flag. Iris hexona. N. O. Iridaceae. Tincture of fresh root collected in early spring or autumn. Trituration of the resinoid. Irin or Irisin. Historical dose: Trituration, tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Cholera. Colic. Diabetes. Goiter. Headaches. Indigestion. Leucorrhea. Migraines. Morning sickness. Nausea. Neuralgia. Pancreas, disorders. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Thyroid, disorders. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sick headaches. Gastric or hepatic sick headaches with blur before the eyes at the beginning. Migraine headaches. Great nausea and vomiting. Vomiting sour or bitter substances, excoriates the throat. Vomiting of stringy, glairy, ropy mucus, hangs in strings down to receptacle on the floor. Burning of mouth, tongue, and throat, can go into stomach, even the anus if there is diarrhea. Affinity for the digestive tract, gastro-intestinal mucus membranes, thyroid, pancreas, and salivary glands. Liver and pancreas affected, producing profuse secretions, which are sour, acrid and burning. Increases the flow of bile. Oily nose, greasy taste and fatty stools. Cholera infantum and cholera morbus. Symptoms set in suddenly, with a rapid elimination. MIND - Mental depression. Despondency. Low- spirited. Dullness of mental faculties. Weak memory. Inability to fix the mind on any subject. Wandering thoughts while writing. Muttering. Laughs at own actions. Ill humor. Censorious. Easily vexed. Irritable mood, disposed to find fault, particularly in morning. Restlessness at night. Nervous fretfulness. General appearance of anguish. Fear of approaching illness.

Head - Dullness of the head. Chronic pain in forehead. Dull throbbing or shooting pains in right side of forehead. Tired headache from mental exhaustion (studying, sewing), worse coughing, cold air, better gentle motion. Headache begins with blurring of vision, after relaxing from a mental strain. Frontal headache over left eye with nausea. Headache alternating sides. Headache as if a band around head. Severe pains, through temples and over eyes, with vertigo, nausea and vomiting. Shooting pain in temples with contractive feeling of the scalp. Scalp feels constricted. Sick headaches with diarrhea, in bilious subjects, worse rest, begins with a blur before eyes. Reflex headache from acid stomach or irritation of stomach from acid secretion. Neuralgic pain usually begins over one eye. Neuralgic pain, one-sided, with gastric symptoms. Right temples affected. Pustular eruption on scalp. Scabs, yellow matter oozing from under crust, with matted hair.

Eyes - Sunken with blue circles. Redness of conjunctiva. Inflammation of eyelids, from cold. Burning in internal canthus. Violent supra-orbital pains. Periodic visual disturbances, blindness, hemiopia. with headache.

Ears - Roaring, buzzing. Ringing in ears with deafness. Aural vertigo with intense noises in ears.

Nose - Oily. Constant sneezing.

Face - General appearance of anguish. Pustular eruptions on face, around nose, lips and cheeks, secreting a bloody, irritating matter. Dry, cracked lips. Neuralgia after breakfast, beginning in infra-orbital nerve and involving whole face. Neuralgic pains in right side of face.

Mouth - Burning in mouth and fauces as if on fire. Feels greasy, burnt or scalded. Stomatitis, with burning pain in mouth and fauces. Tongue burns or feels cold. Greasy or sweetish taste. Flat taste. Loss of taste. Profuse flow of saliva (Merc., IP., Kali-i.).Ropy saliva, drops when talking. Profuse salivation during headache. Salivation after diphtheria, with swelling of parotids. Saliva tastes greasy, slimy. Mouth and tongue feel scalded. Slight toothache in a warm room. Ulcers on mucus membranes of cheeks.

Throat - Heat and smarting in throat. Burning from fauces to stomach, better inhaling cool air or drinking cold water. Shooting pains in tonsils extends to ears. Vomit excoriates throat. Thyroid disorders. Goiter. Vertigo - Aural vertigo with intense noises in ears. Immediate dizziness with pressure in forehead. Slight giddiness, coming on suddenly while walking within doors. COMMENTS - Migraine headaches, worse on the left side, over the left eye (Thuj.. Anae.). Sick headaches, associated with dietary allergies. Sensation of a nail over the left eye, pain as if being driven into supraorbital arch (Thuj., Sang, on right). Constipation preceding the migraine (Bry.). Buzzing and ringing in the ears associated with the headaches. Affinity for the pancreas (Spong., Con., Phos.). Diabetes. Characteristic burning. Stomach troubles accompanied by burning of tongue, throat, esophagus and stomach, and burning of the anus if diarrhea is present. Nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation. The vomiting is not always sour, but may be bitter or sweetish. Profuse saliva. Vomit or saliva may be white, stringy, or ropy (Ip.). Nash once had a case of stomach trouble in a middle-aged woman. She had frequent attacks, vomiting a stringy, glairy mucus which was very ropy. The vomit would hang in strings from her mouth to the receptacle on the floor. Then the vomit became dark colored, like coffee, she became very weak, vomited all nourishment. She al so had profuse secretion of ropy saliva. Thinking she had cancer of the stomach, she made her will and set her house in order to die. Kali-bi. was given with no benefit, but Iris cured her completely in a short time and she remained well. RELATIONS -Antidote: Nux-v. Compare: ( 1 ) Iris-fl. - delirium, convulsions and paralysis. (2) Iris-fa. - headache and hernia. (3) Iris-g. - Blue Garden Iris - dropsy and freckles. (4) Pancreat. (5) Pep. (6) Ip., Podo., Sanguin., Ars., Ant-c. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Nash. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Burning of whole alimentary canal, not better by cold drinks. Burning distress in stomach and pancreas, with watery diarrhea and great prostration. Sour, bitter belchings. Continuous nausea. Nausea from riding, overexertion. Vomiting with burningpain. Vomiting of sweetish water, sour, bloody, bile. Bitter, acrid, watery, sour vomiting. Vomiting during headache. Periodic vomiting spells, every month, six weeks, lasts for two or three days. Protracted nausea and vomiting during pregnancy. Vomiting of sour milk in children.

Abdomen - Cutting pain. Burning in epigastric region, with tenderness, vomiting of food. Awful burning in region ofpancreas. Sharp griping pains in the bowels. Flatulent colic. Colicky pain before each spell of vomiting and purging. Colic, better by bending forward, better by discharge of flatulence. Pain in the abdomen, better by discharge of flatus.

Rectum - Acute mucus enteritis. Constipation with gastric derangement. Constipation succeeded by thin, watery diarrhea. Sudden attacks of diarrhea. Painless cholera morbus. Periodical night diarrhea with pain and green discharges. Summer diarrhea occurring in hottest part of season. Urging to stools with headache, facial neuralgia and pain in teeth. Burning at anus during stool. Burning after stool. Anus feels sore as if sharp points sticking in it. Distressed feeling as if rectum is prolapsed. Hemorrhoids.

Male - Coldness and itching of parts. Coldness and relaxation of scrotum. Excitement of genitals reflex from excessively acid stomach. Nocturnal emissions with amorous dreams. Secondary gonorrhea or gleet.

Female - Neuralgia and rheumatism of uterus. Menses regular, but excessive. Leucorrhea. Morning sickness of pregnancy, vomits sour or bitter, with protracted nausea, profuse ropy saliva, tenderness over stomach. Food - Hunger with inability to eat. Loss of taste and appetite. Bitter, putrid taste. Nausea and empty belchings, from irregularities of diet. Chronic indigestion of milk. Intense and urgent thirst during diarrhea.

Chest - Rheumatism in muscles of chest, with acid indigestion. Cutting pain in left side as if ribs were pressing against lung.

Heart - Accelerated pulse.

Back - Stiffness in the back, increasing on sitting down. Crampy, in right lumbar region.

Limbs - Sharp tearing, shifting, in joints. Shooting, laming pains along limb. Sciatica, as if left hip joint were wrenched. Pain extends to popliteal space. Gonorrheal rheumatism.

Sleep - Sleeplessness. Starting in sleep. Stools - Stools watery, with burning at anus and through intestinal canal. Stools, bilious, acrid, watery, burn like fire. Stools thin, tinged with bile, copious, in a continuous stream. Stools, green, undigested, mushy, pappy with fetid flatus. Stools, fatty, fetid or coppery smelling.

Skin - Great itching at night. Fine eruption, showing black points after scratching. Eczema with nightly itching. Herpes zoster and gastric derangements. Psoriasis, irregular patches with shining scales. Psoriasis on knees, elbows and body. Pustular eruptions on scalp and face, around mouth.

Modalities - Better from gentle, continued motion. Worse in evening, night, after midnight, 2 a.m. to 3 a.m. Worse from mental exhaustion, rest, hot weather. Worse periodically, weekly, spring and autumn.

Liver - Liver sore. Pain in the region of the liver, worse from motion.

Kidneys - Burning along the length of urethra after urination. Cutting and pricking pain in urethra while urinating. Urine very high colored and scanty. Profuse, clear urine with headache. Diabetes.

Cough - Dry cough caused by tickling in larynx with a dry, smarting or burning sensation in throat.

Perspiration - Perspiration over the whole body, but principally in the hypochondria. Sweat smells of vinegar.

Temperature - Chills with sleepiness. Chilliness during the whole night. Chills over whole body, even when well covered. Head and face cold. Fever followed by chill, with cold hands and feet. Bilious and typhoid fevers. Fever with muttering delirium and bilious diarrhea.

CLINICAL - Ears, noises. Hernia. Muscae, volitantes. Stiff-neck. Toothache. Vulvitis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Itu is one of the remedies proved by Mure. All he tells about the source of it is that “This resin, which comes to us from the province of St. Paul is used empirically for hernia.” Symptoms include a sudden report in the ear, with frightful pain extending to teeth for several minutes, repeated as many as eight times in a day, profuse sweat after the reports. Earache when the least dampness sets in. Toothache worse after a cold drink. Chilliness at hypogastrium, especially in evening. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - jab. Jaborandi. Pilocarpus jaborandi. Pilocarpus pennatifolius aut mi- crophyllus. The alkaloid is pilocarpine. N. O. Rutaceae. Tincture of fresh leaves. Tincture of dried leaves and stems. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies, third potency.

CLINICAL - Alopecia. Asthenopia. Baldness. Bronchitis. Burns. Cataract. Ciliary, spasm. Diarrhea. Dysmenorrhea. Erysipelas. Exophthalmic, goiter. Eye. disorders, Eye, surgery. Eye-strain. Gland, disorders. Glaucoma. Hair, loss. Heart, disorders. Hot, flushings. Hypermetropia. Leucorrhea. Menopause. Miliaria. Mumps. Nightsweats. Perspiration, excessive. Pregnancy, salivation. Salivation, excessive. Scalds. Snakebites. Strabismus. Tuberculosis. Worms.

HERBAL - Jaborandi is a South American tree growing up to twenty feet high. It is used by South American natives as an antidote to snakebites of the Trigonocephalus group.

HOMEOPATHIC - A few minutes after a dose of Jab., the face, ears and neck become deeply flushed and drops of perspiration break out all over the body, the mouth waters and saliva pours out in an almost continuous stream. A single dose often produces enormous amounts of sweat and saliva, not infrequently half a pint. The observation of its action on the skin and salivary glands led to extensive provings. A powerful glandular stimulant, it produces hypersecretion from upper respiratory tract and salivary glands. Increases lachrymal, nasal, bronchial and intestinal secretions to a lesser degree. Abnormal sweats, perspiration, salivation . Heavy night sweats, hot flushes. Night sweats of tuberculosis patients. Sweat only on the left side, dry on the right. Drawing pain in joints during perspiration. Exophthalmic goiter with increased heart’s action and pulsation of arteries, tremors and nervousness, heat and sweating, bronchial irritation. Acts upon the thyroid and its sudorific action may be due to it. Limits the duration of mumps. Mumps when metastasized to the testes, causing infertility, metastasized to the breasts. Never well since mumps (Morbill., Parot.). Pronounced action in the eyes, it has been found to be useful in many conditions of eye weakness, especially hypermetropia, ciliary spasm, convergent strabismus and after operations for strabismus. Mydriatic properties. Miosis. Glaucoma. Headaches, more on the left side. Headaches worse at noon every day. Pains appear gradually and disappear gradually. Symptoms are generally more on the left. Kidney disease, especially with uremia, eliminating both water and urea. Nausea. Stomach distress, better from eating. Scarlatinal dropsy. Contra-indicated in heart failure, in post-puerperal uremia, and in senile cases. MIND - Mental confusion. Dullness of mind. Cheerfulness, gaiety. Very nervous and tremulous. Disinclination to speak. Desire to kill loved ones. Fixed idea that she will murder all her family with a hatchet.

Head - Empty, hollow sensation in head. Headache every day about noon. Headache from straining eyes. Headache with smarting and pain in eyeballs. Pulsating in temporal vessels, at vertex. Throbbing pain in vertex and front of head. Pain in lower part of occiput. Light hair turns black. Baldness.

Eyes - Tension in eyes. Pupils contracted, do not react to light. Glaucoma. Atrophic choroiditis. Vitreous opacities. Eyestrain from whatever cause (Ruta.). Eye pain from exertion of vision atfine work. Eyes easily tire from slightest use. Sensation of heat and burning in eyes during exertion. Smarting pain in eyes. Lachrymation during coryza, headache. Irritation from electric or other artificial light. Staring eyes. Irritability of the ciliary muscle. Periodic strabismus. Spasms of the accommodation while reading. Near-sighted. Hyperopia. Exophthalmos, protrusion of eyes. Squints, convergent after surgery. Lids twitch.

Ears - Serous exudation into tympanic cavity. Tinnitus. Nervous deafness, better in noise. Noises and vertigo.

Nose - Copious nasal discharge. Coryza and perspiration (Merc.).

Face - Redness of face and of ears. Pallor with heat of face and throbbing of temporal arteries. Mumps, especially when metastasis to the testes. Inflammation of parotid gland.

Mouth - Tension in salivary glands. Profuse salivation with profuse sweating, with dry skin. Saliva viscid like egg white, or stringy but not viscid. Constant spitting of alkaline saliva. Saliva contained a notable quantity of urea. Salivation during pregnancy. Dryness of mouth.

Throat - Exophthalmic goiter with increased heart's action, pulsation in arteries, tremors and nervousness. Swelling of submaxillary glands (Merc., Calc.). Dryness at back of throat. Soreness and smarting of throat. Vertigo - Headache with vertigo. Vertigo with nausea after exertion of vision. Vertigo as if head were too light, on moving or looking at objects. Vision - White spots before eyes. Everything at a distance appears hazy. Vision becomes indistinct every few moments. Focal distance changes while reading. Dim vision, better looking sideways (Chin-s.). Retinal images retained long after using eyes. COMMENTS - Sandesberg noticed that the internal use of Jab. and pilocarpine in cases of detached retina and choroiditis seemed to occasion opacity of the crystalline lens. He treated a horse for iridochoroiditis and large opacities of the vitreous with infusion of Jab. leaves and injections of Pilo. The disease was quickly arrested, the vitreous cleared up completely, but during the first week the crystalline lens became opaque. Jab. has been used as a remedy for baldness and it forms the principal ingredient in some of the popular hair restorer tonics. In a number of patients taking it, white hair and blonde hair have been observed to turn black. Jab. has a reputation for stimulating breast secretions. A case is quoted from the Lancet in which a woman whose milk had ceased for a fortnight received ten drops of the fluid extract every four hours. The secretion of milk was re-established, but the patient began to suffer from extreme nervous excitement accompanied by a fixed idea that she should murder her family with a hatchet. The drug was stopped and these symptoms disappeared, and with them, the activity of the breast glands. Bell commended it in diarrhea with gushing. painless stools, flushed face, profuse salivation and sweat, and intense thirst with dark urine that is scanty or profuse. Cooper saw Jab. cause violent leucorrhea as well as a discharge of threadworms. He noted its use in relieving “a feeling of coldness and faintness and neuralgic throbbings in head and pelvis with a backache” when the period begins. He suggested treating with a drop or two of Jab. in hot water. The Hom. News, February, 1900, quoted an incidental cure of dysmenorrhea in a woman, age 23, who received five-drop does of Jab. for increased eye-tension which rapidly disappeared. The patient noticed that she passed the next menstrual period without pain though she usually had to spend two to four days in bed. The drug was continued in smaller doses and the improvement was maintained. Hale commended its use in women or young girls who always have dry skin, scanty menses and a tendency of blood to the head. Duncan aborted erysipelas by painting the tincture on the part four to five times daily. A sharp smarting is the first effect, followed by a more agreeable, soothing sensation. For burns, scalds and some forms of eczema and psoriasis. One patient, after having been injected with pilocarpine, complained of great sensitiveness to cold, constantly taking cold and bronchitis, the skin became irritable. Dudgeon recorded a case of a man, 45, who rose at an early hour and went to the other side of his bedroom to get a dose of Nux-v. 3c for some fancied derangement of his stomach. On coming back to bed he was seized with a sudden, violent, crimson flushing of the face followed almost immediately by profuse perspiration, beginning in the face and head and extending all over the body. This was followed by extreme coldness of the limbs and sickness terminating in the vomiting of sour mucus. The attacks recurred every quarter of an hour throughout the day. Not only was he unable to get out of bed, he could not raise himself up in bed or lie otherwise than on his right side without the most distressing giddiness and a feeling “as if he should die.” Pulse 60, regular and strong, temperature below normal. Ten drops of Jab. 1c were mixed in half a tumbler of water and a dessert spoonful given immediately and repeated every half hour. After the second dose the attacks ceased and he was able to take bread and milk without sickness. He had a good night's rest and was perfectly well the next day. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Amyl-n., At- rop., Phys., Lyc, Ruta. (2) Piloc. - Meniere's disease, rapidly progressive tuberculosis with free hemorrhages, profuse sweating, 2x trituration. (3) Atropine is the antagonist to pilocarpine in dose of one one-hundredth grain for one-sixth of pilocarpine. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy-

Stomach - Thirst in morning on waking. Hiccough, before vomiting. Nausea, sudden and retching often with hiccough Vomiting after supper. Nausea worse motion of eyes. Nausea on looking at objects moving, vomiting, pressure and pain in stomach. Stubborn vomiting of pregnancy. Nausea during menopause.

Abdomen - Empty, gone feeling. Cutting in lower abdomen. Severe pains over pubes with strong desire to pass water, which relieved. Ailments of the pancreas. Breasts - Milk absent or deficient. Milk increased, too profuse.

Rectum - Constipation. Hard stools. Diarrhea with flushed face and profuse perspiration. Diarrhea during daytime. Stools are watery, yellow. Frequent, undigested, gushing, weakening, papescent, and large and painless stools. Passage of threadworms.

Male - Orchitis from metastasis of mumps. Orchitis with incipient bronchial trouble.

Female - Menses, start with coldness, throbbing in head and pelvis, and backache. Menses scanty, congested head, dry skin. Leucorrhea. Edema of pregnancy. Puerperal convulsions in a stupor, threatened suffocation from inability to swallow excessive quantity of saliva. Heat and dryness of vagina during labor. Labor pains ceasing or sluggish. Flushing at menopause. Food - Good appetite. Hunger disappeared and he could not eat. Urgent thirst.

Chest - Sticking in chest. Pain in chest and around heart. Pressure on chest with anxiety, palpitation and pain in region of heart. Anxiety in chest with oppression, preventing sleep.

Heart - Pain in heart region. Oppression of chest. Nervous cardiac disorders. Violent ebullitions to heart and chest. Palpitations, during perspiration. Pulse is irregular, dicrotic. Irregularity, weakness and rapidity of action. Cyanosis, collapse.

Sleep - Sleepiness. Profound sleep in daytime. Fell asleep while sitting reading. Night-sweats. Perspiration in bed. Did not sleep well on account of restlessness, with pressure on chest and hurried breathing. Distressing dreams towards morning. Dreams of accidents and fights, waking him twice a night.

Skin - Redness of skin. Persistent dryness of skin. Dry eczema.

Modalities - Worse left side, exertion of eyes, exhaustion, start of menses, cold. Nausea worse motion of eyes.

Kidneys - Scanty, pain overpubes with much urging. Burning in urethra with urging to urinate. Urine dark. Urine increased during the sweat. Lungs - Edema of lungs. Breathing difficult, hurried. Slow, sighing respiration. Bronchial mucus membrane inflamed. Loose cough. Much inclination to cough and difficult breathing. Frothy or profuse, thin, serous expectoration.

Perspiration - Excessive perspiration from all parts of the body. Sweat on forehead, then over whole body, then chiefly on face, legs and feet. Sweat breaks out on the face and upper part of the chest. Sweats with palpitations, general pulsations and tremors. Copious sweating with chilliness, with salivation, with diarrhea (Verat.). Nervous sweats. Semi-lateral or unilateral sweat. Night-sweats. Perspiration in bed. Hot flushes and sweats. Perspiration during menopause. Sweat contains urea. Perspired easily before taking, but did not sweat during the proving.

Temperature - Chilly up and down back at 7 p.m. Shivering. Chilliness with sweat. Cold limbs. Heat flushes, at menopause, with profuse sweat, nausea and vomiting.

PHARMACY - jac-c. Jacarandacaroba. Brazilian caroba tree. Caroba tree. Jacaranda procera. Bignonia caroba. Jacaranda Brasiliensis. N. O. Bignoniaceae. Jacarandae. Tincture of fresh flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

HERBAL - “There are several species of Jacaranda,” especially Jacaranda procera, “that have the reputation of being curative in syphilis” notes the Treasury of Botany. Mure proved Jacaranda caroba, and the symptoms of the proving certainly confirmed this.

HOMEOPATHIC - Jac-c. has a reputation in venereal diseases and rheumatism. The urinary and sexual symptoms are important. Rheumatic symptoms, pains in the limbs. Lancinations in the heart. Morning sickness. Itching at anus. Hering confirmed symptoms including tearing pains affected the whole organism when urine contacts a chancre. Prepuce much swollen, could not be drawn over glans, on attempting to do so, copious discharge of yellowish green pus. Chordee in gonorrhea. Dull pain under sternum on raising head and drawing breath.

Head - Fullness in the head. Pain, as if a plug were pressing on the right side of the forehead. Dull pain between the forehead and right temple. Coryza with heavy head.

Eyes - Eyes pain, are inflamed and watery. Food - Food tastes insipid, nausea while eating.

Ears - Flapping in the ears, as of wings. Stoppage and heat in the left ear, with burning, digging pain extending to the left nostril.

Nose - Sneezing and fluent coryza. Coryza, with heaviness and weariness at the vertex, forehead, and eyes.

Mouth - Dry mouth in the morning in bed. Mouth dry and clammy. Raw pain at the left side of tongue. Food tastes flat or acid.

Throat - Sore and dry. Vesicles in pharynx. Sore throat with constrictions of the pharynx and difficult swallowing. Constrictive sensation at the throat. Vertigo - Vertigo on rising with heavy forehead. COMMENTS - Mahony confirmed symptoms including “Food tastes insipid, nausea during eating.” Motion aggravates. Symptoms come on when walking, raising head, sitting. J. S. Whittinghill cured several cases of muscular rheumatism characterized by a peculiar soreness and stiffness of muscles in the morning. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Thuj. - gonorrhea, rheumatism. (2) Cor-r. - red and sensitive chancre and chancroids. (3) Jac-g. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Fullness at the pit of the stomach, with hurried breathing. Pressure at the pit of the stomach. Painful stitch between the pit of the stomach and the umbilicus. Nausea when eating.

Abdomen - Painful stitch in the right and left side of navel. Acute pain at the hypo- gastrium when pressing upon it. Swelling of the right groin, painful to touch.

Rectum - Constipation. Acute pain with lancinations in the anus. Prickling around the anus. Itching at the anus while sitting. Excrescence at the anus.

Male - Heat and pain in penis. Painful erections. Chordee. Itching pimples on glans and prepuce. Discharge of yellowish white liquid from the prepuce. Prepuce painful and swollen. The prepuce cannot be drawn back. Phimosis. Suppuration between the glans and prepuce. Acute pain in the left testicle when walking. Heat and swelling of the scrotum. Syphilis. Chancroid.

Chest - Dull pain under the sternum on raising head and drawing breath. Prickling under the sternum.

Heart - Sensation as if the heartbeat was in the pit of the stomach. Sharp pain in region of heart. Painful stitch at the heart, extending to the right side. Stitch at the heart, which seems to beat slowly.

Back - Pain in nape. Neck so painful that the head cannot be turned to right. Stiffness in loins.

Limbs - Morning soreness and stiffness of muscles. Weakness of lumbar region. Gonorrheal rheumatism. Gonorrheal and syphilitic arthritis. Rheumatic pain in right knee. Itching pimples on hands.

Sleep - Restless sleep with frightful dreams.

Kidneys - Urethra inflamed, discharge of yellow matter.

Temperature - Internal chill. Dry, prickling heat all over.

full:
PHARMACY - jac. Jacaranda gualandai. N. O. Bignoniaceae. The driedleaves are crushed and macerated in five parts by weight of alcohol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Diarrhea. Ophthalmia. Rheumatism. Syphilis. Ulcers. Vertigo.

HERBAL - Dr. J. S, Whittinghill contributed the following from the Eclectic Medical Journal concerning Jacaranda: “Of this South American remedy the Dispensatory says it is used in Brazil and other South American countries for syphilis, sometimes under the name Carroba.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Jac. has syphilitic symptoms, especially of the eyes and throat. Chancroids. Atonic ulcers. Dark, painless diarrhea. Weakness of memory and inability to study.

Eyes - Pains and inflammation of the eye with redness, more marked in the left eye. Sensation of sand in the eyes. Ophthalmia, which begins in the left eye with lachrymation and night agglutination of the eyelids. Syphilitic-like ophthalmia. Weakness of sight.

Throat - Pain and burning of the larynx, when laughing or reading aloud. Small vesicles in the pharynx. Vertigo - Vertigo on rising after stooping, with momentary loss of sight and sensation of heaviness in the forehead. COMMENTS - Dr. J. F. Con vers, of Bogotá, found Jac. to be useful in certain kinds of rheumatism. He noted the case of one patient who suffered from rheumatism for about 10 years, and never became serious. Sometimes she was nearly relieved from it. She lost a good deal of sleep due to it. Her wrist would become painful and very weak from ordinary labor. She complained of being stiff and had pain from any motion, particularly in the morning. She needed assistance dressing. Upon sudden motion, she had the sensation of the muscles tearing and being bruised, painful on pressure. Convers gave her different remedies as they seemed to be indicated with no result. He thought there could be nothing lost by trying Jac. and did so. In a few days, she was entirely relieved of muscular pains. Six weeks after, her symptoms returned, but a second dose again relieved and the pains did not return. Con vers tried Jac. on three other patients with the same peculiar morning stiffness and soreness. All were relie ved in a few day s and experienced no further muscular pains. Convers used the mother tincture at 5 drops per dose and the 3x dilution of it in the treatment of gonorrhea and chancroids with the great success. Anshutz noted that it is a complementary and antidote to Merc. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke.

Rectum - Diarrhea with dark mulberrycolored stools without pain or tenesmus, but with mucus.

Male - Pain in the penis. Increased secretion of urine. Gonorrhea with a discharge which stains the linen a dirty yellow color. Chancroids.

Back - Weakness of the lumbar region.

author: Murphy
constitution: Asthma. Detoxification. Eye, disorders. Gastric,pains. Heartburn. Kidney, disorders. Kidney, stones.
keynote: PHARMACY - jad. Jade. Nephrite. Jadeite. Jade is found in two varieties. Jadeite and Nephrite and comes in a wide range of colors including white, lavender, red, brown, yellow, orange, blue, and green, each color said to relate more specifically to certain ailments or organs.…
full:
PHARMACY - jad. Jade. Nephrite. Jadeite. Jade is found in two varieties. Jadeite and Nephrite and comes in a wide range of colors including white, lavender, red, brown, yellow, orange, blue, and green, each color said to relate more specifically to certain ailments or organs. Historical dose: The gem mother tincture diluted can be applied externally and given internally. Four to Eight drops of Jade Essence in a cup of pure water. Repeat as needed.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Detoxification. Eye, disorders. Gastric,pains. Heartburn. Kidney, disorders. Kidney, stones.

HOMEOPATHIC - The Portuguese, who brought home jade pieces from their settlement in Canton, China, called jade piedre de ilharga, or stone of the loins, because they believed it to be strong medicine for kidney ailments. Jade objects brought back to Spain from the new world were called by the Spanish version of this phrase piedra de hijada. This became the French ejade and then, finally, jade. Jadeite is from the Spanish, piedra de ijada, “stone of the side,” because its supposed to cure kidney ailments if applied to the side of the body. Suggested healing properties common to all colors of Jade include, ability to mellow one's existence, rid negative thoughts and energy, soothe the mind. Thus making tasks seem easier and less complicated. Strengthen the body’s filtration and cleansing systems. Develop a greater capacity for love, and assist in the removal of toxins. Also said to be a very protective stone. Jade was known as the kidney stone, and it was widely employed as a remedy for renal disease. It was worn over this organ to break up kidney stones. Powdered and mixed with gold and silver, jade strengthened the lungs, the vocal organs, and the heart and prolonged life. A potion of jade, rice, and dew was employed to harden bones, make muscles more supple, calm the mind, and purify the blood. Taken regularly, this prescription eliminated hunger and thirst as well as sensations of heat and cold. Believed to protect the body from decay, jade was used for embalming. When worn around a child's neck jade would guard against infantile disease. It also was worn to relieve gastric pains and heartburn, to calm asthma, and to aid childbirth. Four grains, dissolved in wine, relieved bile. Suggested healing properties common to all colors of Jade include, ability to mellow one's existence, rid negative thoughts and energy, soothe the mind making tasks seem easier and less complicated, strengthen the body's filtration and cleansing systems, develop a greater capacity for love, and assist in the removal of toxins. Also said to be a very protective stone. Health, wealth, longevity stone. Ancient Chinese used also for courage, wisdom, justice, mercy, emotional balance, stamina, love, fidelity, humility, generosity, peace, harmony. Lungs, heart, thymus, immune, kidney and blood detoxification, nervous system. A gentle, steady energy. Increases fertility, longevity. Provides wisdom when evaluating issues or problems. Brings needed energy. Improves concentration. Encourages education. Considered a “Dream Stone.” Benefits eye disorders, kidney stones and female discomfort. COMMENTS - The ancient jade carved in China was what we today call nephrite jade: an ar .phibolite mineral. In the 19th Century , it was discovered that the material from the new world was not the same mineral as the jade from China. The mineral from Central America, a pyroxene, was called jadeite to distinguish it from the original nephrite. Because of its smooth even texture, jade has long been a preferred material for carving. The most common shape is the flat donut-shaped disc called a pi, which is commonly worn as a necklace. The Emerald Buddha, the sacred image that is enshrined at Wat Phra Kaeo in Bangkok, Thailand, is actually beautiful green jadeite. Good fortune, prosperity. A peaceful stone for centuries of primary importance to the people of the Orient (where it is considered to be one of the most importance symbols of purity and serentiy). The Chinese referred to jade as the musical stone, because of the melodic tones it makes when struck. For centuries, jade was thought to be a single gemstone, but in 1863 two types were recognized: jadeite and nephrite. Jade, Venus: Chinese Stone of Heaven. Since at least 2950 BC, jade has been treasured in China as the royal gemstone, yu. The character for jade resembles a capital I with a line across the middle: the top represents the heavens, the bottom the earth, and the center section, mankind. The word yu is used in Chinese to call something precious, as in English we use gold. Jade was thought to preserve the body after death and can be found in emperors' tombs from thousands of years ago. One tomb contained an entire suit made out of jade, to assure the physical immortality of its owner. For thousands of years, jade was a symbol of love and virtue as well as a status symbol. RELATIONS - Compare: Aurum Met. Nat. Mur. Rose Quartz. REFERENCES - Murphy.
