full:
PHARMACY - jal. Jalapa. Ipomoea jalapa. Ipomoea purga. Exogonium purga. Concol- vulus purga. N. O. Convolvulacae. Mexico. Trituration of dried root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anus, soreness. Colic. Coryza. Diarrhea. Gout. Fainting. Restlessness.

HOMEOPATHIC - Jalapa, the well-known purgative of old school practice, had a short proving by Jeanes. Allen cured a case of “coryza in an infant, violent attacks of crying and intense pain, quiet during the day, but screaming all night.” Colic and diarrhea. Severe abdominal pain, “as if the abdomen would be cut to pieces,” severe griping, cutting pains. Pain is better by belchings of frothy matter and flatulence. Cutting colic before and during the stool. Stools are watery, sour smelling and bloody. Stools, watery, muddy or sour, bloody. Infantile diarrhea with general coldness, blueness of face. Pain in sigmoid flexure. General coldness and blueness of the face. Restlessness and anxiety. Great weakness with fainting fits, excessive uneasiness and tossing about of limbs. Symptoms are worse at night. A child may be quite quiet all day, but screams and tossed about all night. MIND - Great restlessness with anxiety. Fainting fits, weakness. Quiet all day, but screams and tossed about all night. Weeping in sleep, good during day. Screams and restless all night. Shrieking in children.

Head - Violent headache. Pain in head, smarting in skin of forehead.

Ears - Humming in ears.

Mouth - Dryness of lips. Tongue, smooth, glazed, dry, smarting and biting. Stinging on tongue and in fauces.

Stomach - Flatulent and frothy belchings with abatement of pain. Nausea.

Abdomen - Abdomen distended. Pain in middle of abdomen and in region of left superior flexure of colon. Pain in right hypochondrium. Pain in cecum. Colic, violent pain in small intestines, as if abdomen would be cut to pieces. Inflammation of intestines. Severe griping, cutting pain in bowels, worse at night. Flatulent rumbling in bowels. Flatulence and nausea.

Rectum - Pinching and griping. Severe cutting, griping pain in bowels. Cutting colic before and during stool. Watery diarrhea, thin, muddy stools. Stools, violent, excessive, bloody, watery, with weak pulse, sour smelling, with great restlessness and anxiety. Infantile diarrhea, general coldness, blueness of face. Pain in sigmoid flexure of colon. Soreness of anus.

Male - Thrilling sensation in urethra while urinating.

Back - Severe pain about superior margin of left scapula.

Limbs - Excessive uneasiness and tossing about of limbs. Aching in arms and legs, mostly right side. Pain in thighs. Pain in large joint of great toe. Smarting on inside edge and at root of left great toenail with heat, tearing and pulsation. Burning of soles of feet.

Modalities - Worse night, belchings.

Kidneys - Pain and pressure in region of bladder.

Perspiration - Great disposition to perspiration of head and superior parts of body.

Temperature - General coldness and blueness of face. Febrile attacks. COMMENTS - Nash cured with Jal. 12c a desperate case of enterocolitis in which there was screaming all day as well as all night. With the screaming there was constant body contortions, bending forward, backward and sideways alternately. RELATIONS-Antidotes: Elat., Cann-s. Compare: (1) Camph. - diarrhea with coldness. (2) Coloc. - colic. (3) Iris-t. - pain in cecum. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Jasminum Officinale
author: Murphy
constitution: Coma. Convulsions. Lockjaw. Tetanus. Vomiting.
keynote: PHARMACY - jasm. Jasminum officinale. White jessamine. N. O. Jasminaceae. Some botanists include jasmine in the Oleaceae. Jasminum should not be confounded with Gelsemium, the “Yellow Jessamine,” or “Carolina Jessamine,” which belongs to a different order of plants. Tincture of…
full:
PHARMACY - jasm. Jasminum officinale. White jessamine. N. O. Jasminaceae. Some botanists include jasmine in the Oleaceae. Jasminum should not be confounded with Gelsemium, the “Yellow Jessamine,” or “Carolina Jessamine,” which belongs to a different order of plants. Tincture of red berries. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Coma. Convulsions. Lockjaw. Tetanus. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - W. H. Hull recorded the case of a boy who ate the red berries, causing vomiting, convulsions, tetanus and acomatose state. Symptoms went from above downwards and from left to right. Muscular movements were observed first about the eyes and face, especially on the left side, towards which eyes and facial muscles were directed. The movements became generally more severe, going from head to left arm, then to left lower limbs, until finally the whole body was thrown into violent convulsions. At one time the spasms were chiefly opisthotonos, when the whole surface was congested almost to a blackened hue, most marked about the muscles of the head and throat, jaws locked, trismus complete, better by a bath. The body was weak and almost helpless for a few days. Lay on the floor in a fainting fit. Perfect insensibility. Surface cool. MIND - Comatose condition. Perfect insensibility.

Eyes - Pupils immoderately dilated.

Face - Face pale. Muscular movement first above eyes and face, especially left side towards which eyes and facial muscles were directed. Lungs - Breathing somewhat bronchial but of unusual frequency.

Stomach - Vomiting. Slight emesis after first sleep. COMMENTS - The Treasury of Botany stated that the bitter leaves of Jasminum floribundum are used in Abyssinia against tapeworms. In India, the bitter root of Jasminum angustifolium, powdered and mixed with the powdered root of Acorns calamus, is considered an excellent application in ringworm. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Pulse - Slow and feeble.

name: Jatropha Curcas
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better by placing hands in cold water. Worse summer, walking in open air, morning, pressure, touch, covering. Patient seeks to cool himself by throwing off covers and lying on ground. Headaches are worse in a room..
constitution: Blepharospasm. Borborygmi. Cholera. Cholerine. Constipation. Cramps. Diarrhea. Eyelids, inflamed. Food, poisoning. Heels, sensitive. Hiccough. Mouth, ulceration. Skin, disorders. Tympanites. Vomiting. Worms.
keynote:
PHARMACY - jatr. Jatropha curcas. Purging nut. Atrophacurcas. Physic nut. N. O. Euphor- biaceae. West Indies.Tincture and triturationof seeds. Historical dose: Trituration, tincture and all potencies, third to thirtieth potency.

CLINICAL - Blepharospasm. Borborygmi. Cholera.…
full:
PHARMACY - jatr. Jatropha curcas. Purging nut. Atrophacurcas. Physic nut. N. O. Euphor- biaceae. West Indies.Tincture and triturationof seeds. Historical dose: Trituration, tincture and all potencies, third to thirtieth potency.

CLINICAL - Blepharospasm. Borborygmi. Cholera. Cholerine. Constipation. Cramps. Diarrhea. Eyelids, inflamed. Food, poisoning. Heels, sensitive. Hiccough. Mouth, ulceration. Skin, disorders. Tympanites. Vomiting. Worms.

HOMEOPATHIC - Jatr. is one of the most active of the Euphorbians and strongly resembles Croto-t. in its action, especially in the urgent gushing stools and the irritation and pimples of the skin. It is also an active purgative, affecting the stomach and intestines. Kent described the sphere of Jatr. in cholera, noting that “The characteristic is rice water discharge, it has vomiting and purging, more or less sweat, more or less cramps. Suppression of urine, the great prostration, syncope and rapid onset peculiar to cholera and it has this to differentiate it from all other remedies. The vomiting and purging and evacuations are thick, albuminous, lumpy instead of thin and watery.” Jatr. corresponds more to the earlier stage than to the collapse stage of cholera. Predominant cramps, gripping cutting pains, sensation as if balls were rolling together in abdomen. Violent cramps that draw the muscles of calf flat. The patient writhes about in bed with pain. Sudden desire for stool and constant noise of liquids in abdomen, especially left side. Marked and peculiar gurgling, like water. Much noise in the abdomen as if a bottle was being emptied, followed later by a thin stool or by profuse gushing stools. Rice water stools. Vomiting, easy, albuminous. Hiccough followed by copious vomiting. Unquenchable thirst. Food poisoning. Icy coldness of the whole body, especially lower limbs. MIND - Apathy. Indifference to pain. Anxiety and anguish, with burning in stomach and coldness of body.

Head - Heat and heaviness of the head. Heat in head, face and ears. Stupefaction with yawning and nausea. Headache with nausea and vomiting. Violentpressing pain in the temples, ceasing in open air and re- appeari ng when entering aroom. Stiffness of muscles on forehead and neck.

Eyes - Itching and smarting of margins of lids. Twitching of left upper lid. Bright and dark spots before eyes. Black points before eyes.

Ears - Burning hot ears with heat in the back part of the head.

Nose - Ulcers in the nose and mouth. Itching of the nose while eating.

Face - Hot face and head, chilliness in the back. Pale face with blue margins around the eyes. Painful cracked lips.

Mouth - Metallic, bloody taste with much spitting of saliva. Increased accumulation of thin saliva. Long continued pain and burning of the tongue. Numbness of tongue with heat and dryness of mouth. Mouth feels as if scalded.

Throat - Burning in the mouth and throat, followed by dryness. Spasmodic constriction in throat, ascending from stomach. Vertigo - Giddiness, followed by unconsciousness and delirium. COMMENTS - Diarrhea associated with coldness, mottled blue surface, cold sweat. Sudden desire for stool. Diarrhea accompanied by copious and easy vomiting of watery, albuminous, ropy liquid. Water is almost immediately vomited. Cholera. Suddenly occurring summer diarrhea. Mouth dry, itching between toes, at night. Profuse, watery diarrhea after midnight. In the morning, stools, headache, are worse. Metallic bloody taste, much spitting of saliva. Farrington noted that it is useful in cases of suppressed measles. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Camph., Verat., Gamb., Crot-t. (2) Jatr-u., Sponge nettle - edema and cardiac paresis. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Stomach - Heat and burning in stomach with crampy, constrictive pain in the epigastrium. Food poisoning. Belchings of air. Hiccough, followed by copious vomiting. Very easy vomiting, of a large mass of dark green bile, with acrid feeling from throat. Nausea and vomiting, brought on by drinking water. Vomiting during pregnancy.

Abdomen - Abdomen swollen and sore to touch. Tympanites. Pain in hypochondria, deep in abdomen, behind the navel. Griping, sticking, in abdomen. Lancinating, stinging pain with the colic. Colic with rumbling in abdomen, better walking in open air. Distended with gurgling noises. Much noise in abdomen, as if a full bottle was emptied, followed by thin stool. Noise like the gurgling of water during the fecal discharge. Sensation as if balls were rolling together in abdomen.

Rectum - Loud noise in abdomen like gurgling of water, associated with coldness, cramps, nausea and vomiting. First stage of cholera, before collapse. Diarrhea, forced discharge. Sudden, profuse, watery, rice- water stool, gushes from him like a torrent. Very copious, mushy stools with quantities of lumbrici and threadworms. Constipation. Stitches in anus and rectum.

Male - Aching in genital as after excessive sexual intercourse. Drawing in genitals, extending along inner side right thigh to navel.

Female - Vomiting during pregnancy. Food - Great thirst. Violent, unquenchable thirst, not satisfied by drinking water. Dreads to drink on account of nausea. Food poisoning.

Chest - Constriction in chest with anxiety, preventing sleep. Violent aching pain in left clavicle. Sticking from above downwards, deep in chest behind sternum. Pain in region of left third rib inside the nipple.

Heart - Feeling of sinking and nausea in the precordial region, followed by soft stool. Violent palpitation, shaking the chest, when moving slowly about the room. Pulse is irregular, small thready and intermittent, greatly slowed. Almost pulseless.

Back - Stiffness of muscles of nape of neck and forehead. Bruised feeling muscles of back and chest. Stiffness in lumbar region.

Limbs - Muscles of limbs contracted by violent spasms. Pain in the limbs and joints. Cramps in muscles, especially calves, legs and feet. Pain in ankles, feet and toes. Heels sensitive.

Sleep - Excessive drowsiness. Restlessness at night on account of rush of thought and palpitations. Attacks of anxiety at night, not permitting sleep.

Skin - Pimples on wrist, back of hand, cheek, back of neck, bend of right thigh. Itching and slightest tension around mouth. Itching between fingers in palms, between toes in bed at night, first worse then better by rubbing.

Modalities - Better by placing hands in cold water. Worse summer, walking in open air, morning, pressure, touch, covering. Patient seeks to cool himself by throwing off covers and lying on ground. Headaches are worse in a room.

Liver - Pain in region of liver and under right scapula to shoulder. Lungs - Painful pressure right side of larynx at night, waking him, not worse by touch. Respiration quick, panting, difficult. Short, hacking, persistent cough. Hollow cough.

Kidneys - Violent urging to urinate. Urine pale yellow, frothy.

Temperature - Chilliness and clammy perspiration. Coldness of the whole body, mottled blue. Chilliness in the back, cold hands, blue nails, with heat in the mouth, throat, face and head.

full:
PHARMACY - jatr-u. Jatropha urens. Spurge nettle. Tread softly. N. O. Euphorbiaceae. Southern United States. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Cardiac, paresis. Edema.

HOMEOPATHIC - According to Allen, this is the most poisonous plant known. He quoted, from the Kew Gardens Quarterly, the experience of Mr. Smith, who touched his wrist against the fine bristly stings of the plant while reaching over it. He experienced numbness and swelling of the lips. His circulation stopped and Smith soon fell unconscious, the last thing he remembered were cries of “Run for the doctor!” COMMENTS - Other Jatropha include Jatr. glauca, or Jatr. glandulifera, of the East Indies. It has a curious nodulated, gouty looking stem. When crushed, the seeds yield an oil that is used as an external application against rheumatism. REFERENCES - Clarke.

author: Murphy
constitution: Amenorrhea. Constipation. Dysmenorrhea. Emaciation. Fibroids. Headache. Hemorrhoids. Hysteria. Leucorrhea. Menopause. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Nausea. Palpitations. Uterine, disorders. Vomiting.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Constipation. Dysmenorrhea. Emaciation. Fibroids.…
full:
PHARMACY - joan. Joanesia asoca. Ashoka bark. Jonosia asoca. Saraca indica. Bark of an IndianTree. N. O. Caesalpinioideae. Tincture of bark or seeds. Dried bark. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Constipation. Dysmenorrhea. Emaciation. Fibroids. Headache. Hemorrhoids. Hysteria. Leucorrhea. Menopause. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Nausea. Palpitations. Uterine, disorders. Vomiting.

HERBAL - Joanesia is a noted plant in India and its therapeutic properties in curing and alleviating all sorts of menstrual troubles and uterine disorders date back from antiquities. Long-lasting costiveness, occasional headache and vertigo associated with uterine derangements are some of the marked symptoms of the drug. Joanesiais a sovereign remedy for amenorrhea or scanty menses with intolerable pain and burning sensation during the passage of urine. In dysmenorrhea its efficacy has been verified by several homeopaths of our country. The Ayurvedic physicians prize it as an uterine tonic. It imparts a healthy tone and an all round strength to the uterus which has been weakened by long-lasting disorders of the uterus. In the cure of leucorrhea its action can never be questioned and upon bloody leucorrhea, whether acute or chronic, it exerts an exhilarating and permanent curative action which sometimes appears to be a miracle. It removes weakness and physical emaciation to the females suffering from long - lasting uterine complaints, or due to those causes. It is generally considered to be an astringent medicine and uterine sedative. It is said to possess a stimulating effect on the endometrium and on the ovarian tissue. Joanesiais extensively employed in uterine ailments especially menorrhagia which is the outcome of uterine fibroids and other causes. In cases of bloody leucorrhea its efficacy is sure and pronounced. Menstrual flow appears too soon, is copious and lasts long and this sort of flow makes the female very weak, anemic and bloodless, she experiences burning sensation all over the face and eyes suffers from pain in the lumbar region and constipation. Joanesia is considered by competent authorities to be an excellent remedy for the eradication of the above complaints. Asoka will be found to be a grand medicine if the menstrual flow be stopped for any cause and for which colicky abdominal pains supervene.

HOMEOPATHIC - Joanesia was introduced by Dr. N. D. Ray, of Calcutta. Extensive sphere of action on female organs. Amenorrhea and metrorrhagia. The remedy is principally used by the native physicians of India for menorrhagia, metrorrhagia, leucorrhea from delayed menses or in the place of menses. Infantile leucorrhea, child getting thin and emaciated in spite of getting usual nourishment. Joanesia has been found to be an excellent medicine for the complaints appearing at the time of menopause. For barrenness it is generally used with success. In bleeding piles, its efficacy has been verified. In bleeding piles, the color of the blood is red. the patient experiences severe pain and stiff feeling in the back and suffers from constipation, there is burning sensation while passing urine, and there is also burning of the hands, feet and eyes in the evening. MIND - The patients are generally affectionate, nervous, sentimental, gloomy and religious. Good-natured, affectionate. Absentminded. Timid. Easily weeping, easily excitable, easily fatigued. Disinclination to work. Not very imaginative. Changeable thoughts. Satisfied with small things. Slow to understand. Disposition to take cold easily, feels better in the open air. Impatient. Cannot bear sufferings. Hysterical exaggerates sufferings.

Head - Stupefying headache, frontal headache, worse sometimes on right temple and sometimes on the left. Unilateral headache. Reflex uterine congestive headache. with scanty menstrual discharge relieved by free flow, nausea, vertigo, disinclination for food or drink, periodical headache, better after bathing, sweat of forehead, relieved of all symptoms in the open air, heaviness of the whole head. Congestive headache, better open air and by free flow.

Eyes - Pain in the eyeballs. Redness of the conjunctiva. Burning and itching sensation. Styes on upper lids. Profuse lachrymation. Short-sightedness. Great sensibility of eyes to light. Supra-orbital pains on one or both sides. Great photophobia. Tired feeling in the eyes with least exertion, such as reading and staring at an object.

Ears - Pains in ear. Hardness of hearing especially after catarrhal or severe cold.

Nose - Nasal catarrh, sneezing, profuse watery discharge from the nose. Nostrils sore. Obstruction of the nose. Loss of sense of smell. Ulceration of the nostrils. Profuse bleeding from the nose of red color.

Face - Paleness of the face, alternately with heat and redness of the cheeks. Pimples on the face.

Mouth - Dryness of the mouth, excessive thirst, drinks large quantities of water at a time, tongue coated with thick, white or brown coating, bleeding of the gums, toothache.

Throat - Redness of the throat, tonsils and uvula, sore throat, easily takes cold, troublesome throat cough. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Ghose.

Stomach - Excessive nausea, sometimes vomiting. Vomiting of bile. Biliousness. Pain in epigastrium. Colicky pain.

Abdomen - Hard distended abdomen, pain on pressure, passage of foul-smelling wind, eructation, flatulent colic, worse in the evening, soreness in lower abdomen or pelvis.

Rectum - Hemorrhoids. Obstinate constipation. Feces are hard. Large stool and passed every third or fourth day. Evacuation difficult, pain before stools. Stools are covered with slime or mucus. Pains on the back. Soreness in anus. Blind or bleeding piles. Protrusion of hemorrhoids with itching, smarting and pain.

Male - Testicles swollen, drawing pain in the spermatic cords, itching in the scrotum, discharge of prostatic fluid, emission at night with or without dreams.

Female - Menses suppressed and irregular. Headache due to suppression of menses. Severe headache due to scanty flow of menses with severe pain all over the lower parts of the abdomen, pain in back and thighs. Menstrual colic. Delayed and irregular menses. Menstrual discharge scanty, pale and watery, sometimes bad odor and blackish, slightly clotted and painful. Leucorrhea. Amenorrhea at puberty with headache, palpitation, hysteria, loss of appetite, constipation. Pain in ovaries before the flow. Congestive feelings in pelvic organs as before menses. Pain in both ovarian regions. Pain in the sacral region, better on the appearance of menses with free flow. Menorrhagia. Food - Want of appetite and dislike for food. No desire for food, eats little. Thirsty. Desire for sweets. Desire for acid and sour things. Drinks large quantities of water. Disinclined to take milk, which when taken agrees well.

Chest - Tight feeling across the chest.

Heart - Palpitations. Pain in the region of the heart. Pulse quick, full and hard. Accentuated first sound. Palpitations, worse on movement or walking or bending forward.

Back - Coldness between shoulders. Pain along spine, radiating to abdomen and thighs. Pain at the ape of the neck along the spine. Pain in sacrum and in back radiates on both sides of the abdomen and down the thighs.

Limbs - Weakness in limbs. Shifting pain from place to place. Pains in small joints. Numbness of the limbs. Pain along the thighs. Lungs - Respiration hurried. Difficulty in breathing when walking, worse in the afternoon and evening. Hacking throat cough.

Sleep - Disturbed sleep. Sleeplessness. Fearful dreams. Dreams of traveling.

Kidneys - Urine scanty, bloody, passes frequently. Involuntary urination at night in bed. Profuse emission of watery urine, pain in loin.

Bladder - Irritable bladder. Bladder irritable, desire for frequent passage of urine. Tenderness of bladder.

Temperature - Chilliness without thirst. Dry heat with restlessness. Redness of cheeks. Flushed face, running from the nose, catarrhal symptoms.

author: Murphy

PHARMACY - jug-c. Juglans cinerea. Butternut. Juglans cathartica. N. O. Juglandaceae. North America. Tincture of bark of root. Triturations of the resinoid Juglandin. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies, tincture to third potency.

CLINICAL - Acne. Angina pectoris.…
full:
PHARMACY - jug-c. Juglans cinerea. Butternut. Juglans cathartica. N. O. Juglandaceae. North America. Tincture of bark of root. Triturations of the resinoid Juglandin. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies, tincture to third potency.

CLINICAL - Acne. Angina pectoris. Axilla, pain. Chest, pain. Gallstones. Coryza. Dropsy. Eczema. Erysipelas. Erythema nodosum. Gallstones. Headaches. Herpes. Hydrothorax. Impetigo. Lichen. Migraines. Pemphigus. Ringworm. Rodent ulcer. Scapula, pain. Scarlatina. Tetters. Vision, lost.

HOMEOPATHIC - The butternut and the black walnut (Juglans nigra) are the American repre- sentativesof the walnut family. It has a reputation as a mild cathartic. Applied to the skin, the juice causes reddening and blistering. It was successfully used in camp diarrhea and dysentery in the early American wars. The green rind, rubbed on tetters and ringworm, has a reputation for curing them. Jug-c. and Jug-r„ or Nux Juglans, have both been proved and studied. With both, the digestion is disordered, accompanied with other acute symptoms, including headaches. These are followed by chronic skin disorders. Sharp, occipital headache, usually associated with liver disturbance. Pain in chest, axilla and scapula with suffocative sensation. Feeling as if all internal organs were too large, especially those of left side. Gallstones. Faulty elimination that produces jaundice and various skin eruptions. Itching is worse when overheated from exercise. MIND - Absent-minded. Confusion. Difficulty concentrating. Dull feeling, cannot remember anything that was read. Depression of spirits. Aversion to company. Want to do nothing but eat and sleep.

Head - Dull, full head. Head feels enlarged. Dull headache, better when getting up. Sharp, occipital headache. Severe headache, can hardly see. Eruption on scalp. Itching of scalp, intense, must scratch constantly. Pustules on lids and around eyes.

Eyes - Eyes red and swollen. Inflammation, with pustules on lids and around eyes. Eyes burning in afternoon. Feeling in eyes as if drawn together. Loss of vision on sudden motion, with faint-like giddiness.

Nose - Tingling in nose, sneezing. Coryza, preceded by pain under sternum, with threatening suffocation. Copious, bland, thick mucus discharge.

Face - Pallor. Erythematous redness with dry, burning sensation. Food - Ferocious appetite. Thirsty, wants to drink all the time.

Mouth - Acrid feeling in mouth and throat. Coppery taste. Tongue coated white, yellow in the morning. Dryness of root of tongue and fauces. Burning and pricking in mouth and throat. Swelling of submaxillary glands, worse right. Soreness in region of tonsils, externally.

Throat - Sore throat in forenoon with roughness on swallowing. Fauces dry. Pain in right side of fauces. Burning in pharynx. Vertigo - Vertigo with slight nausea. Slight vertigo with sinking faint feeling in stomach extending to abdomen. COMMENTS - Scrofulous and scorbutic conditions. Rheumatic pains. Characteristic sharp shooting pain in occiput. Headache, with frequent urination and burning. Morning headaches (Nux-v., Bry., Chef, Iris.). Disturbance of the digestive organs (Iris.). Pains in liver and right scapula. Epigastric sinking, extending to the abdomen, with a headache. Acute diarrhea. Dark, clotted hemorrhage from the lungs (Jug-r., from the uterus). Acute pains and numbness in the axilla (Jug-r. affects the skin and glands of the axilla). Eruptions. Scarlatina. Rodent ulcer. One patient who was taking Jug-c. for acne developed all the symptoms of angina pectoris. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Juglin. - duodenal catarrh, bilious diarrhea. (2) Chef, Bry., Iris. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Burning in stomach. Sinking in stomach extends to abdomen, with headache. Atonic dyspepsia with much belchings and flatulent distention. Nausea in morning. Nausea worse at night.

Abdomen - Soreness in region of liver. Stitches in hepatic region, and under right scapula. Pain in the hypochondrium. Heavy pain in umbilical region. Flatulent pain in different parts of abdomen. Burning in abdomen after stool.

Rectum - Constipation, with griping in umbilical region. Constipation preceded by diarrhea. Diarrhea with burning in anus before and after stool. Yellowish- green stools with tenesmus and burning at anus. A drastic purge, producing irritation and inflammation of mucus membrane of bowels. Bilious, copious, frequent, painless stools. Loose stool, smelling like onions. Camp diarrhea.

Chest - Pain in left chest. Retro-sternal pain. Angina pectoris. Oppression at chest, hindering long breathing with cutting pains in lungs. Tuberculosis with great emaciation. Dropsy of chest, of rheumatic origin.

Back - Muscles of neck rigid, lame. Pricking up and down spine. Pain in lumbar vertebrae. Pain between scapula. Sticking under right scapula on stooping.

Limbs - Aching pains in the limbs. Sharp, rheumatic pain in shoulders and wrists. Pain in right axilla in afternoon. Pain in elbows and knees. Cramp-like pain in hip at night. Pain in thighs and left knee in forenoon. Occasionally sharp pain in calves. Lungs - Expectoration of very tenacious mucus, raising a quantity of dark blood.

Sleep - Constant yawning, without sleepiness. Sleepiness. Sleeplessness after 3 a.m. Sleep restless, light, unrefreshing. Dreams are vivid, frightful.

Skin - Jaundice with pain about liver and right scapula. Red-like flush of scarlatina. Erythema and erysipelatous redness. Itching and prickling when heated. Eczema, especially on lower limbs, sacrum and hands. Pustules.

Modalities - Better getting heated, exercise, scratching, rising in the morning. Worse walking, chest pains. Going up hill causes retro-sternal pain. Stooping causes pain in scapula and back.

Kidneys - Frequent and copious urination, with burning, smarting, with a headache.

Temperature - Chilliness, alternating with flashes of heat. Chilliness along spine, beginning in back when near the fire, without coldness of flesh.

name: Juglans Regia
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Worse by motion. Worse after fat food, evening, at 9 p.m. and after 9 p.m. Migraine worse by speaking. Pain in abdomen worse by laughing. Warmth of bed aggravates toothache. Itching, worse at night. Rash aggravated by undressing, washing..
constitution: Acne. Anus, burning. Axillary glands, suppuration. Chancre. Eruptions. Exhaustion. Eyes, pain. Favus. Flatulence. Headaches. Herpes. Levitation, sensation. Menorrhagia. Purpura. Ringworm. Skin, dis- orders. Scurvy. Spleen, pain. Styes. Syphilis.
keynote:
PHARMACY - jug-r. Juglans regia. Walnut. Nux juglans. N. O. Juglandaceae. Tincture of leaves and of rind of green fruit. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne. Anus, burning. Axillary glands, suppuration. Chancre. Eruptions. Exhaustion. Eyes, pain. Favus.…
full:
PHARMACY - jug-r. Juglans regia. Walnut. Nux juglans. N. O. Juglandaceae. Tincture of leaves and of rind of green fruit. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne. Anus, burning. Axillary glands, suppuration. Chancre. Eruptions. Exhaustion. Eyes, pain. Favus. Flatulence. Headaches. Herpes. Levitation, sensation. Menorrhagia. Purpura. Ringworm. Skin, dis- orders. Scurvy. Spleen, pain. Styes. Syphilis.

HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany noted, “Its plantation should not be too near dwellings, as some persons are affected by the powerful aroma of its foliage. It was said that in the golden age, when men lived upon acorns, the gods lived upon Walnuts and hence the name of Juglans, Jovis glans or Jupiter's nuts”.

HOMEOPATHIC - Excited, as if intoxicated in the evening in bed and a feeling as if the head were floating in the air, or as if flying. Sharp pains in the forehead (Jug-c. in the occiput). Muscles relaxed. Prominent skin eruptions. Exhaustion and disinclination for the usual business. MIND - Mental indolence. Disinclined to talk or argue. Inattention when reading and disinclination to work. Peevishness. Discontented in evening. Excited in evening in bed as if intoxicated. Feeling as if the head were floating in the air.

Head - Confused, feels as if head were floating in air. Occipital sharp pain.

Eyes - Burning in eyes. Pressive pain above eye (left) worse by motion. Styes. Feeling of coryza.

Ears - Aching and fullness in right, then left ear, followed by a discharge of pus from both ears. Burning in left ear, then redness and swelling. External ear inflamed, with painful sores. Eruption behind ears of children.

Face - Swelling of left cheek and upper lip.

Mouth - Tongue coated white in morning with bitter, slimy taste. Salivation. Tearing in hollow teeth, worse warmth of bed.

Throat - Aphonia or great hoarseness. Hawking of much mucus. COMMENTS - Severe flatulence and bloating of the abdomen. Affects the spleen more than the liver (opposite of Jug-c.). Diarrhea and many rectal and anal symptoms. Hemorrhagic, blackandclottedblood (Jug-c., Cary.),particularly uterine hemorrhages. Inflammation and ulceration in the male sexual organs. Pronounced skin symptoms. Scrofula. Scabs on the arms and in axilla. Symptoms go from the right axilla to the left. Farrington said Jug-r. is one of the best remedies in “tinea favosa, especially in the scalp behind the ear, itching is intense at night so that the patient has difficulty in sleeping.” Clotar Miiller, who experienced the axillary skin symptoms in his own person, had never suffered from a skin affection before. One of the provers was cured of an itching eruption of the legs from which he had suffered in winter for four years, the itching commencing as soon as he began to undress. Many of the symptoms closely resembled syphilis and the affection of the cheek in one of the provers was actually diagnosed as syphilitic by a doctor who saw him in Miiller's absence. The left side of head, face and abdomen were mostly affected. Axillary symptoms proceed from right to left. In one case, a nurse poisoned her left arm some years before from septic and possibly syphilitic cause, inflammation of Jugions regia the axillary glands ensued, first of the left then of the right, leaving an eczematous itching condition. The glands of the groin also became affected. Elaps. 200c relieved the bulk of the conditions, but there was still a little irritation occasionally in the axilla and Jug-r. 2c three times a day was given. Five days after beginning the Jug-r., an eruption of minute vesicles appeared on her back, itching a great deal. It extended up the center of her back from sacrum to mid-dorsal region, spreading out below, tapering above. She had scratched holes in two places. The rash was worse after washing. All soreness and irritation had gone from the arms and axilla. The rash was antidoted with Rhus-t. 2c. She had no more trouble with her glands. Muller observed, “In the digestive organs it causes derangement and irritation, which simultaneously call forth abnormal symptoms in other organs, especially in the head. After this action, which is brief, appear various exanthematous symptoms, which appear late and run a chronic course.” RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Rhus-t. Compare: (1) Jug-c., Cary. (2) Rhus-t. - skin. (3) Graph. - tinea favosa behind ears. (4) Rumex - rash worse undressing. (5) Mez., Merc. (6) Cean. - spleen. (7) Lyc. - flatulence. Follows well: Elaps. - axillary affections, black hemorrhages. Sulph. - head hot, cold limbs. Grind. - pain over left eye. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Fullness and bloated of the stomach. Burning in stomach. Hiccough more violent after eating. Belchings are violent, frequent, loud, tasting as after eating fat. Nausea at 6 a.m. and after supper. Vomiting, woke suddenly vomited food eaten four hours before, then slept without further trouble.

Abdomen - Fullness, bloated, tension and heaviness in the abdomen. Pain in epigastric region with distention of abdomen. Drawing with pressure in region of spleen. Pain above umbilicus.

Rectum - Stool twice a day, preceded or accompanied by pain in abdomen. Thin, soft, large, hard, difficult, scanty stool. Large stool, then burning pain and pressure in anus. Stool delayed. Constipation. Itching at the anus in the evening, with stitches, compelling one to walk about.

Male - Frequent erections day and night. Burning in penis after sex.

Female - Menses preceded by pressive drawing pains in the abdomen, worse by motion, accompanied with general exhaustion and loss of appetite. Menstruation early, too profuse, discharge of a large quantity of black, pitch-like clots. Food - Unusually great appetite without increase of thirst. Thirstlessness while eating and aversion to wine. Appetite lost. Thirst increased. Aversion to tobacco smoking in the evening.

Chest - Oppression. Sticking in lungs not dependent on motion or respiration. Itching on the sternum.

Back - Stitches in sacral region. Violent stitches in the small of the back, causing one to tremble.

Limbs - Drawing pain, as if sprained. Paralyzed feeling in legs and knees with weakness. Sticking and itching in right leg and right fingers.

Sleep - Yawning in afternoon with stretching. Sleepiness. Inability to sleep after dinner, though inclined to do so earlier than usual. Restless sleep with frightful dreams.

Skin - Comedones and acne of the face. Itching and eruptions of small red pustules. Pimples on face, red pimples on face, neck, shoulders and back. Scalp red and itches violently at night. Crusta lactea with soreness around ears. Chancre-like ulcer. Axillary glands suppurate.

Modalities - Worse by motion. Worse after fat food, evening, at 9 p.m. and after 9 p.m. Migraine worse by speaking. Pain in abdomen worse by laughing. Warmth of bed aggravates toothache. Itching, worse at night. Rash aggravated by undressing, washing.

Kidneys - Frequent desire to pass water from loss of tone of sphincter. Constant urging and involuntary dribbling. Copious urine, but no thirst. Urine scanty, clear, dark red.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Backache. Calculus. Catarrh. Dropsy. Dysuria. Flatulence. Headache. Kidney, diseases. Rheumatism. Scars…

PHARMACY - june. Juncuseffusus. Softrush. Common rush. Juncus communis. N. O. Juncaceae. Tincture of root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Backache. Calculus. Catarrh. Dropsy. Dysuria. Flatulence. Headache. Kidney, diseases. Rheumatism. Scars disorders.

HERBAL - According to Nowack and Rinks, Juncus is a diuretic and has been used in dropsical, kidney stones and kidney diseases. Hartmann used the tincture with success in dysuria, strangury and ischuria. In Livonia, a decoction is used for stone and gravel. HOMEOPATHIC Junc-e. was proved by Dr. Whale, producing a number of symptoms. The exact preparation used in the proving was not recorded. Fresh plant tinctures should be used in any further experiments. The most notable symptoms were bubbling sensations in various parts. A number of pressive and sticking pains were noted in the chest. Pulling in cervical vertebrae in neck muscles. Rumbling of flatus in abdomen; abdominal symptoms were markedly better when flatus was emitted. Rheumatic pains worse by rest, on left side, appeared or were worse at night and came on again in morning and evening. Worse flexing parts, bending sideways. Better stretching out arm. Chilliness worse on uncovering. Better by motion. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Rhus-t. - worse rest and uncovering, better stretching. (2) Berb. - bubbling sensations. (3) Sil. - scars. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke

name: Juniperus Communis
author: Murphy
constitution: Allergies. Cedar, fever. Coryza. Coughs. Dropsy. Dysmenorrhea. Hay fever. Hemorrhages. Nephritis. Pyelitis.
keynote:
PHARMACY - juni-c. Juniperus communis. Juniper berries. N. O. Gymnosperm of the Conifer. Cupressaceae. Juniperus. Tincture of fresh ripe berries. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Cedar, fever. Coryza. Coughs. Dropsy. Dysmenorrhea. Hay fever.…
full:
PHARMACY - juni-c. Juniperus communis. Juniper berries. N. O. Gymnosperm of the Conifer. Cupressaceae. Juniperus. Tincture of fresh ripe berries. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Cedar, fever. Coryza. Coughs. Dropsy. Dysmenorrhea. Hay fever. Hemorrhages. Nephritis. Pyelitis.

HERBAL - Gin owes its distinctive properties to the oil of juniper berries, perhaps explaining why the spirit is in such popular repute as a remedy for dysmenorrhea. It has a very powerful action on the kidneys and has cured cases of kidney dropsy.

HOMEOPATHIC - Juni-c. has notbeen proved, but sufficient is known of its action to warrant its inclusion and to show the analogy between its action and that of Sabina. Hale commended it in certain coughs with scanty, loaded urine. He said German doctors used juniper in gastric affections, abdominal flatulence and colic. Catarrhal inflammation of kidneys. Dropsy with suppression of urine. Elderly persons with poor digestion and scanty secretion of urine. Chronic pyelitis.

Nose - Coryza. Hay fever. Allergies. Violent sneezing from cedar pollen. Comments - Hale wrote, “I have known cases of dysmenorrhea and uterine hemorrhage cured by the common Juniper, and I have treated some kidney and bladder difficulties with Juniper. The popularity of pure gin in dysmenorrhea is owing to the effects of the oil of Juniper berries which it contains. “In domestic practice, an infusion of Juniper leaves and berries is used successfully in amenorrhea and dysmenorrhea, as well as retention, suppression, and other urinary troubles. “In some cases of dropsy, a tincture of the berries, or the oil of Juniper, will act on the kidneys favorably after the failure of other medicines. “We ought to have provings of the common Juniper, and give it a place in our Materia Medica. I would also suggest that the tincture be made from equal parts by weight of the fresh berries and green leaves. The Oil of Juniper of commerce is made from the berries alone. “German physicians make much use of Juniper in gastric complaints, in abdominal flatulence, colics, and even in some hepatic affections. I know that the 3x of Oleum juniperus is useful in certain coughs, with scanty urine, loaded with solid matters.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) All-c., Wye., Sabin., Tereb. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Hale. Murphy.

Male - Prostatic discharge.

Chest - Painful ribs and sternum from coughing attacks (Bry.).

Kidneys - Nephritis. Strangury, bloody, scanty urine, violet odor (Tereb.). Weight in kidney region. Pyelitis. Kidney hyperemia (Eucal.). Lungs - Severe, painful coughs. Cough with scanty, loaded urine.

PHARMACY - juni. Juniperus virginianus. Red cedar. N. O. Gymnosperm of the Conifer. Tincture of fresh twigs. Tincture of twigs and berries. Tincture of the oil. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Chilliness. Comatose. Convulsions. Cystitis. Delirium. Dropsy. Dysuria. Eyes, twitching. Fever. Nausea. Pyelitis. Strangury. Strokes. Tetanus. Uterine, hemorrhage. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - The effects of Juni. have been largely observed on women who have taken it to stimulate the uterus or bring on the menses. A number of fatal cases have occurred from overdose of the herb. The patients passing into violent convulsions, followed by an apoplectic or stroke condition, insensibility and collapse. Hands at times clenched. Jaws firmly fixed. Staggering. Comatose sleep. Chilliness. Rigors followed by fever. Considerable fever and pain, similar to labor pains. Sweats. Pulse very irregular. Persistent dragging pain in back. Hyperemia of kidneys. Pyelitis and cystitis. Dropsy of the aged with suppressed urine. Violent tenesmus of bladder. Constant urging to urinate. Dysuria, burning, cutting pain in urethra when urinating. Uterine hemorrhage. Mind - Emotional during the paroxysm of fever. Fright. Raved incoherently. Delirious. Insensible state. Moaning.

Head - Head felt as if enclosed with an iron band.

Eyes - Eyes bloodshot. Sclerotic congestion. Pupils dilated. Eyes glare and twitch. Eyes felt as if bursting from their sockets.

Face - Very red, swollen and livid face. Veins of the face, head, and neck fully distended. Ecchymosis.

Throat - Fauces in spots denuded of their mucus covering. REFERENCES - Allen. Clarke.

Stomach - Considerable distension and tenderness at pit of stomach. Stomach pain. Sick and distressed in stomach. Nausea and vomiting a black and then a greenish matter. Heartburn.

Abdomen - Abdomen swollen and hot. Complained of intensity of pain in abdomen. Pain in the bowels. Thirst.

Rectum - Violent purging. Bowels loose.

Female - Uterine hemorrhage. Food - Great thirst.

Sleep - Deep, comatose sleep.

Skin - Skin dry and parched.

Kidneys - Hyperemia of kidneys. Pyelitis. Great difficulty in passing urine.

Bladder - Cystitis. Violent tenesmus of bladder. Constant urging to urinate. Dysuria, burning, cutting pain in urethra when urinating.

PHARMACY - just. Justiciaadhatoda. Malabar nut. Adhatoda vasica. Vasika. Singhee. An Indian Shrub. Acanthaceae. Tincture of the fresh leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Appetite, loss. Asthma. Blood, spitting, Bronchitis. Colds. Constipation. Coryza. Coughs. Depression. Dyspnea. Fevers. Hay fever. Jaundice. Pneumonia. Sneezing. Thirst. Tuberculosis. Vomiting. Whooping cough.

HERBAL - The Ayurvedic physicians of India prize justicia. They are so very sure of its efficacy that they call it Vaidyamata, i.e. mother of physicians. They claim that no death can occur from cough of any kind if Vasika can play its role and find time to display its healing virtues.

HOMEOPATHIC - Dry, spasmodic, constricted cough. Violent dyspnea associated with the cough. Threatened suffocation. Whooping cough, with breath loss, pale, stiff and blue, and rigidity of the body. Cough with tightness of chest, as if it would burst with bronchial rattle, obstruction of breath and sneezing. Vomiting with the cough, no food or drink is retained. Dry mucus membranes, especially of the mouth and throat, with thirst. Tough expectoration. Acute catarrhal conditions of the respiratory tract, particularly in the beginning. Colds. Coryza, fluent, acrid with violent sneezing, coughing or asthmatic attacks. Fits of sneezing with lachrymation and loss of smell and taste. Allergies and hay fever. Bronchitis, pneumonia. First stages of tuberculosis, with spitting of blood. Hoarseness. Functional derangements of the liver. Jaundice. Thirst. Great loss of appetite. Obstinate constipation. Stiffening out, trembling and convulsions with cough or fever. Puffy hands and feet in morning. Chilliness. Fever. Marked oversensitiveness to external impressions. MIND- Irritability, easily angered. Badhumor. Anxious and discouraged. Depression of spirits. Averse to conversation. Sensitive to external impressions.

Head - Hot, full and heavy head.

Eyes - Lachrymation.

Nose - Allergies and hayfever. Profuse, fluent coryza, with constant sneezing. Coryza with cough. Fits of sneezing with lachrymation and loss of smell and taste.

Mouth - Mouth is dry. Loss of taste.

Throat - Hoarseness, larynx painful. Dry and painful during empty swallowing. Tenacious mucus. COMMENTS - Blackwood wrote, “This one of the most ancient drugs in India, the most highly valued by Ayurveda. Its field of use is in colds, coryza, cough of any kind, vomiting, bronchitis, pneumonia, tuberculosis, spitting of blood. Fevers, jaundice, loss of appetite, and constipation. These ailments are what the ancient physicians use it for.” It was proved by two men, twenty-seven and thirty-two years of age; their symptoms were later clinically verified. Proving symptoms included catarrh, violent sneezing, watering eyes, profuse coryza, loss of appetite, vomiting, liver pains, hoarseness and very painful suffocative cough with blood streaked mucus and high temperature. Ghose recorded a case of coryza. “My son had an attack of cold. He had fluent coryza, with constant sneezing; there was hoarseness with swollen nose; there was stoppage of nose at night; there was also thirst; no appetite existed; there were occasional coughing fits, but no expectoration ensued. “I prescribed Justicia 1 x every three hours. After administration of the third dose he fell asleep. He came round within three days. From the second day there was no hoarseness.” Ghose also recorded another case of coryza. The son of Babu Bhupati Choudhuri, of Bhowanipore. suffered from a severe attack of cold. Copious fluent coryza, accompanied by violent coughing, the eyes were somewhat swollen and watered all the time; he was feverish. Ghose prescribed Just, lx every three hours, and he was fully cured within two days. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Seems to come between All-c. and Euphr. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Blackwood. Boer- icke. Clarke. Ghose.

Stomach - Nausea and vomiting.

Chest - Tightness across chest, as if it would burst. Coughs - Cough with sneezing. Dry cough from sternal region all over chest. Paroxysmal cough with suffocative obstruction of respiration. Whooping cough.

Limbs - Puffy hands and feet in morning.

Modalities - Worse in a close room, from dust, noise, eating.

Liver - Jaundice. Liver weakness. Liver pains. Lungs - Acute catarrhal conditions of the respiratory tract. Severe dyspnea with cough. Obstruction of breath and sneezing. Asthmatic attacks, cannot endure a close, warm room. Bronchitis and pneumonia. Rattling in bronchi. Tough mucus. Tuberculosis.

full:
PHARMACY - kali-acet. Kali aceticum. Potassium acetate. Acetate of potash. Kali acetas. Solution in distilled water. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Diabetes. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Urine, alkaline.

HOMEOPATHIC - Kali-acet. is well known in allopathic practice as a diuretic and, to a lesser degree, as a cathartic. Derivatives have been used in cases of dropsy, chiefly ascites and hydrothorax. The homeopathic uses are chiefly in cases of over-secretion of urine and in diarrhea. The provings have brought out a preponderance of abdominal and urinary symptoms. Great disturbance in the circulation of fluids in the tissues (Acet-ac.). Griping diarrhea. Increased flow of urine, which was more watery and alkaline. Bleeding of hemorrhoids. Weakness, trembling, profuse perspiration, especially about the head. Trembling and anxiety in whole body of transient duration. Symptoms generally worse in morning, but there was a headache, worse 4 p.m.

Head - Dull headache in morning. Headache about 4 p.m. Much perspiration of head.

Stomach - Constrictive, dull pain in stomach, extending to low down in abdomen, gradually disappearing after two hours. Dull, pressive, pinching and constrictive pain in epigastric region, coming on a few minutes after each dose and lasting an hour.

Abdomen - Unnatural distention of abdomen after dinner. Griping. An indefinite gnawing pain lasting an hour. Gnawing sensation in abdomen which lasted until evening. Pains in region of umbilicus, lasting until going to bed, when they suddenly disappeared.

Rectum - Bleeding hemorrhoids, several times during day. Diarrhea. Two stools in evening.

Limbs - Extreme weariness and trembling in all limbs in morning. Great weariness of all limbs, with some headache, disappearing half an hour after an afternoon nap.

Kidneys - Urine very much increased in quantity and very watery. Urine strongly alkaline, sweetish odor, yellow color, ammoniacal.

Temperature - Much perspiration on head, especially from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. Profuse perspiration, very offensive during exertion. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Acet-ac., Kali-c., Am-a. (2) Lyc. - worse at 4 p.m. REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Kali Arsenicosum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better on rainy days. Aversion to open air. Worse touch, lying down, warmth of bed, warmth, cold feet, noise. Worse after midnight, from 1 a.m. to 3 a.m..

keynote: PHARMACY - kali-ar. Kali arsenicosum. Potassium arsenite. Fowler's solution (the form in which Kali-ar. has been tested, consists of 1 part arsenious acid, 1 part carbonate of potash, 3 parts compound tincture of lavender, and 95 parts distilled water). Dilutions should be made…
full:
PHARMACY - kali-ar. Kali arsenicosum. Potassium arsenite. Fowler's solution (the form in which Kali-ar. has been tested, consists of 1 part arsenious acid, 1 part carbonate of potash, 3 parts compound tincture of lavender, and 95 parts distilled water). Dilutions should be made from this. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Anxiety, attacks.Asthma. Bright's disease. Cancer. Deafness. Diarrhea. Dropsy Eczema. Emaciation. Epithelioma. Exoph- thalmus. Eye, disorders. Faintness. Herpes, zoster. Jealousy. Measles. Melancholy. Miliary, rash. Lung, disorders. Neuralgias. Neurasthenia. Palpitations. Panic, attacks. Psoriasis. Skin, disorders. Tongue, neuralgia. Tremors. Varicose, veins. Ulcers.

HOMEOPATHIC - It is not possible to separate entirely the pathogenesis of Kali-ar. and Ars. Kali-ar. is the favorite form in which arsenic is prescribed by the allopaths, consequently the bulk of observations from over- dosing are due to this preparation, named Liquor arsenicalis, considered arsenic and nothing else. Much of our knowledge relating to this remedy comes to us from the effects of overdosing and protracted use of the medicine on patients suffering from chronic skin and blood diseases. The arsenic symptoms predominate. Epithelioma developed in a patient after prolonged treatment with allopathic Kali-ar. for psoriasis. During treatment for right-sided herpes, patients noted color changes in their eyes and skin. Sclerotics became thick and yellow instead of clear and bluish. The iris, which was blue, became gray. Skin, instead of being fair and florid, became muddy and older looking. Tendency towards anxiety and skin diseases. Restless, nervous. Great weakness. Emaciation, anemia. Faintness. Neurasthenia. Chilly and sensitive to cold. Cannot get too warm even in summer. Tremors. Sudden noise or touch throws the whole body into a tremor. Inveterate skin diseases, malignant tendency. Intolerable itching, worse undressing, walking, warmth. Chronic eczema. Psoriasis. Herpes zoster, measles, miliary rash. Epithelioma. Numerous small nodules under the skin. Gouty nodosities. Rheumatic, gouty and syphilitic pains. Varicose veins. Dropsy. Cauliflower-like excrescences of os uterus with flying pains, foul smelling discharges and pressure below the pelvis. Black leg ulcer running bloody, foul water with cutting, burning, itching and dyspnea. Phagedenic ulcers, deep base and turned up edges. Burning in throat. The tongue burns, numb. Tongue neuralgia. Exophthalmos, eye affections. Deafness. Aching in stomach. Passes much gas, then diarrhea. Bright's disease. Palpitations with nephritis. All the sufferings are worse at night. MIND - Morose and quarrelsome. Scolding, retired and discontented. Jealous. Anguish. Face looks frightened and anxious. Startled, fixed look, protruding brilliant eyes. Anxiety and panic attacks. Anxiety about health. Anxiety on going to bed. Anxiety with difficult breathing. Hysteria. Fears felt in the stomach. Fear of getting a life threatening disease, of high blood pressure. of having a stroke, of heart disease, of getting cancer. Fear in a crowd, of being alone, of death, dying, of being murdered, poisoned. Fear of thieves, burglars, at night, of evil. Fear that something bad will happen. Superstitious. Mental and physical restlessness. Excitable. Great nervousness. Oversensitive to noise, especially to voices. Starting from noises. Timidity. Capriciousness. Concentration difficult. Confusion. Weak memory. Depression, melancholy. Sadness when alone. Despair of recovery. Suicidal disposition. Apathy. Indifferent to everything, scarcely answered questions addressed to her or replies to them in a peevish tone. Aversion to answering questions. Behaves like amad person. Delusion head is enlarged. Sudden impulse to kill.

Head - Headache from gastric causes or catarrh. Headache in left parietal bone, as if it was sore and pressed upon by hand. Headaches worse after eating, lying, motion and noise. Headaches better sitting, external heat, hot drinks and wrapping up head. Head as if heavy and enlarged. Constricted feeling in head, as if there was a wound in the bone that was being scratched. Crusta lactea. Behaves like a crazy person.

Eyes - Startled look with protruding, brilliant eyes, pale face and sunken cheeks. Eyes red. Whites of eyes look thick and yellow. Jaundice. The blue iris becomes gray. Dark discoloration around orbit. Inflamed, itching of conjunctiva. Conjunctiva glassy. Right eye weaker, watery, as after weeping. Swollen lower eyelids. Heat and itchiness of lids, followed by swelling and tenderness. Eye sensitive to light.

Ears - Otorrhea. Ear discharge bloody, fetid and yellow.

Nose - Colds. Hay fever. Sneezing. Watery, acrid discharge. Sinusitis. Chronic nasal catarrh. Nasal discharge bloody, burning, excoriating, offensive, greenish, thick or yellow.

Face - Face pale and waxy. Complexion muddy. Puffy under eyes. Old looking. Nodular eruption on face, boils. Furfura- ceous eruption on beard.

Mouth - In middle, towards tip of tongue, a smooth, red spot with troublesome burning and numbness. Toothache, better heat, worse eating, cold drinks and during menses. Pulsating and tearing pain, radiates to ears, head and temples. Gums swollen and tender.

Throat - Some gastric cough and frequent raking of throat and fauces of a mucopurulent secretion mixed with specks of blood. Burning in throat. Sensation in throat and larynx as if forced asunder. Throat dry and sore. Throat constricted with copious flow of saliva. Complete aphonia, following skin affection.

Stomach - Anxiety feeling with palpitations from pit of stomach. Empty feeling in stomach. Sinking at epigastrium with faintness. Weight in stomach after eating. Sensation as of a ball rising from pit of stomach to larynx threatening suffocation, better by loud belching. Nausea and vomiting. Constant pain and nausea after food, frequent vomiting of ingesta.

Abdomen - Burning pain in bowels, unquenchable thirst, belly tense and painful involuntary watery stools with sense as if a red-hot iron were in anus. Frequent griping pains in bowels and constant desire for stool, considerable tenderness in whole abdomen, which is distended.

Rectum - Discharge of much gas, followed by diarrhea. Violent diarrhea. Cholera. Diarrhea worse after midnight, from milk. Stools white, watery, frothy. Foul odor, with cramps. Sensation as of a red- hot iron in anus. Hemorrhoids, bleeding, external and internal, worse walking. Sensations - The head feels larger. Protrusion of eyeballs. Burning and numbness of tongue. Tongue feels too large. Anxiety felt in solar plexus. Sensation of a ball rising from the pit of stomach to throat causing suffocation. As if a red-hot iron were in anus.

Female - Cauliflower excrescences of uterine cervix with flying pains, foul smelling discharge and pressure below pubis. Menses absent. Milk entirely arrested. Food - Appetite lost. Aversion to fat, meat. Intense thirst. Drinks in small sips. Desires sweet, sour, vinegar, fruits, lemon, refreshing food. Desires mustard, spices, milk, coffee, warm food, fat. Worse from milk, ice cream, sour, fruits, melon, strawberry, alcohol, spoiled food.

Heart - Heart attacks with anxiety and fear. Palpitations with anxiety and fear. High blood pressure from worry and fear. Weak heart. Pulse weak and contracted, small, scarcely perceptible, rapid.

Back - Backache with sciatica, worse pressure. Much pain and tenderness down spine.

Limbs - Gouty nodosities, worse change of weather. Crampy feeling of lower limbs with partial loss of motion and sensation, livid in places, tending to slough. Aching pain in right shoulder and elbow, followed by herpetic eruption. Knees bent up so he could not move his feet. Swollen ankles. Palms and soles speckled over with corns. Varicose veins of legs. Ulcers on legs with general psoriasis. Black ulcer on leg, running bloody, foul water, with cutting, burning, itching and dyspnea. Lungs - Anxiety with difficult breathing. Asthma with panic attacks. Asthma, rapid, anxious breathing, worse 2 a.m. to 3 a.m. Asthma better from sitting, worse lying down. Pneumonia with stitching pains in pleura.

Sleep - Restless and anxious sleep. Sleeplessness, worse 1 a.m. to 4 a.m. Sleeps with hand over the heart. Nightmares, vivid dreams.

Skin - Dry, scaly, wilted skin. Acne, pustules worse during menses. Chronic eczema, intolerable itching, worse from warmth, walking, undressing. Psoriasis, lichen. Psoriasis in numerous patches, with great itching. Discoloration of skin after psoriasis. Numerous small nodules under skin. Phagedenic ulcers. Fissures in bends of arms and knees. Skin cancer, where suddenly an alarming malignancy without any external signs sets in.

Modalities - Better on rainy days. Aversion to open air. Worse touch, lying down, warmth of bed, warmth, cold feet, noise. Worse after midnight, from 1 a.m. to 3 a.m.

Tongue - Tongue clear, whitish, red like raw beef. Tongue coated on edges only with mucus stripes. Tongue swollen, felt too large in mouth, numb. Neuralgic or burning in tongue. Smooth red spot in middle of tongue toward tip that burns and is numb. Vertigo - Vertigo while walking in the open air. COMMENTS - Cases of Kali-ar. poisoning with massive doses present nothing to distinguish them from cases of other arsenical preparations, but Kali-ar. has had a short proving and a number of cases of allopathic provings are on record. Jonathan Hutchinson recorded a number of cases of right-sided herpes. One of his patients observed that, while taking Kali- ar., her sclerotics became thick and yellow instead of clear and bluish. The iris, which was blue, became more gray. Her skin, instead of being fair and florid, became muddy and older looking. This was a mystery to Hutchinson as he usually gave Kali-ar. to make the skin clearer, but he was compelled to record the fact, though he did not apparently perceive the homeopathic solution of the mystery. Hutchinson also noted cases of epithelioma developing after prolonged medication with Kali-ar. for psoriasis. In another case, an attack of measles was almost exactly mimicked. Useful as a backup for Ars., particularly if Ars. palliates or stops working. Skin symptoms with a tendency toward malignancy. Psoriasis. Herpes. Itching, worse at night, on undressing, and by warmth. Lupus. Indicated for the burning pains of dying cancer patients. Deafness associated with constant sickness. Asthma, worse 2 a.m. to 3 a.m. (Ars. worse 11 p.m. to 2 a.m.). Sinus problems. Shortness of breath, hyperventilate with panic. Weak from going up stairs (Calc., Sil.). Fainting spells and fear of fainting (Gels., Arg-n.). Pulsations in the body followed by shaking and trembling. Sinking sensations. Fevers and shaking chills. Migraines, or fear of getting migraines, causing panic. Panic stricken (Aeon.). Panic attacks, fear of having a panic attack. Chronic hypochondriacs, fear of heart attack, high blood pressure, stroke or cancer. Fear of death. Agoraphobia, claustrophobia. Superstitious (Arg- n., Zinc, Rhus-t., Ars.). Suspicious of others. Periodic rushes of adrenaline, pheochromocytoma. Ailments after fright. Panic with a burning or energy in the solar plexus area (Kali-c., Ign., Calc., Care.). Better when distracted from panic attacks or fears. Despair over recovery. Desires company, insecure (Ars.). Hypersensitive to surroundings (Phos.). Chilly, sensitive to drafts. Restless and sleepless. Anxiety about dead people or dreams about dead people. May dream of fire and wake up in a panic that the house is on fire. Can lie on their left and hold their heart when they sleep. May get palpitations when sleeping on the right. Lump rising from the stomach to the throat. Thirsty, but aggravated by cold drinks. Desires sweets, warm drinks. Marked periodicity (Ars.), symptoms were worse every other day in the morning, mind symptoms worse every third day. Worse after midnight, on right side. The right-sidedness of Ars. was reproduced in the right-sided herpes, repeatedly noticed by Hutchinson, but there was a left-sided headache. RELATIONS - In some cases of overdosing, Kali-i. proved antidotal. Forother antidotes see Ars., which it greatly resembles and with which it must be compared. Compare: ( 1 ) Ars., Lev., Nat-a. and other arsenic compounds. (2) Chin. - periodicity. (3) Cic., Op. - fixed eyeballs. (4) Rumx. and Jug-r.-worse when undressing. (5) lod., Kali-bi., Merc-c., Kali-c. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Grimmer. Murphy. Phatak.

Kidneys - Urine scanty with pellicle.

Perspiration - Sweats when walking.

Temperature - Cold temperature on skin. Fever with lassitude.

name: Kali Bichromicum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from heat, wrapping up, pressure, motion, short sleep. Skin symptoms better cold weather. Open air ameliorates, especially vertigo, but aggravates the gastric complaints and chilliness. Worse from cold, damp, open air, spring, hot weather. Worse from undressing, stooping, sitting, after sleep, morning, 2 a.m. to 3 a.m. Worse from suppressed catarrh, protruding tongue, alcohol, beer. Worse by eating, causes cough, weight in stomach..
