PHARMACY - luf-op. Luffa operculata. Esponjina. Cabacinha. N.O. Cucurbitaceae. Columbia. South America. Tincture of the dried seeds. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Breathlessness. Bronchial, asthma. Coryza. Emaciation. Headaches. Laryngitis. Nasal polyps. Pharyngitis Rhinitis. Sinusitis. Tachycardia.

HOMEOPATHIC - Luf-op. is an exotic plant which comes from Columbia and wa introduced to Europe by W. Schwabe. The symptomatology was undertaken by him oi eleven people (six men and five women), using the 5x, 3x, and 2x potencies. Each potency wa used for one week. Lassitude and physical fatigue. Frontal an< occipital headache. Acute or chronic inflam mation of the mucus membranes in the nasa cavities. Hypertrophy or atrophy of the nasa mucus membranes. Hypothyroid. MIND - Lack of reaction with indifference an prostration.

Head - Violent headaches going from th forehead towards the nape of the necl Pain in the occipital region. Frontal pair with vertigo and musca volitantes.

Eyes - Musca volitantes. Food - Extreme hunger with emaciatior Painful feeling of thirst and hunger, dil ficult to satisfy.

Nose - Acute rhinitis and pharyngitis. Purulent sinusitis. Chronic atrophic rhinitis. Head colds with pale or yellow nasal secretion, especially in the morning. Dryness of the nasal mucus with sticky scab formations. Nasal polyps.

Mouth - Dryness of the tongue, back of the throat and pharynx. Burning sensation at the tip of the tongue.

Stomach - Diffuse gastric pains. Empty feeling in the stomach. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Merc-i-r. - Coryza with hoarseness. Abundant discharge with post-nasal mucus, aggravated in the open air, ameliorated by heat. (2) Cinnb. - Pressing pains in the bones of the skull and nose with discharge of thick mucus and often nosebleed. (3) Hep. - Sour, fetid secretions with blocked nose immediately on going out into the cold air. Ameliorated in a warm room. REFERENCES - Julian.

Rectum - Tendency to constipation.

Heart - Tachycardia. Lungs - Breathlessness from the least effort. Bronchial asthma.

Skin - Formation of small purulent, itching pimples on the face, lower lip and chin. Loses hair in abundance.

Modalities - Better in fresh air, worse in a room in dry air.

name: Luna
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better by cold application. Pains, better in open air, belchings and by passing flatus from vagina. Worse before and after full moon, during increasing moon, exposure to moonlight. Worse after sleep, from milk..
constitution: Acidity. Colic. Edema. Epilepsy. Female, disorders. Headaches. Heartburn. Inter-menstrual flow. Insomnia. Menses, problems. Nightmares. Ovary, pain. Scabies. Sleep, disorders. Sleepwalking. Somnambulism. Sycosis. Worms.
keynote: PHARMACY - luna. Luna. Moonlight. Moon's rays. Sugar of milk is exposed on a glass plate to the moon's rays and stirred with a glass rod meanwhile. The sugar of milk so charged is dynamized in the usual way (Fincke). Higgins made a preparation by exposing pure water to the…
full:
PHARMACY - luna. Luna. Moonlight. Moon's rays. Sugar of milk is exposed on a glass plate to the moon's rays and stirred with a glass rod meanwhile. The sugar of milk so charged is dynamized in the usual way (Fincke). Higgins made a preparation by exposing pure water to the moon's rays for three or four hours in South America and then dynamizing the water so charged. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Acidity. Colic. Edema. Epilepsy. Female, disorders. Headaches. Heartburn. Inter-menstrual flow. Insomnia. Menses, problems. Nightmares. Ovary, pain. Scabies. Sleep, disorders. Sleepwalking. Somnambulism. Sycosis. Worms.

HOMEOPATHIC - Goullon contributed to the Rev. Hom. Beige, January, 1897, a notable article on “The Influence of the Moon on the Human Organism,” in which he mentioned, among other interesting facts, that sleepwalking is a lunar effect, that worm disorders are most troublesome at the full noon, and that goiter changes more or less with the moon. Epilepsy worse at full moon may need Luna (Sil.). Scabies and worm disorders, worse at full moon. Nervous affections, especially in subjects of sycosis, influenced by the moon. Excessive edema of face, neck and hands with neuralgic pains in the swollen parts. Skin diseases. Sour belchings, especially if tasting of ingesta. Acrid yellow leucor- rhea through the day with backache. Pain in right ovary. MIND - Mental faculties, especially ability to receive, retain and express ideas, are most powerfully affected by the full rays of the moon. Worse from exposure to moonlight. Worse from certain moon phases. Worse the day before the full moon. Ailments from full moon. Confusion of mind. Difficult concentration. Absent-minded. Forgetful. Mistakes in spelling, talking. Mindnotclear. Spaced-out feeling. Feeling detached, disconnected. Apathy, lack of motivation. Disinclined for mental or physical labor. Somnambulism. Mood changeable, worse before and during menses. Sensitive, emotionally. Depressed and anxious. Dwells on past disagreeable occurrences (Nat-m.). Irritable and impatient, easily angered, worse before menses. Abrupt. Anger, in outbursts. Temper tantrums. Resentment, indifferent towards husband or partner. Irritable towards own children. Weeping after anger. Irritability on being spoken to. Wants to be let alone.

Head - Slight giddiness with slight bitter taste on left side of tongue with increased saliva. Sharp pain just above root of nose. Congestion of blood to head with sensation of great fullness. Migraine headaches. Pain in occiput, changing to lame feeling on retiring. Headache before menses. Woke with very severe headache. Headache better by magnetic passes. Severe frontal headache during menses.

Eyes - Swollen eyes that burn and sting (Apis). Sharp stinging sensation, leaving a smarting. Stinging in right eye. Weakness of eyes and feeling of sand. Swelling of eyelids and profuse discharge of purulent matter with a painful smarting and profuse lachrymation without heat or change of color.

Nose - Sensation of a cold in head. Coryza, sneezing and pain in occiput. Discharge of yellowish-green mucus from nose. Sensation of heavy cold in head with lachrymation, at 4 p.m.

Face - Edema of face.

Mouth - Bitter taste on the left side of tongue with increased flow of saliva. Increased saliva, all day, on waking, with faint feeling in stomach, with stinging in right eye.

Throat - Some soreness in throat. COMMENTS - Conditions affected by the moon, particularly epilepsy, migraine headaches, insomnia, emotional and hormonal changes, neuralgic pains, and swelling of the hands and face. Conditions worse during full moon (Calc., Sil., Arg-n.). Dreams and nightmares, particularly in children. Dreams of dying. Irritable, unclear mind. Increased worm activity. Growing pains in children, better walking. Swollen eyes that burn and sting (Apis). Sensation of sand or grit in the eyes (Euphr.). Pain in the occiput. Menstrual cramps with bearing down pains. Symptoms better in open air and cool air. Worse from sleep, milk. According to Menuret, skin diseases are frequently influenced by the moon. He noted a case of eczematous affection which increased with each waning moon and was at its maximum intensity at the new moon when it covered the whole face and chest and was accompanied by unbearable itching. Then there was gradual improvement and the face became smooth, but scarcely had the full moon passed when all began again. Moritz Hoffmann observed a young girl (daughter of an epileptic mother) whose whole body became swollen at every new moon, the swelling disappearing as the moon waned. Mead told of a child who was subject to convulsions at each waning moon. Gale remarked that with weakly persons' excitability is most pronounced at the new moon and the full moon. Swan communicated a proving of Luna 1,000c. made on a female physician, Dr. S. J. W. The prover was menstruating at the time the proving was commenced, but was otherwise in good health. Repeated doses were taken for two days. The effects lasted four weeks. Swan cured, with Luna, a case of excessive edema of face, neck and hands with neuralgic pain in the swollen parts. Goullon quoted a remarkable case of sleepwalking from the Cercle Medical. “A youth of fifteen in good health in other respects, had been withdrawn from his apprenticeship, on account of his nightly promenades on roofs. He was put in a private asylum. Although his room was oriented so that no actual moon-rays could reach it, the moon nevertheless exercised a potent influence upon him. “As soon as it reaches the horizon he gets out of bed and carefully with closed eyes, moves towards a window, so high that he has to jump in order to reach and open it. As it is barricaded with an iron trellis he gets down and, crossing the corridor, goes to the outer door, above which is a window. “With cat-like agility he climbs up to this, when he is seized by three warders, who take him back to his room, where, only after the moon has set, can he lie down and go to sleep. In the morning he remembers nothing. At full moon the symptoms are still more extraordinary.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Aeth., Mag-c. - worse from milk. (2) Worse at new moon: Alum., Am-c., Bufo, Calc., Caust., Clem., Cupr., Daph., Lyc., Sabal., Sep., Sil. (3) Worse at full moon: Alum., Calc., Cycl., Graph., Kali- n., Nat-c„ Nat-m., Sabin., Sep., Sil., Spon., Sulph., Teucr. (4) Worse during increasing moon: Am., Clem. (5) Worse during waning moon - Dulc., Thuj. REFERENCES - Clarke. Murphy. Swan.

Stomach - Burning, worse after drinking milk. Flatulency with burning in stomach. Sour belchings, tasting of ingesta. Woke at midnight with severe heartburn and great distress in stomach, had to get out of bed.

Abdomen - Faint feeling in stomach on awaking. Sensation of great distention. Colic, commencing two inches above umbilicus and seeming to pass directly upward to stomach, causing desire to bend forward. Pain around umbilicus, better by belchings. Pain through liver and spleen, worse 3 p.m.

Rectum - Urgent desire for stool, immediately better by passing flatus.

Female - Menstrual cramps with bearing down pains. Menses less free, strings of dark blood, colic pain above umbilicus better by eructation. Mensesflow heavier. Menses returned two days after ceasing. Uterine hemorrhage. Bearing-down sensation. Sharp pain left side vagina, then grows suddenly sharper, again returning to vagina and passing through to rectum. Sharp pains fly from vagina through abdomen, ceasing in stomach-pit. Pain better by passing flatus from vagina. Cramp-like pains in pelvic region, as if uterus were being contracted by a strong electric current. Food - No appetite, slight nausea. Desires something, does not know what. Immediately ejected cup of tea during headache, the tea tasted sour.

Chest - After ascending stairs, a peculiar heating sensation, beginning at lower extremity of sternum and extending outwards. Attachment of diaphragm on each side to a point under each arm, at same time warm glow down arms to fingertips, most in left.

Heart - Pulse rapid. Suffocative sensation around heart. On retching, peculiar feeling around heart as though it stopped beating, better by belchings, worse by lying down.

Back - Very severe pain in sacral region in evening.

Limbs - Swollen feeling. Slight rheumatic pains in shoulders, especially left. Sharp, quick pain in left cervical nerve, intermittent every few seconds. Great lameness in anterior tibial region from walking. After retiring, aching in bones of lower limbs with pain in lumbo-sacral region. Sensation as if tightly bound in right calf and in hypochondria. Pain like growing-pain above left knee, better walking. Sharp pain in left great toe.

Sleep - Insomnia, worse moonlight. Somnambulism. Nightmares after exposure to moonlight, particularly in children. Dreams of murder, death. Wakes after frightful dreams. Symptoms worse on waking. Felt as if had not slept enough.

Skin - Unbearable itching. Stinging, itching right side of body as if an insect was biting the parts, felt most on foot, leg and forearm. Eczema.

Modalities - Better by cold application. Pains, better in open air, belchings and by passing flatus from vagina. Worse before and after full moon, during increasing moon, exposure to moonlight. Worse after sleep, from milk.

Kidneys - Urine profuse, clear and watery, at times darker.

Temperature - Woke 6 a.m. with severe chill, after which he had headache, felt sick and weak all day, at night had horrible dreams of death.

name: Lupulus Humulus
author: Murphy
constitution: Alcoholism. Delirium. Diuresis. Dyspepsia. Dysuria. Excitement. Faintness. Gonorrhea. Headaches. Insomnia. Jaundice. Nausea. Paralytic, weakness. Sexual, weakness. Vertigo. Vomiting.
keynote:
PHARMACY - lup. Lupulus humulus. Hops. N. O. Cannabinacae of the Urticacee. Tincture of the seeded spikes. Trituration. Tincture of Lupuline, small resinous granules covering the scales. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Delirium. Diuresis.…
full:
PHARMACY - lup. Lupulus humulus. Hops. N. O. Cannabinacae of the Urticacee. Tincture of the seeded spikes. Trituration. Tincture of Lupuline, small resinous granules covering the scales. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Delirium. Diuresis. Dyspepsia. Dysuria. Excitement. Faintness. Gonorrhea. Headaches. Insomnia. Jaundice. Nausea. Paralytic, weakness. Sexual, weakness. Vertigo. Vomiting.

HERBAL - The “hops pillow” as a remedy for sleeplessness is well known, and this sleep provoking effect passes into delirium and stupefaction.

HOMEOPATHIC - Lup. has had a somewhat extensive proving, to the symptoms of which have been added the effects of working with hops and of sleeping in rooms where hops were stored. Giddiness and stupefaction. Drawing and twitching in almost every muscle. Nervous tremors, wakefulness and delirium of alcoholics. Unstrung condition of the nervous system attended with nausea, dizziness, headache following a night's debauch. Infantile jaundice. Urethral burning. Slow pulse. MIND - Morbid vigilance. Highly excited. Confusion. Frequent starting from deep sleep with violent delirium from which he could only be aroused with great difficulty, immediately lapsing again into stupor. Delirium of alcoholics. Mental functions remained indolent several months.

Head - Dull, heavy headache with dizziness. Rush of blood to head and eyes. Heat in head and face with confusion and dull headache. Violent pulsating of temporal arteries. Drawing and twitching in every muscle.

Eyes - Pupils remained dilated for several months.

Stomach - Sensation of increased warmth in stomach. Nauseating eructations, tasting of hops. Nausea, vomiting.

Abdomen - Fermentation and dull pains in abdomen. Dull griping in lower abdomen with nausea.

Rectum - Stool softer than usual with urging so great he could hardly reach the closet. Stool retarded.

Male - Diminishes and allays sexual appetite. Painful erections. Emissions, depending on sexual weakness and after onanism. Spermatorrhea.

Female - Diminishes and allays sexual appetite. Food - Appetite lost. Great thirst.

Heart - Slow pulse.

Neck - Strong pulsation of carotids.

Limbs - Great twitching of tendons. Paralytic weakness. Lungs - Respiration is deep, almost stertorous.

Sleep - Drowsy during the day. Sopor. Insomnia.

Skin - Scarlatina-like eruption on face. Feels like insects crawling under skin, feels chapped, skin peels.

Tongue - Tongue thickly coated, dry. Vertigo - Vertigo, stupefaction. COMMENTS - A child of twelve, who remained several days in a room where hops were being picked, experienced frequent starting up from deep sleep with violent delirium from which he could only be aroused with great difficulty, when he recognized the bystanders, but immediately fell backward into stupor. It was months before he recovered. The effects which remained included dilated pupils, mental indolence, unsteady movements, and erythema. Other symptoms are a turning sensation in stomach, fermenting in abdomen. Burning in urethra during urination. Nausea and vomiting. Faintness better in open air. Twitching of tendons. RELATIONS - Antidotes: Coff., vinegar. Compare: (1) Urt-u., Cann-i., Cann-s., Nux- v., Op. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Kidneys - Diuresis. Urine retarded, dark brown, clear. Burning in urethra during urination, not better by coffee.

Perspiration - Perspiration profuse, clammy, greasy.

name: Lycium Barbarum
author: Murphy
constitution: Anemia. Arthritis. Cancer. Cough. Diabetes. Nosebleeds.
keynote:
PHARMACY - lyci-b. Lycium barbarum. Goji berries. Chinese wolfberry. English wolfberry. Matrimony vine. Chinese boxthorn. N. O. Solanaceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anemia. Arthritis. Cancer. Cough. Diabetes. Nosebleeds.

HERBAL - The term “Goji”…
full:
PHARMACY - lyci-b. Lycium barbarum. Goji berries. Chinese wolfberry. English wolfberry. Matrimony vine. Chinese boxthorn. N. O. Solanaceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anemia. Arthritis. Cancer. Cough. Diabetes. Nosebleeds.

HERBAL - The term “Goji” is the common name given to the Lycium barbarum berry by the Tibetans. Goji usually refers to varieties of Lycium called in English wolfberry, matrimony vine, or Chinese boxthorn. The berries flourish in the tranquil valleys that are naturally protected by the Himalayan Mountains, and have been treasured for centuries by the Himalayan people. Traditionally it has been used to treat inflammations, skin irritations, nosebleeds and aches and pains, and has also been used as a sedative. The fruit is the main source of medicinal extracts, although the leaves are also sometimes consumed as food. In China, it is often used in combination with other botanicals to treat poor vision, anemia, and cough. In the tests, a polysaccharide isolated from Lycium has been shown to have anti-cancer effects. It also has some immune enhancing properties. COMMENTS - An evergreen shrub that is often spiny and grows in temperate and subtropical regions, the two species most commonly used in folk medicine are Lycium chinense or Lycium barbarum, both in the nightshade (Solanaceae) family. One legend recounts that during the Tang Dynasty (around 800 AD), a well had been dug beside a wall near a famous Buddhist temple that was covered with goji vines. Over the years, countless berries had fallen into the well. Those who prayed there had the ruddy complexion of good health, and even at the age of eighty they had no white hair and had lost no teeth, simply because they drank the water from the well. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Crat., Sabal serr. REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Lycopersicum Esculentum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better in warm room, from external heat. The headache in one instance was completely better by tobacco smoke. Worse by noise, motion..
constitution: Backache. Catarrh. Coryza. Deltoid rheumatism. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Eyes disorders. Gout. Headache. Leucorrhea. Lupus. Metrorrhagia. Obesity. Polyuria. Rheumatism. Throat sore.
keynote:
PHARMACY - lycpr. Lycopersicum esculentum. Tomato. Solanum lycopersicum. Love apple. N. O. Solanaceae. Tincture of ripe fruit. Tincture of fresh flowering plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Backache. Catarrh. Coryza. Deltoid rheumatism. Diabetes.…
full:
PHARMACY - lycpr. Lycopersicum esculentum. Tomato. Solanum lycopersicum. Love apple. N. O. Solanaceae. Tincture of ripe fruit. Tincture of fresh flowering plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Backache. Catarrh. Coryza. Deltoid rheumatism. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Eyes disorders. Gout. Headache. Leucorrhea. Lupus. Metrorrhagia. Obesity. Polyuria. Rheumatism. Throat sore.

HOMEOPATHIC - Clarke knew of one instance in which the slightest indulgence in tomatoes brings on an attack of gout. Cooper commended the use of tomatoes in cases of obesity. Cooper gave Lycpr. in a case of rodent ulcer and caused sharp pain and temporary spread of the disease. Coryza, worse out of doors (All-c., better out of doors). Polyuria, with great thirst. Diabetes. Marked action on deltoid and pectoral muscles, pain is better lifting arm upward and outward. Pains leave after influenza. Right side principally affected, symptoms proceed from right to left. MIND - Peevish about trifles. Very irritable, noises greatly annoy. Unusually mentally active for short periods, followed by longer periods of mental dullness. Weak memory, forgetful. Thoughts disappear, worse when leaning head against anything. Cannot keep mind fixed on work.

Head - Intense throbbing, bursting headache. Bursting pain in head, especially vertex and when coughing. Dull, heavy pain in occiput. Headache in the occiput, spreads all over the head and settles with great violence in temples, worse tobacco smoke.

Eyes - Dull, heavy, ache. Sore and burning. Pupils minutely contracted. Twitching in left inner canthus. Eyes water on close work. Letters run together when reading. Keeps wiping eyes to see clearly. Light painful. Lids feel heavy and swollen.

Nose - Stopped catarrh. Profuse watery coryza excoriating ale, drops down posterior sinuses, salty taste, markedly worse out of doors.

Face - Face flushed, pale. Pressure in right or left zygoma.

Mouth - Itching and tickling in roof of mouth. Tongue coated thick, yellow, white, more in center. Foul breath, taste.

Throat - The throat slightly sore on swallowing. Mucus membrane of pharynx pale, tip of uvula and arches of pharynx red and inflamed. Burning raw feeling right side of throat, changing to left. Swelling of left tonsil. Constant desire to clear throat. Husky voice. Hoarseness with constant tickling in pit of throat. Hoarseness towards night. Vertigo - Giddiness, with inclination to faint on attempting to walk. COMMENTS - Gross made a proving of Ly- cpr., noting peevishness and loss of memory, sticking and pressing pains, a sense of paralysis, pressing and boring pains in head, and stopped catarrh. Some women cannot eat tomatoes without getting backache, leucorrhea or metrorrhagia. In Gross's proving, the headache was worse in evening, she was obliged to rise in the night to urinate. The mind symptoms were worse and the headache better by leaning the head against something. Dr. Herbert H. Roberts of Derby, Conn., published provings made by himself, two with the 3x and two with the 30x tinctures. “The original tincture was made from the thoroughly ripened fruit, great pains being taken to thoroughly macerate the seeds as well as the pulp.” The rheumatic and congestive symptoms were mostly produced by the 3x, the nervous symptoms mostly by the 30x. Roberts remarked that the natives of Mexico and California eat quantities of the ripe fruit to prevent rheumatism. The right deltoid was very markedly affected and should make Lycpr. a companion to Sang, in shoulder pains. Headaches were intense and characteristic in some, great soreness remained after the pain had gone. Dark-complexioned people seem to be suited to its action from two cases recorded by Roberts. The first case concerned a widow, 50, dark complexion, large, stout, gray eyes. Sudden attack of grip. Very severe aching pains all over, up and down back, limbs, head. Beating, throbbing in head, beginning in occiput, spreading all over head, settling with great violence in temples. Excruciating pain back of eyes and in balls as if they would burst with the pressure. Light causes pain. Delirium. Severe, deep, racking cough. Thirst for large quantities. Pupils contracted. Lycpr. 3x every hour cleared away the fever and acute symptoms by the following morning and rapidly cured the remaining cough. The second case was a man, 40, dark complexion, black hair and eyes, tall, thick-set. Severe bursting, throbbing pain beginning in occiput and settling with great force in temporal and frontal regions, eyes painful, worse from light, pupils contracted. Thirst for large quantities. Temperature 104° F. Pulse full flowing. Lycpr. 3x every hour given in evening removed the headache before midnight. The next day, the right tonsil was swollen and inflamed, sore on swallowing, feeling of a lump there. Temperature 101°. He recovered rapidly. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Tobacco smoke. Compare: (1) Bell., Hyos., Dulc., Caps., Sol-t., Sol-n. (2) Ant- t. - weakness of cervical muscles. (3) In coryza, All-c. but All-c. has better open air, Lycpr. worse open air. (4) Contracted pupils. Op. (5)Deltoidrheumatism, Sang. (6) Diabetes. Uran-n. (7) Headache, sore throat, right side. Bell. (8) Headache worse on coughing, worse in open air, Caps. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Thirst for large quantities of water. Violent belchings of gas with taste of food. Great flatulency between 10 a.m. and 11:30. Burning sensation in stomach towards evening and during evening.

Abdomen - Great flatulency of abdomen. Back - Cannot get into a comfortable position. Backache in lumbar region, making them gloomy and depressed. Rheumatic pain near attachment of trapezius muscle to spine. Heavy dragging in right scapula. Breasts - Sore and tender scirrhous breast.

Stool - Brownish, watery diarrhea, yellow, frothy, no urging, painless.

Female - Profuse leucorrheal discharge. Too frequent menstruation, brought on by free use of canned tomatoes, the flow would return whenever this food was eaten for a few meals.

Chest - Slight sticking beneath left side of sternum, without difficulty of respiration. Oppression in chest in lower lobe of right lung.

Heart - Fine, stitching pains at base of heart. Lame pain in region of heart. Pulse 100, full and flowing.

Limbs - Intense aching, rheumatic pain in muscles of all limbs. Lame, tired feeling in all limbs with great exhaustion. Intense aching pain in lower limbs. Sharp sticking pain along course of right crural nerve. Painful sticking behind articulation of left hip. Sharp pain in right deltoid and pectoral muscles, worse lifting arm upward and outward. Lameness of left wrist, hand and fingers, where it is painful even when not moving it. Lungs - Coughs are deep, harsh, starting from irritation in lower chest. Explosive cough. Dry, hacking cough coming on at night and keeping him awake. Expectoration white and in lumps, early in morning.

Sleep - Unable to fall asleep in evening tosses about, every position uncomfortable. Very restless sleep. Frequent waking and tossing, limbs when pressed feel paralyzed. Confused, disagreeable dreams. Wakened by insignificant dreams.

Skin - Erythematous lupus much relieved (Cooper).

Modalities - Better in warm room, from external heat. The headache in one instance was completely better by tobacco smoke. Worse by noise, motion.

Kidneys - Increase of watery constituents of urine, not of total solids. Must rise at night to urinate. Constant debility when in open air, not at all in warm room.

Temperature - Chilliness towards night, preceded by thirst for large quantities of water. Chilliness and sweat. Sweat on awaking confined to a strip about four inches wide along whole length of back. Temperature from 100.5° to 101 °F.

name: Lycopodium Clavatum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better by motion, belchings, urinating, after midnight. Better from warm food and drink, on getting cold, being uncovered, cold applications. Worse right side, from right to left, from above downward. Worse warm room, hot air, bed, warm applications, except throat and stomach which are better from warm drinks. Worse from pressure of clothes, eating, oysters, milk, vegetables, cabbage, beans, bread, pastry. Worse wind, wet, stormy weather, 4 p.m. to 8 p.m., awakening. Worse before or from suppressed menses..
constitution: Abdomen, weak. Acidity. Albuminuria. Aneurysm. Angina pectoris. Aphasia. Asthma. Axilla, perspiration. Belching. Biliousness. Borborygmi. Bright's, disease. Bloating. Cachexia. Cancer. Cataract. Colic. Colitis. Constipation. Coms. Coughs. Cramps. Cystitis. Day-blindness. Debility. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Dropsy. Dysentery. Dyslexia. Dysmenorrhea. Dyspepsia. Ear, eczema. Eczema. Emaciation.
