full:
PHARMACY - musc-d. Musca domestica. House fly. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Arthritis. Awkwardness. Backache. Boils. Catarrh. Delusions. Dysmenorrhea. Eczema. Headache. Herpes. High, fever. Masturbation. Memory, weak. Mumps. Rashes. Rheumatism. Salivation. Stupefaction. Styes. Toothaches. Weakness.

HOMEOPATHIC - Lassitude. Heaviness, sensation externally and internally. Heaviness, internally, alternating with lightness. Lack of vital heat. Heat alternates with a chill. Sensation of paralysis. Weakness, with restlessness. Worse during a storm. MIND - Fastidious. Conscientious, about trifles. Restlessness with pain. Restlessness, driving from place to place. Desire for exercise and physical activity. Industrious. Elation. Extravagance. Irresolution. Impatience, with children. Easily angered. Cursing. Anxiety, with congestion, when alone. Fear of abandonment, sensation of isolation. Anxiety about health. Anxiety about time. Fear of accident, sexual assault, men. Aversion to company, to certain people. Memory, weakness. Forgetfulness, feels as if he had forgotten something. Confusion of mind. Rapid thoughts. Confounds objects and ideas. Awkwardness. Mistakes in talking, words, localities, names. Confusion of mind, identity. Stupefaction, as if intoxicated. Indolence. Causeless crying. Tendency to weep. Sadness, before menses. Pities herself. Self loathing. Despair, hopeless. Dwells on past disagreeable circumstances. Reproaches others. Desires sympathy. Worries for others. Forsaken. Suicidal thoughts. Delusion, that he died, and is alive again. That body and mind are separated. That he is being watched. That fingers are scratching his body. Everything is dirty, foul. Visions of dead animals. Sees maggots, vermin, insects.

Head - Headache, frontal pressure. Pressure in temples, worse lying down. Dull aching in occiput. Dull, gripping like too much caffeine. Throbbing head and above eyes. Head pain before menses. Dry, flaking, scalp. Kidney - Musty smelling urine.

Eyes - Dryness. Discharge in right eye. Stye, in right eye. Eyelid opens and shuts involuntarily.

Ears - Cutting, aching pain. Oozing eruption on the earlobe. Sensitive to high pitched noise. Ringing noises.

Nose - Obstruction. Catarrh. Acute sense of smell. Odors, imagined and real, fruit, peaches, sulphur.

Face - Eruptions, painful to touch, on forehead, eyebrows, over left eye. Herpetic eruption on lower lip, corners of mouth. Inflammation of parotid gland.

Mouth - Profuse saliva, in gushes. Frothy mucus on waking. Salivation with mumps. Taste of lemons in mouth. Breath, fetid odor. Bleeding, spongy gums. Lower gum line feels thin and stings. Chancre sore on tongue, lip. Lip, split, cracked.

Throat - Sore throat, with tickling in the ears, worse tea. Mucus stuck in throat. Vertigo - Light-headed. Drifts or falls, to the left, worse in morning. Vision - Difficulty focusing. Blurry when reading. As if a bug was flying in peripheral sight. REFERENCES - Sonz, Stewart.

Stomach - Appetite wanting for dinner. Upset stomach, worse drinking cold water. Sharp pain, with belching, gas. Sour eructations. Spikes or flashes of nausea.

Abdomen - Dull, knotting pain, sharp over bowel.

Rectum - Constipation, must strain. Urging absent. Incomplete, unsatisfactory bowel movements. Excessive flatulence, smelly. Stools are dry, pasty, soft, light brown, loose. Sensations - Heaviness sensation. Alternating heaviness with lightness sensation. Paralytic sensation.

Male - Pinching pain in testes. Sexual desire increased. Penis, flaccid. Impotency.

Female - Painful menses, dysmenorrhea. Menses, profuse, brown discharge, spotting, intermittent. Pain in lower vaginal region. Sharp pain in cervix, in left ovary. Herpetic eruptions. Boils on labia. Sexual desire increased. Masturbation. Food - Aversion to water. Desires chocolate, cheese. Desires bacon. Desires vinegar, sour food. Desires coffee. Desires beer in the morning. Worse from cheese.

Chest - Radiating pain, gas in center of chest. Aching pain, constriction. Dreams - Dreams of sexual violence, abortion, sick babies, dying from cholera.

Back - Backache. Dull, throbbing pain. Pain in nape, neck. Neck pulling to left. Tension in neck, shoulders. Pain in coccyx. Sensation of gap in mid-back. As if back were separated. Breasts - Pain and swelling in breasts, before menses. Pain in nipples, in men.

Limbs - Insensibility, limbs. Stiffness of limbs. Joint pain. Numbness in arms on waking. Aching pain, in upper limbs, shoulders, upper arms, at night. Pinching, throbbing pain in wrist. Awkwardness, lower limbs, hands. Throbbing pain in hip. Cracking pain in groin, worse walking. Lancinating pain in knee. Cold, numb feet. Soreness in feet, soles. Lungs - Greenish yellow expectoration. Shortness of breath.

Sleep - Snoring during nap. Overwhelming desire to sleep. Sleeping early. Sleeps in fetal position, right side. Deep, soporific sleep. Recurring vivid dreams, of houses, fire, water, falling into water. Deep, unrefreshing sleep. Restless. Waking groggy, late.

Skin - Greasy skin. Herpetic eruptions. Boils on right upper back. Flat, pink, scaly rash on chest. Eruption in cervical area. Red rash above left axilla, after bathing. Eczema on hand. Raised red bumps on upper thigh.

Modalities - Worse lying down. Worse from cheese.

Teeth - Toothache while eating chocolate. Pain in right lower teeth.

Perspiration - Night sweats.

name: Musa Sapientum
author: Murphy
constitution: Anemia. Blood pressure. Brain, fatigue. Bronchitis. Constipation. Cystitis. Depression. Dyspnea. Hangovers. Headache. Heartburn. Hemorrhoids. Morning, sickness. Mosquito, bites. Overweight. Pre- menstrual syndrome. Seasonal Affective Disorder. Strokes. Tobacco, smoking. Ulcers. Warts.

PHARMACY - musa. Musa sapientum. Banana. N. O. Palmacee. Araceae. Tincture of the dried flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anemia. Blood pressure. Brain, fatigue. Bronchitis. Constipation. Cystitis. Depression. Dyspnea. Hangovers. Headache.…
full:
PHARMACY - musa. Musa sapientum. Banana. N. O. Palmacee. Araceae. Tincture of the dried flowers. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anemia. Blood pressure. Brain, fatigue. Bronchitis. Constipation. Cystitis. Depression. Dyspnea. Hangovers. Headache. Heartburn. Hemorrhoids. Morning, sickness. Mosquito, bites. Overweight. Pre- menstrual syndrome. Seasonal Affective Disorder. Strokes. Tobacco, smoking. Ulcers. Warts.

HERBAL - C. Campbell commended bananas baked in their skins as an ideal food or even a “cure” for brain workers, nervous persons and the anemic. A syrup made with the juice of bananas extracted by heat is commended as a remedy in chronic bronchitis with insufficient expectoration and marked dyspnea. Clarke had a case of profusely bleeding hemorrhoids, which had resisted every kind of treatment, showed improvement and an ultimate cure.

HOMEOPATHIC - Jenner proved the tincture of banana flowers, producing costiveness and a sensation of fullness about the anus in a person of regular habits. He cured a bad case of bleeding hemorrhoids with it. Musa also produced pain in the bladder and passage of mucus with urine. MIND - Brain fatigue. Depression.

Head - Dull, heavy, frontal headache.

Mouth - Dry, rough and extremely astringent taste and feeling in mouth, tongue, and fauces, but afterwards an increase of saliva.

Abdomen - Rumbling in stomach and bowels with expulsion of flatus.

Rectum - Constipation with feeling of fullness about anus. COMMENTS - Bananas contain three natural sugars, sucrose, fructose and glucose, combined with fiber. They also contain tryptophan, a protein that is converted into serotonin. Vitamin B6, which regulates blood glucose levels and affect mood. High in iron, bananas can stimulate the production of hemoglobin. They also contain potassium and are natural antacids. Can be useful for depression, seasonal affective disorder and stress. Anemia. High blood pressure, strokes. Premenstrual syndrome. Morning sickness. Hangovers. Constipation. Heartbum, ulcers. Neutralizes over- acidity and reduces irritation by coating the lining of the stomach. REFERENCES - Clarke. Murphy.

Kidneys - Discharge of large quantities of mucus with the urine, with dull, aching pain in bladder region.

full:
PHARMACY - must-b. Mustard. Sinapis arvensis. The flower heads are picked above any seed pods and boiled for half an hour. The water is strained and prepared as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle, (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.

HOMEOPATHIC - Must-b. belongs to Bach's group “Lack of Interest in Present Circumstances,” along with Clem-b., Honey-b., Wld-r-b., Oliv-b., Wh-ch-b., and Ch-bd-b. Affects of head injury, nerve damage or misalignment of the skull plates along fissures. Dampened consciousness (Hom-b., Scler-b., Wld-o-b.). Depression and gloom. Lowered vitality, lethargy. Chronic fatigue and appetite disturbances (Chic-b, Crb-a- b.). Solace found in eating and constipation (Chic-b., Will-b.), resulting in weight loss or gain. Sleep disturbances (Pine-b., Wh-ch-b.). Disinterest in physical recreation and general decline in healthful interests and habits (see Wld-o-b.). MIND - Depression and gloom, with sensation of a weight or downward pull, better in the sun. Desires light. Sadness, regret, weepy. Introverted. Absent-minded, disinterested in present circumstances. Lack of appeal for life. Boredom, sense of meaningless. Morose and ill-tempered. Sense of desolation, loneliness. Self-pity. Withdrawal and joylessness in retardation (Horn-b., Wld-o-b.). REFERENCES - Bach.

full:
PHARMACY - mut. Mutabile bacillus. Bacillus coli. A bowel nosode. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Cystitis. Eruptions. Malnutrition.

HOMEOPATHIC - Mutabile bacillus is so named because it mutates almost as soon as it is sub-cultured from a non-lactose to a lactose fermenter, and is of interest mainly from a bacteriological point of view as it is an intermediary form between the B. Coli and the true non-lactose fermenting type. This nosode is likely to be of value in treatment where there is alternation of symptoms. Associated with Puls. Skin eruptions alternate with asthmatic symptoms (Calad.). Skin has a sallow color. Cystitis. Malnutrition. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Puls., Calad. REFERENCES - Bach. Paterson.

full:
PHARMACY - mygal. Mygale lasiodora. Black Cuban spider. Bird spider. Mygale avicularia. Aranea avicularia. N. O. Arachnida. Latin America. Tincture of whole spider. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Chill. Chordee. Chorea. Convulsions. Dyspnea. Fever. Gonorrhea. Nausea. Palpitations. Syphilis. Trembling. Twitching.

HOMEOPATHIC - The pathogenic data of Mygale consist of a proving by ayoung woman and the effect of a bite on a man. In the latter case, inflammation ensued which spread along the lymphatics, violet and afterwards green discoloration, chill followed by fever, dry mouth and great thirst, trembling, dyspnea, despondency and fear of death. The prover developed sadness, dry mouth, nausea with great palpitation, trembling, dim sight and great general weakness increased flow of urine, hot, scalding with stinging in urethra. This last symptom led to the successful use of Mygal. in gonorrhea, chordee and syphilis. The “trembling” observed in the man suggests its use in nervous cases, but the sphere of Mygal. in chorea has been developed from the clinical side. In the cases cured with it, twitching and contractions of facial muscles have been very prominent, convulsive movements of head to right side, twitching of one side of body, mostly right. The twitchings may be so violent as to prevent walking. Chorea, especially of the upper parts. Constant motion of whole body. Convulsive, uncontrollable movements of arms and legs. Twitchings and contraction of facial muscles and head, which is jerked to the right side. Limbs are quiet during sleep, movements worse in morning. Unsteady gait, limbs drag while walking. Mouth and eyes open in rapid succession. Words are jerked out in the effort to talk. Nausea with palpitations and dim vision. Intense red streaks along lymphatics. Sexual symptoms, violent erections, chordee. Weakness, nervousness, fear. MIND - Sad, despondent with anxious expression. Fear of death. Delirious, talking about his business, restless all night.

Head - Head jerked to one side.

Eyes - Nausea with dimness of sight, weakness, palpitation.

Ears - Acute aching in right ear.

Face - Twitching of facialmuscles. Mouth and eyes open in rapid succession. Hot and flushed. Food - Excessive thirst. Aversion to food, no appetite. Better after eating.

Mouth - Tongue dry and parched, put out with difficulty. Grating of teeth at night.

Stomach - Nausea with strong palpitations, dim sight.

Urine - Urine is increased, stinging in urethra, burning hot, scalding. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Agar., Tarent., Cupr., Ziz. (2) in chorea, Agar., Cimic., Ign., Stram., Ziz. Tarent., Ant-c. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Male - Violent erections. Chordee (Kali- br., Camph.). Protracted gonorrhea. Syphilis.

Heart - Strong palpitations, with nausea, dimness of sight and general weakness. Pulse frequent. ***Limbs - Constant motion of whole body. Twitching of limbs. Tremulous. Convulsive, uncontrollable movements of arms and legs. Restless hands. Limbs drag while walking. Unsteady gait. Intense redness in streaks, following course of lymphatics. Lungs - Difficult breathing. Words jerked out when effort is made to talk.

Back - Pain in back, extending around to front.

Sleep - Restless all night, with ridiculous dreams.

Modalities - Better during sleep. Worse in morning, eating. Legs in constant motion, worse sitting.

Temperature - Severe chill lasting thirty minutes, then fever with excessive thirst and trembling of limbs.

CLINICAL - Bronchitis, chronic. Bronchor- rhea. Coughs. Emaciation. Lung, disorders.…
full:

HERBAL - Hale collected some clinical experiences with Myosotis symphytifolia, which differs from Myosotis palus tris in having large symphytum-like leaves, showing it to have a strong affinity for therespiratory organs.

HOMEOPATHIC - :Myos-s. affects the left lower lung. Chronic bronchitis and tuberculosis. Bronchorrhea. Cough with profuse muco-purulent expectoration, gagging and vomiting during cough, worse during or after eating. Pain in left lung (lower), painful while coughing and sensitive to percussion. Copious expectoration, emaciation, night-sweats. Profuse sweat day and night. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Symph., Stann. - lung disease. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Myrica Cerifera
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from open air, eating, breakfast. Worse from warmth of bed, after sleep, morning, after breakfast, motion..
constitution: Achilles tendon, pain. Cancer. Catarrh. Conjunctivitis. Diphtheria. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Insomnia. Jaundice. Leuc- orrhea. Liver, disorders. Pharynx, disorders. Stomatitis. Throat, sore, Urticaria.
keynote:
PHARMACY - myric. Myrica cerífera. Bayberry. Wax myrtle. Candleberry. N. O. Myricacee. Tincture of fresh bark of root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Achilles tendon, pain. Cancer. Catarrh. Conjunctivitis. Diphtheria. Headaches. Heart, disorders.…
full:
PHARMACY - myric. Myrica cerífera. Bayberry. Wax myrtle. Candleberry. N. O. Myricacee. Tincture of fresh bark of root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Achilles tendon, pain. Cancer. Catarrh. Conjunctivitis. Diphtheria. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Insomnia. Jaundice. Leuc- orrhea. Liver, disorders. Pharynx, disorders. Stomatitis. Throat, sore, Urticaria.

HERBAL - According to Hale, though Myrica was known to old herbalists, it was Samuel Thomson, of lobelia fame, who established its reputation. Thomson had a crude pathology of his own which served him to some extent. Myrica formed the chief ingredient in Thomson's once famous “Composition powder.” One of his ideas was that the digestive tract was liable to become fouled with a copious mucus lining. This he called “canker” and he stated of Myrica that it “has the power of disengaging the thick, viscid secretions of the mucus membrane of the stomach.”

HOMEOPATHIC - The provings of Myric. confirmed Thomson's observation, that it produced a characteristic abundant, offensive secretion of tenacious mucus in the throat, difficult to detach. Liver disorders with jaundice and mucus membranes. Combined liver and heart disorders. Persistent insomnia. MIND - Gloomy, despondent and dejected. Irritable, indifferent. Cannot concentrate mind on any subject. Dull and drowsy state. Exhilaration, then excitement or depression, preventing sleep, with restlessness. ***Abdomen - Dull pain in the liver with pain under either scapulae. Fullness and burning in gallbladder. Fullness in the stomach and abdomen. Flatus is passed continuously while walking.

Head - Pain and stiffness in nape of neck. Headache with drowsiness, yellow sclerotica, aching in eyeballs. Pressure in vertex and forehead. Dull, heavy aching in temples and forehead on waking in the morning. Scalp feels tight.

Eyes - Yellow sclerotica. Very red eyelids.

Face - Yellow, jaundiced. Itching and stinging. Creeping sensation.

Mouth - Dry, water relieves only partially. Tenacious, thick, nauseous mucus in mouth and throat. Taste bitter andnauseous with offensive breath. Tongue, thick yellowish, dark, furred. Tender, spongy and bleeding gums (Merc.).

Throat - Constricted and rough feeling with a constant desire to swallow. Diphtheria. Stringy mucus, detached with difficulty. COMMENTS - Long-lasting, profuse catarrhal discharges, offensive, tenacious and difficult to detach. Leucorrhea, bronchorrhea intestinal catarrh, pharyngeal catarrh, stomatitis. Nasal obstruction, post- nasal catarrh which often accompanies disordered liver. Drowsiness, despondency. Weakness. Muscular soreness, aching in limbs. Sharp pains about the heart with increased, audible pulsations, but slow pulse, worse lying on left side (Dig.). Pains in left chest and under scapula (especially left) and pain in middle lobe of right lung. Aching pain in liver, fullness. Jaundice. Itching of jaundice. Dull, heavy headache, worse in morning. Dirty, yellow tongue. Yellowish white of eyes. Dirty, lids abnormally red. Ash-colored stools. Douglass noted the case of Miss O., 18, who complained of itching and stinging on face, neck, right forearm and leg. Sensation as if insects crawling on face, must brush them away. Skin yellowish tongue, thickly coated yellow. Felt sick all over and rather irritable. Myric. 6x every two hours improved at once and cured in ten days. Hale said it rivals Guai. as a local application in diphtheria. Burnett used Myric. with excellent effect with jaundice, given in material doses. It has generally been given in the lower potencies. RELATIONS - Antidote: Dig. - jaundice. Compare: (1) Ptel., Com., Chel., Lept., Fago. (2) in tenacious secretions, Kali-bi., Hydr. (3) Jaundice, light-colored stools, slow pulse, Dig. (Dig. has pulse irregular as well as slow, the tongue of Dig. has not the thick, tenacious coat of Myric.). (4) Liver, Berb., Chel., Chim., Podo., Hep., Merc., Choi., Hydr. (5) Urticaria and liverdisorder, Astac. (6) Sore all over, Arn., Bapt. (7) Leucorrhea, Hydr. (8) Pain through left chest to scapula, Ther., Anis., Pix. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Complete loss of appetite, but with a feeling of fullness in the stomach after a hearty meal. Weak, sinking feeling in the epigastrium, approaching nausea increased after eating, relieved by rapid walking.

Rectum - Urging to stools but passes only great amount of flatus. Constant discharge of flatus when walking. Stools, foul, pasty, of gray color. Loose, light-colored stool, ash-colored and destitute of bile. Adhesive mucus in stools.

Female - Acrid, fetid, thick, yellow, long lasting leucorrhea. Food - Desire for sour things. Strong desire for acids. Imagines he cannot eat, the taste is so foul. Loss of appetite, loathing of food.

Heart - Pulse, slow, feeble, irregular Kidneys - Dark, frothy, scanty, high-colored, biliary urine.

Back - Pain under scapulae with liver complaints.

Limbs - Pain under shoulder blades and back of neck, in all muscles, in hollow of right foot. Staggering gait.

Sleep - Drowsiness. Insomnia. Disturbed, bad dreams and frequent waking.

Skin - Yellow and itching. Jaundice. Creeping sensation, as of insects.

Modalities - Better from open air, eating, breakfast. Worse from warmth of bed, after sleep, morning, after breakfast, motion.

Liver - Liver disorders with heart complaints, with urticaria with jaundice. Jaundice of infants. Liver cancer, with bronze-yellow skin.

name: Myristica Sebifera
author: Murphy
constitution: Abscesses. Arthritis. Boils. Carbuncles. Elephantiasis arabum. Erysipelas. Fistulas. Headache. Injuries. Joints, disorders. Panaritium. Parotiditis. Suppurations. Traumatic, infections. Ulcers. Whitlow. Wounds.
keynote:
PHARMACY - myris. Myristica sebifera. Brazilian ucuba. N. O. Myristicacee. Brazil. Trituration of red, acrid, very poisonous gum obtained by incising bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscesses. Arthritis. Boils. Carbuncles. Elephantiasis arabum.…
full:
PHARMACY - myris. Myristica sebifera. Brazilian ucuba. N. O. Myristicacee. Brazil. Trituration of red, acrid, very poisonous gum obtained by incising bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscesses. Arthritis. Boils. Carbuncles. Elephantiasis arabum. Erysipelas. Fistulas. Headache. Injuries. Joints, disorders. Panaritium. Parotiditis. Suppurations. Traumatic, infections. Ulcers. Whitlow. Wounds.

HOMEOPATHIC - Mure proved and introduced Myris., which belongs to the same order as the nutmeg tree, Nux-m. In the proving there was “pain in the fingernails with swelling of the phalanges.” This, apparently, led to its use in whitlow in which many successes have been reported, including some from Chancerel Pere.Spanish homeopaths used Myris. extensively. Olive of Gros reported cures of scrofulous osteitis, callous ulcers, and phlegmonous erysipelas. Works as an antiseptic. Inflammation of skin, cellular tissue and periosteum. Hastens suppuration and shortens its duration. Traumatic infections. Panaritium. Parotiditis. Fistulas. Carbuncles.Phlegmonous inflammations. Inflammation of middle ear, suppurative stage. Coppery taste and burning in the throat. Tongue is white and cracked. Fistula in ano. Hands are stiff, as if from squeezing something a long time. MIND - Heedless and careless. Indifference, apathy to business affairs. Stupefaction, as if intoxicated. Concentration is difficult. Persistent thoughts. Vexed by a song which keeps running in his head. Excitable, alternating with chilliness. Dreams of neglected business, quarrels, strife. Startled during sleep.

Head - Head heavy. Pain with pressure outwards. Headache in frontal eminence, at noon, better in open air.

Eyes - Redness of eyes and eyelids.

Ears - Inflammation of middle ear, tympanum, myringitis. Suppuration of middle ear, tympanum. Abscess of external meatus. Ringing noises.

Face - Very red face. Food - Thirst.

Mouth - Tongue white and cracked. Whole mouth with tonsils and upper pharynx painful and sensitive to contact, every mouthful seems to wound the parts when chewed or swallowed. Taste bitter of copper, which excites spitting of blood. Palate insensible with loss of taste.

Throat - Burning at bottom of throat. Constriction at isthmus of pharynx, pain increases progressively. Difficulty in swallowing saliva.

Abdomen - Sensation as if a foreign body, as large as a walnut, has lodged in left inguinal region, all forenoon.

Rectum - Stools mixed with yellow mucus.

Urine - Red color. Vertigo - Dizziness in morning. Vertigo, right to left on waking in morning. Vertigo, swaying toward left. COMMENTS - Myris. is useful for abscesses from splinters and foreign objects, especially splinters under the nails causing infection, pus and pain (Sil.). Suppuration of the joints. Kippax, according to Hansen, noted that it is the principal remedy in elephantiasis arabum. Cartier noted two cases in which he used Myris. The first was a young girl who had had her leg in a splint for inflammation of the knee and doughy swelling of the entire limb for three months. Cartier came to the conclusion that there was pus in the joint. Myris. 3c, five drops three times a day, was given for three months. Five months later, the swelling and inflammation were all gone, walking gave no pain, but the joint was anchylosed. The second case was an old man, 87, who was seized with sudden arthritis of the shoulder with intense fever. Cartier was sent for and found the shoulder quite full of pus with a particularly painful spot on the scapula, at a point where the bone was said by one authority to be attacked. Myris. 3c, five drops three times a day, was given. In ten days there was no longer suppuration, the size of the joint has become normal and the tender spot was gone. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sil., Nux-m., Calc-s., Sulph., Pyrog. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Chest - Hard pressure during night on both sides of chest, not affecting breathing.

Back - Pinching, right side of neck.

Limbs - Hands stiff as if from squeezing something for long time. Pain in left hand. Pain in hands worse when they touch each other. Formication on left thumb joint. Pain in fingernails with swelling of phalanges. Pinching pain in right calf.

Sleep - Cannot get to sleep. Restless sleep with unconnected dreams, about business, disputes, houses being built commencing with top stories. Violent starting in sleep.

Skin - Malignant pustules. Abscesses. Carbuncles. Two pimples on left cheek, quickly disappearing.

Kidneys - Less frequent urination, scanty although he drinks much. Urine reddish yellow.

PHARMACY - myrrh. Myrrh. Gum myrrh. Commiphora myrrha. Commiphora molmol. Balsamodendron myrrha. N. O. Burseraceae. Middle East and Africa. Tincture from bush or small tree. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies, third potency.

CLINICAL - Abscess. Amenorrhea. Anemia.…
full:
PHARMACY - myrrh. Myrrh. Gum myrrh. Commiphora myrrha. Commiphora molmol. Balsamodendron myrrha. N. O. Burseraceae. Middle East and Africa. Tincture from bush or small tree. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies, third potency.

CLINICAL - Abscess. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Asthma. Bronchitis. Colds. Constipation. Coughs. Debility. Dyspepsia. Flatus. Gastritis. Gum,diseases. Mouth, disorders. Pharygi- tis. Pyorrhea. Sores. Stomach, disorders. Throat, sore. Thrush. Tonsillitis. Ulcers. Myrrh

HERBAL - The Myrrh plant is a shrub or small tree. Myrrh is highly prized for its bitter, cleansing perfume. The aromatic pale yellow, gum resin seeps out from fissures in the bark. It was part of the embalming mixtures of the ancient Egyptians. It is a stimulant, tonic and antiseptic. The tincture is used for sore throats, ulcers and thrush. Mouthwash for infected gums or ulcerated tongue. The dry, powdered resin is often added to tooth formulas. Myrrh is an excellent antiseptic, a slow and mild stimulant, possessed of moderate astringency, and acting as a stimulating tonic. Its use occasions an agreeable sense of warmth in the stomach, large quantities causing decided gastric excitement. It slowly increases the fullness and force of the pulse, and exerts a well-marked influence on the capillary circulation. It diminishes mucus discharges, leaves a sense of warmth in the respiratory passages, arrests decomposition, and removes foul odors from sores. It is also a very good styptic in passive hemorrhages. Emmenagogue properties have been attributed to it.

HOMEOPATHIC - Large doses of Myrrh quicken the pulse, raise the temperature, cause gastric burning, great sweating, and prostration, vomiting and purgation may follow. Myrrh is a remedy for enfeebled states with excessive mucus discharges. Muscular debility. Respiratory weakness with difficult expectoration. Tonsillitis with large and infected glands. Chronic gastritis and dyspepsia. Gas and frequent mucus stools.

Mouth - Pale tongue. Salivation. Abscesses. Sores in the mouth. Inflamed and sore gums. Pyorrhea. Spongy and bleeding gums.

Throat - Sore throats. Pharyngitis. Infected and enlarged tonsils. Abscessed glands. COMMENTS - As a local application in degenerate ulcers, it is of great value. Especially in phagedaenic, malignant and fetid sores. Carbuncles, malignant scarlatina, putrid sore throat and diphtheria. After an indolent bubo has been opened. In all such local cases it may be used in powder, tincture, or watery solution. It is a favorite appliance in aphthous sores, and bleeding or spongy gums. REFERENCES-Clarke.

Female - Dragging and weight sensation in the female pelvis. Leucorrhea. Suppressed menses in anemic young girls.

author: Murphy

He then tried the chekan on members of his own family with equal success. Myrt-ch. ha
keynote:
PHARMACY - myrt-ch. Myrtus cheken. Eugenia cheken. N. O. Myrtacae. South America. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

HERBAL - The constituents and properties of chekan correspond with those which generally characterize the family myrtacea. To this family belong…
full:
PHARMACY - myrt-ch. Myrtus cheken. Eugenia cheken. N. O. Myrtacae. South America. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

HERBAL - The constituents and properties of chekan correspond with those which generally characterize the family myrtacea. To this family belong cloves, allspice, eucalyptus and jambul, all possessing, in the part used, stores of aromatic oil to which, at least, in great part, is due their valuable properties. Dessauer considers it to possess tonic, expectorant, diuretic and antiseptic properties; he states that he has used it with great success in bronchitis, vesical catarrh and other affections of the mucous membrane, also that digestion is improved.

HOMEOPATHIC - Dr. Dessauer, physicianin-chief to the German hospitals in Valparaiso, and Dr. Murrell, of London, both were instrumental in introducing this remedy to the profession. Dr. Dessauer first had his attention called to the plant by the successful self-treatment by one of his patients in a case of purulent bronchitis. He then tried the chekan on members of his own family with equal success. Myrt-ch. has chronic bronchitis with dense, yellowish sputum, difficult to detach. Copious expectoration keeps patient distressed and coughing. Dr. John B. Garrison writes: “Myrtus chekan, should prove a valuable remedy in bronchial catarrh. The chief indications for its use are severe paroxysmal cough with dense yellow expectoration, which is difficult to ‘bring up. * Sometimes the secretion is so abundant Myrtus cheken that it rattles in the deeper bronchial tubes, but, owing to its tenacious character, only small amounts are expectorated. Shortness of breath is also a marked feature, but the cough is the more important of the two symptoms. This remedy is not a ‘cure-all' for all forms of bronchitis, but only in those cases which present, at least, the symptoms, ‘thick, yellow, sticky sputum, difficult to expectorate. ‘ Good results may be anticipated from its use. In all elderly people who suffer from weakened power in expectoration and inability to thoroughly clear the bronchial tubes, Myrtus chekan is most reliable.” COMMENTS - Chekan has done its best work in cases of chronic bronchitis associated with emphysema, particularly in elderly persons suffering from ‘winter cough. ‘ As an example of this reference is made to Murrell's report of fifteen cases of chronic bronchitis which were treated at the Royal Hospital for Diseases of the Chest, London. All of the patients, with one exception, were men. The age of the woman was 51 years; the ages of the men ranged from 36 to 58 years. They were all bad cases, many of them of many years' duration. Most of them had been attended at the hospital for some considerable time, and, almost without exception, they had in former years undergone much medical treatment without much benefit. Their occupations exposed them to cold, wet and draught, and in some cases they had the additional disadvantage of working in a dusty atmosphere. They complained chiefly of a paroxysmal cough with thin, yellow expectoration, and much shortness of breath on exertion. On physical examination of the chest emphysema was detected, with, or without, a little bronchus of the bases behind. They were, in fact, ordinary cases of winter cough. REFERENCES - Boericke.

name: Myrtus Communis
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Worse from changes of atmosphere..
constitution: Bronchitis. Catarrhal, fevers. Chest, pain. Coryza. Coughs. Cystitis. Hemoptysis. Pyelitis. Syphilis. Tuberculosis.

PHARMACY - myrt-c. Myrtus communis. Myrtle. Closely allied to Granatum, the pomegranate tree. N. O. Myrtacae. Tincture of fresh shoots and leaves. Tincture of fresh flowering shoots and leaves. Historical dose: Tincture ahd all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bronchitis. Catarrhal,…
full:
PHARMACY - myrt-c. Myrtus communis. Myrtle. Closely allied to Granatum, the pomegranate tree. N. O. Myrtacae. Tincture of fresh shoots and leaves. Tincture of fresh flowering shoots and leaves. Historical dose: Tincture ahd all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bronchitis. Catarrhal, fevers. Chest, pain. Coryza. Coughs. Cystitis. Hemoptysis. Pyelitis. Syphilis. Tuberculosis.

HERBAL - The leaves contain Myrtol and an active antiseptic.

HOMEOPATHIC - Myrt-c. is an unproved remedy, the symptoms are entirely clinical, of which Hering gives an account. Powerful action on the left lung, especially the upper part (Ox-ac., lower). Chest pains, as found in tuberculosis patients. Incipient tuberculosis. Nerve sedative and stimulant to mucus membranes, bronchitis, cystitis and pyelitis. Breasts - Stitching pain in left breast, running through to scapula (Anis., Ther., Pix.).

Nose - Coryza with cough.

Throat - Dryness in throat, pains in throat and chest with expectoration of blood. COMMENTS - Dr. John B. Garrison writes: “Myrtus communis, the common myrtle, was though highly of by Hering, who made clinical tests with it, and found it to be useful in pain in the upper left lung, going right through, from front to back, under the left scapula. ‘Great lassitude in the afternoon' he considered a very important symptom.” Pain in upper left lung going right through from the front to the left scapula. The pain is mostly stitching, but may be throbbing, aching or burning. It is worse in morning, better evening, worse by breathing, yawning, coughing. Cough is dry, hollow, excited by tickling in upper anterior lobes. Hemoptysis, Tuberculosis, lung syphilis, hepatization. Cough and tickling in afternoon is better in evening. Every atmospheric change causes cough, coryza and catarrhal fever. Hering cured catarrhal fever with tickling cough worse morning and better evening with great lassitude in afternoon. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Myrt-ch. (2) pains through left chest to scapula, Ther., Anis., Pix., Sulph. (3) pain through lower lobe of left lung, Ox-ac. (4) Phos., Bry. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Chest - Acute pressing pain in chest. Pain in upper part of left chest, through to shoulder, worse taking a deep breath and making a strong motion. Stitching in left apex straight through to scapula, worse breathing, yawning, coughing. Burning in left chest with throbbing, aching, tickling. Hepatization of lungs. Tuberculosis from maltreated syphilis. Cough with tightness. Hemoptysis. Lungs - Dry, hollow cough from tickling in upper anterior lobes of lungs, worse morning, better evening, great lassitude in afternoon. Cough, coryza and catarrhal fever setting in with every atmospheric change.

Modalities - Worse from changes of atmosphere.

Temperature - Catarrhal fevers with pain in elbow and knee joints, with dry, hollow cough, caused by tickling in upper and front part of lungs, especially in morning, better evening, accompanied by lassitude Myrtus communis in afternoon.

PHARMACY - nabal. Nabalus serpentaria. White lettuce. Prenanthes serpentaria. Rattlesnake root. N. O. Composite, suborder Chico- racee. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Constipation. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Dyspepsia.…
full:
PHARMACY - nabal. Nabalus serpentaria. White lettuce. Prenanthes serpentaria. Rattlesnake root. N. O. Composite, suborder Chico- racee. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Constipation. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Dyspepsia. Emaciation. Headaches. Leucorrhea. Ophthalmia.

HERBAL - Nabalus is a Native American plant used in domestic practice for diarrhea and dysentery.

HOMEOPATHIC - There is only one proving with 1c and 3c dilutions by a married woman, age 19. The symptoms somewhat resemble those of its botanical relative, Lact-s., especially in constipation and somnolence. Susceptibility to magnetic contact and to the personal aura of others. Pain in the abdomen and rectum, with emaciation. Dyspepsia with acid burning eructation. Craving for acid food. Constipation and chronic diarrhea (Lact.), worse after eating, at nights and toward morning. Leucorrhea with throbbing in uterus. Heaviness, as if blood vessels filled with lead, body heavy, she leans about. Dull pains in joints and numbness on waking. Irritability of temper and occipital pain, worse in the evening. Ophthalmia. MIND - Continued melancholy. Depression followed by unusual buoyancy. Irritability of temper and occipital pain.

Head - Deep-seated frontal pains behind right eyeball and over eye. Occipital pains with stiffness in neck, worse evenings. Headache with irritability and irritation of eyes, throat and skin. Tipsy sensation.

Eyes - Great and lasting irritation of eyelids and margins, the margins sting and smart and are slightly swollen. Sight weak.

Nose - Right nostril sore. Smell and taste slightly impaired.

Throat - Throat sore, tickling and scraping (left), worse lying down and swallowing saliva, then both eyes, worse left. RELATIONS - Compare: Lact-s. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Stomach - Burning belchings.

Rectum - Constipation, only three stools in twelve days, hard, painful, followed by prostration.

Female - Sharp throbbing in uterus. Menses delayed. White, jelly-like discharge from vagina with weakness. Food - Appetite and thirst diminished. Craving for acid food, lemons.

Sleep - Somnolence. Sleep prolonged, afterwards lighter and more broken.

Skin - Subcutaneous glands irritated and swollen, especially behind right ear and in neck. Prickling as from suppressed perspiration, general itching.

Kidneys - Sharp, transient pain in right kidney. Diminished urine.

Temperature - Chilliness, not better by heat of fire. No febrile reaction except occasional flushes over head and face.

name: Naja Tripudians
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Great relief of pain and breathing by lying on right side. Better from walking or riding in open air, sneezing, smoking. Worse from stimulants, alcohol, cold air, drafts, riding in carriage, touch, pressure of clothes. Worse lying on left side, after sleep, after menses. Headache worse at 3 p.m..
constitution: Angina pectoris. Asthma. Collapse. Dysmenorrhea. Edema. Esophagus, stricture. Hay fever. Headache. Heart disorders. Ovariesdisorders. Plague. Sepsis. Spinal irritation. Throat, sore.
keynote:
PHARMACY - naja. Naja tripudians. Cobra venom. Cobra di capello. N. O. Elapide. India. The hooded snake of Hindustan. Tincture of the fresh venom. Trituration of saturated with fresh venom. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Asthma. Collapse.…
full:
PHARMACY - naja. Naja tripudians. Cobra venom. Cobra di capello. N. O. Elapide. India. The hooded snake of Hindustan. Tincture of the fresh venom. Trituration of saturated with fresh venom. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Asthma. Collapse. Dysmenorrhea. Edema. Esophagus, stricture. Hay fever. Headache. Heart disorders. Ovariesdisorders. Plague. Sepsis. Spinal irritation. Throat, sore.

HOMEOPATHIC - P. C. Majumdar noted that cobra poison had been used by Indian practitioners from ancient times in many nervous and blood diseases. Naja, is not a hemorrhagic or septic medicine like Lach, and Crot- h. Naja, produces a typical bulbar paralysis. Causes no hemorrhage but only edema, hence the victims of this reptile frequently bear very little sign of external injury, the only indication is often a small scratch or puncture. The tissue lying beneath the wound is colored dark purple and a large quantity of viscid, blood-like fluid collects in the vicinity of the wound. The first symptom is an intense burning pain at the bite. There is an interval, usually an hour, before other symptoms develop, after which they develop rapidly. A feeling of intoxication is produced, followed by a loss of power over the limbs. Loss of speech, swallowing and the control over the movement of the lips. Saliva is ejected in large quantities. The respiration gradually becomes slower and slower and at length ceases. Victim remains conscious throughout. The action of Naja, settles around the heart, hypertrophy and valvular diseases. Affects medulla and cerebellum, respiration, throat, ovary. Diseases primarily depending upon degeneration of motor cells. Sepsis. Nervous, excited and tremulous with heart disorders, ojien reflex. Marked surging of blood upwards. Heart is enlarged. Affections of heart with paucity of symptoms. Organs seem to be drawn together. Constrictions in chest, throat. Concomitant with the heart symptoms are pain in forehead and temples. Collapse. Swooning fits. Feeling of intoxication. Loss of power over limbs and sphincters, unable to speak. Marked dyspnea, inability to lie on left side. Insensible right side. Left sided symptoms. Very susceptible to cold. Sensation of wasting away. Burnings as of hot irons. Screwed up sensation. MIND - Absent-mindedness. Very forgetful. Stupid and confused feeling. Irresolution, mdecision. Wandering of the mind. Brood- ng, over imaginary troubles and disease. Blurred speech. Insensible and speechless. Aphasia. Aversion to talking. Affected easily by wine or alcoholic drinks. Nervous, excited and tremulous. Wantof self confidence. Anxiety from pain in heart region. Forebodings. Hypochondria. Fear of death, disease, being incurable, rain, accidents, misfortune. Dreads to be left alone. Feels anguish for others. Anguish from pain in abdomen. Melancholy. Sorrow felt in the heart. Depressed, as if everything were done wrong and could not be rectified. Depressed with distress about sexual organs, better in evening. Despair with the pains. Loathing of life. Suicidal disposition (Aur.). Ailments from grief. Insanity. Antagonism with self. Confusion as to his identity. Sensation of duality. Delirium during fevers, with meningitis, typhus, typhoid fever. Sees images, phantoms. Delusion that he is a failure, that he has neglected his duty, that he is being injured. Consciousness almost lost. Comatose.

Head - Pain in forehead and temples with heart symptoms. Pain in left temple and in left orbital region, extending to occiput with nausea and vomiting. Severe throbbing and aching in temples. Constriction across forehead. Severe headache with intense depression. Headache supervening on cessation of menses. Neuralgic headache extending backwards from orbital region. Shooting up occiput. Vertex sensitive to cold. Aching in vertex with cold feet. Feeling as of a blow from behind on head and neck. Sensation as if brain was loose. Entire head feels hollow. Confusion and dullness in head in morning. Sensitiveness of scalp. Hair falls off the vertex

Eyes - Fixed and staring, wide open and insensible to light. Pupils dilated. Loss of vision. Hot pains at back of eyeballs. Ptosis of both lids. Heaviness in eyelids. Lids swollen in morning.

Ears - Burning heat of ear. Otalgia. Chronic otorrhea, black discharges, smells like herring brine. Noises in ears. Whizzing in left ear with insipid, almost nauseous taste in mouth. Noise as of a mill, waking him in morning. Illusions of hearing.

Nose - Hay fever with dry larynx. Hay asthma. Flow of water from nose, then intense sneezing which betters the breathing.

Mouth - Great dryness of the mouth. Wide open, flow of saliva. Foaming at mouth. Taste insipid, bitter, sour, metallic. Tongue cold, coated thick yellow, white, dry, no thirst. Ulcers on frenum. Loss of speech.

Throat - Roughness and scraping in throat. Soreness and pricking in left side of throat. Dryness and constriction of throat and fauces. Dark red color of the fauces. Redness of left side in morning with pain on swallowing. Irritation and tickling in larynx and trachea. Stricture of esophagus, swallowing difficult or impossible. Grasping at throat with sense of choking. As a lump in throat. Much mucus in throat. Shooting in left tonsil. Vertigo - Vertigo, lasting a short time, followed by astounding pain in right side of head. COMMENTS - Naja, was introduced into homeopathy by Russell and Stokes, who made the first provings along with some forty other provers including Gillow, Pope and Drysdale. Provings were made with low potencies. Majumdar had no success with Naja, until he obtained fresh venom from snake charmers and made potencies. Previously the Naja, used by Indian homeopaths had been re-imported into India from England in the form of potencies. Deane, in his experience in the plague epidemic of 1899-1900, found Naja, prepared from the fresh venom more efficacious than Lach. Naja, has an affinity for the medulla oblongata and cerebellum. Heart failure and distress. Weak valves with regurgitations, stenosis, prolapse. Acute and chronic endocarditis. Heart damage after infectious diseases. Low blood pressure. Fluttering palpitation sensations outside the chest. Depression and weakness about the heart. Inability to speak with choking, nervous chronic palpitations. Pulse is slow, irregular. Severe pains in left temple, cardiac and ovarian region. Diphtheria with impending paralysis of heart. Sensation of weight, of a hot iron, on the chest. Sensation as if heart and ovary were drawn together. Pains about heart extending to nape of neck, left shoulder and arm with anxiety and fear of death. Neuralgic pain in head, preceded or followed by nausea or vomiting. Severe throbbing in left orbital region drawing back to occiput, from over-eating, mental or physical exertion. Headache after cessation of menses. Dull, heavy constriction in forehead on waking. Characteristic grasping at the throat with choking sensations. Esophageal spasms. Worse at night, patient wakes gasping, surface blue. Worse by lying on left side. Useful for snake bites (Lach.). According to Hering, nervous phenomena predominate in Naja, over other serpent poisons. It acts primarily upon the nervous system, especially on respiratory nerves, pneumogastric and glossopharyngeal. Majumdar related the case of a young woman suffering from a heart affection who had oppression of the chest amounting almost to suffocation, feeble, irregular, almost imperceptible pulse, anemic appearance, inability to speak. One dose of Naja, was given, followed four hours later by a second. These sufficed for the cure. The next day, when the doctor called, his patient addressed him in a loud voice, “Doctor, you gave me a poison last night.” When asked to explain, she said that after the first dose she “felt awful heat in her system.” Majumdar saved a number of apparently hopeless cases of cholera with Naja, in the collapse stage with lack of pulse and difficulty of breathing. In a case cured by Russell there was dragging and anxiety in the précordia occurring in great grief. Andrew M. Neatby related a cure with Naja. 6c that had nervous palpitations and faintness, frequent sensation of swelling, of “choking” in the throat, with dyspnea and occasionally of anesthesia down the right side. Mahlon Preston cured himself with Naja. 30c of asthma with difficult breathing, worse lying down, better sitting up. He cured many cases of hay fever and autumnal catarrh that had a flow of water from the nose for a few minutes, then intense sneezing, which relieved the breathing. After recurring for a few days, there is dryness in the lungs with great difficulty of breathing, worse on lying down. Bunn cured the case of Miss S., 22, who had dysmenorrhea since her menses were established. Dilatation, galvanism., etc., had been tried in vain. She had shooting pain in the region of the left ovary and faintness. Hypogastrium revealed nothing abnormal except sensitiveness of the ovarian region. Extreme restlessness with the pain. During the menses the pains suddenly became very severe. The flow stopped when the pain was at its worst and returned the next day with relief from pain. Naja. 30c was given and the next period passed absolutely free from discomfort. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Ammonia, stimulants (effects of bite), tobacco (to potencies). Compare: (1) Snake venoms. (2) Bung-f.- this venom produces a condition like an acute polioencephalitis and myelitis. (3) Lach., Crot-h., Spig., Spong. (4) Depression and suicidal tendency, Aur. (5) Ulcer of frenum lingue, Nat-c. Agar. (6) Headache from before backwards, Anae., Bry., Nux-v. (7) from behind forwards, Gels., Lac-c., Sang., Sil., Spig. (8) Diphtheria. Arum-t. (9) Heart, Ars., Cact., Iber., Lach., Spig., Dig. (10) Collapse, Carb-v., Camph.. Tab. (11) Mouth wide open tongue cold, Camph. ( 12) Loss of speech, Dulc., Gels., Caust., Hy., Laur. (13) Dark red, color of fauces. Ail., Bapt., Phyt. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Uneasy, disagreeable feeling in stomach, as from indigestion, pressure as from stones after a meal. Acidity in stomach. Heartburn, belchings tasting like barley water or hot and foul. Nausea with faint feeling, vomiting.

Abdomen - Aching in loins. Cutting, twisting, griping pains. Much flatulence with rumbling and colicky pains. Flatulence during day, at night with pain. Frequent cutting in umbilical region and small of back in afternoon, then profuse and sudden leucorrhea.

Rectum - Urging always sudden, whether followed by diarrhea or not. Sudden urging, then small, bilious stool. Constipation, feeling of a large stool which when voided was small. Diarrhea with pain in abdomen, profuse, sudden, slimy, white or green, bilious. Heat in anal region with itching, smarting at anus. Sensations - Screwed-up sensations and crampy pains. As if head screwed together. As if heart and ovary were drawn up together. Pains in temple and ovarian regions. Pain from heart to scapula. Sensation as if a hair in larynx. Pain as from needles in tonsil. The left side is predominantly affected.

Male - Stinging, somewhat burning pain along right side of penis, immediately under skin, at night in bed and in morning after rising. Increased sexual desire. Desire on going to bed with frequent waking, vivid imaginations. Nocturnal emissions. Involuntary emissions, then prostration and distress. Peculiar distress, great desire, but no physical power, with depression.

Female - Pain in left groin, especially in post-operative cases, seems to be drawn to heart. Neuralgia of left ovary. Crampy pains in left ovary. Aching in left ovary with pains in heart, come on a week before menses, grow worse until menses appear, then easier until next month. Food - Loss of appetite. Thirsty. Craving for stimulants, which aggravate.

Chest - Constriction in chest, in evening. Oppressive weight on chest, as if a hot iron had been run in. Uneasiness and dull, heavy pain in chest. Sharp pains, worse on deep inspiration. Ribs feel broken. Heavy pain over lower half of right chest with stabbing on deep inspiration, cannot cough for the stabbing, worse lying left side, better lying on affected side. Tenderness over sternum and in throat.

Heart - Acute and chronic septic endocarditis . Damaged heart after infectious diseases. Hypertrophy, weakness. Valvular heart disorders. Heart lesions (Spong., Laur.). Low bloodpressure (Elaps., Vip.). Visible palpitations. Palpitations prevent speech because of choking. Chronic nervous palpitations, worse after preaching. Threatened paralysis of heart, body cold. Sharp pain in region of heart. Angina pains extending to nape of neck, left shoulder and arm with anxiety and fear of death. Heart symptoms with pain in forehead and temples. Dragging and anxiety in précordia. Feeling of weight on heart. Irregular in force. Pulse slow, irregular, weak, tremulous.

Back - Rheumatic pains in neck and back. Cutting, aching in nape. Tired feeling in thoracic vertebra all day with burning and exhaustion. Shooting from inner and upper angle of left scapula to front of chest. Pain between the shoulders as if in spine afterwards involving scapula in morning on waking, worse moving arms. Dragging sensation in spine between shoulders. Acute pain in small of back, gnawing pain. Breasts - Milk decreased, next day returned freely, afterwards scanty. Occasional pain at top of both breasts. Causations - Ailments from anticipation, grief, sorrow.

Limbs - Sudden loss of strength in limbs. Rheumatic pains in limbs. Drawing, lacerating, worse motion. Cramps in shoulders, nape or thighs. Aching in ankles, lower part of thighs, wrists and shoulder joints, on waking. Violent racking in marrow of thighs. Numb left arm. Puffy or sweating hands and feet with cough. Acute pain under the left thumb nail running up the arm. Lungs - Labored and difficult breathing. Gasping for breath. Puffing breathing. Breathing very slow, shallow and scarcely perceptible. Suffocative spells after sleeping. (Lach.). Dry or empty feeling in left lung. Asthmatic constriction of chest, cannot expand lungs, followed by mucus expectoration. Asthma preceded by coryza, worse lying, better sitting up. Cardiac asthma. Expectoration of whitish viscid mucus in morning on waking. Spitting of blood, which had no tendency to coagulate.

Sleep - Yawning, great sleepiness. Dozing and moaning. Sleepiness in evening and weakness. Deep, profound, comatose with stertorous breathing. Restless, disturbed sleep. Long and vivid dreams, little recol- lection of the subjects, affairs of the day recalled with additions and new plans for the morrow. Dreams of murders, suicides, fires, etc.

Skin - Itching scars. Creeping, itching and tingling sensation in skin. Skin swollen, mottled and of dark purple, livid color. Gangrene. Small, white itching blisters on inflamed base, on neck, nose and body in afternoon. Large pimples on inflamed base. Pimple on upper lip, on left ala nasi, on tip of nose, sore in consequence, painful on brow. Boil-like swelling on back of middle phalanx of right little finger. Painful chilblains on feet.

Modalities - Great relief of pain and breathing by lying on right side. Better from walking or riding in open air, sneezing, smoking. Worse from stimulants, alcohol, cold air, drafts, riding in carriage, touch, pressure of clothes. Worse lying on left side, after sleep, after menses. Headache worse at 3 p.m.

Kidneys - Uneasiness and pressure in bladder. Urine of deep straw color. Urine deposits red sediment, mixed with mucus, loaded with gravel and mucus.

Cough - Irritating, dry cough. Cough from sticky mucus and saliva. Cough with tightness and fullness in larynx. Cardiac cough. Dry, hacking cough with blood-spitting. Hoarseness, short, hoarse cough.

Temperature - Body cold and collapsed. Limbs very cold, icy coldness of feet. Very sensitive to cold. General sweat, cold, clammy. Free perspiration. Flushes of heat in face at different times of day, worse left side. Head hot and full of blood and much sweat in palms. Feels very uncomfortable, hot and feverish. Heat, but he refused water, heat with prostration with discomfort, dry lips and tender, hot mouth.

full:
PHARMACY - naphtin. Naphthalinum. Tar camphor. Naphthalene. Achemical compound from coal tar. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Amblyopia. Asthma. Bronchitis. Cataract. Diarrhea. Eczema. Flatulence. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Hay asthma. Psoriasis. Retina, detached. Tuberculosis. Typhoid fever. Whooping cough. Worms.

HOMEOPATHIC - Naphthalene is a hydrocarbon obtained by distillation from coal tar. It consists of colorless, transparent, lustrous scales or, when crystallized, of rhombic tables or prisms. Naphtin. is an unproved remedy, though it has been used in old-school practice as an intestinal antiseptic and vermifuge, as an expectorant, as a remedy for eczema and psoriasis, and as an antiseptic application to wounds. Naphtin. is for the expulsion of thread worms after the bowels have been freely opened by a cathartic, given in doses of grains 1/4 to grains 1/2 four times a day for two days. The dose should not be given after a meal and all fats and oils should be abstained from during the treatment, which may be repeated once or twice after leaving a week’s interval. Affinity for the eyes. Detachment of the retina, deposits an exudation in the retina. Opacity of cornea, cataract, amblyopia. Long and continued attacks of coughing, unable to get a breath, sometimes so violent as to cause perspiration. Whooping cough.

Head - Saliva flows from the mouth.

Eyes - Eyes inflamed, painful, bloodshot, in hay fever. Cataract. Amblyopia. Detached retina. Shiny bodies in vitreous. White patches on retina of oxalate, sulphate and carbonate of calcium.

Nose - Coryza, thin, excoriating discharge, much sneezing. Hay fever. Attacks of sneezing. Irritation of nose. Rubs his nose to remove the irritation.

Face - Lips and face cyanotic. Face pale, yellow. Twitching of facial muscles. Food - Loss of appetite.

Abdomen - Incarcerated flatus in the transverse colon causing cardiac distress.

Rectum - Incontinence of urine and feces. Thin, offensive diarrhea of tuberculosis. Skin - Eczema. Psoriasis.

Sleep - Very great drowsiness lasting some days.

Kidneys - Sudden, violent desire to urinate, urethra meatus red and swollen, prepuce edematous. Urine is dark brown, becoming black after standing, albuminous. Incontinence of urine. Gonorrhea. Gleet. Lungs - Breathing is labored and irregular, asthmatic. Cough in violent, incessant paroxysms almost arresting breath, compelling the patient to hold his head for the pain. Cough with blue or purple face. Expectoration free, thick, tenacious, almost absent. Night cough preventing sleep. Male - Edema of prepuce.

Temperature - Sudden onset of a fever, with headache and loss of appetite. Temperature reduced in typhoid. COMMENTS - Some cases of Naphtin. poisoning have been reported. Evers recorded chronic illness, loss of appetite, headache and eczema over both legs as due to Naphtin. which was used as a moth powder and sprinkled on bedding. In another case, a boy, 12, came home one evening apparently drunk, semi-conscious, staggering, unable to answer questions. He had eaten two candies which were really mothdestroyers, each tablet containing two grams of pure naphthalin. An emetic was promptly administered and the next day the boy was still drowsy but quite conscious. The drowsiness lasted four days. Attacks of sneezing from nasal irritation, frequently attempting to remove the irritation by rubbing his nose. In two hours incoordination had increased. Twitching of facial muscles. Saliva flowed freely from the mouth. Lippincott was the first to use Naphtin. in cases of hay fever, having heard that hay fever sufferers who went into factories where Naphtha was much used were always cured. His experience of its value was speedily confirmed by other observers. Naphtin. lx and 2x were used in the first trials. W. Louis Hartmann of Syracuse is the chief homeopathic authority for this remedy. His leading indications for it are acute coryza with fluent excoriating discharge and much sneezing. Paroxysms of coughing, following each other in rapid succession so that the patient is unable to take his breath (as in asthma and whooping cough). He found it more often indicated than any other drug in whooping cough. The spasmodic action and the cyanosis of the drug are good indications here, though it is not necessary to wait until the child is blue before prescribing Naphtin. Followed well by Dros. In a case of tuberculosis of the left lung, Naphtin. removed an inability to sleep for cough. Exhausting night- sweats and offensive, thin diarrhea during the day. In three cases in which Naphtin. had been applied to wounds there was sudden onset of fever, headache, loss of appetite. In one of them, there was temporary mania with incontinence of urine and feces. In two of them, albuminuria. All symptoms rapidly disappeared when Naphtin. was discontinued. J. Meredith cured with the Naphtin. 6x incarcerated flatus in transverse colon causing cardiac distress. Hartmann used the lx trituration, having been disappointed with higher potencies. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Salol., Carb- ac„ Anil., Methyl-b. and coal-tar products generally. (2) In coughs, Dros. which follows Naphtin. well. (3) Coc-c., Arn., Bell., Cor-r. Ip. (4) In tuberculosis, Petr., Basil. In eye af- fections, Choi. (5) In gonorrhea, Thuj., Petros., Salol. (6) In hay fever, Psor., Sabad., Ars., All- c., Kali-i. (7) In worms. Cina, Teucr. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Clarke.

name: Narcissus Poeticus
author: Murphy
constitution: Bronchitis. Coryza. Cough. Diarrhea. Whooping cough.
keynote:
PHARMACY - narc-po. Narcissus poeticus. Daffodil. N. O. Amaryllidaceae. Tincture of unexpended blossom- buds, stem, leaf and flower. The young buds, stems and leaves are macerated in two times their weight of alcohol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL -…
full:
PHARMACY - narc-po. Narcissus poeticus. Daffodil. N. O. Amaryllidaceae. Tincture of unexpended blossom- buds, stem, leaf and flower. The young buds, stems and leaves are macerated in two times their weight of alcohol. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bronchitis. Coryza. Cough. Diarrhea. Whooping cough.

HERBAL - The name of the plant, Narcissus, is not from that of the fabled youth who fell in love with his own image reflected in the water, but is from the Greek Narkao, “tobenumb, ”on account of the narcotic properties of the drug. Theclassic Asphodel and the Narcissusare the Narcissus poeticus same, from which it may be seen that the plant dates back as far as man’s records go. Dr. Charge’s work, Maladies de la Respiration, quoted the great Laennec as an authority in regards Narcissus. Fernie, in his excellent Herbal simples, also said “An extract of the bulbs applied to open wounds has produced staggering numbness of the whole nervous system and paralysis of the heart. Socrates called this plant the ‘Chaplet of the Infernal Gods,’ because of its narcotic effects.” He also noted that a decoction of the dried flowers is emetic and when sweetened will, as an emetic, serve most usefully for relieving the congestive bronchial catarrh of children. On the other hand, the alkaloid from the bulbs after flowering produces copious salivation, increases cutaneous secretion, contracts the pupil of the eye, produces slight relaxation of the pulse and slight faintness and nausea. Daffodil bulbs contain an alkaloid the action of which, according to authorities, varies as to whether the alkaloid is extracted from the flowering bulb or from the bulb after flowering. The National Dispensatory noted that “The emetic action of Narcissus has been used to break up intermittent fever and relieve bronchial catarrh with congestion or obstruction of the air tubes. Like Ipecacuanha, it has also been prescribed in dysentery, especially of the epidemic form. Its influence upon the nervous system is attested by the vogue it has enjoyed in hysteria, chorea, whooping cough and even epilepsy.”

HOMEOPATHIC - The concluding paragraph in Fernie’s section on the Narcissus states: “The medicinal influence of the daffodil on the nervous system has led to giving its flowers and its bulb for hysterical states and even epilepsy with benefit.” Narc-po. is peculiarly homeopathic to long-continued coughs, especially of nervous origin. Bronchitis. Convulsive stage of whooping cough. Coryza, frontal headache. Faintness and drowsiness. Symptoms of nausea followed by violent vomiting and diarrhea.

Head - Frontal headache.

Eyes - Running at eyes. Pupils contracted at first, dilated later.

Nose - Severe coryza.

Mouth - Increased flow of saliva. Free salivation of very ropy saliva.

Throat - Dryness in throat. COMMENTS - A patient of Clarke’s once had a very severe cough set up by daffodils used in some profusion as a decoration of a dinner table. A fatal case of poisoning from eating the flowers is on record. A salad of onions in which were mixed some bulbs of Narcissus poeticus, caused burning, copious stools with dreadful griping, obtuse senses, fainting, cold hands, and cold sweat. Symptoms were not distinguishable from the usual effects of Colch. and similar to those of Narc-ps. J. Meredith made a conserve of flowers, buds and stems by mashing them with six to ten times their weight of sugar in a Wedgwood mortar with a wooden pestle. Counting this as lx, he made sugar potencies to 4x, and with these he cured a case of bronchitis with continuous cough which had resisted many of the standard remedies. In Ringer’s experiments, the bulb preparation produced the greater number of effects including salivation, sinking, vomiting and diarrhea. The flower preparation acted on the head and eyes and dried up a profuse perspiration of the hands. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) All-c., Colch., Lil-t. Narc-ps. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Sinking, sick sensation. Rumbling. Heartburn. Hiccough. Vomiting.

Rectum - Diarrhea with severe aching below left free ribs. Stools are watery, relaxed, loose, some solid.

Heart - Pulse increased.

Skin - Erythema of a papular, vesicular and pustular types, aggravation in wet weather.

Temperature - Hand which was quite wet with perspiration became dry in twelve minutes.

full:

CLINICAL - Bladder, paralysis. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - Narcot. has been rather extensively proved, but very few distinctive symptoms were elicited. The most notable were dry, clammy mouth, thick indistinct speech and paralysis of bladder. The vertigo symptoms were like those of Morph., and the general symptoms those of Op. and its other alkaloids. REFERENCES-Clarke.

HERBAL - Nasturtium is useful in scorbutic disorders and constipation, related to strictures of urinary apparatus. Supposed to be an aphrodisiac.

HOMEOPATHIC - Nast, is antidotal to tobacco poisoning. Sedative in neurotic affections, neurasthenia, hysteria. Cirrhosis of liver and dropsy. REFERENCES - Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - nat-ar. Natrum arsenicum. Sodium arsenate. Atoxyl. Hydric di-sodic arsenate. Solution. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Anemia. Asthma. Blepharitis. Conjunctivitis. Coryza. Cough. Diphtheria. Edema. Emaciation. Esophagus, constriction. Eyes, inflammation. Granular, eyelids. Hemoptysis. Interscapular pain. Leukemia. Miner’s asthma. Nose, disorders. Pityriasis rubra. Post-nasal catarrh. Testicles, neuralgia. Tuberculosis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Nat-ar. has been very extensively proved, notably by Imbert Gourbeyre. The principal clinical useofNat-ar. has been in diphtheria, when it presents with a dark purple throat, great swelling, much prostration, and not much pain. Useful in disorders of the eyes and nose. Generally irritating effects. Miner’s asthma from coal dust. Lungs feel as if smoke had been inhaled. Racking cough with profuse greenish expectoration. Oppression of chest and about the heart. Nasal catarrh with headache, pain at root of nose, dry and painful eyes. Bronchitis of children, chronic. Feels tired all over. Psoriasis (Ars., Thyr.). Leukemia (Ars.). Emaciation. Edema. As if the thyroid gland were compressed by a thumb and finger. Cartier noted that it facilitates the termination of a cold and conserves strength and appetite. MIND - Mental dullness, listless. Concentration difficult while studying, reading. Forgetfulness. Imbecility. Timidity. Depressed, as if something bad impending. Lamenting, bemoaning, wailing. Hysteria. Ailments from anger, vexation. Quarrelsomeness, scolding. Reproaches himself and others. Conscientious about trifles. Fastidious. Nervous restlessness at night. Anxiety with palpitations. Anxiety about the future. Frightened easily. Fear of impending disease, that something bad will happen, of evil. Fear of people, in a crowd, anthropophobia. Aversion to company. Suspicious.

Head - Heat and fullness in head. Floating sensation on turning head quickly. Aching pain in frontal region, root of nose, and over orbits. Boring pain in temples. Headache, worse pressure. Headache from tobacco smoke. Periodical headaches, worse noise.

Eyes - Catarrhal conjunctivitis and blepharitis marginalis. Dry, painful, burning, stinging. Eyes feel weak, soon tire. Stiffness of eyeballs, feel too large. Smarting and lachrymation on going into open air. Agglutination in morning. Tendency of lids to close, cannot open them as wide as usual. Edema of orbital region. Supraorbital pain.

Ears - Ears feels heavy and drooped.

Nose - Feels stopped up, pain at root. Nasal catarrh, withpainatrootofnose. Coryza, worse open air, fluent alternating with dry. Watery discharge, drops into throat. Post-nasal dropping of thick, bland, yellowish mucus. Crusts in nose. Dry crusts, on removal, leave mucus membrane raw. Smell defective or lost.

Face - Feels puffed, bloated. Swollen face. Hot and flushed. Malar bone feels large, as if swollen. Masseter muscles stiff, painful to move jaw. Eruptions around mouth. Corners of mouth fissured.

Throat - Dark, purplish, swollen, edematous. red and glassy. Roughness causes hemming, with spasmodic cough. Hawking of tough, gelatinous, greyish yellow mucus from throat and posterior nares. Dark slate-colored, scanty mucus in larynx, detached with difficulty. Elongation of uvula. Sensation as if thyroid were compressed by a thumb and finger.

Stomach - Stomach tender. Sensation of fullness. Sinking sensation, with dull feeling in supraorbital and frontal region. Hematemesis. Belching and sour eructations.

Abdomen - Pain from abdomen at times, shifting through bowels, better by passage of flatus or stool. Gas forms rapidly, better when bowels move, colic from flatus and before stool. Pain in groin.

Rectum - Diarrhea, alternating with constipation. Stool thin, dark, soft, followed by burning at anus. Yellowish, watery, copious, painless, hurries out of bed in morning. Diarrhea worse at night. Diarrhea from milk. Sensations - Some of the peculiar symptoms are wavering, floating sensation on turning head. Eyeballs feel stiff, feel too large for lids to close over. Scratching beneath lids on rolling eyeballs. Pain at root of nose. Feeling of lump in throat of blow on testicle, as if smoke inhaled into lungs. Feeling as if the body were compressed by thumb and finger.

Male - Dull, cutting pain along inguinal ligament, followed by sickening sensation in left testicle as from a blow, testicle very sensitive while pain lasts.

Female - Menses protracted, scanty. Leucorrhea, thick, offensive, yellow.

Chest - Oppression of chest and about heart, worse exertion and full inspiration. Roughness and irritation in bronchi mornings, with slight cough. Eruption on chest, dark brown scaly spots on a red base, no itching. Coughs - Teasing, dry cough, during day. Dry cough, with feeling of tightness and oppression in chest. Dry, hacking cough, from an uneasy feeling and soreness beneath ribs, worse any exertion. Racking cough with profuse, greenish expectoration. Hemoptysis.

Heart - Oppression about heart on least exertion. Can feel heartbeat through chest distinctly .Sounds heard through nearly ev- ***ery part of chest. Pulse irregular, variable in volume. Pulse slower than usual.

Back - Pain and soreness in back. Neck stiff and sore. Soreness at lower cervical vertebra down to joints of scapula and under both scapula. Severe pain between scapula, better moving forward, worse from inspiration. Pain in lumbar region.

Limbs - Neuralgic pain, recurring frequently. Pain in anterior crural nerves. Pains erratic, worse in joints and on left side. Feels tired all over. Joints stiff. Knee joints crack. Aching in arms, worse in shoulder. Lungs - Oppression of chest and about heart and also larynx. Pneumonia and tuberculosis. Lungs feel as if smoke had been inhaled. Asthma, worse dust and smoke. Miner’s asthma produced by inhalation of coal dust.

Sleep - Drowsy, heavy sleep. Restless sleep, when aroused awakes nervously as from a fright.

Skin - Squamous eruption, scales thin, white, and when removed leave skin slightly reddened. Scales cause itching, worse getting warm from exercise.

Modalities - Worse on moving, jarring, least exertion, pressure, during the day.

Tongue - Tongue coated yellow, deep red, corrugated, anterior part fissured. Tongue large, moist, fissured, flabby. Vertigo - Floating sensation on turning head quickly. Vision - Vision weakened, objects blur when he looks at them for a short time, eyes sensitive to light. COMMENTS - Leukemia (Ars., Nat-m.), especially in children. Pain between scapula, better bending forward. Headache, worse from heat. Restlessness, thirst, chilliness with a hot head (Ars.). Nasal obstruction and chilliness, worse at night. Sensitive to cold air. Itching is worse when heated, by exercise. Warm things cause burning in stomach, cold drinks aggravate nausea. Wind causes conjunctivitis. Right side of head, left testicle and left leg are most affected. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ars., Kali-c. - edema about eyes and face. (2) Apis - diphtheria with sac-like swelling of uvula, but Apis has much pain, Nat-a. has not. (3) Arum-t. - diphtheria, Arum-t. has less swelling and more pain. (4) Kali-bi. - tenacious mucus. (5) Nat-m. - throat. (6) Lyc. - stopped catarrh. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Kidneys - Dull, aching pain in kidneys, with profuse urine. Sore feeling in region of bladder, worse urinating. Urine copious, frequent, clear. Urine contains some epithelial scales, casts and fat globules.

Perspiration - Surface cool, covered with cold, clammy sweat.

author: Murphy

full:
PHARMACY - nat-cac. Natrum cacodylicum. Sodium cacodylate. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Dermatitis. Neuritis. Paralysis. Tuberculosis. Wrist-drop.

HOMEOPATHIC - This acid (and more particularly its sodium salt) has been used on the retommendation of Armand Gautier, Professor of Chemistry at the Faculty of Medicine of Paris, as a “cure” for tuberculosis. The non-poisonous nature of this salt enables the patients to take it in large doses, but it is not always harmless. Cacodyl, which signifies evil-smelling, is like Cyanogen, a compound radical. It was first obtained by Bunsenis 1873 as di-cacodyl. It is a clear liquid that refracts light strongly, heavier than water, of insup- portably offensive smell, its vapor being highly poisonous. Cacodylic acid is a crystalline arsenic compound, soluble in water, odorless and, though containing 54.4 percent of metallic arsenic, not an active poison. Useful for malignant diseases and growths. Tuberculosis. Foul breath and mouth with bad odor. Dry dermatitis of the skin of abdomen. COMMENTS - Murrell gave Nat-cac. in pills of one grain, three times a day, to a young woman, 21. Poisoning symptoms set in suddenly after the eleventh dose, including constant vomiting, tongue like a piece of raw beef, inflamed conjunctive, eyelids edematous. Breath of gangrenous odor, peripheral neuritis, wrist-drop, paralysis of left leg. The odor was noticed on second day, the other symptoms came suddenly. REFERENCES - Clarke.

author: Murphy
