PHARMACY - org-p. Organophosphate. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Ataxia. Chronic fatigue. Chemical, sensitivity. Colic. Coma. Convulsions. Cramps. Dementia. Dystonia. Food, allergies. Heart disease. Incoordination. Multiple sclerosis. Muscle weakness. Nausea. Neuropathy. Palpitations. Paralysis. Parkinson's disease. Osteoporosis. Twitching. Vertigo. Vomiting. Weakness.

HOMEOPATHIC - Organophosphate compounds are a diverse group of chemicals used in both domestic and industrial settings. Examples include insecticides (malathion, parathion, diazinon, fenthion, dichlorvos, chlorpyrifos), nerve gases (soman, sarin, tabun, VX), ophthalmic agents (echothio- phate, isoflurophate), and antihelmintics (trichlorfon). Herbicides (tribufos [DEF], merphos) are tricresyl phosphate-containing industrial chemicals. Severe anxiety. Restlessness. Confusion. Impairment of concentration and memory. Confusion, irritability, lethargy. Tearfulness. Depression, with suicidal tendencies. Hallucinations. Psychosis. Muscular contractions. Ataxia. Seizures. Convulsions. Dysarthria, tremors. Polyneuropathy. Paralysis. Insomnia. Cancer. Coma. Respiratory distress. Bronchospasm and .laryngeal spasm, can lead to airway obstruction. Weakness and paralysis of respiratory muscles. Chest pain. Cerebral ischemia. Chronic fatigue syndrome. Malaise. General sick feeling. Severe, debilitating fatigue which is physical and mental. Loss of muscular strength. Muscle aching, flitting from one group of muscles or joints to another. Degeneration of handwriting. Episodic blurred vision. Immune weakness, tendency to acquire infections and difficulty getting rid of infections, autoimmunity. Multiple chemical sensitivity. Drug intolerance (such as alcohol, antidepressants). Food intolerances. Birth defects. MIND - Poor short term memory. Unable to learn new things. Poor concentration, Speech difficulty with poor word finding. Irritability and aggression. Severe anxiety. Nervousness and apprehension. Impairment of concentration and memory. Destabilization of mood. Mood swings. Increased tearfulness. Depression and psychosis. Impulsive suicidal thoughts. Dementia. Rage. Hallucinations.

Head - Headache. Cerebral ischemia.

Eyes - Optic neuropathy. Retinal degeneration. Myopia, and miosis. Pupils dilated. Excess lachrymation. Blurred vision.

Nose - Allergies. Acute sense of smell. Perspiration - Increased sweating.

He dissolved five or six globules of this dilution in four teaspoonfuls of fresh water and the young masturbator takes of this every two days, a quarter of an hour before the meal, one teaspoonful. If the cure is not accomplished eight days after this solution is used up, the same dose is repeated in the same way. When desired, this remedy can be used according to Gallavardin without the knowledge of the patient, by pouring a teaspoonful into the soup, milk or chocolate. The effect frequently appears very rapidly, but some- times it does not appear. Clarke verified the power of Orig. in morbid sexual excitement in both sexes. The sexual symptoms were developed chiefly in the female provers and included sadness followed by joyfulness and thoughts of marriage. Lascivious dreams. Increased desire for sex. Swelling and itching of nipples and pains in breasts. “Impulse to run.” “Heat of head, as the heat increased the head was involuntarily turned from side to side.” Symptoms were worse evening on lying down (vertigo) and worse at night (excessive thirst). (4) In masturbation, desire to run, heat to head and movements of head, disorders of breasts, Bufo. (5) In impulse to run, lod. (6) Canth., Cann-i., Coll., Hedeo., Helon., Plat., Valer. HERBAL - Oregano grows wild in the mountains of the Mediterranean region. The name is derived from a Greek word meaning “joy of the mountains.” It was used by Greek physicians for trauma, wounds, headaches, lung disorders and venomous bites and was the traditional cure for hemlock poisoning. Over the centuries it gained widespread use for lung conditions, asthma, pneumonia, bronchitis, sinusitis, allergies, and cough. Britain's Gerard, in his 17th century manuscript, explained the use of oregano as a top remedy for head colds. The 19th Century eclectic physicians used oregano as a general tonic and a promoter of menstruation (which is why it should not be used during pregnancy). REFERENCES - Murphy.

full:
PHARMACY - omi. Ornithogalum umbellatum. Star of Bethlehem. N. O. Liliaceae. Hyacinthaceae. A plant of which there are many varieties, nearly allied to garlic, Allium sativum. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Cancer. Constipation. Depression. Flatulence. Gastric, ulcer. Prostration. Restlessness. Stonuich, cancer. Stomach, ulcers. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Orni. is to be considered in chronic gastric and other abdominal indurations, like cancer of intestinal tract, especially of stomach and cecum. Pains in stomach with sickness, vomiting two or three times a day. Swollen feeling across lower chest. Flatulence. Heartburn and rising of food. Gastric ulcer and cancer. Painful contraction in the pylorus with duodenal distention. Feels as if a bag of water turns when she turns over in bed. Complete prostration. Cold before the pains. Feels a pressure in every nerve of the body, sometimes in one part or another with pain across chest, sometimes after food or at night and sometimes on an empty stomach. Restlessness on account of creepy feeling in feet, cannot sit still, cannot read without walking about. Painful sinking across pit of chest and a feeling of sickness that kept her awake the greater part of the night. Writhing in agony, unable to keep anything long on stomach, better by warm food, worse by cold drinks. MIND - Hateful. Depression and desire for suicide.

Mouth - Tongue red, coated towards back. Nasty taste in morning.

Stomach - Loss of appetite. Painful sinking across epigastrium. Agonizing feeling in chest and stomach, starting from pylorus with flatus that rolls in balls from one side to the other. Pains increased when food passes pyloric outlet. Frequent belching of offensive flatus. Phlegm retchings and loss of weight. Vomiting of coffee-ground looking matter. Gastric ulceration with hemorrhage. COMMENTS - For stomach cancer (Hydr., Cad-s.), stomach ulcers, or a history of ulcers followed by stomach cancer. Stomach cancer after a vaccination. The abdomen is distended and hardened. Writhing in agony from stomach pain. Keynote belching. Emaciation (Hydr.). Used in the Bach Flower system for shock. In his “Cancer and Cancer Symptoms” Dr. Cooper published several cases of cancer helped by Orni. Cooper particularly insisted on his method being followed: a dose of a single drop being allowed to act until all trace of its action has disappeared. Cooper noted the case of a man named George, 40, who suffered from stomach cancer. His father had died of a stomach ulcer at 73. He was sent to the cancer hospital in London. They began to operate, but abandoned the operation because of overwhelming numbers of adhesions. Cooper first saw him July 22, 1898. The patient was writhing in agony on his bed, unable to keep anything down. He was better by some warm foods, worse by cold drinks. The pains were worse at night. Cooper gave one drop of Orni. tincture on July 23 at 6:00, this was followed by an aggravation of great pains and the patient was frantic until 3:00 a.m. At 1:00 p.m. the next day he had a bowel movement. Then he developed flatulence and pain, and was given Carb-v. 3x as an acute, which cured those symptoms. Three days later, Cooper saw the patient and the pain that was in his stomach had begun spreading out to the rest of his body. A second dose of Orni. was given on the evening of July 28. Immediately after taking that dose, he vomited a black, jelly-like substance that greatly relieved the pains and generally improved his energy and appetite. From that time on there was steady progress. On August 29th, the patient reported that he was getting some pain in the lower abdomen. He had difficulty getting to sleep and he had started getting creeping sensations in his legs. He repeated a dose on September 9. On September 18, he reported that he was sleeping better, there was more pain in the legs, but it was not so bad, and there were slight pains in the stomach. His appetite and energy were improved. On September 23, his right leg felt bruised and began to swell. He started choking on food. He was given another dose. Some flatulence returned. In a few days, the man came to Cooper's office in a great fright. Both his legs were swollen with red streaks. Believing these were to do with the rapid elimination of the cancer. Dr. Cooper thought he was being too aggressive in the case, so he gave no medicine. The man was astonished. The legs became swollen and inflamed, then returned to normal. In July 1901, Cooper visited his patient to find him in good health without any signs of cancer or pain. In the same volume, Cooper reproduced from H. W. (April, 1898) cases of ulceration of the stomach in elderly women cured with the same remedy. Miss J., 50, was a thin, drawn-featured woman. Her sister died of stomach cancer. She had vomited blood fifteen years ago and had been subject to gastric pains since. Pains in stomach with sickness. Vomited two or three times a day. Felt a pressure in every nerve of body, sometimes in one part, sometimes in another, with pain across Ornithogalum umbellatum the chest. Pain at night, or after food and sometimes on an empty stomach. She had a great deal of wind and sometimes a swollen feeling across the lower chest. Occasional heartburn with rising of food. Nasty canker taste in the morning. Could not sleep from the pains, had wandering dreams. Bowels were confined. Orni. tincture was given, one dose, on November 6. On November 13, the patient was seen again. Symptoms had moderated, vomiting ceased. A new symptom appeared, “wakes in perspiration at night.” That diminished by November 27. Pains better, “gets cold before the pains.” No heartburn, still a nasty taste and confined bowel. The dose was repeated. The day after this dose, the bowels loosened with general relief. This went on, increasing under more doses of the remedy, until the patient regained almost perfect health and was quite changed in appearance. Mrs. K., 62, had been seized with profuse vomiting of blood eighteen months before. Since then she lived on slops and Quaker oats. Lately, she spat up clots. Whenever she turns in bed she “feels as if a bag of water turns also.” Feet and legs swollen, unable to walk with ease. A brother is said to have died of cancer. On January 12, 1898, one dose of Orni. in tincture was given. On January 23, she was so much better that she could hardly believe the effect. The oppression of the stomach was gone. The “fluid sack” that rolled about in her seemed to go down and she felt nothing of it. She felt cheery and light. On February 10, there was a threatened return of the symptoms, but another dose permanently removed them. Cooper added the account of how he was led to think of Orni. in cancer. “My acquaintance with it in cancer cases was due to the very distinctive disturbance it produced in a woman very sensitive to all alliaceous flavor- ing substances in food. The dose was taken at midday and the same evening distention of the stomach and duodenum came on. “Also frequent belching of mouthfuls of offensive flatus obliging her to loosen her clothes. This was accompanied by the most hateful depression of spirits and desire for suicide. A feeling of complete prostration and painful sinking across the pit of the chest. A feeling of sickness that kept her awake the greater part of the night and that did not pass off for several days. “The subject of this disturbance was about fifty-four years of age of quite a sanguine temperament inclined to the enfeebled digestion and with a history of pleuritic seizures and a possible tubercular tendency, but otherwise not subject to any settled form of disease. Since the medicinal thrill above recorded, her general strength, digestion and capacity for the enjoyment of life have manifestly improved. “The Ornith. in those sensitive to it goes at once to the pylorus, causes painful spasmodic contraction of it and distends the duodenum with flatus, its pains being invariably increased when the food attempts to pass the pyloric outlet of the stomach.” Clarke had several opportunities to confirm Cooper's observations on the action of Orni. for cancer the stomach, including the case of Mr. W., 44, who came to him in August, 1899. Both parents had died of cancer. He had a weak stomach for two or three years and was wasting. He had to get up in the night to vomit, bringing up green and yellow liquid. He had much flatus, “swells up in balls of wind.” His abdomen was large and hard, with a rather large spleen. Venous zigzag. Stools were loose, watery, slate-colored. Urine was scanty, dark. He had been vaccinated three or four times. He made good progress under Thuj. 30c once a week, the vomiting ceased and he began to put on flesh. He developed an offensive body odor, which disappeared under Sulph. 30c, but on October 13, symptoms were rather worse. He had some distention, wind did not pass freely. Rumbling before stool. Balls of wind rolled about, but not as badly as at first. Frothy, acid vomiting, which relieved. Clarke then gave Orni. tincture, one dose, repeated three weeks later with manifest improvement in the symptoms. His body was much less hard and distended. Sleep and appetite were good, cessation of vomiting and gain of three pounds in weight. When he returned, the symptoms were different and another remedy was required and then he considered himself cured. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) All-s„ in flatulent indigestion. (2) Abies-n., Cham., Chin., Carb-v., Lyc. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Abdomen - Hardness and distention of abdomen, with frequent belching of mouthfuls of offensive flatus. Wind rolling in balls from side to side. Obliged to loosen clothing.

Sleep - Great difficulty in going to sleep because of acreepy feeling in limbs. Sleep disturbed by pains. Waking in perspiration at night. Wandering dreams.

HOMEOPATHIC - In the year 1925, Joseph Roy is believed to have observed in some conditions of a culture the existence of a germ animated by an oscillating movement. He named the nosode Oscillococcinum because of this fact. These researches helped him to describe a remedy of which the clinical experiments in the infections of influenza were carried out in particular by Paul Chavanon. Oscilloc. was developed by Boiron Laboratory in France. Pierre Schmidt said Oscilloc. is for “influenza at the beginning as a preventive, as well as during convalescence” Influenza of all types, especially in the earlier stages. Epidemic influenza. B ursting headaches and muscle aching. Gastro-intestinal troubles with the influenza. Beginning of influenza, rhinitis and otitis. Tendency to get influenza. Given early it is very efficacious. To obtain good results in a case which begins and to cut short the manifestations of influenza, it is necessary to use one dose of Oscillococcinum 200c every 2 to 3 hours or repeat only if necessary. Anxiety, paleness, chill. Sensitiveness to barometric weather changes. Tuberculous patients sensitive to cold. Asthenia, hyperthermia. Eye and nasal catarrh. Bronchial congestion. Painful congestion of the ear drum. Schmidt noted it for “Mastoiditis, at the beginning of a disease which does not develop.” MIND - Subjects with fixed ideas, obsessions. Obstinate. Agony, anxious without any motive. A busy body. Maniac, cannot bear disorder. Fear of dirt, of being polluted. Has the need to wash his hands very often and is afraid of giving his hand to others for the fear of pollution, contagion.

Head - Bursting headaches. Headache with considerable throbbing.

Eyes - Yellow conjunctiva. Conjunctivitis of influenza. Eye catarrh.

Ears - Pains sometimes as if from needles in one or both ears. Tympanum red and swollen. Mastoiditis. Diminution of hearing acuity.

Nose - Nasal voice. Nasal catarrh. Stuffed nose, nasal obstruction, sneezing. Serous discharge from the nose, then mucopurulent.

Face - Pain in the frontal and maxillary region. Food - Can digest neither milk nor eggs.

Mouth - Tongue white.

Throat - Aphonia, dry painful cough. RELATIONS - Eup-per. is to be associated with it. Compare: ( 1 )Eup-per., Gels., Pyrog..Bapt., Ars., Influ. (2) Gaulphimia glauca - Hyperse- cretion of the nasal and ocular mucous, sneezing, hypersensitivity to change of weather. (3) Gelinsoga purviflora - Morning headache, makes mistakes when writing numbers and letters, stuffed nose, augmentation of diuresis, joint pains, lassitude, feels as if bruised. (4) Gink. . Pale face, drawn traits, numbness and chill. Laryngeal irritation with cough, frontal and left supra - órbita pain. (4) Luf-op. - Frontal-occipital headache, acute or chronic inflammation of the mucus membrane of the nasal fossa, lassitude and bodily fatigue. REFERENCES - Julian.

HOMEOPATHIC - Osmium is a metal of the platinum group in association with which it is always found. It is the heaviest of them all and the most refractory, having never been fused. It derives its name from the pungent odor of the fumes of osmic acid, which are evolved in the process of separating platinum from its ore. The odor of Osmium closely resembles that of chlorine, as also do its irritating effect on the respiration mucus membrane. The odor imparted to the secretions is various, it makes the urine smell like violets, the belchings like radishes, the axillary sweat like garlic. Triturations of the pure metal have been proved. The symptoms of the metal and of the acid are taken together. Osm. affects the respiratory tract, especially the trachea. Irritation and catarrh of respiratory organs. Pain in trachea. Pains go up and down. Crawling on back and shoulders. Increases and gives odor to local perspiration. Albuminuria. Eczema. Causes adhesion of the nail fold. MIND - Morose, irritable, impatient. Weeping mood, screaming with cough. Weak, gives up. Consciousness of mental weakness, misplaces words. Thoughts of accidents having happened to others. Disinclination for work.

Head - Feels as if a band around head. Dull, heavy headache. Violent headache above and under the eyes. Sharp bewildering pain in center of forehead. Aching in base of brain and jaws at night. Pain in vertex and occiput, worse throwing head backward. Falling off of hair (Kali-c., Fl-ac.).

Eyes - Increase in intra-ocular tension, dim sight, photophobia. Conjunctivitis. Glaucoma with iridescent vision. Green colors surround candlelight. Greenish or rainbow colors around the light. Violent supra and infra- orbital neuralgia, violent pains and lachrymation. Food - Aversion to cocoa, coffee and tobacco, disgust at their odor.

Ears - Earache evenings, first right then left ear. Perforations with irritation of meatus. Itching in the ears, profuse nasal catarrh. Tingling and pain in right ear. Ringing in right ear. Deafness, ears pain when nose is blown, mouth open, sleep noisy.

Nose - Nose and larynx sensitive to air. Full feeling in nose. Coryza, fluent with a feeling of stoppage. Snuffling. Small lumps of phlegm from posterior sinuses.

Mouth - Aching in jaws, pain in muscles of mastication. Mouth sticky and pasty. Copious salivation. Taste of blood, metallic, cigars cannot be smoked, because they provoke cough and worse the rawness in larynx, taste blunted.

Throat - Acute laryngitis, cough andexpec- toration of tough, stringy mucus. Talking causes pain in the larynx. Hoarseness, sore sternum.

Stomach - Feels full of broken stones or lumps. Qualmishness and extreme discomfort with dull pain and heaviness in pit of stomach. Belchings smelling like radishes. Nausea in morning. Vomiting of watery mucus of the odor and taste of the acid. Chronic vomiting, with pressure in stomach.

Abdomen - Distention of stomach and abdomen in evening, with difficult passage of flatus. Rumblings. Pain in groins, on coughing the pain extended into testicles. Weakness in groins towards spermatic cords. Pressure on inguinal rings. Constriction in epigastrium before dinner.

Rectum - Constipated. Stool hard, then soft, mushy, frequent. Bilious stools with burning at anus. Burning in anus during and after stool. Tendency to hemorrhoids. Sensations - As of a band around head. As if he had swallowed broken stones. Cough as if caused by resonance of contiguous parts. As if insects crawling on back and shoulders. Legs and feet as if too full.

Male - Steady aching in glans penis. Violent pain on the point of penis and prepuce. Pain in testes and spermatic cord. Pain in testicles, preventing sleep. Erections every morning, earlier and harder.

Chest - Oppression, better deep inspiration. Tightness. Dryness in chest. Sticking near left lower rib. Pain beneath sternum on coughing, extending to sides of chest. Sternum is sore, painful to touch, independent of cough. Shooting up and down in sternum. Wandering pneumonia.

Heart - Anxious palpitations. Pulse rapid.

Back - Crawling on back and shoulders. Pressive pain in back and loins. Pain in sacral region. Peculiar pain extending from scapula to sacral region, worse motion and cough.

Limbs - Heaviness and weariness of limbs, worse knees. Twitching of fingers with spasmodic cough. Fold of skin remains attached to growing nail. Axillary sweat smells like garlic. Lungs - Sensitive air passages. Dread of breathing, sore pain when air enters lungs. Moist rales on breathing and in larynx. Convulsive cough, feels as though membrane were torn from larynx. Noisy, dry, hard, cough in violent short bursts, coming from low down, shaking the whole body. Spasmodic cough, sounds as if coughing in an empty tube with torn loose feeling and sticky sputum. Twitching of fingers with spasmodic cough.

Sleep - Sleepless. Restless sleep, with painful dreams. Sleepiness is overpowering. Sleep heavy, interrupted by nightmare. Dreams of fire, confused, but not frightful. Dreams of activity and of serious events. Dreams not remembered.

Skin - Irritated skin. Eczema. Itching pimples. Bromidrosis, sweat in axilla smelling of garlic, worse evening and night. Fold remains attached to growing nail.

Modalities - Open air helps the smarting in eyes. Worse coughing, talking, riding, touch. Worse in evening. Cough worse until midnight. Open air aggravates coryza, cough.

Tongue - Tongue coated, red stripe in middle, fissured, one spot denuded. Tongue edges rough and covered with pimples. Tongue sensitive to touch when eating and drinking. Bad taste to coffee. COMMENTS - The respiratory tract is irritated and pained from beginning to end. The nostrils and larynx are sensitive to cold air. Pain in larynx, trachea and in and under sternum on coughing. Talking causes pain in larynx. Cough convulsive in paroxysms, hollow sounding as if one coughed into an empty tube, caused by irritation in larynx or low down in chest. Violent headaches, affecting the base of the brain. Skin irritation, irritating eruptions, eczematous and herpetic. In the provings, the erections were severe almost to priapism and the ejaculations were longer-lasting and more copious than normal. A woman, 62 to whom Clarke once gave Osm. 2x for a spasmodic cough with pain in the head had a severe aggravation, the headache taking this form: “Sharp pain in center of forehead going through to back, better by hard pressure on forehead.” She discontinued Osm. and in two or three days that pain went away, leaving only an ordinary headache. The cough was not relieved. S. Norton suggested that Osm. may be a remedy in many cases of glaucoma. Cooper had a case of a girl of 14 with postnasal growths who improved rapidly under Osm., 3x, but was seized with exhaustion, then under Hydr-ac., got quite well. In one of Blackley's cases, a child born during the time that his father was under the influence of Osm. developed eczema, though none of the previously born children were eczematous. The kidneys were affected in another of Blackley's cases, incipient nephritis being set up. M. Boger cured a case in which there was pain in both directions, “Stitching pain upward in left spermatic cord. Creeping sensation downwards in left spermatic cord. Weakness in calves, they give out while walking.” Shootings in the sternum are up and down. In another case of a man, 44, syphilitic was cured of “dull, steady pain in hypo- gastrium, sore to pressure. Steady aching in glans penis.” RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Sulfuretted hydrogen, Phos-ac., Sil. - swollen gums. Hep. and Psor. - pain in larynx, Bell, and Merc. - laryngeal catarrh. Compare: ( 1 ) Arg-n., Sei., Mang. (2) Irid., Tell., Thal., Plat., Pall. (3) In eyes and lungs, Chlor., Brom. (4) Skin of nails, Fl-ac. (5) Itch, Sulph. (6) Coryza, cough with pain in larynx, All-c. but it has better in open air. (7) Eruptions, Ars., Rhus-t. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Kidneys - Bright's disease. Diminution or suppression of the urinary secretions. Urine is albuminous, strong- scented, smelling of violets. Urine is high-colored, full of bile, dark brown and scanty. Deposits bright-red sediment.

Temperature - Shivering, worse back. Fever, with difficult respiration, fever, with hot and dry skin. Sweat in axilla, smelling of garlic, worse evening and night.

State of stupor, indifference to others. Extreme weakness with somnolence in the afternoon and profound sleep. Weakness, worse in the morning when waking up. Great desire for sleep, with deep sleep at night. MIND - Apathy. State of indifference. Nonchalance. Idleness, no desire to work. Indecision, needs relaxing. Irritability, worse towards evening.

Eyes - Styes of upper eyelid of the left eye.

Male - Increase of sexual desire in men. Furuncle on the scrotum.

Limbs - Pain in the right shoulder. Temporary redness and swelling of the right shoulder. Redness and swelling of the right forearm and right wrist. Muscular pain of the right hip. Pain of the Achilles tendon. Pain aggravated by the first movement, ameliorated by continued movement.

Skin - Furuncles. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Calc., Calc-p. REFERENCES - Julian.

Modalities - Aggravation by the first movement, at night. Better by prolonged movement. Worse right side.

Kidneys - Highly colored urine and less abundant, worse at noon.

HOMEOPATHIC - Ost. is sometimes regarded as a variety of the common Hornbeam naturalized in America, though native to southern Europe. The chief difference between them is that Ost. vulg. has pendulous catkins, and Ost. virg., upright. The wood is exceedingly hard and heavy. The preparations of which the provings by Burt and others were made were from the wood. Marked action on the liver with the usual dull headache and pain in back and shoulders, cutting, sinking pains in abdomen. Nervous, languid, weak, uneasy. Very nervous with dull headache. Increased appetite, hunger wakes the patient at 4 a.m. Sinking at the epigastrium. Sickening pains. Black stools. Bilious conditions and intermittent fever. Anemia from malaria.

Head - Dull headache with numb, prickly feeling in head, face and hands, worse head. Dull, frontal headache with nausea. Right side headache, morning.

Ears - Drawing pain deep in left ear.

Face - Moist freckles in face, head and hands. Food - Appetite greatly increased, woke with hunger at 4 a.m. Loss of appetite.

Mouth - Tongue yellow, coated at the root. Taste is coppery, slimy, sweet, slimy, bitter, rough. Boring and sharp pain in right lower molars.

Stomach - Sour stomach. Nausea and distress after riding in cold air. Burning distress in epigastrium. Hard sickening pains in epigastric and umbilical region, awaking him at night. Sinking in epigastrium. Frequent nausea with dull, frontal headache. Sickening pains.

Abdomen - Dull pains in right lobe of liver with sour belchings. Retraction of umbilicus. Rumbling, flatus, pain waking him in night.

Rectum - Rectum feels sore, protruded feeling after stool.

Stool - Loose stools, bilious with tenesmus and straining, loose without tenesmus. Tenesmus followed by diarrhea stool. Mushy stool with burning at anus and tenesmus. Black stools, dry lumps. COMMENTS - Allen mentioned "Tongue coated yellow at root. Loss of appetite for breakfast and dinner. Frequent nausea with the dull frontal headache.” RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Macro., Bry., Nux-v. (lumbago). Compare: (1) Waking in night hungry, Ign., Lyc. (2) Black stools, Lept. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Back - Back so painful, can hardly turn in bed, cannot sit up (better from Macro., Bry., Nux-v). Dull pain in whole dorsal region, extending to left hypochondrium. Constant lumbar and sacral pain, worse stooping or walking.

Limbs - Aching, dull pains in arms and legs. Fine drawing rheumatic pains in left fingers, morning. Drawing pains in right ankle.

Modalities - Worse moving, walking, stooping. Worse 6 a.m., 4 a.m., 3 p.m.

HOMEOPATHIC - Ov. has been used with much success in cases of suffering following excision of the ovaries (Sep.) and for the menopausal sufferings of women. Clarke had good results with it in such cases in the lower triturations. Ov. has been suggested as a remedy in ovarian cysts. Menopausal disturbances in general. Cutaneous disorders and acne rosacea. Prurigo.

Female - Menses are frequent, too early. Menses are clotted, coagulated, copious. Menses of short duration. Infertility. Hot flashes. Menopause. Infantile genitalis. COMMENTS - Characteristic amelioration from the menses, all symptoms better during menses (Lach., Zinc.). Generally associated with ovarian conditions, often after removal of ovaries (Staph., Phos.). Ovarian cysts (Thuj., Sil.), when nothing else works. Useful for menopausal symptoms, particularly hot flashes (Sep., Puls., Thuj.). Severe hormonal acne (Sep., Puls., Thuj.). Spacey. Indecision, difficulty deciding who they are, about changing careers, about health. E. Saalfeld, in view of Landau's observations on the effect of Ov. on the nervous sufferings of women at menopause, gave Ov. to women suffering from acne rosacea and other skin disorders of menopause. A woman, 20, after a double oophorectomy, had lichen-like eczema. This was relieved by Ov. as well as the accompanying nervous symptoms and adiposity. Saalfeld also obtained good results in some non-menopausal cases, including acne and seborrhea in chlorotic women. He had a case of prurigo that had lasted from childhood in a woman of 26. In this case, the itching was better for a short time after the period. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Orchitinum, Testicular extract - after ovariotomy, sexual weakness, senile decay. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

name: Ovi Gallinae Pellicula
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Dyspnea better bending backward, jarring or beating breast. Worse by movement, reaching, lifting arms, descending stairs, over-exerting. Worse pressure and touch, pressure of clothing, at full moon. Worse before, during and after menses, though some symptoms were better when flow appeared. COMMENTS - This preparation was made by Swan. He noted that it has an ancient reputation for “immoderate flux of the menses” (Calc.) and for nocturnal bedwetting. The first prover was a young woman, a patient of J. C. Boardman, who was known to be unable to bear any extra exertion, but the details of this were not known until after she had taken the first dose of the Ovi-g-p. 100,000c sent by Swan. Some years before, she had felt something “give way” in the groin while shoveling snow, bringing on a left ovarian pain, extending down the left limb. The trouble was suddenly removed after the dose. The sensitiveness to exertion never returned, though the dose created much disturbance of the generative functions before it had finished its action. The symptoms of a second prover, a married woman who took the Ovi-g-p. 30c, confirmed the symptoms experienced by the first. This prover had also hemorrhage from the rectum, incontinence of urine while sneezing or coughing, and post-nasal catarrh. Yingling contributed the case of H. E., 42, blonde, who had a dull, hard, heavy aching in region of heart, generally about apex, extending at times to left ovarian region. Occasionally a cutting which extended to base of heart and prevented breathing, after the cutting a sensation as if something went “thud,” after which pain seemed to recommence at apex. At times, heavy aching in base of heart, which made breathing very difficult. Only bending backward alleviated respiration. Ovi-g-p. (a preparation of Fincke's) was given, one dose, dry on the tongue. In a very few minutes the pain was all gone. “Feels splendidly since taking the remedy.” Without knowing what it was, said she had “a taste of fresh eggs in the mouth since taking the powder.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Calc., Naja. (2) Ova tosta - Tosta preparata, Roastedegg-shells. Calc-o-t. - has leucorrhea and backache. A feeling as if the spine were broken and wired or tied together with a string. Pain of cancer. Warts. (3) Egg vaccine for asthma. Much interest is shown in Dr. Fritz Talbot's method to cure one form of asthma in children by the use of egg vaccine. Asthma due to susceptibility of the protein substance in eggs can be cured by immunizing against egg poisons by repeated doses of egg white. After the skin has been cleansed with soap and alcohol the egg-white is rubbed into a slight scratch. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke..

name: Oxalicum Acidum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better after stools. Change of position helps pain in back. Worse thinking of symptoms. Worse from light, mental exertion, motion, left side, slightest touch, shaving, cold. Worse from strawberries, sour fruits, grapes. Worse evening, night and early morning. Worse from being aroused about 3 a.m. with gastric and abdominal pain. Lying down causes swimming sensation..

full:
PHARMACY - ox-ac. Oxalicum acidum. Oxalic acid. Sorrel acid. Hydrogen oxalate. Trituration. Tincture. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Angina, pectoris. Aphonia. Backaches. Bedwetting. Chest, disorders. Cholera, infantum. Convulsion. Deltoid, rheumatism. Dyspnea. Eyes, disorders. Gastrodynia. Gout. Gravel. Hernias. Hives. Indigestion. Kidney, stones. Meningitis. Myelitis. Nails, blue. Neuralgias. Neurasthenia. Nose, disorders. Numbness. Oxaluria. Pains, severe. Paralysis. Pregnancy, sickness. Side, pain. Spasms. Spernuitic cord, pain. Stomach, disorders. Tetanus. Testes, pains. Tongue, disorders. Tuberculosis. Urine, abnormal. Voice, altered.

HOMEOPATHIC - Although certain oxalates are constant constituents of vegetable food and of the human body, the acid itself is a violent poison when taken internally, producing gastro-enteritis, motor paralysis, collapse, stupor and death. If Op. is the painless remedy, Ox-ac. may be considered its antithesis. It causes the most excruciating pains beyond description, which are all worse when the patient thinks of them. Thinking of pains and conditions will bring them on when they are not actually present. Symptoms are worse by touch (small spots on head), slightest touch causes excruciating pain. Worse motion andthink- ing of pains. Neuralgias. Excruciating pains like lightning in streaks, burning in spots. Violent pains in spots (Kali-bi.). Rheumatism of left side. Periodical disorders. Periodical remissions. Neurasthenia. Weak, cold, livid and numb all over, worse lower limbs. Influences the spinal cord and produces motor Oxalicum acidum paralysis. Paralysis of the left side from spinal meningitis. Spasmodic symptoms of throat and chest. Angina pectoris, sharp, sharp pain in left lung coming on suddenly, depriving of breath. Tuberculosis. Severe back and kidney pains. Kidney stones. After eating pains at navel, colic, rumbling in abdomen, urging to stool, weakness. Pain in stomach, better from eating. Gnawing in stomach better from soup. Cannot eat strawberries, severe allergies. Sugar, coffee and wine disagree. Worse from shaving. MIND - Exhilarated, quicker thought and action. Nervous and sleepless. Symptoms worse by thinking of them, thinking of the conditions will bring them on when they are not actually present.

Head - Headache, before and during stool. Band like sensation about the head, as of a screw behind each ear, better after stool. Sense of heat. Numb pricking in occiput. Sore tender spot on scalp.

Eyes - Severe pain in eyes, feel expanded. Hyperesthesia of retina. Small, and especially linear objects, appear larger and more distant than they are. Sight vanishes with the nosebleed.

Face - Pale, cold, livid. Feeling of heat. Food - Cannot eat strawberries, severe allergies. Sugar, coffee and wine disagree.

Mouth - Sour taste. Belchings, with difficult swallowing.

Throat - Hoarseness with cardiac derangements. Voice altered. Low voice. Nervous aphonia (Coca, Hydr- ac.). Aphonia from paralysis of vocal cords. Vertigo - Confusion and vertigo. Vertigo, swimming sensation on lying down, while looking out of window. COMMENTS - Ox-ac., the chief constituent of Sorrel (Rumx-a.) and Wood Sorrel (Oxal.), exists in plants that are ordinarily deemed anti-scorbutic and are remarkable for the grateful acidity of their herbage. Ox-ac. is said to enter largely into the inspissated juice of the Clover (Trif-p.) which formed Thomson's “Cancer plaster,” and which is strongly escharotic. Inspissated solutions of sorrel have been used successfully as local applications for epithelioma and with a solution of Ox-ac. and of Tannic acid, applied locally. With a solution of 5 grains to 3 ounces of water. Cooper removed troublesome small nevi in infants upon the face and elsewhere, using it for weeks or even months. Cooper removed a large patch of erythematous lupus on the cheek. From this it would appear, taking into account that Ox-ac. produces wart-like growths, it may have a beneficial influence, locally and probably internally as well, upon epithelial proliferations of the cuticle. In an interesting study of Ox-ac., J. W. Ellis cited a fatal case of poisoning recorded by Boericke through exposure of the hands to a saturated solution used for chemical purposes. The symptoms were intense pains in head, hyperesthesia, especially to light. Spasms of pain down limbs, along throat muscles and through spermatic cord. Sensitive spots on spine. Excruciating pain in lower back and loss of power in the lower limbs shows an unmistakable action on the spinal cord and its meninges. These symptoms are better seen in less severe cases of poisoning. In animals poisoned with Ox-ac. the first symptom is stiffness of hind limbs. . Farrington summed up the indications of Ox-ac. in spinal affections, including weak loins, hips, legs, numb back, numb limbs. Limbs blue and cold, weak and numb, worse going up stairs. Limbs stiff, paroxysm of dyspnea (as in spinal meningitis). Pains in small spots, especially linear spots. Pains worse when thinking of them. Erections with dullness in occiput. Left-side rheumatism. Sharp shooting pain in left lung and heart, extending down to epigastrium. In afternoon, stitches several times in left lung. Sharp, sharp pain in lower lobe of left lung, coming on so suddenly that it deprives him of breath for a few seconds. Sore sticking in chest extending back to between scapula. Pleurisy, pneumonia, tuberculosis. The heart may be paralyzed, becomes flaccid or distended with blood. Angina pectoris. Coldness of surface, numbness. Mottled skin, blue nails. Generally left sided. Sugar aggravates the stomach pain. Wine causes headache. Oxaluria, with backache, numbness. Frequent ineffectual urging to stool, preceded by a sick, distressing feeling from navel downwards, worse when thinking of it, worse from drinking coffee. Faintness and vomiting during stool. Pain in back better after stool. John Moore reportd the case of a sea captain who suffered from indigestion. Two years before Moore saw him he had to undergo an operation for strangulated hernia. Ever since he had been subject to pain in region of navel coming on two hours after eating, accompanied by much flatulence and bitter and sour belchings. Pain worse in night, arousing the patient 3 a.m. and keeping him awake. Burning sensation from throat downwards to the region of the pain. The patient had always has a weak digestion and had met with many severe accidents at sea. He was given Ox-ac. 3c, two drops, an hour after meals. He was a little better the first night and after that slept the night through and said he had not had so much comfort for years. Bedwetting has been cured with Ox-ac. 6c in a blonde boy of six. The guiding symptom was “Sharp shooting pain in left chest, close to sternum and parallel to it.” C. Walker told Clarke of a case of his in which the patient, an elderly, gouty man, was suddenly seized with congestion of spinal meninges with great coldness, blueness and numbness with complete prostration of strength. Ox-ac. 6c rapidly cured. A patient of Clarke who used Ox-ac. in his work suffered from “Rheumatism of left side. Starting on falling asleep. When actually at work, acidity.” W. M. Butler gave great relief with Ox- ac. 3c. in a case of paraplegia, affecting first the right then the left leg of a year's duration in an American woman, mother of four children. In a few weeks the motor symptoms were better then the sensory. Sensation to heat and cold was restored, general tactile sensibility was improved. Some control was gained over bladder and rectum. Hale cured a case of palpitation with action of heart irregular in force and rhythm, alternating with aphonia with Ox-ac. 6c. It was a favorite remedy with S. A. Jones in cardiac trouble, occurring in highly “nervous” patients. Ellis suggested that Ox-ac. corresponds to many cases of neurasthenia. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Carbonates of lime and magnesia. Lime water, antidote to poisoning of Ox- ac.Compare;(l)Ars.. Colch., Arg-n., Pic-ac. (2) Cice.. Chickpea - Lithiasis, jaundice, liver affections, diuretic. (3) Scol. - terrible pains in back and loins, extending down limbs, return periodically, commencing in head to toes. Angina pectoris. Inflammation, pain and gangrene. Pustules and abscesses. (4) Caes. - Pain in lumbar region and testicle. Headache, darting through temples. Diarrhea and colic. Languor. (5) Kali-ox. (6) In cholera infantum, Ars., Ip., Verat. (7) In gastralgia, Colch. (8) In spinal disease, Pic-ac., Arg-m., Ph-ac. (9) Induration of testicles. Puls. (10) Headache worse from wine, Zinc. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Emptiness with gnawing, compelling one to eat. Burning pain goes upwards, worse slightest touch, sugar. Cannot eat strawberries. Violent pain in epigastrium, discharge of flatus relieves. Gastralgia, heartburn, sensation of coldness below epigastrium. Bitter and sour eructation, worse at night.

Abdomen - Stitching pains in the liver, better deep breathing. Burning in small spots in abdomen. Pain in upper part of abdomen after eating, with much flatulence. Chronic inflammation of bowels. Colic about the navel or involuntary muddy brown stools better lying. Flatus passes with difficulty. Fainting and vomiting during stool.

Rectum - Diarrhea from coffee. Sensations - Sensation as if all blood had left the brain. As if blood in head was coursing upward and outward. As from a screw behind each ear. Hypogastrium as if bound. Back as if broken or bruised. Wrist as if sprained. Hands as if dead. Jerking pains like short stitches, confined to small spots, lasting only a few seconds. Sensation as from chafing during shaving.

Male - Seminal vesiculitis. Neuralgic pains in spermatic cord, worse from slightest motion. Testes, throb or feel crushed. Testicles feel contused and heavy.

Chest - Chest fixed. Sharp pain through lower region of left lung, extending down to epigastrium. Left lung painful.

Heart - Precordial pains which dart to the left shoulder. Angina pectoris, sharp, sharp pain in left lung coming on suddenly, depriving of breath. Palpitations and dyspnea in organic heart disease.worse when thinking of it. Palpitations worse lying down. Pulse feeble. Beats of heart intermit when thinking of it. Aortic insufficiency. Fluttering in heart. Heart symptoms alternate with aphonia.

Back - Numb pricking in back. Backaches, feels numb. Back feels too weak to hold the body. Cold creeps up spine.

Limbs - Multiple sclerosis. Myelitis. Muscular prostration. Numb, tingling. Numbness extends from shoulders to fingertips. Lower limbs blue, cold insensible. Weak trembling, hands and feet. Hands cold as if dead. Drawing and sharp pains shooting down limbs. Pains start from spine and extend through limbs. Sharp pains in various parts, jerking pains. Wrist painful, as if sprained (Ulm.). Pain in fleshy part of thumb (right).

Skin - Sensitive, soreness, smarting, worse shaving. Mottled, marbled in circular patches. Perspires easily.

Modalities - Better after stools. Change of position helps pain in back. Worse thinking of symptoms. Worse from light, mental exertion, motion, left side, slightest touch, shaving, cold. Worse from strawberries, sour fruits, grapes. Worse evening, night and early morning. Worse from being aroused about 3 a.m. with gastric and abdominal pain. Lying down causes swimming sensation.

Liver - Stitches in liver. Lungs - Spasmodic breathing with constriction of larynx and chest. Dyspnea, short, jerking inspirations. Burning sensation from throat down. Left lung painful. Hoarseness. Paralysis of the tensors of vocal cord. Aphonia.

Kidneys - Severe kidney pains. Kidney stones. Must urinate when thinking of it. Frequent and copious urination. Oxaluria. Burning in urethra and pain in glans when urinating.

full:

HERBAL - Diuretic, refrigerant. Reputed of value in febrile diseases, urinary affections, catarrh, and hemorrhages. The herb may be infused with water or boiled in milk and administered freely, although excess should be guarded against. Joseph Miller said, “The juice, when clarified is a fine red color and makes a very agreeable syrup.” RELATIONS - Compare: Ox-ac. Rumx-a. REFERENCES - Potter.

name: Oxydendron Arboreum
author: Murphy
constitution: Ascites. Bladder stones. Dropsy. Prostatic enlargement.
keynote:
PHARMACY - oxyd. Oxydendron arboreum. Sorrel-tree. Sour-wood. Elk-tree. Andromeda arbórea. N. O. Ericacee, tribe Andromedee. Rich woods of the Alleghenies. Tincture of leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Ascites. Bladder stones. Dropsy. Prostatic…
full:
PHARMACY - oxyd. Oxydendron arboreum. Sorrel-tree. Sour-wood. Elk-tree. Andromeda arbórea. N. O. Ericacee, tribe Andromedee. Rich woods of the Alleghenies. Tincture of leaves. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Ascites. Bladder stones. Dropsy. Prostatic enlargement.

HOMEOPATHIC - Oxyd. is the only species of its genus. It is an unproved remedy for dropsy, ascites and anasarca. Deranged portal circulation. Prostatic enlargement. Suppressed urine. Bladder stones. Irritation of neck of bladder. COMMENTS - M. E. Douglass treated Mrs. H. for general dropsy, ascites and anasarca, which dated from an attack of measles treated with ice-drinks and ice-applications seven months before. When Douglass saw her, the urine was nearly suppressed, but contained very little albumen. Great difficulty of breathing even when sitting, lying down impossible. Had to sit in one chair with feet in another. Menses suppressed. After the failure of Apoc. and several carefully chosen medicines, the legs having burst in several places, Douglass was about to tap the abdomen, but before doing so put Oxyd. 3x in a tumbler of water and gave three teaspoonfuls every three hours. In forty eight hours the breathing was better and urine increased. Oxyd. was continued (with the exception of three days during which Rhus-t. was given to combat erysipelas which had set in on left leg). On the tenth day, the patient lay down on the bed and slept for three hours. Appetite increased, and in two months she was quite free from dropsy and felt perfectly well though much emaciated. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ceref. - dropsy, Bright's disease, cystitis. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

name: Oxygenium
author: Murphy
constitution: Anemia. Cancer. Canker, sores. Coryza. Cough. Diabetes. Influenza. Morphine, poisoning. Mouth, sores. Strychnine, poisoning. Whooping cough.
keynote:
PHARMACY - oxyg. Oxygenium. Oxygen. Ozonum. Nascent Oxygen. Oxygen including ozone, which is nascent oxygen. Oxygen (At. Wt. 16). Dilutions of distilled water charged with the gas. Dilutions. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anemia. Cancer. Canker, sores.…
full:
PHARMACY - oxyg. Oxygenium. Oxygen. Ozonum. Nascent Oxygen. Oxygen including ozone, which is nascent oxygen. Oxygen (At. Wt. 16). Dilutions of distilled water charged with the gas. Dilutions. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anemia. Cancer. Canker, sores. Coryza. Cough. Diabetes. Influenza. Morphine, poisoning. Mouth, sores. Strychnine, poisoning. Whooping cough.

HOMEOPATHIC - Oxyg. is said to liberate oxygen in nascent state in the tissues when it is taken internally, diluted with five or six parts of water. Undiluted, its taste is disagreeably metallic, though it can be used as a gargle without inconvenience. Diluted, it has no taste at all. When taken as directed in doses of a tablespoonful with six of water it sometimes causes relaxation of the bowels followed by constipation. Clarke said it set up all the symptoms of a common cold. Clarke found it of great value as an anti-septic lotion and application, and as a gargle in cases of sore throat. It has been known to stop the irritation of a raw throat, when ushering in a cold, from going further either up or down. In cases of gonorrhea. Oxyg. renders the urine anti-septic, supplying an anti-septic lotion from within without interfering with the action of a specific homeopathic remedy. Clarke gave it in a number of cases of cancer, and obtained favorable temporary results in some. Inhalations of oxygen have palliated some late cases of cancer, producing profuse discharges from the ulcerating mass of tumor with reduction of its growth, but no cure followed and death supervened.

Head - Dull frontal headache, worse in spot over left eye. Headache in outer half of right eyebrow, pain still in frontal region. Pain in left temple, which feels cold to touch. Continued sweat on scalp.

Eyes - Lancinating, paroxysmal pain in right eyeball, a little to left of pupil. Occasional rush of pain, filling whole right eyeball and extending into right temple, which then became hot. Tingling of conjunctive and skin of face.

Nose - Much indurated mucus in nose, necessitating frequent picking in morning, blowing out of lumps, generally tough, opaque, whitish yellow. Sneezes with the cough.

Face - Tingling of skin of face. Rawness in throat.

Mouth - Canker sores in mouth and cheeks.

Throat - Rawness in throat. Irritation of fauces and glottis. Slight hoarseness, dryness of throat towards evening dryness increased around rim of glottis, at midnight woke with choking, burning dryness of glottis and upper larynx, no thirst. Aphonia with difficulty of controlling voice. COMMENTS - Oxyg. is not chemically distinguishable from hydrogen peroxide, but it has none of the disagreeable features of that substance; it does not bleach articles it may touch or cause effervescence. A cure of diabetes with large doses of Oxyg. is on record and many cases of whooping cough have been cured with inhalations of ozone. Dilute Oxydol is a useful preparation as a mouth wash in canker sores. D. T. Playfair cured a desperate cases of morphine poisoning (30 grains Morph, had been taken) in a young woman of 37 with inhalation of oxygen kept up for ten hours. All the usual antidotes had been given before without avail. The patient was entirely well in twenty-four hours. In one case, an elderly working class woman had a large fungating cancer of the left breast. Oxyg. was given internally and applied externally. It caused excessive discharge with corresponding reduction of the tumor. After several, weeks the patient's legs suddenly swelled, rapidly increasing, and she sank, the tumor had at least three-quarters disappeared. The effect of the Oxyg. was probably to liberate the disease elements too rapidly for the organism to eliminate them, as Dr. Cooper suggested in his account of Orni. Oxyg. 1,000c cured a case of cough from dryness in upper larynx and constant tickling in throat-pit. Hard, shaking cough causing soreness in epigastric region. Expectoration with every cough, thick, lumpy, tasteless. Oxyg. 100,000c cured a cough excited by tickling in throat and causing soreness of chest, 2 to 3 a.m., better lying on back. In another case, Oxyg. 100,000c cured a case in which the patient was passing quantities of uric acid like ruby sand. RELATIONS - Antidote to: Morphine and strychnine poisoning. Antidotes, Camph. Compare: Ozone. Chr- ac., Kali-bi., Kali-chl., Kali-perm., Osm., and oxidizing agents generally, Chlor., Electr. REFERENCES - Clarke. Grimmer. Mur- Phy.

Abdomen - Great flatulence, passing large quantities at stool.

Rectum - Flatus seems to accumulate in rectum, causes desire for stool and fears to pass flatus lest stool should also pass.

Male - Fine stinging rash on right side of scrotum, lasting one day.

Chest - Bursting sensation in chest. Suffocating feeling in chest, tendency to breathe slowly. Tightness under sternum, worse bringing shoulders forward.

Back - Excessive pains in whole sacral region, apparently in articulations, especially a sensation of tiredness all through pelvic viscera, even in perineum. Causations - Morphine. Strychnine.

Limbs - Thighs and legs as if overworked, excessively fatigued. Eruption of pimples in the fold of right side of buttocks, near anus, becoming very sore and seemingly like blisters, as skin rubbed off it was left very sore. Itching of skin of metacarpal end of first phalanx of left index finger, no redness of eruption. Lungs - Irritation of respiratory tract as when recovering from attack of influenza. Violent irritating cough and sneezing, followed by rawness in throat and air passages. Hoarseness and hard, shaking, tearing cough from tickling under sternum in night, worse lying either side, better lying on back with profuse, lumpy, tasteless whitish sputa. The sputa occasionally yellow, purulent. Dry, hacking cough, 2 to 5 a.m. Cough causes hawking, blowing nose, and a bursting sensation in chest.

Skin - Tingling of skin of face and conjunctive.

Perspiration - Sweat all over and headache between eyes. Sweat on scalp and slight moisture over body.

name: Oxytropis Lamberti
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better after sleep, on side lain on. Pains better when moving about, better in cool air. Worse thinking of symptoms, every other day. Worse immediately after eating, better an hour after..
constitution: Amblyopia. Apathy. Belch- ings. Bladder, irritability. Coughs. Delirium. Depression. Fevers. Impotence. Locomotor ataxia. Mania. Ovary, pain. Paralysis. Rheumatism. Spermatic cord. Sphincters, relaxation. Staggering, gait. Testicles, pain. Vertigo.
keynote:
PHARMACY - oxyt. Oxytropis lamberti. Locoweed. Oxytropis campestris. Rattle-weed. Astragalus campestris. N. O. Leguminose. Papilionoideae. Tincture of fresh plant without the root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amblyopia. Apathy. Belch- ings. Bladder,…
full:
PHARMACY - oxyt. Oxytropis lamberti. Locoweed. Oxytropis campestris. Rattle-weed. Astragalus campestris. N. O. Leguminose. Papilionoideae. Tincture of fresh plant without the root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amblyopia. Apathy. Belch- ings. Bladder, irritability. Coughs. Delirium. Depression. Fevers. Impotence. Locomotor ataxia. Mania. Ovary, pain. Paralysis. Rheumatism. Spermatic cord. Sphincters, relaxation. Staggering, gait. Testicles, pain. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - The “Crazy-weed” or “Loco-weed” is of Spanish origin and has been variously identified by Gray as Astragalus legum, by others as Astragalus mollisimus, and by W. S. Gee, who made the proving, as Oxytropis Lamberti. In Gee's proving, the tincture and potencies from lx to 30x were used. A number of mind and brain symptoms were produced including despondency, forgetfulness, a feeling as if consciousness would be lost, fullness in the head and instability standing. There were pains both in testes and ovaries, and one male prover, naturally passionate, became impotent. W. D. Gentry in June. 1895, sent Boericke & Tafel specimens of Oxyt. and as this firm is extremely careful about the botany of the plants they make their tinctures from, Gentry made these remarks concerning the plants he sent: “My attention was first called to this plant last winter during January. Soon after my arrival on the territory, as it was almost the only green thing showing itself above the snow. Which covered the ground at that time for two or three days. “Some cattle had been eating the weed and as I approached them they tried to move away, but in spite of their efforts they backed towards me and in their efforts to escape made some ludicrous maneuvers. I observed them closely for more than an hour and was reminded most forcibly by their actions of the symptoms of locomotor ataxia.” Gentry's observation of loco-disease in winter bears out what is said by other writers, namely, that it is only in winter, when food is scanty, that animals can be induced to commence eating the weed and then they cannot leave off. Gentry made provings of the tincture of the whole plant and seeds on three persons. Two provers had “symptoms worse when thinking of them.” They had “pleasant intoxicated feelings.” Both Gentry’s and Gee’s provers had well- marked pains in the eyes and disturbance of vision and Gentry's had “numb, pithy or woody feeling about and on the spine,” and “loss of power to control movements of limbs.” Marked action on the nervous system producing uncertain, staggering or backward gait. Staggering gait. Reflexes lost. Trembling, sensation of emptiness. Vertigo. Congestion of spine and paralysis. Pains come and go quickly. Sphincters relaxed. Urging to urinate when thinking of it. Great mental depression. MIND -All symptoms worse when thinking of them (Ox-ac.).Stimulation of mind, pleasant, intoxicated feeling (Gent.). Mono-maniac tendency. Cannot think or concentrate his thoughts. Very forgetful of familiar words and names. Indifference to all interests. Depression. Feeling as if he would lose consciousness. Disinclination to talk or study. Desires to be alone.

Head - Full, warm feeling about head. Feeling of intoxication with loss of vision. Pain in maxillary bones and masseter muscles. Pressure on head, better after sleep.

Eyes - Sight obscured, pupils contracted, do not respond to light. Paralysis of nerves and muscles of eyes.

Ears - Roaring sound in ears.

Nose - Frequent, violent sneezing with fluent coryza. Fluent coryza, somewhat bloody. Nose very dry, scabs form in it. Nose feels as if sunburned, red and shining, especially on ale. Feeling of pressure over bridge of nose.

Mouth - Mouth very dry, especially in morning. Metallic taste in mouth. Gumboil on left lower jaw, profuse saliva. Pain in left lower jaw.

Throat - Throat dry and sore. Slight inflammation of pharynx, a “husky” feeling. Slight accumulation of mucus in larynx, hard to cough it up. COMMENTS - The botanical articles in the Century Dictionary noted that Loco-weed is “any one of the several Leguminous plants producing the loco-disease in animals. Among them are Astragalus mollisimus and A. Hornii with several other species of the genus and Oxytropis Lamberti.” Henry's Botany reported that the foliage of “Oxytropis Lamberti is said to be injurious to cattle,” so Dr. Gee was quite justified in taking this plant for the proving. The Astragali are very closely related to the Oxyt. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Astrag., Lath., Ox-ac.,Bar-c. Loco plantisrich inBaryta. Lol. (2) Lath., Astra-me., Phys, and other Legumi- nose. (3) In symptoms worse when thinking of them, Ox-ac. (better, Camph.). (4) Pain in cord and tests, Ox-ac. (5) Pains right to left, Lyc. (6) better moving about, Rhus-t. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Gen- try.

Stomach - Belchings with colicky pains. Belchings, as after taking soda-water with colicky pains. Stomach cold during the chill.

Abdomen - Full feeling in abdomen, causing short breathing after lying down in bed. Sharp, sharp pains all through abdomen. Sharp pain, running from right to left across bowels. Slight griping pain in region of umbilicus. Tenderness in epigastric region.

Rectum - Sphincter seems relaxed. Looseness of bowels. Stools slip from anus like lumps of jelly, mushy.

Male - No desire or ability. Pain in testicles and along spermatic cord and down thighs.

Female - Pain in left ovary like something grasping or holding tightly. Food - Loss of appetite. Appetite gradually increasing. Symptoms worse after eating, better after an hour.

Chest - A warm tingling sensation over left chest, just under skin. Oppression in lungs at 9 p.m.

Back - Pain and stiffness of muscles of back of neck. Numb, pithy or woody feeling about and in the spine (Gent.).

Limbs - Pain along ulnar nerve. Pains come and go quickly, but muscles remain sore and stiff. Numb feeling about spine. Staggering gait. Patellar tendon reflex lost. Loss of coordination. Lungs - Short and quick breathing from the full feeling in abdomen. Hard breathing, as though lungs and bronchials were closing. Short cough with tightness across chest. A dry cough, from any little exercise.

Sleep - Twitching of muscles on falling asleep. Wakes often. Restless, dreams of quarrel. Dreamed of spiders, bugs, of swimming in water. Dreams of a pleasant or lascivious nature. On rising feels sad, weary, despondent.

Modalities - Better after sleep, on side lain on. Pains better when moving about, better in cool air. Worse thinking of symptoms, every other day. Worse immediately after eating, better an hour after.

Kidneys - Pain in kidneys, worse in right, with some tenderness (Berb.). Awoke with a heavy pain in kidneys. Urging to urinate when thinking of it. Profuse flow of urine.

Temperature - Chill lasted until 2 p-m., then disappeared. As chill passes off a smarting in throat and a feeling as though lungs and bronchials would close up, making breathing very difficult. No thirst in either stage.

name: Ozonum
author: Murphy
constitution: Aphonia. Backaches. Belching. Cancer. Heartburn. Hoarseness. Keloids. Nausea. Night-sweats. Photophobia. Sinusitis. Vertigo. Vitiligo. Vomiting.
keynote:
PHARMACY - ozone. Ozonum. Ozone. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Aphonia. Backaches. Belching. Cancer. Heartburn. Hoarseness. Keloids. Nausea. Night-sweats. Photophobia. Sinusitis. Vertigo. Vitiligo. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - The name ozone derives from…
full:
PHARMACY - ozone. Ozonum. Ozone. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Aphonia. Backaches. Belching. Cancer. Heartburn. Hoarseness. Keloids. Nausea. Night-sweats. Photophobia. Sinusitis. Vertigo. Vitiligo. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - The name ozone derives from the Greek, which means “to smell,” “to spread an odor.”

Eyes - Tired eyes. Burning and twitching. Photophobia.

Nose - Sinusitis. Thick nasal discharges. Sensitive to smell.

Throat - Dry throat in heated rooms, better fresh air with open window. Feeling as if a lump of mucus in throat, worse swallowing. Tries to get the lump out by coughing and clearing my throat, but this doesn't help. Shrill voice. Hoarseness. Husky voice when singing. Aphonia. Vertigo - Vertigo, tottering, staggering on rising from crouching, with nausea. Sensation of falling, worse bending down, better lying down. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Oxyg., Carb-v. REFERENCES - Murphy. Schadde.

Stomach - Heartburn. Sour belching. Nausea and vomiting.

Back - Backache in lumbar region. Lancinating and cutting pains.

Sleep - Falling asleep difficult despite tiredness, with tension. Sleep unrefreshing, troubled, wakes up often, tosses and turns. Frequent yawning and tired eyes, better after nap.

Skin - Dry skin. Darker coloration of different parts of skin. Vitiligo. Itching. Scars that itch. Keloids.

Perspiration - Night-sweats.

name: Paeonia Officinalis
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Drinking water helps vertigo with nausea. Worse from touch orpressure, motion. Worse coming into warm room, night, during stool..
constitution: Abscess. Anal, disorders. Bedsores. Breast, ulcerations. Ciliary, neuralgia. Coccyx, ulcer. Colic. Fissure. Fistula. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Nausea. Nightmares. Perineum, ulcer. Sternum, pain. Ulcers. Varicose, veins. Vertigo. Vomiting.
keynote:
PHARMACY - paeon. Paeonia officinalis. Peony. N. O. Ranunculaceae. Tincture of the fresh root dug in spring; in autumn the root is said to be inert. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscess. Anal, disorders. Bedsores. Breast, ulcerations. Ciliary,…
full:
PHARMACY - paeon. Paeonia officinalis. Peony. N. O. Ranunculaceae. Tincture of the fresh root dug in spring; in autumn the root is said to be inert. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscess. Anal, disorders. Bedsores. Breast, ulcerations. Ciliary, neuralgia. Coccyx, ulcer. Colic. Fissure. Fistula. Headaches. Hemorrhoids. Nausea. Nightmares. Perineum, ulcer. Sternum, pain. Ulcers. Varicose, veins. Vertigo. Vomiting.

HERBAL - Paeon, belongs to the great order of Ranunculaceae, which includes the aconites, acteas and hellebores.

HOMEOPATHIC - Chronic ulcers on lower parts of body, leg, foot toes, also breast, rectum. Skin is very sensitive, ulcerations from pressure of tight boots, bed sores etc. Shooting or splinter like pains. Rolls on floor from pain. Congestion. Rush of blood to head. face. chest, burning heat and redness of eyes and face, burning, itching and swelling of anus, heat in throat in skin. Varicose veins. Anal varicose veins. Anal disorders such as fissure, fistula, abscess and hemorrhoids. Biting, itching, swelling, burning. Intolerable during and after stool. Oozing of moisture. Both Dioscorides and Pliny cured nightmares with Paeon., the former with the seeds, the latter with the root. The dreams experienced by the provers were of a terrifying nature. MIND - Ill-humor. Depression with irritability. Much affected by bad news. Excitement. Nervous. Apprehension in evening with anxiety. Anxious, afraid to talk with any one. Delirium.

Head - Rush of blood to head and face. Pain and confusion of head. Dullness, heaviness, vertigo and feeling of heat in head. Gnawing headache. Boring outward in right temple. Pain in occiput and in nape. Heaviness in occiput.

Eyes - Eyes red and watery. Dry and smarting, not easy to open. Burning, itching and dryness of eyes and lids. Conjunctivitis with lachrymation and contracted pupils. Inflammation of left ball with pain as if a grain of sand were under upper lid. Sticking in right upper lid towards inner canthus.

Ears - Jerking in cartilages. Sticking outward in right ear. Pinching behind right ear. One ear cold, the other hot. Itching in concha. Ringing, roaring in ears.

Nose - Stoppage of nose, in evening in morning in bed with dryness. Crawling in tip of nose.

Face - Face red and puffy. Burning heat in face. Crawling in upper lip.

Mouth - Tongue red.

Throat - Biting posteriorly in palate in evening. Swallowing difficult. Scraping in throat. Sensation as if an acrid, burning vapor ascended throat. Heat extending to pharynx in throat and esophagus, worse hawking. Hawking caused by tenacious mucus in throat. Vertigo - Vertigo when moving. Vertigo on every motion in a warm room. Vertigo with constant reeling and staggering. COMMENTS - “Small ulcers on perineum near anus that constantly oozes very offensive moisture, painful for eight days.” This symptom has been expanded by clinical observation, principally Ozanam's, into ulceration in general, ulcers from pressure, as bedsores and from ill-fitting boots. “Sensation of splinter sticking in skin of right great toe when touched and violent pain as from pressure in left little toe.” Ulcers are the seat of severe shooting pains. Tissues sensitive to pressure and injury, sensitive mind (Hell.). “Griping pain in the abdomen, preceded and especially followed, by anxiety, trembling of legs and arms as though he were frightened, he became apprehensive if any one spoke to him and unpleasant news affected him exceedingly.” Fainting with diarrhea, stools are followed by intense chilliness, occurring generally a few hours after he felt the worst. Bad pain in anus compelling him to walk the floor all night or to roll on the floor. Symptoms worse by motion, walking. The right side is more affected than the left. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Aloe., Rat. Compare: (1) Glech. - rectal symptom. (2) Harn., Sil., Aesc. (3) Rat. - great constriction of anus, stools forced with great effort. (4) in varicose veins, Ham. (5) In splinter sensation, anal fissures and abscess in ulcer, Nit-ac. (6) In splinter sensation and ulcers, Arg-n„ Hep. (7) In ulcers, Hell., Hell-v., Sil. (8) In ulcers about the toes, M-aust. (9) In diarrhea, Sulph. (10) In effects of bad news, Gels. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Anxious aching in epigastrium. Periodical sticking upward from middle of epigastric region. Burning in epigastric region at night. Nausea. Vomiting and painful diarrhea.

Abdomen - Griping pain. Pinching in muscles. Cutting in umbilical region. Sensitiveness, worse along transverse colon and epigastric region. Crawling in abdomen. Colic with diarrhea, transversely across upper abdomen. Borborygmi.

Rectum - Diarrhea with burning and internal chilliness. Sudden, pasty diarrhea with faintness in abdomen. Excruciating pain at anus, continues long after stools, must rise and walk about. Biting, itching in anus, orifice swollen. Burning in anus, then internal chilliness. Ulceration of anus and perineum, purple, covered with crusts. Painful ulcer, oozing offensive moisture on perineum. Analfissures. Analfistula. Hemorrhoids, large and ulcerated.

Female - External genitals swollen and painful. Food - Appetite lost. Thirst.

Chest - Heat in chest. Dull shooting from chest to back through the heart. Sticking pain in left chest. Cutting in left side when sitting bent over. Sharp pain in ribs above hepatic region in morning.

Heart - Pain beneath the heart as from anxiety. Dull shooting from front to back through heart. Pulse contracted.

Back - Sticking in last cervical vertebra. Pinching or griping. Boring in left scapula, better motion. Ulcers over sacrum, bedsores. Breasts - Ulcer on lower part of left breast, consequent on abscess.

Limbs - Pain in wrist and fingers, knees and toes. Cramp in ulna at wrist. Weakness of legs, inhibiting walking. Jerking and tearing in limbs, then numbness. Weary pain in ankles when sitting. Pain in corns.

Sleep - Sleepiness all afternoon. Sleep is restless. Sleep unrefreshing, disturbed by many dreams. Terrifying dreams, nightmares, of the death of relatives.

Skin - Sensitive, painful. Sensitive ulcers on lower part of body. Ulcers from pressure, bedsores. Painful ulcer, oozing offensive moisture on perineum, near anus. Ulcers below coccyx, around sacrum, varicose veins. Itching, burning, as from nettles.

Modalities - Drinking water helps vertigo with nausea. Worse from touch orpressure, motion. Worse coming into warm room, night, during stool.

Kidneys - Frequent and copious urination, disturbing sleep at night. Constriction in region of neck of bladder, so that urine passed only in droplets. Burning and scanty urine.

Temperature - Shivering. Coldness of limbs with (burning) heat in face, back and chest. Rush of blood to head and face with sweat. Hot skin. Heat at night, disturbing sleep.

name: Palladium Metallicum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from diversion, touch, pressure, rubbing, after sleep, rest and stools. Sciatica, and colic are better from warmth (hot cloths). Worse from lively emotions, chagrin, social excitement, social functions. Worse standing, exertion..
