PHARMACY - pall.Palladiummetallicum.Pal- ladiummetal. (Pd, At. Wt. 1065). Trituration. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Constipation. Egotism. Eyelids, blisters. Flatulency. Headaches. Hysteria. Leucorrhea. Oophoritis. Ovaries, disorders. Ovarian, tumors. Sciatica. Sexual weakness. Tumors. Uterus, disorders. Uterine, prolapse. Warts.

HOMEOPATHIC - Palladium, one of the rare metals, was first separated from native platinum by Wollaston in 1803 and was named after the planet Pallas, which had been discovered just before that time by Olbers. The metal is closely associated with platinum and gold. Hering, who made the first provings in 1850, said that platinum and palladium, both proved in dust form, showed such similarity in their effects that the question arose whether corresponding differences might be found. Subsequent clinical experience has done much to distinguish between these two remedies. F. Aguilar noted that Pall, is indicated in gynecological conditions where the disease had its inception in the right ovary, the uterine prolapse and retroversion, sub-acute pelvic peritonitis and concomitant symptoms be- ing secondary. Pall, affects the ovaries, especially the right, the uterus and the mind. Disorders of the right ovary, attended with pains that are better from pressure. Chronic oophoritis. Bruised soreness. Stitches, rheumatic pains, suddenly changing and often lasting but a short time. Pains fleeting, transient. Every step causes pain in groin. Motor weakness, averse to exercise. Undressing causes itching all over body. MIND - Love of approbation. Seeks the good opinion of others and attaches great importance to them. Desires flattery. Haughty. Pride, easily offended. Wounded pride and fancied neglect. Effected profoundly by slight offensives, real or imaginary. Irresolution in morning. Irritability, takes everything in bad part. Irritability and impatience from headache. Very impertinent. Tries to appear as amiable as possible, but is obstinate. Anger with trembling. Inclined to use violent language. Curses and swears (Anae.). Weeping mood. Keeps up brightly when in company, much exhausted afterwards and pains aggravated. Excitement in company. Conversation aggravates. Desire for company, worse when alone. Averse to mental exertion. Apprehension that something horrible will happen. Depressing news aggravates all symptoms. Ailments from bad news. Feels as if she were going crazy. Time passes too slowly. Delusion that he is neglected, that she is not appreciated, that he has been insulted. Delusion had grown taller while walking. Abdomen - Soreness of abdomen, swelling in right groin. Hollowness in groins. Shooting pain from navel into breasts or pelvis, better after stools. Intestines feel strangulated. Sensation as if intestines were bitten off. Flatulency. Abdomen feels sore after menses. Pain in abdomen worse coughing and sneezing.

Head - Headache, causing irritability and impatience. Headache, better fixing attention on it. Morning headache with weakness in back. Pain across top of head from ear to ear, worse after an evening's entertainment with irritability and sour belchings. Temporo-parietal neuralgia with pain in shoulder. Sensation as if head were swung from behind forward, as if brain were being shaken. Itching on sides of head.

Eyes - Blue half-circles under eyes. Dryness and itching of eyes in evening, which is not better by rubbing. Sensation of dryness on the edges of the lids. Small watery blisters on edges of lower lids. Dull, heavy pain in and behind left eye. Pain around left eye, extending beyond right eyebrow. Pain in right eye, temple and ear. Pustule under right eyelids, worse touch.

Nose - Burning in nose with coryza, in evening. Painful pustule on point of nose, bleeds long after being squeezed. Blood' pustule on right cheek, near wing of nose. Abdominal pain worse when sneezing or coughing.

Face - Sallow complexion, blue. Soreness and painfulness of the right corner of the mouth. Pain in right and left lower jaw. Itching pimples on the face, the nose, behind the ears, in facial hair. Slower growth of facial hair.

Mouth - Tongue red in the middle (morning). Burning sensation on surface of tongue near tip. Tough mucus in mouth, slimy taste. Sensation as if upper incisors projecting. Left upper and outer incisor sensitive and feels like a foreign body.

Throat - Tough mucus in throat, slimy taste. Glairy mucus from throat. Frequent hawking of small solid lumps, which he must swallow. Tickling (or sticking) as if a crumb of bread had lodged in throat. Sensation when swallowing as if something hanging near hyoid bone. Dryness in throat and on tongue without thirst. Vertigo - Reels on coming into a room from exhaustion. COMMENTS - Right-sided ovarian tumors (Thuj. for the left side). Uterine and ovarian disorders. Bearing down feeling, achiness. Uterine prolapse. “Headache across top of head from one ear to the other.” Hering noted that the pains are fleeting, transient and hard to describe. Pressure relieves pains. “Love of approbation.” Easily hurt from slights, real or imaginary. “Wounded pride and fancied neglect.” Depressed, weep easily (Puls.). Irritability, leading to violent expressions. Can curse and swear (Anae.). Better in society and worse after the party or entertainment. Skinner cured a young woman who had excessive pain in the right ovary during the menses with Pall. The only relief she could get was by inducing her sister to sit on that region. This “better by pressure" distinguishes the pain of Pall, from the similar ovarian of Plat. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Chin, (diarrhea), Glon. and Bell, (headache). Compare: (1) Irid., Osm., Plat. (2) Right ovary, Apis, Graph.. Podo., Plat. (3) Left ovary, Arg-m. - feeling as if left ovary growing enormously large. Lach. - worse pressure. Lil-t., Cimic., Sulph. (4) Tired backache, Helon. (5) Hysteria introverted state of mind, Tarent. (6) Crumb in throat, Hep. (7) Pain in spleen, Cean. (Pall, at menses). Complementary: Arg-n., Helon., Lil-t., Apis. Plat. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Nausea. Tasteless belchings, which do not relieve.

Rectum - Constipation, stools are hard, frequently whitish like chalk. Dull pains in rectum, as from too long retained stool without urging. Frequent soft stool. Diarrhea with very little pain, night and day. Sensations - As if he had grown taller. As if she could not touch anything. As if head were swung from behind forward. As if brain were being shaken. As if neck becoming stiff. As if bladder was filled. As if uterus would prolapse. As if parts of groins would tear. As if testicles were bruised. As if heads of femurs were forced out of their sockets and expanded. As if hand shattered.

Male - Single stitches in urethra, extending down to corona glandis. Sensation as if testicles were bruised with pain in abdomen. In evening and at night no proper erection could be obtained.

Female - Menses come on at full moon. Menstrual discharge while nursing. Glairy, yellow leucorrhea before and after menses. Pain and swelling in region of right ovary. Ovarian tumors. Ovarian pains, better pressure. Uterine prolapse with retroversion. Cutting pains in uterus, relieved after stool. Sub-acute pelvic peritonitis with the right-sided pain and backache, menorrhagia. Pelvis leaden heavy, worse standing. Shooting or burning pain in pelvis. Bearing-down pains, relieved by rubbing. Soreness and shooting pain from navel to breast. Food - No desire for beer. Headache at dinner and after coffee.

Chest - Stitches in right side of chest, through to the back. Worse from taking a long breath, better when walking in the open air.

Heart - Pain in region of heart. Heart pain with paralysis of left arm. Pressing deep in the left side of the chest periodical, as if in the heart.

Back - Tired feeling in small of back. Frequent, painful spasm in muscles of right side of neck, especially morning. Painful drawing in neck, shoulders and down left arm. Pain in back and hips with coldness of limbs. Breasts - Sharp, stitching pain in right breast near nipple, worse from deep inspiration. Causations - Ailments from bad news.

Limbs - Fleeting neuralgic pains in various parts of the body. Sciatica. Rheumatic pain in right shoulder, in right hip. Heavy and tired limbs. Tired feeling in small of back. Darting pains from toes to hips. Itching. Lungs - Stitches in chest on taking a deep breath. Frequent hawking of small solid lumps that he must swallow. When ex pectorating, sensation as if something were pushed into head. Abdominal pain is worse coughing and sneezing.

Sleep - Great sleepiness in afternoon (3 p.m.) and early evening. Wakeful until 2 a.m. Starting in afternoon sleep. Dreams every night of buildings, wide stairs, many rooms. Symptoms better by sleep.

Skin - Itching all over after undressing. Itching and crawling as from fleas on different spots, back, arms, abdomen, thighs, ankles. Redness of knuckles, warts on knuckles.

Modalities - Better from diversion, touch, pressure, rubbing, after sleep, rest and stools. Sciatica, and colic are better from warmth (hot cloths). Worse from lively emotions, chagrin, social excitement, social functions. Worse standing, exertion.

Kidneys - Cutting pain in bladder, better stool. Pressure in bladder, as if very full, but little urine is passed. Dark urine with brick-dust sediment or coloring the vessel red. Muddy (not dark) urine, urine like water mixed with blood.

Temperature - Chilliness with cold hands and feet, with colic. Coldness of the limbs with pain in the back.

PHARMACY - palo. Paloondo. Gobernadora. Zy gophyllum tridentatum. Larrea mexicana. Creosote-bush. N. O. Zygophyllaceae. Northern Mexico, California and Texas. The tincture is prepared from the leaves and young branches. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Allergies. Anorexia. Bone, disorders. Colds. Influenza. Migraines. Nausea. Neuralgia. Osteoporosis. Rheumatism. Sinusitis.

HERBAL - Paloondo is a Mexican plant already familiar to the Aztecs. It grows in the dry territories of Northern Mexico, in California and in Texas. Dr. Willmar Schwabe introduced it into Europe. Paloondo has been used for different illnesses affecting the locomotor system, especially for arthritic and rheumatic afflictions.

HOMEOPATHIC - Schutt proved the remedy in 1960 on two groups of pro vers, producing few symptoms of rheumatism. A clinical proving was first undertaken using 3x and 4x, for cases of muscle pain and polyarthritis with favorable results. Palo, has allergic complaints, sneezing, face puffy on waking. Nasal allergic syndrome. Neurotic pains. At times, the pains are accompanied by vertigo. The pains are aggravated in the evening, on waking and after mental exertion. Nerve and rheumatic pains in the lower limbs and vertebral column. Growth dystrophy of the bones and cartilages. Bone dislocations, fractures and inflammations. MIND - Irritable, extreme sensitivity to noise. Tired, stunned. Depressive or euphoric condition with excitability. Bad-tempered, but more often, euphoric to the point of hyperexcitability.

Head - Acute pains in the head. Drawing pains coming from the occiput and spreading across the top of the head to the eyes. Occipital neuritis.

Stomach - Distention. Nausea, especially in morning. Cramping abdominal pains.

Rectum - Foul smelling, constipation or diarrhea.

Female - Menses early and painful. Food - Anorexia.

Heart - Heartbeat irregular with extra systole.

Limbs - Feeling of lead weight in the legs. Sensation of cracking. Pricking sensation in the limbs. On waking, pains in the limbs and the back, better by moving. Iliac and sacral pain, worse by being seated or lying down, ameliorated by walking.

Sleep - Dreams lively, especially in people who do not usually dream at all. Anguished dreams.

Skin - Redness with sensation of heat. Dryness of the skin with itching. Dry eczema.

Modalities - Better from walking. Worse in the evening, after mental exertion, on waking.

Temperature - All the pro vers experienced a febrile influenza-type condition. Shivering. as at the onset of influenza. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Rhus-t. - Generalized stiffness with physical and cerebral restlessness. (2) Eup- per. - Generalized stiffness and sensation of cracking with pains between the bones. (3) Asar. (4) Ther. - Intolerance of the slightest noise. REFERENCES - Julian. .

full:
PHARMACY - pancreat. Pancreatinum. Pancreas extract. Pancreatic glands of ox or sheep. Sarcode. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Diabetes. Diarrhea. Gout. Hypoglycemia. Mumps. Pancreas, disease.

HOMEOPATHIC - Pancreat. has been used with success in conditions due to disease or faulty action of the pancreas on the analogy of thyroid and the other sarcodes. Pancreat. is a combination of several digestive enzymes. Pancreas disease. Pancreatic diabetes. Hypoglycemia. Atonic dyspepsia, due to impaired secretion or defective composition of the digestive enzymes secreted. Dyspepsia, when the power of digesting fatty and starchy food is deficient. Acid dyspepsia, resulting from abnormal digestion of food. Intestinal indigestion, pain an hour or more after eating. Indigestion of fats and starches. Indigestion of children who are fed chiefly upon milk and sweets, and starches. Lienteric diarrhea. Mumps. COMMENTS - Burnett noted that Pancreat. is often of great service in gout. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) In action on pancreas and salivary glands, Iris, Nux-v., Puls., Merc., lod., Jab., Piloc. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

HERBAL - Buah Merah is grown only at the eastern portion of the Indonesian Islands, Papua, (east of Borneo and Bali). It is reported to be an effective tonic for the blood and immune system. The active substances are high in antioxidant and antivirus effects, proven to support the body's natural defenses in illness. Useful to assist the healing process of multifarious diseases including cancer and tumors. Leukemia. Lymph, bone cancer, brain, liver, breast, uterine, and ovarian cancer, cysts. Lung spots in infants.Hypertension. Heart disease. Lung weakness. Stroke. Parkinson's disease. Epilepsy. Rheumatism and osteoporosis. Hepatitis and cirrhosis. Diabetes mellitus. Eye irritation, blindness. Sinusitis. Lack of stamina, emaciation. HIV, AIDS. Dengue fever. Toxoplasmosis. Baldness. COMMENTS - People who took Buah merah were found to have much less incidences of HIV/AIDS, hepatitis, cancer, heart and hypertension diseases. REFERENCES - Buttimer. Murphy.

full:
PHARMACY - papay. Papaya vulgaris. Carica Papaya. Papaw. N. O. Cucurbitaceae. A tincture is made of the milky juice of the green fruit of the “Papaw.” Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Colds. Constipation. Cough. Dyspepsia. Eczema. Epithelioma. Headache. Itching. Nausea. Neuralgia. Numbness. Pimples. Toothache. Tumors. Vertigo. Warts.

HERBAL - The ripe fruit is refreshing and palatable, it is sometimes used as a sauce, the seeds are very similar to capers, it is sometimes preserved in sugar or boiled like turnips. The juice is used to remove freckles and is also a strong vermifuge. The leaves are used as a substitute for soap. Papain is the dried, white, powdered, unripe juice of Papaw, a ferment, and strongly suggests pepsin in odor, taste and appearance. When the unripe fruit is pierced with a knife, a milky juice exudes which is collected in a basin and allowed to coagulate. This is dried in the sun and contains a propeolytic enzyme which acts as a neutral or alkaline solution, and is given for impaired digestion. It is said to dissolve the fibrinous membrane in croup and diphtheria when a solution over the pharynx painted every five minutes. When injected into the circulation in large doses, it paralyses the heart. Glossal fissures and ulcerations, and particularly syphilitic ulcerations of the throat, mouth and tongue, are asserted to have yielded to alkaline solutions of papain. Applied to the skin, it renders it softer and smoother, and appears to destroy the projections formed at certain points by a greater thickening of the epidermis. Hardened tissues, produces by irritation, etc. Warts, corns, chronic forms of scaly eczema. Cutaneous tubercules, epithelioma. Injected into indolent glandular tumors to promote their absorption. It is not caustic or astringent, but has the virtue of dissolving muscular and connective tissue. The seeds possess an identical property, and will probably be found preferable for administration. It is likewise said to cause the destruction and expulsion of the tapeworm. Catarrh of the stomach. Atonic and fermentative dyspepsia, with painful acid eructations, flatulence, and constipation. Digestive failure accompanying continued fevers. Stimulates the stomach in the beginning of convalescence, and in some cases increases the appetite and promotes absorption of the digested pabulum.

HOMEOPATHIC - Muscular debility. Languor and drowsiness. Dull feeling in morning on rising. Pains worse towards evening, better by rubbing. Loses flesh. Catches colds easily when riding, during menses. Nervous before and during menses. MIND - Impatient. Unusually active, can study longer without weariness, likes to read. Unable to think quickly. Stupid, confused feeling. Could hardly trust herself to do anything during menses for fear of making mistakes. Forgetful. Listless, lacking in ambition. Wants to be alone. Dislikes to be talked to or to answer.

Head - Headache towards evening. Headache after eating popcorn and candy. Headache worse bright light, warm air and motion, better cold air, rubbing, sleep. Pain involving eyeball, passing backward to occiput and nape, drawing head backward. Frontal pain. Piercing pain traveling like lightning from right side of head to right side of foot. Bruised feeling in left side. Soreness of parietal region with throbbing. Dullness. Fullness in evening. Itching greater, but dandruff less than usual.

Eyes - Prickling in eyes. Pain in eyeballs. Dry feeling in eyeballs. Inflammation of right lid, feeling as if a foreign substance were in it, preventing much reading by artificial light. Vision not as good as usual.

Ears - Itching behind left ear.

Nose - Nose stopped, worse left side. Thick discharge from nose watery, colorless, bland coryza.

Face - Neuralgia on left side of face. Female - Itching on mons veneris. Food - Appetite diminished in morning. Thirst, but inability to drink cold water on account of toothache. Drinks much water.

Mouth - Toothache in lower molars, with soreness, worse cold water. Tongue dry at night. Food tastes flat.

Throat - Pain in larynx. Hoarse in evening. Vertigo - Vertigo and throbbing frontal headache with nausea. COMMENTS - Psoric conditions, particularly when caused by suppression of an itch. Digestive disorders causing great pain when food is taken. Digestive disorders of pregnancy, stimulating appropriation and assimilation, particularly when the digestion is seriously interfered with during the last three months of pregnancy. REFERENCES - Allen. Ellingwood. King. Murphy.

Stomach - Faint for want of food, but food distresses stomach. Pain around waist. Tasteless eructations. Nausea after dinner.

Rectum - Irregular bowel movements. Constipation. First part large and hard, breaking into balls, later part mushy, with wind. Soft stool.

Male - Pain running from perineum to middle of penis as if a rough, jagged body forced its way out. Pain in left testicle, waking him at night. Instinct abnormally aroused. Erections towards morning. Erections, but no emissions, not long-lasting and not due to sexual thoughts. Emissions without lascivious dreams. Flaccid and lifeless. Functions depressed.

Heart - Shooting pain in heart. Pulse slow and weak. Pulse 100, temperature 102.

Back - Sore pain in point under left scapula. Bruised pain in left side. Pain in region of kidney region, of left kidney, running around ilium.

Limbs - Numbness, pricking and sleepiness. Limbs go to sleep easily. Numbness, better walking. Trembling of lower limbs, with weakness of them. Prickling in lower limbs, but not in foot, with tingling. Right leg went to sleep when writing. Pain on ball of right foot under little toe, with swelling and with heat extending to toes. Itching on right ankle on going to bed. Itching forearms and anterior part of thighs, with diffused redness, worse warmth of bed. Rheumatic pain in left shoulder, left arm helpless. Numbness of right hand and fingers while asleep, especially little finger. Numbness of right ring finger, worse on outer side. Lungs - Cough keeping him awake at night. Violent, sudden, spasmodic cough with easy expectoration and soreness of left lung. Shooting in lungs and around heart. Pain in left lung. Deep pain in upper lobe Papaya vulgaris of left lung. Pain from left chest to left thigh and knee. Heavy pain, in left lung, extending through to back and becoming stabbing. Lungs feel tired and hot.

Sleep - Y awning and stretching. Drowsy, but cannot sleep. Disturbed, frequent waking. Heavy sleep. Horrible, vivid dreams, of shipwreck, drowning, being shot, fire.

Skin - Itching all over body. Red, itching elevations, worse evening and warmth to bed, better scratching. Itching eruption over right eye. Eruption in groins, bends of knees and right elbow, extending along flexor surface, and on right forearm and abdomen. Pimples on face and body. Red, sore, elevated points, like acne, on thighs. Pinkish erysipelatous swelling on dorsum of left great toe, with itching, better scratching or rubbing. Eruption like nettle-rash after scratching.

Bladder - Tearing in bladder, with desire to urinate. Frequent desire to urinate. Irresistible desire at sound of running water, even in horse's throat when drinking. Straining with the first urinary effort in morning, with burning as if an obstruction were being overcome, which being removed, the urine passes easily. Burning in urethra during and after urination, with continuous desire. Urine increased, scanty. Less sediment than formerly.

Temperature - Chilly at night, in open air. Cold hands and feet, forefingers, with deadness, stoppage of circulation.

CLINICAL - Abdomen, swelling. Breasts, disorders. Constipation. Diaphragmitis. Indigestion.…
full:
PHARMACY - paraf. Paraffinum. Purified paraffin. Obtained by distillation of wood peat bituminous coal petroleum and others. Trituration. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Abdomen, swelling. Breasts, disorders. Constipation. Diaphragmitis. Indigestion. Leucorrhea. Menorrhagia. Musca, volitantes. Spinal, pain. Spleen, pain. Umbilicus, pain. Uterus, disorders. Vertebrae, disorders. Vision, disorders.

HOMEOPATHIC - Paraffin as a generic term includes all those substances which have no affinity for sulphuric acid and cannot be destroyed by it, including petroleum. Specifically, Paraffin is a tasteless, inodorous, fatty matter, which resists the action of acids and alkalis, obtained by the dry distillation of wood, peat, bituminous coal, petroleum, etc. In the distillation of petroleum, naphthalin is the first substance that comes off, paraffin the next. The homeopaths of Rome found it serviceable in uterine and other troubles, particularly constipation. Pains in the groins, stabbing in mons veneries, cutting pain from one iliac crest to the other. Leucorrhea, pruritus vulvae and other disturbances of the female generative system with pains. Uterine disorders. Knife-like pains. Pains extend from one part to another and alternate. Pain in stomach alternates with pain in throat and spine. Aversion to tobacco, smoking causes pain in stomach. Stomach pain with palpitations. Constipation.

Head - Left side of head and face suffer most, pains stinging and twisting. Pain as if a nail were driven in left side of vertex. Twisting in left ear.

Eyes - Vision dim, with black specks. Sensation as if there were fat on the eyes. Lids red.

Ears - Roaring in right ear like rumbling of a mill wheel, afternoon. Gurgling in left ear like beating of pulse. Ringing in both ear, morning. Stinging and twisting in left ear.

Nose - Odor of cordials in nose. Nose moist, frequent desire to blow it, but without sneezing. Nosebleed, dark red.

Face - Itching in face as from urticaria, smooth red spots appear.

Mouth - Tearing, twisting pain in teeth down to lower jaw. Full of saliva, feels sticky, bitter taste.

Throat - Dryness of throat, fauces as if dried up, but without thirst. Sense of suffocation in pharynx. COMMENTS - Knife-like stabs, twisting, wrenching pains, stinging and twisting, electric pains. Pains extend from one part to another and alternate. Pain in the stomach alternates with pains in throat and spine. Clarke recorded the case of Mrs. W., 37, mother of three children, who suffered since her last confinement, five years before, with bearing-down pains, excessive menses, and leucorrhea. Constant and violent indigestion with morning retching or vomiting. Pain in back, shoulders and abdomen after, any food, however light. The pains, which “double her up” were worse on standing. Much thirst. Constipation with hemorrhoids. Constant desire to pass water. After Murx., and Alstonia constricta had given some relief, the indigestion returned in full force. A few globules of Paraf. 30c were dissolved in water and a teaspoonful taken every two or three hours. In a few days, all symptoms of indigestion were gone and did not return. Other symptoms were ameliorated. The menses, instead of recurring too soon, were delayed much beyond the normal time. Paraf. also has a remarkable action in joints with nodules. Cooper saw swollen joints lessen considerably from its use as a liniment. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Napht., Petr., Eupi. (2) Desire to walk fast, Buff., lod. (3) Uterine symptoms, Sep., Murx., Nat-m„ Nat-s. (4) Intolerance of tight clothing, Lach. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Hungry all the time. Pain across stomach. Pain in stomach alternates with pain in throat and spine, extends to chest with belching. Fixed pain in left hypochondrium, as if parts were being twisted. Stomach pains with palpitations.

Abdomen - Pain in lower abdomen, extending to genitals, rectum and coccyx, better sitting.

Rectum - Frequent desire for stool. Chronic constipation with hemorrhoids and continual urging to stool without result. Obstinate constipation in children (Alum., Nyct.).

Female - Menses too late, black, abundant. Milky leucorrhea. Nipples pain when touched, as if sore inside. Stabbing pain in mons veneris. Very hot urine with burning pains in vulva.

Chest - Chest pains as if compressed. Stinging in chest. Diaphragm, as if it was inflamed.

Heart - Pulse weak, thready, increased in frequency.

Back - Pains in spine, extending into lumbar vertebra. Pains in spine as if it had been injured, as bad during rest as when in motion. Back pains are worse by bending. Drawing and stinging between the shoulders. Pains as if from fatigue in both loins. Breasts - The nipple is painful on touching them, as if sore inside.

Limbs - Pain in spine extending to inguinal region and in both loins, when ascending the stairs. Feeling of electric shocks in all joints. Wrenching pain in calves, extending into toes in joints. Feet swollen with tearing in ankles and soles.

Sleep - Continued yawning, although the joints of the jaw are painful. Frequent gaping with great somnolence. Cannot keep awake and goes to sleep in her chair, her feet go to sleep. Sensual, lascivious dreams.

Skin - Frost bite. Burns, even of third degree with sloughing and sepsis; wash with sterile water and dry and spray with paraffin and cover with thin layer of cotton.

Modalities - Better after sleep, rest. Better by supporting the part. The pains are worse bending over. Worse standing or walking (soon bring back the symptoms).

Teeth - Tearing in teeth. Stabbing pain in . one of the left lower molars. Twisting in teeth with stinging in ear. Twisting pain in left lower teeth and left temple, sleep impossible.

Temperature - Chill, heat, and sweat, frequently alternating. Chill, followed by dry heat with thirst, which is soon followed by sweat. Face and hands hot and red, hot sweat on upper part of body, especially forehead.

PHARMACY - paraq. Paraquat. Nitrogen herbicide (1,1 ’-dimethyl-4,4'-bipyridinium). Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Abdominal pain. Coma. Convulsions. Diarrhea. Dyspnea. Eye, problems. Incoordination. Kidney, failure. Liver, problems. Lung, problems. Lung, scarring. Nail, problems. Nausea. Pulmonary, edema. Respiratory, failure. Skin, problems. Tachycardia. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Paraquat is a quaternary nitrogen herbicide widely used for broadleaf weed control. It is a quick-acting, nonselec- tive compound, that destroys green plant tissue on contact and by translocation within the plant. It is also used as a crop desiccant and defoliant, and as an aquatic herbicide. Paraquat affects the lungs, heart, liver, kidneys, cornea, adrenal glands, skin, and digestive system. It causes skin and eye irritation and also has caused skin sensitization. Paraquat splashed in the eye can irritate, burn, and cause corneal damage and scarring of the eyes. Direct contact with paraquat solutions or aerosol mists may cause skin burns, dermatitis, and damage to fingernails. After prolonged skin exposure, workers get damaged fingernails as indicated by discoloration, nail deformities, or loss of nails. Effects due to high acute exposure to paraquat may include excitability and lung congestion, which in some cases leads to convulsions, incoordination, and death by respiratory failure. If swallowed, burning of the mouth and throat often occurs, followed by gastrointestinal tract irritation, resulting in abdominal pain, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. After a person ingests a large amount of paraquat, he or she is likely to immediately have pain and swelling of the mouth and throat. The next signs of illness following ingestion are gastrointestinal symptoms, such as nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and diarrhea (which may become bloody). Severe gastrointestinal symptoms may result in dehydration, electrolyte abnormalities (not enough sodium and potassium in the body), and low blood pressure. Ingestion of small to medium amounts of paraquat may lead to development of liver, kidney or heart failure, or lung scarring, within several days to several weeks. Ingestion of large amounts leads to pulmonary edema, lung scarring, respiratory failure, leading to possible death, heart injury, increased heart rate, confusion, seizures, or coma, within a few hours to a few days. Other toxic effects include thirst, shortness of breath, rapid heart rate, kidney failure, lung sores, and liver damage. Some symptoms may not occur until days after exposure. Persons with lung problems may be at increased risk from exposure. Many cases of illness and/or death have been reported in humans. REFERENCES - Murphy.

name: Parathyroidinum
author: Murphy
constitution: Arthritis. Bone, disorders. Calcium, deposits. Chilblains. Emaciation. Fibrocystic, osteitis. Hematuria. Kidney, stones. Multiple, myeloma. Muscular, hypotonia. Myasthenia. Osteogenesis, imperfecta. Osteoporosis. Paget's disease. Pancreatitis. Polyuria. Rheumatism. Tabes. Varicose, ulcer.
keynote:
PHARMACY - parathyr. Parathyroidinum. Parathyroid hormone. Sarcode. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Arthritis. Bone, disorders. Calcium, deposits. Chilblains. Emaciation. Fibrocystic, osteitis. Hematuria. Kidney, stones. Multiple, myeloma. Muscular, hypotonia.…
full:
PHARMACY - parathyr. Parathyroidinum. Parathyroid hormone. Sarcode. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Arthritis. Bone, disorders. Calcium, deposits. Chilblains. Emaciation. Fibrocystic, osteitis. Hematuria. Kidney, stones. Multiple, myeloma. Muscular, hypotonia. Myasthenia. Osteogenesis, imperfecta. Osteoporosis. Paget's disease. Pancreatitis. Polyuria. Rheumatism. Tabes. Varicose, ulcer.

HOMEOPATHIC - Parathyroid secretion plays an important part in phosphorus and in the regulation of calcium in the blood. The hypercalcémie parathyroid hormone was first isolated in 1925 by Hansen. It increases the level of calcium in the blood, reduces the level of calcium in the urine and increases the amount of phosphorus in the urine. General weakness. Asthenia. Fatigue. Depression. Pallor. Emaciation. Tabes. Dry skin, eczema. Hair loss. Grave's disease. Hypersensitivity. Nervous irritability. Hypomania. Paralysis agitans. Puerperal convulsions and epilepsy. Tetany, when there is a disturbance of the calcium metabolism and it is associated with muscular irritation and hyperexcitability. Chronic rheumatism. Pains in the thorax, lumbar region and lower limbs. Arthritis of the wrists, ankles, knees, hips. Demineralization of the bones. Osteoporosis. Diffuse pain in the bones, especially in the long bones. Paresis of the limbs. Walking painful, difficult, dragging. Myasthenia gravis. Muscular hypotonia. Paget's disease. Belated gastric attacks. Polyuria. Hematuria. Increased level of calcium and reduction of phosphorus in the blood, increased alkaline phosphate liberating enzymes. Great calcium loss. MIND - Depression. Mental confusion. Agitation. Hypomania.

Eyes - Scleritis.

Face - Pale face.

Mouth - Caries and arthritis of the tooth sockets.

Stomach - Gastric acidity. Painful aftermeals gastric attack. Stomach and duodenal ulcers. Vomiting of blood. Sickness of pregnancy. COMMENTS - Experimental results have indicated the existence of a parathyroid secretion whose action diminishes the level of calcium in the blood. It was the clinical syndrome of the primitive hyperparathyroid hormone which drew Fouche's attention to establishing a homeopathic symptomatology- Primary hyperparathyroidism is explained by an osseous syndrome whose clinical manifestation is expressed by pain in the bones, aggravated by standing or walking and also expressed by spontaneous fractures, swelling in the bones and bone deformities. In radiology, one can observe abnormal transparency of the skeleton, the cortex of the long bones is decalcified, the medullary canal is enlarged and these signs are especially present in the hands and jaws. Cavities can also be seen, again, primarily in the hands and jaws, as well as tumors, which enlarge the bones by pushing back the periosteum. The extra-osseous syndrome occurs in 40% of the cases. It is characterized by its effects on the urinary organs, polyuria, kidney stones and nephrocalcinosis. Effects on the digestive system with anorexia, post-prandial epigastric pains and constipation. Gastric atony and ulcers in the low duodenum. Effects on the heart muscles with palpitations, tachycardia and shortening of the Q. T. interval on the electrocardiogram. Effects on the muscles with asthenia and muscular hypotonia. Psychological effects with depressive tendency and mental confusion. The syndrome is characterized by an increase of calcium and reduction of phosphorus in the blood, as well as an increase of phosphates in the urine and an increase of the alkaline phosphate-liberating enzymes. Fouche noticed that the removal of the parathyroid gland improved the condition of patients with chronic ankylosing rheumatism, but only temporarily. Secondary hyperparathyroidism can occur as a defense reaction by the organism, which aims to maintain the normal level of calcium in the blood. The level can become reduced as a result of a diminution in the calcium deposits in the bone or disorders of alimentary deposits or because of absorption complaints. It can also be reduced from destruction of the skeleton following osseous carcinoma or myelomas, or from kidney infections, kidney malfunctioning, glomerulonephritis, tubular nephritis, idiopathic increase in the level of calcium in the urine. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Calc., Calc-p., Calc-f. (2) Syph. - Nightly linear pains in the bones, loss of memory, especially of proper nouns, obsessions. (3) Astra-e. - Confused state, paretic weakness of the limbs. (4) Mez. - Periosteal pains at night, worse in cold, damp weather. REFERENCES - Blackwood. Julian.

Abdomen - Slow digestion, eructation of gas. Chronic pancreatitis. Gastric and duodenal ulcer.

Rectum - Atonic constipation or frequent stools, abundant, whitish and fetid.

Female - Dysmenorrhea and rare menses. Uterine fibromyoma. Food - Anorexia, loss of appetite.

Heart - Palpitations and tachycardia. Infarction of the myocardium. Precordial pains. Inflammation of the coronary arteries.

Back - Weakness and curved spine. Strong pain in the lumbar region, spreading towards the bladder and thigh, tenesmus of the bladder with occasional vomiting.

Limbs - Diffuse pains in the bones, especially the long bones, aggravated by standing and walking. Deformity of the fingers. Bones sensitive to pressure.1 Paget’s disease. Demineralization of the bones. Painful post- traumatic osteoporosis. Osteoporosis. Osteogenesis imperfecta. Fibrocystic osteitis. Painful non- inflammatory lesion of the bones. Chilblains.

Skin - Strumous edema of the legs. Varicose ulcer.

Kidneys - Increase in the level of calcium in the urine with or without an increase of calcium in the blood. Calcium deposits in the kidney parenchyma. Calcium kidney stones. Polyuria and hematuria. Disorder of glomerular clearance and urea clearance.

Blood - Increase in the level of calcium in the blood. Reduction in the level of phosphorus in the blood. Increase in the alkaline phosphate-liberating enzymes. Constitutions - Syphilitic condition in a phospho-fluoric type.

name: Pareira Brava
author: Murphy
constitution: Bladder, catarrh. Calculus. Dysuria. Gonorrhea. Kidney, disorders. Leucor- rhea. Prostate, enlargement. Kidney, colic. Urethritis. Urine, slimy.
keynote:
PHARMACY - pareir. Pareira brava. Virgin vine. Cessampelos pareira. Velvet leaf. Chondrodendron tomentosum. N. O. Meni- spermacae. Tincture of fresh root. Tincture of dried root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bladder, catarrh. Calculus. Dysuria.…
full:
PHARMACY - pareir. Pareira brava. Virgin vine. Cessampelos pareira. Velvet leaf. Chondrodendron tomentosum. N. O. Meni- spermacae. Tincture of fresh root. Tincture of dried root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bladder, catarrh. Calculus. Dysuria. Gonorrhea. Kidney, disorders. Leucor- rhea. Prostate, enlargement. Kidney, colic. Urethritis. Urine, slimy.

HERBAL - Pareira is a climbing plant, a native of the West Indies, Central America and India. The root has a traditional use in diseases of the bladder and urinary organs.

HOMEOPATHIC - Pareir. affects the genitourinary organs and the left side. It is useful in kidney colic, prostatic disorders and catarrh of bladder. Cartilaginous induration of mucus membranes of the urethra and bladder. Sensation as if bladder were distended with pain. Kidney colic, enlarged prostate with retention of urine and catarrh of the bladder. Dysuria. Constant urging to urinate, violent pain in the glans penis and down the thighs during efforts of urination, must get on knees and hands pressing head firmly to the floor to urinate. Urine contains thick, stringy, white Pareira brava mucus or red sand.

Urine - Urine smells strongly of ammonia and contains a large quantity of viscid, thick, white mucus. Black, bloody, foaming urine, depositing a brick-dust sediment of uric acid, deep red and mucus urine. COMMENTS - A short proving by C. M. Fox of Denver, Colorado, brought out some characteristic symptoms which have been clinically confirmed. Violent pains with strangury, must go on “all-fours and press head against floor to pass water at all. Urethritis with severe pain when passing water and discharge of mucus from urethra. Pains down thighs and even to feet when attempting topass water. Violent pain in glans penis” with the straining. Fox related two cases of prostatic enlargement with dysuria in which Par. gave complete relief. The first concerned a man, 68, who had an old prostatic affection, constant urging with entire inability. Feet and legs much swollen, had to be put in a warm bath before catheter could be passed. Only on hands and knees with forehead pressed on the floor, could he pass a few drops of scalding urine. Pareir. lx gave rapid relief. Swelling disappeared from legs and he was able to resume his business and continue at it for ears. Fox's second case recorded a man with an enlarged prostate with retention, severe attacks two or three times a years, when he would have to have the urine drawn off for a week or two. After using Pareir., the catheter was not required more than twice in two years. When he felt the symptoms coming on, a few drops of Pareir. would relieve him at once. Many other remedies had been used in vain before Pareir. was prescribed. RELATIONS - Compare: (l)Pariet. (2) Chim. - chronic catarrhal congestion following cystitis, acute prostatitis, feeling of a ball in perineum when sitting. (3) Fab. - dysuria, post-gonorrheal complications, gravel, bladder catarrh. (4) Uva., Hydrang., Berb., Oci., Hedeo. (5) Cocc. (6) Spasm and burning in bladder, ropy urine, Chim., Uva. (7) Prostatic affections, Hydrang., Sabal. (8) Kidney colic, Oci., Berb. (9) Dysuria - Berb. has pain in back extending to hips, Pareir. has pain extending to thighs and even toes. Berb. urine lacks the ammoniacal smell of Pareir. (10) Dribbling urine after urination, Sei. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Male - Urethritis with prostatic disorders. Enlargement of prostate glands with retention of urine, pains extending down thighs. Severe pain when urinating and discharge of mucus from urethra. Violent pain in glans penis. Gonorrhea.

Back - Excruciating pains in the left lumbar region, pain radiates from left kidney to groin, following course of ureter.

Limbs - Dropsical swelling of feet and legs. Lungs - Viscous matter lodged in and obstructing bronchi.

Kidneys - Bruised pains in region of kidneys. Constant urging, great straining, pain down thighs during efforts to urinate. Dysuria. Painful urination since confinement cannot urinate in any position except on hands and knees. Dribbling after urination (Sel.).Urethritis with prostatic trouble.

Bladder - Feeling of the bladder being distended. Almost cartilaginous induration of mucus membrane of bladder. Itching along urethra. Can emit urine only when he goes on his knees, pressing head firmly against the floor.

name: Paris Quadrifolia
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from rest, pressure, belching. Worse touch, hiccough, eating. Worse from thinking of problems, mental exertion, thinking, eyestrain. Smoking tobacco causes headache..
constitution: Acidity. After-pains. Brachial neuralgia. Ciliary neuralgia. Ciliary paralysis. Digestion, weak. Gonorrhea. Headache. Hic- cough. Hoarseness. Hysteria. Mania. Neuralgia. Panaritium. Paralysis. Saliva, sour. Spine, affection. Touch, sense, disordered.
keynote: PHARMACY - par. Paris quadrifolia. One berry. True Love. Herb Paris. N. O. Trilliaceae. Sometimes consideredasub-orderofSmilacee or of Liliaceae. Europe. Moist, shady woods in Great Britain. Tincture of whole plant when in fruit. Historical dose: Tincture and all…
full:
PHARMACY - par. Paris quadrifolia. One berry. True Love. Herb Paris. N. O. Trilliaceae. Sometimes consideredasub-orderofSmilacee or of Liliaceae. Europe. Moist, shady woods in Great Britain. Tincture of whole plant when in fruit. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acidity. After-pains. Brachial neuralgia. Ciliary neuralgia. Ciliary paralysis. Digestion, weak. Gonorrhea. Headache. Hic- cough. Hoarseness. Hysteria. Mania. Neuralgia. Panaritium. Paralysis. Saliva, sour. Spine, affection. Touch, sense, disordered.

HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany said of Paris that the leaves and stems were “formerly used in medicine, the juice of the berry, though considered poisonous, has been employed in curing inflammation of the eyes.” Paris betrays its relation to the lilies and arums in the symptoms of irritation which it causes in mucus membranes and the skin with burning sensations and cramps.

HOMEOPATHIC - The provings made by Hahnemann, Stapf and others, brought out a very marked and characteristic action on the eyes and developed some of the keynote symptoms of the drug. Affects the head, spine, eyes and one side. Sensation of expansion and consequent tension. Sensation of heaviness, numbness, parts feel too big or drawn together. Whole body painful especially when touched. Broken feeling of joints. Generally a left side remedy, but it has coldness of the right side, while the left side is namral or hot. Catarrhal complaints, stuffed feeling at root of nose. Disorder of sense of touch, objects feel rough. The scalp is very sensitive to touch. Pressure on a sore spot on head causes cries. Mucus secretions are green and tenacious. The eyes give out of fetid, ulcer-like smell. Great sensitiveness to offensive odors, also imaginary bad smells, milk and bread smell like putrid meat. Diarrhea stool smells like putrid meat.“Hunger soon after a meal,” the “sinking” of the anti-psorics, hellebores, and veratrums. MIND - Loquacious mania. Garrulous, prattling, vivacious. Inclination to treat others with rudeness and contempt. Silly conduct. Feels too large. Imaginary foul smells.

Head - Chronic headaches. Headache worse by thinking. Headaches as from pulling a string from eyes to occiput. Occipital headache with a feeling of weight. Head feels very large, expanded. Numb feeling on left side of head. Head feels as if distended and the scalp too tight. Sensation as if scalp were contracted and bones scraped. Soreness of top of head, scalp sensitive, cannot brush hair.

Eyes - Eyes feel too large and heavy for their sockets. Sensation of a string through eyeballs, drawing them tightly backward to the middle of the brain. Eyes as if they were projected. Expanded, as though eyelids did not cover. Affections of the eyebrows.

Ears - Pain as if the ears were pressed out or forced apart by a wedge, worse swallowing.

Nose - Imaginary foul smells. Bread, fish, and milk smell putrid.

Face - Neuralgia, hot stitches in left malar bone, which is very sore. Seems drawn into root of nose. Inflammation of the antrum, where eye symptoms coexist.

Mouth - Tongue feels too large. Tongue dry when awaking. Coated white without thirst with bitter or diminished taste.

Throat - Burning, when eating and drinking. As of a ball in the throat. Hawks up tough, green mucus. Periodical painless hoarseness. Vertigo - Vertigo on reading aloud. COMMENTS - Par. is one of the drugs which are credited with producing garrulity, vivacity, with love of prattling, like tea. B. Nath Banerjee recorded a case of loquacious insanity cured with Par. 3c. Mrs. B., 45, suddenly become loquacious and insane. After a mouth of Kavirajee treatment without benefit she came under his care, October3, 1893. A year before, the last of her five children, a grown-up son, died and she could not be consoled and gradually became morose and dull. She ceased to menstruate in February, 1893, but had no uterine troubles or any other illness previous to the present. Loquacity, but not continuous. Every three or four days, if interfered with, maniacal attacks lasting about half an hour. At times foolish behavior. With difficulty Banerjee obtained the following symptoms from the patient: vertigo and whenever she thinks of her lost son, severe headache, the vertex being sensitive to touch. When telling these symptoms, suddenly her looks became wandering and her eyes appeared as if protruding from their sockets. She could not relish her food because everything, especially fish, smelt putrid. Whole body painful, especially when touched. She complained of a ball lodging in the throat and giving her trouble with burning. Acidity and badly smelling diarrhea. A peculiar feeling of coldness of right side of the body while the left side was hot. All symptoms worse in evening and on motion. Ign. 30c and later 200c, was given without any effect. Par. acted promptly, and on the third day the patient assured the doctor that she was quite well. The remedy was not repeated and the cure held. Clarke cured with Par. a “numb feeling of left side of head.” Numbness affects the upper limbs. The left arm is paralyzed, and it feels stiff with fingers contracted. “Numbness and prickling in lefthand” was removed in a case of spinal affection. “Fingers often feel as if asleep, objects seem rough to touch.” Disorder of the sense of touch, with great sensitiveness of the surface. Hot stitches in left malar bones. Acidity, sour saliva. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Coff. Compare: (1) Past., Sil., Calc., Nux-v, Rhus-t. (2) In spinal headache rising from nape, Sil. (3) Wild look in eyes. Bell. (4) As if eyes drawn back by thread, Croto-t. (5) Eyeballs feel too large. Sil. (6) Garrulity, Lach., Meph., Stram., Cimic., right, Agar. (7) Laryngeal affections, Arg-n. (Par. has expectoration noticed mostly in morning and it is green and tenacious). (8) String-like pain, All-c. (9) Heart, Lil- t., Conv. (10) Panaritium, Bor-ac. (11) Imaginary foul smells, Anae. (12) worse from motion, Bry. Compatible: Calc., Led., Lyc., Nux-v., Phos., Rhus-t., Sep., Sulph. Incompatible: Ferr-p. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Heavy as from a stone, better by eructation. Weak digestion. Red curved streak above navel.

Abdomen - Tensive pain throughout abdomen. Hard pressure in abdomen. Rumbling and rolling in abdomen, cutting, griping pains. Incisive drawing and boring in one side of abdomen.

Rectum - Frequent but scanty evacuations of the consistency of pap. Loose, fetid evacuations, which smell like putrid flesh. Sensations - Sensation of expansion and consequent tension. As if scalp were contracted and bones scraped sores. Heavy load on nape. As if a thread were drawn tightly through eye to middle of head. Ear as if forced apart by a wedge, as if pressed out or torn out, as if a burning heat was rushing out of ears. Tongue feels too large. Ball in throat. Throat constricted. Stone in stomach. As if internal parts contracted. Fingers as if asleep, dead. All joints as if broken, swollen or dislocated at every motion.

Female - Premature menses. Increased sexual desire. Intense after-pains. Suppressed lochia with ineffectual urging to stool. Food - Voracious appetite. Hunger very soon after a meal.

Chest - Shootings in chest and sides of chest. Aching in the right side of chest.

Back - Weight and weariness in nape of neck. Violent pain on both sides of neck extending down to fingers worse mental exertion. Stitches in coccyx on sitting. Causations - Ill effects of injury, suppressions.

Limbs - Numbness of upper limbs. Sense of weight and weariness in nape of neck and across shoulders. Neuralgia, beginning in left intercostal region and extending into left arm. Neuralgia of coccyx, pulsating, sticking, when sitting. Joints feel broken, swollen or dislocated at every motion. Arm becomes stiff, fingers clenched. Fingers feel numb. Everything feels rough. Lungs - Stuffed condition and fullness at root of nose. Periodical,painless hoarseness. Cough as from vapor of sulphur in trachea. Constant hawking, on account of viscid, green mucus in larynx and trachea.

Skin - Painfully sensitive.

Modalities - Better from rest, pressure, belching. Worse touch, hiccough, eating. Worse from thinking of problems, mental exertion, thinking, eyestrain. Smoking tobacco causes headache.

Temperature - Unilateral coldness or heat. Heat descending the back from the neck.

name: Paronichia Illecebrum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Worse from movement or the slightest effort. Worse left side, but not exclusively..
constitution: Angio-hematic typhus. Appendicitis. Blepharitis. Bronchial pneumonia. Cancer. Conjunctivitis. Encephalitis. Endometritis. High fever. Infectious diseases. Mastoiditis. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Rhinitis. Septicemia. Sinusitis. Typhoid fever. Typhus.
keynote:
PHARMACY - paro-i. Paronichia illecebrum. Tiangius pepetla. Alternanthera sessilis. Sanguinaria of Cuba. Illebraceae or Paronychi- aceae family. Cuba. The tincture is prepared from the whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Angio-hematic…
full:
PHARMACY - paro-i. Paronichia illecebrum. Tiangius pepetla. Alternanthera sessilis. Sanguinaria of Cuba. Illebraceae or Paronychi- aceae family. Cuba. The tincture is prepared from the whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Angio-hematic typhus. Appendicitis. Blepharitis. Bronchial pneumonia. Cancer. Conjunctivitis. Encephalitis. Endometritis. High fever. Infectious diseases. Mastoiditis. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Rhinitis. Septicemia. Sinusitis. Typhoid fever. Typhus.

HERBAL - This plant is a very close relation to the Caryophyllaceae, which gives the saponarias to the Materia Medica. Paronichia illecebrum is a grass whose trailing stem has branches, oblong pale green leaves and capitate flowers.

HOMEOPATHIC - The proving was established by Manuel M. De Legarreta. Paro-i. has fever, dry, oppressive heat and symptoms of catarrh. The patient wants to uncover himself all the time. When lying on his side, he can no longer move, feels weary, weak and sleepy. Acute congestion of the nerves, lungs and blood vessels. Feeling of emptiness in the brain and doubling of personality. High fever. Encephalitis in eruptive juvenile diseases. Involuntary passing of stools and urine. Poisoning of the nursing child. MIND - Calm, tranquil state of mind. Sleepy and in a semi-awake state. Nervous weakness. Doubling of personality. Feeling that there are two different people inside him, who contradict each other and argue about their illness (Anae.).

Head - Acute pain in the temples, as if compressed by an iron helmet. Scalp very painful, cannot tolerate combing. If he moves his head, he hears a rush of water.

Eyes - Eyes look sad. Eyes bloodshot, red, tearful. Conjunctivitis. Blepharitis. Eyelids heavy, burning with need to refresh them.

Ears - Outer ear hot and painful. Auditory canal dry. Discharge of a hot, excoriating serum from the left ear, forming crusts which, when scratched, bleed easily. Acute congestive otitis. Suppurating inflammation of the ear-drum (Sil.). Mastoiditis. Hears well.

Nose - Ozaena. Rhinitis. Sinusitis. Nostrils blocked by crusts. Light nosebleeds. Loss of sense of smell.

Mouth - Tongue pasty, covered with a yellow-white coating. Mouth dry, tongue coated, rough. Breath fetid, putrid, nauseating. Taste of copper in the mouth. Saliva thick and dark yellow. Teeth covered with thick, yellow tartar. Cracks at the corners of the lips. Lips chapped.

Stomach - Acute gastritis. Acridity, bringing up of air and food. Nausea.

Abdomen - Rumbling in the right iliac cavity. Gas difficult to expel. Acute inflammation of the gallbladder and biliary passages. Sub-phrenic abscess. Chronic appendicitis.

Rectum - Involuntary intestinal evacuation and fetid odor. Diarrhea with greenish stools, smelling of sour milk. Perianal burning with anal excoriation and anal trickling. Rectal hemorrhaging.

Male - Prostatic congestion with tenesmus and burning during urination. Prostatic adenoma.

Female - Hemorrhaging endometritis. Menorrhagia or metrorrhagia during the menopause with violent headaches. Uterine cancer. Food - Thirsty for water, which is vomited as soon as it is absorbed. Thirsty for ice-cold water with stomach, as if burning.

Chest - Chest painful. Dyspnea with intercostal pains. Shooting pains in the left intercostal region. Thoracic pains when changing position.

Heart - Pulse violent, full and bounding, resounds in the ear and is annoying. Myocarditis. Pericarditis.

Sleep - Sleepy and in a semi-awake state.

Skin - Petechial exanthema on the backs of the hands. Rheumatoid purpura. Hyperglobulinémie purpura. Infectious purpura. Pressure sores. Copious sweating, especially from the groin and armpits. Sweating with excoriation of the skin which forms wounds.

Modalities - Worse from movement or the slightest effort. Worse left side, but not exclusively.

Kidneys - Acute glomerulonephritis. Involuntary urination. Urine dark, but copious. Hematuria. Dysuria with tenesmus, with involuntary passing of stools. Lungs - Painful cough with great dif ficulty in expectorating and desire to vomit. Bronchial crepitant rales, abundant expectoration, sputum frothy, rusty or blood-streaked. Pleurisy. Bronchial pneumonia. Pneumonia. Abscess on the lung. Pulmonary gangrene.

Temperature - Temperature between 39.5°C and 41 °C. Copious sweating, smelling of curdled milk. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Anae. - Clouded mental state, feels as if he had two opposed wills, headaches, nausea, vomiting, amelioration by eating. (2) Bapt. - Prostration with putrid odor of all discharges. Feeling of painful cracking in the muscles. Putrid smell of breath. Diarrhea is fetid, sometimes involuntary. (3) Anthr. - Septic infections, burning pains, prostration, bleeding from the orifices or black blood, which decomposes rapidly. (4) Ars. - Prostration, agitation, anxiety about death. Burning pains, with burning diarrhea, peri-anal excoriation, oppression, palpitations, worse between midnight and 3 a.m. REFERENCES-Julian.

HOMEOPATHIC - This nosode is prepared from inactivated mumps viruses, which belong to the paramyxovirus grcap and can cause mumps. Parot, has been used as a prophylactic against infection by mumps. The well-known complications which sometimes occur with mumps, ceicbral inflammation and orchitis, suggest its possible use in these conditions. The main indications are painful swellings of the parotid gland, fever, otalgia, difficulty hearing, and sometimes pancreatic involvement. Pancreatic affections. Diseases of the oral mucosa such as stomatitis, tonsillitis. Eustachian catarrh and hearing problems of catarrhal origin. Cryptorchism, benign or malignant tumors of the testes. Fibroma, myoma, lymphangioma, adenomatoid tumors. Teratoma and dermoid cysts. COMMENTS - Mumps is to be distinguished from the parotitis which is seen in scarlet fever, cholera and other infectious diseases, and also from the secondary parotitis, arising from throat infections and diseases of the oral mucosa. Parot, is generally given in the 30c two or three times a day to those exposed to the infection .1 cases of mumps, it may be given every four hours, either by itself or alternated with other indicated remedies. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Merc., Jab., Piloc. REFERENCES - Clarke. Reckeweg.

PHARMACY - parth. Parthenium hysterophorus. Bitter-broom. Congress grass. Escoba amargo. N. O. Composite, Synanthereae, tribe Helianthee. The dry plant is macerated in five parts by weight of alcohol. Trituration of solution of the alkaloid Parthenia. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Cheyne-Stokes breathing. Debility. Dyspepsia. Ear disorders. Fainting. Fevers. Headaches. Liver, pain. Milk increased. Miscarriage. Neuralgia, periodic. Salivation. Spleen, disorders. Toothache. Vision, disordered.

HOMEOPATHIC - ACuban remedy forfevers, especially malarial. An alkaloid, Parthenia, was isolated by C. J. Ulrice of Havana; and Dr. J. '.. Duenas published experiments with this on humans and animals. In the proving, the pains were sudden, congestive, out-pushing. Pains in the head and ears. Singing and fullness in the ears. Heaviness and dullness of head. Tendency to vertigo. Malaise, apathy, lassitude. Stupor, desire to be quiet. Indifference. Profuse and very fluid salivation. Sensation of heat and weight in the stomach. Increased appetite, or refusal of food. Gastric intolerance, nausea and vomiting. Increased flow of milk. Amenorrhea and general debility. Cheyne- Stokes breathing. After-effects of quinine. Antidotal action to quinine. MIND - Feels dull and stupid. Difficult to fix attention. Malaise, apathy, lassitude. Indifference.

Head - Headaches, extending to nose, pain in frontal eminence. Stitching pain in left temple of short duration. Aching pain at left supra-orbital foramen. Pain at root of nose, feels swollen. Heaviness and dullness of head. Full feeling in vertex, pressing from within.

Eyes - Eyes heavy, drowsy. Aching in eyeballs. Aching over eyes, wants to close them. Disordered vision. Must look intently to see the words, when writing the letters seem pale and eye ache.

Ears - Sharp pain in ears. Stabbing pain in left ear. Dullness and aching in ears, coming suddenly. Stitching at lobe of left ear, deep in and above external auditory meatus. Tinnitus, ringing in ears, worse left.

Nose - Pain at root of nose, in nose, in bones of nose, worse left. Stuffed feeling at root of nose, as with dry coryza. Nose feels swollen and tender to touch. Aching in bridge of nose ( worse left side) and of upper left molars. Aching at end of nose, which feels full of blood.

Face - Seems as if bloods would burst through face. Bursting pain in right malar bone. Aching pains run up from above left eye-tooth to eye and over face, occurs by starts and stops.

Mouth - Tingling in tip of tongue. Profuse, very fluid salivation.

Stomach - Emptiness sensation in epigastrium, hunger. Heat and weight in stomach. Irrepressible, tasteless belchings. Belch- ings tasting of the drug.

Abdomen - Spleen disorders. Spleen painful to pressure, pain in right side, worse in some parts than in others, with shiverings. Severe pains in the left hypochondrium with tertian fever. Loud rumbling in bowels, about navel. Slight colicky pains at navel. Colic deep in pelvis, pains run down backs of thighs to knees. Breasts - Great increase of milk in breasts of nursing women.

Rectum - Stabbing pain runs up rectum after passing flatus. No desire at usual time, 10:30 p.m., mushy stool.

Female - Given to pregnant women for fevers, it has caused miscarriages and premature deliveries. In a case of subacute tuberculosis, it restored the menses, which had been absent since the illness commenced.

Heart - Excited heartbeat. Progressive slowness of pulse, followed by syncope, cardiac paralysis and death. Pulse slow, soft compressible.

Limbs - Pains run from pelvis down backs of thighs to knees. Marked diminution of reflex in hips and extinction of voluntary movements. Lungs - Slow, irregular, breathing. Cheyne- Stokes.

Sleep - Restless night, wakes at 3 and 4 a.m., then dozes and dreams until 7:30. Increased stupor, desire to be quiet.

Modalities - Better after rising and walking about. Worse after sleep, from sudden motion.

Teeth - Teeth feel on edge, too long. Aching in teeth. Upper teeth, pricking pains in sockets. Sharp aching twinges in upper molars. Upper incisors tender at sockets when biting.

Kidneys - Kidneys enlarged and congested. Increased urine.

Temperature - Rise and fall of temperature, shivering, diminished perspiration. Vertigo - Vertigo, while sitting with heat of face and blurred vision. COMMENTS - Dr. B. H. B. Sleight proved increasing doses of the tincture and, later on, of 6x, which reproduced most of the symptoms of the first proving. Fornias reported the case of his niece, 5, living in Havana, who had been suffering from a continued fever with periodical midday exacerbations, which later on assumed an intermittent form. She had been saturated with quinine and complained at the time of malaise, lassitude, headache, gastric intolerance, etc. Dr. Govantes prescribed an extract of Parth., three doses a day, each the size of a pea. In four or five days she was free from fever and made a quick recovery. Dr. Ramirez Tovar reported several cures by Parth. The first was a woman living in the lower part of the city, where the rain left channels of infection, who had daily attacks of intermittent, more intense each day. One grain of the alkaloid was divided into six powders, one every hour after the attack. No further attacks. The patient was nursing at the time and she noticed a marked increase of milk in the breasts. Half a grain divided into five doses completed the cure. In the second case, a tailor, 30, moved to a lower part of the city and contracted tertian intermittent, the fourth seizure being attended with much pain in the left hypochondrium. One grain in five doses cured, though the conditions were unchanged. (The removal of this left hypochondriac pain is important in connection with Burnett's experience with Helia.) The third case was a girl, 6, lymphatic, who lived near the harbor, ill for seventeen days with malaise, loss of appetite, sleepiness and fever. She had quinine internally and externally, and was wasting visibly. The alkaloid, aided by a tonic wine prepared from the extract of the plant, cured In his fourth case, Tovar noted a man, 45 of delicate constitution, poorly nourished, straw-yellow face, yellow sclerotics, enlarged liver and spleen, spleen painful to pressure. He had a fever in Panama, had taken quinine, complained of a pain in right side, which commenced 1 p.m. with shiverings, disappeared in two hours and returned at precisely the same hour the next day. Five doses of ten centigrams each removed the pain. About six weeks later there was a relapse, the pain this time being located in the stomach. One grain in five doses, one dose every two hours, removed the pain, but it returned the third day. The same treatment then removed it permanently. The fifth case concerned a young woman, 18, who had periodical facial neuralgia, cured by the same treatment. RELATIONS - It antidotes quinine. Compare: (1) In spleen affections, Helia., Cean. (2) In malaise and periodic neuralgia, Malar. Off., Chin., Cedr. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke.

HERBAL - Passion flower is a climbing plant, leaves cordate, ovate and palmately three lobed. The plant bears solitary, large, and very beautiful flowers, white with a purple center. The edible fruit is a large berry. Passion flower is a safe and Used as a herbal remedy in nervous, irritative, and neuralgic pains with debility, harmless soporific herb that will allay irritation of the brain and central nervous system. It is a nerve sedative, narcotic, antispasmodic. Used in derangements of the nervous system such as insomnia, chorea, convulsions and headache. Nervous headache. Hysteria spasms. Convulsions, especially in those of childhood when it should be given in large doses before the approach of the convulsion. Insomnia from exhaustion and excitement. Wakefulness of infants and elderly people. Produces a restful sleep, the patient awakens refreshed. Hypnotic. Should not be given in insomnia with flushed face and determination of blood to the head.

HOMEOPATHIC - Passi. has not been proved. Hale introduced it to homeopathy, citing a paper by Phares in the New Remedies. Its curative action appears to be a direct kind. Quieting effect on the nervous system, hence an efficient nervine and anti-spasmodic remedy. Excitement with spasms. Hysteria, puerperal convulsions. Convulsions in children with neuralgia. Convulsions of children during teething. Tetanic convulsions affecting mainly the muscles of the trunk, with predominant opisthotonos. Violent tetanus, with opisthotonos, trismus, and convulsions. Tetanus infantum. Neuralgias, internal and of the limbs. Worm fever, teething and spasms. Insomnia of infants and the aged. Sleeplessness, with great restlessness and suicidal mania. Restlessness of fevers. Nervous disorders. General atonic condition. Mentally worried and over-worked persons. Asthma. Whooping cough. Painful diarrhea. Cholera infantum with restlessness. Tedious labor pains when the patient becomes nervous and excitable. Delirium tremens. Alcoholism. Abuse of narcotics. Drug addictions. Breaks off morphine habit (Aven.). MIND - Mentally worried and over-worked. Insomnia of infants and the aged. Sleeplessness, with great restlessness and suicidal mania. Nervous and excitable. Restlessness. Hysteria. Acute mania. Excitement and spasms. Neurosis of children. Alcoholism. Delirium tremens. Drug addictions. Abuse of narcotics. Breaks off morphine habit (Aven.).

Head - Violent ache as if top of head would come off. Top of head seemed to lift off.

Eyes - Sensation that the eyes are being pushed out.

Stomach - Leaden, dead feeling after or between meals, flatulence and sour belchings. COMMENTS - Phares learned its action from W. B. Lindsay, who used it with extraordinary success in tetanus of the newborn. Lindsay commended an aqueous extract of the root as an application for chancre, erysipelas, irritable hemorrhoids and new burns. Phares confirmed the efficacy of Passi. in erysipelas, ulcers, neuralgia and tetanus. He cited the case of an old woman who was seized with convulsions of a tetanic nature as well as the case of his hors, cured by himself and his son, J. H. Phares. One of his own horses was seized with tetanus and all hope of saving him was given up, when Phares gathered some Passi. stems, leaves and flowers. They were pounded, moistened with water, expressed ten or twelve ounces and poured it down the animal's throat through a tube introduced at the side of his mouth. Though not expected to live half an hour, the horse was found grazing the next morning. J. W. Covert reported the case of Mrs. X., 28, who had epileptic convulsions for years from one to twenty fits in a week. The aura was a tight feeling in the chest. By homeopathic treatment, Covert succeeded in diminishing the frequency of the attacks, but they would invariably return at the menstrual period. Passi. tincture 6 drops, six times a day, was given. The next period passed without a convulsion, but the patient had a violent headache as if the top of the head would come off. This was rapidly controlled by Glon. 6c. The three following period passed without any attack. Farrington considered Passi. suited especially to tetanus of hot countries and referred to two cures by Archibald Bayne of Barbados with the tincture and lx. It has also been used in convulsions of children and other complaints of dentition, and even in epilepsy. E. S. Prindle related a case of delirium tremens. A German, driver of a beer wagon, was laid up with a broken arm when he was seized with delirium tremens of a most ferocious type, which the usual remedies entirely failed to control. Passi. succuss was then given, two drachms every half-hour. After the third dose the patient quieted down and slept three hours. On waking, he again began to rave, but not as badly as before. Another teaspoonful of Passi. put him to sleep and the next morning he was quite sane and allowed his arm to be reset. G. C. Buchanan observed some curious effects in a patient, Mrs. V., to whom he gave teaspoonful doses for neuralgia, sleeplessness and nervousness. “Her eyes seemed to push out of her head and lie on the quilt, her heels seemed to be up in air top of her head seemed to lift off.” To the observer, the eyes seemed to protrude. Later a severe attack of hemorrhoids developed. The dose was reduced to halfteaspoonfuls, which produced sleep and caused no ill effects. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Valer., Cypr. (2) In tetanus and epilepsy, Oena., Nux-v. (2) Heels seem to go up, Ph-ac. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Rectum - Severe attack of hemorrhoids. Irritable hemorrhoids.

Female - Painful menses, dysmenorrhea.

Back - Pain in coccyx.

Limbs - Sensation that her heels are up in the air. Lungs - Nocturnal cough.

Sleep - Restless and wakeful, resulting from exhaustion. Insomnia with tendency to convulsions. Insomnia in screaming children, of infants, the aged, the mentally worried and overworked. Sleeplessness in alcoholics. Sleeplessness with delirium.

Skin - Chancre. Erysipelas.

full:
PHARMACY - pear. Pearl. Oyster Pearl. Aragonite, about 82-86%; conchiolin, 10-14%; and water. 2%. Pearls are calcified objects made by oysters and are usually pale white or cream colored, though darker blue, gray, and even black variations exist. Layers of aragonite, known as nacre, are secreted around the irritant and gradually build up to form the solid pearl . Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Arthritis. Breasts, disorders. Coughs. Headaches. Hypertension. Infertility. Tuberculosis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Soothing influence. Enhances curative powers. Promotes body fluids and the blood, nourishing the body tissues and the nerves. Said to lessen stress and related maladies (hypertension, headaches, and exhaustion), which may help prevent heart attacks and strokes. Pearls supposedly aid in digestion and may reduce the chance of developing ulcers. Strengthens the female reproductive system, improves fertility, and calms the emotions. A good pearl (not pierced) triturated in rose or kewra water, made into paste, dried and taken orally, is very beneficial for diseases caused by calcium deficiency. The ashes provide relief to body heat, are good for the eyes. Cures tuberculosis, chronic fevers, cough, breathing problems, palpitations, high blood pressure, heart ailments, exhaustion and weaknesses. MIND - Pearl increases emotional stability, mental strength, friendliness and contentment. Weakness or afflictions are shown by anxiety, mental and emotional swings, worry, isolation or the inability to cope with relationships and people. COMMENTS -The Arabs called pearls “tears of the gods,” and said they were formed by drops of rain falling into oyster shells. The Chinese, regard pearls as the hidden soul of the oyster. “Margarithe,” another name for this gem, means “child of light.” It has become a symbol of purity and virtue. Pearls were essential toiletry articles, used to clean face and teeth. Applying the oyster shell containing a pearl to the affected area was said to heal leprosy and other skin diseases. The gem was considered beneficial for easing indigestion, curing hemorrhoids, and counteracting poison. Taken in milk, they were used to cure ulcers. Nursing women took pearl concoctions to make their milk healthy and plentiful. 6 grains in water sweetened with manna (ash tree sap) was said to ward off the plague. Burnt pearl powder drunk in water stopped hemorrhages; inhaled, it cured headache. Oil of pearls was believed to fortify the nerves. A pearl tonic can be made to increase vitality, relieve eye strain, and soothe burning urination; place several small pearls in water overnight and drink the water following day. The tonic is a natural antacid and anti-inflammatory. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Calc., Luna, Arg-n. REFERENCES - Murphy.

Pulse very quick and wiry. Fullness of the head. Cough worse after 6 p.m., at night. COMMENTS - T. Franklin Smith reported a case of humid asthma, with quick, labored breathing, cannot lie flat or on left side. Constriction of chest, especially right side. Cured quickly and permanently with Pect. 1,000c and 100,000c potencies. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

HERBAL - The seeds of this Middle-Eastern shrub have a long history of medical and psychoactive use. Widely known and used in its native areas, the seeds yield a dye (“Turkish” or “Syrian” red) long used in “Persian” carpets. The seeds and roots contain b-carboline alkaloids, mostly harmine, as well as harmaline, harmalol, etc. Egyptian studies found the extract to be markedly fungicidal and bactericidal, mostly due to harmine. It is reported to be used as an incense and spice, and as an abortificant, narcotic, aphrodisiac, stimulant, sedative, emmenagogue, emetic, vermifuge, or soporific. Consumption of the seed in quantity induces a sense of euphoria and releases inhibitions. It has been used in the past as a “truth drug.” The seed has also been used as an anthelmintic in order to rid the body of tapeworms. Harmine, which is being used in research into mental disease, encephalitis and inflammation of the brain. Small quantities stimulate the brain and are said to be therapeutic, but in excess, harmine depresses the central nervous system. A crude preparation of the seed is more effective than an extract because of the presence of related indoles. The seed is used externally in the treatment of hemorrhoids and baldness. The oil obtained from the seed is said to be aphrodisiac, and to have galactagogue, ophthalmic, soporific and vermifuge properties. The root has been used as a parasiticide in order to kill body lice, and used internally in the treatment of rheumatism and nervous conditions. A decoction of the leaves is used in the treatment of rheumatism. This remedy should be used with caution, and preferably under the guidance of a qualified practitioner, since excessive doses cause vomiting and hallucinations.

HOMEOPATHIC - Peg-h. has been reported to be used in India for syphilis, fever in North Africa, and elsewhere for fever, hysteria, malaria, neuralgia, parkinsonism, prolapse of the womb, rheumatism, colic, asthma, and eye complaints. The fruit and seed are digestive, diuretic, hallucinogenic, narcotic and uterine stimulants. They are taken internally in the treatment of stomach complaints, urinary and sexual disorders, epilepsy, menstrual problems, mental and nervous illnesses. MIND - Excitement. Euphoria. Indifference. Sadness. Ailments from grief. Irritability. Anger. Desire to curse, fight, to strike others, to break things, to kill, to die. Hatred of close relatives, parents. Delusion of belonging to the opposite sex. Confusion as to their sexual identity. Delusion ofbeing surrounded by vampires. Delusion that he is a vampire. HERBAL - Pelarg. is a Kafir remedy for dysentery. The root is cut up finely or bruised, and then boiled in milk for a considerable time. Many British soldiers were cured of dysentery with it in the Boer War. Pelarg. was also used for purging in horses. When a horse was attacked during a journey the root (which is very thick) was wrapped up and tied to the bit. The juice mingled with the saliva and was swallowed. REFERENCES - Clarke.
