PHARMACY - phyt. Phytolacca decandra. Poke root. Poke weed. Virginian Poke. Pole-root. Red ink plant. Garget weed. N. O. Phytolaccaceae. Tincture of fresh root dug in winter. Tincture of the ripe berries. Tincture of fresh leaves. Solution of the resinous extract, Phytolaccin. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Adenitis. Albuminuria. Angina pectoris. Anus, fissure. Asthma. Barber's itch. Boils. Bone, diseases. Breasts, disorders. Breast-feeding. Breasts, tumors. Cancer. Cholera. Ciliary, neuralgia. Colic. Conjunctivitis. Constipation. Cough. Dentition, difficult. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Diplopia. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Ears, disorders. Erythema nodosum. Eustachian tubes disorders. Galactorrhea. Gland, disorders. Glands, enlarged. Glossitis. Gonorrhea. Gout. Headaches. Hearing, disorders. Heart, disorders. Hepatitis. Hemorrhoids. Impotence. Influenza. Laryngismus. Leucorrhea. Lichen. Liver, disorders. Lumbago. Lupus. Mastitis. Mercury, effects. Miscarriage, threatened. Mouth, ulcerated. Mumps. Nephritis. Neuralgia. Nipples, painful Nursing, painful. Obesity. Orchitis. Ozaena. Paralysis, diphtheria. Parotiditis. Prostate, disorders. Rectum, cancer. Respiration, abnormal. Rheumatism. Ringworm. Rodent, ulcer. Salivation. Scabies. Scar. Sciatica. Sewer-gas poisoning. Spinal, irritation. Spleen, pain. Stiff-neck. Syphilis. Tetanus. Throat, sore. Tinea capitis. Tonsillitis. Toothaches. Tumors. Ulcers. Uterus disorders. Venereal buboes. Warts. Wens.

HERBAL - Phytolacca is a branching herbaceous plant with a thick, perennial root, sometimes larger than a man's leg in diameter. The plant is common throughout North America, the Azores, North Africa and China. It grows in damp places. The young shoots, though extremely acrid, are rendered harmless by boiling and are eaten like asparagus in the United States. The berries have a popular repute as a remedy for cancer and rheumatism. The berries of Phytolacca octandra are used in Mexico and the West Indies as a soap. According to Raffinesque, the ash of the plant is 45 percent caustic potash, and the plant contains an acid, phytolactic acid, which is closely allied to malic acid. Phytolacca has been used as an escharotic in cancers, ulcers, etc.

HOMEOPATHIC - Phyt. is pre-eminently a glandular and rheumatic remedy. It powerfully affects the fibrous and osseous tissues, and the sheathes and fascias of muscles. Hence it becomes an admirable remedy in rheumatic affections. It has a special affinity for the muscles of the shoulders and arms. Acts on the muscles of the neck and back, tendons and joints, periosteum, throat, digestive tract and the right side. General soreness over the whole body, the patient moans and groans every time he moves. Lameness, soreness and a bruised feeling are felt all over the body. It combines with the pain, intense prostration and great exhaustion. Rheumatic pain, tendency to affect the outer aspect of limbs. Sudden achiness. Pains come and go suddenly, change places. Sore, hard aching pains. The pain occurs in such quick succession that it renders the leg powerless numb and heavy. Each movement elicits groans. Spreading pains. Rheumatism after tonsillitis. Lassitude with rheumatism, makes him lie down every now and then. Sciatica and hip joint disease, with pain shooting from sacrum down the outer aspect of thighs to knees and toes. Syphilitic bone pains, chronic rheumatism. Glandular swellings with heat and inflammation, particularly breasts and tonsils. Hard and painful nodes. Acts on scar tissue. Hastens suppuration. Pus is watery, fetid, ichorous. Discharges are shreddy, stringy, stools, menses etc. Affinity for the breasts and glands of women, which are prone to become cancerous in those of a cancer constitution. Breast cancer, as well as cancers of the uterus and rectum. Mastitis, breast disorders . Pressure with hand ameliorates pain in breasts. Great sensitivity in breasts. Sore throat, quinsy and diphtheria. Sore throats, right-sided, relieved by swallowing cold drinks, worse from warm drinks and empty swallowing. Enlarged and painful cervical glands accompany the inflamed sore throats. Bluish-red parts, throat glands. Burning pains in cancerous ulcerations and in inflamed throats. Restlessness and prostration. Tetanus, general muscular rigidity, alternate spasms and relaxation of muscles. Opisthotonos. Decrease of weight. Obesity. Retarded dentition. MIND - Irritable and nervous. Restlessness. Indisposition to mental exertion. Disgustfor business. Feels faint on rising. Stupefaction with vertigo and dimness of vision. Refuses food in spite of continuous insistence. Irresistible compulsion to clench the teeth. Melancholy, gloom, indifference to life. Depression of spirits with headache. Weeping at night during menses. Great fear, sure she will die. Predicts death, with mastitis. Desires death in morning on waking. Confusion while sitting, better open air. Delirium. Loss of personal delicacy, complete shamelessness and indifference to exposure of her person. Oversensitiveness to pain. Cannot endure pain, it is intolerable. Unconsciousness from pain.

Head - Pain from frontal region backwards. Pressure in temples and over eyes. Brain feels sore, head as if beaten. Violent headache, with stupid expression of face and enlarged pupils. Headache with vertigo and dim vision. Nausea and headache better eating, but returns soon with vomiting. Rheumatism of scalp, pains come on every time it rains. Cold sweat on forehead. Scaly eruption on scalp. Tinea capitis.

Eyes - Dull aching in eyes, worse motion, light or exercise. Orbital cellulitis. Burning, smarting, tingling in eyes. Feeling of sand under lids. Profuse hot lachrymation. Fistula lachrymalis (Fl-ac.). Lids agglutinated and edematous. Lids as if on fire. Tarsal edges feel hot. Photophobia. Green vision. Eyeballs ache on reading and writing. Diplopia. Motion of one eye only, independent of the other.

Ears - Shooting pains in both the ears, worse swallowing. Obstruction in left Eustachian tube. Irritation in one Eustachian tube. Increased sense of hearing with pain in forehead.

Nose - Coryza with lachrymation and photophobia. Acrid coryza. Coryza, flow of mucus from one nostril and from posteriorsinuses. Thin watery discharge from nose. Feels congested and heavy. Pain at root of nose, with stoppage. Obstruction of nose while riding. Mucus hangs down in strings from posterior nares, hawked with difficulty. Cancerous affection of nose, lupus.

Face - Face very pale, hippocratic. Yellowish, sickly. Blotches in face, worse evening, after washing and eating. Blueness around eyes. Chin drawn closely to sternum. Glands swollen at the angle of jaw. Jaws ache, as in mumps. Aching malar bones. Mumps. Tension and pressure in parotid gland.

Mouth - Dry sensation in mouth, from cough. Metallic taste in mouth. Much stringy saliva. Profuse saliva, sometimes yellowish, often thick, ropy, tenacious. Bleeding from mouth. Very painful small ulcers on side of cheek, cannot chew on that side. Jaws firmly set, chin drawn down on sternum. Ulcers on lips. Upper lip excoriated. Lower lip drawn down. Lips everted and firm.

Throat - Aphonia. Dark red or bluish red. Much pain at root of tongue, soft palate and tonsils swollen. Sensation of a lump in throat (Bell., Lach.). Throat feels rough, narrow, hot. Ulcerated sore throat and diphtheria, throat feels very hot, pain at root of tongue extending to ear. Pseudo-membranous exudation, grayish- white, thick, tenacious yellowish mucus. Shooting pain into ears on swallowing. Cannot swallow anything hot (Lach.). Tension and pressure in parotid gland. Tonsils swollen, especially right, dark- Phytolacca decandra red appearance. Tonsillitis with fauces swollen with burning pain, cannot swallow even water. Uvula large, dropsical. Follicular pharyngitis.

Stomach - Hunger soon after eating. Heat in stomach. Stomach cramps and coldness. Pain in region of pylorus. Pains, worse deep breathing. Nausea, eructations of flatus and sour fluids, with severe pain in umbilical region. Easy vomiting without nausea. Violent vomiting with retching, desires death to relieve vomiting. Vomiting of clotted blood and mucus. Vomiting and diarrhea, with griping pains and cramps in abdomen.

Abdomen - Great rumbling in abdomen and pain in umbilicus. Heavy aching pain in the hypochondrium, worse lying on affected side. Sore spot in right hypochondrium. Soreness and pain in right hypochondrium during pregnancy. Rheumatism of abdominal muscles. Bruised feeling through the epigastrium and abdomen. Colic at navel, with burning griping pains. Bearing down pains. Intense vomiting and purging with griping pains and cramps in abdomen. Ulceration of mucus membrane of upper part of digestive tract.

Rectum - Continuous urging to stools, even in sleep. Constipation of the aged and those with weak heart. Diarrhea after lemonade. Dysentery, passage only of mucus and blood or like scraping from the intestines. Stools thin, dark brown. Bloody discharges with heat in rectum. Bleeding from rectum. Bleeding hemorrhoids. Fissures of anus. Cancer of rectum. Sensations - Brain as if bruised. Right side of head as if pressed firmly. As if sand in eyes. As if eyes too large. As if lids granulated. As if tarsal edges raw. As if lids on fire. As if lump in throat. As if apple core in throat. Throat so full it felt choked. Pharynx feels like a cavern, chest as if it were a big empty cask. Body as if bruised, pounded all over. As if joint were being chopped with an ax.

Male - Shooting along perineum to penis. Painful induration of the testicles. Orchitis, acute and chronic, with suppuration and fistulous ulcer. Spermatic cord sore. Gonorrhea and gleet. Venereal buboes. Ulcers on genitals. Impotency.

Female - Amenorrhea, with ovarian irritation or disease. Menses too copious and frequent, followed by leucorrhea. Menses with salivation and lachrymation. Dysmenorrhea in barren women with erosion of cervix membranous. Leucorrhea, thick, tenacious and irritating. Leucorrhea profuse, thick, tenacious. Ovarian neural- gia of right side. Ovaritis with rheumatic complications. Venereal buboes. Swollen nabothian cysts. Glandular swellings and abscesses. Suppression of lochia. Food - Intense thirst. Hunger, soon after eating. Loss of appetite. Can't swallow any hot food ordrinks (Lach.), causes choking. Diarrhea after lemonade. Vomiting of food and milk, in teething children. Glands - Swelling and induration of glands. Swollen glands and burning pains, worse at night. Glands swollen at the angle of jaw. Glandular abscesses. Venereal buboes. Hardness of glands in right side of neck. Swelling of axillary glands.

Chest - Aching pains in chest, through mid-sternum with cough. Rheumatism of lower intercostals, from exposure to cold and dampness. Tenderness and lameness of muscles of chest, as if bruised. Swelling of axillary glands. Constitutions - Suited to rheumatic or syphilitic subjects, sensitive to damp weather. Cancer constitution.

Heart - Feeling as if heart leaped into throat (Podo.). Pains in region of heart, worse walking. Shock of pain in cardiac region alternating with pain in right arm. Fatty heart. Small, irregular pulse with great excitement in cardiac region.

Back - Pains streaking up and down the spine. Back stiff, especially in morning on rising and during damp weather. Aching pain in lumbar and sacral region. Shooting pain in sacrum. Weakness and dull pain in region of kidneys. Hardness of glands in right side of neck. Neck stiff in morning on waking. Pale red spots on neck and arms. Both scapulae ache continually. Breasts - Heavy, stony, hard swollen or tender breasts. Severe stinging pains, throughout breasts, with oozing out of milk, better pressure with hands. Swollen breast. Irritable breasts, before and during menses. Tender and sore breasts, before and during menses. Mastitis, with breasts hard and very sensitive. Mastitis from taking cold. Mastitis during pregnancy. Galactorrhea (Calc.), causes great exhaustion. When child nurses, pain goes from nipple all over body. Milk thick, scanty and unhealthy, dries up too soon. Breast hard as a stone, after weaning. Cracks and small ulcers about nipples. Nipples, cracked, very sensitive inverted. Tumors or hard nodes of the breasts with enlarged axillary glands. Breast is hard, painful and of purple hue. Breast cancer, with shooting, lancinating pains, great exhaustion and prostration. Breast abscess. Bloody, watery discharge from breasts. Affection of old scars in breasts. Causations - Emotions, grief, injuries, blows, bathing, and exposure to cold, damp weather.

Limbs - Rheumatic pains, worse in morning. Syphilitic sciatica. Pains fly like electric shocks, shooting, lancinating, shifting rapidly (Puls., Kali-bi.). Wandering pains passing from one joint and place to another, with swelling and redness. Muscular soreness all over. Shooting pain in right shoulder with stiffness and inability to raise arm. Painful, hard, shiny swelling of finger joints. Pain in hips and thighs on change of weather. Sharp cutting, drawing pains in the hip, legs drawn up, cannot touch floor. Pain in legs, patient dreads to get up. Aching of heels, re lie ved by elevating feet. Feet puffed, pain in ankles and feet. Neuralgia in toes. Cold hands and feet.

Sleep - Frequent yawning and drowsiness. Restlessness at night. Pains drive him out of bed. On awaking, feels wretched.

Skin - Dry, harsh, shriveled. Skin becomes dry, shrunken, pale. Itching. Papular and pustular lesions. Erythematous blotches, irregular, slightly raised, pale red, ending in dark red or purple spots. Disposition to boils and carbuncles, with swollen glands and burning pains, worse at night. Painful boils on back and behind ears. Squamous eruptions. Syphilitic eruptions. Swelling and induration of glands. Scarlatina-like rash. Warts and moles. Lipoma. Corns. Barber’s itch. Lipoma. Pityriasis. Ringworm. Ulcer, chronic, surrounded by boils. Cancerous ulcers.

Modalities - Better warmth, dry weather. Better from lying on abdomen or left side, lying on stomach, rest. Rubbing Phytolacca decandra ameliorates pain in hip. Pressure on trachea facilitates expectoration. Sensitive to electric changes. Worse exposure to damp, cold weather, rain, cold night, changes of weather, washing, heat. Worse movement, raising up, stepping down from high step, right side, from touch, during menses. Worse from swallowing, particularly hot drinks. Pressure aggravates pain in joints and ulcers. Riding aggravates nose and breathing.

Teeth - Difficult dentition, better biting on something hard. Teething children with irresistible desire to bite the teeth together. Teeth and jaws clenched. Teeth feel sore and elongated. Inflamed gums and teeth, with mercurial ptyalism.

Tongue - Tongue thickly coated, yellow at base, fiery red at tip. Tongue mapped, indented, fissured, with yellow patch down center. Tongue feels rough and scalded, burnt on back of tongue. Pains at root. Tongue protruded. Vertigo - Vertigo on rising, feels faint. Vertigo, staggering with danger of falling. Vertigo with dim vision. COMMENTS - Closely related to Merc, and Kali-i., especially in syphilitic rheumatism. General action of tissue absorption, especially new growths. Tumors and indurations of the glands. Muscles, joints, bones, brain and spinal cord, as well as the special senses, were all more or less disordered. In cases of poisoning, the most common symptoms were vomiting, diarrhea, frontal headache and a sore throat. Irritation of the eyes, nose and throat, a severe headache and diarrhea have occurred after inhaling the dust of the powdered dried root, or from the odor of the fresh root when it is sliced. Phyt. has caused convulsive symptoms, vomiting and vomiting of worms when given to animals. Wild pigeons and other birds that eat the berries acquire a red color and lose fat. This observation has led to the use of a tincture of Phyt. berries as an anti-fat remedy, and successful results have been reported. Hale tells us that among American dairymen the root is used to regulate any abnormality in cows' milk, whether it is scanty, thick, watery, curdy, or containing blood or pus. Its chief repute is for caked udders. One boy, who drank two or three drachms of a tincture of the root, developed complete tetanus in which his limbs were stiff, hands firmly shut, feet extended toes flexed, lower lids drawn down, teeth clenched, lips everted and firm, general opisthotonos. Respiration was difficult, rales were heard all over the room. For an hour muscular rigidity increased with convulsive action of muscles of face and neck, chin drawn close on sternum. This condition lasted five or ten minutes, followed by perfect relaxation and return in twenty minutes more with the same violence. After cold-water infusion, cupping, and mustard plasters, the boy slept about twenty-five minutes. On waking he had some twitchings, especially of lower limbs, pain in back of head and stomach. The next day he was quite recovered. A boy, 8, who ate a quantity of the berries, was found in great agony, complaining that his stomach was “inched together.” He had nausea, violent vomiting, his throat was sore and dry, fauces dark red, tonsils swollen. After his vomiting ceased, purging set in, stools dark brown and thin, severe pain in stomach on pressure, extorting a cry. Later he had burning griping in umbilical region, dim vision, tongue coated white, and spasmodic jerkings in his arms and legs. In a woman, 45, who took Phyt. as a “blood purifier,” a general rash in appearance not unlike the rash of secondary syphilis was set up. A family of four was poisoned by eating the root with their food by mistake. They had a dread of movement. Seemed stupid, fell asleep after a paroxysm of cramping pain had ceased. Pain in the forehead, worse after eating. Vomited clotted blood and slime. Copious discharge of blood and mucus that looked like scrapings of the intestines. Involuntary stools from straining, which occurred even in sleep. In the mother of the family, who was seven months pregnant, it nearly produced miscarriage. The uterus could be felt contracting under the hand, and there was involuntary straining and hemorrhage from the vagina. Intense griping pain in small of back and cramps in legs coming and going suddenly. Coldness and withered appearance of limbs, the whole body cold. Phyt., used externally, produces good results in cases of ulceration. Clarke found that a gargle of a few drops of the tincture in a tumbler of water was useful in many throat cases. Hundall successfully used a preparation of the leaves as an external application for cancerous growths in dogs. An ointment prepared with a strong tincture of the leave, as well as the juice of the leaves, has been used for malignant ulcers in humans. A case of cancer of the rectum was cured with Phyt. 3x. Nash removed many breast tumors by giving a single dose of Phyt. 100,000c during the wane of the moon. The tincture may take away nondescript lumps in the breast when there are few symptoms. Breast cancer, especially with axillary involvement, especially right sided. Breast cancer that suppurates with horrible burning pains in the breasts. Advanced cases of cancer or tumors. Hard nodules with a bluish appearance and enlarged axillary glands. Scirrhus tumors, hard like cement (Con.). Scars of the breast, cicatrix (Graph., Sil.). Sharp pain from the breast. Breast neuralgias, painful nerve irritation. Swollen glands, indurated (Brom.). Paget's disease of the breast. Breast induration and abscesses in nursing women. Mastitis with a hot, painful, congested and sensitive breast, worse cold and damp. Breasts are hard and lumpy, heavy with mastitis (Bry.). Cracks and fissures in the nipples. Blocked ducts in the breast. Problems with nursing, if the milk dries up, bad milk, thick or lumpy milk. Painful, sore nipples in nursing women. Pain radiates all over the body when the child is put to the breast. Rheumatic swellings are hard, tender and intensely hot. Arthritis, particularly of the shoulder (Rhus-t.), the joints swell before a storm or when damp. Worse at night, change of weather. Wandering pains, migratory arthritis. Sciatica with sharp, cutting pains in the hip and down the thigh. Stiff neck. Generally swollen, stiff and sore, worse on the right side. Electric shocks, sharp pain in the joints with the stiffness (Ruta.). Very restless, but worse from motion. The tendons feel too short (Ruta.). When pain in intestines disappears, pain in limbs comes on. Pain leaves heart and appears in right arm. Pains in head and chest go from before backward. Pains run down spine from nape, from sacrum down outer aspect of thighs to toes. The outer aspects of the limbs are chiefly affected. Frontal headaches, pressive, involving the eyes, worse right side. Headache associated with increased sense of hearing. Apathetic, gloomy. Restless with a fear of dying (Ars.). Generally self-centered (Ars.). Nervous irritability. Disorders of dentition. Teething, better pressure. Teething with bad breath and sores in the mouth. Irresistible inclination to bite the teeth or gums together. Toothache with digging in pain, shooting pain. Sensation as if the teeth are too long. Jaw problems, with or without swollen glands. The tongue feels burnt and rough, may be blistered, with a red tip (Rhus-t.). Influenza with general body ache, back pain and wandering joint pains. Swollen, tender glands with throat symptoms. Stiffness. Bone ache. Fevers with pain and vertigo (Gels.). Apathetic, internal shivering (Gels.). Feels sore and bruised (Bapt., Eup., Arn.). Delirium. Diphtheria (Lac-c.). Sore throat, strep throat, tonsillitis. Burning in the throat with a stiff neck (Rhus-t.), worse from warmth. Dry, raw, rough sore throats. Throat appears dark and purplish. Very swollen and tender glands, particularly on right side of the throat. Great pain at root of tongue when swallowing, pains shooting from throat into ears on swallowing, worse on right side. Hot feeling as if a red-hot ball in throat, burning worse by hot drinks. As if a red-hot iron in the throat (Kali-c., in the rectum; Alum., in the spine). Throat feels plugged (Caust.). Dark redness of fauces. White or gray patches on the tonsils, with offensive breath. Tonsils may appear ulcerated, with crypts. Tenacious, thick mucus in the throat, especially in the morning. Burning of the tongue. Ulcers of the mouth. The Eclectics gave the expressed juice of the berries in “spasmodic or membranous croup or diphtheria.” Clarke used Phyt. 30c for the so-called “diphtheria sore throat.” With the throat symptoms there are generally headache, backache, wandering rheumatic pains and fever. Nash relieved chronic follicular pharyngitis in public speakers when there was much burning, as if a hot substance in throat. Rapid and profound prostration. Diphtheriaparalysis. Faint and dizzy when standing. Soreness of the muscles. Restlessness, but he fears to move because motion worse the pains. Stiff neck, especially right side. Angina. Sense of constriction in the chest. Radiating pains down the right arm (Lil-t.). Heart palpitations followed by severe aching down the right arm. Sensation of the heart beating in the throat. The right side is most affected. Many symptoms were experienced in the liver and the spleen. Liver pains were worse lying on right (painful) side. The spleen pain was better lying on left (painful) side. Hepatitis with an enlarged, indurated liver. Sensation in the stomach as if something is being pinched with violent vomiting attacks and pains in the pit of the stomach. Colic during teething, clenching their teeth with severe stomach or abdominal cramps, diarrhea. One characteristic pain, noted in a case of constipation, is a shooting pain from anus to lower part of rectum, along perineum to middle of penis. “Gurgling sensation in the prostate gland, repeatedly in the afternoon,” was noted by one prover along with pains in spermatic cords. Suspension of sexual appetite with relaxation of the genitals. Syphilis, with bone pains, ulcers on the genitals and sore throats, worse at night. Discharges are tough, stringy, difficult to detach. Generally offensive and acrid. Clinkers. Shreddy discharge in certain forms of intestinal catarrh and dysmenorrhea. Hemorrhagic and hemorrhoidal, acting strongly on rectum and anus, curing tenesmus, bloody discharges and heat. Psoriasis, ringworm and barber's itch. Chronic eczematous eruptions of the face. Old scars that never heal, and when the weather changes the scars flare up and become painful (Graph.). RELATIONS-Antidotes: Milk and salt, Bell., Mez. Compare: (1) Tincture of Phyt. berry - sore throats and in the treatment of obesity. (2) Bry., Rhus-t., Kali-hp., Merc., Sang., Arum-t. Inimical: Merc. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Liver - Chronic hepatitis (Chin., Phos.), with enlargement and induration of liver. Lungs - Difficult breathing. Pains and suffocating feeling in throat and lungs. Panting breathing. Hoarseness. Paroxysmal cough and very profuse and exhausting expectoration of thick starch-like mucus. Dry hacking, tickling cough, worse at night (Menth., Bell.). Cough with burning in trachea. Cough as soon as he lies down. Cough with pain in chest and side. Croupy cough, with burning in larynx and trachea, worse night and in cold, damp weather. Chronic cough, generally hard and dry. Thick, tough expectoration. Thick expectoration, starch- like mucus, profuse and exhausting. Copious, yellow mucus.

Kidneys - Dull and sore pains in kidneys. Pains in kidney region, with scanty, suppressed urine. Hard aching pain in kidney with scanty urine. Nephritis. Urine coffee-colored. Dark red urine, chalky sediment. Urine stains the clothes yellow. Albuminuria after diphtheria, scarlatina. Copious nocturnal urination.

Temperature - Chills at night and every morning. Cold hands and feet. High fever, alternating with chilliness and great prostration. Mastitis. Mumps.

full:
PHARMACY - pic-ac. Picricum acidum. Picric acid. Picronitricum acidum. Trinitrophenolum. Carbazotic acid. Tri-nitro-carbolic acid. Trituration. Solution in rectified spirit. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne. Anemia. Backaches. Bedwetting. Boils. Brain, pain. Brain-fag. Burns. Cachexia. Cancer. Condylomata. Conjunctivitis. Deafness. Debility. Dementia. Diabetes. Ears, boils. Emissions. Erythema. Hands, sweat. Headaches. Hemiplegia. Hemoglobinuria. Jaundice. Leucorrhea. Leukocythemia. Liver, congestion. Locomotor. ataxia. Masturbation. Memory, weakness. Myelitis. Neurasthenia. Nosebleeds. Otitis. Ovary, pain. Paralysis. Paraplegia. Pernicious, anemia. Priapism. Pruritus, vulvae. Sexual, mania. Spinal, exhaustion. Spinal, irritation. Spinal, sclerosis. Styes. Sycosis. Uremia. Urine, bloody. Writer's cramp.

HOMEOPATHIC - Pic-ac. was discovered by Hausman in 1788. It is formed by the action of nitric acid on carbolic acid, salicin, silk and many other substances. Pic-ac. and its compounds are among the most powerful explosives known, lydite being an example. Picric acid crystallizes in bright yellow needles or scales of very bitter taste, sparingly soluble in water. The yellow color is imparted to the eyes and skins of patients who take it in the crude, and it not only produces a semblance of jaundice, but actually disorganizes the liver if pushed. Acts upon the brain, spinal cord, lumbar region, occiput, kidneys and sexual organs. Weakness, heavy, tired feeling in body and mind. It causes degeneration of the spinal cord with paralysis. It acts upon the generative organs probably through the lumbar centers of the spinal cord. Occipital and bursting headaches (Glon.). The headache, frontal or occipital is worse on any attempt to use the mind and it may extend down the spine. Headache extending from the top of the spine up over the head to the eyes. Neurasthenia (Ox-ac.). Worn out persons, mentally and physically. Cachexia. Progressive, pernicious anemia. Prostration, weakness and pain of back. Muscular debility. Heavy tired feeling. Numbness. Formication. Pins and needle sensation in limbs. Burning in many parts, along spine in legs. Sallow complexion. Uremia with complete anuria. Brain-fatigue and sexual excitement. Degeneration of the spinal cord with paralysis. Myelitis with spasms and prostration. Acute ascending paralysis. Typist's or writer's palsy. Thery of Paris accidentally discovered in Pic-ac. solution a remedy for burns. He twice dropped burning matter on his hands while working with a Pic-ac. disinfectant and was astonished at the absence of pain or injury. From that date Pic-ac. became his principal remedy for burns and though others have complained that it caused violent pains, Thery has only once in some thousands of cases had to abandon its use on that account. A one percent solution applied on lint is the best application for burns until granulations begin to form. MIND - Anxiety. Dread offailure at examination. Mental weakness after prolonged strain and anxiety. Memory, weakness. Forgetfulness. Mental exertion aggravates. Mental prostration after reading a little, worse after writing a little. Inability to collect thoughts or to study. Brain-fag. Inability to exert the mind, talk or think. Lack of willpower, disinclined to work. Aversion to talking or movement, during headache. Sits still and listless, does not take interest in surroundings. Cerebral softening. Dementia with prostration, sits still and listens. In women, although enjoying the society of men, idea of marriage unendurable. Lascivious thoughts in presence of any woman. Lewdness. Delusion that parts of body enlarged. As if stairs or ground coming up to meet him.

Head - Headaches, relieved by bandaging tightly. Headache, worse mental exertion, better nosebleed. Headache, worse with sexual excitement and violent erections. Headache during daytime better in sleep. Headache of businessmen, teachers and students from grief and other depressing emotions. Brain-fag. Occipital pain, worse slightest mental exertion. Heavy Picricum acidum occiput, down spine and lower limbs.

Eyes - Pupils dilated. Eyes yellow. Catarrhal conjunctivitis with copious, thick yellow discharge. Lachrymation. Styes with a sore pain.

Ears - Boils within ears and back of neck. Painful boils in meatus. Puffy and burning sensation in ears. Buzzing and hissing in ears. Noises in ears with vertigo and headache at the base of brain. Chronic deafness.

Nose - Boil in left nostril. Stinging on right side of nose. Acne. Nose full of mucus, can breathe only through mouth, better open air.

Mouth - Bitter taste with thirst. White, frothy saliva hang in strings to the floor.

Throat - Redness of throat with raw, scraped, stiff and hot feeling. Soreness back of and above soft palate with debility. Dry and husky. Vertigo - Vertigo and noises in ear. COMMENTS - Grimmer said this remedy's sphere of action centers in the brain, spinal cord and the bloodstream. It produce in the provings a marked cachexia and pernicious anemia and these conditions in the sick have many times been cured. In some experiments by Parisel, symptoms were observed including buzzing and whistling in ears, sparks, whirling around of objects, heaviness of head alternately with sense of emptiness. Copious, oily-looking, yellowish stool with amelioration of cerebral symptoms. Pulse slow, small, very feeble. Great weakness, compelling to lie down, limbs hardly able to stir themselves, no anxiety, profound calm. Vivid coloration of sclerotics and tissues, urine colored blood-red. These were effects of 0.5 grains doses. Slow poisoning set up an intermittent fever of quotidian type and “anorexia, thirst often sweat, cancerous tint about skin, tendency to cachexia.” These observations give the chief features of the remedy's action: fatigue, mental and bodily, symptoms worse by least exertion, fatigue going into actual paralysis, brain fatigue, nerve fatigue, at the same time absence of anxiety indifference. The right upper part of the body is more affected than the left, the left leg more than the right. Cachectic tint to skin, suggestion of malignancy, skin merging into a jaundice as the disease advances. Cachexia and cancerous tints. “Tired-out, washed-out feeling must give in.” Jaundice, with itching. Small, pain- ful furuncles, particularly in the auditory meatus. Fig warts. Erythema and itching of abdomen and feet. Heat and congestion of the head, with nosebleeds. Heaviness of head alternates with emptiness. Frequent severe headache. Pain in eyes, worse from lamp light, strong light, moving the eye. Spinal congestion. Colds. Chilliness predominates. Amorous fancies. Lascivious thoughts in the presence of any women. Great sexual desire with emissions. Terrible erections, disturbing sleep. Long-continued erections at night with emissions, followed by more erections and lewd dreams, priapism day and night. Priapism, penis distended almost to bursting. Gonorrhea. Burning during and after urination. Exhaustion and complete prostration of mind and body from sexual excesses, mental and physical fatigue. Over-excitement of sexual system is associated with spinal or cerebral disorders in either sex. A. C. Blackwood detailed the uses of Pic-ac. for burns of the first and second degree. He used a saturated solution diluted with one quart of water. The clothing was removed and the burnt surface cleansed with the solution and absorbent cotton. Blisters were opened but he carefully preserved the epithelial covering. If extensive, the whole surface might be bathed with the solution and strips of sterilized gauze soaked and applied to entirely cover it, a layer of absorbent cotton held with a light bandage over all. After three or four days the dressing was removed carefully after thorough moistening, as it adhered closely. The second dressing was applied as at first and allowed to remain a week. The staining of the hands and linen caused by the dressing can be removed by boric acid. Blackwood found it painless, anodyne, antiseptic, preventing inflammation, suppuration and septic poisoning. It coagulates the albuminous exudation and healing takes place under the coagulum. Gaucher removed acute vesicular eczema by the same treatment. He noted that the skin and kidneys are intimately related and Pic- ac . has a powerful action on the latter. Among other disorders, it has cured diabetes. Kent said Pic-ac. cures fig-warts and gonorrhea, he was led to infer its relation by its power over pernicious anemia, which he had often traced to a gonorrheal base. In a case of spinal irritation, Clarke relieved with Pic-ac. 30c a pain which shot up from the spine into the head. The pains referable to the spinal cord are strongly marked. Any attempt to study causes burning along spine with great weakness of back and legs, soreness of muscles and joints. Halbert reported a case illustrating the power of Pic-ac. over the effects of fatigue in professional neuroses. A stenographer and typewriter, after using her right index finger continuously for six years, noticed weakness of her thumb and index. Then, she noticed the inability to hold a pen or pencil. Next there was difficulty in striking correctly the keys of the typewriter and some wrist-drop. The finger, when Halbert first saw her, was quite rigid and straight, showing extreme spasticity. Massage, electricity, etc., had failed to give any relief. Pic-ac. 3x six times daily cured the case and made great improvement in the patient's general health. Halbert reported the case of Mrs., C., 49, who had “nervous prostration” since the shock of the loss of a child three years before. Wasting with great appetite. Intense thirst and copious urination, especially at night. Great perspiration and some jaundice. Heart flabby, mitral bruit, Dyspnea, emaciation, anemia, exhaustion. Urine 1040,7 1/2 percent of sugar and some albumen. Pic-ac. 6x six times daily was given, rapid and continuous improvement followed. Nash cured an old man who have been failing for a year with Pic-ac. 6c trituration. The man complained of heaviness in the occiput, inability to exert the mind, talk or think and general “played-out” feeling. Nash had feared brain softening. Evans found it curative in girls and young women who, under the strain of many studies, show signs of breaking down. They lose appetite, sleep lightly and lie awake, exhaustion after the day's studies, fatigued even from a short walk, twitchings of muscles when asleep or awake, hysterical state, loss of will power, constant headache, irregular menses. Such patients are usually given iron, which does little or no good. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ox-ac., Gels., Phos., Sil., Arg-n. (2) Zinc-pic. - facial palsy and Parkinson's disease. (3) Ferr-pic. - buzzing in ears, deafness, chronic gout, nosebleed, prostatic troubles. (4) Calc-pic. - boils in and around ears. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Vomits suddenly, without warning. Vomit bright yellow, bitter.

Abdomen - Fullness of the abdomen. Sharp pain in left side of umbilicus. Shooting, wandering pain. Crawling, stinging. Rumbling in small intestines with colic. Crampy pain and flatus. Emission of flatus during the day in evening.

Rectum - Diarrhea from mental exertion. Stools thin, yellow, oily. Burning in rectum while passing stools. Sensations - As if sand or sticks in eyes. As if throat would split. As of a lump back of thyroid cartilage. As if chest encircled in a tight band. As if legs enclosed in elastic stockings. Pricking as from needles in legs. As if stairs or ground coming up to meet him. As of ants crawling over surface.

Male - Enlargement of the prostate gland. Hard erections with pain in testicles up spermatic cord. Priapism, penis distended. Lascivious thoughts in presence of any woman. Extreme prostration from frequent seminal emissions. Impotency with tendency to boils and carbuncles.

Female - Pain in left ovary and leucorrhea before menstruation. Extreme exhaustion at menstrual periods. Pruritus vulvae. Food - Appetite increased, then lost for breakfast. Aversion to food, at noon. Great thirst with bitter taste, unquenchable. Thirst for cold water.

Chest - Tightness of chest, as if encircled by a band. Numbness in lower part of sternum. Constitutions - Suited to dark complex- ioned persons with a dirty appearance from bile pigments, anemic and cachectic persons. Worn-out person, overtaxed mentally and bodily.

Back - Burning along spine. Painful boils on nape of neck. Backache with languor, patient is unable to sit straight and burning along spine, worse study. Keeps legs wide apart when standing. Aching, tired legs. Writer's cramps orpalsy. Back seems as if bandaged, also limbs. Anesthesia of legs as if one has on elastic stockings. Legs weak, heavy like lead, lifts with difficulty.

Limbs - Great weakness, tired, heavy feeling all over body, especially limbs. Worse exertion. Acute ascending paralysis. Feet cold. Cannot get warm.

Sleep - Sleepy during day and sleepless during night. Sleepiness. Sleep sound but unrefreshing.

Skin - Jaundice. Small, painful, sore boils, especially on neck.

Modalities - Better from cold air, cold water, sun. Better tight pressure, bandaging, rest. Worse least exertion, especially mental, fatigue, study, mental shock. Worse after sleep, seminal losses. Worse wet weather, hot weather.

Liver - Liver full of fat granules. Sticking through hepatic region, worse in muscles. Tendency to jaundice. Jaundice with itching.

Kidneys - Inflammation of kidneys with profound weakness, dark, bloody, scanty urine. Dribbling urine. Albuminuria. Ammoniacal. Urine contains much indican, granular cylinders and fatty degenerated epithelium. Uremia with complete anuria. Diabetes. Nightly urging.

full:
PHARMACY - picro. Picrotoxinum. Picrotoxin. Alkaloid obtained from the fruit of Coc- culus indicus. Menispermaceae. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Dysentery. Dyspepsia. Hernia. Locomotor ataxia. Night-sweats. Urine, excess.

HOMEOPATHIC - Falk noted that Cocc. is used to stupefy fishes and when Picro. is added to water in which fishes are swimming “they make winding and boring movements of the body. Alternating with quiet swimming, open their mouths and gill caverns frequently, fall on their side and rapidly die of asphyxia.” J. H. Henry proved Picro. on himself. The symptoms were so severe that he was alarmed and took Op. and Camph. to antidote them. Nausea with tendency to faint, violent intestinal pain and purging, dysenteric diarrhea and excessive secretion of urine, cramps and paralytic sensations were experienced. The symptom which gave the most concern was the pain in the bowels and sensation as if the bowels would protrude at left inguinal ring. COMMENTS - Brunton said the local application of Picro. as an ointment to the head for tinea capitis and to destroy lice has been followed by convulsions and death. Hansen mentioned that it has been given at bedtime to relieve the night-sweats of tuberculosis. With Pictx-ac 3x, Dorr cured in a few weeks a case of advanced locomotor ataxia with amaurotic amblyopia. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cocc. (2) In tetaniform convulsions, Nux-v. with Piero, respiration is accelerated more from spasm of glottis then of respiration and there is less susceptibility to slight touch, more chorea symptoms. REFERENCES - Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - piloc. Pilocarpinum hydro- chloricum. Pilocarpine. Jaborandi alkaloid. Pilocarpinum muriaticum nitricum purum. Rutaceae. Solution in distilled water. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Alopecia. Convulsions, uremia, Deafness. Exhaustion. Eye, disorders. Faintness. Hair, loss. Meniere's disease. Mumps. Myopia. Paralysis. Perspiration, excessive. Pregnancy, nausea. Salivation. Tinnitus. Vertigo, aural.

HOMEOPATHIC - Piloc. is one of the most characteristic of several alkaloids which have been isolated from jaborandi (Pilocarpus pin- natus). It has been used like Jab. to produce and cure profuse sweating, and by oculists to produce contraction of the pupil, which it does whether it is injected subcutaneously or applied directly to the eye. It has also an action on the ear. The hair as well as the skin is affected by Piloc., which is an ingredient in many “hair restorers." Schmitz of Cologne treated two bald men with injections of Piloc. mur. to produce absorption of inflammatory residue within the eye. In both a secondary effect occurred, the growth of young downy hairs on the bald parts of the scalp. One, age 60 in four months and his head covered “partly with gray and partly with black hairs” of considerable growth, so as to entirely obliterate his previous baldness. Piloc. has also been known to turn white hair black. In a case of lead paralysis, it produced profuse salivation and sweat with sensation of great coldness and excessive tremors of limbs. Salivation and sweating speedily occur. Dilatation of blood vessels, temporal artery becomes a thick, pulsating cord, veins of forehead stand out blue. Exhaustion (after the perspiration) during which most of the patients fell asleep. Faintness.

Head - Throbbing in temples with acceleration of pulse. Turns white hair black.

Eyes - Profuse lachrymation. Pupils contracted to pin-head. Sight for distance improved.

Ears - Aural vertigo. Tinnitus of left ear. Deafness with tinnitus. Labyrinthine deafness, worse when tired. Increased secretion of wax.

Nose - Nasal secretion increased.

Face - Forehead and face red, veins stand out. Perspiration begins on face.

Mouth - Saliva thick, stringy, exceedingly tenacious. Sudden salivation, maximum reached in fifteen minutes, continues two hours, one and a half pints of thin saliva being secreted in that time.

Stomach - Nausea, only occurring when salivation is complete (does not go on to vomiting as that of Jab. does). Nausea and retching.

Rectum - Urging to stool.

Female - Menses two days early. Food - Intense thirst following the sweating.

Heart - Weakness of the heart. Pulse accelerated, blood pressure diminished. After the perspiration the pulse sinks to normal. Lungs - Increased bronchial mucus, much cough and expectoration. Constantly taking cold and in fear of bronchitis.

Sleep - Patients fall asleep under its influence.

Skin - Irritable skin.

Temperature - Sensation of coldness and shaking chill without fall of temperature. Increase of temperature with feeling of intense cold. Sweat profuse, may lose Vom tow to tow powvts tu fet sw catwg. After sweat, thirst, feeling of relief and sense of increased vigor. COMMENTS - G. P. Field gave it with good effect in labyrinthine deafness, tinnitus and auditory nerve vertigo. The cases least amenable to its influence were those in which the hearing was better in a noise as of a train, etc. and those in which the hearing is worse after a cold. Subjects of syphilis, hereditary or acquired and patients who are more deaf when tired, are the most suitable. Wood went to see a woman three months pregnant. She was a picture of distress and despair. For eight weeks she had saturated from six to ten handkerchiefs daily with tenacious saliva. Nausea and vomiting were constant, emaciation extreme. Nausea worse by slightest movement. Alternate redness and paleness of face, flushes of heat and perspiration. Urine scanty, high colored, depositing much uric acid. Very chilly, obstinate constipation. Piloc. was given, a teaspoonful every two hours. The next day Wood found his patient sitting up, cheerful and free from nausea and salivation. The improvemen,t with some fluctuations, continued. Merc., Ip., Nit-ac., Kali-bi., Hydr., Cimic. had all previously failed. A woman who had Piloc. injections complained to Cooper that thereafter she had been constantly catching colds and had fears of getting bronchitis. Her skin too, became irritable. Piloc. 3x is Burnett's chief remedy in mumps. He regarded it (and Jab.) as an organ remedy of the sweat glands, parotid and pancreas. Frohling related a case showing the power of Piloc. over debilitating sweats left after acute diseases. With Merc. 12c he cured a case of rheumatic fever so far as the joint affection was concerned, but the sweats persisted and strength declined in spite of remedies until Piloc. was given, when the sweating stopped after the first dose. RELATIONS-Antidoted by: Atro., Am-c. (sal volatile), brandy. Compare: (1) Jab., Myos., Esin., Phys. Follows well: Merc, (in sweating of rheumatic fever). REFERENCES - Clarke.

HOMEOPATHIC - The majority of the symptoms were obtained by Shelling from chewing the fresh root. The rest were contributed by Berridge, who proved the lx on a man. Marked chilliness, chilly in the back even in a warm room and much worse if a window was opened. Sensitive to drafts. Sensation of coldness in occiput as from a cutting wind behind. Cold stream from hip and into right leg. the pains and sensations extended from one part to another, principally from above downward and from before backward (temples to nape, forehead to eyes, nape to shoulders) from within outward or alternated between different parts. Rush of blood to head, followed by nosebleed, whizzing in head, roaring in ears. Sinking sensation in intestines. Weariness and falling asleep of parts rested on. Frequent yawning and desire to take a long breath, which was difficult. Great drowsiness.

Modalities - V ertigo and sweat worse morning. Heat and rush of blood to the head, worse afternoon. Weary pain in limbs worse from rest. Worse reading, writing, reflecting. keynote: PHARMACY - pine-b. Pine. Pinus sylvestris. N. O. Pinaceae. Twigs with male and female flowers are picked and boiled for half an hour. The boiled water is strained and prepared as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle,…
full:
PHARMACY - pine-b. Pine. Pinus sylvestris. N. O. Pinaceae. Twigs with male and female flowers are picked and boiled for half an hour. The boiled water is strained and prepared as medicine. Historical dose: Take two drops from the stock bottle into a one ounce dropper bottle, (add brandy or alcohol, if this bottle will be used for days or weeks). This is the dosage bottle, take a few drops straight into the mouth or as needed in a little water or juice.

HOMEOPATHIC - Pine-b. belongs to Bach's group of Despondency and Despair, with the remedies of Crb- a-b., Oak-b., Will-b., Star-b- b., Sw-ch-b., Elm-b. and Lar-b. States of guilt, regret and self-reproach. Obsessive-compulsive states and too much over-conscientiousness. The body may show signs of becoming burdened, depressive, or rigid, due to excessive introversion and self- blame. Deep-seated conflict and obsessive guilt. Gastric and duodenal ulcers, irritable colon, nervous breathing syndrome and insomnia (Must-b., Wh-ch-b.). Skin disorders with itching. MIND - Introverted, subdued by the burdens of guilt and regret. Preoccupied or obsessed with guilt and self- reproach. Deep sense of unworthiness. Internal sense of failure. Overconscientiousness. Feelings of shame, regret and self-blame at not having fulfilled one's high ideals. Despondency and despair. Unable to forgive self. May assume responsibility and blame for failure caused by others. Frustration, anger, rigidity and alienation from oneself and others. Obsessive-compulsive, self-punitive and perfectionist or ritualistic behavior and thinking, as in obsessive- compulsive personality disorder (Crb-a-b., Rck-w-b., Verv-b.). Delusions and paranoid personality disorders. Fear of being punished or persecuted (Asp-b.). REFERENCES - Bach.

HERBAL - The inspissated sap of Pinus lambertiana makes a sugary substance like manna. A small quantity from a bit the size of a pea to a teaspoonful, has a decided but gentle laxative action, and in larger quantities emphatically so.

HOMEOPATHIC - Pin-1, has also an action on the menstrual function, restoring menses when suppressed and producing abortion in pregnant women. It was used by Indian women to restore the menstrual flow and remove painful sensations resulting from the suppression. It has a gentle cathartic action. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sabin., Juni., Pin-s. and other coniferae. REFERENCES-Clarke.

Liver, enlargement. Lumbrici. Palpitations. Rheumatism. Scrofula. Squint. Tinnitus. Urine increased, strong. Vertigo. Walking, late. Worms.

HERBAL - Pine baths may also be made by adding Oleumpinus sylvestris to an ordinary bath in the proportion of one minim to the gallon. These baths have a reputation in the treatment of rheumatism, gout, paralysis, scrofula and skin diseases.

HOMEOPATHIC - Pin-s. was proved by Demeures in the tincture, and Patzack observed the effect of bathing in an infusion of the leaves. Rheumatic, bronchial and urticaria symptoms. Rheumatic, gouty and paralytic pains in limbs, bones and joints. Stiffness. Glandular swellings. Enlarged and painful liver and spleen. Sensitiveness to touch. Scalp sensitive. Chest walls sensitive with a feeling of thinness, as if they would give way at a touch. Chilliness alternating with flushing, the face is alternately red and pale. Itching in general. Emaciation of lower limbs. Weak ankles. Late walking in scrofulous and rickety children. Bronchial mucus was increased. The kidneys were stimulated, burning on urination, flow increased, urine strong. Itching of the nose and discharge of round worms was noted. The menstrual function was deranged. MIND - Anxiety. Despondency. Mind dull, unable to think, caused by any exertion. Wants to do many things, undertakes all and finishes none.

Head - Dullness, fullness, heaviness of head. Tearing in temples. Pressive headache. Headache worse by any movement of eyes. Scalp sensitive.

Eyes - Eyes inflamed. Margins of lids red. Vision dim, veiled. Squint.

Ears - Sticking in ears. Roaring in ears.

Nose - Violent nosebleed several days in succession. Mucus discharge from nose. Sensation of coryza. Itching of nose.

Face - Face alternately pale and red. Tearing in face.

Mouth - Pain in teeth with heat of face and pain in head. Dry mouth with increased thirst.

Throat - Uneasiness in throat as if something in the way. Painful swelling of submaxillary glands. Vertigo - Vertigo, even to falling down. COMMENTS - In a patient of Cooper's, Pin-s. caused a “headache worse by any movement of the eyes” and it cured a case of squint. Hansen gave “emaciation of lower limbs” and “weak ankles in children" as indications for it and mentioned that the tinctures may be used externally, while the potencies are given internally. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Pin-1. - constipation, amenorrhea, miscarriage. Pinus lamber- tina sap is a decided cathartic. Delayed and painful menstruation. (2) Abies-c., Abies-n. (3) Terebe., Sabin., Juni., Thuj., Aloe., Pix. (4) Strong urine, Benz-ac. (5) Red margin of eyes, Sulph., Bac. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Pressure in pit of stomach after eating with great distention.

Abdomen - Distention of hypochondrium with pressive and burning pains. Enlargement of liver. Pressure and fullness in liver and spleen. Colic with incarcerated flatus. Pain in inguinal glands with swelling.

Rectum - Constipation. Stool thin, pasty with colic and great excitement, bilious. Bloody, slimy, hemorrhoidal discharge. Troublesome itching at anus. Discharge of round worms.

Female - Menses, earlier, delayed. Menses, usually scanty, became more profuse. Food - Appetite at first decreased, afterwards increased.

Chest - Oppression. Anterior portion of chest painful to touch. Burning in sides of chest. In middle of sternum sensation - as if a cupping-glass had been applied inside.

Heart - Palpitations.

Back - Drawing and stiffness in nape extending into occiput. Pressive, tensive drawing pain between shoulders and small of back, motion difficult.

Limbs - Stiffness, gouty pain in all joints, especially finger joints. Cramps in calves. Lungs - Hoarseness. Breath tight, especially when walking. Increased bronchial mucus. Short, dry cough. Expectoration greater when coughing.

Sleep - Great sleepiness, especially forenoon with restless sleep in evening. Sleepless. Dreams which seem when remembered like real occurrences.

Skin - Nettle-rash. Itching all over, especially about joints and on abdomen. Nose itches.

Modalities - Worse by exertion, walking, touch. Worse in morning, evening.

Kidneys - Violent boring-burning pains in kidneys, extending along ureters. Burning pains when urinating. Spasms of bladder. Urination is difficult. Very greatly increased secretion of urine. Urine of strong odor.

Temperature - Chilliness, especially towards evening, alternating with flushes of heat. Perspiration general, easy.

HERBAL - Piper methysticum furnishes the root called Kava in Polynesia. The natives use it as astimulant, either chewing the root or drinking a beverage made of it before undertaking any important business or religious rites. Kava causes exaltation of the mind, lively and inclined to work. Faculties sharpened, capable of working more without fatigue or brain-fag. From increased doses, there is intoxication of a sorrowful, silent and sleepy character, different from that produced by alcohol. Excessive indulgence in it produces a skin disease like leprosy, calledTahiti Arevareva. Lutz described the disease as observed amongst natives of the Sandwich Islands, “The skin, par marked ichthyosis, associated with a certain degree of atrophy, such as is observed in senile skin. There is an absence of inflammatory symptoms.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Kava-Kava is an intoxicant which produces liveliness and inclination to do more work without fatigue. Silent and drowsy intoxication, with incoherent dreams, loss of muscular power. Nervous system strung up to its highest tension. Trembling. Uneasiness and weakness during day with timidity and apprehension. Weakness in morning, better rising and moving around. Want of tone and life in all functions towards night. Dizziness and vertigo, better on closing eyes. Full forehead, “solid with pain,” shifting to occiput and cervical spine, where it became a compression, extending as a constricting sensation to stomach and chest. Marked and persistent sensation of enlargement of head. All the symptoms, especially pains are temporarily better by diverting attention, changing position or topic. Arthritis deformans. Emaciation and decrepitude. Colic with flatulence. Urinary and skin symptoms have been verified. MIND - Mental symptoms, excitement or depression, and the headache, better by diversion of mind. Amelioration of pains by diverting the attention. Restless desire to change position. Intoxication with fantastic ideas and desire to skip about, although he cannot for a moment hold himself on his legs. Exaltation of mind. Very sensitive. Mental tension. Lively and inclined to work. Faculties sharpened, capable of working more without fatigue or brain-fag. Lazy and drowsy. Want of vigor, timid, apprehensive.

Head - Brain tired in morning on waking, better getting on feet. Heaviness of head. Feeling as though the head were enlarged even to bursting. Headache with pressure in upper part of orbits with sleepiness.

Eyes - Conjunctivae red. Pain along right optic nerve when reading. Pain deep in left eye as if ball would be pressed out. Dizzy blindness when dressing

Ears - Singular pressure in lobules of pinna of left ear.

Face - Pressure outward in face at 7 p.m. Food - Appetite is formidable, but not able to eat much.

Mouth - Burning in whole mouth followed by numbness. Dryness of mouth on waking from afternoon nap with sweat (on a hot day). Salivation. Taste is nauseous, sweet, then piquant and sharp, pappy, everything tasteless, lost to food, but ravenous haste in eating. Taste and relish to food not as usual, at noon, but appetite usually good.

Stomach - Warmth in stomach. Crampy pain, better pressure against edge of table. Sour belchings, worse an hour before meals.

Rectum - Urging all day, every evening. Continuous desire, next day forced a large stool, which caused prolapsed anus. Constipation, hard, large, light-colored. Stool difficult, large, soft. Pain after first stool. Burning in rectum.

Male - Shooting in penis. Pain in right testicle. Erection in afternoon, at night after an emission. Emission early in morning without dreams. Amorousness.

Chest - Constriction of chest and stomach, extending from base of brain. Heaviness behind upper part of sternum, as from wind that cannot be belched out.

Back - Pain in back only felt on pressure. Soreness about second dorsal vertebra.

Limbs - Numbness of the lower limbs. Weakness, as if unable to stand. Heaviness of legs when walking. Sticking in left knee at 4 p.m. when walking. Pain in right arm. Numbness of right elbow. Pain in right wrist, worse writing. Weakness of left hand. Hands feel paralyzed. Pain in the thumb joint.

Sleep - Difficult falling asleep. Sleepless. Sleepiness at 10 p.m., soon afterwards irresistible liveliness and wakefulness. Restless sleep last part of night. Stupid sleep. Heavy sleep with disturbing but unremembered dreams. Dreams are curious, nonsensical, wild, amorous of traveling by rail, active, vivid, last part of night of a fire, heard the engines and firemen.

Skin - Dryness, especially where it is thick, as on hands and feet with scales, cracks and ulcers. Ichthyosis. Leprosy. Scaly. Fall of scales leaves white spots, which often ulcerate.

Modalities - Better moving, open air. Better by turning mind to another topic, changing position. Vertigo better closing eyes. Worse reading and thinking. Worse in open air, motion, walking. Going down stairs causes symptoms to rush up. Sour belchings worse before meals. Burning in urethra worse urinating.

Teeth - Teeth deep yellow. Teeth sensitive to cold water, cold air, brushing,

Tongue - Tongue feels as if covered with velvet or fur at night. Burning on tongue. Vertigo - From 5 to 9 p.m. very dizzy, swimming sensation and faintness. Vertigo in morning in bed with frontal pressure. COMMENTS - W. N. Griswold proved the third and second dilutions and developed a large number of nervous, mental and brain symptoms, among which are some which have proved to be keynotes. The mental symptoms of Pip-m. or the “Intoxicating Pepper” are the most interesting feature of the drug's action. Feeling of buoyancy, as if every nerve was strung up to the highest pitch, feels he can work without fatigue, quickly followed by a feeling of tired brain and over-sensitiveness to all external impression. Griswold cured a case having burning in chest, better by diverting mind, and three cases having “Agonizing pain with tossing, twisting and writhing, patient driven irresistibly to change position, which generally gives little or no better.” These cures were with the lx or tinctures. Skinner gave fractional doses of tincture in water to a highly excitable young girl. She had severe toothache and earache and had worn out her family by the incessant day and night attendance she required. The pains were dragging, heavy, worse at night in bed and after or when eating, forgets all about her pains if amused with anything, but directly she is tired of it she exclaims ‘Oh. my tooth or ear!' ” She had “Agonizing pain with tossing, twisting and writhing, irresistibly driven to change position.” The patient slept well that night the first time for a fortnight and had no more pain. The remaining swelling was removed by Puls. 200c. Skinner also reported the case of Miss R., 20, who had a toothache in a decayed molar, better if attention is diverted by anything, is diverted by anything sufficiently exciting. When pain is at all violent she has no rest in any position, must keep continually changing it. Pip-m. 500c (F. C.) was given and there was relief very soon after the first dose. A few doses completely removed the pain. Farrington said convulsions simulating catalepsy are produced. Cerna, as a result of his investigations, found Pip-m. a general and local anesthetic. It diminishes reflex action by its action on the cord and kills by paralyzing respiration. Cerna illustrated its relationship to Cub. by citing cases of gonorrhea, acute and chronic cystitis, gleet, prostatorrhea, vaginitis, cured with it. RELATIONS-Antidoted by: Puls, and Rhus-t. (partially). Compare: ( 1 ) Cub., Pip-n., Mati. (2) Is better by diverting mind, Ox-ac. (3) better by motion, Rhus-t. (4) Feeling of buoyancy, Coff. (but with Coff. the reverse condition of brain-fatigue does not quickly follow). (5) Neurasthenia, Pic-ac., Arg-n., Aven. (6) Unbearable pains, Coff., Aeon., Cham. (7) Chaul. (8) Bix. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak

Kidneys - Chordee. Cystitis. Burning in urethra during urination, gonorrhea and gleet. Urine increased, scanty in morning. Urine nearly neutral, hot and over-acid at night.

HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany noted that the peppers are tropical climbing shrubs. Pip. nigrum, yields the pepperof commerce. When ripe, the fruit is red. Black pepper is gathered before it is fully ripe and spread on mats in the sun, when it loses it red color and becomes black and shriveled. White pepper is the same fruit freed from its outer skin by maceration in water and subsequent rubbing.

HOMEOPATHIC - The symptoms of the Pip- n. proving are Houat's. The only additional symptom is one recorded by Berridge as having occurred in a woman on two occasions from taking a large quantity of pepper: “Feeling as if temples and mal ar bones were pressed in, worse on left side.” Sensation of burning and pressure everywhere. Clarke can confirm the full, heavy headache of Houat's provings by personal experience. He gets the headache whenever he takes food highly peppered and he knows of others who do the same. MIND - Sad, apprehensive. Unable to concentrate, starts at any noise. Hot-headed, irascible and often gay. Amorousness with hypochondriasis. Fear of being poisoned.

Head - Heavy headache, as if temples were pressed in, pressure in nasal and facial bones.

Eyes - Bursting aching in eyeballs. Eyes inflamed and burning. Lachrymation and photophobia. Lids ulcerated and bleared. Dim sight and vertigo with headache, nausea and vomiting.

Ears - Crusty ulcers in concha of ears.

Nose - Nose itches, sneezing, nosebleed.

Face - Red burning face. Lips dry and cracked.

Mouth - Burning dryness of mouth and throat. Heat and dryness of palate and tongue, as if burned.

Throat - Sore, feels raw, burns. Burning pain in tonsils. Constant accumulation of mucus in throat and expectoration. Paralysis of muscles of throat, can cry but not articulate intelligibly.

Stomach - Full feeling. Gastric discomfort. Sensation of heat and dryness in stomach. Cramps and drawing in stomach. Vomiting with great exertion, it seemed as if stomach itself would be vomited.

Abdomen - Disposition of abdomen to obesity. Abdomen swollen, hard, burning. Inflammation of intestines with great thirst. Tympanites. Borborygmi. Colic and cramps, sensation as intestines would burst. Flatulence.

Rectum - Inflammation of rectum, anus swollen and burning. Diarrhea. Fear to go to stool on account of the difficulty and pain. Fissures in the anus. Long-lasting constipation, then involuntary, thin stools. Worms. Large flowing hemorrhoids. Sensations - Burning sensation. Pressure in nasal bones in temples and facial bones. Sensation of a foreign, round body rising to stomach. Contraction of uterus and sensation as if something about to enter it.

Male - Inflammation and swelling of penis with priapism and burning pains. Burning, pricking, excoriating pains in glans.

Female - Menses difficult, retarded, capricious, irregular. Menses with colic and black blood. Ovaries and uterus congested with pricking and sharp pains. Burning and distending pains in uterus. Food - Desire for coarse and extravagant food. Constant, unquenchable thirst.

Chest - Dyspnea, cough with pain in chest in spots, feels as if spitting blood.

Heart - Palpitations, cardiac pain, slow, intermittent pulse.

Back - Burning in loins and kidneys with contractive movements. Breasts - Great flow of milk.

Limbs - Inflammation and swelling of joints. Lungs - Dyspnea and attacks of suffocation. Severe coughing, especially in evening and when going to sleep. Cough is violent, occasionally spitting of blood, croupy, hollow.

Sleep - Irresistible drowsiness. Lethargic sleep. Nightmares. Wakens at night without being able to sleep again.

Skin - Large pustules on face, leaving scars. Very tender skin. Itching, by scratching, heat and motion. Eczema on lips. Crusty ulcers in ears.

Modalities - Worse from change of temperature, damp weather, evening. Worse by motion.

Teeth - Tooth decays. Violent toothache, worse in warmth and evening.

Tongue - Eruption of little vesicles on margin of tongue. Painful, heavy tongue, impeded speech. Whitish coating on middle of tongue. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Piper-m. (2) Cub., also mental, genito-urinary, skin and general symptoms. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Kidneys - Bladder feels full, swollen, frequent inclination without success. Burning in bladder and urethra. Difficult urination. Priapism.

Temperature - Dryness and coldness of skin, heat with biting dryness. Heat in forehead with heaviness of head and vertigo. Cold sweat with great heat through whole body. Sweat which seems to corrode the skin.

full:
PHARMACY - pipe. Piperazinum. Piperazidine. Diethylen-diamine. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Glaucoma. Gout. Lead paralysis. Kidney, colic.

HOMEOPATHIC - Pipe, is a synthetic product which was intended to replace Spermin and was named Dispermine. It was found, however to be a different body both in chemical and physiological properties. It occurs in well-defined, colorless, acicular crystals (Helbing) or in lustrous tables (J. Gordon), is deliquescent and mostly soluble in water. It readily unites with uric acid, forming a very soluble compound (urate of piperazine). When taken by the mouth it is not entirely oxidized, as part is discoverable unchanged in the urine. John Gordon experimented with Pipe, and found that a 1 percent solution in normal urine at body temperature dissolved to a large extent a fragment of uric acid calculus and converted undissolved portions to a granular and pulpy condition. The amount of urea is increased in the urine of those taking it. J. R. Hamilton of Hawick reported success in treating kidney colic with Pipe, and Walter of Odessa, cleared up two cases of glaucoma, giving one grain daily in carbonated water, all the symptoms disappearing within three weeks. According to Cooper, a patient, after a teaspoonful dose of an effervescing preparation of Pipe., complained that he was seized with a bad attack of acute gout, that was quite unexpected. Helbing said it has been used with success in mental diseases and in a case of lead paralysis with “very remarkable results.” RELATIONS - Compare: Phlor., Hydrang., Urt-u. REFERENCES - Clarke.

HERBAL - This small tree has unequally pinnate leaves and entire, oval leaflets. The flowers are in lateral clusters, and appear in profusion before the leaves. The bark of the tree is very astringent, and acts as a narcotic poison. When Pise, is chewed, there is an unpleasant acrimony in mouth like thatof Mez. Locally the tincture is used for toothaches in decayed teeth. Piscidia is sedative, hypnotic and narcotic. A good nerve sedative and pain killer. The pounded leaves and young branches of Piscidia and some allied species are used like cocculus, for poisoning fish hence the name Piscidia (Piscis-caedere).

HOMEOPATHIC - Excessive restlessness and insomnia. Insomnia due to pain, worry or nervous excitement, it usually produces a quiet, deep sleep. Dysmenorrhea pains. Pains of irregular menstruation, regulates the flow. Neuralgias, ovarian or uterine. Neuralgic and spasmodic affections. Tetanus. Toothaches in decayed teeth. Spasmodic coughs, especially cough of phthisis. Bronchial catarrhs, bronchitis. Asthma, nervous cough. Fevers with a violent sensation of heat generally increasing in intensity, the sensation of burning gradually extended to the surface and a profuse diaphoresis burst out from every pore. COMMENTS - The experiment recorded in Allen is by W. Hamilton, who took a drachm of the Pise, tincture in water for toothache and went off to sleep with great suddenness. Profound sleep, he remained motionless the whole night, when he awoke, twelve hours later, he was still holding the glass and uncorked vial from which he had taken the dose. When he returned to consciousness, he was free from every pain or ache and without any of the unpleasant sensations which invariably succeed an overdose of opium. RELATIONS - Compare: Coff. and Op. REFERENCES - Allen. Boericke. Clarke.

HOMEOPATHIC - The proving was established by the Hering Proving Committee in 1935 on five provers, using the potency 12x. George Fuller noted that Pitu-gl. exercises a superior control over the growth and development of the sexual organs, stimulates muscular activity and overcomes uterine inertia. Uterine inertia in second stage of labor where os is fully dilated. Affects the female glands. Painful menses with disturbed cycle. Cervical pains. A vasoconstrictor and parturient, used chiefly for its action on the uterus either to aid in childbirth or to check bleeding after delivery. Cerebral hemorrhage. It will check hemorrhage and aid absorption of clots. High blood pressure. Chronic nephritis, prostatitis. Bedwetting. Incontinence when the patient loses a few drops. The action of this remedy has a clear antispasmodic tendency, especially affecting the vessels in the head. Vertigo, difficult mental concentration, confusion and fullness deep in frontal region. Congestive headaches. Pigmentation disorders and loss of hair. MIND - Mental weakness. Difficult concentration. Nocturnal anxiety and anguish. Anxiety, aggravated at nightfall. Weeping, the patient cries involuntarily and even without noticing. Obsessive ideas linked to the uro-genital area; fear of impotence, of passing urine. Obsession of ideas, especially of depressive, or of erotic, of impotence.

Head - Congestive headache. Pulsating, throbbing headaches, related to hypertension. Headaches, starting at the occiput and spreading towards the base, cervical column and shoulders. Headaches, aggravated by heat, confined space, at the end of the day. Alopecia of the scalp, which is very dry.

Eyes - Mydriasis. Pupils very dilated. Weeping, the patient cries involuntarily and even without noticing. Styes, especially on the left. Conjunctivitis. Blepharitis.

Ears - Earache. Buzzing. Deafness in the left ear.

Nose - Coryza.

Mouth - Excessive salivation. Saliva tastes salty.

Throat - Tonsillitis. Pharyngitis. Vertigo - Vertigo when not moving body or head. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ign. - Cortical and visceral rhythm disorders, characterized by mobihty instability and paradoxical, contradictory state of symptoms. (2) Syph. - Changing moods, forgets proper nouns, obsessions, all aggravated at night. (3) Thuj. - Fixed ideas, sad, varicosities in the nostrils, skin sticky. REFERENCES - Boericke.

Stomach - Nausea and post-prandial distention, worse after the evening meal.

Abdomen - Enterocolitis. Recto-colitis. Spasmodic colon infection. Inflammation of the gallbladder.

Rectum - Rectal tenesmus, the patient wants to pass stools, but cannot. Diarrhea with painful intestinal spasms. Hemorrhaging recto-colitis. Proctitis.

Female - Amenorrhea with breast atrophy. Menses late, cycle longer than 30 days. Menses scanty. Menses with pain during the day. Menses very painful, especially the day before and the day after the start. Dysmenorrhea. Uterine pains from muscular contraction. Painful uterine contractions during childbirth. Difficult childbirth. Food - Desires cold drinks.

Chest - Growth of hair on chest. Constitutions - Phosphoric, flouric types, tubercular poisoning or syphilitic, with obsessions or depressive complaints.

Heart - Feeling of heaviness in the precordial region, aggravated by the slightest movement. The patient can “feel his heart.” Sensation of heart constriction, aggravated by the slightest exertion. Arterial hypertension with the feeling of pounding arteries in the temples and carotid arteries. Coronary arthritis. Angina pectoris. Valvular disease. Cardiac neurosis. Arrhythmia. Tachycardia. Hypertension. Septicemia.

Back - Pains in the nape of the neck, spreading to the occiput and shoulders. Neck ache. Backache. Breasts - Breasts hypertrophy or atrophy. Amenorrhea with breast atrophy.

Skin - Skin cold, discolored or strongly pigmented. Alternating white and dark patches. Vitiligo. Skin is swollen, edematous, itching. Eruptions of aurticaria type. Skin very dry, scaly.

Modalities - Better from fresh air, open air. Worse from the heat, in a closed room, at the end of the day.

Kidneys - Nephritis. Anuria. Incontinence of urine, worse in the evening. Incontinence of urine in women with fibromatous uterus, the patient loses a few drops of urine on rising. Presence of albumin in the urine. Lungs - Asthma. Asthmatic dyspnea, accompanied by intestinal and rectal spasms. Dyspnea from anguish. Dyspnea with abundant, watery, salty-tasting sputum, sensation of constriction in the thoracic cage. Laryngitis. Tracheitis and bronchitis.
