Gangrene. Gout. Hay fever. Hemorrhages. Kidney, disorders. Leucorrhea. Nephritis. Ophthalmia, scrofulous. Phosphaturia. Prostate, enlarged. Prostate, weak. Rheumatic fever. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Scrofula. Tuberculosis. Urine, suppressed

HERBAL - The common golden rod is the only British species of Solidago. It is common in woods and healthy thickets. “This herb,” said Rademacher, “is a very old and good kidney medicine. It is a specific for kidneys and brings the patients back to the normal condition.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Solid, has helped diseases arising from or complicated with defective functions of kidneys. It affects the digestive tract, lower limbs and blood. Hemorrhages. Feeling of weakness, chilliness alternating with heat. Homeopathic replacement for the catheter. Pain in region of kidneys with dysuria. Kidneys sensitive to pressure. Bright’s disease. Chronic nephritis. Uremic asthma. “Clear, stinking urine” is an indication of Cooper’s. Hay fever when golden rod is the exciting cause. Takes cold easily. Inhalation of the pollen has caused hemorrhage from the lungs in tuberculosis. Repeated colds of tuberculosis. Naso-pharyngeal catarrh, burning in throat, pains in limbs and thoracic oppression.

Eyes - Conjunctivitis. Scrofulous, herpetic inflammation. Red with enlarged prostate gland.

Ears - Sudden deafness with ringing in the ears and albuminous urine.

Nose - Allergies and hay fever. Dry, inner surface of the nose covered with blood crust, scalding and very scanty urine. Paroxysms of sneezing with abundant mucus discharge.

Mouth - Continuous bitter taste. Tongue heavily coated, clears when urine becomes normal. Flat ulcers in the mouth and throat.

Abdomen - Costiveness, sensation of pain in the abdomen on both sides of the navel, upon deep pressure, gas. Severe pricking in both hypochondria to the region of the kidneys, reaching to the lower limbs.

Rectum - Chronic catarrh of the bowels. Dysentery, diarrhea. Profuse involuntary mucus stools.

Urine - Dark urine, especially at night with very scanty brown and sour urine. Scalding and very scanty urine. Urine, dark and scanty or clear, stinking. Urine, voided with difficulty. Urine, albuminous, mucous, phosphatic. COMMENTS - Anshutz wrote, “A lady, by administering, morning and evening, an infusion of the dry leaves and flowers of Golden Rod (Solidago virgaurea) tells me that she cured her husband of an affection of the bladder which had compelled him to use a catheter for a year or more. “A friend of homeopathy desired to test the energetics of this plant. He had the first dilution of its tincture to be taken three times a day by seven patients. From forty-two to seventy-fours years of age. They had been obliged to catheterize themselves for weeks, months and years. “Homeopathy cured them so thoroughly that they had no relapses. Surgeons who spend much time in catheterizing such patients for months and years could often cure them much more rapidly by prescribing for them the remedy just mentioned.” Gallavardin told of a woman who cured her husband, who had been compelled to use the catheter for more than a year, by administering an infusion of the dried leaves and flowers of Solid, morning and evening. Dr. White said “I have used it in several other cases where it seemed indicated by the tenderness in kidney region and the inability to control the water from whatever cause, always the perfect satisfaction to patient and myself.” Gucken confirmed Rademacher’s clinical observations and quoted further confirmations and cures by Dr. Buck of Wurtemburg. The grand keynote of this remedy lies in the condition and the action of the kidneys and the quality of their secretions. Diseases arising from or complicated with defective action of the kidneys are very likely to be benefited by Solid. Pain and tenderness in kidney region, pains extending from kidneys to abdomen, bladder and down limbs, urine dark, red- brown, scanty, thick, voided with difficulty, albuminous, mucus and phosphatic urine. Affections of any other parts or organs complicated with these symptoms will probably find their remedy in Solid. Buck mentioned scrofulous inflammation of the eyes. Clarke saw very sharp attack of conjunctivitis produced in a patient who was taking Solid. Also for prostatic troubles. Buck noted several cases, including that of a boy, age 8, who had severe membranous diphtheria with scarlet rash, which was removed by Merc-cy. and Bell., but a fever of the typhoid type remained. The urine was albuminous and scanty, pulse weak and intermittent, feet swollen. Kali-ar. 4c was given, but the symptoms grew worse. A thorough examination of the patient showed great sensitiveness of the kidneys to pressure in spite of the otherwise apathetic condition. Solid. 3x was given and in one day the urine became more profuse with corresponding improvement in the general condition. The body peeled and recovered completely. A clerk, 45, had sleeplessness and pain in the back. He casually mentioned that it took him a long time to urinate for want of the necessary pressure. This he attributed to gonorrhea, which he had years before. No sleep until 3 a.m. when he got some sleep, which was not refreshing. On rising, tired, especially upper part of thighs, then would begin the pain in the back, which extended to the loins and lasted until bedtime. Nux-v. did not relieve. The urine was found dark, slimy, reddish, slightly acid, not albuminous. Kidneys sensitive to pressure. Solid. 3x, taken steadily for three months, cured. A year afterwards there was a relapse, but this time it took the form of sciatica and Solid, again proved to be the remedy. Mrs. F., 53, wife of a farmer, stout, freshlooking, had her present trouble twenty-six years. After her confinement, which was difficult and followed by prolapse uterus, still existing. Her legs began to swell and an itching rash broke out by degrees. Menstruation had always come on at the proper time, but suddenly stopped six months before Buck saw her. Since then the itching had been almost intolerable, the legs more swollen and always cold. Appetite very poor, constant bitter taste in mouth tongue thickly coated, at the same time a rising from the stomach as if she would suffocate and at the least exertion she lost her breath. Urinated very little and mostly at night. No pains in the back, but the kidneys were sensitive to pressure. “The appearance of the lower limbs of this patient,” said Buck, “frightened me. From knee to heel they formed a bluish-red mass in the shape of a stove- pipe and were covered with little blotches and crusts.” The prolonged use of Solid. 3x, though it did not effect a cure, produced a mitigation of the whole body, so that the woman induced her eldest son to consult the doctor. This man had also trouble in his lower limbs not unlike his mother’s. A year before he had some severe throat trouble after which his lower limbs began to swell and itch. They were also tinted blue-red and covered with vesicles, his urine was scanty and his kidneys sensitive to pressure. Solid. 3x cured him in a few months. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) In prostatic and urinary affections, Sabal., Santa., Hydrang., Tritic. (2) Kidney- ache, Santa. (3) Gonorrhea and its effects, sciatica, Med. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Male - Enlarged prostate gland, obstructing flow of urine or inflammation. Weak prostate gland.

Female - Uterine enlargement organ pressed down upon the bladder. Fibroid tumors. Hemorrhage. Chronic leucorrhea in connection with copious, watery urine and sediments of mucus particles and uriniferous tubules, epithelium.

Chest - Rheumatism of the inter-costal muscles. Constitutions - Especially suited to scrofulous subjects.

Back - Backache. Lumbar ache, makes her sick all over.

Limbs - Chronic pains in the loins. Rheumatic pains in the leg. Pains in the thighs, the leg can be moved horizontally. When limbs are moved perpendicularly they feel lame. Limping, dragging gait. Lungs - Oppressed breathing. Continuous dyspnea. Allergies. Asthma. Periodical asthma with nightly dysuria. Bronchitis. Chronic catarrh of the lungs. Cough with much purulent expectoration blood- streaked. Heavy expectoration in coughing, croup and diminished urine.

Sleep - Insomnia.

Skin - Petechiae, on lower limbs with edema and itching, Gangrene, diabetic. Eczema worse from suppressed urine. Scrofulous rash, little blotches on hands and feet. Very obstinate, itching exanthemas. Exanthema of the lower limbs without swelling of the inguinal glands, but with disturbance in urinating.

Modalities - Better from profuse urination. Worse from pressure, at night.

Kidneys - Kidneys, sore and tender, ache, feel distended. Pain in kidneys extends forward to abdomen, bladder, down the thighs. Chronic nephritis. Urine, voided with difficulty.

Bladder - Cystitis. Catarrh of the bladder. Obstructed flow of urine. Scanty urine. Nightly dysuria. Catheterizing of bladder.

Temperature - Rheumatic fever, very frequent pulse, high fever.

CLINICAL - Adenoids. Amaurosis. Angina pectoris. Anorexia. Anxiety. Ascarides. Bulimia. Ciliary, neuralgia. Colds. Colic. Concussions. Constipation. Depression. Diaphragm, stitches. Dyspnea. Exophthal- mic, goiter. Eyes, pains. Face, pains. Gastric, catarrh. Glaucoma. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Hernia, inguinal. Iritis. Jaw, pain. Migraines. Nausea. Neuralgias. Otalgia. Palpitations. Pericarditis. Photophobia. Post-nasal, catarrh. Prosopalgia. Prostatorrhea. Pterygium. Rectum, cancer. Rheumatism. Scarlatina. Sigmoid flexure, cancer. Stammering, speech. Strabismus. Tinnitus. Tobacco habit. Toothache. Vertigo. Worms.

HERBAL - Spigelia anthelmia is a common weed in South America. Spigelia Mary- landica, ‘‘Pink-root’’ or “Worm-grass,” is a native of the southern states of North America. Spig. was known in Europe in Hahnemann’s time as an anthelmintic, the drug properties were learned from the natives of the Antilles.

HOMEOPATHIC - Spig. markedly affects the nerves, trifacial, heart, eyes, teeth, fibrous tissue and left side. Useful for pericarditis and other diseases of the heart. Heart disorders and neuralgias. It produces combined heart and eye symptoms, or the latter as an accompaniment. Affected by the sun. Headache beginning at sunrise, at its height at noon, declining to sunset. Pains of neuralgias and headaches increases and declines with sun. Sun pains. Neuralgia of the fifth nerve. Stabbing pains. Pains are violent, burning like hot needles or wires, jerking, tearing, stitching, radiating to other parts. Very sensitive to touch. Parts feel chilly, send shudder through frame. Body feels light while walking, heavy and sore when rising from a seat. Moves very carefully. A remedy for stitches due to the presence of worms. Child refers to the navel as the most painful part (Gran., Nux-v., Plb., Mosch.). MIND - Mental exertion difficult. Weakness of memory. Absence of ideas. Difficulty of thinking. Unfit for intellectual labor. Confusion on stooping. Sadness and discouragement. Stammering, repeats first syllable three or four times. Sits as if lost in thought, stares at a single object. Agitation and anxiety, with restlessness. Anxiety about future. Restless and anxious. So nervous he can’t control himself, feels as if he must run. Anxiety on seeing any one move quickly, on breathing deeply. Afraid ofsharp, pointed things, pins, needles (Sil., Apis.). Delusions about pins. Excitement after sadness. Irritability during chill. Mental irritability. Easily offended. Very restless and anxious. Cannot tolerate thinking of pain. Can become suicidal because the pain is too severe. Gloomy, suicidal mood. Desires death during chill. Great dejection in evening, he could have killed himself. Timidity.

Head - Feels too large. Migraines. Awn from beneath frontal eminence and temples, extending to eyes (Onos.). Semi-lateral involving left eye, pain violent, throbbing, worse making afalse step. Pain as if a band around head (Carb-ac., Cact., Gels.). Pain from left occiput to over left eye, worse stooping, making a false step, opening mouth. Supra-orbital neuralgia.

Eyes - Pupils dilated. Rheumatic ophthalmia. Feel too large, pressive pain on turning the eyes. Severe pain in and around the eyes, extending deep into socket, worse thinking of them. Ciliary neuralgia, neuritis. As if needles were thrust in. Profuse lachrymation, from affected side, tears acrid. Eyes, red, sore, drawing ache. Yellow rings about the eyes. Difficulty in raising the eyelids with painful sensation of stiffness. Evertedeyelids. Inclination to wink. Difficult to fit glasses, no settled focus, no fixed vision, latent errors of vision. Pricking in lids. Squints with worms. Photophobia.

Ears - Roaring, buzzing and pulsation in ears. Stoppage of ears. Periodical deafness, ears feel as if stuffed.

Nose - Tickling and itching of nose. Forepart of nose always dry. Chronic catarrh with post-nasal drip of bland mucus. Discharge through posterior sinuses. Flow of water during prosopalgia.

Face - Prosopalgia involving eye, zygoma, cheek, teeth, temples. Worse from touch, stooping, from morning until sunset, drinking tea, suddenly going and coming. Food - Ravenous hunger. Anorexia with violent thirst. Bulimia, sometimes with nausea and thirst. Putrid, fetid taste. Aversion to coffee, tobacco smoke and snuff. Craving for hot water which relieves chest pain.

Mouth - Foul odor from mouth. Offensive taste. Tongue, coated yellow or white, cracked, with burning or stitching pain. Tongue fissured, painful. Opening mouth aggravates headache.

Throat - Sore throat with lancinations and swelling in palate. Discharge of mucus from fauces all day, most from posterior sinuses. Swollen cervical glands. Vertigo - Vertigo on stooping with heat of head. Vertigo as if they are drunk. Vertigo, the feet as if higher than head. Vertigo worse looking down, must look straight ahead, worse standing, walking. Vertigo, hearing exalted. COMMENTS - Hahnemann said Spig. has the peculiarity that the primary action of a single unrepeated dose usually increases somewhat daily during the first seven to ten days. Experiments should be conducted with caution, seeing that 60, 80 to 100 drops of the tincture produce violent effects even in robust persons. Keynote violence. More left-sided than right, but by no means exclusively leftsided. Primarily affects the head, eyes, face, teeth and heart. Sensitivity to cold, wet and stormy weather. Produces intense pains in all parts. Hypersensitive to all pain. Burning, jerking, tearing, pressing and stitching pains, radiate and extend to other parts. Pains are largely out-pressing and proceed from within outward and below upward. Pains are worse by noise, jar, movement, change of weather, especially stormy weather. The pains were worse night and morning and in damp weather. Sensitive to pain remedies (Cham., Nux-v., Ign., Hep.). Darting and aching pains in head, nose and eyes and similar pains about the heart with slow, irregular action, but no murmur. Sudden pains at bottom of back. The body is painfully sensitive to touch. Pain feels like shiver in the body, eye or face. The part touched feels chilly. Touch sends a shudder through the whole frame. Pain radiates from a spot, not in a straight line. Darting pain. Pain will transfix (Bry.). Neuralgia, especially facial neuralgias. Pains over the left eye or the left side of the face, trigeminal neuralgias. Neuralgias with burning sensations or electric-like sensations. Intercostal neuralgias (Ran-b.). Often with neuralgia, their whole left face consists of tearing pain as if someone is cutting their face or tearing the skin off their face. Neuralgias and inflammation of the eye, amaurotic conditions, and glaucoma. Exophthalmic goiter. Intolerable pressive pains, worse on motion. Stabbing pains through eye backwards into brain. Uveitis. Ciliary neuralgia or affection to the optic nerve with cutting, stabbing pain, the eye becomes inflamed and watery. Sensation as if eye would burst. Deep pain in eye socket. Dilated pupils, can see sparks and rays of light. Severe photophobia, especially with headache, they want to be in the dark with a hand covering their left side and making no noise and staying from noise. Migraine, from occiput, settling in or over left eye (Sang, starts at the occiput and settles in the right eye; Sil. and Gels, are from occiput to forehead.). Occiput feels numb and stiff. Heart attack, aching pain. Acute heart attacks with sharp, stabbing, burning pains down the left arm (Lat-m.), or it feels as if a hot, red, burning knife is stuck into the heart and turned. The heart feels as if squeezed or compressed, sense of suffocation. Palpitation as if the whole chest will shake. Violent palpitation, can hear or see the heart beating. Irregular heartbeat. Left-sided angina. Suffocative attacks, can become anguished, think they are going to die. Chest pain, worse during deep breathing (Bry.). The movement of the rib cage aggravates. Stitching pains synchronous with the pulse. Heart disorders from rheumatism. Rheumatism. Abdominal ailments with worms. Masses of lumbrici have been expelled and also threadworms. Itching of anus and nose, colic and borborygmus. Fetid breath and fetid flatus. In one prover, the accustomed evening smoke caused violent toothache. Clarke cured a case of cardiac neuralgia caused by tobacco. He saw cardiac murmurs appearing in acute rheumatism disappear under Spig. Hochecker related the case of Miss O., 27, who was blonde, tall, and robust, and had neuralgia for several weeks without traceable cause. Pains came suddenly, twitching and tearing of left side of face, now in ear, then in lower jaw, particularly worse by mastication. Whenever the pains were about to commence a diarrhea set in. A single powder of Spig. 6c cured. Hochecker also cured with Spig. 3c, 6c, 10c and 20c a case of tic douloureux of the right side that had lasted fifteen months. In this case, each lower potency, after first relieving, caused an aggravation. So the potencies were successively raised. Spig. 20c completed the cure. This patient had dark hair and dark complexion. She attributed her trouble to taking cold in a draft when heated by dancing. A patient Clarke successfully treated for a serious heart affection with Spig. 3c said that under the treatment he had lost a pain in the right knee that he had for eighteen months and which he had not mentioned at first. The pain was as if dislocated, unable to rise from kneeling, could not find an easy position often for hours at night. Clarke found it especially useful in heart cases where constipation has been a troublesome complication. Hering gave this case, “Helminthiasis: dilated pupils, strabismus, putrid smell from mouth, itching of nose, griping pain in belly, throat inflamed, swallows often, pale redness in throat and swelling of mucus membrane, palpitation.” Meninger had a severe case of nausea during pregnancy that he cured with Spig. The only leading symptom in the case was that she was afraid of pointed things and asked her husband to take away a fork, crochet- needle, etc. Sil. has a somewhat similar symptom, but the Sil. patient hunts for pins although afraid of them. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph., Aur. (restlessness in limbs), Cocc., Puls. Antidote to: Merc., Colch. (heart). Compare: (1) Spig-m., Nux-v., Ign., Cur. (2) Aeon., Cact., - Cimic., (3) Arn., Spig. is a chronic Arn. (4) Cinnb. - supra-orbital pain. (5) Naja, Spong. - heart. (6) Sabad., Teucr., Cina - worm symptoms. (7) Pains, left eye, Aeon. (8) Neuralgia in left eye, Ther. (9) Headaches, coming and going with sun, Nat-m., Sang., Tab. (10) Eye pains, Bell., Ciliary neuralgia, Cedr., Mez. (11) Heart pains, white stools, Dig. (12) Stitches in heart. Hep., Nat-m., Kali-c., Ars., Caust. (13) Headache begins occiput and goes to left eye, (Sang, to right, Sil. to both). (14) Tic douloureux, Thuj., Cocci- s. (15) Neuralgia with pallor (with redness, Bell.). (16) Worms, Sabad., Cina, Teucr., Scirr. (17) Worse tight clothing, Lach., sensitiveness to touch, Kali-c. Compatible: Aeon, (endocarditis), Ars., Dig., Kali-c., Zinc, (heart), Iris (prosopalgia), Arn. (Carbuncle). REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Pressure in stomach. Accumulation of mucus in the stomach. Sour risings. Nausea with sensation of a worm rising in throat. Nausea when fasting.

Abdomen - Abdomen hard and painfully tight. Contact and pressure of clothes is unbearable. Colic with pinching pains in the umbilical region. Expulsion of fetid flatus.

Rectum - Constipation and diarrhea. Frequent, ineffectual urging to stool. Faints at stool. Stools of large lumps of mucous. Itching, tickling and crawling in anus and rectum. Worms, ascarides. Sensations - As if he would fall. As if intoxicated. As if head would burst. As of a band around head, as if head tightly bound. As if electric sparks in temples. Brain as if loose. As if eye would be pushed out of head. As if hairs or feathers on lashes. Face feels as if it had been scorched. As if heart compressed or squeezed with a hand. As if everything in chest were too short, loose and wobbling about. As if something tearing in chest.

Male - Discharge of prostatic fluid from the urethra.

Chest - Aching at the chest with painful oppression. Angina pectoris. Contraction of chest with anguish and obstructed respiration. Stitches in diaphragm with dyspnea. Craving for hot water which Spigelia anthelmintica relieves chest pain. Constitutions - Adapted to anemic, debilitated, rheumatic and scrofulous subjects. Suited to persons with light hair, pale, thin, bloated, weak with wrinkled, yellow, earthy skin. Children afflicted with worms, ascarides and lumbrici.

Heart - Violent sticking or compressive pains, radiating to throat, arms, scapula, worse least motion or bending double. Soreness, purring, cracking in the region of heart. Angina pectoris. Neuralgia extending to arm or both arms. Craving for hot water which relieves. Violent palpitations, audible, attending other symptoms. Frequent attacks of palpitations, especially with foul odor from mouth. Throbbing of carotids and subclavian arteries. Precordial pain and great aggravation from movement. Pericarditis. Rheumatic carditis, trembling pulse, whole left side sore. Pulse intermittent with palpitations, weak tremulous irregular.

Back - Neck stiff, pains into right temple or pain from left shoulder to neck. Cutting about the left scapula. Causations - Concussions. Worms, ascarides and lumbrici. Sunlight. Tobacco.

Limbs - Fatigue. Drawing, tearing, twitching pains in limbs and joints. Left arm numb. Pulsation in patellae. The limbs are affected mostly when walking. Lungs - Dyspnea, must lie on right side with head high, worse moving in bed, raising arms. Hydrothorax. Trembling in chest. Stitches in chest worse least motion or when breathing.

Skin - Pale, wrinkled skin of body. Painful sensibility when touched. Painful glandular swellings. Red pimples with pain when touched, as from excoriation.

Modalities - Better from rest, lying on right side with head high. Better inspiring, steady pressure, warmth. Pressure helps the neuralgia, cold application helps temporarily. Better while eating, worse immediately after. Worse light touch but better firm pressure. Worse motion, jar. Worse turning, rising, raising arms, stooping. bending forward. Worse from sex. Worse slightest draft, cold, damp, rainy, stormy weather, cold air, cold washing. Worse with the sun (Nat-m.). Worse morning, on waking. Worse blowing nose, expiration, tobacco. Worse noise. Worse thinking of problems.

Teeth - Tearing pains, worse after eating, cold, and when thinking of it. Toothache with facial pain, better by warmth or the warmth of the bed. Nerve toothache. Toothache, worse cold drinks (Mag-p., better warm drinks.), better by smoking tobacco.

Kidneys - Frequent want to urinate with profuse emission, even at night. Sudden and involuntary dribbling of urine with burning sensation in anterior part of urethra. Urine with whitish sediment.

Temperature - Chilliness on the slightest motion. Cold, offensive sweat on upper part of the body, on hands. Heat, flushes at night in back.

CLINICAL - Mania. Strabismus. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - The symptoms of Spig- m. are mainly from overdosing. A state of mania was induced…
full:
PHARMACY - spig-m. Spigelia marylandica. Worm grass. N. O. Loganiaceae. Tincture of dried root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Mania. Strabismus. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - The symptoms of Spig- m. are mainly from overdosing. A state of mania was induced in a boy from large and frequent doses of a decoction of the root. Strabismus of right eye was noted in one case. On attempting to assume erect position, seized with general tremor lasting a few seconds and leaving her exhausted. Maniacal excitement, paroxysmal laughing and crying, loud, disconnected talking, vertigo, dilated pupils, congestions. On attempting to assume erect position, seized with general tremor lasting a few seconds and leaving her exhausted. MIND - Suddenly affected with complete mental derangement(Stram.).Countenancedistorted, running and skipping. Fits of laughing and crying. Wild and incoherent talking.

Eyes - Pupils greatly dilated. Irregular movement of adductors and abductors of eyes. Strabismus of right eye. Pain in and about the eyes. Sensation of stiffness of eyelids.

Face - Wild, staring, ludicrous expression. Swelling of face and about eyes. Face flushed.

Heart - Pulse is accelerated, irregular. Mouth - Tongue pointed and tremulous. Skin - Hot and dry.

Sleep - Drowsiness. Vertigo - Dizziness. REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Spilanthes Acmella
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better moving about. Better in open air. Worse leftside. Worse indoors. Worse moving head, sneezing..
constitution: Bites. Conscientiousness, morbid. Convulsions. Eclampsia. Epilepsy. Esophagus, stricture. Eyelids, disorders. Gleet. Hydrophobia. Prostatorrhea. Ptosis. Rabies. Urine, deposits.
keynote:
PHARMACY - spil. Spilanthes acmella. Toothache plant. Paracress. N. O. Aster- aceae. Paraguay cress. Brazil. Tincture of fteshleaves, root and flower heads.Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bites. Conscientiousness, morbid. Convulsions. Eclampsia.…
full:
PHARMACY - spil. Spilanthes acmella. Toothache plant. Paracress. N. O. Aster- aceae. Paraguay cress. Brazil. Tincture of fteshleaves, root and flower heads.Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bites. Conscientiousness, morbid. Convulsions. Eclampsia. Epilepsy. Esophagus, stricture. Eyelids, disorders. Gleet. Hydrophobia. Prostatorrhea. Ptosis. Rabies. Urine, deposits.

HERBAL - Also known as “Toothache Plant” or “Paracress,” Spilanthes acmella is a flowering herb in the Asteraceae family. Its leaves and flower heads contain an analgesic agent that may be used to numb toothaches. It is native to the tropics of Brazil, though it is grown as an ornamental (and occasionally as a medicinal) in various parts of the world. Chewing on one of the flower buds will numb your mouth and make you salivate. The leaves may be used topically to treat bacterial and fungal skin diseases such as ringworm. Leaf decoction is used as diuretic and lithotriptic. Root decoction is used as purgative. The whole plant is used in treatment of dysentery. Useful for enhancing the immune sy stem’s resistance to infections. It stimulates wound healing, protects the individual from colds and flu. Decreases allergic symptoms. Antibacterial. Inhibits the yeast/fungal organism Candida albicans. Indicated for swollen glands, gum disease and all manner of acute bacterial, viral and fungal infections. Herpes. Sore throats. Useful against blood parasites, particularly malarial spirochetes, either as a prophylactic or as a treatment for malarial paroxysms. Lyme disease. Because of their high isobutylamide content, both Spilanthes and Prickly Ash have similar stimulating and therapeutic actions. REFERENCES - Murphy. ***SPIRAEA ULMARIA (Meadow-sweet) PHARMACY - spirae. Spiraea ulmaria. Meadow-sweet. Hardback. Queen of the Meadows. N. O. Rosacea. Tincture of fresh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

HOMEOPATHIC - Bojanus proved Spiraea ulmaria, taking substantial doses. A leading symptom was the production of general and local heat. Heat in throat in esophagus, under sternum, under ensiform cartilage. Bojanus was seized with remorse, a kind of morbid conscientiousness. Fullness and heaviness of head. Washing with cold water was very unpleasant and caused a feeling as if the head were too large. A scurfy condition of eyelids and heaviness of lids after afternoon sleep were noted. The urine was turbid as if mixed with clay and deposited red sand, had an oily film on the surface. The burning in esophagus was better by eating and drinking but not by empty swallowing. Burning and pressure in esophagus, feels contracted but not made worse by swallowing. Relieves irritation of the urinary passages influences the prostate gland. Checks gleet and prostatorrhea. Bites of mad animals. Heat in various parts. Hansen mentioned that Spirae. was recommended in hydrophobia, epilepsy and eclampsia. MIND - Restlessness, obliged to rise and walk about. Morbid conscientiousness. Remorse over a long-past slight indiscretion. Fearful qualms of conscience. Loathing of himself. Hydrophobia.

Head - Headache on shaking the head. Pulsations. Dullness and heaviness in the head. Pain as if a ring were tightened about the head. Sensation as if the brain wobbled to and fro. Food - Hunger disappeared. No relish for smoking.

Eyes - Sclera is bright red. Sensation as if something hot in the eyes. Eyes filled with mucus. Lachrymation with smarting and increased sensation of warmth. Indistinct vision, as through a mist, relieved by blinking and rubbing the eyes. Heaviness of the eyelids with headache.

Face - Redness of the face. Sensation of heat in the face and eyes.

Mouth - Drawing pain. Toothache in back teeth.

Throat - Sensation of increased warmth in the pharynx.

Stomach - Cold sensation in the esophagus. Burning pressure in the esophagus, better belching. Heartburn. Frequent eructations of odorless gas.

Abdomen - Sensation of heaviness in the lowerpart of the abdomen. Very offensive flatus. Odorless flatus.

Rectum - Sensation as if drawn rectum inward. Sensation as if the anus would not open sufficiently. Prickling constrictive sensation in the anus. Crawling and prickling in the rectum. Frequent desire for stool, that suddenly disappeared. Hard stool. Feces lumpy, like balls of rabbit’s dung, without being hard.

Urine - Urine turbid. Bright lemon yellow urine, almost straw-colored. Cloudy urine with an iridescent film. Looks like red sand, brick-dust powder. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Salicylic acid is in Spirae. (2) Bell. REFERENCES - Allen. Boericke. Clarke.

Male - In the morning, in bed, violent erections, with great sexual desire.

Limbs - Heaviness in all the limbs. Lungs - Dry cough. Cold feeling in lungs on inspiration.

Sleep - Overpowering sleepiness. Restless sleep, frequent waking and tossing about. Sleep full of vivid dreams. Lascivious dreams and emission.

Modalities - Better moving about. Better in open air. Worse leftside. Worse indoors. Worse moving head, sneezing.

Bladder - Burning in the urethra while urinating.

name: Spiranthes Autumnalis
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better lying on left side, on back. Worse by touch, stooping. Worse bending or raising arm, raising breast. Rheumatism of shoulders worse when bending over. Laughing causes heat in lower abdomen..
constitution: Acidity. Belching. Breasts, painful. Breath, putrid. Bums. Colic. Coryza. Dyspareunia. Eczema. Hysteria. Jaundice. Kidneys, pain. Lumbago. Milk, excessive. Nausea. Nosebleed. Rash. Rheumatism. Skin, disorders. Toothache. Vision, dimness. Vomiting.
keynote:
PHARMACY - spira. Spiranthes autumnalis. Lady’s tresses. N. O. Orchidaceae. Tincture of the root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acidity. Belching. Breasts, painful. Breath, putrid. Bums. Colic. Coryza. Dyspareunia. Eczema. Hysteria. Jaundice. Kidneys,…
full:
PHARMACY - spira. Spiranthes autumnalis. Lady’s tresses. N. O. Orchidaceae. Tincture of the root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acidity. Belching. Breasts, painful. Breath, putrid. Bums. Colic. Coryza. Dyspareunia. Eczema. Hysteria. Jaundice. Kidneys, pain. Lumbago. Milk, excessive. Nausea. Nosebleed. Rash. Rheumatism. Skin, disorders. Toothache. Vision, dimness. Vomiting.

HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany reported that the genus to which this orchid belongs received its name from the spiral arrangement of flowers. Spiranthes is an anti-phlogistic remedy akin to Aeon. Its symptoms showing congestion and inflammation. The tuberous roots of Spira, were formerly esteemed as an aphrodisiac.

HOMEOPATHIC - Spira, has been used for milk-flow in nursing women, lumbago and rheumatism. Pulsations in arteries over whole body. Acidity and burning in esophagus with eructation. Colic with drowsiness and spasmodic yawning. Appears intoxicated. Lies on left side rather than right. MIND - Melancholy. Complaining and sobbing. Ill-humor. Confusion of ideas. Indolence and boredom. Worse from mental effort. The least emotion or excitement causes palpitations.

Head - Brain troubles, worse bending or raising arm. Heaviness and heat in brain. Sensation of band tied about head. Weight on forehead. Pain in forehead and nasal bone. Pain in roots of hair. Hair falls out.

Eyes - Eyes brilliant, fixed. Pain in eyes on looking up. Burning in eyes with lachrymation. Eyes hot inflamed. Vision dim, obscured with sleepiness instantaneously lost, objects at a distance seem to move, on closing lids, sees wheels of fire. Lids swollen. Heaviness of brows.

Ears - Pain in left auditory canal. Itching in ear, externally and internally.

Nose - Pain in right nasal bones. Burning, itching at root of nose. Itching of right nostril. Dry coryza. Dripping of water from nose. Nosebleed in clots. Smell very acute.

Face - Swollen, red and hot, black, pale. Fixed, meditative expression. Burning in upper lip. Chin is red with pain. Burning itching in left cheek near mouth.

Mouth - Putrid odor from mouth. Taste acid, sweetish like nitre, bitter in morning. Salivation with dryness of mouth. Irritation of sublingual glands. Numerous small excresences on palate, which was bloody. Gums red and burning. Sensation of coldness in teeth. Pain and elongation of teeth. Toothache only at night.

Throat - Globus rising from lower abdomen to esophagus. Burning in larynx. Sensation of foreign body in throat. Incessant desire to clear throat, caused by a thick mucus. Burning in pit of throat. Irritation of tonsils. Tickling in throat, provoking cough. Sensation of acidity and burning in esophagus. Incarceration of air in esophagus. Pain on swallowing. Vertigo - Vertigo, obliged to lean head against wall, on rising from bed, worse sitting or lying. COMMENTS - The tincture of the root was proved by Dr. Patti Chagon, Duc de Sorentino, who said of it, “The action of this drug begins with decided symptoms of inflammation of the eyes, chin, chest, which become red and hot, the whole skin is dry and hot, the hands are burning, the limbs of the feet are cold most of the time, there is a sensation of oppression and heat with palpitation and a desire to uncover. “This condition lasted two hours and gave place to others including desire to meditate and complain, vertigo, pains in shoulders, boredom, loss of appetite. “The last symptoms to appear are: pains in scalp, on vertex, distress in kidneys and intestinal troubles after eating. The secretions of urine and milk were first diminished afterwards increased. “The aphrodisiac property of Spira, was shown in some of the symptoms of the proving and this bears on the increased secretion of milk. A number of symptoms appear in the lower abdomen. The globus hystericus rises from thence to esophagus. Heat in lower abdomen, preceding belchings, caused by laughing.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Cypr. (2) Skin and mucus membranes, Arum-t. (3) Desire for tight clothing, dryness of vagina, Nat-m. (4) Pain followed by numbness, Gnaph. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Epigastrium distended, intolerant of touch, painful after a meal, the pain corresponding to the pain in loins. Heat rising from stomach to head. Regurgitations. Belchings preceded by heat in lower abdomen and lancinations in colon, acid, bitter, difficult, empty. Nausea after eating. Vomiting of food right after eating.

Abdomen - Intermittent pressure in umbilical region. Pain, weakness, tympanites after a meal. Borbory gmi. Desire to tighten clothes. Piercing, sharp insupportable pain in colon, on becoming erect. Laughing heat in lower abdomen. Eruption in groin.

Rectum - Burning and itching in anus, worse during evacuation. Stool preceded and followed by prickling and itching in anus. Diarrhea or constipation, stools sour in children. Sensations - Sensation of a band tied around head. Sensation of a foreign body in throat. Coldness of teeth. Coldness of the affected part. Pulsation in arteries over whole body. Preference for lying on left side or else on back. Pain followed by numbness.

Male - Constant erections, on waking. Great desire for or repugnance to sex. Pricking pain in cords.

Female - Pressing pain in uterus. Dryness of vagina. Itching, red vulva and burning in vagina. Burning pain in vagina during sex. Bloody discharge from vagina. Yellowish leucorrhea. Food - Loss of appetite. Desire for acid, sour foods. Constant thirst.

Chest - Sensation of weakness of lungs. Sensation of dilatation of left lung. Pleuritic and intercostal pains, worse left side.

Heart - Pain in heart. Palpitations with difficult respiration from least emotional excitement. Pulse full and hard at beginning of proving afterwards small and quiet.

Back - Cramp-like pain in neck at night compelling change of position. Lumbago preventing walking. Pain in center of scapula. Pain in scapula, when standing, worse walking.

Limbs - Trembling in limbs, weakness. Sciatic pain, especially right side. Pain in shoulders. Swelling of veins of hands. Pain in all articulation of hands. Coldness of feet and toes.

Sleep - Incomplete yawning. Sleeping during day. Late falling to sleep in evening. Sleeplessness in infants. Starting up during sleep. Lascivious dreams with emissions.

Skin - Dryness of skin. Jaundice. Yellow spots. Whole skin red, red in spots. Miliary rash. Eruption of red points on buttocks with itching and heat. Blisters as from a burn with purulent secretion. Pricking over whole body. Itching in axilla in pubes, scrotum, forearms at night, backs of hands.

Modalities - Better lying on left side, on back. Worse by touch, stooping. Worse bending or raising arm, raising breast. Rheumatism of shoulders worse when bending over. Laughing causes heat in lower abdomen.

Liver - Pain in liver and spleen, on pressure. Lungs - Breathing difficult, short, panting on walking. Hacking cough, caused by tickling in larynx. Dry cough at night with burning in throat.

Kidneys - Cramp-like pain at night in kidneys, obliging change of position. Burning pain preventing stooping, worse going up stairs, better lying on back, coldness and heat.

Bladder - Bladder, pain on urinating, pain and burning after waking. Urine, abundant, scanty, decomposes rapidly. Urine, deposits a gelatinous red sediment. Breasts - Pain in breast on raising it. Burning on tips of breasts, especially the left. Milk abundant, more in left breast.

Temperature - Alternations of cold and heat. Hands alternately hot and cold. Coldness, evening, especially of hands. Affected part colder than rest of body. Coldness of feet and toes. Heat of whole skin, flushes of heat in head, followed by sensation of cold. Flushes of heat. Fever, followed by thirst. Fever at night, sweat in morning. Hands very hot. Sweat of palms.

name: Spongia Tosta
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better descending. Better lying with head low, resting in horizontal position. Better eating or drinking warm food or drink. Frosty weather helps the cough. Worse from dry, cold, wind. Worse warm room. Worse from sweets. Worse from exertion, motion, walking, stooping, rising, raising arms, ascending. Worse talking, singing. Worse touch, pressure. Worse lying on the right side. Worse at night, before midnight, full moon, after sleep..

full:
PHARMACY - spong. Spongiatosta. Roasted sponge. Common Sponge. Porifera. Radiata. N. O. Coelenterata. Tincture of the powdered sponge after toasting. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Aneurysm. Angina, pectoris. Asthma. Bronchitis. Catalepsy. Chin, disorders. Clumsiness. Colds. Constipation. Coughs. Croup. Diphtheria. Diplopia. Dyspnea. Endocarditis. Epididymitis. Exhaustion. Exophthalmos. Fainting. Gland, disorders. Goiter, exophthalmic. Headache. Heart, hypertrophy. Hernia. Hyperthyroid. Jaw joint, pain. Laryngismus. Laryngitis. Lung, disorders. Myopia. Orchitis. Rheumatic, fever. Rheumatism. Somnambulism. Testicles, disorders. Thyroid, disorders. Tuberculosis. Varicose, veins. Whooping cough. Worms.

HOMEOPATHIC - According to Hahnemann, toasted sponge was first mentioned as a specific for goiter by the alchemist Arnold Von Villanova in the thirteenth century, but it was generally given mixed with other substances and had fallen into disuse when Hahnemann proved it. The virtues of Spong, have been attributed to the iodine contained in it and partially liberated by the presence of roasting. But Spong, contains many other elements besides iodine and has a distinctive action of its own. Affects the heart valves, larynx, trachea and glands, especially ductless. Useful for the symptoms of the respiratory organs, cough, croup, heart disorders and tubercular diathesis. Keynote dryness of mucus membranes, of tongue, pharynx, larynx, and trachea. Cough is caused by dryness, hacking, crowing, “dry as a bone,” sounding like a saw being driven through a pine board. Cough is excited by talking, by dry, cold winds, better by eating or drinking, swallowing, especially from warm food. Dry, chronic, sympathetic cough of organic heart disease. Anxiety with pain in the region of heart or dyspnea. Hypertrophy of the heart. The right heart is affected, with asthmatic symptoms. Anxiety and difficult breathing, terrible sinking sensation. Dry asthma. In laryngismus, croup and asthma the patient rouses up generally after midnight with fear of suffocation and death. Contraction of larynx as if suddenly grasped. The larynx is sensitive, but has not the hyperesthesia of Lach. The sputa cannot be raised, must be swallowed, swallowing relieves. Exhaustion and heaviness of the body with slight exertion, he must lie down with orgasms of blood to chest, face etc. Feels stuffed up. Hard swelling of glands, thyroid. As if everything were shaking and moving about in goiter. Clothes feel uncomfortable. Numbness of lower half of the body. Stiff without ability to move. Faint, when losing her breath, on raising hands above head. Worse after sleep (Lach.). Rises up in sleep as if in a great fright. MIND - Timidity. Anxiety and difficult breathing. Fear of future. Terror. Anxiety with pain in the region of heart or dyspnea. Aggravated from excitement and thinking of symptoms. Every excitement increases the cough. Starting from sleep. Starting from trifles. Fear of death from suffocation (Puls., Aeon, Phos., Stram.), wakes frightened and anxious. Fear of dying. Anxiety about his heart, fear of heart disease. Attacks of anguish and pain with fear. Anxiety during flushes of heat. Obstinate and improper behavior. Abusive. Quarrelsome. Tired of life. Despair during fever. Apprehension of a fatal termination of his disease. Inconsolable. Despondent about loss of sexual power. Suicidal disposition during perspiration. Weeps with dreams, whooping cough, fever, sweat. Ill humor, crying, indifference to everything, during croup. Taciturn and discontented mood, not disposed to talk. Indifference to everything. Cheerful alternating with aversion to work. Irresistible desire to sing with excessive mirth, followed by sadness. Singing alternating with distraction.

Head - Rush of blood, bursting headache, worse forehead. Throbbing, pulsation, heaviness and fullness of head. Headache with lachrymation. Pressing headache. Sensation as if hair were standing on end, on vertex. Violent itching in scalp.

Eyes - Protrude, staring. Red with lachrymation and burning. Watering, gummy or mucus discharge. Diplopia, better lying down.

Ears - Otalgia with contractive pain. Ulceration of external ear. Boils on left ear painful to touch. Inflamed nodule in left concha. Heat, pressure in ears. Hard of hearing. Dull ringing in ears.

Nose - Nose pinched, cold. Chronic dryness. Dry, nasal catarrh. Dry coryza, nose feels stuffed up. Fluent coryza, alternating with stoppage. Nostrils wide open, fan like motion.

Face - Terrified, anxious expression. Blue lips. Pale from exercise instead of ruddy glow. Cold sweat on chin. Chin numb.

Mouth - Sweetish taste. Salivation. Tongue dry and brown. Mouth and edge of tongue covered with vesicles. Burning pain. Speech difficult.

Throat - Burning and stinging. Stitches and dryness. Bitter taste. Sensation as if plug in larynx. Diphtheria. Larynx, painful, dry, constricted worse touch, singing, talking or swallowing, he grasps it. Laryngeal tuberculosis. Sore throat, worse eating sweet things. Clears throat constantly. Throat symptoms better lying on back. Swallows water in small quantity and with difficulty. Numb externally. Hoarseness with many complaints, cough, coryza. Voice gives way when singing or talking. Vertigo - Vertigo with giddiness to such an extent as to fall. Vertigo with a sensation as if head were about to fall on one side. Vertigo with nausea, on waking at night. COMMENTS - The action of Spong, on the respiratory organs is closely connected with its action on the glandular system, Spongia tosta the lymphatics. The thyroid and testes are indurated. The blood, heart and veins are also involved and, with the protruding eyes, a perfect picture of exophthalmic goiter is produced. Tuberculosis of the larynx. Tuberculosis of apices, with commencing solidification, tubercles spreading downwards. Tuberculosis of the lungs with weakness of the voice and a chronic, dry, hacking cough. Congestion of chest coming on when the patient is moving about, with sudden weakness as if he would fall. Croup (Aeon., Hep., Samb., Brom., and lod.), of the larynx. Croupy deposits on the valves of the heart. Chronic bronchitis with a deep, resonating cough, especially in the elderly, worse excitement or exertion, with constant dryness, hacking. Must sit up and lean forward. Respiratory symptoms in excited children. Dry asthma with asthmatic cough, wheezing and whistling. Laryngitis with change of voice, the throat feels plugged up, like the larynx was grabbed. Rapid and suffocative breathing with a deep, resonating cough. Slow and deep breathing. Paralyzed with dryness and constriction, must breathe slowly. Sensation of a sponge in the throat, as though they had to breathe through a sponge. Wakes up at night suffocating (Aeon., Lach.), with dryness. Fear of suffocation. General dryness of the mucus membranes (Bry., Alum., Nux-m.). Suffocating, constricting dryness. Dry nasal passages with dry cough, worse in acold, dry wind (Aeon.). Chronic sore throat, especially with swollen glands and cough. Dry, hacking coughs (Bry., Rumx.). Deep, resonating coughs. Foghorn coughs with a shrill at the end, peaks at the end. Burning and rawness in the chest with the coughing. As though the chest would burst because of all the coughing. Cough is worse in cold, dry weather, wind, warm and stuffy rooms. Cough worse from exertion. Tobacco aggravates the cough. Worse lying down and with head lowered. Talking aggravates, can’t talk during attacks. Desires warm fluids. Hypertrophy of the heart with asthma. Sensation as though the heart will burst. In a heart attack the heart feels bigger and bigger (Cact. feels smaller and smaller.). Constriction of the chest and the heart (Cact.). Stinging, pressing pain in the heart with violent gasping. Excitement of the nerves, tendency to start, twitching of muscles with fever. Stiff, without ability to move. “Conscious but unable to act on her limbs” as in a cataleptic state. Clumsiness of the body. Faint when losing breath. Feeling of numbness of lower half of body. Thyroid problems (Calc-i., Fuc., Sep., Nat-m., Thyr.). Hyperthyroid. Goiter. Exophthalmic goiter, protruding eyes, staring, headaches and enlarged thyroid. Keynote sensation of something alive in the goiter, as if something moving there. Swollen and hard glands, causes difficulty in breathing, suffocative dryness. There may be tingling or shooting pain in the thyroid. Testicular problems. Metastasis of mumps to the testes (Puls., Carb-v.), orto the breast. Hard, swollen, indurated testicles. Pressing, squeezing or sharp pains in the testicles. The testicles are swollen and very painful (Clem., Aur., and Puls.). Orchitis, with heaviness and screw-like squeezing pain in cord and testicles. Orchitis from suppressed gonorrhea (Thuj.). Chill usually commences across the back, cannot be warmed. Chill, followed by heat, extendiung over the whole body except the thighs, which remain numb and chilly. Frequent flashes of heat. Skin is hot and dry. Etiology of exposure to cold, dry wind (Aeon.), but takes a day or so to come out. Worse after sleep, or sleeps into the aggravation (Lach.). Worse when thinking of the symptoms (Ox-ac.). Aversion to tobacco and aggravated from it. Problems may start on the right and go to the left. Kent gave the indication “Rheumatic fever after having been over-heated with arising heart complications.” Nash gave the keynote of Spong, in valvular diseases^ “Awakes out of sleep from a sense of suffocation with violent, loud cough, great alarm, agitation, anxiety and difficult respiration.” Nash said it is better than Lach., and relieves the “dry, chronic, sympathetic cough of organic heart disease” more frequently and more permanently than Naja. Psor. also meets thickening of joints after rheumatic fever. Boenninghausen’s croup powders consisted of a sequence of Aeon., Spong., and Hep., given in that order. Spong, is dry. Hep. rattling, Spong, worse before midnight, Hep. worse after midnight. RELATIONS - Anlidoied by: Camph. Compare: (1) Aeon., Hep., Brom. (2) lod. - goiter. Hep. (3) Lach., Merc., Prot. (4) Laryngitis, Samb., Lach. (5) Cough better by eating, Anae. (6) Dry tongue, Nux-m. (7) Better warm drinks, Ars., Alum., Lyc., Nux-v. (8) Heart, Naja, Sep., Kalm., Lach. (9) Orchitis, Gels., Puls., Ham. (10) Jawjoint as if dislocated, Rhus-t. (11) Worse thinking of symptoms, Ox-ac., Pip-m. (12) Tubercular diathesis, Bac., Tub., Dros. Follows well: Aeon., Hep. Followed well by: Brom., Carb-v. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Cannot bear tight clothing. Stomach feels flaccid as if standing open. Chill in pit of stomach. Sour regurgitations. Frequent hiccough. Nausea with acidity in mouth. Vomiting after having partaken of milk.

Abdomen - Violent action of abdominal muscles during inspiration. Viscera drawn up against diaphragm. Pain in abdomen instead of menses.

Rectum - Hard and retarded evacuations. Loose, whitish evacuations. Tenesmus in the anus during the evacuation. Itching, smarting and pain as from excoriation in anus. Passage of ascarides from rectum and tingling in rectum. Diarrhea with ascarides. Sensations - As if head would fall to one side. As if tipsy. As if skull would burst. As if hair were standing on end. Eyes as if twisted around. As if a battery of guns were discharged in ears. Stitches as if passing through tympanum. As if skin of neck were compressed between fingers. As if air were passing up and down thyroid and cervical glands.

Male - Screwing, squeezing or stitches up into cord and testes. Orchitis. Testes hard and swollen. Swelling of spermatic cord and testicles with pain and tenderness. Epididymitis. Fistulous opening in scrotum with little, thick, white discharge. Genitals hot.

Female - Hunger and palpitations of heart before menses. Pain in sacrum before menses or instead of menses. Awakes with suffocative spells during menses (Cupr., lod., Lach.). Amenorrhea with asthma (Puls.). Food - Excessive úúist. great hunger. Desire for dainties, sweets aggravate. Glands - Glands painful on pressure. Swelling and induration of glands. Cervical glands swollen with tensive pain on turning head. Thyroid disorders. Hyperthyroid. Thyroid gland swollen, even with the chin. Exophthalmic goiter. Goiter with suffocative spells, worse touching neck or pressure or pains with heart.

Chest - Oppression and heat of chest with sudden weakness. Chest weak, can scarcely talk, choking on falling to sleep. Fullness and obstruction in chest. A fixed, sharp and pressive pain. Spasmodic, constrictive pains. Shootings in chest. Burning, rawness, soreness in chest. Constitutions - Suited to blue-eyed, fair-haired patients (lod. acts best on brunettes). Children with a fair complexion, lax fiber, swollen glands. Suited to scrofulous disorders.

Heart - Angina pectoris, faintness and anxious sweat. Surging of heart into chest, as if it would force out upward. Blood surging up to neck, head and face with closure of eyelids and tears. Hypertrophy of heart, especially right, with asthmatic symptoms. Valvular insufficiency. Aneurysm of the aorta. Rheumatic endocarditis. Pulse frequent, hard, full or feeble. Rapid and violent palpitations with dyspnea, cannot lie down, feels best resting in horizontal position. Awakened suddenly after midnight with pain and suffocation, flushed, hot and frightened to death (Aeon.). Dry, chronic sympathetic cough of organic heart disease (Naja.).

Back - Neck as if a cord about. Pain in sacrum instead of menses. Cramps in the muscles of neck. Coldness in back, not better by warmth of stove.

Limbs - Fingers numb. Numbness of lower half of the body. Thighs, numb and cold. Pain in the knees, when rising from kneeling. Thickening of joints after rheumatic fever. Lungs - Great dryness of all air-passages. Noisy, whistling inspiration on falling to sleep. Suffocation, as from a plug, valve or leaf. Anxious, gasping breathing. As if breathing through a dry sponge. Respiration short, panting, difficult. Asthma, must throw head back, worse full moon. Croup, worse during inspiration and before midnight. Bronchial catarrh with wheezing, asthmatic cough, worse cold air with profuse expectoration and suffocation.

Sleep - Sleeplessness with fantastic dreams and delirium on going to sleep. Generally worse after sleep or sleeps into an aggravation (Lach.). Awakes in a fright andfeels as if suffocating with terror and fear. Starting from sleep. Sad, anxious, frightful dreams. Somnambulism.

Skin - Sensitive to touch. Biting, itching of the whole body. Red, itching blotches. Herpes. Ringworm. Ulcers with scanty discharge. Erysipelas, erythema. Pricking, itching during fever. Measles. Itching in swollen glands.

Modalities - Better descending. Better lying with head low, resting in horizontal position. Better eating or drinking warm food or drink. Frosty weather helps the cough. Worse from dry, cold, wind. Worse warm room. Worse from sweets. Worse from exertion, motion, walking, stooping, rising, raising arms, ascending. Worse talking, singing. Worse touch, pressure. Worse lying on the right side. Worse at night, before midnight, full moon, after sleep.

Cough - Dry, barking, croupy cough, larynx sensitive to touch. Deep, resonating coughs. Foghorn coughs. Croup, worse during inspiration and before midnight. Asthmatic cough. Cough abates after eating or drinking, especially warm drinks. Irrepressible cough from a spot deep in chest, as if raw and sore. Dry, chronic, sympathetic cough of organic heart disease. Cough is caused by dryness, hacking, crowing, “dry as a bone,” sounding like a saw being driven through a pine board. Cough is excited by talking. Cough worse by dry, cold winds, better by eating or drinking, swallowing, especially from warm food. Whooping cough.

Temperature - Attacks of heat with anxiety. Heat, redness of face, perspiration. Heat in flushes with anxiety, cardiac pain, would rather die, with cold moist thighs, worse thinking of it. Heat and sudden weakness after walking in open air, must lie down.

name: Squilla Maritima
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from rest, lying down in bed, sitting up, wrapping warmly. Better expectoration even a small quantity. Worse early morning. Worse motion, exertion, ascending. Worse inspiration, coughing, cold air, uncovering. Drinking cold water causes cough..
constitution: Angina, pectoris. Ascites. Asthma. Bright’s, disease. Bronchitis. Broncho-pneumonia. Conjunctivitis, phlyctenular. Coryza. Cough, caiarrhaL Diabetes, insipidus. Dropsy, splenic. Dyspnea. Eyes, disorders. Fidgets. Heart, palpitations. Hydrothorax. Lungs, disorders. Measles. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Spleen, disorders. Toothaches. Urine, excessive. Whooping cough. Worms.
keynote:
PHARMACY - squil. Squilla maritima. Sea onion. Squill. N. O. Liliaceae. Red variety. Hyacinthaceae. Tincture of fresh bulb. His- iorical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina, pectoris. Ascites. Asthma. Bright’s, disease. Bronchitis. Broncho-pneumonia.…
full:
PHARMACY - squil. Squilla maritima. Sea onion. Squill. N. O. Liliaceae. Red variety. Hyacinthaceae. Tincture of fresh bulb. His- iorical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina, pectoris. Ascites. Asthma. Bright’s, disease. Bronchitis. Broncho-pneumonia. Conjunctivitis, phlyctenular. Coryza. Cough, caiarrhaL Diabetes, insipidus. Dropsy, splenic. Dyspnea. Eyes, disorders. Fidgets. Heart, palpitations. Hydrothorax. Lungs, disorders. Measles. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Spleen, disorders. Toothaches. Urine, excessive. Whooping cough. Worms.

HERBAL - Squilla maritima grows on the shores of the Mediterranean Sea and has had a place in medicine from the most ancient time. The genus Squillais distinguished from Allium by having the flowers inserted one above the other on the scape, and from Ornithogalum by having the petals deciduous. Green’s Herbal noted that Squil. promotes expectoration and urine in large doses, vomiting and purging. “Its cardiac action is exactly the same as that of Digitalis.” An old rule runs “Put squills in every coughmixture.” Mile recorded “Diuretic, expectorant, emetic, cathartic and a narcotic-acrid poison in large doses it produces inflammation of the alimentary and urinary canals and a dose of 24 grains has proved fatal.” According to Hamilton, Avicenna employed Squil. “in complaints of the gums in inveterate coughs in diseases of the spleen in dropsy and jaundice and forbids its use in ulceration of the viscera,” the last caution also being mentioned by Celsus.

HOMEOPATHIC - Cooper noted that Squil., if much handled, irritates the skin, and in large doses excites nausea, strangury, bloody urine and hemorrhoids. Fatal inflammation, gangrene of stomach and bowels in small doses. The continuous use of squills seems to cause teeth and gums to ache. The reputation of Squil. as a splenic was revived by Rademacher, whom Burnett quoted, “I have found it quickly and surely helpful in painful spleen diseases disorders painful and beyond any doubt in and of the spleen. In those dull pains on the border of the left hypochondriac and epigastric regions, there being no signs of any liver affection, I have used Squil. as a remedy with advantage.” Rademacher also mentioned as cured by Squil. those so-called “stomachpains” that are made much better by lying on the left side and probably in reality splenic, one case of asthma from a splenic affection with nocturnal exacerbation, and possibly splenic dropsy. Burnett improved on Rademacher’s teachings and applied Squil. successfully in cases of spleen-cough. Hahnemann’s proving brought out many symptoms, apparently arising from the spleen, notably stitches under the free'ribs of the left side. Squil. affects the serous and mucus membranes of the respiratory and digestive tract and acts also on the kidneys, heart and Squilla marítima spleen. Slow acting, useful for those condition which require several days to reach their maximum. Persistent, dull, rheumatic pains throughout the body. A spleen remedy, stitches under left free ribs. Heart and kidney ailments. Bronchopneumonia. Valuable in chronic bronchitis of old people with mucus rales, dyspnea and scanty urine. Exudations and profuse secretions. Dropsy with profuse urine. Gurglings. Cardio-urinary effects. Action is like Dig.; follows Dig. when it fails to relieve dropsical conditions. MIND - Great anxiety of the mind. Angry about trifles. Malicious. Haughty. Aversion to mental and bodily labor. Inclination to sit, aversion to bed. Confusion after sleeping, on walking. Delirium after hemorrhage. Fear of death.

Head - Stinging headache. Headache in morning on waking, with pressing pains. Painful sensitiveness of vertex every morning. Pulsation in head when raising it.

Eyes - Left eye looks much smaller than right. Child rubs eyes and face much, as if to relieve itching in brain affectations, measles. As if swimming in cold water. Tears with cough. Staring look, eyes wide open.

Ears - Tearing behind left ear. Tearing pains in both ears.

Nose - Violent sneezing with fluent acrid coryza. Sneezing during cough. Copious running worse in morning. Coryza with ulcerated nostrils. Humid eruptions under nose with itching.

Face - Changeable expression and color of face. Distorted countenance. Child rubs the face with fist during cough. Lips twitch and are covered with yellow crusts. Humid, spreading eruption on upper lip. Black, cracked lips and black teeth.

Mouth - Taste, sweet of food, especially soup and meat. Bitter taste to bread. In- Squilla maritima creased saliva. Open, dry mouth. Scraping, burning on palate. Vesicles on tongue. Black spots on teeth.

Throat - Dryness in throat. Burning in mouth and throat. Irritation in throat causing constant cough. Pain in submaxillary glands. Vertigo - Vertigo in the morning with nausea. Vertigo as if he would fall sideways on rising from bed. Cloudy dizziness. COMMENTS - Burnett used the Acetum Squil. and Clarke gave this (five drops of in water three times a day) with excellent effect in the case of an elderly woman, very gouty, who had a distressing paroxysmal cough with a pain extending from splenic region into the throat. The cough caused sneezing, flow of tears, spurting of urine and even involuntary stools. The kidneys are acted on by Squil. and many of the traditional uses of the drug have been with the idea of eliminating dropsical effusions by reproducing a great flow of urine. Hahnemann pointed out that the excessive flow of urine accompanying dropsy and other complaints was one of the best indications for its use. Boger added the heart to the organs primarily affected by Squil. He gave three cases. Mr. B. suffered from angina pectoris, forcible cardiac contractions, profuse urine, much loose mucus in throat and trachea, heart pain indefinite but very severe. Squil. 30c relieved in a few hours and kept him free from an attack for three months. Miss L., pleuro-pneumonia, pulse 132, temperature 103 F, respiration 30, must sit erect in bed. Stitching pains in left chest, constant hacking cough. Frequent, hot, scanty urine, great weakness and anorexia. Squil. 100,000c cured. A boy, 7, hay fever for third year in succession. Teeth show black marks, constantly rubs eyes and sneezes, bloated about eyes and face, loose cough. Under Squil. there was complete relief in two days and no further trouble that season. Boger mentioned that Lippe noted “black teeth” as a symptom of Squil. Boger added that the nails become brittle and split and that veterinarians use Squil. for cracked hoof in horses. The use of Squil. as an “expectorant” depends on its power of producing free secretion from the respiratory mucus membranes; in homeopathy this free secretion is one of the leading indications. Hering said Squil. is suited to the pleurisy and pneumonia that follow blood-letting. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph. Compare: (1/Headache, worse motion, chest symptoms, Bry. (2) Bry. cough is worse change to warm, Squil. cough worse change to cold air. (3) Stitches, swollen upper eyelids, Kali-c. (4) Cold drink causes or worse cough, Lyc., Sil. (better by cough, Caust.). (5) Expectoration sweetish and offensive, Calc., Stann. (6) Spurting of urine when coughing, Caust., Alum., Con., Nat-m., Puls. (7) Dig., Stroph., Apoc., Bry., Kali-c. Compatible after: Bry. Squil. follows Dig., if this fails to relieve water-logged cases. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Pressure in stomach as from a stone. Stomach pains are better lying on left side. Constant nausea in pit of stomach. Nausea during the morning cough.

Abdomen - Painful diseases of the spleen. Aching in hypochondria. Cutting pain in abdomen. Rumbling and gurgling in paroxysms above pubic region, better eating. Bubbling sensation in muscles of right side. Frequent discharge of fetid flatulence. Ascites with scanty urine.

Rectum - Stitches in anus when walking. Itching in anus. Painless constipation. Stools dark, brown, frothy, very offensive. Diarrhea, stool very offensive, watery. Passes thread worms and white tissues with tenesmus. Sensations - Prominent stitches, in teeth, in chest, in head. Eyes as if swimming in cold water. Nostrils as if sore. As if chest too tight. Tickling creeping in chest. As if intestines would burst through abdomen. As if diarrhea would set in.

Male - Erotic pollutions. Dull stitches in glans causing anxiety. Compressive pain in testicles.

Female - Atony of the cervix, uterus. Hemorrhage from uterus. Food - Insatiable appetite. Longing for acids. The food tastes bitter, especially bread. Tastes sweet, especially soup and meat. Tastelessness of tobacco when smoked. Thirst for cold drinks. Drinks in sips during dyspnea.

Chest - Stitches in chest. Perspiration in armpit.

Heart - A cardiac stimulant affecting the peripheral vessels and coronary arteries. Pulse small and slow, slightly hard.

Back - Stiffness of nape of neck. Bubbling beneath scapula. Painful jerking above left scapula. Drawing in left scapula.

Limbs - Hands and feet cold, body hot (Meny.). Feet get sore from standing. Nails become brittle and split. Lungs - Wheezing. Splenic asthma. Dyspnea and stitches in chest and painful contraction of abdominal muscles. Sneezing, throat irritated, short, dry cough, must take a deep breath. Pleurisy. Bronchopneumonia. Fluent coryza, margins of nostrils feel sore. Sneezing with coughing. Cough, stubborn, dry, rattling, disturbs sleep. Child rubs face with fist during cough (Caust., Puls.). Violent, exhausting cough with much mucus, v,ilh involuntary spurting of urine and sneezing. Expectoration, easy, heavy, difficult in small round balls of sweetish taste, white or reddish offensive. Profuse, salty, and a slimy expectoration. Cough provoked by taking a deep breath or cold drinks from exertion. Cough changes from warm to cold air. Cough of measles.

Sleep - Frequent yawning without sleepiness. Restless sleep, with much tossing about. Dreamed that his body was excessively swollen.

Skin - Handling the fresh squills caused blisters. Eruptions like itch, with burningitching. Small red spots all over the body with pricking pain. Soreness in the bends of the joints. Hard swellings. Gangrene.

Modalities - Better from rest, lying down in bed, sitting up, wrapping warmly. Better expectoration even a small quantity. Worse early morning. Worse motion, exertion, ascending. Worse inspiration, coughing, cold air, uncovering. Drinking cold water causes cough.

Kidneys - Great urging, much watery urine, involuntary spurting of urine when coughing (Caust., Puls.). Frequent calls to urinate at night, passing large quantities (Ph-ac.). Bloody urine. Feces escape when urinating.

Temperature - Chill internally at night with external heat. Heat with aversion to uncover. Heat, dry, burning, internally predominates. Whenever he uncovers himself during the fever he suffers from chilliness and pain. Perspiration wanting, even during the violent burning heat.

PHARMACY - stach. Stacnys betónica. Wood betony. N. O. Labiate. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Belching. Colds. Diaphragm, paralysis. Headaches. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - Berridge published the proving of Stach. made by Croker and himself with some others. Pains in various parts, dizziness, fullness in head and eyes with disposition to take cold. Tired, especially in legs. Great sensitiveness to take cold. A feeling of oppressed breathing as from paralysis of diaphragm. Stach. has been used in eye-waters and as a remedy for headaches. MIND - Inability to concentrate mind. Distracted easily. Mental dullness.

Head - Stitches in right temple. Fullness over and in eyes as if they would burst. Dull, heavy action in frontal region better walking about in room.

Eyes - Heavy, sleepy feeling in eyes. Pain in eyeballs as if too tense, worse looking at light, reading, thinking, bending head down.

Ears - Slight earache.

Nose - Frequent sneezing, increased nasal mucus on going indoors from open air.

Stomach - Warmth in stomach increasing to sharp cutting pain. Weight in stomach with feeling of sickness. Belchings, tasting of drug.

Abdomen - Pains in abdomen, hepatic region and of transverse colon, also in gallbladder and right inguinal region and spermatic cords.

Limbs - Shooting pain in back of both wrist joints. Wrist drops. Pain in right popliteal space down leg, which feels paralyzed.

Liver - Pains in hepatic region and gallbladder. Lungs - Breathing oppressed as from paralysis of diaphragm, constriction just behind ensiform cartilage, on walking up hill must keep mouth open.

Kidneys - Woke with desire to urinate in night. Urine high-colored, ammoniacal.

Temperature - Free perspiration. In night profuse sweat, limited to head, neck and chest. Vertigo - Dizziness better open air, worse closing eyes or moving head. RELATIONS - Compare: (6) Lycps. and the Labiate. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - stann-i. Stannum iodatum. Tin iodide. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Coughs. Lung, disorders. Tuberculosis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Stann-i. is valuable in chronic chest diseases characterized by tissue changes, with persistent inclination to cough. It is indicated in cases that ‘hang fire’ and need an alternative. Stann-i. has been used in preference to Stann. in some tubercular cases in which the general features of Stann. were present. Persistent inclination to cough, excited by tickling dry spot in the throat, apparently at root of tongue. Dryness of throat. Tracheal and bronchial irritation of smokers. Pulmonary symptoms, cough, loud, hollow, ending with expectoration (Phel.). Purulent infiltration. Stonham noted that in advanced tuberculosis when Stann-i. has not taken effect, an additional dose of iodine in milk caused the drug to have its usual beneficial effect.

Chest - Feeling of dryness, weakness in chest and throat and increased oppression. Lungs - Persistent cough, excited by tickling, dry spot in the throat. Cough beginning with a weak sounding cough with short breath, soon gathers strength and sound. Coughs up a copious, pale yellowish expectoration. Consolidation in middle of right lung. COMMENTS - O. S. Haines considered Stann-i. especially indicated where the patient “has a clear complexion and long eyelashes and where the progress of the disease is rapid.” He used the 2x trituration. M. D. Youngman found it a deeply acting drug, chiefly of value in chronic chest diseases characterized by plastic tissue changes. Stann-i. is indicated in cases that “hang fire” and need an “alterative.” Youngman gave the keynote, “A persistent inclination to cough. Cough excited by a tickling dry spot in the throat, sometimes in one place, sometimes in another often apparently at root of tongue.” This cough, which begins as a weak- sounding cough, accompanied by shortness of breath. The cough soon gathers strength and sound and induces raising of a free, copious, pale yellowish expectoration, which at first aggravates. Buf is soon followed by a feeling of dryness, weakness in throat and chest and increased oppression. An inveterate smoker, who had a cough of this kind, said it came from his throat and ascribed it to his smoking. Youngman found consolidation areas in the middle of the right lung. There was weak feeling in chest after coughing. Stann-i. 3x trituration, greatly relieved. The man was sent to a high altitude, where he enjoyed perfect health and was freed from his smoking habit. REFERENCES-Clarke.
