full:
PHARMACY - stram. Stramonium. Jimson weed. Thornapple. Datura stramonium. Jamestown-weed. Stink- weed. N. O. Solanaceae. Grows in vicinity of cultivation on rank soil where refuse is deposited in all parts of the world. Tincture of fresh plant in flower and fruit. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Anasarca. Aphasia. Bedwetting. Bums. Catalepsy. Chordee. Chorea. Delirium. Delirium tremens. Delusions. Ecstasy. Epilepsy. Esophagus, spasms. Eyes disorders. Fevers. Headache, sun. Hiccoughs. Hysteria. Injuries. Insanity. Lochia offensive. Locomotor ataxia. Mania. Meningitis. Nym- phomania. Parkinson’s disease. Rabies. Sexual mania. Scarlatina. Schizophrenia. Stammering speech. Starting. Strabismus. Strokes. Sunstroke. Tetanus. Thirst. Tremors. Trismus. Typhus.

HOMEOPATHIC - According to Teste, Stoerck, one of Hahnemann’s predecessors, was the first to use Stram. in modern times. Stoerck first tried it in mental alienation, because it was supposed to produce “a marked and persistent disorder of the mental faculties.” Hahnemann proved it and introduced it into the Homeopathic Materia Medica. In his introduction to the remedy he pointed out that, although it produces many symptoms, it does not in its primary effects cause actual pain. Hahnemann attached a good deal of importance to this. Hahnemann said “Stram. allays some spasmodic movements and restores suppressed excretions in several cases in which absence of pain is a prominent symptom.” Teste specifically mentioned its usefulness in some kinds of mania, particularly in nymphomania of lying-in women. Marked and persistent disorder of the mental faculty. Hysteria, weeping, laughing with sexual excitement. Certain forms of religious mania in exaggerated and ridiculous scruple of conscience. Fixed notion that some unpardonable sin has been committed which the patient is unable to remember. Notion that he is possessed of the devil. Hallucinations. Delusions as to size and distance. Sensation as if limbs were separated from the body. Delirium tremens. Suppressed secretions and excretions, including urine and stool. Absence of pain and muscular mobility especially of muscles of expression and of locomotion. Gyratory and graceful motions. Increases the mobility of the muscles of expression and of locomotion, the motions may be graceful, rhythmic or disorderly of head and arms. Parkinson’s disease. Trembling of limbs. Nervous tremors. Convulsions, spasms worse at night after masturbation. Tonic and clonic spasms alternately. Paralysis of one side, convulsions of the other side or unilateral paralysis with twitching. General paralysis of the insane. Chorea, epilepsy from fright. Catalepsy, limbs can be moved by others. Traumatic neuritis. MIND - Hallucinations, fixed notions, terrifying delirium etc. Active variable delirium, delirium tremens. Delirium with desire to escape (Bell., Bry., Rhus-t.). Raving mania with cold sweat. Maniac, curses, tears ones clothes with teeth. Devout, earnest, beseeching and ceaseless talking. Violent and lewd speech. Paranoid. Schizophrenia. Manic-depression. Religious insanity. Wants to kill people or himself. Exposes himself. Rapid changes from joy to sadness. Wife thinks husband neglecting her. Man thinks his wife faithless. Stupid, imbecile. Fearful hallucinations that terrify the patient, sees ghosts, vividly brilliant or hideous phantoms, animals, jumping sideways out of ground or running to him. Wildly excited, as in night terrors. Hears voices, talks with spirits. Delusions about his identity, thinks himself tall, double, a part missing. Terrors, cannot bear solitude or darkness, must have light and company. Dread of darkness and has a horror of shining objects. Fear and anxiety on hearing water run. Sight of water or anything glittering brings on spasms. Anxiety when going

Head - Headache with tendency to speak incoherently. Pain in forehead and over eyebrows, beginning at 9 a.m., worse until noon. Boring pain, preceded by obscure vision. Headache from sun. Rush of blood to head, staggers with tendency to fall forward and to the left. Meningitis irom suppressed ear discharge. Raises head frequently from the pillow and drops it again during unconsciousness, delirium, puerperal fever.

Eyes - Fixed, sparkling, staring wide open. Half open in sleep. Pupils dilated. Lachrymation with headache, fever, otalgia. Diplopia. Night-blindness. Green vision. Hallucinations in which everything looks jumbled. An objects look black, crooked, small, large. Parts of the body seem enormously swollen. Small objects look large. Loss of vision, complains that it is dark and calls for more light. All objects look black. Squint in brain disorders during convulsions, worse terror, fear. Strabismus.

Ears - Sensation as if air rushing out of ear. Deafness. Hallucinations of hearing.

Nose - Alae nasi white with a red face. Obstruction of the nose. Nasal discharge yellow, bad-smelling. Nose feels obstructed and dry, though she is able to breathe through it.

Face - Pale face. Red, bloated, hot, circumscribed redness of cheeks. Blood rushes to face, distorted. Expression of terror. Expression rapidly changing, now flushed, now pale, a sardonic grin, then expression of terror. Thinks face elongated. Forehead wrinkled, frowning in brain diseases. Lips, dry, glued together. Chewing motion. Lockjaw.

Mouth - Dry, dribbling of viscid saliva. Constantly spits saliva. Cannot swallow on account of spasm. Chewing motion. Grinding of the teeth. Fine red dots on tongue. Tongue, dry, parched, swollen, hangs out of the mouth. Stammering. Aphasia. Risus sardonicus.

Throat - Dry with great thirst, yet dreads water, it chokes him. Spasms, twitching of larynx. Up and down movement of larynx as in swallowing. Swallowing, difficult, hasty. As if boiling water rising in throat. Voice hoarse and croaking, suddenly fails in higher tones. Vertigo - Vertigo, worse walking in dark or with eyes closed. Head bent backwards in vertigo, supports head with hands while bending or rising after sunstroke. COMMENTS - J. Emmons Briggs recorded a case of poisoning. Briggs had an urgent call to see James M., 4, in “convulsions.” He found him lying on the bed in a state of wild delirium, requiring the constant combined efforts of two people to keep him in bed. Face was exceedingly flushed, expression rapidly alternated between pleasant and anxious. Pupils widely dilated, iris scarcely visible, giving the eye a very brilliant appearance. Marked convergent strabismus, skin hot and dry, resembling scarlatina eruption. Abdomen tense. The most alarming symptom was rapidly recurring convulsions with twitching of the arms and lower limbs. Clonic spasms and contractions. Grasped at imaginary objects before the eyes, when expression frequently became anxious, as if the patient was trying to ward off imaginary foes. At times the mind was very active and the patient talked rapidly and incoherently. Between the spasms, laughter and crying frequently occurred. The boy, it transpired, had been chewing a thorn apple. When he came home he seemed rather dazed, and vomited. He then threw himself on the sofa and slept very soundly until he awoke in the convulsions. The boy recovered under Kali-br. in five-grain doses, though it was with great difficulty that he was made to swallow. Schizophrenia (Lach., Anae.). Paranoid schizophrenia. Religious mania. Insanity, mania, and dementia. Violent mania (Lach., Hyos. has a passive mania), rages, and wild violence. Loquacious (Lach.). Characteristic wild, animal-like look in the eyes. Clinical possession, they talk in other languages, other voices, violent speech, rages and ravings. Primitive instincts and fears. Vithoulkas described it as an “uncontrolled eruption of the unconsciousness.” May have a history of frights, strokes, head injuries or meningitis leading to mania. Fear of dogs and wolves, often hallucinate that they see dogs attacking them. Visions of animals. Claustrophobia. Fear of the dark, of tunnels. Fears of mirrors and crosses. Afraid of shiny objects, fire. Hydrophobia, rabies (Bell., Lyss.). Cries as if from sight of hideous objects. Terrifying delirium. Delirium tremens. Delirium with high fever, hallucinations. High fevers with sudden onset, flushed face, dilated pupils, rashes, hallucinations (Bell.). Scarlet like scarlatina, petechiae, vésications, and spots on the arms like flea bites. Burns and scalds. Mania after exposure to the sun (Bell.). Absence of pain. Epilepsy and convulsions. Extreme muscular mobility. Movements are generally gyratory and graceful when they occur in the arms. Continually jerks head up from pillow, head bent back, boring head into pillow. Twitchings of single muscles, squint. Chorea. Moving fingers as if searching for something. Coxalgia and morbus coax, with severe pain. Characteristic difficulty swallowing, with intense thirst, delirium and hallucinations. Suppressed secretions, menses, lochia, sweat, or eruptions. Discharges are foul, even cadaverous. Congestions without actual inflammation, but with high mental exaltation and furious delirium and little or no fever without pain but with some coma. Constriction of the chest, asthmatic symptoms and cough of the whooping cough type. The common practice of smoking stramonium leaves for asthma is roughly homeopathic. Clarke had a case of severe pleuropneumonia of right side, supervening on scarlatina, in which the patient, a young man, said he saw a large black dog about the room. This led Clarke to give Stram., which rapidly altered the whole case for the better including the pneumonia, and resolved the situation. Nash reported a case or a woman, 30, with acute mania after being overheated in the sun. She called Nash for 6 days straight to come watch her die. She imagined herself eternally lost and begged everyone to pray for her. Talked day and night. Thought her head was as big as a bushel, her legs as large as a church. Nash cured with Stram. 6c after Glon., Lach., and Nat-c. failed. All symptoms and any traces of mania were gone after 24 hours. S. A. Jones related the case of a little girl with brain symptoms for whom he had prescribed aremedy. The report was brought late at night that the patient was much worse. “She vomits,” said the father, “if she even raises her head from the pillow.” The vomit was green. Jones found this under Stram., which he gave, and the next morning the case was entirely changed for the better. Acting on this analog, Jones also cured a “vomiting of green stuff always induced by bright light.” RELATIONS -Antidotes: Bell., Tab., Nux-v. Antidoted by: Lemon juice, Vinegar tobacco injections, Senn, for cerebral symptoms, Bell., Hyos., Nux-v. and “Particularly Camphor" (Teste). Antidote to: Merc., Plb.

Stomach - Hiccough obstinate. Nausea. Vomiting of mucus andgreen bile. Watery vomiting with colic and diarrhea.

Abdomen - Abdomen inflated, hard, distended. Contusive pain in abdomen during movement. Violent pains in abdomen, as if navel were being torn out. Hysterical spasms in abdomen. Borborygmi with fermentation in abdomen. Expulsion of much flatus. Swelling of inguinal glands.

Rectum - Putrid, dark, painless involuntary diarrhea with a squint and pale face. Cholera infantum. Stools suppressed. Sensations - As if spinning or weaving. As if objects were smaller than they really are. As if dizzy. As if drunk. As if he was seeking something. As if he had no limbs. As if bones were sawed through. Head as if drawn backward. As if pins and needles were in forehead. As if nose were shifted. As if front teeth would fall out. Teeth as if pressed together.

Male - Sexualpassion exalted with indecent speech and action. Hands constantly kept on genitals.

Female - Excessive menstrual flow, preceded by sexual excitement. Menses have strong smell as of semen. Loquacity and singing during menses. Sobs and moans after menses. Uterine bleeding with loquacity. Hands constantly kept on genitals. Nymphomania, lewd talking, sings obscene songs. Puerperal, convulsions, mania with mental symptoms and profuse sweating. Convulsions after childbirth. Food - Food tastes bitter, like straw. Aversion to all fluids. Violent thirst. Great desire for acids, citric acid better. Lemon juice ameliorates.

Chest - Constrictive oppression on chest with dyspnea. Pressure on chest, worse by speaking. Spasm in pectoral muscles. Red rash on chest. Constitutions - Suited to ailments of young, plethoric persons, especially of children (chorea, mania, fever, delirium).

Heart - Pressure about heart. Heart disorders with constrictions of the chest and mental symptoms. Angina pectoris. Palpitations. Feeble, pulse irregular.

Back - Neck stiff, cannot bend it backwards. Drawing pain in the back. Spine sensitive, slightest pressure causes outcries and ravings. Opisthotonos. Causations - Ill effects of shock, fright, sun, childbirth. Dog bites. High fever. Head injury. Hydrophobia.

Limbs - Chorea, spasms partial, constantly changing. Convulsions of upper limbs and of isolated groups of muscles. Graceful and rhythmic motions. Clasps hands over head. Hands open and shut. Wringing of hands. Staggering gait. Misses step of stairs while descending. Heels numb, sometimes painful. Violent pain in left hip. Abscess of left hip joint with violent pain. Trembling of limbs. Inside of right thigh red and swollen. Hemiplegia with convulsions in unparalyzed parts. Lungs - Inspiration slow, expiration quick. Nervous asthma. Cough with jerking of lower limbs, when sitting. Cough worse looking at light, fire or bright objects. The spasmodic cough of alcoholics, whooping.

Sleep - Sleepy, but cannot sleep (Bell.). Sleepless in darkness. Deep snoring sleep. Lies on back with thighs and knees flexed. Frightful dreams. Weeping in dreams. Laughs, screams, starts during sleep. Awakes terrified, knows no one, screams with fright, clings to those near him (child). Comatose.

Skin - Fiery red patches on skin. Shining red flush. Burns and scalds. Crawling as of many bugs. Chronic abscesses, fistulae. Abscesses and tumors with severe pain. Non-appearance of exanthemata. Effects of suppressed eruption in scarlatina with delirium.

Modalities - Better from bright light, company, warmth. Worse from shining objects, mirror, surface of water. Worse from fright, when alone. Worse sun, cloudy days, in dark room. Worse suppressions, intemperance, after sleep. Worse by touch, pressure, swallowing.

Compare - (1) Hyos. and Bell. It has less fever than Bell., but more than Hyos. It causes more functional excitement of the brain, but never approaches the true inflammatory condition of Bell. (1) Metrorrhagia, from retained placenta with characteristic delirium, Sec. (2) Pyrog. with fever and septic tendency. (3) Delirium, Bell., Lach., Agar., Cupr., Zinc. (4) Illusions of shape, Bapt., Petr., Thuj. (5) Erysipelas, Bell., Rhus-t. (6) Stuttering, unable to combine consonants with vowels, Bov. Bright light causes convulsions, Kali-br. (7) Better light, Stront. (8) Hears voices from far off talking to him, behind him, Anae. (9) Loquacity, Cupr., Hyos., Lach., Op., Verat. (10) Laughs and weeps by turns, Aur., Puls., Alum., Lye., Caps., Graph., Phos., Sep., Sulph., Verat. (1 l)Tetanicconvulsions worse touch and light, Nux-v. (12) Desire to escape in delirium, Bell., Bry., Op., Rhus-t. (13) Rabies, Lyss. Follows well: Cupr., Bell. Incompatible: Coff. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Kidneys - Suppression of urine, especially during typhoid, bladder empty. Loss of power of bladder in the aged, stream flows slowly, cannot make haste. Rigor during urination. Bladder empty.

Temperature - Profuse sweat which does not relieve. Cold sweat during spasms. Violent fever. Heat over whole body with red face and perspiration. Heat with anxiety and redness of cheeks or else with thirst and vomiting. Retention of urine in any fever.

full:
PHARMACY - strept. Streptococcinum. Streptococcinum bacteria. Nosodes. Made from streptococcus pyogenes and marcy. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Adenitis. Arthritis. Bronchitis. Cellulitis. Chorea. Colds. Debility. Ear, pain. Epilepsy. Fevers. Fibrositis. Infections. Mastoiditis. Otalgia. Otitis media. Psoriasis. Rheumatism. Scarlatina. Sinusitis. Sore, throats. Tonsillitis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Strept. should be considered in chronic disease where there is a history of acute streptococcal infection, including severe infection in the mother during pregnancy. Especially when the strep- tococcal infection immediately precedes chronic illness or when it is an outstanding event in the history of the patient. Rapid action, especially in its effect on temperature. Anti-febrile action. Chilliness. Oversensitive. Intolerance to the least current of air caused by the moving of a person. Intolerance to noise, light. Chronic sore throats and streptococcal infections. Severe or repeated tonsillitis or quinsy. Susceptible to catching colds and sore throats. Acute sinusitis. Severe influenza, pneumonia, bronchitis, pleurisy. Debility after streptococcal infections. Septic symptoms in infectious diseases. Puerperal sepsis. Epileptiform attacks. Chorea-like movements. Acute rheumatism. Retarded growth in delicate children. Erysipelas. Otitis media. Meningitis. Dental caries. Acute parenchymatous nephritis. Peritonitis and cholecystitis. Intestinal toxemia, sometimes with amebic dysentery or other intestinal infection. Scarlet fever has its own nosode, but Stept. is often effective when Scarl. fails. MIND - Depressed. Weeping without reason. Streptococcinum weeps on being given sympathy. Despair of recovery. Oversensitive. Highly strung, emotional, apprehensive. Exaggerated obsequiousness. Tormenting thoughts and anxiety. Obsessions. Thinks that he will become fnad. Auditory hallucinations, hears cry for help.

Head - Tenacious migraine with vomiting of bile. Pain of the whole head as if it is going to burst.

Eyes - Troubles of vision with ocular hypertension. Eye fatigue with the need of wearing glasses. Visual hallucination, sees the room full of flies.

Ears - Otitis and mastoiditis. Otalgia specially if the person is lying down on the left. Intermittent puffs of wind in the ear. Auditory hallucinations, hears cry for help.

Nose - Serous nasal discharge, mucopurulent with nasal crusts. Sinusitis with headache.

Mouth - Feeling of having salty lips. White tongue with the tip red, without papilla in the front and in the back part. Gums painful when chewing.

Throat - Persistent pain and redness of the throat. Acute and chronic laryngitis. Red angina. Adenopathy of the neck. Big, infected, purulent tonsils. Vertigo - Vertigo while rising and while lying down. COMMENTS - When there has been a number of severe acute illnesses, Dr. Gordon, of Edinburgh, maintained that the best results can be obtained by antidoting the most recent infection first by its appropriate nosode, proceeding backwards and thus “curing in layers.” Another view is that, other things being equal, the first lapse from health is of greatest importance and that this should be antidoted first to undermine the superstructure and then deal with the case according to the remaining symptoms. Ghose wrote, “I have used Streptococcin with very remarkable results in acute Bacillary dysentery with excessive hemorrhage and high rise of temperature with toxemia. The more the blood the more it is indicated like Mercurius, but there is no tenesmus or urinary complications of Mercurius in Streptococcin. “In very bad cases of bacillary dysentery, very bad complications will follow and take a very long time to cure if it cannot be checked in the very beginning. In chronic cases of Dysentery where blood with mucopurulent discharge does not respond to indicated remedies or recurs and prolongs unduly. I have seen it to stop the bloody and mucopurulent discharge within a very short time with a dose of Streptococcin 200c.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bell., Pyrog, Rhus-t. (2) Staphycoc., Scarl. REFERENCES - Boericke. Foubister. Ghose. Julian.

Stomach - Sudden pains in the esophagus after meals. Dull, deep pain in the epigastric region. Nausea with vertigo and vomiting of bile.

Abdomen - While lying down cannot bear the weight of hand on the abdomen. Pain in the appendix.

Heart - Sensation of weakness of the heart. Pain of the point of the heart. Cramping pain in the precordial region.

Back - Pain of the backbone. Acute pain on the clavicles. Sensation of vibrations in the vertebral column and in the limbs. Causations - Streptococcal infections. Ailments after tonsillectomy.

Limbs - Muscular pain. Rheumatism of small articulations of the wrist, of the hand, with local redness, sometimes with hydro-arthrosis. Parethesiaof lower limbs. Cold feet.

Sleep - Agitated sleep. Dreams of violence, scuffles.

Skin - Vesicular and pustulous eruptions. Cellulitis. Exanthema. Erysipeltoid patches of the limbs. Fibrinous dermatitis, edema of the face. Scarlatina. Recurrent suppuration. Abortive pus formation. Loss of hair.

Modalities - Better from movement, in open air. Worse by consolation. Worse by humid weather, wet weather. Worse on beginning to move, better from subsequent movement.

full:
PHARMACY - stront-br. Strontium bromatum. Strontium bromide. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Cellulitis. Dyspepsia. Gravel. Indigestion. Legs, swollen. Phlebitis. Varicose veins. Urine, offensive. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Stront-br. often gives excellent results where a bromide is indicated. Anti-fermentative and neutralizes excessive acidity. Nervous dyspepsia. Vomiting of pregnancy. COMMENTS - Cooper gave several experiences with Stront-br., including the case of a woman, 40, who had tenderness of her limbs and veins of legs showed up and were inclined to inflame. Chronic cellulitis, left ankle inclined to swell, vertigo, at times darkness comes over sight, appetite not good, bowels regular, menses every three weeks, cannot keep awake in evening. Great relief came from Stront-br. 3x, but after taking it for ten days, severe ardor urine with constant bedwetting day and night set in, which yielded to Ferr-p. 6x. after failure with other remedies. Woman, 60, had left leg and left foot swollen, hard and tender, red and pitting. The right also but less in degree. Indigestion with pain after food and sickness after food. For seven or eight years has been rheumatic and has had sciatica off and on. For two years, bowels confined, sleep very restless generally. Stront-br. 3x was given and in two weeks the legs had gone down very much and she felt altogether better. Urine had become clear, but though ravenous for food had to stop eating and felt more sick and the bowels were more confined. After this, the patient got quite well without further medicine. Stront-br. 30 gave great relief to a woman broken down by sorrow who could not digest food. Stront-br. 6x produced in a woman, 70, thick and offensive urine, dark-looking with grains of red sand. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Strontium Carbonicum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Aversion to darkness. Better from light, heat, and sun. Better immersing in hot water. Better wraps, hot bath, covering, warm stove. Worse change of weather. Worse cold, uncovering, drafts. Worse evening, night and early morning. Worse 2 a.m. or 3 a.m., from being quiet. Worse when beginning to move, walking, stooping Worse sprains, bleeding. Worse touch, rubbing, scratching..

full:
PHARMACY - stront-c. Strontium carbonicum. Strontium carbonate. Strontianite. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Ankle, sprains. Anus, burning. Arteriosclerosis. Bedwetting. Bones, diseases. Cardialgía. Constipation. Cramp. Diarrhea. Emaciation. Feet, cold. Femur, decay. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Hemorrhoids. Hiccoughs. Hoarseness. Leucorrhea. Menses, disorders. Neuritis. Phlebitis. Photophobia. Sciatica. Shock. Sprains. Sternum, pains. Strokes. Sycotic, eruptions. Varicose, veins. Vision disorders.

HOMEOPATHIC - Strontianite was first discovered in the lead mines of Strontain in Argyllshire, from which it received its name. It occurs in massive, fibrous, stellated, rarely ortho-rhombic, crystals. The metal stronlium is dark yellow. Strontium carbonate varies in color from white to yellow and pale green. Stront-c. was proved by Nenning, Schreter, Seidel, Trincks and Woost. It affects the circulation, causing a congestive feeling of tension. The heart, kidneys, marrow, ankles and right side are also affected. Rheumatic pains, chronic sprains and stenosis of esophagus. Pains make patient faint or sick all over. Pain and itching alternate. Pains are fleeting, can hardly tell where they are, seemingly felt in marrow of bones. Pains increase and decrease gradually or make the patient faint and sick all over. Burning, gnawing. Right side most affected. For the shock after surgical operations. Chronic sequelae of hemorrhages, after operations with much oozing of blood and coldness and prostration. Arteriosclerosis. High blood pressure, with flushed face pulsating arteries, threatened strokes. Edema, especially about the ankles as a concomitant. Numbness. Soreness. Restlessness at night, smothering feeling. Affections of bones, especially femur. Violent involuntary starts. Immobility of one side. Sense of paralytic weakness. Formication in limbs. Neuritis, worse cold. Coldness in spots, on calves. Pressure in stomach is better by eating and worse after a meal. Emaciation. MIND - Depression of spirits. Excessive forgetfulness. Inquietude and anguish. Apprehension as from bad conscience. Irritable, suddenly becomes angry, beats anything that comes in his way. Peevishness with tendency to fly into a rage.

Head - Aches into upper jaw with vertigo and nausea. Headaches from nape of neck, spreading upwards, better wrapping head up warmly (Sil.). Distensive pressure on head. Aching eyebrows. Supra-orbital neuralgia, pains increase and decrease slowly (Stann.).

Eyes - Burning and redness of eyes. Pain and lachrymation on using eyes, with dancing and alternation of colors of objects looked at. Photophobia, remaining after operation, especially when objects appear covered with blood. Green spots before the eyes in the dark.

Ears - Tearing in front of right ear as if in the bone. Sticking in front of left ear in frequent paroxysms. Humming in the ears.

Nose - Itching, redness and burning of nose. Bloody crusts in nose. Blowing of dark scabs from nose. Quivering on one side of nose. Twitching of left side of nose.

Face - Flushed face, worse from exertion. Violent, pulsating flushes in face. Red with burning heat or very pale, every time the patient walks. Red face, burns, itches.

Mouth - Feels numb and dry on waking. Bad odor from mouth. Teeth as screwed together.

Throat - Hoarseness and roughness in throat, which excites a cough. Vertigo - Vertigo with headache and nausea. COMMENTS - Congested state. Flushing in the face and violent pulsation of the arteries, congestion to heart, lungs and head. Symptoms better by warmth and wrapping up and worse by cold. All complaints are worse walking, particularly headache, leucorrhea, dyspnea and pressure in the sternum. Headaches are boring, pressive and tensive. Tension from vertex to upper jaw, as if head were expanded from within and as if scalp were too tight, worse in evening, when lying with head low, slowly increasing and decreasing, better from heat. Tension in the nape, as if the tendons were drawn up. Tensive drawing in dorsal and lumbar muscles. External soreness, numbness. Venous tension in the arms. “The veins of the arms and hands are injected and tense with great prostration and ill-humor." Phlebitis, varicose veins. Angina pectoris. Predisposition toward strokes and high blood pressure. Surgical shock after blood loss. Great exhaustion after surgery. Pressure in the stomach, better by eating and worse by walking. Pressure after eating. Diarrhea and constipation. Stools are accompanied and followed by burning in the rectum. Diarrhea is worse at night, urgent, with yellow stools. Emaciation. Calcification, osteoporosis. Weak and brittle bones that break easily. Bony growths and enlargements. Bone pains, especially the femur, the thighbone. Bone disorders, particularly the femur. Bone disorders in scrofulous children when associated with diarrhea. Characteristic weak ankles (Nat-c.). Chronic sprains of the ankle with edema. Sciatica associated with weak ankles. Ice cold feet. Leg and foot cramps (Calc.). C. M. Boger cured a sciatica accompanied by edema of left ankle with Stront-c. after other remedies had failed. A. P. Bowie cured a case occurring after a tedious labor. The stools were large and hard, expelled with great effort, followed by great pain in anus, burning, lasting a long time and compelling patient to lie down. Anus violently contracted after stool. Complained of coldness in spots on calves of legs. Stront-c. 6c entirely relieved. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph. Compare: (1) Arn., Ruta, Sil., Bar-c., Chin. (2) Stront-br., Stront-n., Stront-i. - Arteriosclerosis. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Pressure in stomach during digestion. Heartburn. Belchings after eating. Violent hiccough causes chest pains, cardialgía. Nausea, with burning heat in face.

Abdomen - Sticking in the abdominal ring. Uncomfortable fullness and swelling of abdomen. Colic in umbilical region.

Rectum - Exhausting di arrhea with constant urging of yellow water with gripping, worse at night, better towards morning. Periodical diarrhea. Burning in anus lasts a long time after stool (Rat.). Hard, knotty Strontium carbonicum stools, evacuated slowly with much effort, then burning in anus lasting for a long time. Sensations - As if head were expanded from within. As if scalp were too tight. As if tendons of neck were drawn up. As if a load on chest. As if all power had left right arm. As ifbruised in back and sacrum. Gnawing as if in marrow of bones. Symptoms as if in marrow of bones. Symptoms like phantoms, difficult to locate.

Female - Flushes of heat, worse during menopause. Profuse perspiration at night, menopausal. Food - Loss of appetite, food tasteless. Craving for bread, beer. Aversion to meat.

Chest - Pressure at chest in sternum. Constriction, pressive pain, worse walking. Drawing pain in muscles of chest. Angina pectoris. Constitutions - Suited to bone disorders of scrofulous children when associated with diarrhea.

Heart - Heart feels smothered. Heart block. Dull, intermitting pressure in precordial region. Violent beating of arteries and of heart.

Back - Pain, as of a fracture in loins and back. Drawing pain in back and lumbar region. Causations - Hemorrhages, chronic sequelae. Injuries, sprains. Shock. Surgical shock after blood loss. Great exhaustion after surgery.

Limbs - Rheumatic pain, in joints, in right shoulder. Rheumatism with diarrhea. Sciatica with edema of ankle. Immobility of the limbs of one side only, like paralysis. Gnawing as if in marrow of the bones. Chronic sprained joints. Ankles sprained or swollen. Swelling of ankle remaining after a sprain. Weakness of ankles. Chronic spasms, especially of ankle joints. Cramps in calves and soles. Icy-cold feet. Veins of hands engorged. Hands numb. Lungs - Pressure, as of a load on chest. Pain in the left breast, with oppression, worse after meals. Dry cough, excited by irritation in trachea, worse at night. Dyspnea, when walking with heat and redness of face.

Sleep - Retarded sleep. Jerking in body and starts when sleeping. Frequent waking at night, principally caused by a dry cough. Many fantastic dreams.

Skin - Sprains of ankle joint with edema. Moist, itching, burning eruption, better in open air, especially warm sunshine. Violent perspiration at night.

Modalities - Aversion to darkness. Better from light, heat, and sun. Better immersing in hot water. Better wraps, hot bath, covering, warm stove. Worse change of weather. Worse cold, uncovering, drafts. Worse evening, night and early morning. Worse 2 a.m. or 3 a.m., from being quiet. Worse when beginning to move, walking, stooping Worse sprains, bleeding. Worse touch, rubbing, scratching.

Kidneys - Pale urine with strong smell of ammonia. Increased secretion of a yellow, deep-colored urine. Diminished secretion of urine. Nocturnal emission of urine.

Temperature - Flushes of heat in face, with aversion to uncovering. Profuse perspiration at night, menopausal.

PHARMACY - stront-n. Strontium nitricum. Strontium nitrate. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

HOMEOPATHIC - C. M. Boger had a case in a menopausal woman of passive congestion of the kidneys completely relieved by Stront-n. The menses, which were usually exceedingly…
full:
PHARMACY - stront-n. Strontium nitricum. Strontium nitrate. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

HOMEOPATHIC - C. M. Boger had a case in a menopausal woman of passive congestion of the kidneys completely relieved by Stront-n. The menses, which were usually exceedingly scanty, became profuse. Morbid cravings. Eczema behind ears. Headaches. Kidney congestion. Menses scanty. , COMMENTS - Boger recorded the following caseofMissD., 18,brunette, who haddull pains over eyes worse by sunlight, motion, loss of sleep, sewing, reading. Pains were better after stool, with headache, swelling of upper lids, worse in morning. Bad taste in mouth. Menses irregular, profuse, dark. Felt tired and weak. Addicted to eating cloves. In hot weather, sweats profusely and easily about head and chest, staining yellow. Very susceptible to cold. Cough provoked by op- pression of breathing and talking. Formerly had catarrh, followed by rightsided deafness. She had typhoid fever two years before and during the fever was allowed unlimited quantities of ice. Preceding the fever she had a post auricular eczema suppressed by salves, now is anemic and bloated. Urine contained epithelium, excess of chlorides, calcium oxalate and a trace of albumen (due probably to the clove habit). Glon. helped the case, but for a time only. Stront-n. was chosen because Stront. irritates the kidneys and Nit- ac. corresponds to the vasomotor disturbance besides having cravings for odd things. Stront-n. 6x was given and in a few days the headache vanished. At the end of a month the post-auricular eruption had reappeared. Five months later there had been no return of headache or palpebral edema, the craving for cloves had gone, the patient had taken on good flesh and color. The eruption had not all gone. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Strophanthus Hispidus
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from rest, lying down. Worse from exertion, exercise, standing. Worse tobacco, tea, alcohol. Worse from emotions..
constitution: Alcoholism. Anasarca. Anemia. Arteriosclerosis. Colitis. Cough. Cystitis. Diplopia. Dropsy, cardiac. Edema. Exophthalmia goiter. Faintness. Heart, disorders. Hemoptysis. Hives. Levitation. Nausea, obesity. Pneumonia. Urticaria.
keynote:
PHARMACY - stroph. Strophanthus hispidus. Kombe seed. Strophanthus gratus. Inee. Onaye. Onage. Poison of Pahonias. N. O. Apocynaceae. Tincture of the seeds.Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Anasarca. Anemia. Arteriosclerosis. Colitis. Cough.…
full:
PHARMACY - stroph. Strophanthus hispidus. Kombe seed. Strophanthus gratus. Inee. Onaye. Onage. Poison of Pahonias. N. O. Apocynaceae. Tincture of the seeds.Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Alcoholism. Anasarca. Anemia. Arteriosclerosis. Colitis. Cough. Cystitis. Diplopia. Dropsy, cardiac. Edema. Exophthalmia goiter. Faintness. Heart, disorders. Hemoptysis. Hives. Levitation. Nausea, obesity. Pneumonia. Urticaria.

HOMEOPATHIC - Strophantus is an ornamental, evergreen and a climbing shrub, native of tropical Africa and Asia. The mother tincture comes from the seeds of the plant. It is used as an arrow-poison by natives of Africa. Among the alkaloids is strophanthin. Stroph. occasions no gastric distress, diuretic. It has no cumulative action, safe for corpulent, aged persons with rigid arteries, as it does not affect the vaso-motors. Restores tone to a weak tissue, especially of the heart muscle and valves. Stroph. increases the contractile power of all striped muscles, especially the heart, increasing the systole and diminishing the rapidity. Acts on the heart increasing the systole and diminishes the rapidity. Tones the heart and run off dropsical effusions. Especially useful in failing compensation dependent upon fatty heart. After the long use of stimulants. Arteriosclerosis, rigid arteries of aged. Precordial anxiety. Retrosternal pain. Functional disturbances of heart from alcohol, tobacco, tea. In small doses for weak heart, that feels enlarged. In mitral regurgitation, where edema and dropsy have supervened (Dig.). Severe prostration from hemorrhage after operations and acute diseases. Anemia with palpitations and loss of breath. Faintness. Pneumonia. Rapid alternations of symptoms with slow pulse. Undulating sensation in whole body. Throbbings. Stitching pains. Twitchings of the muscles. Obesity. Increased secretions. Nausea with special disgust for alcohol. Alcoholism, with drop doses of Stroph- h. tincture. Hives. Exophthalmia goiter. MIND - Worse from strong emotions. Irritable. Anxiety and fear. Fear of ordeals. Feels lifted up during sleep. Precociously talkative children.

Head - Temporal pains with double vision, impaired sight, brilliant eyes, flushed face. Violent, pulsating headache, aggravated by movement.

Eyes - Pupils quivering, dilating and contracting alternately. Eyes brilliant. Glimmering in vision. Impaired sight of left eye with nausea and faintness. Double vision.

Face - Flushed, red spots. Lips scarlet.

Mouth - Dryness of tongue and fauces.

Throat - Seems dry, constricted. Burning in throat and esophagus to stomach, compelling empty swallowing. Vertigo - Vertigo with swimming vision. Senile vertigo. Undulations in head. COMMENTS-The homeopathic proving was conducted by Templeton on five provers, using 2x, 3x, 6c, 12c, 30c and by O’ Hanlon on twelve provers, using 6c, 12c and 30c. Piedvache proved the tincture, but only with reference to the pulse. Gise vius proved Stroph-h. tincture, beginning with 5 drops increasing to 80 drops during the five days of his proving. Matthes proved Stroph-h. tincture in 10 drops doses. Some well-marked symptoms were produced on two chemists from preparing the tincture. Other effects curative and pathogenetic have been observed on patients taking the drug. Stroph-h. disorders the digestion, causes burning in the esophagus and stomach, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea. A. P. Skworzow gave an infusion of Stroph. to an alcoholic, 63, for weak heart and intermittent pulse, 7 drop doses three times a day. The first dose caused nausea and a repugnance to alcohol which proved to be permanent. The man entirely discontinued the habit. On this hint, Stroph. was given to two other alcoholics with the same result of abolishing the taste for alcohol. It caused nausea and profuse sweating and the sudden withdrawal of alcohol was not attended with delirium. A case of Clarke’s illustrates the gastric and cardiac action of the remedy. W. G., 16, a delicate-looking boy, was admitted to a hospital. He had rheumatic pains for three months and an attack of rheumatic fever two years previously. He had been laid up a month before admission and a week before was taken with cough, shivering and occasional vomiting. When admitted, he had a frequent, short, dry cough, worse lying down, had to be propped up in bed, had edema of feet, especially left. Tongue white, unable to retain any food for three days, no pain after food, but much flatulence, belchings giving much relief. Heart greatly dilated, pulsation diffused, double mitral bruit. Dullness at bases of both lungs, moist rales, halfway up right lung. Expectoration of bright blood for seven days. Stroph. tincture, one drop every four hours, was given. Improvement in all the symptoms was immediate, sickness, cough, hemoptysis and dropsy all disappeared and the heart sounds had cleared up to a large extent when the boy went home, less than three weeks after admission. Hamer mentioned that Stroph. cured “functional disturbance of the heart from alcohol tobacco and tea.” This agrees with the relation of Stroph. to alcoholism and symptoms of indigestion. A writer gave his experience with Stroph. : a woman had constant outbursts of urticarial rash dating from exposure to an offensive effluvium from a dead whale cast on the sands. The attacks would recur after drinking a glass of table beer. Stroph-h. cured. Any accompanying cardiac weakness would be an additional indication. The same writer considered Stroph. of great service in the anemia of young girls when palpitation and breathlessness are marked features. An accidental proving on a girl of five was made through the mother giving twenty drops of the tincture by mistake. Some half an hour later her face was flushed, lips scarlet, eyes brilliant, temperature raised, skin dry, tongue normal. Pupils quivering, dilating and contracting every few seconds. Pulse 140, arteries distended. Heart sounds vigorous, slight regurgitant mitral murmur. Intellect clear, precociously loquacious during the five hours the poisonous symptoms lasted. An ipecac emetic was administered. No urine passed for ten hours after the dose. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Heart dropsy, Apoc. (2) Heart, Dig. is cumulative, Stroph-h. is not. (3) Crat., Phase., Cact. (4) Anemia, Fenr. (5) Alcoholism, Chin., Nux-v., Aven., Querc. (6) Kali-c. - heart weakness, fatigue, chill, acute stinging pains, aggravated by the cold and at 2 a.m. (7) Aeon. - Sharp intolerable pains, much more agitated with fear of death. (8) Lach. - worse left-side, aggravated on waking, hyperesthesia of the skin, tendency to hemorrhage. (9) Sarcol-ac.- Pains and muscular weakness, extreme asthenia, aggravated by the slightest movement. (10) movement, feeling of fullness in the epigastrium, constipation. Compatible: Ferr. in anemia. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Bulky feeling in the stomach. Twitching in stomach. Burning in esophagus and stomach with loss of appetite and extreme gastric distress. Cramping, acrid stomachache with belching and nausea. Eructation and hiccough. Nausea with special disgust for alcohol.

Abdomen - Abdomen distended, painful, especially in the umbilical and inguinal regions. Rumbling and pinching at navel. Shooting pains in right hypochondrium. Stitches in region of sigmoid flexure. Acute entero-colitis. Colic.

Rectum - Stool with burning and tenesmus in anus. Diarrhea with burning and tenesmus in anus. Frequent diarrhea with violent colic but good appetite. Infectious or toxic diarrhea.

Female - Uterine hemorrhage. Uterus heavily congested. Food - Craving for alcohol, tea, coffee, stimulants. Nausea with special disgust for alcohol. Loss of appetite. Loathing of food, followed by choking and vomiting after eating.

Chest - Pressive pain in middle of right third rib on anterior half, worse by pressure. Thoracic pain on left side. Constrictive, cramping pain behind the sternum, crushed, gnawing, needle-like sensation.

Heart - Weak heart with aching or anguish. Heart’s action weak, rapid, irregular, due to muscular debility and insufficiency. Cardiac pain and dyspnea. Chronic, nervous palpitations and arrest of breathing. Violent palpitations, worse by emotion and exercise. Sense of lively action. Mitral regurgitation. Stitches and twitches at apex beat. Pulse, rapid, alternating with slow, weak, small irregular.

Back - Joint and muscular pains in the limbs, back and lumbar region with stiffness, muscular weakness, coldness at the limbs. Causations - Alcohol, tea, tobacco.

Limbs - Swollen, dropsical. Anasarca. Swelling of legs. Itching and stitching in both feet. Dorsum of foot painful and tense. Muscular and joint pains with stiffness and coldness of the limbs. The pains are aggravated by movement. Heaviness and pain in forearms and the fingers.

Skin - Hives, chronic, receding. Urticaria, especially more chronic forms.

Modalities - Better from rest, lying down. Worse from exertion, exercise, standing. Worse tobacco, tea, alcohol. Worse from emotions.

Liver - Pressure in liver region. Lungs - Edema of lungs. Bronchial and cardiac asthma. Breathing deep, difficult, thirsty for air, feeling of dryness in the mucus membranes, aggravated by movement. Cough worse by lying down. Expectoration of bright red blood.

Kidneys - Kidneys become hyperemic. Cystitis. Urinary tract infections. No urine passed for hours. Frequent urination. Urine increased secretion or scanty albuminous. Urine strong, odor is fruity or like horse urine, pale.

Temperature - Coldness of limbs. Temperature raised, skin dry. Profuse sweat.

name: Strychnia Phosphoricum
author: Murphy
constitution: Atelectasis. Heart, disorders. Headache. Paralysis. Pulse, irregular. Spinal cord, disorders. Tachycardia.
keynote:
PHARMACY - stry-p. Strychnia phosphoricum. Strychnine phosphate. Alkaloid obtained from several species of Strychnos. Solution. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Atelectasis. Heart, disorders. Headache. Paralysis. Pulse, irregular. Spinal cord, disorders.…
full:
PHARMACY - stry-p. Strychnia phosphoricum. Strychnine phosphate. Alkaloid obtained from several species of Strychnos. Solution. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Atelectasis. Heart, disorders. Headache. Paralysis. Pulse, irregular. Spinal cord, disorders. Tachycardia.

HOMEOPATHIC - Stry-p. is useful in chorea, hysteria, acute asthenia after acute fevers. Hands and axilla covered with clammy perspiration. Cold and clammy feet. Better rest and in open air, worse from motion. Acts through the cerebro-spinal system upon muscles, causing twitching, stiffness, weakness and loss of power. Anemia of spinal cord, paralysis, burning, aching and weakness of spine, pain extends to front of chest, tenderness on pressure in mid-dorsal region. Atelectasis and break in the compensation of a hypertrophied heart, the beginning of fatty degeneration of the heart muscle. Tachycardia. Irregular pulse. Rapid and weak pulse. MIND - Affects upon the mind, producing lack of control, uncontrollable desire to laugh and disinclination to use the brain. COMMENTS - A woman to whom Clarke gave Stry-p. 3x in five-drop doses twenty minutes before meals, felt at once constriction of the throat and after each meal violent headache in forehead over the eyes. The choking sensations were a constant feature in provings and poisonings. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Royal.

keynote:
PHARMACY - stry. Strychninum. Strychnine. Alkaloid obtained from several species of Nux vomica, Loganiaceae. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Aorta, pain. Aphonia. Asthma. Athetosis. Bedwetting. Bladder, paralysis, pains. Breasts,…
full:
PHARMACY - stry. Strychninum. Strychnine. Alkaloid obtained from several species of Nux vomica, Loganiaceae. Trituration. Solution. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Aorta, pain. Aphonia. Asthma. Athetosis. Bedwetting. Bladder, paralysis, pains. Breasts, pains. Coughs. Cramps. Diaphragm, spasms. Emphysema. Exophthalmos. Eye, disorders. Headaches. Hemiplegia. Influenza. Joints, stiffness. Laryngeal, crises. Locomotor, ataxia. Malar, bones, pains. Neurasthenia. Night-blindness. Paraplegia. Proctalgia. Rheumatism. Scrotum, abscess. Spinal irritation. Tetanus.

HOMEOPATHIC - Liquor Strychnie is responsible for many of the poisonings, the powdered crystals, either pure or mixed in pills or rat-poison, for others. Strychnia itself is very sparingly soluble in cold water (1 in 5760). A homeopathic proving of Stry. was made by Henry Robinson on two provers, a man and a woman. The man took 900 drops in twenty-three days, the woman 445 drops in fifty-three days. These have furnished the most distinctive symptoms. Extreme nervous excitability. Visions of an ugly face. Fits of laughing with light. Idiotic-like chuckle. Confusion of ideas, stupor and weariness were some of the mental symptoms. Swimming sensation in the head and giddiness involuntary. Stimulates the motor centers and the reflex action of the spinal cord. Stimulates the central nervous system, mental activities, special senses rendered more acute. All reflexes are made more active. Spasmodic rigidity. Spasms of muscles, cramps from an undue reflex excitability of the cord, spasms of the bladder, etc. Stiffness in muscles and face and neck. Athetosis. Tetanus with violent jerking, twitching and trembling. Tetanic convulsions with opisthotonos. The muscles relax between paroxysms, worse slightest touch, sound, odor. Influences more directly the spinal cord and is less appropriate in visceral derangements than Nux-v. Explosive nervousness. The pains and sensations come suddenly and return at intervals. Darting, pinching lancinating, fulgurating, electric pains. Spine is cold. Gushing sweat from head and chest. Drowsiness, with headache. Frontal headaches, momentary dartings like electric shocks. Respiration increased. Inability to take deep breath, fixation of chest walls. Sudden palpitations. The direct “tonic” action of Stry. was shown in one of Robinson’s provers, who had “unusually good appetite, she enjoys her food amazingly.” Stry. is an antidote to chloral, used in asphyxia from gas and chloroform and early stages of opium poisoning.

Head - Over irritability. Restless. Full and bursting headache with heat in eyes. Vertigo with roaring in ears. Jerking of head forwards. Scalp sore. Itching of scalp and nape.

Eyes - Hot, painful, protruding, staring. Pupils dilated. Spasmodic contraction of ocular muscles, twitching and trembling of lids. Sparks before eyes.

Ears - Hearing very acute, burning, itching and roaring in ears.

Face - Pale, anxious, livid. Jaws stiffened, lower jaw spasmodically closed.

Throat - Dry, contracted, feeling of a lump. Swallowing impossible. Burning along and spasms of esophagus. Violent itching in roof of mouth. COMMENTS - Innumerable poisonings with strychnine are on record, the symptoms being convulsions of a tetanic nature, in the fatal cases ending in asphyxia. The spasms are intermittent and the least touch or movement is sufficient to induce an attack. Lying on the back is the only tolerable position. “Lying on her back, body rigid, jaws set, arms and hands flexed, the thumbs nearly touching across the chest and the whole muscular system convulsed with shortjerky spasms. Which would continue for about a minute and then remit, the muscles remaining contracted and as hard as wood during the intervals between the paroxysms.” The convulsions generally take the form of opisthotonos, cries, terror, hippocratic countenance and frothing at the mouth are common occurrences. Meyhoffer experimented with Stry. on himself and two other persons, one of whom was a woman of lymphatic temperament. “It always brought on electric shocks, occurring whenever the prover was touched or whenever any one lightly shook the bed on which he or she was lying. This happened to all, only the woman (lymphatic and feeble) needed a stronger dose.” Any touch on any part of the body caused a voluptuous sensation. Gamper of St. Petersburg experimented with Stry-n. on healthy young hospital assistants and found that it increased the amount of gastric juice secreted, the general acidity and the quantity of free acid in the secretion. It hastened the absorption from the stomach and strengthened mechanical movements. The effects continued some time after the administration was stopped. Marked action on the rectum and genitourinary organs (Ign. and Nux-v.). The male prover had his left testicle and cord swollen and an abscess of the scrotum developed and discharged. “Gurgling noise in rectum with electric darts” is a symptom of one prover. Many pains center about the lips and eyes. Pains and chills occur in the occiput and nape and run down whole length of spine. Stiffness is a leading note of Stry. and Cooper gave “rheumatism with stiff joints” as an indication. Itching of the whole body and “violent itching in roof of mouth.” Jerkings, twitch- ings and shocks in all parts. Increased activity of the spinal senses. Dread of touch, shrinks from drafts. Clarke found Cooper’s suggestion that many cases of persistent cough recurring after influenza are met by Stry. to be correct. The influenza cough has in it a strong spasmodic and asthmatic element, whether dry or not, and this seems to give one point of correspondence. C. W. Lawson related the case of a medical man who took continuously for two years, Stry. hydrochlor., 5 to 10 minims, thrice daily with a little sal volatile. He was at first benefited, but afterwards experienced a desire to take deep insoirations. “He felt that to do so would overcome the inhibitory power over the lung, probably the action of the diaphragm.” One morning after a dose of Stry., he was taking such an inspiration and from that moment experienced the sensations complained of an inability to take a deep breath. Fixation of chest walls compelled him to stoop, weakness on exertion, great confusion of thought and memory, occasional clay-colored feces, usually greater in amount than ordinary. After six months, the apex beat descended to the 6th interspace and headache and drowsiness became marked. He traveled for six months without benefit. All attempts to act on the heart with drugs increased the headache. Lawson then found the heart dilated, wide sub-costal angle, chest emphysematous, moving en mass. After a full year of treatment with Hyos. tincture at bedtime, which proved strikingly beneficial, drowsiness ceased entirely and improvement in all other respects followed. Hale mentioned the following uses of Stry. and its salts as observed by him and others. Stry. 6c. in the tetanic spasms of cerebrospinal meningitis. Amaurosis from atony of retina. Diplopia and night-blindness. Stry-s., and in one case when all other Stry. preparations had failed, Stry-val. cured facial neuralgia and neuralgic headache. Spasms of esophagus in an hysterical woman. Stry-val. 2x. cured brain exhaustion of women in whom high nervous weakness exists. Stry. 12c or 30c for chorea, when the convulsions do not cease during sleep. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Eucal. - neutralizes ill effects of strychnine. (2) Cic., Arn. (tetanus). (3) Stry. ars. - Paresis in the aged, relaxed musculature. Prostration. Psoriasis, chronic diarrhea with paralytic symptoms. Compensatory hypertrophy of heart with beginning fatty degeneration. Stry-ar. - Marked dyspnea when lying down, edema of lower limbs, urine scanty, high specific gravity, heavily loaded with glucose. Diabetes, use the 6x trituration. (4) Stry-f-c. - chlorotic and paralytic conditions, dyspepsia with vomiting of ingesta, 2x and 3x trituration. (5) Stry-n. - 2x and3x. Saidtoremovecravingforalcohol. Use for two weeks. (6) Stry-s. - Gastric atony. (7) Stry-val. - exhaustion of brain-power, women of high nervous weakness, 2x trituration. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Constant retching. Violent vomiting. Nausea of pregnancy.

Abdomen - Sharp pain in abdominal muscles, griping pain in bowels.

Rectum - Very obstinate constipation. Feces discharged involuntarily during spasms. Sensations - Feeling as if head and face were enlarged, after affects of debauches (Nux-v.). As if an iron cap were on head. Paralyzed feeling in left half of head and face. Scalp sore, as if hair had been pulled. As if nerves suddenly pulled out of teeth. As of a lump in throat. As if water dripped off right elbow, at intervals and off right shoulder. As if chopped in half at waist, at night.

Female - Desire for sex increased (Plat.). Any touch on body excites a voluptuous sensation.

Back - Rigidity of cervical muscles. Sharp pain in nape and down spine. Back stiff, violent jerks in spinal column. Icy sensation down spine.

Limbs - Cramp-like pains. Rheumatism with stiff joints. Limbs stiff. Violent jerking, twitching and trembling. Tetanic convulsions and opisthotonos, spasms provoked by slightest touch and attempt to move. Shocks in the muscles. Lungs - Spasm of muscles about larynx. Sharp, contractive pains in muscles of chest. Excessive dyspnea. Persistent cough, recurring after influenza.

Skin - Itching of whole body, especially nose. Icy sensation down the spine.

Modalities - Better from lying on back. Worse morning, after meals. Worse touch, noise, motion, exertion, walking.

Temperature - Cold chills down spine. Perspiration in a stream down head and chest. Lower limbs cold.

name: Strychnos Gaultheriana
author: Murphy
constitution: Albuminuria. Boils. Cancer. Carbuncles. Colic. Convulsions. Diarrhea. Eczema. Fatigue. Hydrophobia. Leprosy. Paralysis. Prurigo. Pustules. Rabies. Snakebites. Syphilis. Ulcers. Vertigo.
keynote:
PHARMACY - strych-g. Strychnos gaultheri- ana. Hoang nan. Tropical Bind-weed. N. O. Loganiacee. Tincture of dried bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Boils. Cancer. Carbuncles. Colic. Convulsions. Diarrhea. Eczema. Fatigue. Hydrophobia.…
full:
PHARMACY - strych-g. Strychnos gaultheri- ana. Hoang nan. Tropical Bind-weed. N. O. Loganiacee. Tincture of dried bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Boils. Cancer. Carbuncles. Colic. Convulsions. Diarrhea. Eczema. Fatigue. Hydrophobia. Leprosy. Paralysis. Prurigo. Pustules. Rabies. Snakebites. Syphilis. Ulcers. Vertigo.

HERBAL - The Strych-g. plant is indigenous to Tonquin, where it has a great reputation as aremedy for leprosy, hydrophobia, snakebites and diseases of the skin. The red dust of the bark contains the most active properties.

HOMEOPATHIC - The native method of Strychnos gaultheriana preparing the medicine is by moistening the mixture of the three powders with a little vinegar and forming the paste into pills of about a centimeter in diameter. When taken by a healthy person these pills cause fatigue, general indisposition, vertigo, tingling of the hands and feet involuntary movements of jaw. When a person is bitten by a poisonous animal, a dose of three or four grams is administered in vinegar. If none of these symptoms appear it is understood that the medicine is antagonized and the dose is increased until some of the symptoms manifest themselves, when the poison is considered to be destroyed. The use of alcohol is forbidden while a patient is taking this medicine. Vinegar appears to modify its virulence. In animals poisoned with it, tetanic convulsions always begin in the hind legs and spread all over the body. Brain, liver, kidneys and lungs were found congested post mortem. Generally improves nutrition, especially in constitutional syphilis. Exhaustion with vertigo, numbness and tingling in hands and feet involuntary action of lower jaw. Tetanic convulsions beginning in legs and spreading over body. Eczema, prurigo. Pustules and boils. Old ulcers. Leprosy. Snakebites. Tertiary syphilis and paralysis. Glandular disorders. Cancer of glandular structures. Removes fetor and hemorrhage in cancer, revives the healing process. MIND - Apathy. Lassitude, indisposition to make mental effort.

Head - Vertigo, headache.

Abdomen - Colic and diarrhea.

Skin - Malignant ulcers, pustular eczema, boils, carbuncles, leprosy. COMMENTS - In 1883 a proving of Strych-g. was made by seven people, producing a few symptoms. According to Hansen, there is prurigo, pustular eczemain parts well supplied with sebaceous glands (face, neck, genitals). General malnutrition. Glandular cancer. Boils, carbuncles, constitutional syphilis. The dose of which is 5 to 30 drops of the tincture three times a day. RELATIONS - Compare: Nux-v„ Cur., Ang., Bruc., Hydre. Follows well after Ars. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Kidneys - Albuminuria. Mucus casts.

name: Succinum Acidum
author: Murphy
constitution: Asthma. Fears. Globus. Hay fever. Hiccough. Hysteria. Leucocythemia splenica. Spleen disorders.
keynote: PHARMACY - succ-ac.Succinum acidum. Succinic acid. Amber oil. A mineralized fossil resin not to be confounded with Ambergris, Ambra. Trituration. Solution of the non-recti- fied oil prepared by dry distillation of Amber. Solution of Succinic acid. Historical dose: All potencies.…
full:
PHARMACY - succ-ac.Succinum acidum. Succinic acid. Amber oil. A mineralized fossil resin not to be confounded with Ambergris, Ambra. Trituration. Solution of the non-recti- fied oil prepared by dry distillation of Amber. Solution of Succinic acid. Historical dose: All potencies. Drop doses of the oil.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Fears. Globus. Hay fever. Hiccough. Hysteria. Leucocythemia splenica. Spleen disorders.

HOMEOPATHIC - Dr. Morris Weiner tested Succ-ac„ which he prepared himself from amber by dry distillation. The fumes of the crude acid, he said, are inflammable and produce asthma, cough, sneezing, weeping, dropping of watery mucus from nostrils, pain in chest and headache. On this indication, he treated thirty people suffering from hay fever and cured them all, saving them the necessity of making an annual exodus. He gave one or two grains of the 3x trituration of Succ. diluted in twelve teaspoonfuls of water, a teaspoonful every two hours. Burnett wrote in Diseases of Spleen, that the non-rectified oil is used as an organ remedy in spleen affections, especially when accompanied by nervous and hysterical phenomena. The crude oil is a thick brown liquid having a strong empyreumatic odor. It is a powerful local irritant and has been used with success as such in lumbago, rheumatism and sciatica. Succ-ac. enters into the composition of “Roche’s Embrocation,” and “Haarlem Oil,” and has a popular reputation as a remedy for whooping cough, the directions being for it to be rubbed into the spine night and morning. Succ-ac. produces many nervous and hysterical symptoms. Asthma. Fear of trains and closed places. Affections of spleen. Burnett noted it for hysterical convulsions in women. MIND - Fear of trains and closed places.

Head - Headaches. Lungs - Pains in chest. Asthma. Incipient tuberculosis. Chronic bronchitis. Whooping cough.

Eyes - Lachrymation.

Nose - Sneezing, dropping of watery mucus from nostrils.

Throat - Globus. COMMENTS - A tablespoonful dose, said Murrell, has caused persistent vomiting, diarrhea and symptoms of collapse and the patient aborted. He gave the oil, six ounces of acorn-water added half a scruple of the oil. They do not mix chemically, but by shaking each time a dose is taken the required division and potency is attained. Burnett’s keynote was “Painful spleen disorders where there are convulsive attacks such as the hysterical and hypochondriacal often have.” Burnett related in his book a most remarkable case of “chronic enlargement of the spleen with hyperesthesia, head pain, Dyspnea orthopnea, convulsions” in a young woman “towards the end of her teens.” After years of treatment, Burnett concluded from Rademacher’s account of Succ-ac. that it might provide the remedy. It was given in five-drop doses three times a day. In forty-eight hours the convulsive attacks ceased and all the phenomena slowly disappeared. A keynote of Burnett’s is “Fear of trains and close places.” His dose is five drops of the oil three times a day. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1) Amber gemstone. Succinum purum. (2) Ars-i. - Hay fever. Paroxysmal sneezing, dropping of watery mucus from nostrils, asthma. Inflammation throughrespiratory tract, causing asthma, chest pains, etc., itching of eyelids and canthi and nose worse drafts. (3) Arund., Wye., Sabad, Sinapis nigra. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Persistent hiccough. Violent vomiting.

name: Sulfanilamide
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from hot compresses, discharges..

PHARMACY - sulfa. Sulfanilamide. Para- amino-phenylsulfamide. Allopathie drug. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Addison’s disease. Anemia. Audio-visual, disorders. Boils. Cataract. Coma. Cyanosis. Delirium. Dermatitis. Goiter. Hypoglycemia. Jaundice. Ménière’ sdisease. Muscular, atrophy. Myxedema. Nephritis. Schizophrenia. Thyroid, deficiency.

HOMEOPATHIC - In medicine, Sulfanilamide is known in one form as Exoseptoplix. It was the active part in the decomposition ofprontosil which was used in experiments by Domagk in 1935. The homeopathic proving of sulfanilamide was conducted by Sutherland, who used the 3x. 6x and the 200th potency. Sulfa, has a slowing down of all physical and mental functions. Halt in development and puberty comes late in the child. Myxedema. Fatigue, general weariness. Indefinable discomfort with giddiness or vertigo, with apathy. Febrile condition with rash, aching, conjunctivitis, which may be accompanied by fever with shivering, pain in the joints increase in leucocytes with granulocytosis. Paresis and muscular atrophy of the feet and hands. Cramping pains in the hypogastric region. Oliguria and kidney colic. Hypoglycemic conditions. Heart rhythmic anomaly, cyanosis and comatose condition. Cyanosis with violet or livid coloring of the lips, nose, ears, fingertips. Vesicular eruptions. Goiter. Thyroid deficiency and congestion of the thyroid gland. MIND - Mental backwardness. Clouded mental state. Idea association complaints. Concentration complaints. Difficulty in determining contrasts and shapes. Loss of memory for graphic movements and for sounds and words. Loss of memory with diminution in auditory acuity. Physical and mental apraxia. Alternating psychological condition. Cyclical moods. At times happy, joyful, then sad and dejected. Indolence, apathy, state of confusion. Attacks of delirium. Schizophrenia.

Head - Frontal or occipital headache increasing towards evening.

Eyes - Chemosis of the left eye. Cloudiness of the crystalline lens or capsule. Cataract. Hemorrhaging of the retina. Optic neuritis. Stye on the lower left eyelid. Eruption of yellow pustules on the edge of the eyelids.

Ears - Pustules and papules on the outer ear. Buzzing in the ears, as if produced by a bell. Bilateral diminution in auditory acuity. Deafness through atrophy of the auditory nerve. Ménière’s disease. Boils in the auditory canal.

Nose - Pustules in the left nasal fold. Sneezing. Boils.

Face - Acne of the chin. Food - Hypoglycemic syndrome with condition of weakness, sweating, hunger pangs and tendency to faint with or without convulsions. Loss of appetite.

Stomach - Nausea, vomiting.

Abdomen - Sensation of fullness. Pain in the hypogastric region. Cramping abdominal pains. Congestion of the liver with alternate constipation and diarrhea. Gastric and duodenal ulcer. Jaundice.

Rectum - Alternate constipation and diarrhea.

Male - Inhibition of the production of spermatozoa. Sterility.

Chest - Pain and heat in the chest.

Heart - Rhythmic anomaly, especially in elderly people.

Limbs - Severe muscular pains. Acute rheumatism. Sciatica. Neuritic, especially sciatic pains. Progressive symmetrical muscular atrophy, beginning in the hands. Paresis or paralysis of the feet with muscular atrophy and absence of the Achilles' reflex. Acrocyanosis with formication and numbing of the limbs of the legs. Pain in the right leg. Pain and weakness in the small muscles of the feet and hands. Lungs - Dyspnea, difficulty in breathing deeply. Bronchial asthma.

Skin - Burns. Acne of the chin. Burning papular and pustular eruptions. Dermatitis. Sycosis of the beard. Chronic eczema. Pityriasis rubra. Erythema. Pigmentation disorders of the skin. Vesicular eruptions on uncovered areas exposed to the sun. Dermatitis from photosensitization. Measles-type, urticarial eruptions. Eruptions ameliorated by hot compresses and by discharges.

Modalities - Better from hot compresses, discharges.

Kidneys - Chronic interstitial nephritis. Kidney colic. Kidney stones. Paresis of the bladder with retention of urine. Slow urination, urinary stream weak. Urine cloudy. Oliguria. Presence of porphyrin in the urine. Hematuria. Uremia.

Blood - Anemia. Aplastic anemia. Hemolytic anemia. Chronic leukemia. Thrombopenia. Acetone elimination in the urine or excessive nitrogen in the blood. Agranulocytosis syndrome with fever, leucopenia, necrotic angina and light hemorrhaging of the skin and mucus membranes.

Temperature - Basal metabolism reduced. Vertigo - Vertigo with nausea, ameliorated in the open air and by leaning forwards. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ars. - Anxiety and agitation, especially between 1 a.m. and 3 a.m. Burning pains. Edema of the lower eyelids. Thirsty for small amounts of iced water. V omiting and diarrhea with severe prostration. Oppression. Scaly, burning eruptions and itching, worse between 1 a.m. and 3 a.m. (2) Cresol. - Asthenia with euphoria. Loquacious mood, talks non-stop. Paresis of the lower legs with ataxia. Hypertrophy of the muscles in the hands. Hypertension and oliguria. Hardening of the cartilages. Thickening and hardening of the skin. Itching, pigmented erythema of the skin. (3) Cic. - Convulsions, contraction of the muscles of the entire body. Pupils dilated. Pustular eruptions with thick, yellow scabs. REFERENCES - Julian.

full:
PHARMACY - sulfon. Sulfonalum. Sulfonal. Diethylsulphone dimethyl methane. Coal tar product. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Chorea. Constipation. Cramps. Cyanosis. Diarrhea. Epilepsy. Headaches. Heart failure. Hematoporphyri- nuria. Insomnia. Locomotor ataxia. Nausea. Paralysis, ascending. Ptosis. Reflexes, abolished. Tinnitus. Twitching. Vertigo. Vomiting. Weakness.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sulfonal was at first regarded as one of the safest of hypnotics, but many cases of poisoning by medicinal doses have occurred and the schema is made up of reported effects produced on patients. Sulfon. is a coal tar product which produces ataxic symptoms, staggering gait, anesthesia of legs with absence of knee jerks. Chorea. Cerebellar disease. V ertigo of cerebral origin. The symptoms disappear slowly. Reflexes abolished. Epilepsy, with overexcitability of the cortical substance. Twitching of muscles, especially of face and flexors, worse by voluntary movement, but always present in sleep. Muscular incoordination. Paralysis of body, better by cold water, and cold douches. Great prostration. Paralysis progressive sometimes with hyperesthesia and abnormal sensation, affecting first legs, then arms. Profound weakness, faint feeling and despondency. Fainted and vomited. Loss of control of sphincter. Livid, especially the face. Cyanosis. Death by respiratory failure preceded by unconsciousness. MIND - Mental confusion, incoherence, illusions, apathetic. Alternation of happy, hopeful states with depression and weakness. Extreme irritability. Stupidity. Unconscious with dilated and fixed pupils, profuse sweat.

Head - Headache and tinnitus aurium. Pain on attempting to raise head.

Eyes - Pupils dilated and fixed. Eyes bloodshot and restless. Ptosis, heavy look about eyes. Double vision.

Ears - Tinnitus.

Face - Livid.

Mouth - Breath smells of onions. Tongue as if paralyzed.

Throat - Aphasia, dysphagia, difficult speech. Vertigo - Vertigo of cerebral origin, unable to rise from seat. COMMENTS - Ataxic gait and diminished or abolished reflexes. Locomotor ataxia. Ascending paralysis. Stupor. Headache with noises in ears. Rashes on the skin, purpura, erythematous, etc. Vomiting and diarrhea. Urine retained or secretion arrested, claretcolored, containing albumen, porphyrin. Weak Sulfonalum heart, fainting occurs and death takes place by heart failure. One man observed uniform skin effects every time he took Sulfon., more intense the larger the dose. This occurred from 5 grains: patches of erythema appeared first on inner side of first phalanx of right little finger, next over proximal ends of metacarpal bones of left thumb and index, on posterior surface of left forearm a little below elbow, fourth on prepuce. The symptoms were better by cold douches. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Trion. - insomnia associated with physical excitement, vertigo, loss of equilibrium, ataxia, nausea, vomiting. Diarrhea, stertorous breathing, cyanosis, tinnitus, hallucination. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Stomach - Constant retching, vomiting and sorenessoverepigastrium. Vomiting, diarrhea and violent chills. Great disturbance of digestion with scanty urine.

Abdomen - Spleen enlarged, hyperemic. Back - Chronic leptomeningitis.

Rectum - Diarrhea and vomiting. Great constipation.

Male - Erythema on prepuce.

Heart - Heart failure and edema of lungs. Heart’s action feeble, occasionally intermittent.

Limbs - Restlessness, muscular twitchings. Ataxic movements, staggering gait, cold, weak, trembling, legs seem too heavy. Knee-jerks. Plantar reflex deficient. Cramps of legs and single muscles. Stiffness and paralysis of both legs. Anesthesia of legs. lutings - Congestion of lungs, stertorous breathing. Sighing dyspnea. Edema of lungs. Signs of bronchopneumonia.

Sleep - Insomnia. Fidgety, wakeful, drowsy. Sleepiness and weariness with unsteady gait. Stupor. Heaviness and drowsiness.

Skin - Itching, bluish purpura. Discolored patches like purpura on skin. Erythematous measles-like eruption.

Kidneys - Constant desire to urinate. Retention of urine, had to be drawn off, darkcolored. Urine very scanty, albuminous, almost solid when cooled, with casts. Pink color. Urine cherry-color, later like dark port wine. Hematoporphyrinuria, urine oscillated between deep claret and light claret color. Dark brown urine.

Temperature - Violent chills.

name: Sulphur
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better dry, warm weather, dry heat. Better open air, motion. Better sweating, walking. Better lying on right side, drawing up affected limbs. Standing is the most uncomfortable position. Worse at rest, stooping, reaching high. Worse talking, looking down. Worse crossing . running water, washing, bathing. Worse in morning, 11 a.m., at night. Worse full moon, atmospheric changes. Worse from alcoholic stimulants. Worse periodically. Worse from suppressions, milk, sweets. Worse warmth, over-exertion in bed. Worse woolens. Worse vaccinations. Worse suppressed hemorrhoids. Worse menopause..
