full:
PHARMACY - sulph. Sulphur. Brimstone. Sulphur lotum. Sulphur sublimatum. Sul- phur(At. Wt. 31.98). Trituration of Flowers of Sulphur. A saturated solution of Sulphur in absolute alcohol constitutes the tincture. A trituration of amorphous Sulphur has also been used. Sulphur prepared by precipitation from a solution of Calc-s. with hydrochloric acid, are included. Historical dose; All potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne. Adenoids. Alcoholism. Allergies. Amaurosis. Amenorrhea. Anemia. Anus, prolapsed. Asthma. Atelectasis. Backache. Bedsore. Belching. Biliousness. Boils. Brain, congestion. Bright's disease. Bronchitis. Cataract. Catarrh. Chancre. Chest, pains. Chilblains. Chloasma. Colds. Constipation. Corns. Cough. Crusta, serpiginosa. Dental fistula. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Eczema. Epilepsy. Eruptions. Esophagus, constriction. Eyes, disorders. Faintness. Feet, burning. Fever. Freckles. Ganglion. Glands, disorders. Gleet. Globus hystericus. Gonorrhea. Gout. Headache. Head, congestion. Hemorrhoids. Herpes. Hydrocele. Hydrocephalus. Hydrothorax. Hypochondriasis. Impotence. Influenza. Intermittents. Irritation. Itching. Jaundice. Keloids. Laryngitis. Leucorrhea. Lichen. Liver, disorders. Lumbago. Lungs disorders. Mania. Masturbation. Measles. Memory, weak. Meningitis. Menstruation, disorders. Miscarriage. Molluscum. Nettle rash. Neuralgia. Nipples, sore. Nosebleed. Ophthalmia. Phimosis. Phlegmasia dolens. Peritonitis. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Pregnancy, disorders. Prostatorrhea. Psoriasis. Rectaidisorders. Rheumatic fever. Rheumatism. Ringworm. Scabies. Sciatica. Senile, dementia. Skin, disorders. Sleep, disorders. Smell, illusions. Spinal curvature. Spleen, pain. Stomatitis. Taste, illusions. Tenesmus. Tonsillitis. Toothache. Trachea. Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Urticaria. Uterus, prolapsed. Vaccination. Varicocele. Varicose veins. Vertigo. Warts. Worms.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sulphur is an elementary substance, occurring in nature as a brittle crystalline solid, burning in the air with a blue flame, being oxidized to Sulphur dioxide (Sulphurous acid). Sulphur is a product of volcanic eruptions, found free in nature and was used from ancient times to remove skin disorders. The reputation of Sulphur as a remedy is perhaps as old as medicine. “As early as 2,000 years ago,” said Hahnemann, “Sulph. had been used as the most powerful specific against the scabies. “The itch with which the workers in wool are so much affected, causes an intolerably agreeable, tingling, itching, gnawing as of vermin. Some designate it as an intolerably voluptuous titillating itching, ceasing as soon as the parts are scratched and commencing to burn, which burning continues after the scratching. “Sulph. frequently produces in healthy persons burning-itching pimples and vesicles resembling the itch vesicles and especially itching in the joints and in the night.” The domestic use of Sulph. as a “Spring medicine” is based on its anti-psoric properties. “It is one of the most popular diaphoretics of the day,” said Milne, “few old women failing to use it when any eruption is supposed to be struggling through the skin.” The specific power of Sulph. to cure itch can be abused if applied externally as baths and ointments. Instead of being cured, the skin affection can be repelled and a host of secondary disorders will appear in its place. Sulph. is a major anti-psoric. A great reabsorbent and is frequently needed after acute illnesses which do not entirely clear up. Complaints that relapse. When carefully selected remedies fail to act, especially in acute diseases. It is often of great use in beginning the treatment of chronic diseases and in finishing acute ones or when the reaction is deficient. Irregular distribution of circulation, causing local burning, throbbing or congestion, flushes of heat, rush of blood to head, chest, heart. Its action is centrifugal from within outward. Ascending effects. Affinity for the skin, where it produces heat and burning with itching, made worse by heat of the bed. Dry, unhealthy hair and skin. Very red lips and face, flushing easily. Redness of orifices or of single parts is another prominent feature due to irregular circulation, lips, ears, nose, eyelids, anus, vulva. Weak faint spells, frequently during the day after nursing or night watching with great sleepiness. Empty, sinking feeling, in stomach. Sensation of fullness, roughness or numbness. Inertia and relaxation of fiber, characteristic feebleness of tone. Chorea, chronic after suppressed eruptions. Epilepsy with a feeling that mouse is running up arms to back, before the fit. Child jumps, starts and screams fearfully. As if swinging or standing on wavering ground. Nutrition is affected on account of defective assimilation in spite of voracious appetite, the patient emaciates (especially children). Thin and weak, even with good appetite. Hungry and always tired. Cat-nap sleep. Glandular swelling indurated and suppurating. Mucus discharges and exhalations are acrid, blood streaked offensive and cause itching. Serous effusions or deposits are absorbed slowly. General offensive character of discharge and exhalations. Body offensive in spite of washing. Aversion to being washed, always worse after the bath. Aversion to water. Child looks dried, a little old man, big head, big belly with emaciated limbs. Dirty, filthy people, prone to skin disorders. Patient is unable to walk erect, stoop shouldered, unwashed, tall and lean, untidy. Coal miner’s disorders. Ragged philosopher. MIND - Absent-minded. Dullness of mind. Brain fatigue. Difficult thinking. Very forgetful. Weak memory, especially for names. Misplaces things, words, cannot find proper words when talking or writing. Scatter- brained, burntout brains (Sil., Ph-ac., Med., Cann.). Repeats everything said to him on account of difficult comprehension. Awkwardness at his work. Aversion to do mental or physical work. Bored easily. Lazy, cannot arouse himself. Lazy, hungry and always tired. Averse to business, or busy all the time. Workaholics, ambitious, aggressive (Nux-v.). Often irritable, depressed. Irritated greatly by least advice. Dislikes having anyone near him. Quarrelsome and impatient nothing pleases. Impatience about trifles. Censorious, critical. Despises literary people and education. Anger over his mistakes. Alcoholism. Melancholy. Sadness from injuries of head. Sadness during labor. Tired of life. Strong impulsive tendency to suicide by drowning or leaping from a window. Imagines giving wrong things to people, causing their death. Worried by trifles. Anxiety about others, imagination leads them to worry. Anxiety from pressure on chest. Anxiety about friends at home. Fear of failure, or poverty, of starving. Fear of ghosts at night, of robbers. Childish peevishness in adults. Moaning and complaining day and night, with wringing of hands. Anxiety with an overactive mind, preventing sleep. Restlessness at night. Persistent thoughts, expressions and words heard recur to his mind. Absorbed in thoughts in evening. Obsessive, curious. Intellectuals. Haughty. Egotistical and obstinate. Very selfish, no regard for others. Indifference to the welfare of others. Megalomania. Delusions of grandeur. Foolish happiness and pride. Imagines himself a great person. Fear of not being recognized. Insecurity, poor self-confidence. Indifference to personal appearance. Monomania. Strong tendency to philosophical or religious reveries with fixed ideas. Makes many plans and theories. Philosophical mania, wants to know who made this or that and how. Racks his brain about metaphysical subtleties. Ragged philosophers. Religious melancholy. Religious aversion to opposite sex. Indisposition to play in children. Religious affections in children. Laughing over serious matters. Thinks himself in possession of beautiful things, everything looks pretty. Senility. Senile dementia.

Head - Hot head with cold feet. Constant heat on top of head (Cupr., Graph.). Hot, throbbing, heavy, sore vertex. Heaviness and fullness, pressure in temples. As of a band about or pain deep in brain. Beating headache, worse stooping and with vertigo. Sick headaches recurring periodically, on every Sunday, preceded by photopsia. Head bent forward when walking. Fontanelles remain open too long. Hydrocephalus with convulsions, red face and pupils dilated. Tinea capitis, dry form. Itching, scratching causes burning. Scalp dry. Sweaty scalp. Hair, dry, cold, hard, falling off, worse washing.

Eyes - Painful inflammation of eye from presence of foreign body. Cutting as from sand. Heat and burning in eyes (Ars., Bell.). Bursting pain in eyeballs. Trembling of eyes, quivering of eyelids. Chronic ophthalmia with much burning and itching. First stage of ulceration of cornea. Photophobia. Parenchymatous keratitis. Keratitis, cornea like ground glass. Retinitis caused by overuse of eyes. Oily tears. Burning ulceration of margin of lids. Agglutination of lids. Styes and tarsal tumors. Eczema of lids. Trachoma. Opacities of vitreous. Obscuration of vision like black gauze or motes before eyes. Halo around lamplight. Objects seem more distant than they are.

Ears - Purulent, offensive otorrhea, catarrhal discharge even on the eighth day. Bad effects from the suppression of an otorrhea. Very red ears in children. Sensation as if sounds do not come through the ear but through forehead. Whizzing in ears. Swashing as of water. Deafness preceded by exceedingly sensitive hearing, catarrhal deafness.

Nose - Pale, red and scabby. Fluent burning coryza, worse outdoors, stopped indoors. Frequent sneezing. Obstructed on alternate sides. Chronic dry catarrh, dry scabs and readily bleeding. Nosebleeds, worse at night, on lying on right side. Polyps and adenoids. Herpes across the nose. Freckles and black pores on nose. Tip of nose or alae nasi red, swollen, worse cold. Sensitive to smell. Imaginary odors.

Face - Pale, sickly and old looking. Circumscribed redness of cheeks. Lips, bright red, swollen (upper), dry, rough, cracked, burning, twitching or trembling. Freckled, spotted. Acne. Mumps. Swollen veins on forehead.

Mouth - Bitter taste in morning. Sour, sweetish, foul taste. Food tastes like straw or too salty. Profuse saliva, with nauseous taste. Nursing sore mouth. Aphthae, thrush. Tongue white with red tip and borders. Dry, tremulous tongue. Sensitive, tender teeth. Jerking, shooting, throbbing pains in teeth. Grinding of the teeth. Gums bleeding. Swelling of gums, throbbing pain. Lips dry, bright red, burning.

Throat - Burning, redness and dryness. External redness. Sensation, as of a lump, hair or splinter or as of a vapor rising in. Ball seems to rise and close the pharynx. As if swollen. Dry, exciting cough. Deep, hoarse voice. Aphonia. Vertigo - Vertigo in forehead, worse when crossing a river, stooping with headache. COMMENTS - Sulph. is used in various countries for allaying pain in a variety of forms. A piece of stick Sulph. carried in the pocket is commonly used in England to ward off rheumatism. Natives of South America apply Sulph. in solid form to painful parts and allow it to act for an hour before result is effected. For lumbago and chronic rheumatic pains a bag filled with Flowers of Sulphur, heated and applied to the part, immediately relieves the pain. An experienced sea captain testified to the extreme frequency of rheumatism among his sailors, but, he added, when carrying cargoes of Sulph., he had never had a case of acute rheumatism on board. Dr. Laugardiere of Toulouse, reported to the Academy of Medicine that he had discovered a cure for croup: a tablespoonful of Flowers of Sulphur dissolved in a tumbler of water. After three days of this treatment his patients were rescued from imminent death and fully recovered. Many practitioners spoke highly of a local application of Sulph. to the fauces in the treatment of croup and diphtheria. Nettle rash is often relieved by a little Flowers of Sulphur, water and Sulph. mixed with sea sand and rubbed over itch vesicles destroys the acarus at once. In the early days of vaccination it was found that the action of Sulph. was adverse to the receptivity of vaccine. According to Dr. Tierney, Dr. Jenner failed in vaccinating thirty soldiers, all under treatment by Sulph. Cooper noted that operatives in sulphur mines enjoy an immunity against ague when prevalent in surrounding districts, and that, before going on hunting expeditions in malarious districts, men in Ethiopia sub- Sulphur mit themselves to fumigations with Sulph. and find it an efficient prevention of ague. Cooper thought there was a great probability of Sulph. having a power of destroying the organisms in the blood of ague patients. Hahnemann found in Sulph. the homeopathic counterpart of the peculiar constitutional weakness which tends to manifest in itch-like eruptions and which he named Psora. Sulph. is the chief of the anti-psoric remedies. It is this property of Sulph. to divert to the surface constitutional irritants which renders it the chief of Hahnemann’s anti-psorics. Sulph. has also an anti-psoric action independently of its power of “bringing out” rashes. The psoric poison may be present and active in a case of disease and “apparently well-indicated remedies may fail to act” in consequence. In such cases, one or two doses of Sulph. will frequently antidote the psora and either clear up the case or open the way for the action of other remedies. In such cases there will almost certainly be some Sulph. indications present. Sulph. is a potent antiseptic and is one of the most certain destroyers of scabies. The exact relation of acarus itch to psora and other itching eruptions need not be considered, but as Sulph. has the power of repressing constitutional eruptions when locally applied, as well as the power of destroying the acarus, it is best to use other means (e.g., oil of lavender) for the latter purpose and give Sulph. or other indicated remedies internally. The symptoms of latent psora are detailed in Hahnemann’s Chronic Diseases. They are. for the most part, almost exact reproductions of the symptoms of Sulph. But while Sulph. is the chief of anti-psorics, it is only one of many and Sulph. is in no way limited in its uses to cases of latent or declared psora. When well-selected remedies fail to act or act too short a time because of the patient’s feeble reactive powers, Sulph. will often build up the vital powers of the patient to effect the cure. It will clear the way by removing the psoric miasm to permit other similar remedies on their indications to cure the patient. Useful for complaints that are always relapsing (menses, leucorrhea, etc.), patient seems to get almost well when the disease returns again and again. Irregular distribution of the circulation, flushes of heat, rush of blood to the head, chest, and heart. Plethora from suddenly suppressed eruptions, hemorrhoids, discharges. Heat and burning sensation of all parts or coldness, and sweating of many parts. Hot flushes during the day with weak, faint spells, passing off with a little moisture. Sensation of burning on vertex, of vesicles in mouth, and dryness of throat. Smarting in eyes, cutting, stabbing pain in right eye. Congestions to single parts, eye, nose, chest, abdomen, ovaries, arms, legs or any organ of the body, marking the onset of tumors or malignant growths, at menopause. First right, then left in stomach, in rectum, in anus and itching. Heat in chest rising to face and skin, with hot flushes in spots below scapulae. Burning soles, must find a cool place for them at night. Hot head with cold feet. Lutze found that Sulph. 1,000c will make feet that have been cold for years comfortably warm. Irregularities may go on to actual inflammation with effusions and to fever of intermittent or other types. Will cause absorption of effusions from pleuritis, hydrocephalus or synovial. Periodical headaches, headaches occurring every week, every month. Sick headaches. Headaches are accompanied by red face and hot head, are better in warm room, at rest, worse in open air, worse from stooping. Headache on coughing. Clarke cured a severe occipital headache worse on coughing with Sulph. 30c. Stopped catarrh, nose obstructed indoors, better outdoors. Nasal catarrh where the nose is stopped indoors and free out of doors. White, frothy expectoration. Asthma. Alternation between skin irritation and asthma. Tuberculosis with marasmus, with hunger at 11 a.m., sore, red orifices, flushes of heat. Tuberculosis of the lungs when the “body feels too hot.” Must have windows open. Rheumatism and sciatica, better morning and worse at night in bed. Rheumatism, begins below and spreads upwards. Unhealthy skin, tendencies to eczema, psoriasis. Burning and heat. Voluptuous itching, worse scratching, scratching causes burning, worse from heat of bed, soreness infolds. Red blotches. Sores that don’t heal well. Boils, coming in crops in various parts or a single boil is succeeded by another as soon as the first is healed. Offensive odor of body despite frequent washing. Aversion to bathing. Aggravated by water (Petrol.), with itching and burning. Poor hygiene or poverty (Psor.). Unkempt appearance. Allergic to wool. Skin disorders that have been treated by medicated soaps or creams, hemorrhoids that have been treated by ointments. Redness of orifices and parts near orifices. Red ears, eyelids and borders around eyelids. Brilliant red lips, bright red anus in children, red meatus of urethra, red vulva. Red nose, worse by cold, the colder the redder. Orifices are red, congested, sore and hypersensitive. The passage of all discharges or excretions is painful. Feeling of emptiness. “Faint, sinking, allgone sensation at 11 a.m.” Empty sensation in head, heart, stomach, abdomen. “Must have something between breakfast and dinner-time.” Low blood sugar. Ravenous hunger. Defective assimilation, hungry yet emaciated. Poor breakfast eaters. Poor dietary habits. Toxicity. Ulcers and burning in the stomach. Dyspepsia from suppressed eruptions, from farinaceous food. After eating, dyspeptic patients feel puffed up, heavy, sluggish, and low-spirited. Cannot take milk, vomits it at once. Sour vomit with undigested food. Crave sweets, fats, spicy foods, wine, beer and marijuana. Alcoholism (Nux-v.). They crave beer, and marijuana. Aversion to eggs. Dyspepsia of alcoholics. Craving for alcohol. Chronic alcoholism, dropsy and other ailments in alcoholics, they reform but are continually relapsing. Gallavardin cured many apparently hopeless alcoholics with Sulph. 1,000c. Scalding urine like fire. Portal congestion. Constipation with ineffectual urging, constipation alternating with diarrhea. Stools are hard, dry, knotty, as if burnt, large, painful. Child is afraid to have stool on account of pain, or pain compels child to desist on first effort, alternating with diarrhea. Diarrhea, after midnight, painless, driving out of bed early in morning, as if bowels were too weak to contain their contents. Hemorrhoids with burning and itching. Drowsy in afternoon, after sunset, wakeful the whole night. Chronic insomnia from an overactive mind. Nightly suffocative attacks, wants doors and windows open. Becomes suddenly wide awake at night. Happy dreams, wakes up singing. Cramp in calves and soles at night. Will stick their feet out from the covers to cool down the body at night in bed. “Worse by heat,” by warmth of the bed, humidity. Worse at night, 11 a.m. Aversion to being washed, always worse after a bath. Not well since vaccinations, especially skin problems. Ailments from the abuse of metals. Taken altogether there are more symptoms on the left side than the right. It acts strongly on the left side of the chest. “Sharp stitching pains through left lung to back, worse lying on back, worse by least motion.” The child looks dried up, a little old man, skin hanging in folds, yellowish, wrinkled, flabby. Head large in proportion to body. Lymphatic glands enlarged. Clarke frequently cured ganglion of the wrist with Sulph. given on general indications. Sulph. 30c rescued a patient from a condition that seemed desperate in a case of left pleuro-pneumonia following a violent hemoptysis. Lippe cured a case of menorrhagia with “a single dose of Sulph. at new moon,” the patient had not been well since her last miscarriage. Skinner gave a single dose of Sulph. 100,000c with instructions to take it on a certain date (when the moon was full) to a man who had paresis of the lower limbs. The man recovered suddenly. Cooper used it to keep his regiment of sepoys in India healthy when many others were in the hospital with fever. One writer treated nine cases with the pilules and arrested the fever in twenty-four hours. One of the cases was a particularly obstinate one and had been pronounced by the doctors to be complicated with liver affection. Quinine had been tried before to Sulph. cured. Cooper, in a case of “Charges fever” of West Indies, which had lasted three months, ordered a Sulphur bath as well as the Sulph. pilules. That single bath seemed to alter the whole condition and the patient, an unhealthy, anemic, bilious-looking man, rapidly became the picture of health. RELATIONS-Antidoted by: Aeon., Camph., Cham., Chin., Merc., Puls., Rhus, Sep., Thuj. Antidote to: Aeon., Aloe., Chi., lod., Merc., Nit-ac., Olean., Rhus, Sep., Thu., ailments from abuse of metals generally. Compare: (1) Aeon., Ars. - Sulph. often follows in acute diseases. (2) Merc, and Calc., Lyc., Sep., Sars., Puls. (3) Tann- ac. - nasal hemorrhage, elongated uvula, gargle, constipation. (4) Pyrar. - a fish caught in the Amazon, clinically used for various skin affections, leprosy, tuberculosis, syphilis, varicosities, etc. (5) Meningitis, Apis. (6) Early- morning diarrhea, Bry. (as soon as he moves), Nat-s. (with much flatus), Podo, (stools changeable, go on all day, though worse at noon, Sul. raw, sore anus), (7) Defective reaction, Psor., Op., Care. (8) Hot flashes at menopause, Lach., Sul-ac., Amyl-n., Kali-bi. (9) Intermittent fever and neuralgia, Chin., Ars., Bapt. (10) Ravenous hunger with heat at vertex, Calc., Phos. (11) Tuberculosis, Bac., Calc., Tub., Phos. (12) Itch, Merc., Sep., Caust. (13) Dyspepsia, Lyc., Nux-v., Sep. (14) Pneumonia, restoration imperfect, Sang. Complementary: Aloe, Psor., Aeon., Ars. Nux-v., Lyc., Sars., Sep., Puls., Thuj. Follows well: Merc-s. complements Rhus-t. in paralysis. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Burning, painful, weight-like pressure. Heaviness in stomach. Very weak and faint about 11 a.m., must have something to eat. Great acidity, sour eructation. Belchings on pressing on stomach. Putrid belchings tasting like bad eggs, worse eating or at night. Milk causes sourtaste andsour belchings. Vpmitingof undigested food or sour vomiting. Nausea during pregnancy.

Abdomen - Sore, very sensitive to pressure, internal feeling of rawness and soreness. Abdomen heavy, as of a lump. Movements as of something alive (Croc., Thuj.), as of the fist of a child. Stitches in region of spleen, worse coughing or deep inspiration. Intestines feel as if strung in knots, worse bending forward. Bearing down against rectum. Colic after eating or drinking, obliging one to bend double, worse sweet things. Colic after drinking. Colicky babies. Big belly, emaciated limbs in children. Eczema about navel. Baek - Curvature of spine. Drawing pain between shoulders. Neck stiff. Muscles of neck weak, child cannot hold head. Boils on neck. Sensation as if the vertebrae glide over each other or crack on bending backwards. Aching between scapulae. Lumbar pains to stomach, walks bent from pain in the back, can only straighten up after moving. Supports weight on hands when sitting. Coccyx pains during stools. Aching in small of back, worse when urinating. Breasts - Sharp burning in breasts. Nipples, cracked, around the base, smart, burn, bleed after nursing, pain extends to back. Cancer of breast or uterus. Breast and uterus develops imperfectly. Causations - Suppressions. Alcohol. Sun. Chills. Sprains, over-exertion, reaching high. Falls, blows. Bedsores.

Rectum - Redness around the anus with itching. Pain, urging and burning in rectum. Involuntary stools on sneezing or laughing with emission of flatus. Morning diarrhea, drives out of bed with prolapsed rectum. Painless diarrhea, changing, mushy, foul, painless, watery, grayish, frothy worse milk. Stools flat and thin. Diarrhea of infants with profuse sweating, drowsiness, suppression of urine and the child wakes up screaming. Children afraid, hold stools back on account of pain. Diarrhea alternating with constipation. Habitual constipation. Frequent, unsuccessful desire, hard, knotty, insufficient. Odor of stool follows him as if he had soiled himself. Hemorrhoids, oozing and belching. External and internal hemorrhoids, great bunches that are sore, tender, raw, burn, bleed and smart. Hemorrhoids during pregnancy. Sensations - As if a band were tied tightly around forehead or cranium. Vertigo as if swinging. As if one stood on wavering ground. As if hair on vertex stood on end. As if hernia would form. As if lungs came in contact with back. Heart as if enlarged. Like a weight on shoulder. Asif something heavy hanging on upper arm. Arms as if beaten. As of a mouse running up arms and back. Thigh as if broken. As if too short in popliteal space. As if bed were not large enough to hold him.

Male - Hydrocele. Testes hang low. Induration of testes. Discharge of prostatic fluid after urination and stool. Stitches in penis. Penis cold. Prepuce stiff, hard like leather with copious smegma, causes itches. Fetid sweat on genitals. Itching of genitals when going to bed. Organs cold, relaxed and powerless. Involuntary elaissions. Seminal emission on touching a woman. Seminal emission with burning in urethra. Semen, odorless, watery. Sexual power weak, impotence. Exhaustion in the morning after seminal emission. Backache and weakness of the limbs after sex, with sadness and irritability.

Female - Amenorrhea. Suppression of men - ses from excitement. Menses preceded by headache. Menses too late, short, scanty and difficult, thick, black, acrid, making parts sore. Leucorrhea of yellow mucous, burning, excoriating. Weak feeling in genitals. Offensive genitals with offensive sweat on thighs. Pudenda itches. Vagina and vulva burn, itch and sore, worse sitting is scarcely able to keep still. Sore feeling in vagina during sex. Bearing down in pelvis towards genitals, worse standing. Puerperal sepsis with high fever, profuse sweat of whole body, tenderness of abdomen and drowsiness. Prolapse of uterus from reaching high. Cancer of uterus. Uterus develops imperfectly. Food - Complete loss of appetite or ravenous appetite. Feels hungry, but when comes to the table, he loathes the food, turns away from it. Eats anything and everything. Headache or feels tired if he does not eat often. Food tastes too salty. Aversion to meat. Desire for sweets (Arg-n.), for raw food. Sweets, milk disagrees. Water fills the patient up. Drinks much, eats little.

Chest - Burning sensation in chest. Oppression, as of a load on chest. Shooting pains in chest extending to back worse coughing, lying on back and deep breathing. Pain backward from left nipple. As of a band or load on chest. Red, brown spots all over chest. Heat, throughout chest. Sensation of burning or coldness in chest, extending to face. Feeling of weakness in chest, while talking. Constitutions - Suited to lean, stoopshouldered persons, who walk and sit stooped, standing is the most uncomfortable position. Persons of psoric temperament, nervous, quick-motioned, quick-tempered, plethoric, skin excessively sensitive to atmospheric changes. Dirty, filthy people with greasy skin and long, straight, matted hair, prone to skin disorders. Children who cannot bear to be washed or bathed, emaciated, big-bellied, restless, hot, kick off clothes at night, have worms. Persons of scrofulous diathesis, subject to congestions, especially of portal system. Lymphatic temperaments, nervous constitutions disposed to hemorrhoids with constipation or morning diarrhea, diseases caused especially by suppressed eruptions. Emaciated children, old-looking faces, big bellies, dry, flabby skin. Full-blooded persons with great irritability, restlessness and hastiness. Old people. People with hot, sweaty hands. “Ragged philosophers,” dirty-looking persons who are always speculating on religious or philosophical subjects.

Heart - Heart feels too large. Pericarditis with effusion. Sharp pains go through chest to between shoulders. Palpitations, worse lying at night in bed, going up an ascent. Pulse more rapid in morning than in evening.

Limbs - Heaviness, paretic feeling in limbs. Jerks one limb on dropping to sleep. Rheumatic gout with itching. Swelling of the joints with hydro-arthrosis. Joints stiff, especially knees and ankles. Tense hamstring (left). Cramp in calf (left). Soles, burn, wants them uncovered, at night, cold in bed, dry. Poplitiae tight on stooping. Tuberculosis of the knee and hip joints. Unsteady gait. Ganglion. Cannot walk erect, stoop-shouldered. Heavy shoulders. Rheumatic pain in left shoulder. Left arm numb, worse lying. Numb fingers. Tremulous sensation in hands, when writing. Palms, dry, bum, crack, peel, eczema on, warts on. Ulcers around the nails. Whitlow with rapid swelling of the finger, redness, stiffness and excessive burning stitching. Involuntary contraction of hands as if about to grasp something. Hot, sweaty hands. Sweat in armpits, smelling like garlic.

Sleep - Drowsy, then migraine. Sleeps in catnaps, slightest noise awakens. Drowsy by day, wakeful at night. Heavy, unrefreshing. Talks, jerks and twitches during sleep. Awakes with starts or screams. Sings during sleep or wakes up singing. Vivid dreams, remain impressed on the memory. Wakes frequently and becomes wide awake suddenly. Cannot sleep between 2 and 5 a.m.

Skin - Skin as if denuded and sore. Unhealthy skin, breaks out, dry, scaly. Skin festers and would not heal, every little injury suppurates. Excoriation, especially in folds (Lyc.). Voluptuous, violent itching, worse at night, heat of bed, scratching and washing. Burning when scratched, painfully sensitive to air, wind, washing. Itching, especially from warmth in evening, often recurs in spring, in damp weather. Pimply eruption, pustules, cracks, hangnails. Freckles. Crops of boils. Scabies. Cracks. Eczema. Ulcers. Creeping erysipelas. Suppuration with air bubbles. Varicóse veins, ulcerate, rupture and bleed. Eruptions, can alternate with other complaints, asthma etc. Skin disorders after local medication. Feeling of a band around bones.

Modalities - Better dry, warm weather, dry heat. Better open air, motion. Better sweating, walking. Better lying on right side, drawing up affected limbs. Standing is the most uncomfortable position. Worse at rest, stooping, reaching high. Worse talking, looking down. Worse crossing . running water, washing, bathing. Worse in morning, 11 a.m., at night. Worse full moon, atmospheric changes. Worse from alcoholic stimulants. Worse periodically. Worse from suppressions, milk, sweets. Worse warmth, over-exertion in bed. Worse woolens. Worse vaccinations. Worse suppressed hemorrhoids. Worse menopause.

Liver - Pain and soreness of liver. Stitches in region of liver. Gallbladder colic and çhronic jaundice. Relapsing jaundice. Lungs - Difficult respiration, wants windows open, nightly suffocative air hunger. Dyspnea in middle of night, relieved by sitting up. Irregular breathing. Asthma preceded by colds. Loose cough, worse from talking, morning, greenish, purulent, sweetish expectoration. Much rattling of mucus and heat in chest, worse 11 a.m. Pleuritic exudations. Cough, violent in two or three incomplete bouts, tickling as from down in larynx. Greenish, sweetish and purulent expectoration. Violent cough with headache worse lying on back. As of rivet through upper third of left lung. Neglected pneumonia.

Kidneys - Painful, ineffectual efforts to urinate, retention. Itching, burning in urethra during urination, lasting long after. Parts sore over which it passes. Thin stream, intermits. Great quantities of colorless urine, greasy particles, mucus and pus in it. Sudden call to urinate, must hurry. Urination involuntary while passing flatus or on coughing. Frequent urination, especially atnight. Bedwetting, especially in scrofulous, untidy children. Every cold settles in the bladder.

Temperature - Dry skin and great thirst. Chill spreading up back. Flushes of heat. Feels too hot. Frequent flashes of heat, violent ebullitions of heat throughout entire body. Heat with general throbbing, between scapulae. Sweat on single parts in axilla, hands and feet. Profuse sweat at night with sulphur odor. Night sweat, on nape and occiput. Sweat without relief. Sweat may occur on one side of the body only or on neck only. Remittent fever. Septic, puerperal fever.

PHARMACY - sul-h. Sulphur hydrogenisatum. Sulfuretted hydrogen. Solution of the gas. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Asphyxia. Asthma. Blood, poisoning. Convulsions. Delirium. Fever. Headache. Mania. Prostration. Tetanus. Typhoid fever.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sul-h. is a colorless inflammable gas, having a sweetish taste and an exceedingly fetid smell resembling rotten eggs. It is extremely poisonous when inhaled. It is evolved when animal or vegetable tissues containing sulphur decay. It also occurs in mineral springs, being liberated by the reduction of gypsum or other sulphates through the action of a microbe. Sulph-h. is one of the remedies which help “blood poisoning” especially when bad smells are encountered. Asphyxia, tetanus, delirium, low continued fever have been observed as resulting from the gas. COMMENTS - J. Wiglesworth recorded two cases of insanity, one certainly and both probably, due to inhaling the gas. The first concerned R. H., 32, an engine man at chemical works, who had been kept at home with an attack of bronchitis for ten days. A few days after his return to work he became “gassed” (i.e., accidentally inhaled Sul-h.). This caused headache, stupor, prostration, compelling him to stay at home for a few days, when he became wildly delirious. He passed into a very excited state, shouting and gesticulating, said he was Jesus Christ. He tried to bury his head in the floor and to raise his feet above his head. Three days later he was admitted to Rainhill Asylum and there was still very violent and excited, gesticulating and talking incoherently, chiefly on religious subjects. At the end of a month there was some improvement and he was discharged, he recovered five months after admission. In the other case, that of a laborer at chemical works, Wiglesworth is not quite certain that Sul-h. was the poison inhaled. This patient was greatly excited, threw his arms about, shouted and laughed by turns, was excited and talkative. He remained permanently insane. REFERENCES - Clarke.

PHARMACY - sul-i. Sulphur iodatum. Sulphur iodide. Trituration. Historicaldose: All potencies, third trituration.

CLINICAL - Chorea. Rheumatoid, arthritis. St. Vitus’s dance.

HOMEOPATHIC - Sul-ter. is referred to in the Hon. Robert Boyle’s works. A Sul-ter. lx dilution cured a most obstinate case of St. Vitus’s dance and has often relieved pain in chronic rheumatic arthritis. REFERENCES - Clarke. Cooper.

Head - Headache better sundown. Hair seems erect.

Eyes - Zigzag before vision.

Face - Acne. Suppurating pimples. Parotid hypertrophy after mumps.

Mouth - Raw, dry, wants to moisten it. Cold sores on lips. Tongue is glazed, thickened after inflammation. Teeth feel soft. Parotid hypertrophied.

Throat - Raw, dry, painful in swallowing. Uvula and tonsils enlarged and red. Swollen. Vertigo - Vertigo worse stooping, binding of the hair, fasting, before and during menses. COMMENTS - Dr. Berlin treated with Sul-i. two cases of “weeping eczema” associated with varicose veins of the leg and pronounced itching. Also a child with eczema of arms. The keynote was “dark red, swollen and sweeping eczematous surface which itches terribly.” Sul-i. 3x trituration, was given. Hansen mentioned, among the therapeutic uses of Sul-i., thickness of tongue remaining after glossitis. Hypertrophy of parotids after parotiditis. Chronic hypertrophy of tonsils. Lichen planus, chronic and simple. Bradford reported a case of burning at the end of penis, dull pain in prostatic region, weakness across kidneys. Frequent desire to urinate with slight flow, eats very little, does not go out of doors is much discouraged about himself. Sul-i. 3x cured. Violent attack of pain in kidney region with shootings down ureters, pain and weakness about kidneys, constant desire to urinate, urine thick and whitish with creamy sediment. Sul-i. 3x and 6x cured. Stricture after gonorrhea, chordee, very painful urination, twisted stream. Yellow discharge. Sul-i. cured. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Band across forehead, Mane. (2) Difficult expectoration, Kali-bi. (3) Heat in heart, Lachn., Rhod. (4) Sleepy by day, restless at night, Staph. (5) Acne, Bell-p., Kali-br. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Phatak. ***SULPHUR TEREBINTHINATUM (Terebinthinated Sulphur) PHARMACY - sul-ter. Sulphur terebinthina- tum. Terebinthinated sulphur. One part of purified Sulphur is dissolved by heating in one hundred parts of Turpentine. Dilutions. Historical dose: All potencies.

Stomach - Tremors in epigastrium on exertion.

Abdomen - Mesenteric disease.

Rectum - Stubborn constipation. Bright yellow stools. Foul anal discharge. Sensations - Hair feels as if erect. As if a band across forehead. As if heat in heart.

Male - Testes soft. Prepuce cracked. Hydrocele of small boys. Deficient erections.

Female - Irregular menses. Copious thick, burning, leucorrhea worse before and after menses. Food - Anorexia. Appetite increased in marasmus of children. Desire for acids.

Limbs - Aching soreness below knees. Soles of feet ache, bum and sore, when standing. Lungs - Chest constricted, dropsy of pleura and eruptions on chest. Breathing asthmatic, irregular, rattling and suffocative. Cough worse a.m., spasmodic. Expectoration greenish, purulent, copious, viscid and yellow.

Skin - Moist eczema. Suppurating acne. Barber’s itch. Lichen planus. Papular eruption on face. Itching. Ulcers. Itching on ears, nose and in urethra. Arms covered with itching rash. Boils on neck. Hair feels as if erect.

Modalities - Better by expectoration. Better from cool air, winter. Better standing. Worse from exertion, even slight. Worse lying on right side, leaning forward, stooping, ascending stairs, rising. Worse before storms. Worse night, in morning.

Kidneys - Urine, scanty, purulent, with brown sand. Urine smells like raspberries. Stricture after gonorrhea, painful urination, stream twisted. Burning at the end of penis, dull pain in prostate.

Worse concussion of brain. Worse during menopausal period..

Constipation. Corns. Debility. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Diphtheria. Dyspepsia. Erythema nodosum. Esophagitis. Gangrene. Gastritis. Glossitis. Hair, ioss. Heartburn. Hemorrhoids. Hernia, inguinal. Hiccoughs. Hot, flushes.
