HERBAL - The poisonous properties of the yew have been recognized and disputed from ancient times. Gerarde said that in his school days he and his companions ate their fill of yew berries and slept not only under its shade, but on its branches without any ill effect, but there is plenty of evidence on the other side. In the Med. Press, May 29, 1901, a patient of Mullingar Asylum died suddenly from eating the leaves. Some years ago a correspondence in the Times brought to light instances of the lethal effects of yew leaves on cattle. One correspondent, Mr. James Simmons of Haslemere, mentioned an observation made by himself and others, that yew leaves are more poisonous some time after they have been cut than when fresh. “Yew cropped green from the tree has no fatal effect,” and animals do not eat it fresh, they prefer grass, but if Yew has been cut and allowed to wither cattle will eat it in large quantities and in that state it is deadly poison.” “My people,” said Mr. Simmons, “once buried some Yew cuttings deep in the dung of a farmyard, a number of large hogs dug it up, ate it and all died.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Tax. is for pustular diseases of skin and night-sweats. Gout and chronic rheumatism. Pains in the knees, elbows and back. Slight tremor over whole frame. Trembling. Convulsions. Fainting and collapse. Relaxation of muscles. Cancer, chemotherapy effects. MIND - Impatience, which unfits the patient for mental application. Delirium. Stupor.

Head - Supra-orbital and temporal pain on right side with lachrymation.

Eyes - Pupils widely dilated. Drawing with lachrymation and pressure. Lachrymation of left eye. Itching of external angle of left eye. Burning itching in eyelids. Vision dim.

Ears - Polyps in the ears.

Nose - A round spot of a reddish-brown color, on the end of the nose with desquamation of skin.

Face - Puffy and pale. Looks ill. Face livid, convulsed. Lips are purplish, livid, black brown, especially upper. Frothing at mouth.

Mouth - Sensation of coldness in teeth. Mouth dry. Burning pricking on tongue. Tongue excoriated, moist, tremulous. Saliva hot, acrid. Saliva increased, extremely viscid, acrid. Bitter taste like that Taxus baccata of Cinchona.

Stomach - Feeling of emptiness, must eat frequently. Violent hunger, soon after breakfast with general uneasiness and weakness in region of stomach. Aching, burning and pinching in region of stomach. Pain in pit of stomach and region of navel. After eating, cough. Feeling of pins and needles at pit of stomach. Nausea with accumulation of saliva. Retching. Vomiting ending in death. Vomit, tenacious, containing bile.

Abdomen - Tension in abdomen, as if the stomach were overloaded. Squeezing and tension across abdomen. Aching in umbilical region. Borborygmi.

Rectum - Hard, difficult, dry evacuations. Occasionally a stool which is soft or of a natural consistence. Diarrhea with insupportable tenesmus and burning at every evacuation.

Male - Flow of semen without erection or sexual pleasure for several successive nights. Great excitement during sex. After sex, weakness and great oppression.

Female - Uterine cancer and tumors. Food - Violent hunger. Frequent want to eat with activity of digestive functions.

Chest - Oppression, when stomach is either too full or too empty or else with pain below xiphoid cartilage. Sharp pain in left side. Chest full and hot. Lungs engorged.

Heart - Irregular action of heart. Pulse rapid, slow, feeble, small, wiry, almost imperceptible.

Back - Drawing pain in muscles of neck (left). Constant pain in back. Sacral pains, which allow no rest either in a standing or sitting posture and which compel the patient to remain in bed. Incisive pain in sacrum. Pain in shoulder blade, which subsequently removes to loins.

Limbs - Numbness of limbs and paralysis after several sweats. Sharp, transient, wandering pains. Contusive and incisive pain, which hinders walking. Abscess at right knee. Violent pinching in left calf. Tingling crawling sensation in whole left foot. Lancinations in hand. Burning dryness of palms of hands. Dull pain in joints of fingers. Rheumatic pain in fingers. Lungs - Violent and fatiguing cough. Short cough after every meal, excited by full inspirations with oppression.

Sleep - Sleeplessness during whole night, yawning without inclination to sleep.

Skin - Large, flat, itching pustules. Badly smelling and offensive night-sweats. Peculiarly offensive sweat with eruption of vesicles. Podagra. Erysipelas. All hairy parts become denuded. Black jaundice. Skin red. Body covered with pustules. Miliary eruption. Eruption of large pimples. Dry tetter causing much itching.

Modalities - Worse by pressure, by application of liquids. Worse before and after each meal. Worse after sex. Coughing causes headache. Deep breathing causes cough. Rubbing improves the itching of eyelids.

Kidneys - Cutting pain at base of kidneys which allows him neither to sit still nor stand up and even prevents turning in bed. Urinary tenesmus. Frequent want to urinate with difficult emission in a fine stream. Strangury, urine red.

Temperature - Perspiration from least exertion with great prostration of strength. Profuse night-sweats. Commencing with shivering followed by dry heat of hands and feet. Offensive viscid sweats with itching and redness. COMMENTS - The symptoms of the Tax. pathogenesis are made up of poisonings by leaves and berries and also of provings by Gastier. Fainting is a very prominent feature with Tax. And, in the fatal cases there are convulsions, collapse and syncope. Death from yew poisoning, said Cooper, is remarkably painless. “Empty feeling” in the stomach was prominent and it was noted that the digestion was very rapid. “Must eat frequently.” Gastric catarrh is set up with vomiting of tenacious mucus. Increased saliva, viscid. Pustular skin affection. Large, flat, strongly itching pustules. Viscid sweat. Shooting pains in the toes. Gout. Irritation in the kidneys and bladder. Disturbed heart. Tax. has been recommended as a substitute for Dig., being considered superior to the latter in having no cumulative effect. On the suggestion of Cooper, Clarke once gave a single dose of Tax. tincture in a case of ear polyps (bright red) with catarrh in a youth with the result that the polyps shriveled up to one-third of its former size. RELATIONS -Antidotedby: Staph - prostration with oppression after an embrace. Compare: (1) Ars., Bell., Nux-v., Colch., Dulc., Kali phos., Lyc. (2) The Coniferae. (3) Load at stomach, Abies-n. (4) Rapid digestion, Sulph. (5) Podagra, Urt-u. RÉFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

PHARMACY - tela. Tela araneae. Cobweb. Araneae tela. Spider’s web. Aranearum tela. N. O. Arachnida. The cobweb of the black spider found in barns, cellars, dark places. Tincture or trituration. Historical dose: Tinc- ture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Aphthae. Asthma. Chills. Chorea. Coryza. Coughs. Delirium. Eczema. Fatigue. Headaches. Hectic fevers. Hiccoughs. Hydrothorax. Insomnia. Intermittent fever. Leucorrhea. Nervous, weakness. Numbness. Sleeplessness. Tuberculosis. Urticaria.

HOMEOPATHIC - The spider’s web has been used as a remedy since ancient times. Tela, has been experimented with on healthy persons; t very rapidly lowers the frequency of the pulse rate. In some it produced “a calm and delightful state of feeling, followed by a disposition to sleep. The most delicious tranquility, resembling the action of opium and followed by no bad effects.” Twenty grains given to an old and infirm asthmatic produced “slight but pleasant delirium.” Muscular energy is increased, could not be kept in bed, but danced and jumped about the room all night. In cases of febrile depression, deficient animation or indifference to surrounding objects, the exhibition of eight or ten grains of cobwebs was often followed by exhilaration, the eyes sparkled. The countenance assumed a temporary life and, though the course of the disease might not be changed or the danger averted, more respite was obtained than is gotten from wine, opium or anything else within my knowledge. “In spasmodic disorders of various kinds in asthma in periodic headaches in general restlessness and muscular irritability, its good effects are often signal. The cobweb gives sleep, but not by narcotic power, tranquility and sleep here appear to be the simple consequence of release from pain and irritation.” Tela, acts on arterial system. The pulse is full, strong, and compressible. Lowers pulse rate frequency. Cardiac sleeplessness increased muscular energy. Excitement and nervous agitation in febrile states. Dry asthma, harassing coughs, periodic headaches with extreme nervous weakness. Obstinate intermittents. Masked periodical diseases, hectic, broken down patients. Symptoms come on suddenly with cool, clammy skin. Numbness of hands and legs when at rest. Continued chilliness. MIND- Absent-mindedness. Mental dullness, brain as if enveloped in a fog. Makes mistakes in spelling, time. Disoriented feeling. Spaced-out feeling. Thoughts, disconnected. Prostration of mind. Tranquility and a sense of well-being. Sadness, despondency, depression with heaviness of body. Pities herself. Sighing. Offended easily by jokes. Censorious, critical. Cursing. Irritability. Aversion to being touched. Kleptomania. Anxiety with chest constriction. Anxiety about health. Fear of disease. Fear of being bitten. Bites himself.

Head - Headaches with flushes of heat. Boring and pressing pains. Tingling pains in scalp.

Eyes - Dryness of eyes. Heaviness sensation. Aching pain, better cold application. Eye inflammation, better from cold. Discharges are green. Pains, burning and sore. Injected, inner canthus. Lachrymation, in the wind.

Ears - Boring pains. Heaviness sensation in ears. Heat sensation. Noises while eating. Sounds seem far away.

Nose - Coryza, as if about to get a cold or flu, with anxiety. Coryza with fever. Nosebleed during exercise. Twitching of nose.

Face - Fullness, heat sensations. Numbness, heaviness of jaw. Heat flushes. Aphthae on lips. Twitching of lips. Facial paralysis.

Mouth - Metallic taste. Aphthae on the tongue. Biting sensation on tongue. Itching inside cheek. Mucus on teeth.

Throat - Constriction of throat. Dryness, sore pain, on waking. Congested. Sensation of a lump. Unsteady speech and voice. Vertigo - Vertigo after exertion, exercising. Vision - Focusing difficult. Vision is blurred, worse after eating chocolate. COMMENTS - Dr. Chapman wrote of Tela., “I have cured some obstinate intermittents, suspended the paroxysm of hectic fevers. Overcome morbid vigilance from excessive nervous mobility and quieted irritation of the system from other causes and particularly as connected with protracted coughs and other chronic pectoral disorders.” Dr. Gillespie of Edinburgh reported, “I cured an obstinate intermittent with cobweb after other means had failed.” Dr. Jackson wrote, “I think I may venture to say that it prevents the recurrence of febrile paroxysms more abruptly and more effectively, than quinine bark or arsenic or any other remedy employed for that purpose with which I am acquainted: that like all other remedies of the kind, it is only effectual as applied under a certain conditions of habit, but that the condition of susceptibility for cobweb is at the same time of more latitude than for any other of the known remedies.” “If the cobweb,” said Dr. Jackson, “was given in the time of perfect intermission, the return of paroxysm was prevented, if given under the first symptoms of a commencing paroxysm, the symptoms were suppressed and the course of the paroxysm was so much interrupted that the di sease, for the most part, lost its characteristic symptoms. “If it was not given until the paroxysm was advanced in progress the symptoms of irritation, viz., tremors, startings spasms and delirium, if such existed as forms of febrile action, were usually reduced in violence, sometimes entirely removed. In this case sleep, calm and refreshing, usually followed the sudden and perfect removal of pain and irritation. “Vomiting, spasms and twisting in the bowels, appearing as modes of febrile irritation, were also usually allayed by it, there was no effect from it where the vomiting or pain was connected with real inflammation.” Jackson noted particular changes induced on the existing state of the system, and characterized it as powerfully stimulant base on its affects. Where the pulses of the arteries were quick, irregular and irritated, they became calm, regular and slow after the cobweb had passed into the stomach. The effect was accompanied, for the most part, with perspiration and perfect relaxation of the surface. When the pulses were slow, regular and nearly natural, they usually became frequent small, irregular, sometimes intermitting. Languor and depression characterize the disease, sensation of warmth and comfort are diffused about the stomach and increased animation is conspicuous in the appearance of the eye and countenance. Dr. Jackson likewise effected perfect cures with it in some troublesome spasmodic disorders and gave it with the most marked benefit in dry, irritating coughs, usually termed nervous. In the advanced stage of tuberculosis it procured a respite beyond his expectation. He also found it useful in restraining a troublesome hiccough. Remembering the fame of Mygale avicularia in chorea, this other spider to be of use “in some troublesome spasmodic affections.” Dr. Thatcher cited the following case from apaperofDr. Jackson’s: “W. Sands has been afflicted for many years a distressing asthma, which has proved fatal to his father and two sisters. The complaint being hereditary and aggravated by malformation of the thorax, no remedy gave any permanent relief, nor did change of climate procure any alleviation of symptoms. “For a considerable time back he has never been able to lie down in bed on account of a sense of suffocation, but is obliged to be supported half sitting by pillows and is seldom able to sleep. “He swallowed nearly a scruple of the spider’s web, he swallowed it at bed time and to his utter astonishment enjoyed sound and uninterrupted sleep all night, a blessing to which he had been an entire stranger above six years. “Since he began with the cobweb thinks his health is improved, the cough has entirely abated, but whenever the remedy is omitted the complaint returns.” Dr. Oliver found that by the use of this remedy a patient laboring under organic disease of the heart and hydrothorax obtained great relief and refreshing sleep, who had not before slept for three nights. Another, under similar affection, experienced uncommon relief from the same prescription. To one suffering much pain from cancer, it afforded ease and comfortable sleep. A patient in tuberculosis pulmonalis being affected with distressing agitation of mind and nervous irritation, it answered like a charm and soon induced great sleep like a moderate dose of opium. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Appetite increased. Indigestion. Hiccoughs. Vomiting, with spasms and twisting.

Abdomen - Distension. Sensation of full ness, heaviness. Abdomen sensitive to clothing. Stabbing pain in left hypochondria. Spasms and twisting in the bowels

Male - Stitching pains in penis.

Female - Leucorrhea, offensive smell. Sexual desire decreased or increased. Food - Appetite increased. Desires beets, chocolate, ginger, ice, warm soup. Fruit aggravates.

Chest - Anxiety with chest constriction. Heaviness feeling. Stabbing pain. Stinging pain in sternum. Wave sensation, behind sternum. Pain in axilla. Perspiration in right axilla. Hydrothorax.

Heart - Anxiety with constriction. Cardiac sleeplessness. Piercing pain, heart, region. Pulsation in heart region. Pulse is full, strong, and compressible. Lowers pulse rate frequency.

Back - Heat flushes. Heaviness sensation. Pain in dorsal region, left scapulae. Stabbing, sensation of a knife in the back. Pulling sensation. Burning pain in cervical region. Stiffness in cervical region. Stiffness of spine. Desire to stretch, neck region. Sensation as if stretched backwards.

Limbs - Awkwardness. Chilliness. Heaviness sensation in limbs, hip. Numbness. Aching pains. Stitching pain in knee, patella. Eczema in the hollow of the knee. Urticaria on the leg, calf. Heat with alternating cold in feet. Weakness of legs during stool. Sharp pain in shoulders. Trembling of hand, right. Lungs - Difficult breathing with palpitations, stabbing pains. Dry, irritating coughs.

Modalities - Aversion to air, drafts. Cold, better applications. Better when it rains.

Perspiration - Clammy, offensive sweat. Perspiration of hands, feet. Perspiration with fever.

full:
PHARMACY - tell. Tellurium metallicum. Tellurium metal. An element (Te, At. Wt. 125). Trituration of the precipitated element. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Axilla, sweat. Backache. Barber’s itch. Boils. Cataract. Cholecystitis. Conjunctivitis. Coryza. Coughs. Eczema. Entropion. Eruptions. Eye, inflammation. Deafness. Emphysema. Foot, sweat. Gastritis. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Heartburn. Hepatitis. Herniated, disks. Herpes. Hoarseness. Injuries. Insomnia. Levitation. Mastoiditis. Migraines. Numbness. Offensive, sweat. Otitis. Pityriasis, versicolor. Post-nasal, catarrh. Psoriasis. Ringworm. Scarlet fever. Sacro-iliac, pain. Sciatica. Spinal, irritation. Threadworms. Vertigo. Worms. Yawning.

HOMEOPATHIC - Tellurium occurs in the native state and in combination with gold, silver, lead and antimony. It resembles sulphur and selenium in its chemical reactions. Tellurium is an element situated between antimony and iodine; it was discovered in a gold mineral by the Austrian Muller in 1782. The proving was conducted by Hering in about 1850 on fourteen provers, using the low potencies. A new proving was established by Raeside in London. He conducted a proving on seventeen provers, eleven women and six men. The provers took the remedy night and morning for fourteen days. The potencies 6x and 6c produced the maximum symptoms. The most notable feature of the provings was the irritation of the skin, including the skin of the eyelids and ears, of the spinal column and of some nerves. Dryness of the skin and mucus membranes. Herpes circi- natus, ringworm, especially of the face and body. Vesicular, burning, itching eruptions. Itching, urticarial or macular eruption. Offensive discharges. Chronic fetid suppuration from the ear. Persistent fetid body odor. Heavy perspiration from the feet, extremely foul-smelling. Restlessness and pains all over body. Very sensitive back. Pain in the cervical, right lumbar and sciatic regions. Sacral and sciatic pains. Slight amnesia with frontal headache. Lassitude. Afraid, cannot bear to be touched on sensitive areas. Slow development of symptoms (Rad-br.). MIND - Rough and angular disposition. Excitable, disposed to fly into a passion. Afraid of any movement and of anyone approaching them. Fear of being touched in sensitive places. Lassitude. Quiet disposition. Absentminded. Neglectful and forgetful, when engaged in doing one thing, forgets and neglects others. Incapable of mental activity. Amnesia, inability to fix the memory on immediate events. Depressed. Depressive psychosis. Serene and cheerful, then impatient and irritable.

Head - Feeling of heat in the head. Heaviness and fullness of head in morning. Pain in left side of head and in forehead above left eye. Periodic headaches. Migraines. Sudden rush of blood to head. Congestion to head and nape of neck, followed by weakness and faintness in stomach. Brain feels as if beaten on slightest movement. Violent linear pain in small spot over left eye. Itching of scalp, red spots. Numbness of nape and occiput.

Eyes - Pustular conjunctivitis, with eczema on lids and much purulent discharge from eyes. Deposit of chalky- looking white mass on anterior surface of lens. Cataract, following ocular lesions. Aids the absorption of infiltrations in iris and choroid. Herpes conjunctivae, phlyctenules near edge of cornea, worse from crying. The eyelids are thickened and inflamed, with pustules, pale red, edematous and oozing. Feeling as if lashes of lower lid were turned in.

Ears - Catarrh of middle ear. Chronic suppurating otitis. Otitis after scarlet fever. Fetid, irritating discharge, smells of brine from the ear, especially the left ear. Chronic mastoiditis. Itching, swelling, throbbing in meatus. Dull, throbbing pain in ears, day and night, thin, watery, excoriating discharge. Ache in the left ear. Vesicular eruption on the eardrum, suppurating and perforating. Eczema behind ears with formation of thick crusts. Deafness. Buzzing, ringing in the ears.

Nose - Hawks dried yellowish-red phlegm from posterior sinuses, salty tasting, in mornings. Coryza, lachrymation and hoarseness, better in open air (All-c.). Nose obstructed, must breathe through mouth. Head cold with running of a blood- streaked liquid accompanied by tears and hoarseness, ameliorated in the open air. Nostrils itch. Boils.

Face - Heat in face. Sudden flushes of redness over face. Distortion and twitching in left facial muscles, left corner of mouth drawn up when talking. Ringworm on face. Barber’s itch. Pimples on face. Burning in lips.

Mouth - Dryness of the lips and mouth with raw, irritated areas. Ulcerations on the gums tongue, mouth, palate. Gums bleed easily and profusely. Tongue somewhat swollen, furred white, shows print of teeth. Breath has odor of garlic. Copious saliva. Tenacious mucus runs from mouth. Taste earthy, metallic. Coldness of mouth and pharynx on drawing in air.

Throat - Hoarseness in morning with fluent coryza, a rough, pressing, tickling sensation in larynx. In morning, hawks pieces of salty, yellowish-reddish phlegm. Painful dryness of fauces. Rough, scratching sensation in throat, worse towards evening. Throat feels sore with a prickly, rough sensation evening and morning. Throat sore on swallowing, better after eating or drinking. Pain in throat extends into ear. Vertigo - Vertigo, when going to sleep, morning after rising. Vertigo worse walking, sitting up or turning head. Vertigo better lying perfectly quiet and still. COMMENTS - Ringworm, herpes. Offensive, garlic-like odor of the body and sweat. Fishy odors and discharges (Hep., Sanie). Offensive foot sweats (Sil.). Vesicating effect on the skin, hair-roots, breasts, perineum and anus. Acrid discharge, blisters any part of the skin it touches. Otorrhea. Discharge of the ear smells of fish brine. Nash cured several cases of postscarlatina otorrhea using Tell. 6c, higher potencies had failed. Eyelids are inflamed. Phlyctenular conjunctivitis. Itching in the rectum after stool. Threadworms. Great sensitiveness to touch. Neuralgic hypersensitive state of the spine. Painful spots along the spinal cord (Agar.). Injuries to the spine and pelvic bones. Radiating pain down both thighs from an injury to the sacroiliac area. Pains are sharp and radiating, or electric-like. Contractures. Pressing pain in the scapula. Neuralgic symptoms, especially on the right side. Sciatica. Sciatic pain deep in the leg, behind the knee. Herniated disks (Aesc, Agar.). Sacro-iliac problems with radiating pains (Aesc, Hyper.). Worse lying on the affected part, from touch, worse in C7 to T5 and in the Sacro-iliac joint. Many of the pains and symptoms come and go suddenly. The ears are suddenly stopped. Sudden rushes of blood to the head. Drowsiness. Yawning after retching, drowsy after eating. Clarke once gave Tell, to a child for an eruption and cured it incidentally of constant yawning with which it had been troubled. The eruption improved at the same time. Clarke also cured with Tell, an Indian officer home on furlough whose body was covered over with a ringworm- like eruption. Kent had a case in which a boy, 4, slid down banisters and struck his head on a tiled floor. He became unconscious and a surgeon was summoned, who found him unconscious with a clear, watery discharge from the ear, which the surgeon pronounced to be cerebrospinal fluid. This condition lasted three days and the case had been pronounced hopeless when Kent first saw the boy. Kent noticed that the discharge was acrid and reddened whatever part it came in contact with. One dose of Tell, was given. In two hours the child vomited, a sign of reaction, and in two weeks was well. Shelton related three cases using Tell. The first concerned a widow, 50, who had pain and soreness in the upper part of her back for a long time. She shrank from the slightest touch on the part. The sensitiveness was so acute that, when touched, the pain extended into the occiput and all over the upper region of the back. Tell. 6c cured in eighteen days. The second case concerned Miss X., 45, who had a fall, striking a severe blow on the sacrum. She suffered for some weeks from concussion with one point of great soreness in the sacral region, just above the spot where the blow was received. She was kept in bed for some weeks and improved generally, but the painful spot remained and sensitiveness appeared over the back, especially its upper third. Tell. 6c cured all completely. The third case concerned Miss Y., 29, who had severe spinal meningitis ten years before, and consulted Shelton for a burning, pressing pain at base of brain. He diagnosed the condition as meningitis. The patient grew worse and gradually ptosis, and then right and then left hemiplegia set in. Finally hyperesthesia of the back became so distressing that it was a question of finding any support that did not intensify the pain. She could not bear the slightest touch, complaining that it not only hurt her at the point of contact, but that she felt it in the head and in remote parts of the body. Tell, cleared up the case. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Nux-v. (epigastric oppression). Compare: (1) Rad-br., Berb., Hyper., Sei. (2) Tet. - coccygodynia, ulceration of nails, pains in hands in small spots, ankles, heels and Achilles tendon, (3) Sep., Ars., Rhus-t. (4) Restlessness, garlicky odor, Ars. (5) Coryza, All-c. (6) Otitis, Puls., Bell., Ter. (7) Ringworm, Bac., Sep., Nairn. (8) Ringworm in clusters Sep., Calc. (9) Threadworms. Teucr. (10) Pains come and go suddenly, Bell., Lyc. ( 11) Worse laughing, Phos. (12) Worse straining at stool ind. (13) Cough and skin, Osm. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - Empty and weak feeling. Sensation of weakness, like faintness in the stomach after local congestion of blood to head and nape, also with chest symptoms. Heartburn with warmth in stomach as from alcohol. Belching with taste of food eaten. Fullness in pit of stomach, must lie down after dinner. Constrictive feeling in stomach as if strapped together.

Abdomen - Fullness and oppression in hypogastrium, clothing must be loosened. Pressing first left, then right side, as from wind. When lying on left side, throbbing under right ribs, and vice versa. Pinching in abdomen. Frequent spasmodic pains in bowels as from incarcerated wind, mostly from 5 to 9 p.m.

Rectum - Very offensive flatus. Spasmodic pains with urging to stool. Stools soft at first, then hard. Copious stool with feeling of flatulence in bowels. Costive. Itching anus, rectum and perineum after stool. Tetter on perineum, itching. Passes many threadworms with stool. Sensations - As if in air on going to sleep. Brain as if beaten. As if lashes were turned in. As if air whistled through left Eustachian tube. As if strapped together in epigastric region. As if fluid wanted to discharge in lobe of right lung.

Male - Herpes on scrotum and perineum. Secondary gonorrhea. A drop of viscid fluid in meatus. Increased sexual desire, followed by long-lasting indifference. Erections all night.

Female - Shooting deep in pelvis across to left. Premenstrual colic in lower abdomen. Menses painful and late. Menses too early in menopausal years. Long intervals between menses. Food - Craving for apples, fatty bacon, salt, bread during the evening, cold drinks, beer. Hungry at night. After meals, great drowsiness. Vomits after eating rice.

Chest - Pain in the sternum, aggravated by deep breaths and by bending. Pressure in middle of chest under sternum, better in open air. Shooting in left chest, fifth rib. Feeling as if some fluid is pressing downward in, from right lung.

Heart - Dull pain in region of heart when lying on left side, better lying on back. Heart irregular when lying on the back or right side. Palpitations with throbbing through whole body and full pulse, folio wed by sweat. Palpitation with sensation of thoracic constriction and pain. Rapid pulse rate.

Back - Weak feeling in back. Vertebral pain from last cervical to fifth dorsal vertebra, very sensitive to pressure and touch (Chin-s., Phos.). Herniated disks (Aesc, Agar.). Sensitive spinal column with coughing, straining. Pressing ache in scapula. Numbness in nape and occiput. Pain in sacrum. Neck pain, spreading to the shoulder and between the scapulae. Lumbar pain spreading to the right thigh, ameliorated by walking. Afraid of any movement and of anyone approaching. Breasts - Cutting around and in left nipple, through to scapula. Eruption about nipple. Causations - Falls, injuries. Eating rice causes vomiting. Eating and drinking improves sore throat.

Limbs - Aching all over, mostly in limbs, worse right side and in walking. Sciatica, right side, worse lying on affected side. Sciatica with sensitiveness of vertebral column. Weakness of the legs in the morning. Bruised pain in hip joints after walking. Contraction of tendons in bends of knees. Sharp, quick pains in elbows, ankles and other parts. Fetid sweat on feet, mostly on toes. Fingertips feel dead on stretching hand. Rheumatism of right little finger, worse moving it.

Sleep - Drowsy after a meal. Yawning and belching. Insomnia with unpleasant dreams. Sleepless, restless turning from weariness and bruised feeling. At night, pains all over. On going to sleep, feels as if in air, quick drawing towards feet wakens him. Wakes with a start during the night.

Skin - Skin dry, hot. Stinging in skin. Barber’s itch. Herpetic spots, ringworm (Tub.), worse lower limbs, on single parts. Ring-shape lesions. Circular patches of eczema. Small red pimples, very bright red and very sharply defined with minute vesicles upon them. Psoriasis. Scrofulous eczematous eruption. Eczema, back of ears and occiput. Itching of hands and feet. Itching worse in cool air. Offensive odors from affected parts. Fetid exhalations (Sulph.).

Modalities - Better lying on back. Worse while at rest, at night, lying on painful side. Worse in morning, on waking. Worse cold weather. Worse coughing, laughter. Worse from touch, friction. Spine sensitive to touch. Eating causes drowsiness.

Liver - Hepatitis and gastritis. Chronic cholecystitis. Lungs - Coughing on laughing, worse aching in small of back. Wakened by cough. Cough towards morning, looser after a few days. Wheezing, scraping cough with mucus. Emphysema.

Kidneys - Painful soreness in kidneys, extending downward like a weight, worse morning, making her irritable. Increased, high-colored, acid urine.

Perspiration - Offensivefoot-sweat. Heavy perspiration from the feet, extremely foul-smelling. Offensive sweat of armpits, smelling of garlic. Sweat on face, on spots.

Temperature - Inner shivering and fever, fetid, repulsive sweating, forcing him to be alone. Chilly with pains. Sweat on face, on spots, with increased itching of these places, often throbbing through whole body, generally warm, while sitting in a cool breeze. Skin hot and dry, sensation as if overstrained, as if bruised, as if he had taken cold after severe exertion.

name: Teplitz Aqua
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better by friction. Better drinking cold water. The symptoms are worse at night, especially bone pains. Worse from motion. COMMENTS - On moving head it seems as if something fell from one side to the other. Cold feelings in upper arm in foot. Increased sensitiveness to cold. Paralysis of tongue of limbs. Vesicles in mouth and on tongue. Vesicular erysipelas. Burning sensation in many parts. Burning in stomach, better drinking cold water. Hemorrhage, nosebleed, hemorrhoids with stool, metrorrhagia. Better from hemorrhoid bleeding. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Nat-c., Nat-m., Kali-s., Mang., Lith., Sil., Alum. REFERENCES - Clarke..
constitution: Amenorrhea. Bones disorders. Breast, tumors. Eruptions. Erysipelas. Flatulence. Gout. Hemorrhoids. Irritability. Leucorrhea. Metrorrhagia. Nosebleed. Paralysis. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Scurvy. Speech, difficult. Spine, pains. Tongue, paralysis. Toothache. Ulcers. Vertigo.

PHARMACY - tep. Teplitz aqua. Teplitz Mineral Springs of Teplitz in Bohemia. Teplitz aqua, contains: Natrumcarbonicum, Natrum muriaticum, Natrum fluorica, Natrum sili- cata, Kali sulphuricum. Kali muriaticum, Calcarea carbónica, Silica, etc. Dilutions. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Bones disorders. Breast, tumors. Eruptions. Erysipelas. Flatulence. Gout. Hemorrhoids. Irritability. Leucorrhea. Metrorrhagia. Nosebleed. Paralysis. Rheumatism. Sciatica. Scurvy. Speech, difficult. Spine, pains. Tongue, paralysis. Toothache. Ulcers. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - The waters of Teplitz are chiefly in repute for the treatment of gouty patients, especially those suffering from atonic gout. The springs are alkaline and hot, and the temperature forms a leading feature in their action. The symptoms of Tep. are from Perutz, who experimented on himself and several healthy individuals, together with symptoms by Hromada. Symptoms of Nat-c. and Nat-m. appear throughout. Tearfulness, low spirits and irritability were noted and giddiness of much intensity. “Giddiness, when she walks all the houses seem to move too.”

Modalities - Better by friction. Better drinking cold water. The symptoms are worse at night, especially bone pains. Worse from motion. COMMENTS - On moving head it seems as if something fell from one side to the other. Cold feelings in upper arm in foot. Increased sensitiveness to cold. Paralysis of tongue of limbs. Vesicles in mouth and on tongue. Vesicular erysipelas. Burning sensation in many parts. Burning in stomach, better drinking cold water. Hemorrhage, nosebleed, hemorrhoids with stool, metrorrhagia. Better from hemorrhoid bleeding. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Nat-c., Nat-m., Kali-s., Mang., Lith., Sil., Alum. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Worse at night, 1 a.m. to 3 a.m. Worse walking in open air. Worse lying, sitting. Worse pressure, touch. Worse by pressure in region of bladder it causes convulsions. Worse lying on left side, better turning to right. Pain in crest of ilium worse from motion and least jar. Damp dwellings aggravates. Damp cellar causes diarrhea. Damp weather causes neuralgia in legs..

Dropsy. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Enteric, fever. Epilepsy. Erysipelas. Erythema. Fibroma. Gallstone, colic. Glands, swelling. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Headaches. Hematuria. Hem- orrhage. Hemorrhoids. Hernia. Herpes. Hypochondria

full:
PHARMACY - ter. Terebinthiniae oleum. Oil of Turpentine. Turpentine. Oleum terebinthine. Pinaceae. The oil distilled from the oleo-resin (turpentine) obtained from various species of Pinus, purified by repeated rectification with water. Solution in rectified spirit. Ozonized oil of Turpentine (prepared by exposure of the common oil to sun and air in a half-filled bottle and shaking from time to time'). Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Amblyopia. Ascites. Asthma. Backache. Bladder, irritable. Brachial neuralgia. Bronchitis. Chilblains. Chordee. Chorea. Ciliary neu ralgia. Coma. Cystitis. Dentition. Dropsy. Dysentery. Dysmenorrhea. Enteric, fever. Epilepsy. Erysipelas. Erythema. Fibroma. Gallstone, colic. Glands, swelling. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Headaches. Hematuria. Hem- orrhage. Hemorrhoids. Hernia. Herpes. Hypochondriasis. Injuries. Insanity. Intestines, ulceration. Iritis. Jaundice. Kidneys, disorders. Lumbago. Nephritis. Neuralgias. Ovaries, dropsy. Ovaries, pains. Peritonitis. Pityriasis. Purpura hemorrhagica. Rabies. Scabies. Scarlatina. Sciatica. Spermatorrhea. Strangury. Stricture. Tetanus. Tympanites. Uremia. Urethritis. Urine, retention. Worms.

HOMEOPATHIC - Ter. was introduced to homeopathy by Hartlaub. The symptoms have been added to from poisonings and overdosings in allopathic practice. According to Dr. Taylor, children are particularly sensitive to its action. Illness caused by sleeping in newly painted rooms is due in great part to the turpentine. Milnes noted that Ter., as an internal remedy, is “A stimulant and tonic to the mucus membranes, especially of the bladder and urethra: it proves useful in leucorrhea and gleet.” Selective affinity for the mucus membranes of kidneys, bladder, respiration, bronchi, heart and blood. Bleeding mucus surfaces, oozing hemorrhage of a passive, black offensive fluid. Purpura hemorrhagica. Marked tympanites and urinary symptoms. Inflammation of kidneys with dark, passive, fetid hemorrhages. Affections of kidneys with rheumatism. Goullon indicated it for Bright’s disease preceded by dropsy. Aching, soreness and stiffness of the muscles. Even minor bumps cause bruises. Unbroken chilblains. Burning in various parts, tip of tongue, epigastrium, small of back, kidney, uterus etc. Exhausted, sensitive and tired. Disturbed sense of equilibrium. Drowsiness and strangury. Coma. MIND - Anxiety on going to bed. Confusion of mind, better when urinating freely. Tired and difficult concentration of thoughts. Intense irritability, children fly into tern- per during dentition. Muttering delirium. Hydrophobia. Despondent during nervous headache. Fear of apoplexy during fullness and pressure in head. Loathing of life. Suicidal disposition, by hanging. Comatose, can be roused only by shaking out of apparent stupor, but falls immediately into it again. Unconsciousness after stool.

Head - Dull pain like from a band around the head (Carb-ac.).

Eyes - Opens eyes when swallowing in coma. Eyes dark red, face red on affected side. Intense pain in eye and side of head. Ciliary neuralgia over right eye. Amblyopia from alcohol.

Ears - Disturbed sense of equilibrium. Own voice sounds unnatural, humming as of a seashell. Loud talking is very painful. Otalgia. Sensation in ears as of striking of a clock.

Nose - Discharge of serum without coryza. Cold in head with sore nostrils, with disposition to bleed. Passive nosebleed in children.

Face - Pale, earthly, sunken. Hot flushes followed by sweat.

Mouth - Foul, cold breath. Dry, red, sore, shining, smooth and glossy tongue, burning in tips with prominent papillae (Arg-n., Bell., Kali-b„ Nux-m.). Choking sensation in throat; Aphthae from mouth to anus. Dentition.

Stomach - Rancid, flatulent, acrid belchings. Burning in epigastric region. Nausea and vomiting with intense burning. Nausea, better loose stool. Aversion to meat.

Abdomen - Bruised soreness. Dropsy, pelvic peritonitis. Enormous distention. Tympanites. Ascites. Flatulence. Enterocolitis, hemorrhage and ulceration of bowels. Bowels were drawn towards spine. Bleeding ulcers in the intestine.

Rectum - Pain before flatus with and relief after stool. Fainting after every stool. Diarrhea with watery, greenish, fetid stool. Diarrhea with tetanic spasms. Bloody stools. Hemorrhage from bowels. Worms, lumbrici. Sensations - As of a band around head. As if sand thrown violently in eye. As of a seashell sounding in left ear. Sound in ear as of a clock striking. As from hasty swallowing in epigastrium. As if he had swallowed a bullet, which had lodged in stomach. As if he would pitch forward on walking.

Female - Intense burning in uterine region. Metritis and puerperal peritonitis. Metrorrhagia with burning in uterus. Uterine diseases after wearing pessaries. Food - Hunger and thirst with debility. Diminished appetite, loss of appetite, great thirst. Desire to eat more after a satisfying meal. Aversion to animal food.

Chest - Burning and tightness across chest. Constitutions - Suited to children, dentition, nosebleed, worms. Complaints of elderly people, people of sedentary habits. Chronic rheumatism and gouty complaints. Bleeders. Nervous women with headaches, amenorrhea and dysmenorrhea. Hydrogenoid.

Heart - Warmth in heart while sitting in evening, obliged to yawn a great deal. Frightful oppression in precordial region. Palpitations. Rapid, small, thready, intermittent pulse.

Back - Backache and soreness in kidney disorders. Burning pain in region of kidneys. Drawing in right kidney, extending to hip. Causations - Ill effects of alcohol, falls, strains, tooth extraction, damp cellars.

Limbs - Brachial or sub-scapular neuralgia. Intense pain along the larger nerves, worse damp weather. Stiff muscles. Hands feel swollen. Cramps in knees. Stands with feet apart, has no power of balancing the body. As if pitched forward while walking. Walks bent like an old man. Lungs - Dyspnea. Difficult breathing, the lungs feel distended, hemoptysis. Bronchitis of children with drowsiness and retention of urine. Bronchial asthma or catarrh with profuse expectoration. Bloody expectoration.

Sleep - Drowsiness with urine retention. Lethargy. Retarded sleep. Agitated sleep at night with tossing and frequent waking. Many dreams, nightmares. Wakes frightened at night, looks ghastly and shrieks.

Skin - General sensibility increased. Acne. Erythema, itching pustular, vesicular eruption, urticaria. Purpura hemorrhagica, advancing. Ecchymosis, dropsies. Scarlatina. Chilblains with excessive itching and pulsative pains. Aching soreness of the muscles.

Modalities - Better from motion, stooping. Better belching and passing flatus. Loose stool better nausea. Burning in anus better cold water. Worse from dampness, cold. Worse at night, 1 a.m. to 3 a.m. Worse walking in open air. Worse lying, sitting. Worse pressure, touch. Worse by pressure in region of bladder it causes convulsions. Worse lying on left side, better turning to right. Pain in crest of ilium worse from motion and least jar. Damp dwellings aggravates. Damp cellar causes diarrhea. Damp weather causes neuralgia in legs.

Kidneys - Nephritis after exanthemata with violent bronchitis. Burning, drawing pain in region of kidney, along ureters. Cystitis. Urethritis with painful excretions (Canth.). Bleeding bladder. Constant tenesmus. Strangury with bloody urine. Scanty, suppressed urine, odor of violets. Urine, smoky with coffee grounds or thick, yellow, slimy, muddy sediment. Pains alternate between navel and bladder, better walking.

Perspiration - Suddenly checked sweat causes neuralgia. Suppressed foot sweat causes rheumatic iritis. Cold sweat on legs. Cold, clammy, all over with prostration. Profuse sweat on legs in evenings in bed.

Temperature - Heat under the skin. Heat with violent thirst, dry tongue, profuse cold, clammy sweat. Cold sweat on legs. Typhoid fever with tympanites, hemorrhages, stupor, delirium. Prostration. Vertigo - Vertigo with vanishing of vision, nausea. Disturbed sense of equilibrium. Vertigo as if intoxicated, as if he would fall forward, when walking. COMMENTS - Brunton noted that Ter., when applied to the skin, acts as an irritant and rubefacient, causing vesicles and a sensation of burning if applied for any length of time. Inhaled, it causes sneezing, tightness across the eyes and dyspnea. Given internally, it causes burning in the mouth and salivation in stomach, sensation of heat or cold, gastro- enteritis with vomiting and diarrhea, and ulceration of the intestines. The pulse is sometimes slowed, sometimes quickened. Respiration is quickened and spasmodic, the chemical is partly excreted by the lungs and acts on the mucus membrane, lessening its secretion. The temperature sometimes rises, or falls. Voluntary movement is dimin- ished, reflex action lowered, blood pressure lowered and vessels dilated. Acute and chronic nephritis. Kidney infections. Protein or blood in the urine. Albuminuria and hematuria after scarlatina and also to the consequent dropsy. Effects of chemical inhalation of exposure, particularly if there is kidney damage. Diminished quantity of urine. Urine has an odor of violets. Lumbar pain, burning in urethra, painful urination. Hematuria with smoky, turbid urine depositing a sediment like coffee-grounds. Dull pain or burning pain in region of kidneys. Burning during urination. Brunton mentioned its usefulness in treating gallstone colic, given in ether in the proportion of one part of the oil of turpentine to three of ether. Homeopaths have confirmed the value of this treatment. Characteristic burning. Burning in gums, tongue, tip of tongue, mouth, throat, stomach, rectum and anus, kidneys, bladder and urethra, uterus, air passages, and chest. Burning in the sternum, particularly after warm drinks, the pain running along the sternum with the drink and spreading in the chest. Burning extends from kidneys along ureters. “Burning in uterus.” Peritonitis, metritis, metrorrhagia with burning. Passive, dark and fetid hemorrhages. Hemorrhages from any orifice. Purpura hemorrhagica with fresh ecchymoses in great numbers from day to day. Smooth, glossy, red tongue, as Terebinthiniae oleum if deprived of papillae. Drowsiness. Drowsiness with capillary bronchitis, in child. Stupor and great weakness, particularly in cases of typhus, typhoid, and uremic poisoning. “Drowsy with retention of urine.” Excessive tympanites, with extreme sensitiveness to touch. Sensitivity of the hypogastrium and pains in symphysis pubis with cystitis. Urogenital and rectal troubles. Pains go from left to right across bowels and then shoot upward. Sense of anxiety and utter prostration about epigastrium. Umbilical region feels as if covered with a round, cold plate. Sprained pains, contusive pains and rheumatic pains appear, notably pressure and drawing pains. Irritation of the meninges and often ascarides or other intestinal worms. Maniacal fury. Cooper found Ter. indicated in children (especially teething children) when they fly into passions. Lippe observed that this irritability manifests itself in some cases of spasms and convulsions. He had a case of a woman who had made her feet sore by walking and applied turpentine to them. This was followed by a state like hydrophobia, she had spasms whenever she saw water, heard it poured, or saw a bright object and also whenever she attempted to urinate. Cooper noted the case of a woman, 35, who, from being exposed to the odor of turpentine, got pain as from pinchings in the throat with lifeless feeling in the tongue and dryness of the mouth, followed by pain in her right eyeball, which extended back to the same side of occiput. S. H. Roberts maintained that Ter. had a specific effect in tonsillitis when applied externally. Marc Jousset gave Ter. lx with marked benefit in two cases of bronchial asthma. He was led to give it in the first case by coincident hematuria, but this was not present in the second. A young man who was badly poisoned by a low potency of Phos. got more relief from Ter. 3x than from any other remedy. Brunton argued that it is only ozonized Ter. that is effective in such cases. Dr. Hering says the ozonized oil is recommended as a prophylactic in malarial and African fevers, a few drops being given daily on a lump of sugar. George Royal gave three cases illustrating the action of Ter. The first concerned a man, 24, with typhoid in the third week. He had extreme distention, with a rapid, small and compressible pulse. Cold sweat in lower limbs. Ter. 6x was given, two drops in water every half-hour. Oil of Ter. was applied locally to the abdomen, mixed with lard. Later in the evening, when there was already slight improvement, an injection containing turpentine was administrated. This relieved the patient of a large quantity of flatus and he began to recover the next morning. The second case concerned pyemia after miscarriage at the third month, brought on by the patient herself. Enormous distention, lower limbs covered with cold sweat, lochia thin, scanty offensive. Ter. given in another case brought about slow improvement for three days, when Chin. 30c was indicated and finished the cure. The third case from Royal concerned a teamster, 36, who had severe nephritis after being out in cold rain. He had a constant desire to urinate, severe pain in back, down ureter to bladder, urine scanty, very high-colored. Temperature 102. Pulse weak, 130. Ter. 6x was given every half-hour and hot fomentations on kidneys greatly relieved. After three days he was able to leave his bed. Royal considered cold sweat of lower limbs and rapid pulse with the distention, as leading indications. A keynote of Burnett’s forTer. is “Pains in the bowels which causes frequent urination.” RELATIONS-Antidotedby: Phos. Antidote to: Phos., Merc. Compare: ( 1 ) Alumn., Sec., Canth., Nit-ac. (2) Terebe. lx - chronic bronchitis and winter coughs, sub-acute stages of inflammation of respiratory tract. Loosens secretion, relieves tightened feel- ing, makes expectoration easy. Neurotic coughs. Huskiness of public speakers and singers. (3) Cystitis when urine is alkaline and offensive. (4) Onon. - Diuretic. Chronic nephritis, diuretic effects like Juniper, calculus, nosebleed, worse washing face. Followed well by: Merc-c. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

PHARMACY - term-a. Terminaba arjuna. N. O. Combretaceae. Bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Boils. Contusions. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Ecchymosis. Fractures. Gonorrhea. Heart, diseases. Hemorrhages. Palpitations. Spermatorrhea. Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Wounds.

HERBAL - Terminaba arjuna is a large, deciduous tree measuring a height of 60 to 80 feet. Sanskrit writers found the bark to be a cardiac tonic. Bagbhata was the first to prescribe the bark in heart diseases. The ayurvedic physicians of India have been using this herb independently or as one of the ingredients in all sorts of heart diseases with marked success for a long time. They use it in both functional and organic diseases of the heart. Angina pectoris, palpitations of the heart, pain in the heart, weakness of the heart. Fractures. Pains all over the body owing to a fall. Ecchymosis. Hemorrhages. Spermatorrhea and gonorrhea. Charaka used it in hematemesis. He prescribed equal quantities of the bark, pulverized red sandalwood, sugar and rice water. Its leaves are also used for boils. Sushruta used a decoction of the bark with equal quantity of white sandalwood in spermatorrhea. Harita found it useful in gonorrhea. Bangasena has recommended it in chronic diarrhea and dysentery. Bagbhata recommended its decoction for suppression and retention of urine. He also recommended an ointment prepared of the bark and honey in acne. Chakradatta found it useful in bloody Terminalia arjuna dysentery and in cardiac affections. He also recommended it in fractures. Bhavaprakasha recommended it for tuberculosis of the lungs and for suppression and retention of urine. COMMENTS - R. N. Khory in his Materia Medica of India, vol. II, wrote, “Astringent ad tonic given in heart disease. Locally used as a wash for wounds, ulcers, contusions and specially used in promoting union of fractures and dispersion of ecchymosis. Internally, largely used by the natives in hemorrhagic and other fluxes and as a lithontriptic.” REFERENCES – Ghose

HERBAL - R. N. Khory. Materia Medica of India, vol. II, p. 260, said, “Purgative, astringent and alternative. The ripe fruits are generally purgative and the unripe ones astringent and aperient.” Lt. Col. R. N. Chopra, I. M.S., wrote in his book Indigenous Drugs of India, p. 532, “It is astringent, laxative, alternative; used in scorpion sting.” Charaka found it useful in bleeding piles, diseases of the stomach, chronic dysentery, jaundice due to cough, cold and catarrhs, and vomiting. Sushruta recommended it in rheumatism, blind piles, elephantiasis, chronic enlargement of the spleen and glandular enlargement of the abdomen and hiccough. Bagbhata prized it is an excellent remedy for piles, stone and calculus and throat affections ad as a tonic. Harita recommended it in hemorrhages of the stomach and lungs.and delirium tremens. Chakradatta found it useful in rheumatism, dropsy and in several affections of the eye. Bhavaprakasha recommended it in typhoid fever, chronic diarrhea and dysentery and biliary colic. Bangasena said that it is an excellent remedy in diarrhea associated with colicky pains and also in whitlow.

HOMEOPATHIC - Term-c. is an indigenous remedy, very much used in ayurvedic medicine. The symptoms for homeopathic use are ineffectual desire, hard stools, distended abdomen, and bleeding hemorrhoids. Therapeutic action to clear the bowels. Constipation, chronic dysentery, dropsy, chronic diarrhea. Frequent in effectual desire to pass stools, but the patient passes only small quantity of feces with great force. Sweat breaks out during stool. For piles, some skin diseases. Vertigo, relieved by cold bathing. Profuse salivation with great thirst which accompanies all affections. Offensive odor comes out of the mouth. Tongue is flabby, dry, and covered with a brown coating on tip of the tongue. MIND - Mind indifferent. Single mindedness. Easily indisposed to yawn, constant yawning.

Head - Headache in occiput and right cranium with intense vertigo. Stitching pain in right temporal region and occipital suture.

Mouth - Fetid odor in mouth. Profuse salivation with intense thirst. Sensation of dryness in upper jaw. Gums of teeth swollen and hard.

Stomach - Sensation of fullness in stomach. Distension of stomach. Downward pain in stomach and epigastrium. Rumbling and gurgling sounds in stomach. Fetid eructation. In the morning constant acid, empty eructation.

Abdomen - Rumbling and gurgling sounds in abdomen. Flatulence. Pain in right lower abdomen.

Rectum - Sweats while passing stool. Pressive itching and full sensation in rectum. Constipation, stool hard, of small quantity, and slightly yellowish. Diarrhea, stools is liquid, and small in quantity. Feces mixed with some mucus, flatulence associated with burning sensation in the stomach.

Stool - Frequent ineffectual desire for passing stool, but passes very small quantity of feces with great force or sometimes with ineffectual action to pass stool. After much trying a little quantity of feces comes out with great force.

Urine - Quantity of urine is slightly diminished. Frequency of urination is increased at night. Vertigo - Vertigo remains all the day and night for hours. Vertigo is worse by hot sun’s rays, hard pressure and motion. Vertigo is better by cold bathing, evening dry cold air and during sleep and eating. Intense vertigo begins in occiput and spreads to the whole right side of the head (right temporal region to right frontal region). RELATIONS - Compare: Chin., Nux-v., Lyc. REFERENCES - Ghose.

Chest - Intense pressive pain in right chest. Food - Thirst for drinking cold water.

Heart - Pressive pain in region of heart. Pulse is accelerated and quick in motion, irregular. Pulse for some moments is rapid, hard and for some moments is weak simultaneously. Some heartbeats are feeble or of low sound, some normal and some of loud sound, everything in successive order.

Back - Intense pain in back (right lumbar region and lower spinal column). Sitting is painful due to pain, often at intervals. Pain increased while sitting straight, and decreased altogether while lying on bed and during sleep. Pain in back of neck.

Limbs - Muscular pain in right upper hand. Pain in the region of deltoid muscle. Itching pains relieved by scratching.

Modalities - Every complaint is better by cold bathing. Better dry, cold air. Better while eating. Better closing the eyes, sleeping, evening. Better during complete rest of mind and body.

Tongue - Flabby, dry, tongue. Brown coating on tip of tongue. Sore and raw tongue.

Liver - Slight pain in the region of liver (large lobe). Pain better temporarily by external pressure. Lungs - Hot deep breathing.

full:
PHARMACY - test. Testosterone. Male hormone. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne. Baldness. Bleeding. Cancer. Emaciation. Fatigue. Hepatitis. Im- potency. Jaundice. Menstrual, disorders.

HOMEOPATHIC - Low levels of Testosterone can cause symptoms of fatigue, malaise, loss of sex drive, and loss of muscle tissue. Anabolic steroids are compounds related to testosterone. The most common side effects of using Testosterone in both men and women include increased facial and body hair, oily skin or acne, male pattern baldness, water retention joint stiffness, and soreness at the injection site. Lab tests may show increased levels of liver enzymes. A deepened or hoarsened voice, growth of the clitoris, and menstrual irregularities have been reported in women. The masculinizing side effects may be irreversible in women, even with short term use. At higher doses over longer periods, increased or decreased sex drive, mood swings, aggressive behavior, persistent painful erections, shrinking testicles, and breast growth have been reported in men. Long term use of high dose anabolics can damage the liver, causing jaundice, hepatitis, bleeding, or, possibly, cancer. RELATIONS - Compare: Orch., Sep. REFERENCES - Murphy.

Ringing in the ears. Muscle weakness. Extreme allergic reactions. Rash. Skin peeling. Skin eruptions. Inflammation of the tongue, of the upper digestive tract. Hives, inflammation of large bowel. Genital or anal sores or rash. Inflammation of the penis. Sore throat and inflammation. Sore mouth and perineal itching due to overgrowth of yeasts. Difficult or painful swallowing. Indigestion. Irritation of the gastrointestinal mucosa. Autonomic dystonia. Diarrhea or loose stools. Cramps or burning of the stomach. Abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting. Loss of appetite. Bone deformation. Discoloration of teeth. Swelling due to fluid accumulation. Liver poisoning. Photosensitivity. Prone to sunburns. Exaggerated sunburn. RELATIONS - Compare: Ars., Fl-ac., Nit- ac. REFERENCES - Murphy. full:
PHARMACY - teucr.Teucriummarumverum. Cat-thyme. Marum verum. N. O. Labiatae. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies. Locally for polyps, dry powder.

CLINICAL - Anorexia. Anus, itching. Ascarides. Cachexia. Colic. Concussion. Eyelids, tumor. Fibroma. Hiccoughs. Ingrown, toenail. Nasal, catarrh. Otalgia. Ozaena. Polyps. Psoriasis. Rheumatism. Threadworms. Urethra, excrescences. Uterine, fibroids. Worms.

HERBAL - The Germander group of the Labiatae, to which the Teucriums belong, had an important place in old herbal medicine, and homeopathy has placed Teucr. on a firm foundation. Stapf and others proved it.

HOMEOPATHIC - Worm infestations, irritation of anus and nose. Threadworms. Worms and polyps suggest a tubercular taint and Clarke has used both Teucr. and Teucr. scorod. in tubercular cases. Nasal polyps. Guernsey noted “Polyps with stoppage of nose on side lain on. large red pimples under right nostril near septum, sore and smarting to touch.” Chronic nasal catarrh with atrophy, large offensive crusts and clinkers. Ozaena. Loss of sense of smell. Fibrous tumor of the eyelid. Affections of children. Suitable after too much medicine has been taken. Over sensitiveness. Desire to stretch. Urethral granulations following gonorrhea and also uterine fibroids.

Head - Excited, tremulous feeling. Frontal pain, worse stooping. Strengthens brain after delirium tremens.

Eyes - Eyes red, inflamed. Smarting in canthi, lids red and puffy, tarsal tumor (Staph.).

Ears - Otalgia. Shootings and tearings in ears. Hissing and ringing.

Nose - Catarrhal condition of both anterior and posterior nostrils. Mucus polyps. Chronic catarrh, Discharge of large, irregular clinkers. Crawling in nostrils with lachrymation and sneezing. Coryza with stoppage of nostrils.

Mouth - Foul breath. Mouth clammy. Much mucus in mouth. Smarting as from pepper, first on left, later also on right side. Smarting in root of the tongue.

Throat - Sore throat with shooting pain and impeded deglutition. Pressure or drawing and tearing in throat. Frequent necessity to hawk. Hawking up of much mucus of a moldy taste. COMMENTS - Clarke gave Teucr. tincture in five-drop doses three times a day to a man of 44 who had tuberculosis affecting the right lung with severe recurrent hemorrhages. Teucr. helped him, and with other remedies he got quite well. While taking Teucr. he noticed that he passed a large quantity of threadworms to which he was not at all subject. C. M. Boger related a case of cough in which his patient had with the cough a moldy taste in the throat when hawking up mucus. Expectoration profuse. Rapid loss of weight and strength. Anorexia. A brother had died of tuberculosis four years before with very similar symptoms. Teucr. 3x helped and 20x finished the cure. Teucr. has the craving hunger of the anti- psorics and worm remedies, it prevents sleep at night. Nervous, irritable, sensitive. Rheumatic and gouty symptoms and scapular pains, both in the bones and joints. Limbs go to sleep with tingling when sitting. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Camph. Compare: (1) Teucr-s. (2) Cina, Ign., Sang., Sil. Compatible: Chin., Puls., Sil. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Vomiting of large quantities of dark-green masses. Constant hiccough, attended with pain in back. Hiccough on eating after nursing.

Abdomen - Pressure in abdomen. Expulsion of much flatus, having the smell of rotten eggs. Incarceration of flatus. Colic with tearing drawings. Cutting pain after drinking beer or water.

Rectum - Itching of anus and constant irritation in the evening in bed. Crawling in the rectum after stool. Ascarides with nightly restlessness. Swelling, itching, and creeping at anus as from ascarides. Frequent itching and tingling in anus, often after the evacuations. Copious fetid evacuations of the consistence of pap. Sensations - As if air forced through mucus in ear. As if right nostril were partly stopped. Chill as from abdomen. Sensation as from flea bites. As if nail had grown into flesh of right great toe.

Male - Sexual desire decreased. Drawing pain behind left side of root of penis, extending to left side of scrotum, became sore to touch. Pressive, drawing sensation from abdomen into cords and testes. Burning, pressing, biting in fore part of urethra when not urinating. Excrescences in urethra following gonorrhea.

Female - Smooth pedunculate, pear-shaped polypus of vagina, protruding three inches beyond hymen. Food - Hunger in morning and evening. Appetite increased. Sensation of hunger, as if the food were unsatisfying and which hinders sleep. Bitter taste in gullet after dinner. Cuttings or nausea with inclination to vomit after drinking water.

Chest - Chest loaded, with sensation of dryness in trachea. Squeezing pressure in lower part of chest, with anxious uneasi ness, without affecting the breathing. Constitutions - Suited to elderly persons and children. When too much medicine has produced an over- sensitive condition and remedies fail to act.

Back - Burning in left scapula. Rheumatic drawing and tension in back. Causations - Concussion (brain). Injuries likely to set up tetanus.

Limbs - Tearing pains in arms and legs. Affection of fingertips and joints of toes. Pain in toenails, as if they had grown into flesh. Lungs - Dry cough, excited by a tickling in trachea, as if dust had been inspired, worse by coughing. Moldy taste in throat when hawking up mucus, expectoration profuse.

Sleep - Sleep retarded in evening. Restless with twitching, choking and starting up frightened. Unrefreshing sleep and difficulty in waking in morning. Agitated sleep at night, from excessive excitement. Vivid dreams and frequent starts.

Skin - Very dry skin. Itching causes tossing about all night. Suppurating grooves in the nails.

Modalities - Desires exercise in open air, which does not fatigue. Moving improves. Worse by touch. Worse sitting, stooping, on side lain on. Disinclined for exertion. Worse warmth, warmth of bed, wet weather. Worse evening and at night.

Temperature - Shivering and shaking, often with icy coldness in hands, and frequent yawning. Chilliness after eating, and when talking about unpleasant things. Heat worse in evening, with exaltation and great loquacity. Frequent feeling of flushing in face, without external redness.

full:
PHARMACY - teucr-s. Teucrium scorodonia. Wood sage. Wood germander. N. O. Labiatae. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historicaldose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Bronchorrhea. Catarrhs. Coryza. Coughs. Epidymitis. Nasal, catarrh. Testicle, tuberculosis. Tuberculosis.

HERBAL - Teucrium scorodonia is an extremely bitter plant with the smell and taste of hops, for which it has been substituted. Some have observed an alliaceous smell and Cazin said that it gives agarlicky taste to the milk of cows, goats and sheep which eat it.

HOMEOPATHIC - Teucr-s. has been used in tuberculosis with muco-purulent expectoration. Dropsy orchitis and tuberculous epidymitis, especially in young, thin individuals with tuberculosis of lungs, glands, bones and uro-genitals. It is used as an adjuvant in severe afflictions of the lungs. Remarkable results have been observed in chronic catarrhs of the lungs and bronchi, in nasal catarrhs, coryza, cough and asthma bronchiale. COMMENTS - Dr. Criquelion told how Dr. Martiny one day in the Ardennes, had occasion to examine a man of thirty who was apparently in the last stage of consumption and had a cavity in one apex. Martiny gave his opinion that he had not long to live. A year later, being in the same district, he called at the house and inquired of a man whom he saw there, apparently in perfect health, what had become of the in valid. “I am he,” was the reply. It was the fact, though it took some time to convince Martiny of it. An old woman had recommended him to make a tisane of the wood germander which grew abundantly about there. He had taken it daily and got well. “A similar case,” said Cooper, “was told me by a distinguished scientist. Martiny introduced Teucr-s. into his practice and used a tisane of it with much success in bronchorrhea and consumptive disorders with tuberculous elements and muco-purulent expectoration. Clarke confirmed this, using the tincture in five or ten-drop doses two or three times a day. Criquelion pointed out that Teucrine has been used as a subcutaneous injection in tubercular cases as a substitute for Koch’s Tub. Criquelion had a patient, a farmer of scrofulous habit, high color, thick neck, who had for ten years an enlarged testicle the size of a quince, which he diagnosed to be tuberculous. Teucr-s. 6c was given, one drop in four spoonfuls of water, a spoonful three-quarters of an hour before each meal. After three months the testicle was softer in six months it had almost returned to its proper size. RELATIONS - Teucr-s. is allied to Marrubium vulgare (Common or White Horehound), a well-known cough remedy. Also to Nepeta glechoma (Ground Ivy), which was formerly muchused with snail-jellyforchest affections.” Compare: (1) Bac., Tub., Teucr., Helix. REFERENCES - Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - thala. Thalamus. Gray nuclei around the encephalon. Nerve-hormonal tissue from brain. Sarcode. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Catatonia. Contractures. Cyanosis. Hebephrenia. Hyperthyroidism. Menopausal, complaints. Neuralgias. Pains. Parkinson’s disease. Raynaud’s syndrome. Sciatica. Vasomotor, complaints.

HOMEOPATHIC - Thala. belongs to the group of gray nuclei around the encephalon. It is a large ganglion, even and symmetrical. Situated in front of and outside the quadrigeminal bodies inside the striped bodies. Laterally bordering the third ventricle, surrounded on its convexity by the caudate nucleus. It is egg-shaped and the distal end is large. Hardy conducted a clinical proving, but there is no homeopathic proving. Complaints of the psychological system, including spasmodic laughter and cry ing, consciousness disorders inner sensitivity disorders. Patient misinterprets his illnesses. Pseudo-bulbar paralysis. Neuralgias, cervical and brachial, sciatica. Tabes. Painful stumps. Vasomotor disorders. Parkinson’s disease. Pre-cancerous conditions, predominantly painful. Paresthesia in the female during the menopause. Formication, painful numbness situated particularly in the arms and which keeps the patient awake. Tingling, which is always distal and which appears with no apparent cause. Neuralgia of the left cervical region and arm with formication. Pains accompanied by phenomena of anguish, ill-defined feeling of uneasiness, painful discomfort. Spontaneous pains, appear suddenly and then immediately reach their peak intensity. The painful sensation is much greater than the stimulus. Exaggerated pain. Violent attacks of paroxysm. Pains reside in one half of the body, predominantly of the limbs. Pain accompanied by sweating. MIND - Catatonic conditions. State of inertia, desire for solitude and peace, loss of initiative. The patient does not want to do anything. He sits in a comer, immobile. Condition of psychological strain, which causes the feeling of being ill at ease in his body. Hebephrenia. Spasmodic laughing and crying without any real cause, expressed by involuntary, automatic contracture of the muscles in the face and by mimicry, which is either ill-times or irrelevant or exaggerated.

Head - Occipital headaches, worse on the left side, spreading to the entire left side of the body.

Eyes - Sight becomes weaker on one side of the field of vision. Objects seem lost in a halo of light. Diminution of sight on one half of the field of vision.

Ears - Hallucinations of hearing with feeling of strangeness and fright. Buzzing in the ears, sound of a bell in the fog or of a foghorn. Noises in the ears. Feeling of confusion in the ears.

Nose - Ozaena. Reduction in the olfactory sensitivity. Sensation of evil-smelling, unpleasant whiffs like sulphur. Smells are badly tolerated.

Stomach - Pains with nausea, worse after ingestion of food. Cramping stomachache, accompanied by nausea and meteorism.

Abdomen - Epigastric pain in a continuous transverse bar, not changed by eating, but aggravated by emotion. Pain is diffuse, badly localized. Accompanied by discomfort. Abdominal meteorism ameliorated by emission of wind. Abdominal pains with emission of soft stools.

Male - Impotence with dwindling or libido and lack of orgasm. Sex painful with premature ejaculation.

Female - Frigidity. Libido disturbed, impotence, frigidity, sexual asthenia. Menopausal complaints with hot flashes, aggravated at night. Hyperthyroidism during the menopause with swelling at the base of the neck.

Chest - He feels as though his thoracic cage were trapped inside an iron corset. Constitutions - Psoric, syphilitic or tubercular disposition. Nervous, biliary and lymphatic temperament.

Heart - Vasomotor complaints. Vascular disorders, accompanied by pain. Pain in the left side of the thorax, which may spread to the arm, aggravated by physical exercise and capable of stimulating an attack of angina pectoris.

Limbs - Raynaud’s syndrome. Cyanosis of the limbs with tingling and burning sensation. Movements badly coordinated for the upper as well as the lower limbs. Often drops things. Hands in a contracted state without total paralysis. Numbness of the hands with cyanosis and trembling. Numbness of the feet with cyanosis, formication, swelling and edema of the ankles. Copious perspiration from the feet. Spastic gait. Lungs - Asthmatic dyspnea, the patient has difficulty in exhaling.

Skin - Dermographia. Burning sensation on the skin, aggravated by heat and cold. Excessive sweating, predominantly on one half of the body. Lesion caused by parasites, on the nails. Deformity of the nails, which are concave, ridged, breaking. Nails extremely fragile. Inflammation beneath the nails.

Modalities - Better by fresh air and movement. The pains are better at night. Worse by the cold, heat. Worse from emotions, especially unhappy emotions.

Temperature - Vascular complaints, the skin is either very red or very pale, but always cold. Cyanosis and edema at the limbs, accompanied either by an increase in the local heat or, the opposite, by decrease in the heat. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1) Agar., Op., Hyos., (2) Hypoth., Pitu-gl. REFERENCES - Julian.

full:
PHARMACY - thal. Thallium metallicum. Thallium metal. Thallium aceticum. A Rare Metal. Trituration. Solution of the Sulphate. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne. Alopecia. Amenorrhea. Atherosclerosis. Baldness. Cachexia. Conjunctivitis. Cyanosis. Dysuria. Emaciation. Emphysema. Folliculitis. Glomerulonephritis. Hair, loss. Hematuria. Hyperthyroidism. Insomnia. Locomotor ataxia. Malaria. Muscular, atrophy. Myelitis. Neuritis. Night-sweats. Paraplegia. Paralysis. Pleurisy. Pneumoconiosis. Polyneuritis. Rheumatism. Sciatic pains. Trembling. Tremors. Tuberculosis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Thallium is a rare metal discovered by Crookes in 1861. He found it in the residue left from the distillation of selenium and named it thallium (a green shoot) from the green it gives in the spectrum. Thallium and its derivatives are toxic.Thallium has been experimented with by Lamy and Marme. The symptoms picture of Thallium were established in 1965-66 by Panos, Rogers and Stephenson, on seven male and nine female provers. Combermale of Lille, used Thal, with success in the night-sweats of tuberculosis, but this treatment had the effect of causing profuse falling of the hair, so serious as to contraindicate its use. Huchard had patients become quite bald in several days. Hansen said Thal, relieves the violent pains of tabes dorsalis. Horrible, neuralgic, spasmodic shooting pains. Pains like electric shocks. Muscular atrophy. Tremors. Trembling. Chorea-like movements. Locomotor ataxia with pain. Paralysis of lower limbs. Paraplegia. Poly- neuritis. Neuritis. Trigeminal neuralgia. Spinal neurasthenia. Pseudo-bulbar paralysis. Intermittent paralysis. Muscular pains. Muscular atrophy. Numbness or formication starting in the fingers and toes, extending up to lower limbs and down to feet and involving lower abdomen and perineum. General emaciation with a lack of strength. Hyperemia, swelling and excessive secretion. Night-sweats of tuberculosis. Dermatrophic lesions. Alopecia, hair loss following acute, exhausting diseases. Loss of body hair and hair of the head. Influences the endocrine glands, especially the thyroid and adrenalin. Hyperthyroidism symptoms. Emaciation, hypotonia, chilliness. Pains in the legs, aggravated when lying on the affected side. Unable to find a position in the bed which eases the pain. Pain in the right knee on bending or stretching it. Pain in the sciatic nerve. Discomforts are of a periodic nature, recurring in strength, at the same hour and then disappearing again. Permanent state of jangled nerves. Trophic conditions of the nails. MIND - Growing impatience. Extreme irritability and violence, uneasiness with insomnia. Extreme anxiety for no reason. Hysterical symptoms with hyperesthesia and then hypoesthesia. State of jangled nerves of excitability and bewailing with weeping and shouting. Attacks of weeping, excitement. Bursts into tears for the least thing, only to blow up soon after. Stubborn. Indifferent resignation. Apathy. Depression.

Head - Headaches. Pain in occiput in morning. Alopecia. Hair falls off with great rapidity. Falling out of hair after diseases. Hair falls off in handfuls. Hair loss in spots

Eyes - Dacryocystitis. Iritis. Blepharitis. Purulent conjunctivitis. Frequent conjunctivitis with abundant production of mucus. Muco-purulent discharge from the right eye, worse in the morning. Glittering spots in front of the eyes with formication on the face. Visual complaints with feeling of heaviness behind the eye. Scotoma. Eyebrows fall out.

Face - Facial neuralgia. Hair loss from beard.

Mouth - Lips dry with thirsty feeling. Bad breath, irritation of the mucus membranes in the mouth with excessive salivation. Stomatitis. Aphthae. Gingivitis. Dental caries. Toothache. Numbness.

Throat - Goiter. Swollen thyroid gland. RELATIONS - Thal, belongs to the Lead group of metals and approaches Plb. closest in its symptoms. Compare: (1) Thal-s. Plb., Lath., Caust., Arg-n. (2) Baldness, Jab., Pilo., Petr. (3) Baldness and tuberculosis, Phos. (4) Aran. - Feeling of constant coldness. Periodic return of symptoms. Severe pain in the heels.(5) Cedr. - Periodicity of symptoms, supra-orbital neuralgia, periodic migraines. (6) Aran-ix. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Julian. Phatak.

Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Bitterbelchings and bitter taste in the mouth. Feels nauseated but cannot vomit. Nausea and vomiting. Pain in stomach and bowels, terribly severe lancinations, following each other with the rapidity of electric shocks.

Abdomen - Retraction or depression of abdomen. Distention of the abdomen. Heavy flatulence, even after a light meal. Spasmodic pain in the stomach and intestines with abdominal pains. Pain in intestinal canal.

Rectum - Spasmodic, stubborn constipation, alternating with attacks of diarrhea and anal and rectal pains. Diarrhea, bloody stools.

Male - Impotence. Loss of pubic hair.

Female - Menses prolonged with black blood. Amenorrhea. Loss of pubic hair. Food - Thirst. Voracious appetite. Loss of appetite.

Chest - Painful, heavy feeling on the sternum. Retro-sternal pain in the esophagus. Neuralgia after herpes zoster.

Heart - Diminished frequency of pulse. Pulse rapid with precordial constriction.

Back - Formication on the back. Lumbar aching.

Limbs - Sharp pains like electric shocks. Very tired. Disorders of movement coordination. Chorea-like movements and rapid movements like convulsions. Exaggerated reflexes and muscular atrophy. Trembling. Paralytic feeling. Chronic myelitis. Numbness in fingers and toes with extension up lower limbs involving lower abdomen and perineum. Paralysis of lower limbs. Cyanosis of limbs. Formication, beginning in fingers and extending through pelvis. Emaciation of fingertips. Deformed nails.

Sleep - Sleep is light, wakes often. Great difficulty in falling asleep again.

Skin - Dryness of the skin. Red stripes after scratching. Acne. Folliculitis. Skin pigmentation disorders. Loss of hair on the body (axillary and pubic). Skin sensitive in particular areas, especially on the soles of the feet. Pustular formations. Trophic complaints of the nails, which are deformed. Inflammation beneath the nails. Deformed nails.

Modalities - Better from walking. Worse at night. Worse from contact, pressure.

Liver - Gallbladder distended. Coating of liver white and granular-looking. Lungs - Slow and difficult breathing. Dyspnea. Respiration difficult with pain all over the thoracic cage. Emphysema. Pleurisy. Pneumoconiosis. Cyanosis.

Kidneys - Involuntary passing of urine. Casts in urine. Acute glomerulonephritis. Dysuria. Proteinuria. Hematuria.

Blood - Attacks of hypertension with hyperthyroid phenomena. Bleeding from the capillary vessels. Atherosclerosis. Cyanosis. Increase of carbon dioxide in the blood plasma.

Temperature - Profuse sweating in cases of severe illness. Night-sweats of tuberculosis.
