full:
PHARMACY - thea. Thea sinensis. Chinese tea. Camellia thea. N. O. Temstromiaceae, Theaceae. Tincture or infusion of dried leaves and flowers. Trituration of Theine. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Delirium, tremens. Mania. Homicidal. Insanity. Insomnia. Kidney, disorders. Mania. Megrim. Nervousness. Neuralgias. Paralysis. Sleeplessness. Suicidal.

HERBAL - Tea contains an alkaloid, Thein, which is considered by some identical with caffeine, and both tea and coffee are used to stimulate the jaded faculties. The stimulation will enable persons to endure fatigue and get more enjoyment out of themselves than they could obtain by mere food. Coffee and tea are different in their effects though they may be alike in their chemistry. The after-effect of all stimulation is reaction, unless it is kept off by a repetition of the stimulant as the effect of the last dose wears off. The sign that the first dose of tea is wearing off is a nervous, restless, depressed, ill- tempered state, which is visible in persons who rely on tea, at about 5 p.m.

HOMEOPATHIC - Neuralgia and insomnia. All-gone, sinking sensation at the epigastrium. Nervous sleeplessness, heart troubles, palpitations and dyspepsia of old tea-drinkers. Sensitive kidneys. Sick head- aches. Allen noted it was antidotal to Tab. MIND - Nervousness and want of confidence. Great nervous excitability with exaltation of intellectual faculties. Ill-humored. Peevish. Disposition to quarrel at the most harmless speech. Nocturnal fright, suicidal thoughts. Temporary mental exaltation. Delirium with ecstasy, laughed incessantly, talked in rhyme. Delirium tremens. Mania. Suicidal and homicidal. Impulses to kill. Impulse to jump out of the window.

Head - Rush of blood to head. Sick headache radiating from one point. Sleepless and restless. Hallucinations of hearing. Cold damp feeling at back of head. Scalp tender can scarcely comb hair.

Eyes - Eyes are unusually bright. Dilated pupils. Neuralgia of eyes. Sight is dim, dark before eyes, fiery lines, sparks.

Ears - Neuralgic pains in cartilage of ears. Roaring in ears. Hallucinations of hearing.

Nose - Dryness, soreness of nose. Sensation at root of nose as if nosebleed would occur. Nosebleed before menses.

Face - Wild, distressed expression. Face is pale, with congested redness, flushed.

Mouth - Bitter taste in mouth. Much viscid saliva. Whole mouth cavity dry and sensitive. Tongue clean and pale. Tongue red, blistered, painful as if scalded. Teeth frequently decayed.

Throat - Scraping in larynx. Hoarseness. Diphtheria sore throat. Painless swelling of mucus membrane. Uneasy feeling in pharynx, as if obstructed by a foreign body. Vertigo - Vertigo with darkness before eyes, sudden in open air. COMMENTS - The symptoms are made up of observed effects of overdosing and some direct provings. A woman who was addicted to dri nking tea showed very pronounced delirium tremens indistinguishable from that caused by alcohol, though there was no alcoholism in the case. Another woman, who kept a pot of tea boiling on the stove and drank several bowls every day, developed both suicidal and homicidal mania, impulse tojump out of the window, to cut her baby’s throat or throw it downstairs. Thea 100,000c, Fincke, cured. A man who had been many years in the East and was used to one-story houses, on his return to the West had a curious impulse tojump out of the window, which he traced to tea-drinking and which disappeared when he left it off. Teste noted that the homicidal impulse appeared in the dreams of one prover, who was so far from being horrified by his dreammurders that he even took pleasure in them after awaking. The talkativeness of Thea, is one of its chief allurements. Among tea-tasters, who do not drink the tea they taste, but only hold it in the mouth a short time, yet long enough for the mouth to absorb some, there is sometimes developed what is known as tea-tasters’ paralysis, affecting mostly the lower limbs with loss of sensation of both upper and lower. A man, after drinking tea, had pain in his epigastrium going through to his back with a feeling as if he wanted to be sick and could not, better sitting down and stretching out. Thuj. 30c cured. Guernsey gave these as indications for Thea, “Nervous sleeplessness, heart troubles, of old tea-drinkers, palpitations of the heart, can’t lie down.” RELATIONS -Antidote: Thuj., Ferr., Kali-hp. - Material dosesfortea-taster’scoughAnridoted by: Beer.

Stomach - A sinking sensation at the epigastrium. Faint, gone feeling (Sep., Hydr., Olean.). Weakness about stomach. Sudden production of wind in large quantities. Nausea, and vomiting after eating. Vomits bile, when pain at its height.

Abdomen - Borborygmi. After lunch, stitch below ribs in paroxysms. Intestines relaxed. Liability to hernia.

Rectum - Swelling of lower end of rectum, with slight itching. Chronic relaxed bowels. worse by beer, better by port wine. Constipation. Sensations - As if on the verge of fainting. As if a foreign body in throat. As if the stomach hung down relaxed in the body like an empty bag. As if the weight of a sheet on the feet would crush the toes. Cold sensations are prominent, cold, damp feeling at back of head with pain spreading thence to eyes, also dryness and swelling of mucus membrane.

Male - Erections. Unnatural excitement.

Female - Soreness and tenderness in ovaries. Menses delayed, scanty with severe cramp-like pains. Uterine bearing down from beginning to end of period. Food - Very hungry, but little satisfies. Thirst, but every mouthful of cold water affects the head like a shock. Craves acids, lemons.

Chest - Oppressed and constricted. Fluttering in left side and feeling of suffocation.

Heart - Anxious oppression. Precordial distress. Palpitation, unable to lie on left side. Fluttering. Pulse rapid, irregular Thea sinensis intermittent.

Limbs - Paralyzed numbness of limbs. Joints of hands and feet tender. Nervous excitability in wrists, hands, and feet. Hand trembled violently. Restlessness of feet. Neuralgic pains in outer hamstrings. Sensation as if the weight of a sheet even would crush toes. Lungs - Edema of respiratory tract. Breathing increased in frequency and amplitude. Breathlessness on least exertion. Paroxysm of asphyxia. Cough is dry, severe and bloody expectoration.

Sleep - Sleepy in daytime, sleepiness at night with vascular excitement and restlessness and dry skin. Horrible dreams cause no horror.

Skin - Skin dry as if pores obstructed. Skin of fingertips peels from excessive dryness. Eruption of red, indolent pimples. Itching, crawling, prickling in different parts.

Modalities - Better warmth, warm bath, applying hand or warm clothes to occiput. Worse at night, from cold water, walking in open air. Worse after meals.

Compare - (1) Gone, faint feeling, sick-headache radiating from one point and pain in left ovary, Sep. (2) Averse to work, especially writing, Hydr. (3) Relaxed feeling in stomach. Ip. (4) Desire for acids, Verat., Sulph., Ant-c., Phos., Sabin. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Kidneys - Very marked increase of urine. Must pass water immediately after drinking tea.

Temperature - Intense coldness passing over whole head. Lowered temperature. Hands and face cold as marble. Beaded with chilly moisture. Excessive internal heat with flushes of heat on the surface, coming and going quickly. Disposition to perspire.

name: Theridion Curassavicum
author: Murphy

full:
PHARMACY - ther. Theridion curassavicum. Orange spider. Latrodectuscurassavicus. N. O. Arachnida. West- Indies. Tincture of the whole spider. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Angina pectoris. Anthrax, sheep. Bone, disorders. Decay. Menopause. Coughs. Dysmenorrhea. Eye-teeth, pains. Fainting. Headaches. Hysteria. Liver, disorder, abscess. Marasmus. Ménière’s disease. Nausea. Necrosis. Nose, catarrh. Ozaena. Photophobia. Pregnancy, sickness. Rickets. Scrofulosis. Seasickness. Spinal, irritation. Tetanus. Toothache. Tuberculosis. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - Ther. was introduced and proved by Hering in 1832. The spider is found in the West Indies, chiefly in the island of Curacao. It is about the size of a cherry-stone and is found on orange-trees. It is velvety black when young with antero-posterior lines composed of white dots, on the posterior of the body there are three orange-red spots and on the belly a large square yellow spot. The spider is very poisonous. It produces a highly sensitive, nervous condition with weakness, trembling, coldness, anxiety, faintness and easily excited cold sweat. Venom produces hypersensitiveness of the ***nerves. Sensitive to noise, which penetrates the body. It affects the teeth, causes nausea, chills and pains all over, strikes the painful parts etc. Nervous hyperesthesia. Noises seem to strike on painful spots over the body. Affinity for the tubercular diathesis. Tuberculosis, stitch high up in left apex (Anthr.). Where the indicated remedy does not hold long. Rickets, decay, necrosis. Vertigo, sick headache, peculiar pain around heart region, tuberculosis florida, and scrofula. Spinal irritation. Decay and necrosis of the bones. Bones feel broken. Rickets. Burning pains. Water feels too cold. Bounding internally, as of a child. Sense of duality. Effects of sunstroke. Hysteria during puberty and at menopause. Infantile atrophy, glands enlarged with marasmus. Nodes on various parts especially buttocks. Seasickness. Left side most affected. MIND - Restless, finds pleasure in nothing. Time passes too quickly. Sensitive to slightest noise. Startled by least thing. Confusion of mind, worse laughing. Insanity during menopause. Hysteria. Talkativeness and hilarity. Wantofself confidence. Aversion to work. Joyful during headache. Depression during headache. Weeping from toothache. Feels and looks as if dying, but hears and understands all that is said.

Head - Head internally hot, oppressed and heavy. Head feels thick, thinks it belongs to another, that she can lift it off or she would like to remove it. Migraine. Headache, felt during sleep, worse jarring, with nausea and vomiting, at menopause. Headache worse after stool. Cannot lie down with headache. Pain worse anyone walking over floor.

Eyes - Glittering vision, on stooping. Luminous vibrations before eyes. Blurred vision. Sensitive to light. Pressure behind eyeballs. Throbbing over left eye.

Ears - Least noise, even sound penetrates her whole body, especially teeth. Rushing in both ears like a waterfall.

Nose - Pain over root of nose. Ozaena. Chronic catarrh, yellow-green, thick offensive, discharge. Discharge is yellowish and offensive. Post-nasal catarrh (Puls., Thuj.). Sensations - As if her head was another strange head. As if vertex did not belong to her. Like a pressing pain in root of nose and about ears. As of a veil before eyes. As if something in esophagus were slipping towards epigastrium. Like labor pains in lower abdomen. As if a child were bounding in body. As if bones were broken and would fall asunder. As if dying.

Face - Pale. Jaws immovable in the morning.

Mouth - Mouth feels furred, benumbed. ***Froth before the mouth with shaking chill. Teeth feel as if cold water is too cold. Bites tip of tongue during sleep. Lockjaw, morning on waking. Remains open involuntarily, cannot close.

Stomach - Seasickness. Nausea and vomiting when closing eyes and on motion (Tab.). Nausea worse least motion, looking steadily at one object from noise. Nausea and retching better drinking warm water.

Abdomen - Violent burning in liver region. Abscess of liver. Pain in the groins after sex, motion and drawing up the limbs. Stinging pain on left side over anterior aspect of spleen.

Male - Gonorrhea. Prostate enlarged, sense of a lump and heaviness in perineum, worse at even step. Seminal emission during afternoon sleep.

Female - Hysteria during puberty, at menopause. Menses suppressed. Food - Constant desire to eat and drink but knows not for what. Craves oranges and bananas, acid fruits and drinks, wine, tobacco smoke.

Chest - Stitches high up in chest, back through apex of left lung. Pain in upper left chest (Myrt., Pix., Anis.). Pain in left floating ribs. Pinching in left pectoral muscle. Constitutions - Tubercular diathesis.

Heart - Cardiac anxiety and pain. Anxiety about the heart, sharp pain radiates to arm and left shoulder. Pulse slow with vertigo.

Back - Stinging pains. Spine is sensitive to pressure and jar, sits sideways in a chair to avoid pressure. Sensitiveness between vertebra. Causations - Seasickness. Washing clothes. Riding.

Limbs - Burning in upper arm. Restless feeling in hands, wrings them. Stinging from elbow to shoulder. Lies or sits with feet crossed, cannot uncross them. Lungs - Cough, jerks body together, head forward and knees upward. Too much air seems to enter the chest. Breathing difficult going up and down stairs, hysteria. Tuberculosis.

Skin - Stinging, stabs everywhere. Itching sensations. Sensitive skin on the thighs.

Modalities - Better from rest in horizontal position. Warm water improves nausea and retching. Warmth improves. Worse touch, pressurerai, leftside. Worseleastmotion, exertion, stooping, rising, walking, going up or down stairs. Worse sex, particularly groin pain. Worse on shipboard, riding in carriage. Worse from noise. Worse from cold, washing clothes, sunstroke. Worse closing eyes.

Kidneys - Increased urination, at night, does not pass much during day.

Temperature - Shaking chill with foam at mouth. Internal coldness. Cold sweat easily excited. Vertigo - Faints after washing clothes. Vertigo with nausea, worse stooping, kneeling. Vertigo with nausea and vomiting on least motion, worse when closing eyes. COMMENTS - Grimmer stated. “The orange spider poison can cure when indicated on the totality of its symptoms. Decay of bones, abscesses and cancer of the liver and lungs. It acts profoundly on the nervous system, producing extreme sensitivity to noise the vibration penetrating to the teeth.” Keynotes extreme sensitiveness to noise, worse by least noise, “sounds penetrate the teeth.” The sensitiveness extends to vibrations of any kind, jar of a step, riding in a carriage or in a boat. “Worse closing eyes,” especially in vertigo and symptoms of the head and stomach. Seasickness or sickness of pregnancy. Severe headaches, affecting the eyes, especially the left. The ears are highly sensitive. Intoler ance of light. Frequent cough, convulsive, head spasmodically jerked forward, knees jerked up to abdomen. Hallucinations of sight and hearing, luminous vibrations and rushing sounds. A kind of intoxication is induced, hilarity, talkativeness. “Time passes too slowly.” Burning pains and itching are common and a stitch high up in apex of left chest has proved a guiding symptom for Ther. in the cure of cases of tuberculosis. “Burning in liver region” led to the cure of abscess and even cancer of that organ. H. C. Allen noted it for spinal irritation and disease of the spine and other bones. Decay, necrosis and scrofulous disease of bones have all been cured with it. “In scrofulosis when the best remedies fail to relieve.” Chackravarti related a case of headache cured with Ther. Mr. B., 35, well built of bilious temperament, had for three months severe headache with nausea and vomiting like seasickness and shaking chills. Dullness and fullness in the head with throbbing beginning in occiput, preceded by flickering before the eyes. Head felt large and heavy. The pains began in the morning increase during the day and last until evening. Excessive irritation with loss of sustaining power. Worse from least overwork and motion, better by keeping quiet in horizontal position. Constipation, stools hard, small, dry. Ther. 3x was given, one drop in water twice daily. The pain was much better the next day and was gone in less than a week. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Aeon, (sensitiveness to noises), Mosch, (nausea), Graph, (more chronic effects). Follows well: Sulph., Calc., Lyc. (scrofula). Compare: (1) Aran- d. and Spiders generally. (2) Hemicrania worse closing eyes, worse noise, Sep. (But Sep. worse from noise is less intense). (3) Vertigo and faintness on closing eyes, Lach. (4) Headache, nervousness, hysteria. Tarent. (5) Stooping down, violent stitch high up in left chest, thence to back, Myrt-c. through to left scapula. (6) Time passes too quickly (too slowly Cann-i., Arg- n., Nux-m.). (7) Vertigo on closing eyes, Lach., Thuj. (on opening them, Tab., on looking up, Puls. Sil.). (8) Headache, worse lying down, Lach. HERBAL - Thiosinaminum belongs to the same chemical group as Urea. The colorless, bitter crystals are soluble in water, alcohol and ether.

HOMEOPATHIC - Thiosin. has been effective in curing adhesions, scars, lupus and enlarged lymphatic glands. It’s a dissolvent, externally and internally, for dissolving scar tissue, keloids. It has been used for tumors, enlarged glands, lupus, strictures, adhesions. Inflamed, swollen glands, adenitis. Ectropion, opacities of cornea, cataract, ankylosis, fibroids, scleroderma. Noises in ear. Tinnitus aurium, deafness. Gastric, vesicle and rectal crises. Strictures of rectum. Tumors of the uterus appendages. For tabes dorsalis, improving the lightning pains. Sensation of heat and burning in affected parts. Increases body weight and reduces glandular swellings. Dr. A. S. Hard suggested Thiosin. for retarding old age. MIND - Depression of spirits. Aversion to consolation. Moody, alternating moods. Alzheimer's disease. Senile dementia.

Eyes - Cataract of the lens or comea. Stricture of the lachrymal duct.

Ears - Ménière’s syndrome, vertigo. Noises in ear. Tinnitus caused by fibrous bands. Formation of fibrous bands impeding free movement of the ossicles. Otosclerosis. Suppurative otitis media. Thickened eardrum. Catarrhal deafness with scar thickenings. Deafness due to some fibrous change in the nerve. Adhesions of the Eustachian tube. Eustachian tube catarrh.

Nose - Allergies.

Stomach - Indigestion, flatulence of stomach and bowels, worse after eating. Pyloric stenosis. Stricture of esophagus. Vertigo- Arteriosclerotic vertigo. Ménière’s syndrome, vertigo. COMMENTS - The mustard seeds of Sin-n. are of a reddish-brown color. Mixed with those of Sin-a., they are crushed between rollers and subsequently powdered and sifted at least twice. A fixed oil is obtained by pressure from the residue left on the sieve. The powdered mustard is mixed with a considerable quantity of wheaten flour and a small quantity of turmeric powder. The Treasury of Botany noted that “The term ‘flour of mustard’ is not quite accurate, as the mustard seeds themselves contain little or no starchy material. The chemical ingredients are somewhat complex. Among them are a peculiar acid called Myronic acid, noticeable as containing a large proportion of Sulphur. When mixed with water and a peculiar substance called Myrosine, (analogous to albumen), also found in mustard seeds, yields a volatile Oil of Mustard. “This has no separate existence in the seeds, but is formed artificially in the manner just stated. This oil is very acrid and has been used as a rubefacient. The fixed oil before mentioned as existing in the seed itself has little or no acridity and has been used as a purgative and vermifuge.” Scar tissue and adhesions. Ringing in the ears. Tinnitus or deafness in elderly people from otosclerosis. The bones of the ears get calcium deposits. Scarred eardrums or eardrums that thicken and cause hearing difficulties. Chronic ruptured eardrums in children (Calen, acutely). Ménière’s disease Thiosinaminum (Chin-s.). Vertigo. Opacities of the cornea, cataracts. Torn ligaments, especially in the shoulder. Painful adhesions affecting mobility of a joint. Internal adhesions of the uterus, adhesions after surgery. Strictures of the urethra and painful urination. Dr. McCullogh found that it exerts a marked beneficial action on ear diseases accompanied by the formation of new connective tissue. He believed that this beneficial action was due to an increased pliability of this tissue. Its administration should always be accompanied by mechanical measures; better and more prompt results may be obtained in recent cases. McCullogh also noted a beneficial action on vertigo and better results may be obtained with it in the relief of tinnitus aurium than with any drug used previously. C. H. Pennoyer related the case of Mrs. C., 69, who had been ill for several years with gastric distress, sciatica, pains in hips down to knees, worse by motion. She had indigestion, flatulence of stomach and bowels, worse after eating. Pain in back. Inability to walk, much perspiration, depression of spirits and subnormal temperature. Her father had died at 69 of stomach trouble, mother at 58 of stricture of the bowel. Examination showed stricture of the rectum two inches above the anus, there being a tense fibrous band forming a ring opening, which would not admit the index finger. Bougies and mechanical measures failed to relieve. Weakness was so great, the patient would faint at stool. Nutrition improved under general treatment, but the local condition was unchanged. A year later the stricture was slightly increased. Thiosin. was then given, 2 grains, twice daily. The following year the patient was found to be much improved. Examination showed that the scar band had gone, the speculum could be introduced and the mucus membrane was normal in appearance, though not as elastic as a normal rectum should be. W. Spencer applied this property of ***resolving scar tissues in cases of tinnitus aurium “where the ossicles are bound down and the function of the tympanic cavity so much impaired by fibrous bands or adhesions.” In such cases he had encouraging success. Enlarged lymphatic glands have been reduced in the same way. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Sil., Calen., Sinapis and Cruciferae. (2) Uterine tumors, Thlaspi. (3) Diuresis - also chemical. (4) Urea. Lup., Tub. (5) Scars. Sil., Graph., Fl-ac. (6) Affections of rectum, Nit-ac., Graph., Scirr. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Grimmer. Murphy. Phatak.

Abdomen - Flatulence. Internal adhesions after surgery, after hysterectomy, etc. Intestinal strictures.

Rectum - Stricture of rectum.

Female - Painful uterine adhesions, pelvic inflammation. Uterine tumors. Infertility- Food - Increased appetite.

Back - Tom ligaments in the shoulder. Frozen shoulder.

Skin - Wounds that are slow to heal. Wounds that form a lot of scar tissue. Scar tissues. Granulations, scars, keloids after burns, wounds. Inelasticity of the skin. Indurations. Urticaria. Lupus.

Kidneys - Strictures of the urethra and painful urination. Urine increased in quantity, no albumen or formed elements. Increased urination at night. ***Limbs - Locomotor ataxia. Stiffness of joints. Lungs - Accelerated respiration. Emphysema.

full:
PHARMACY - thlaspi. Thlaspi bursa pas- toris. Shepherd’s purse. Bursa pastoris. Capsella bursa pastoris. N. O. Cruciferae. Tincture of fresh flowering plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Colic. Cystitis. Dropsy. Dysentery. Dysuria. Fibroma. Fibroids, uterine. Flatulence. Gallstones. Gonorrhea. Hematuria. Hemorrhages. Kidney, stones. Leucorrhea. Liver, disorders. Metrorrhagia. Miscarriage. Nausea. Nosebleed. Ranula. Strangury. Urethritis. Uric acid, diathesis. Uterine, bleeding. Uterus, cancer. Whitlow.

HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany noted that Thlaspi is “A native of Europe, it has accompanied Europeans in all their migrations and established itself wherever they have settled to until the soil.” It does not refuse to grow in the poorest soils, but it luxuriates in the richest. Burnett noticed that it flourished best in the neighborhood of dunghills and the odor of the tincture is much suggestive thereof. Some have seen in the seed-vessel the signature of the shape of the uterus. Burnett found in it an organ remedy of vast importance. He said the tincture is the best thing to give for menses that have been checked, for uterine hemorrhages he preferred the potencies. Thlaspi bursa pastoris HOMEOPATHIC - Hemorrhagic and uric acid diathesis. Hemorrhages are profuse, periodic, blood dark, clotted. Uterine hemorrhage with cramps and expulsion of clots. Hemorrhage from uterine fibroid with aching in back or general bruised soreness. Bleeding fibroids. Bleeding between the menses. Tendencies to miscarriage. Bleeding at ovulation or postpartum hemorrhage of dark, red, oozing blood (Ham.). Passive bleeding. Hemorrhage with burning or a mild bladder problem. Uterine hemorrhages concomitant with bladder infections. Albuminuria during pregnancy. Kidney and bladder irritation. Kidney stone formation (Sars., Lyc.). Chronic cystitis. Craves buttermilk. The toes are affected along with cramping pain in stomach. Chronic neuralgia. Aching between scapulae. MIND - Impulse to walk far. Restless, goes from room to room. Agony because of pains. Spells of causeless weeping. Stupefied and dull, as if she had not slept enough.

Head - Headache, with great fullness. Frontal pain, worse toward evening. Pain from above eyes up over head to nape. Scaly eruption behind ears. Sharp pain over right eye, drawing eye upwards, behind right eye. Heaviness over eyes. Pressing pain in forehead. Stupefying pressing pain in forehead. Violent headache, lasting all night.

Eyes - Eyes puffy. Dusky eyes, shiny and with dilated pupils. Dull ache behind eyes on awaking in the morning with aching in nape. Blurred vision. Sensation as if eyes are swollen, as if the ball was pressed inward. Sensation as of dust in eyes, worse after sewing or using eyes.

Ears - Deafness and pain in left ear. Sensation as if something pushing in right ear. Spasmodic drawing from right ear to right lower jaw. Dry eruptions behind the ears. Small vesicles, with yellow points, above right ear. Scaly eruptions behind ears, with fissures in the fold. Sensation as of an insect entering the left ear, making buzzing noise, relieved by boring in ear with fingers.

Nose - Dull pain at root of nose. Gnawing pain in nasal bones. Soreness in nose, with tenderness on touch. Dryness of nose, preceded by sensations of bleeding. Bruised feeling each side of bridge, with bleeding from nose. Frequent nosebleeds. Nosebleed after nasal operations. Especially passive hemorrhage. Free discharge of blood and mucus from left nostril.

Face - Eyes and face puffy. Face feels parched and dry. Miserable countenance.

Mouth - Bitter, slimy taste with dryness of mouth. Taste like bad eggs. Scratchy feeling in the palate. Mouth feels raw, as if from smoking strong tobacco. Mouth cracked in right corner and sore. Upper lip cracked. Teeth sore on closing jaws. Gums sore, neuralgic feeling in teeth.

Throat - Hoarse in morning with slight sore throat. Soreness of upper part of throat. Swelling of throat and face, worse left side. Tonsils swollen. Dry throat on swallowing. Dryness of fauces, with sensation of con- striction of the throat. Dry sensation and scraping. Violent sore throat. Sensation as if the throat was laced together.

Stomach - Sick, faint feeling in stomach. Emptiness feeling in stomach. Cramping pain in stomach, toes hurt as well as stomach. Flatulence. Sour rising like heartburn. Attacks of nausea. Nausea so severe, could hardly raise head from pillow. Tobacco smoke, of which she was fond, now nauseates her. Nausea in the forenoon. Nausea with loathing of food. Vomited brown, sourish blood in the afternoon. Vomiting and purging, with great debility.

Abdomen - Flatulence. Pain between end of sternum and umbilicus like needles or an electric shock. Cramping pain, better bending over. Bloated after eating, with loud emissions of flatus; bowels feel as if drawn down and out.

Rectum - Passage of blood. Diarrhea mushy, brown, dark, urgent, and sometimes with nausea. Diarrhea yellowish color. Constipation. Slow and difficult stool. Obstinate slow stool with severe pressure and urging without effect. Hard, difficult, dry stool, leaving anus sore. Bleeding after hard stool. Troublesome itching and protrusion of hemorrhoids. Sensations - Sensation as of needles or shocks between end of sternum and umbilicus. As if neck and left shoulder would break with pain.

Male - Spermatic cord sensitive to concussion of walking or riding. Stitching in penis, running through to anus. Soreness of prepuce with intense itching or cold sensation (Agar.).

Female - Menses bright red and profuse. Menses too frequent and copious. Every alternate period very profuse. Menstrual blood stains indelibly. Leucorrhea before and after menses, bloody, dark offensive. Leucorrhea stains indelibly, smells foul, excites itching. Scarcely recovers from one period before another begins. Metrorrhagia. Cutting pain from side to side across pubes, worse by standing. Sore pain in uterus on rising. Uterine bleeding with violent uterine colic. Uterine fibroids with cramps and expulsion of clots. Sexual excitement. Food - Aversion to the sight of food. Aversion to potatoes. Craves buttermilk, juicy fruits. Oat cakes are eaten with a relish. Desire for bread and butter, which does not taste good. Nausea better after strawberries.

Chest - Pulsative pain in left chest. Pain, uneasiness, and pressure behind the sternum.

Heart - Feels large and sore, then throb- bings go up into back of neck. Stitching pains at the apex. Palpitations worse in the morning in bed. Palpitation ending with cough. Pain left side of apex.

Back - Continued pain in small of back. Morning backache. Wakes with violent pain between the shoulders. Weakness between scapula. Weakness between shoulders on rising. Breasts - Milky water from right nipple. Shooting pains in right breast. Causations - Suppression of hemorrhages or vaginal discharges.

Limbs - Weariness in lower limbs, can hardly stand. Drawing pain in left thigh like gout. Severe pain and stiffness in right knee cap. Tearing, gouty pains left leg, worse in forenoon. Strained pain in right shoulder. Gouty pain in arm. Tearing, gnawing pain from elbow to throat. Rheumatic pain in left arm and shoulder blade, extending to throat. Hands tremble when holding anything. Swelling of veins of hand and arm. Tearing, wrenching pain in left wrist. Redness around root of nails. Lame feeling in right forefinger. Pain in the periosteum.

Sleep - Restless tossing about. Frequent wakening. Sleeplessness. Sleepy after eating or falls asleep while eating. Confused and unpleasant dreams when asleep.

Skin - Skin dry, hot, even to burning.

Modalities - Better bending over. Better cold bathing, dampness, Better open air, rapid motion. Worse every other month. Worse toward night. Worse suppression of hemorrhages or vaginal discharges.

Tongue - Tongue and palate feel as if scalded. Ranula, caused enlargement of submaxillary duct. Tongue white, coated. Taste like bad eggs. Vertigo - Vertigo with sensation as if drunk. Dizziness in the forehead, like seasickness. Vertigo, worse rising. COMMENTS - “Shepherd’s purse,” said Gerarde, “stayeth bleeding in any part of the body, whether the juice or the decoction thereof be drunk or whether it be used poultice-wise or in both or any way else. In a clyster it cureth the bloody flux, it healeth green and bleeding wounds, it is marvelous good for inflammations new beginning and for all diseases which must be checked back and cooled.” Gerarde added that the decoction will stop diarrhea, blood-spitting, hematuria and all other fluxes of blood. Burnett noted it for the effects of suppressed uterine disease. Burnett observed it cause sexual excitement like Canth. It aided him in the cure of an inveterate case of gallstones, the origin of which he traced to the uterus. Dudgeon reported the case of a woman who had recovered from jaundice. She then had a peculiar discharge after the menses flux of a brownish-green blood which was attended with obscure abdominal pains. The cervix uterus was swollen and soft but not ulcerated. Dudgeon failed to cure this, but Rafin- esque of Paris, after trying other remedies, succeeded with Thlaspi. 6c, which had an immediate positive effect. Rafinesque then gave the tincture, and then again the 6c, and in a few weeks the cure was complete. Dudgeon, in an article on Thlaspi., quoted a case of Rademacher’s showing the action of Thlaspi. on uric acid excretion. A woman whom Rademacher had relieved ten years before of a large quantity of urinary sand, again presented herself; her abdominal cavity was full of water, extremely swollen and she was passing urine of a light red color with bloody sediment. Thlaspi. tincture, 30 drops five times a day, was given solely with the idea of stopping the hematuria. The result was a more copious discharge of urinary sand than ever before, the urine increased, the dropsy disappeared and the woman was cured. Dudgeon's own cases are no less striking. One such case concerned a woman, 76, who had rheumatic muscular pains in various parts and an abundant secretion of uric acid, which passed away with every discharge of urine. Sometimes small stones formed and there was much pain in their passage along the ureter, but generally it passed in the form of coarse sand, which formed a thick layer at the bottom of the utensil. This sand continued to pass after the cessation of the rheumatic pains, which lasted six or seven weeks. Puls., Pic-ac., and Lyc. had no effect. Thlaspi. 1c diminished the sand to an insignificant amount. Dudgeon also noted the case of a man, 57, who, in addition to other dyspeptic symptoms, had unusually large discharges of coarse uric acid, coming away in masses as large as a big pin ’ s head but without pain. Thlaspi lx stopped this. He also recorded the case of a woman, nearly 80, who suffered from the presence of a calculus in left ureter. She had previously passed much sand. Thlaspi. lx caused a great discharge of sand and a speedy relief of her pain. Dudgeon referred to a case of Harper’s illustrating the action of Thlaspi. on the bowels. An elderly woman had suffered for years from a copious discharge of mucus, pus, sometimes mixed with blood, sometimes nearly all blood, which passed from the bowels after each evacuation. She had been under high homeopathy, oxygen treatment and for a long time under Harper’s care, all without effect. He then gave Thlaspi. tincture in 5 drop doses and cured the case in a few days. Clarke, with Thlaspi. lx, saved a woman who had been curetted several times with little success from a further curetting, which was advised as being essential to the cure. Thlaspi. stopped the hemorrhages, restored the periods to their proper term and the patient immediately began to recover her strength, which had been drained to the last degree. There was no return of the trouble. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Urt-u., Croc., Trill., Mill. (2) Cruciferae, especially Sinapis. (3) Thiosin. - fibroma, uterine tumors. (4) Matth. - inspissated secretions, grows near sewage stream. (5) Kidney stones, Oci. (6) Uric acid, pain in shoulder, Urt-u. (7) Uterine hemorrhages, Trill., Vib., Ust., Senec. (8) Hemorrhages from bowel, Merc., Nit-ac., Sulph., Caps., Merc-c., Phos. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Liver - Gallstone colic, liver affection being secondary to uterine condition. Lungs - Accumulation of phlegm in lungs. Convulsive cough, relieved as soon as phlegm is loosened. Hemoptysis. Dry cough on lying down with aching under left breast. Cough with irritation behind sternum. Fits of coughing as if the sternum pressed inward.

Kidneys - Chronic cystitis. Kidney colic and stones. Urethritis, urine runs away in little jets. Frequent desire. Urine heavy, phos- phatic. Accumulation of gtave\,brick-dust sediment. Hematuria. Albuminuria during pregnancy. Dysuria and spasmodic reten tion, after forceps delivery. Dysuria in the elderly, with dribbling. Often replaces the use of the catheter.

Perspiration - Sweat profuse at night.

Temperature - Alternate chill and sweat during headache. All night chills, with wakefulness and slight diarrhea with swelling of tonsils. Chill at 9 a.m. or from 7 p.m. to 9 p.m. Chilly when uncovering during fever. Chill worse from going into warm room during fever. Continued fever with quick pulse.

HERBAL - Thuja was introduced to France from Canada during the reign of Francis I, and it now has an honored place in many gardens and shrubbery. HOMEOPATHIC - Thuj. is one of Hahnemann’s discoveries. Most of the remedies of his Materia Medica had been known in a fashion before his time, but practically nothing was known of the therapeutic properties of Thuj. until Hahnemann proved it. COMMENTS - Millspaugh noted that the American Arbor Vitae is a “spiry evergreen attaining a height of from 20 to 50 feet, though generally not above 40 and a diameter of about 10 to 20 feet through the greatest breadth of foliage. It assumes a conical form with such true lines as to appear ‘clipped.’ thus forming one of our most valued high-hedge trees. “It abounds in the northern zones of North America from Pennsylvania northwards. There it “often forms what are commonly known as cedar-swamps. It grows upon the rocky banks of rivers and in low, swampy spots, blossoming from May until June and maturing its fruit in autumn.” Teste remarked that in the period when the doctrine of signatures prevailed, the “Resinous callosities of the stems and leaves of Thuja might have seemed an indication that the plant was the specific for sycosis and warts.” Teste dismissed this idea, but he did ask whether resinous substances that have the power of modifying vegetable juices in a peculiar way may not affect the animal fluids in the same manner. He included Castoreum canadense in his Thuj. group and followed by giving an instance in which it acted on fig-warts. Castoreum canadense is the product of an animal that subsists on the bark of resinous trees. Hering described Thuj.’s action on fluids as “dissolution of fluids of the body, which become acrid, probably caused by Thuja perverting lymphatic secretions, disturbs digestion and sanguification.” He went on to discuss Thuja’s action in the vegetative sphere: “A surplus of producing life, nearly unlimited proliferation of pathological vegetations, condylomata, warty sycotic excrescences, spongy tumors and spongy pock exudates which organize hastily. All morbid manifestations are excessive, but appear quietly, so that the beginning of the diseased state is scarcely know.” Boenninghausen found Thuja both preventive and curative during an epidemic of smallpox. It aborted the disease process and prevented pitting. In veterinary practice, Thuja has proved curative in farcy and in “grease.” These clinical uses point to Thuj.’s affinity to vaccinations. No one has written more forcibly or lucidly on this than Burnett did in his book, Vaccinosis and its Cure by Thuja. “Arbor Vitae: nomen omen,” said Burnett on his title page. In his hands, Thuj. proved to be a tree of life to numberless sufferers from the vaccination miasm. By “vaccinosis” Burnett meant the disease known as vaccinia, the result of vaccination, in addition to “that profound and often long-lasting morbid constitutional state engendered by the vaccine virus.” Thuj. is homeopathic to this state, and therefore curative and preventive of it. Burnett made the observation, which Clarke confirmed, that the vaccination does not need to take in order to produce the vaccination miasm. Many people date their ill health from a so-called unsuccessful vaccination, so vaccinosis may exist apart from vaccinia. The anti-vaccinosis action of Thuj. is part of its anti-sycotic action, therefore vaccinosis is a sycotic disease. Burnett noted the case of an infant, ten weeks old, whom he was called to see as it was supposed to be dying. He found it ghastly white and in collapse. There was Thuja occidentalis nothing to account for this except that the baby had its wet-nurse changed two or three days before. The wet-nurse was questioned and declared herself quite well and looked it, but “her arm was a little painful.” She had been revaccinated in the Marylebone Workhouse the day before she took charge of the patient. Burnett found the vaccine eruption just turning into the pustular stage. He concluded that the infant was sucking in the vaccine poison with its nurse’s milk. He gave Thuj. 6c to both infant and nurse. The baby gradually improved the same day and the next morning, though still pale, was practically well and the vaccine vesicles on the nurse’s arm had withered. Burnett quoted a case of vaccine rash in an infant following the vaccination of its mother, who was nursing it. The effects of chronic vaccinosis are protean. Prominent among them are asthma, neuralgias, skin disorders, indigestion and constipation, warts and new growths of many kinds. Emaciation, brain damage, epilepsy and blindness. Hyperactivity, attention deficit disorder and autism. In these effects, a favorite method of Burnett’s was to give a course of twenty- four numbered powders, only three or four of them medicated with Thuj. 30c, one to be taken at bedtime. With the same prescription, he cured many cases of paralysis; his indications included paralysis of left side of body, very chilly, worse in morning, in wet weather and in cold. Burnett also found enlargements of the spleen to dissolve with these indications. The first case Clarke treated homeopathically was one involving new growths. There was a cluster of small warts on the forehead of a boy that had lasted eighteen months, following a cat’s scratch. Thuj. in small doses and tincture painted on permanently cured in three weeks. A gentleman, about 50, consulted Clarke about a wart on the right side of his head. He was then bald and the wart developed in the same locality soon after and has since remained. The patient had been twice vaccinated. Clarke gave him Thuj. 30c, twenty-eight powders, one in seven medicated, one at bedtime. In one month there was much reduction, Thuj. was repeated and in little over two months the wart was goift. Burnett suggested Thuj. for fatty tumors, which he regards as sycotic in nature. Thuja not only produces symptoms of the secondary stage of gonorrheal and vaccine affections, it also produces urethritis and a variolous eruption. This lasted an hour or more. Asked if they wanted to urinate they would refuse to answer, strike at attendant, or even say “No.” Finally it was found that if they were taken up and put on the closet they would urinate and then go to sleep readily. Worse at 3 a.m. and 3 p.m. Worse periodically, yearly. Worse touch, stretching. Worse after breakfast, after eating, chewing. Worse during menses. Worse urinating, sex. Worse after gonorrhea, after vaccinations, after suppressed warts.

Teeth - Very sensitive teeth. Gnawing, in teeth, worse cold. Toothache before and after menses. Toothache on blowing nose. Teeth crumble, turn yellow. Teeth decay next to gums. Gums retracted. Gums swollen, inflamed, dark red. Pyorrhea alveolaris.

Tongue - Tip of tongue very painful. Tongue as if it has been burnt. White blisters on side close to root,painfully sore. Ranula, varicose veins on tongue and mouth. Frequently bites tongue, from swelling of tongue. Tongue swollen, worse right side. Ranula. Varicose veins on tongue and mouth.

Kidneys - Nephritis with swollen feet. Pains from left kidney to epigastrium, worse motion. Lithemia. Diabetes mel- litus. Cutting, squeezing in bladder and urethra. Urethra swollen, inflamed. Forward cutting in urethra on urinating. Desire sudden and urgent, but cannot be controlled. Frequent urination, with profuse flow, with pain in other parts. Urine burns, dribbles, foul, foamy. Sensation of trickling after urinating, as if drop running down urethra. Involuntary urination at night, when coughing.

Bladder - Paralysis of sphincter of bladder. Bladder feels paralyzed, must wait for urination. Violent burning pain in fundus of bladder. Burning in urethra. Urethra swollen, inflamed. Cutting pains after urination (Sars.). Pain and burning felt near neck of bladder. Jerking, voluptuous sensation in fossa navicularis. Sensation as if a drop were running down urethra, after urination. Urinary stream forked and small. Frequent urging to urinate, with profuse flow. Frequent urination at night. Involuntary urination at night. Lithemia. Diabetes mellitus. Breasts - Aching, pressing pains. Drawing pains, with swelling of both breasts. Sensitiveness and heaviness after the menses. Stinging and itching. Breast cysts, lumps and tumors. Indurations in left breast. Retracted nipples. Causations - Suppressed sycosis. Badly treated or suppressed gonorrhea. Syphilis. Vaccinations. Sulphur, mercury. Sunstroke. Sexual excess. Tea, coffee, beer, tobacco. Sweets, fat meat, onions.

Perspiration - Profuse, sour. Sweetish and strong, smelling like honey. Sweat is foul, oily, pungent, sweetish, sometimes garlicky. Staining brownish, yellow. Profuse sweats at night, staining clothes yellow. Profuse sweat on genitals, gushing, worse company. Sweats only on uncoveredparts or all over except head, when sleeping. Cadaverous exhalation of skin. Profuse, oily sweats, after asthmatic attacks.

Temperature - Chilly from least change of weather. Shaking chill with yawning, worse urinating, not better by heat. Chill, beginning in thighs. Chill without thirst. Coldness of one side. General coldness during menses. Shivering from slightest uncovering in warm air. Heat rises into chest with icy told hands, nosebleed or cough. Orgasm of blood in the evening with throbbing in the blood vessels. Intermittent fever with chronic gonorrheal contamination.

full:
PHARMACY - Thymol. Thymolum. Thyme camphor. A phenol from the essences of many Labiatae, Lamiaceae or some Um- belliferae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Adenoma. Colitis. Diarrhea. Dyspnea. Enterocolitis. Fainting tendency. Hookworms. Laryngitis. Leucorrhea. Migraines. Neurasthenia. Sexual weakness. Whooping cough.

HERBAL - Thymol exists in the essences of certain plants belonging to the Labi atae family or to the Umbellifers. It is a phenol made up of para-isopropyl-metacresol. Thymol can be extracted from them by combining with alkaline lye (soda or potash). It is used therapeutically as an intestinal anti-septic and as vermifuge against tapeworm.

HOMEOPATHIC - The proving was conducted by Griggs, on eight pro vers, six males and two females, as well as one control using a placebo, in 1940-41. The experiment began by using 3x for two weeks, 2x for the next two weeks and lx for about ten days. The provings show an action limited to the sexual organs, producing a typical sexual neurasthenia. Thymol’s general action is on the stomach, genital organs and to a small extent, on the central nervous system. Genito urinary diseases. Pathological emissions, priapism and prostatorrhea. Nightly seminal discharge.

Head - Headache with sadness. Constricting pain in the temples, in women, ameliorated when lying down or from external heat. Bilateral temporal headache and at the occiput. Menstrual migraines.

Ears - Noises in the ears. Buzzing in the ears. Sound like bells. Temporary deafness.

Mouth - Salivation reduced when eating. Watery salivation with nausea. Ptyalism. Nauseating belchings.

Throat - Spasmodic laryngitis. Irritation of the larynx and trachea. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Carb-tcl. (2) Canth. - Irritation and inflammation of the digestive, urinary and cutaneous mucus membranes. Intense burning in the digestive passages with frequent, compelling need to urinate. (3) Merc-c. - Burning pains in the pharynx, painful, frequent urination, urine comes drop by drop, diarrhea with tenesmus. (4) Ter. - Irritation of the digestive and urinary mucus membranes with tendency to hemorrhage. REFERENCES - Julian.

Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Glairy belching with sensation of burning in the stomach, nausea and gastric heaviness. Nausea, ameliorated by eating. Vomiting.

Abdomen - Enterocolitis.

Rectum - Hookworms. Diarrhea after constipation. Glairy or membranous diarrhea. Anal pain following diarrhea. Mucous, membranous stools, gray in color.

Male - Increased sexual desire. Priapism. Seminal discharge when going to stool. Nightly seminal discharge. Profuse, nightly, seminal emissions with lascivious dreams of a perverted character. Ejaculation with erotic dreams. Prostatitis. Adenoma of the prostate gland. Cancer of the prostate.

Female - Brown, blood-streaked, evilsmelling, watery leucorrhea. Menses thick, scanty, drawn-out. Pains before and during menses in the ovaries and uterus. Pain from hypogastric heaviness. Metritis of the cervix. Cancer of the uterus or cervix.

Back - Tired, aching throughout lumbar region. Worse mental and physical labor. Back pain during the headaches. Pain in the lumbar and sacral regions, spreading to the buttocks.

Limbs - Cyanosed limbs. Numbness at the limbs. Chronic lumbar rheumatism. Lungs - Dyspnea. Irritating laryngeal and tracheal cough. Whooping cough.

Sleep - Awakes tired and unrefreshed. Lascivious and fantastic dreams. Erotic dreams.

Skin - Skin blue and cold. Scarlet fever-like or pustulous exanthema.

Modalities - Better from eating. Worse mental and physical labor. Worse from tobacco.

Kidneys - Pains in the kidneys, spreading to the buttocks. Retention of urine. Frequent urination with urging. Increased urination at night. Urinary burning and subsequent dribbling of urine. Urine copious, proteinuria, hematuria. Urates increased; phosphates decreased.

Blood - streaked leucorrhea. Glairy or membranous diarrhea. Hookworm disease (Chen-a.). General weakness with headaches. Constricting headache. Skin blue, cold. Spasmodic laryngeal cough. Excessive salivation with nausea. Frequent urination with compelling urging. Pains in the dorsal and lumbar region, spreading to the buttocks. MIND - Irritable, arbitrary, must have his own way. Uneasy feeling and agitation. Nervous agitation, loquacity, mental confusion. Bewildered state. Craves company. Morose, sad, uneasy. Energy gone.

Pulse - Pulse weak, slow or rapid.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Respiratory, infections. Whooping cough.

HERBAL - Thymus serpyllum belongs to the mint family; all the members have a…
full:
PHARMACY - thymu. Thymus serpyllum. Wild thyme. N. O. Labiatae. Tincture of the whole plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Respiratory, infections. Whooping cough.

HERBAL - Thymus serpyllum belongs to the mint family; all the members have a marked action on the urinary organs and especially on the elimination of uric acid. It contains a volatile oil thymol, tannin, a gum and woody fiber. Thymol is a very powerful germicide, killing the germs of typhoid fever in thirty minutes.

HOMEOPATHIC - Respiratory infections of children, dry nervous asthma, whooping cough, severe spasms but little sputum. Ringing in ears with feeling of pressure in head. Burning in pharynx, sore throat worse empty swallowing, blood vessels distended, dark. COMMENTS - Small doses of Thymu. act as a sedative and contra-stimulant, the depressive action being preceded by a period of excitation. Large doses dull the nerves and produce motor incoordination and sleep. Animals poisoned by Thymu. sleep standing and are insensible to the prick of a pin. They have muscular contraction and tremors, vertigo and turning movements. Increase of diarrhea, vomiting appears, prostration is extreme, the skin becomes cold and death sets in with all the symptoms of a depressant position and with complete anesthesia. These final symptoms are due to the thymic acid, which is a camphor. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke.

name: Thyroidinum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better after or during menses. Better evening, rest, lying on abdomen or reclining position. Worse in women, before and during menses. Worse least exertion, stooping. Worse cold. Heart worse lying down..
constitution: Emaciation. Dyspnea. Glycosuria. Goiter. Hoarseness. Obesity. Thyroid, disorders. Thyroid, nodules. Urine, increased. Weight, loss.
keynote:
PHARMACY - thyr. Thyroidinum. Thyroid gland extract. Thyreoidinum. Thyroidea. Glándula thyreoidea. Thyroidin. A sarcode. Trituration of the fresh or dried thyroid gland of sheep or calf. Potencies of a liquid extract of the gland. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL -…
full:
PHARMACY - thyr. Thyroidinum. Thyroid gland extract. Thyreoidinum. Thyroidea. Glándula thyreoidea. Thyroidin. A sarcode. Trituration of the fresh or dried thyroid gland of sheep or calf. Potencies of a liquid extract of the gland. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Emaciation. Dyspnea. Glycosuria. Goiter. Hoarseness. Obesity. Thyroid, disorders. Thyroid, nodules. Urine, increased. Weight, loss.

HOMEOPATHIC - Thyroiodine is now more generally named lodothyrine, but Clarke retained the former as more convenient. Hoenigschmied said of it that it is present in only small quantities in the thyroid of sheep. It is completely free from albuminous substances, stable and directly assimilated. The general effects of the drug are increased secretion of urine and corresponding loss of flesh. Thyri. is the active principle isolated form thyroid gland, a substance rich in Iodine and nitrogen, affects metabolism, reducing weight, may produce glycosuria. It should be used cautiously in obesity, for a fatty heart may not be able to maintain the accelerated metabolic rhythm. Milk contains the internal secretion of the thyroid. COMMENTS - Hoenigschmied gave some cases, including that of a laborer, 42, for several years had enlargement and induration of all lobes of thyroid, the enlargement caused compression of the structures of the neck, dyspnea, whistling respiration, hoarseness, short, dry cough, vertigo. Thyri. was given, 5-grain tablets, one every evening, at the end of a week twice daily. After using twenty-five tablets, the gland was smaller and softer, the previously hard and resistant nodules were elastic after two more weeks only remnants of the goiter remained. Another case, that of a man, 60, thyroid enlarged in all its lobes with a glandular cystic swelling in the right one, dyspnea, loud whistling breathing. Two, three and at last four tablets were given daily for two months, by which time the goiter had vanished, but the cyst was not changed. A man, 45, medium height, sedentary, suffered from obesity, vertigo, dyspnea, weariness. Pulse feeble, 76, functions normal, appetite and sleep good, weight 230 pounds. With increasing doses of Thyri., up to ten tablets daily the weight steadily went down to 160 pounds, activity increasing in proportion. When the dose had reached four tablets daily the urine became very abundant, but was free from albumen. The daily dose was Thyroiodinum increased one tablet every four days. REFERENCES – Clarke

Head - Feeling of lightness in brain. Fullness and heat. Persistent frontal headache, heaviness over eyes. Headaches ameliorated after menses. Heavy throbbing headache worse in the frontal region, worse from concentrating the mind, better out of doors, worse using the eyes. Fullness in the head with throbbing of the temporal arteries, worse morning and afternoon, from motion, physical or mental, from heat or indoors, better in cool fresh air, often better from external pressure. Falling of hair.

Eyes - Progressive loss of sight with central scotoma (Carbn-s.). Conjunctivitis and chemosis, itching with weeping. Stinging pain in the right eye. Eyeballs prominent. Exophthalmic goiter. Irritation of the eyelids.

Ears - Sclerosis of ossicles. Difficult hearing. Pain on the right side. Pain in the left ear lobe.

Nose - Dry mucus membrane indoors, fluent coryza, profuse, watery and bland outdoors. Dryness and sticking pain in posterior nares, worse on swallowing. Rhinitis with sneezing and edema of the nasal mucus membranes. Pain in the sinuses. Tickling sensation with headaches and dry throat.

Face - Flushed. Dry, red lips, burn with free desquamation. Eruption of acne, worse on the right cheek. Sensation of something heavy, which falls from the cheeks.

Mouth - Dryness of mouth. Bad taste, metallic, bitter and sour. Tongue, metallic taste at tip. Tongue coated grayish white in center with red edges or tip. Papillae enlarged and prominent. Tongue thickly coated. Swelling of the upper lip.

Throat - Dry larynx, congested, raw, burning, worse on left side. As of a splinter stuck across the throat. Pharynx congested, red and dry, with rawness and burning. Vertigo - Vertigo, in the morning on rising, on leaning forwards. COMMENTS - Thyr. has a profound action on the heart. Fatal syncope occurred in a number of cases under “thyroid feeding.” Cyanosis was produced in many cases. Burnett gave a patient 3x, producing severe angina pectoris. The connection between the heart and the thyroid gland is very close, as seen in cases of exophthalmic goiter, of which many cases have been cured. In a case of valvular heart disease following rheumatism in a man, 24, Thyr. 3x, thrice daily, quickly relieved a squeezing pain at the heart with inability to lie down, and hastened the patient’s recovery. Dr. F.C. Skinner cured a case of dysmenorrhea in a goiter subject with Thyr. 1,000c. In myxedema, cachexia, cretinism and similar conditions, the thyroid gland is absent or defective and the idea is to supply a physiological want. As such, a state of puffiness and obesity may be regarded as a keynote indication for Thyr. Clarke gave Thyr. 3x to a living skeleton of a child, 5, who looked not older than 2. He had been kept in a box in a cellar all his life until brought into the hospital, when he weighted only 14.25 pounds. Under Bac. 200c and careful feeding he gained .25 pounds per week. When Clarke commenced Thyr. he put on weekly .75 pound and gained the use of his legs, being able to stand by holding on to a chair. In a case of universal and very aggravated psoriasis in a schoolboy, fair, very chilly, cold, clammy hands and feet, Thyr. 3x and later 30c completely cured after a prolonged course. An obese lady, age 60, developed diabetes. Clarke cured her completely with Thyr. 3x and 30c. She then could take any kind of food. H. O. Nicholson related a case of toxemia of pregnancy in a woman, 32, during her third pregnancy. She had a fit on October 3. Thyroid feeding was begun the next day. Marked improvement followed. Edema of face and body diminished. On October 23, the patient was about her usual duties. On November 6, she was delivered of a healthy boy without any untoward symptoms. Pityriasis rubra, intense redness and scales of legs, and also with intense itching. Ichthyosis, syphilitic eruptions and scleroderma. Acromegaly. Myxedema with hair loss. Increases the flow of milk in nursing women when the flow has been deficient. Insanity, puerperal insanity with fever. Paranoia that they are being pursued or persecuted. Nightmares. Optic neuritis and accommodative asthenopia. Exophthalmic goiter, with bulging eyes. Weak heart, valvular problems, shortness of breath. Tachycardia. Operative and idiopathic tetany, worse from spasms by cold. Stitching, aching or heavy pains. Tingling sensations. Thyr. has poor nutritional development in children. Low thyroid function, with skin problems. It can stimulate function of thyroid gland, or decrease the need for thyroid medications. Thyroid treatment nearly always raises the body heat. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Spong., Calc., Fuc., Lycps. (2) Thyri. (3) Thym-gl. extract - arthritis deformans, metabolic osteoarthritis, 5 grain tablets 3 times daily. High potencies very effective cases of exophthalmic goiter. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak. ***THYROIODINUM (lodothyrinum) PHARMACY - thyri. Thyroiodinum. lodothyrinum. The iodine exists in organic combination and Thyr. contains 0.003 parts of iodine to every gram. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

Stomach - Increased appetite. Thirst for cold water. Pains, tenderness, aggravated by eating, ameliorated in the evening. Dyspepsia before menses. Flatulence, much flatus in abdomen. Nausea, worse riding in a car, better in cool air. Vomiting of pregnancy.

Abdomen - Bearing and aching down through pelvis into anterior thigh. Acute cramping pains with cold sweating. Pain after eating. Pain midway between umbilicus and either anterior superior iliac spine. Sharp, cutting, colicky pains with fullness, worse on pressure and walking, better bending forward and after passage of flatus. Large quantities of flatus passed from bowels often smelling of hydrogen sulphate. Rolling flatulence with gurgling, then loose, gassy stool.

Rectum - Stools dark, fragmented with cadaverous or sulphurous smell. Stools soft, watery.

Female - Amenorrhea in young girls. Pelvic congestion ameliorated by menses. Amelioration of premenstrual discomforts by the menses. Menses often too early. Metrorrhagia. Endometriosis. Gnawing in the uterus. Uterine fibroids. Vomiting of pregnancy. Puerperal, convulsions insanity. Tendency tomiscarriage or premature birth. Puerperal psychosis. Uterine atony after giving birth. Sterility. Food - Insatiable appetite, always wants something more interesting to eat. Desire for sweets and thirst for cold water. Aversion to greasy foods.

Chest - Angina pectoris. Anxiety about chest. Chest feels as if constricted. Constitutions - Suited to the phosphoric or carbonic types, generally hyperthyroids. Nervous temperament. Psoric, tubercular and sycotic range of dispositions.

Heart - Ready excitability of heart. Heart’s action weak with numbness of fingers. Tachycardia (Naja.). Palpitations, worse least exertion, hammering, beats felt in ear. Heart pains radiate into axilla. Clutching, constricting pains, worse lying down, causing short breath. Severe heart pains. Angina pectoris. Hypertrophy after hard labor. As if blood were rushing downwards, through the body. Jumping sensation at heart. Large veins on arms and hands. Valvular diseases of heart (Naja). Weak, frequentpulse with inability to lie down.

Back - Backache. Breasts - Breasts tumors and cysts. Deficient in breast milk.

Limbs - Rheumatic arthritis with tendency to obesity, coldness and cramps of limbs. Aching pains. Trembling of limbs and entire body. Edema of legs. Numbness, left fingers then right leg. Itching without eruption, worse night. Peeling of skin of lower limbs. Cold limbs. Cold, clammy hands. Left hand icy cold. Abnormal growth of limbs due to excessive exertion.

Sleep - Insomnia. Difficulty in falling asleep. Nightmares. Wakes for no reason.

Skin - Eczema. Psoriasis associated with obesity. Very dry skin. Itching without eruption, worse night. Brown swellings. Swelling of glands of stony hardness. Symmetrical serpiginous eruptions. Jaundice with itching, in the newborn child, accompanied by vomiting. Urticaria. Ichthyosis. Lupus. Peeling skin of lower limbs. Scleroderma.

Modalities - Better after or during menses. Better evening, rest, lying on abdomen or reclining position. Worse in women, before and during menses. Worse least exertion, stooping. Worse cold. Heart worse lying down.

Liver - Cutting pain in liver, worse deep breathing. Jaundice with itching, in the newborn child, accompanied by vomiting. Lungs - Breathlessness better lying in recumbent position. Dry, painful cough with scanty, difficult expectoration and burning in pharynx. Cough on entering a warm room from cool air. Asthma. Allergies.

Kidneys - Pressing urge to urinate. Frequent urination during the day. Burning along urethra, increase of uric acid. Increased flow of urine, polyuria, some albumen and sugar. Urine smells of violets. Bedwetting in weakly children who are nervous and irritable. Diabetes mellitus.

Perspiration - Drenching sweats. Oily, musty sweat.

Temperature - Hot flushes, then chills or drenching sweats.

name: Tilia Europea
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better in cool room. Better from motion, walking about in open air. Better closing eyes. Better from coffee. Worse talking, walking, stooping, sneezing. Worse in afternoon and evening. Worse cold water, drafts. Worse from sweating, warm room, heat of bed, after sleep. Skin symptoms worse heat of bed..
constitution: Bedwetting. Dentition. Hemorrhages. Leucorrhea. Lichen. Neuralgias. Nosebleeds. Peritonitis. Puerperal, metritis. Rheumatism. Toothache. Urticaria. Uterus, prolapsed.
keynote:
PHARMACY - til. Tilia europea. Common Lime. Linden. Tilia cordata. Tilia sylvestris. N. O. Tiliacae. Tincture of fresh blossoms. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bedwetting. Dentition. Hemorrhages. Leucorrhea. Lichen. Neuralgias. Nosebleeds. Peritonitis.…
full:
PHARMACY - til. Tilia europea. Common Lime. Linden. Tilia cordata. Tilia sylvestris. N. O. Tiliacae. Tincture of fresh blossoms. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bedwetting. Dentition. Hemorrhages. Leucorrhea. Lichen. Neuralgias. Nosebleeds. Peritonitis. Puerperal, metritis. Rheumatism. Toothache. Urticaria. Uterus, prolapsed.

HERBAL - The sap of the linden contains sugar, and the flowers an abundance of honey, which makes the tree particularly attractive to bees.

HOMEOPATHIC - A tincture of the fresh blossoms was proved by the Austrian Society. The most striking characteristic is “an intense sore feeling about the abdomen and profuse warm sweat which gives no relief.” This led to its successful use in cases of peritonitis. In addition to this are marked bearingdown symptoms in the whole genito-urinary and rectal regions, especially in the uterus and these combined with the others have indicated Til. in puerperal metritis and other disorders of the female generative sphere. Til. is of value in muscular weakness of the eye. Hemorrhages of thin, pale blood. Puerperal metritis. Disease of the antrum (Hydr., Chel.). Intense soreness of the abdomen, uterus. Bearing or dragging down pains in genito-urinary and rectal region. Bed feels too hard. Edema. Neuralgia. Rheumatism. The more he sweats the greater the pain. MIND - Love-sick. Dread of society. Melancholy, disposed to weep. Irritable. Disinclined to work.

Head - Neuralgias, first right, then left side, with veil before eyes. Confusion with dimness of vision. Much sneezing with fluent coryza. Bleeding from nose.

Eyes - Binocular vision imperfect. Sensation as of gauze or a veil before eyes (Calc., Caust., Nat-m.). As if a piece of cold iron pressed through right eye causing burning.

Ears - Stinging in ears.

Nose - Tickling of nose. Much sneezing with fluent coryza. Nosebleeds, blood thin and pale, but coagulates quickly.

Face - Face pale, or flushed, frequent alternations. Cutting pains. Sensation of something alive under skin of face. Quivering of lips. Sprained pain in left jaw-point.

Mouth - Much mucus in mouth, causing fuzzy feeling, affecting speech. Taste bitter, bitter-slimy, pasty. Stinging pain in all the teeth, worse by cold water. Drawing pains in gums.

Throat - Burning in throat. Sensation of swelling of the palate, with desire to swallow, and hoarse voice. Tickling in palate causing cough. Vertigo - Vertigo, with staggering, and like gauze before the eyes. Intoxication. COMMENTS - An intense facial neuralgia was developed in the proving and also a very aggravated condition of skin irritation with pimples of the lichen order. Pains above the root of the nose, nosebleed of thin, pale blood which coagulated quickly. The left side was most affected. Great sensitiveness to draft of air was induced. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Lil-t., Bell. (2) Puerperal metritis, Bell. (3) Uterine bearing down, Lil-t. (4) Sweat without improvement. Merc. REFERENCES - Buericke. Clarke. Phatak.

Abdomen - Bloated abdomen, pains as from incarcerated flatulence, repeated noisy discharges of it, which aggravates. Peritonitis. Soreness with warm sweat which gives no relief.

Female - Intense sorefeeling about uterus. Bearing-down pains with hot sweat, but without relief. Soreness and redness of external genitals (Thuj., Sulph.). Pelvic inflammation, tympanites, abdominal tenderness and hot sweat which does not relieve. Much slimy leucorrhea when walking (Bov., Carb-an., Graph.). Puerperal metritis.

Chest - Oppression. Whole chest weak, acute pressure and pinching under sternum. Throbs as from a dull stitch from thorax to back. Bruised pain and swelling. Tearing from left pectoralis major to axilla.

Back - Tearing from nape to top of shoulder. Stitching, drawing, and heat in right back between liver and kidneys. Heaviness in sacral and dorsal region.

Limbs - Trembling, weariness, bruised feeling in limbs. Paralytic heaviness of arms, especially upper arm. Heaviness and painful lameness in left shoulder. Drawing in small spot left hip while sitting. Cramp in left sole. Ulcerative pain in ball of left great toe. Lungs - Cough from tickling in throat. Tickling, scraping, irritating, provoking slight cough, especially in left side of larynx. Fine stitches in larynx, worse talking. Hoarseness. Frequent sighing.

Sleep - Yawning, sleepy, exhausted, worse during pain. Sleeplessness with restlessness, Bed seems too hard. Vivid frightful dreams, bathed in perspiration. Sudden wakings.

Skin - Urticaria. Eruption of small, red itching pimples. Violent itching and burning like fire after scratching.

Modalities - Better in cool room. Better from motion, walking about in open air. Better closing eyes. Better from coffee. Worse talking, walking, stooping, sneezing. Worse in afternoon and evening. Worse cold water, drafts. Worse from sweating, warm room, heat of bed, after sleep. Skin symptoms worse heat of bed.

Kidneys - Heavy dragging pain in urethra. Constant painful pressure on bladder and urethra. Frequent, copious urination. Scanty urine.

Perspiration - Sweat warm and profuse soon after falling asleep. Sweat increases as rheumatic pains increase. Sensations - As if a piece of cold iron pierced through right eye, causing burning. Burning as if a piece of ice were drawn over ear and face. As if something living were under skin of face. Tearing in anterior muscles of thigh, as if they were too short.

Temperature - Profuse warm sweat, soon after falling asleep without relief.

name: Tillandsia Usneoides
author: Murphy
constitution: Blood, sugar. Breast, milk. Childbirth. Diabetes. Epilepsy. Hemorrhages. Rheumatism.
keynote:
PHARMACY - till-u. Tillandsia usneoides. Spanish moss. Tree hair. Old mans beard. Florida moss. N. O. Bromeliaceae (Brome- liad or Pineapple family). Historical dose: Tincmre and all potencies potencies.

CLINICAL - Blood, sugar. Breast, milk. Childbirth. Diabetes. Epilepsy.…
full:
PHARMACY - till-u. Tillandsia usneoides. Spanish moss. Tree hair. Old mans beard. Florida moss. N. O. Bromeliaceae (Brome- liad or Pineapple family). Historical dose: Tincmre and all potencies potencies.

CLINICAL - Blood, sugar. Breast, milk. Childbirth. Diabetes. Epilepsy. Hemorrhages. Rheumatism.

HERBAL - Tillandsia is usually an epiphytic plant with reduced to absent stems. Found mostly in tropical to temperate Americas. Hangs in the trees and swamps of the southeast coastal plains. Many Native American tribes used the moss while cooking to absorb unwanted liquids, for bedding, for tanning hides, and to rub on newborn babies heads for curly hair. It is also used as fodder for animals. Colonial pickers harvested moss with long poles during the winter. The harvest hung for several months to cure in a moss yard. Curing loosened the outer gray scales making it ready for commercial ginning. Medicinal use of Spanish moss has a long history. Extracts from it have been used in the treatment of diabetes and it has been used to help control blood sugar levels. Spanish moss was taken, while green, and brewed into tea for expectant mothers, supposedly to aid the flow of breast milk and make the delivery easier. Tea from the plant was also used as a folk remedy for rheumatism. In Mexico, it has been used to treat infantile epilepsy. In the early 1950s. it was used as an estrogen substitute and scientists have found the plant exhibits anti-bacterial properties. In the West Indies it has been used to make a styptic ointment for the purpose of stopping bleeding. COMMENTS - Dr. C. W Mayo reported that, in the Feb. 9, 1944 “Staff Meetings of the Mayo Clinic,” the absorptive qualities of Spanish Moss for use in surgical dressings had been investigated with interesting results. “The dried moss will retain its absorptive power better than a substance like cotton, as the liquid taken up is stored chiefly inside the leaves and cells, instead of merely being held between adjoining strands. Spanish moss will take up from six to ten times its dry weight of water.” REFERENCES - Buttimer. Murphy.

PHARMACY - tinos. Tinospora cordifolia. Gulancha. N. O. Menispermaceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bilious. Cough. Dysuria. Elephantiasis. Fever. Flatulence. Gonorrhea. Hemorrhoids. Impetigo. Intermittent, fever. Jaundice. Malaria. Palpitations. Rheumatism. Skin, disorders. Syphilis. Urticaria. Vomiting. Worms.

HERBAL - The stem and root are used medicinally; they possess a bitter taste. The root and stem contain starchy extract, bitter principle and a trace of berbomic. Fresh stem is more efficacious than the dry one and is a good substitute for Calumbu. The Ayurvedic physicians used it as a febrifuge and named it “Indian quinine.” They have found it to be bitter tonic and strength giving. It destroys wind, bile and phlegm. It is good for thirst, burning sensation, gonorrhea, cough. Useful in enlarged spleen. Secondary syphilis, rheumatism, leprosy, skin diseases such as impetigo. Jaundice, torpidity of the liver, splenic affections. Leprosy, rheumatism. Acute and chronic fevers. Worms, vomiting, hemorrhoids, dysuria, flatulence and palpitations of the heart. As a diuretic and demulcent it is given in dysuria, in scanty, high-colored urine due to catarrh of the bladder. It is stomachic, bitter, tonic, alternative, aphrodisiac, anti-periodic, and demulcent. It is given in dyspepsia and in debility caused by repeated attacks of fever.

HOMEOPATHIC - No proving of Tinos, has been made, but many Indian homeopaths have been using it clinically with excellent results. Debility. Rheumatism. Skin diseases, leprosy, secondary syphilis. Jaundice, torpidity of the liver. Splenic affections. Acidity of urine, urinary diseases such as gonorrhea and dysuria. Intermittent fevers. Acute and chronic malarial fevers, the temperature generally rises in the afternoon with chilliness or shaking chill. Fevers with bilious vomiting associated with thirst and headache. Chronic slow fevers, especially where there is a history of gonorrhea and weakness due to seminal emissions. Fever due to an excessive use or maladministration of quinine. Fever with burning sensation is felt in face, hands and feet, and enlargement of the liver and spleen, jaundice with yellow color of the eyes, no desire for food, and headache. Vomiting, specially bilious vomiting. Decreased quantity of urine, passes it frequently, burning while urinating? The urine is mixed with pus-like discharges. Gonorrhea. Rheumatism, leprosy and skin diseases. Secondary syphilis. Tonic, widely used as a stimulant remedy where the patient has become extremely weak owing to repeated attacks of fever and also to exhausting seminal emissions. COMMENTS - R. N. Khory noted, in the Materia Medica of India, vol. II., that the juice of the Tinospora stem combined with Pakanbhed and honey is given in gonorrhea. The starchy extract is nutritious, largely used in native practice in cold fevers and seminal weakness, also in urinary affections. W. Dymock, in the Pharmacographia Indica, vol. 1. noted that it is favorably spoken of by those who have tried it as a tonic, anti-periodic and diuretic. Charaka recommended it in chronic fevers, jaundice, bilious vomiting and some other diseases. He found it useful to purify the breast-milk after delivery. Baghbhata spoke highly of it as an excellent tonic, and noted that it is generally used in chronic fevers and jaundice. Chakradatta reported that Tinospora is an excellent remedy in urticaria, fevers, leprosy, and elephantiasis. Tinospora cordifolia Bangasena recommended it in vomiting and flatulence associated with extreme palpitations of the heart. “It is useful in general and seminal debility, fever, jaundice, torpidity of the liver, skin diseases, secondary syphilis, rheumatism, acidity of urine and urinary diseases, some forms of dyspepsia, splenic affections, chronic gonorrhea, leucorrhea, etc.” Nadkarni wrote “In malaria Tinospora is sometimes more efficacious than quinine.” R. N. Chopra, in the Indigenous Drugs of India, wrote “An infusion is prepared from the stem and root which is a valuable tonic in debilitating diseases, intermittent fever and dyspepsia.” RELATIONS - Compare: Chin., Chin-ars. REFERENCES - Ghose.

full:
PHARMACY - titan. Titanium metallicum. Titanium metal. Trituration of the copper-red crystals obtained from the slag at the bottom of a blast iron furnace. Consisting of Titan, cyanide and Titan, nitride. Titanium is found in the bones and muscles. Apples contain 0.11 percent of Titan. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Bright’s disease. Eczema. Hemiopia. Lupus. Nasal, catarrh. Premature, ejaculation. Rhinitis. Sexual, weakness.

HOMEOPATHIC - Titanium stands midway between silicon and tin in some of its relations and in other respects it is closely related to iron, chromium and aluminium. The crystals were proved by Sharp who took 2 grains of the first trituration, daily for a week. It was believed to be the pure metal, but was proved later to be the cyanonitrid. Titan, has been used in lupus and tuberculosis processes externally, also in skin diseases, nasal catarrh, etc. Giddiness with verticalhemiopia. Bright’s disease. Eczema, lupus and rhinitis. “Imperfect vision, the peculiarity being that half an object only could be seen. ” Another symptom, which Burnett has turned to good account in cases of sexual Titanium metallicum weakness is “Too early ejaculation of semen during sex.” RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Half-sight, Nat-c., Lyc., Aur., Lith. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

HOMEOPATHIC - Topaz has been said to cure insomnia, asthma, and hemorrhages. Depression, exhaustion, said to increase stamina. Mood swings, worries, fears, anxiety, stress. It was thought to cure cowardice. Insomnia, sleepwalking, nightmares. Restlessness. Stomach, liver and pancreas disorders. Disturbed blood sugar. Indigestion. Diabetes. Tumors. Weak eyesight. Strengthens weak tissue and backbone. Said to be a powerful aphrodisiac and was often used to treat sexual dysfunction. COMMENTS - Topaz occurs not only in the transparent yellow, yellow brown, orangey brown, and pinky brown colors most popularly associated with it, but also in a very light to medium red. In the past, almost any yellow stone was called topaz. Yellow topaz is used for protective purposes, specifically against envy, jealousy, intrigue, disease, death, negativity and lunacy. Mounting in gold is said to enhance these properties; rings, wrist bracelets and necklaces with the stone next to the heart are thought to be the most projective. Topaz was also said to change color in the presence of poisoned food or drink. Its curative powers waxed and waned with the phases of the moon. Supposedly helped to break up stagnation of energy within the body, and elimination of toxins. Powdered and mixed with rosewater, topaz prevented bleeding. Nosebleeds could be stopped by pressing a stone against the side of the nose. It was believed that madness could be cured by a dose of topaz and wine. REFERENCES - Murphy.
