PHARMACY - toxi. Toxicophis pugnax. Moccasin snake. N. O. Ophidia. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Edema. Fever. Periodic neuralgia. Skin, dry. Snake, bites. Toxicophis pugnax

HOMEOPATHIC - Some effects of bites with this snake have been recorded. A peculiar feature of the cases was that the symptoms of pain and fever recurred annually at exactly the same period for many years with decreasing intensity each year. In one case, the pains spread to other parts after some years. The right leg became painful and swollen rapidly. For several years the pain was confined to the knee of the bitten limb, in a few years it left the knee and seized the hip and finally attacked the shoulder. Skin rather dry. Pain and fever recur annually after a bite from this snake (Cedr., Lach.), but without swelling, decreasing in intensity each year. Pains will sometimes change location with disappearance of first symptoms. Unusual dryness of the skin. Edematous swellings and periodical neuralgia. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Hydrophobia.

HERBAL - Ikshugandha is an East Indian remedy useful in urinary affections, especially dysuria, and in debilitated states of the sexual organs, as expressed in seminal weakness, early emissions and infertile semen. The root is demulcent, diuretic, and given in dropsy, gonorrhea, hepatic obstruction, and in urinary affections. A paste of the seeds is applied to rheumatic joints. The seeds are used as an aphrodisiac.

HOMEOPATHIC - The Tribulus plant is full of thorns, which cause intolerable burning, swelling and redness. It produces small red pimples and eruptions which look like meals and eruptions due to prickly heat. Malarial attacks associated with urticaria. Fevers appear in the morning, no chill or thirst, urticaria-like eruptions come on along with the rise of temperature, intense itching which is relieved by cold applications. Sexual neurasthenia. Impotency. Ailments from masturbation, prostate emissions and spermatorrhea. Impotence caused by overindulgence of advancing age or when accompanied by urinary symptoms incon- tinence, painful urination, etc. Prostatitis. Leucorrhea. Gonorrhea. Dropsy. Urinary affections. Urinary calculus. Kidney stones. Hepatic obstruction. Skin diseases, worse from heat and better from cold. Ulcers due to impurities of blood. Rheumatism. Insomnia. COMMENTS - Charaka found it useful in stone, gravel and calculus in the bladder, and strangury. Sushruta recommended it as a great sexual tonic. Bagbhata recommended it for all skin diseases due to impurities of blood. Chakradatta thought that it could be effectively used in dropsy. Bangasena acknowledged its efficacy in effecting safe delivery. Harita recommended it for sleeplessness. He also said that it can produce sound sleep if the root is placed on the head. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Ghose.

full:
PHARMACY - trich-d. Trichosanthes dioica. Wild snakegourd. N. O. Cucurbitaceae. Roots and leaves. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Anasarca. Bilious. Catarrh. Chickenpox. Cholera. Diarrhea. Dropsy. Dysentery. Fever. Headache. Hemoptysis. Jaundice. Kala-azar. Nausea. Rheumatism. Smallpox. Synovitis. Vomiting. Water brash.

HERBAL - The leaves of Trichosanthes dioica are tonic, febrifuge. Fruits of the bitter variety are used in scorpion stings. The fruit is described by Sanskrit writers as febrifuge, laxative and anti-bilious. Ayurvedic physicians of India found this drug to be of great use in multifarious complaints. Charaka found it to be a sovereign remedy in cases of dropsy, anasarca, bilious and catarrhal fevers, slow chronic fevers associated with hemoptysis and also in synovitis. Chakradatta recommended it in bilious and catarrhal fevers and rheumatism. Su- shruta found it efficacious in hemoptysis and bilious fevers. Bhavaprakasha recommended its use in smallpox with predominance of bilious symptoms. In the opinion of some Ayurvedic physicians, it is an excellent remedy in smallpox and chickenpox.

HOMEOPATHIC - The root-bark of Trichosanthes dioica possesses highly purgative properties. It causes purging to such a great extent that a little overdose may cause death. At first the stool appears to be loose, gradually the patient passes bilious and mucous stools, and finally bloody stools and vomiting of blood appear producing the stage of collapse. Useful for diarrhea, dysentery, cholera and cholerine. Copious loose stools, of green or yellow color, may be mixed with bile and mucus. Prolapsed rectum. Burning in anus. Smarting after stool. Passage of involuntary and bloody stool. Bloody stools appear without cessation and cause profound prostration and exhaustion. The stools may be mixed with particles of mucus. Frothy stool, during its passage no pain or uneasiness is felt, after stool, urging and straining continue for a long time. Cholera where there are copious stools and vomiting associated with restlessness, thirst, burning, sweat, extreme weakness, coldness of extremities, pulselessness and other symptoms. Pain and gurgling in stomach. Gurgling with copious yellow stools. Nausea before vomiting, water brash and rumbling in abdomen. Nausea after drinking water. Constant water brash. Vomiting, copious stringy mucus which may be streaked with blood. Vomiting of bile. Jaundice. Yellow eyes, with dropsy. Chronic fevers, with enlargement of the liver and spleen. Fevers with bilious symptoms, with headache, water brash, nausea, and especially bilious diarrhea. Acute, chronic and malarial fevers and also in kala-azar. The fever comes on at 11 a.m. or 12 noon with chilliness, and thirst and headache exist. After this stage headache continues, but it increases with the rise of temperature. The fever may be of short duration one day and of longer duration the next day. Fever with vomiting (Ip.). Trichosanthes bears a close resemblance to Podo, and it may be safely used in those cases where Podo, is indicated or where Podo, fails to do any good. RELATIONS - Compare: Trich-d. may be a grand substitute for Ip. and Podo, or it may be employed where these two medicines fail to do any good. REFERENCES - Ghose.

PHARMACY - trif-p. Trifolium pratense. Red clover. N. O. Papilionoideae. Tincture of flower heads. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bladder, catarrh. Blood, disorders. Cancer. Cough. Crusta, lactea. Diabetes. Dysentery. Fainting. Fibroids, bleeding. Hemorrhages. Hoarseness. Menopause. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Tumors. Whooping cough. Writer’s cramp.

HERBAL - Red clover is an herbal blood tonic and puriher. It has a reputation among herbalists in whooping cough and the coughs of measles and tuberculosis. Felter gave red clover to persons disposed to cancer. He found it retarded the progress of cancerous tumors and improves the general condition of the patient.

HOMEOPATHIC - T. C. Duncan and others proved it and elicited some very decided respiratory symptoms, dry, tickling cough, oppressed breathing with fever. One peculiar symptom was a cough followed by hiccough. Marked salivation. Feeling of fullness with congestion of salivary glands, followed by increased flow of saliva. Crusta lactea, dry, scaly crusts. Stiff neck. Feeling as if mumps were coming on. Preventive for mumps and cancer. Retards progress of cancerous tumors before ulceration has taken place. Cancerous diathesis. MIND - Mental breakdown. Confusion of ideas, morning. Loss of memory.

Head - Confusion and headaches on awaking. Dullness in anterior brain.

Mouth - Increased flow of saliva (Merc., Syph.). Lungs - Hay fever. Coryza like that which precedes hay fever, thin mucus with much irritation. Hoarse and choking, chills with cough at night. Cough on coming into the open air. Spasmodic cough. Whooping cough, paroxysms, worse at night.

Throat - Sore throat with hoarseness. COMMENTS - Trif-p. has many symptoms of congestion. Dull, stupid feeling generally. The head and lungs feel full of blood. Sensation in lungs as if breathing hot air, as if air full of impurities. Persistent headache on waking. Unreffeshing sleep. Weak and intermittent pulse, later full and bounding. Irritation of the pharynx and trachea. “Sharp pain through uvula causing tears to start.” Dryness of trachea causing him to clear throat of some foreign substance. Secretion of urine increased. Farrington noted “Hoarseness and choking spells at night with cough, the neck is stiff, cramps in sternomastoid muscle better by heat and friction.” Cooper said of Trif-p. that it causes salivation in horses and diarrhea if they eat much of it and that it cures mumps and disorders of the pancreas and salivary glands. Hale said it causes “heaves” in horses. Felter noted “scaly and ulcerated conditions of the tibial region of the old.” The symptoms are worse in close room, better in open air. “When I became very warm with the fever my breathing stopped, lungs felt as if breathing hot air.” Worse after sleep. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Trif-r. Complementary: Calc-p. - menstrual andhemorrhagic affections. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Abdomen - Griping pains in abdomen and headache. Colicky pains all day.

Back - Neck stiff, cramp in sterno-cleido muscles, relieved by heat and irritation. Constitutions - Cancer diathesis.

Limbs - Hands and feet cold. Tingling in palms. Tibial ulcers. Lungs - Sensation in lungs as if breathing hot air. Air feels as if full of impurities.

Sensation as if heart would stop with great fear, better sitting up or moving about, worse when alone with cold sweat on face. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Jab., Pilo. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

CLINICAL - Abscesses. Baldness. Beriberi. Boils. Bronchitis. Burns. Cancer. Carbuncles. Cataracts. Cellulitis. Colic. Constipation. Convalescence. Cough. Cysts. Dermatitis. Diabetes. Diarrhea. Eczema. Gout. Hernia. High blood pressure. Hives. Hyperthyroidism. Hypoglycemia. Impotence. Indigestion. Infections. Leg, edema. Leukemia. Lice. Liver disease. Lymphadenitis. Menopausal symptoms. Muscle aches. Peptic ulcer. Rickets. Sores. Spleen, enlargement. Tuberculosis. Ulcers. Vaginal, dryness. Wounds.

HERBAL - Fenugreek is native to southern Europe, the Mediterranean region, and Western Asia. The words foenum - graecum mean Greek hay and arise because of the appearance of the plant which has long slender stems. Fenugreek seeds contain a high percentage of mucilage, a natural gummy substance present in the coatings of many seeds. Although it does not dissolve in water, mucilage forms a thick, gooey mass when exposed to fluids. The resulting soft mass is not absorbed by the body, but instead passes through the intestines and also triggers intestinal muscle contractions. Both actions promote the emptying of intestinal contents. Therefore, fenugreek is a mild but effective laxative. In addition, fenugreek seeds contain chemicals that slow down the time that food takes to go through the intestinal tract. As one result, sugars are absorbed from foods more slowly and blood sugar levels may not rise as high or fluctuate as much as usual. Fenugreek may further affect blood sugar levels by decreasing the activity of an enzyme that is involved in releasing stored sugar from the liver into the blood. Some evidence suggests that fenugreek may also have other medical uses. Fenugreek lowers cholesterol levels as well as blood sugar levels. It may reduce the amounts of calcium oxalate in the kidneys. Calcium oxalate often contributes to kidney stones. Fenugreek also appeared to lessen the chance of developing colon cancer. It may have some ability to protect the liver against damage from alcohol and other chemicals. Fenugreek is a skin softener and is often an ingredient of soothing facial masks. Fenugreek is also used for hair care as it prevents hair fall, cures dandruff, and promotes hair growth. A paste of fenugreek seeds is usually applied to the scalp at least 40 minutes before washing hair to help get rid of dandruff, and act as a remedy for hair loss. The use of shampoo to wash hair can be skipped if fenugreek seed paste is applied on the scalp as the paste helps to remove oil and dirt from the hair and also makes the hair soft. The paste of fresh fenugreek leaves is also used to get rid of dandruff, increase the length of hair, soften the hair, and help preserve its natural color. Paste of the fresh leaves of fenugreek, applied on the face every night before going to bed and washed with warm water, prevents pimples, blackheads, dryness of the face, and early appearance of wrinkles. It improves complexion and leads to younger looking skin. Fenugreek paste made by grinding fenugreek seeds when used as a mask has a granular texture that helps remove blackheads. The topical application of the gelatinous texture of fenugreek seed may also have some benefit for soothing skin that is irritated by eczema or other conditions. Fenugreek helps to remove excess oil from the skin. It has also been applied as a warm poultice to relieve muscle aches and gout pain. A poultice of the leaves can be used for boils, cysts, burns, ulcers, hives, eczema, abscesses, carbuncles, etc. It is also used to treat cuts and sores. Excessive topical use of fenugreek on the same areas may cause itching, redness, rash, or other reactions. Individuals who have allergies to peanuts or soybeans may also be allergic to fenugreek. RELATIONS - Compare: Alf., Avena. REFERENCES - Murphy.

PHARMACY - tril. Trillium pendulum. Lamb’s quarter. White bethroot.Trillium erectum. Purple trillium. Bethroot. Birthroot. Rattlesnake root. Wake Robin. Three-leaved nightshade. N. O. Smilaceae orTrilliaceae of the Liliaceae. Tincture of the fresh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bladder, catarrh. Menopause. Diabetes. Dysentery. Fainting. Fibroids, bleeding. Headache. Hemorrhages. Menorrhagia. Metrorrhagia. Nosebleeds. Writer’s cramp.

HERBAL - The chief uses of Trillium pendulum come to us from herbalists, who learned some of them from the Native Americans. The popular name Birth-root sufficiently ' indicates one part of its reputation.

HOMEOPATHIC - Tril. is a great hemorrhagic medicine. Hemorrhage with great faintness and dizziness. Hemorrhages of all kinds with pregnancy. Hemorrhages after childbirth, menopause, from fibroid tumors, gushing, bright red. Uterine hemorrhage. Threatened miscarriage. Cramp-like pains. Relaxation of pelvic region. Chronic diarrhea of bloody mucus. Tuberculosis with purulent and copious expectoration and spitting of blood. MIND - Irritable .Anguish, agitation and tossing about, impossible to keep still. Repugnance to conversation. Melancholy with sadness.

Head - Dull pain, worse noise, walking, coughing, better bending forward. Pain in forehead, worse noise. Headache worse by least noise, walking, coughing. Confused, eyeballs feel too large.

Eyes - Feel too large and as if would fall out from their sockets. Vision blurred, Trillium pendulum everything looks bluish.

Nose - Profuse nosebleed (Mill., Meli.).

Mouth - Very offensive taste, especially on rising in morning. Greasy feeling on tongue and gums. Bleeding from gums. Bleeding after tooth extraction.

Stomach - Sickness, excessive pain, cramp of stomach. Faintness and sinking at stomach, with heat. Heat and burning stomach rising up in esophagus. Hematemesis.

Abdomen - Swelling of abdomen as in ascites. Much flatulence and grumbling. Constitutions - Suited to women who bleed after every labor pain, flabby subjects.

Rectum - Chronic diarrhea with bloody discharge. Dysentery with passing of almost pure blood. Diarrhea thin, watery, tinged with blood, painless. Constipation succeeded by thin, watery, very offensive diarrhea. Sensations - As if eyes too large. As if a crumb were in larynx. As if the chest was tightly bound and could not be expanded. As if hips and small of back were falling to pieces. As if sacroiliac joint were falling apart, wants to be bound tightly. As if bones were broken. Left side most affected.

Female - Leucorrhea is copious, yellow, and stringy (Hydr., Kali-bi., Sabin.). Menses every two weeks. Uterine hemorrhages with sensation as though hips and back were falling to pieces, better tight bandages. Gushing of bright blood on least movement. Hemorrhage from fibroids (Calc., Thal., Spig., Phos., Ust.). Prolapsed uterus with great bearing-down. Metrorrhagia at menopausal. Lochia suddenly becomes bloody. Profuse long-lasting bloody lochia. Varicose veins of pregnancy. Dribbling of urine after labor.

Heart - Palpitations with great anxiety.

Limbs - Cramping pains in muscles of arms and calves. Lungs - Suffocative attack of irregular breathing with sneezing. Shooting pains through chest. Aching at end of sternum. Cough with spitting of blood. Copious and purulent expectoration. Hemoptysis.

Skin - Skin hot and dry, with itching and burning, worse by scratching.

Modalities - Better by exercise in open air. Better from a tight bandage, bending forward. Worse from motion, sitting erect. Worse menopause. Worse after eating. Motion aggravates the hemorrhages. Standing or walking causes bearing down in pelvis.

Temperature - Feverish during pain in abdomen, on the subsidence of which a profuse perspiration broke out. Vertigo - Vertigo on rising in morning. COMMENTS - Millspaugh considered Tril. erectum as the proper source of the homeopathic tincture. According to Millspaugh, Tril. pendulum is the white variety of Tril. erectum. The Treasury of Botany gave the names as synonymous. The symptoms of H. Minton, the original prover, were given in Allen under Tril. cernuum. Minton’s proving ofTril. cernuumbrought out the hemorrhagic property in the blood tinged diarrhea. Copious hemorrhages, either active or passive, usually bright red and profuse. Hemorrhage, ante-partum and menopausal, fibroid tumors. Hemorrhage, with faintness and sinking at the stomach, also cold limbs and rapid, feeble pulse. “Flooding with fainting.” Hemorrhages with restlessness and exhaustion. Blue vision, craving for ice water. Tendency to putrescence of fluids. Tril. has been used as a local hemostatic in nosebleed and for bleeding after tooth extraction. Minton’s proving brought out “Sensation of emptiness in abdomen.” He also noted extreme debility, palpitation and anxiety. Restless tossing agitation, fear of being sick, and great anguish were experienced by Minton. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Tril-c. - eye symptoms, everything looks bluish, greasy feeling in mouth. (2) Fic. - hemorrhages, menorrhagia, hematuria, nosebleed, hematemesis, bleeding hemorrhoids. (3) Hir., Leech - hemorrhages, bleeding from anus. (4) Ip., Sabin., Lach., Ham. Complementary: Calc-p. (menstrual and hemorrhagic affections). REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - trinit. Trinitrotoluenum. T.N.T. Trotyl. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Anemia. Cramps. Cyanosis. Depression. Dermatitis. Dyspnea. Faintness. Fatigue. Heart, disorders. Hemorrhages. Insomnia. Jaundice. Palpitations. Vertigo. Vesicles.

HOMEOPATHIC - TNT is a high explosive, obtained by nitrating toluene, a product of coal tar distillation. When the skin or hair is exposed to TNT by contact a characteristic yellow or tawny-orange stain is produced, which lasts for some weeks. Indicated in graver forms of anemia (pernicious) and jaundice. Produces fatal toxic jaundice. Symptoms were noted in ammunition workers handling TNT who inhale and ingest it, and also absorb some through the skin. They were compiled by Dr. C. Wesselhoeft and published in the December, 1926 issue of the Journal of the American Institute of Homeopathy. The destructive action of Trinit. on the red blood corpuscles is responsible for the anemia and the jaundice with their secondary symptoms. The hemoglobin is changed so it cannot act satisfactorily as an oxygen carrier and as a result there is breathlessness, dizziness. Headaches, faintness, and palpitations. Undue fatigue, muscle cramps and cyanosis, also drowsiness, depression and insomnia. Later stages of the poisoning produce toxic jaundice and aplastic anemia. The jaundice is the result of cellular destruction in contrast to obstructive jaundice. Faintness, dizziness, mental sluggishness, delirium, convulsion, coma. Face very dark. MIND - Depression. Apathetic and cries easily. Aversion to company. Mental sluggishness, delirium. Food - Aversion to tea. Alcohol aggravates.

Head - Frontal headache and depression.

Nose - Sneezing, coryza.

Stomach - Bitter taste, much thirst, sour regurgitation, dull burning behind the ensiform, nausea, vomiting, constipation followed by diarrhea with cramps. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Zinc., Phos., Cina, Ars., Plum. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Heart - Palpitations, tachycardia and bradycardia. Intermittent pulse.

Skin - Tendency to hemorrhage under the skin and from the nose. Hands stained yellow. Dermatitis, nodular erythema, vesicles, itching and burning, puffiness. Tired pain in back of knees.

Modalities - Worse alcohol, falls after one or two drinks of whisky.

Kidneys - Sudden desire, incontinence and retention. High colored urine, burning on urination. Lungs - Nose dry with stuffed sensation. Burning of trachea, choking weight on chest, dry, convulsive cough, raising mucus plugs.

full:
PHARMACY - trio. Triosteum perfoliatum. Fever-wort. Fever root. Wild coffee. Horsegentian. N. O. Caprifliaceae, Tribe, Lonicereae. Tincture of fresh root. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Adenoma. Angina pectoris. Arteritis. Asthma. Backaches. Biliousness. Blepharitis. Breast pain. Conjunctivitis. Coughs. Cystitis. Dyspepsia. Encephalitis. Erysipelas. Erythema. Fevers. Headache, bilious. Herpes zoster. Infections. Influenza. Joints, stiff. Measles. Menorrhagia. Numbness. Otitis. Ozaena. Pyelonephritis. Rheumatism. Scarlet, fever. Typhoid, fever. Typhus, fever. Urticaria. Vomiting.

HERBAL - The name “fever-wort” tells its traditional reputation. Hale said it is one of the ingredients of the “fever powder” of the herbalists.

HOMEOPATHIC - Trio, is an energetically acting drug and has been proved by Williamson, Neidhard, Gatchell and other experienced provers. The symptoms were established by Raeside on fifteen provers (eight men and seven women) in 1959-60. Raeside used the 8c potency, at the rate of one dose every morning until the symptoms appeared. Trio, is traditionally prescribed as a febrifuge. Above all, it causes vomiting, gastric pains, generalized pains, fever with agitation and insomnia. Talmadge, one of the provers, found it of great value in typhoid and gastric fevers. It produced acute rheumatic symptoms and an intense urticaria. Biliousness. Gallbladder colic. Diarrhea attended with colicky pains and nausea. Numbness of lower limbs after stool. Increased flow of urine. Dryness of the mucus membranes of the lips, mouth and throat. Dry cough. Influenza with aching pains all over with heat in the limbs. Acute encephalitis in infancy, especially after diphtheria, measles, whooping cough. Sudden weariness around 2 a.m. and4 p.m. Sensation of sleeping standing up. Sensation of needles all over the body when hot. Generalized pain in the upper and lower limbs. Nervous symptoms (Coff., Hyos.). Generalized itching, especially on the scalp and limbs of the upper and lower limbs. Erythema, eruption of flat, hard nodules, brown or purple in color, on the joints in the limbs. MIND - Irritated by noise and in the evening. Irritability, difficulty in controlling himself. In the evening, feels in a rage, difficult to control himself. Tends to quarrel bitterly, argumentative. Nervous and sleepy, cannot concentrate. Mental exhaustion. All mental activity requires a great effort. Euphoria, followed by a state of depression. Feels isolated, better when alone.

Head - Occipital pain with nausea on rising, followed by vomiting. Frontal headache. Dull pain, pulsating or pressing, located at the forehead, occiput or temples. Pressing headache at the left temple and occiput and on the right side of the forehead. Stinging, needle-like pain in the left orbital region. Painful tenderness of the scalp and hair when touched.

Eyes - Conjunctivitis. Smarting and hot, painful, especially when closed. Left eye swollen, red and hot. Eyes water, difficult to focus. Blepharitis. Eyelids irritated, especially the right side. Twitching of right eyelid in the evening.

Ears - Otitis. Constant earache in the left ear and discharge. Itching around the ears. Buzzing noises, worse when lying down.

Nose - Spots on the nose. Dryness of the nose and ears. Dull, continual aching behind the root of the nose. Painful rightsided sinusitis and hyperesthesia of the left side of the face. Rhinitis. Ozaena. Sinusitis, spasmodic coryza. Coryza with running nose, thick, green discharge with sneezing. Nosebleed and smell of blood in the nose.

Mouth - Dry mouth and lips. Mouth like parchment, hot with paresthesia of the lips. Fissure on the lower lip, painful ulcerated areas on the mouth, palate and lips. Sensation of a bitter taste, upper teeth painful. Tongue white and seems swollen.

Throat - Painful, irritated, especially at night and on waking. Pharynx red, causing a sensation of constriction. Tickling feeling causes coughing, the left tonsil is painful. Better by drinking cold drinks, even though swallowing is painful. Hoarseness, aggravated when speaking and in fresh air. Tickling feeling at the back of the throat with constriction, stifling feeling, causing a dry cough. COMMENTS - Talmadge said of the effect on himself, ‘Trios, acted promptly and emphatically, causing aching pains in nearly every part of the body, especially of lower limbs and head.” The right side of the head was more affected than the left. The stomach was very much disordered. Severe vomiting and pain in the stomach. Itching at the anus, exudation of mucus. A peculiar concomitant of the evacuations was numbness of the lower limbs after stool. Many symptoms came on in the early morning hours. One prover, though sleepy, could not sleep after midnight. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bapt. - Gastric fever. Digestive complaints, putrid excreta, exhaustion, muscle pain. (2) Rheumatism, Bry., Rhus-t. (3) Load at epigastrium, Abies-n. (4) Sleepy but cannot sleep, Bell. Bell. - Fever, heat, restlessness, thirst. (5) Aeon. - Skin dry, anxiety, extreme restlessness. (6) Ars. - Anxiety, restlessness, burning pains ameliorated by the heat. (7) Coff. - Palpitations insomnia, restlessness. (8) Lach. - Congestive rush of blood, pharyngeal constriction, worse on waking. (9) Lat-m. - Pre-stemal pains resembling angina. ( 10) Lyc. - Distention aggravated after 4 p.m. (11) Sulph. - Itching and heat on the feet, alternating with coldness. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Acrid dyspepsia. Loathing of food, nausea on rising, followed by vomiting and cramps. Nausea, worse after meals, thirsty for cold drinks, which soothe.

Abdomen - Distended and full of gas. Pain in the coccyx. Sharp pain in the left side of the groin. Epigastric pain spreading to the thorax and throat. Enterocolitis. Colic, especially in the right iliac fossa and the hypogastrium. Flatulence, after drinking milk.

Rectum - Proctitis. Constipated, great effort to pass stools, which produces small, hard stools. Stools followed by diarrhea and nauseating wind. Stools watery, frothy. Rectal pains, stabbing, aggravated by pushing to evacuate, worse after passing stools. Rectal burning with anal itching, especially at night. Hemorrhoids.

Female - Irregular cycle, either late or early menses. Menses long and late. Menses painful, scanty. Menorrhagia. Food - Loathing of food. Painful hungry feeling, aggravated around 11 a.m. and in the evening. Worse after drinking milk.

Chest - Angina pectoris. Pressing pain in the precordial region when lying on the left side. Dull ache all over the thorax, predominately in the retro-sternal region with thoracic constriction. Swollen glands in right axilla.

Heart - Angina pectoris. Arteritis of the coronary arteries. Pulse slow and weak.

Back - Painful stiffness of the back.

Limbs - Generalized pains in the upper and lower limbs. Stiffness of all joints, calves numbs, aching in the bones. Rheumatic pain in back. Pains in limbs. Numbness of the lower limbs after going to stool. Burning, pulsating pains in the right axilla, where the glands are swollen. Cramping pain in the left shoulder and arm in the two lower limbs and in the fingers of the right hand. Lungs - Sensation of choking, has to grope for breath. Asthma. Bronchitis. Dry cough, caused by irritation of the larynx after eating. Cough, especially in the evening, aggravated in a warm room.

Skin - Erysipelas. Eczema. Itching welts. Urticaria from gastric derangement. Itching of the whole body. Itching, especially of the feet, scalp, palms of hands, where there isadry eruption. Erythematous eruption on the calves, back, scrotum and on the inside of the thighs. Soles of feet itchy in the evening and in bed. Itching eruption on the shoulders and between the scapulae. Patches of brown on the skin. Peeling of the skin on the abdomen. Hyperesthesia of the skin, profuse perspiration, worse at night and from exercise.

Modalities - Better from rest, solitude. Better fresh air, cold drinks. Worse early morning, 3 a.m. to 7 a.m. Worse in the Triosteum perfoliatum evening, at night, lying, turning in bed, after sleep, rising from bed, waking. Worse sitting up, movement. Worse from heat, drinking cold water.

Kidneys - Pyelonephritis. Cystitis. Frequent urination. Smell of ammonia in the urine. Adenoma of the prostate gland.

keynote:
PHARMACY - tritic. Triticum repens. Couch grass. Agropyrum repens. Cooch-grass. Cutch-grass. Quitch grass. N. O. Gramineae. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bladder, disorders. Cystitis. Dysuria. Gonorrhea. Incontinence. Prostate,…
full:
PHARMACY - tritic. Triticum repens. Couch grass. Agropyrum repens. Cooch-grass. Cutch-grass. Quitch grass. N. O. Gramineae. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bladder, disorders. Cystitis. Dysuria. Gonorrhea. Incontinence. Prostate, enlarged. Pyelitis. Strangury.

HERBAL - Burnett told how he learned from an herbalist the use of Tritic.; the herbalist cured a patient of Burnett’s with it, the man suffered from dysuria. Burnett found it no less valuable for women than for men. “Frequently in dysuria from an inflamed state of the urethra, Tritic., ten drops in a little water, frequently repeated of prompt effect often giving complete relief in a few hours and if the ailment is primarily in the urethra the relief is an abiding cure, if from a tugging of the heavy womb, it is only relief.”

HOMEOPATHIC - Excessive, chronic irritability of the bladder. Dysuria, cystitis and gonorrhea. Strangury, pyelitis. Enlarged prostate. Incontinence, constant desire. Dysuria, frequent, difficult and painful urination (Pop.). Catarrhal and purulent discharges (Pareir.). Urine is filled with gravel and sediment which causes irritation of the mucus surfaces. Always blowing nose. COMMENTS - Burnett gave the case of a widow who was suffering from a complete procidentia uterus and very bad hemorrhoidal bleeding. She wrote that she was driven almost mad with painful urination, the burning and straining were truly awful. Tritic., as above, was ordered and brought a most grateful letter from the patient. She kept a supply always at hand. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Chim., Senec., Pop., Buchu, Uva., Trad. (2) Polytr. - Ground Moss - Painful urination of old people, dropsy, urinary obstruction and suppression). REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

name: Trombidium Muscae Domesticae
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Warm drink improves toothache. Open air improves coryza. Worse from anyfood ordrink, after stool. Worse by touch, pressure. Worse shaking head, moving. Cold air aggravates toothache. Cold bath aggravates pain in abdomen..
constitution: Anus, prolapsed. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Hip joint, pain. Liver, pain. Nose, catarrh. Sciatica. Tibia, pain. Toothache.

full:
PHARMACY - from. Trombidium muscae domesticae. Acarus. Red acarus of the fly. N. O. Acarudea, class, Arachnida. Tincture of the animals. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Anus, prolapsed. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Hip joint, pain. Liver, pain. Nose, catarrh. Sciatica. Tibia, pain. Toothache.

HOMEOPATHIC - Trom. is a parasite found singly or in groups upon the common house-fly of a bright red color, nearly circular in shape. The alcoholic tincture, a brilliant orange in color was prepared from specimens, about 115 in number, collected in Frankfort, Philadelphia in 1864. The provings, under the supervision of Hering, were made with the 3x, 6x, 9c, 18c. and 30c potencies. Trom. has cured dysentery with brown, thin, bloody stools and tenesmus. Dysentery, worse by food and drink. Brown, thin, bloody stools, much pain before and after stools. Stools only after eating. Mucus discharge from nose while eating dinner. Weakness. Felt better in evening, better in open air. Rising up causes fainting. Reading aloud causes toothache. Rheumatic pains in left shoulder, arm, knee, and region of heart. Inability to keep quiet. MIND - Talkative during day. Disposed to be contrary. Constant disposition to gape. Inability to collect ideas. Absence of ideas. Loss of memory.

Head - Oppressive headache. Dullness of head in forenoon. Head heavy, sometimes sharp pains in temples. Lungs - Hoarseness. Hacking cough from irritation in throat.

Eyes - Redness of internal part of conjunctiva, similar to a pterygium. Lachrymation in open air. Itching at right inner canthus. Food - Appetite lost.

Ears - Shooting in ears in afternoon, worse swallowing or blowing nose. Itching in ears after rising. Burning in ears in evening.

Nose - Nose obstructed on rising. Fluent coryza in open air and on eating. Mucus discharge from nose, worse during dinner. Dryness of nose in evening, with scabs. Nosebleed in morning, afternoon.

Mouth - Tongue coated white.

Throat - Throat sore on right side. Vertigo - Lightness of head. Dizziness, on every attempt to rise from bed, with faintness. COMMENTS - The grand keynote of Trom. is “worse by eating or drinking,” in the nose, teeth or tonsils. On this indication, Clarke cured some of the worst cases of diarrhea and intestinal pains coming on when the patient eat or drinks. “Much pain before and after stool, stool only after eating.” Congested liver with urgent, loose stools on rising from bed. During stool, sharp pain in left side, shooting downward. Skin symptoms, especially itching of scalp and in whiskers. Restlessness, inability to keep quiet. Fainting on rising up. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Staph, (toothache), Merc-c. (diarrhea), Compare: ( 1 ) Rheumatism, Led. (2) Diarrhea. Sulph. (3) Worse blowing nose. Cube, Thuj. (4) Stitches up anus, Ign., Nit-ac., Sul-ac. with prolapse, Podo. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Griping in pit of stomach, worse after dinner. Belching after meals, tasting of ingesta. Vomiting after breakfast, thought it was from drinking coffee.

Abdomen - Congestion of the liver. Griping in hypochondrium in morning. Much pain in abdomen before and after stool.

Rectum - Burning in anus. Sharp pain in left side, shooting downward during stool. Urgent, loose, stools on rising. Stool only after eating. Brown, thin, bloody stools with tenesmus. Sensations - As if there were no weight in ear, lightness. As from incarcerated flatus in abdomen. As if excoriated after tenesmus. As if everything were coming out of anus. As if hot air blowing over lower abdomen and thigh. As if abdomen needed support. As if three toes on left foot would be twisted off. As if her breath were leaving her.

Chest - Cutting to right of lower part of sternum. Sharp pain in lower part of chest. Throbbing all over chest from 9 to 11 a.m.

Sleep - Constant inclination to gape through day, in afternoon. Sleepiness. Restless sleep. Lewd dreams. Wakefulness after 4 a.m., with restlessness.

Skin - Pimples on nape in evening. Itching in spots on chin and among whiskers, in evening, and about neck.

Modalities - Warm drink improves toothache. Open air improves coryza. Worse from anyfood ordrink, after stool. Worse by touch, pressure. Worse shaking head, moving. Cold air aggravates toothache. Cold bath aggravates pain in abdomen.

Teeth - Toothache, better warm drinks. Aching in left decayed tooth, worse lying down, eating, talking, and cold air.

Temperature - Chilliness at night, worse morning on waking. Fever in afternoon, with pulsation in arteries of head and aching on occiput and small of back.

full:
PHARMACY - trop. Tropaeolum majus. Indian cress. Garden Nasturtium. N. O. Tro- paeolaceae. Tincture of fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

HERBAL - Tropaeolum is a native of Peru. The taste of the leaves were considered like the taste of cress, and they have been used like cress in salads. The seeds make pickles and are used as a substitute for capers. A patient to whom Cooper gave Trop, noted that it made the urine extremely fetid in smell. On this keynote, Cooper relieved several cases of urinary difficulty, giving single doses of the tincture. REFERENCES - Clarke.

name: Tuberculinum Aviaire
author: Murphy
constitution: Bronchitis. Broncho-pneumonia. Chronic fatigue. Colds. Coughs. Debility. Emaciation. Influenza. Lung, disorders. Measles. Pneumonia. Prostration. Tuberculosis. Weakness.

full:
PHARMACY - tub-a. Tuberculinum aviaire. Chicken tuberculosis. Tuberculinum avis. Nosodes. A preparation of chicken tuberculosis. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Bronchitis. Broncho-pneumonia. Chronic fatigue. Colds. Coughs. Debility. Emaciation. Influenza. Lung, disorders. Measles. Pneumonia. Prostration. Tuberculosis. Weakness.

HOMEOPATHIC - Tub-a. is prepared from the infected liver of chickens. Dr. Cartier gave an account of this nosode in his paper read at the International Homeopathic Congress, 1896. The bacillus of avian tuberculosis has been identified with that of human tuberculosis. But the clinical properties of the two nosodes are not identical. Tub-a. acts most prominently on the apices of the lungs and it corresponds most closely to the bronchitis ofinfluenza, which simulates tuberculosis, having cured several hopeless-looking cases. It has also done Tuberculinum aviaire excellently in some cases of bronchitis following measles. H. D. Baker noted “Tub. aviare has served me better than any remedy in the long lasting prostration after the influenza." Dr. Francois Cartier of France found it useful in broncho-pneumonia of children and persistent cough after influenza and measles. Symptoms similar to tuberculosis, relieves the debility, diminishes the cough, improves the appetite and braces up the whole organism. Acute broncho-pulmonary diseases of children. Itching of palms and ears. Coughs are irritating, incessant and tickling, loss of strength and appetite. Emaciation (Hydr. to fatten patients after tuberculosis). Acts on the mind, spinal nerves and branches, muscles, joints, bronchi and mucus membranes. Influenza and its sequelae. Chronic fatigue. Muscular or nerve pains are better by motion, but the patient tires easily. Pains and mental symptoms are better in the open air. Relaxed, degraded conditions of tissues and secretion. Dingy, unhealthy, doughy or aged appearance and feeling of the skin and soft tissues and an old catarrhal aspect of mucus excretions. In acute conditions the rapidity of the emaciation is notable. MIND - Depressed. Easily frightened. Mentally changeable in feeling and purpose. Desires change. Dissatisfied with present conditions and surroundings. Desperate, wicked feelings. Lack of moral sense. Rest- lessness, the desire for change is physical as well as mental. COMMENTS - Anshutz related a case of a woman who entered the hospital suffering from influenza and who, a few days after a slight amelioration of her symptoms, was attacked with a pulmonary congestion, clearly localized in the top of the left lung and accompanied by all the clinical symptoms of tuberculosis. Rales and moist crepitation, dullness, exaggeration of the thoracic vibration, expectoration, fever, perspiration, spitting of blood. Examination of the sputa showed distinctly the presence of Koch’s bacilli. Anshutz gave her Tub-a. and in three weeks all the symptoms had left. That woman left the hospital completely cured and a year later her health was still perfect. Anshutz noted ten cases of influenzal bronchitis with incessant coughs, fever and expectoration, rapidly cured by Tub-a. It seems that Tub-a. does not act in diminishing the cough like an anodyne, but braces up the whole organism. The relief of debility and the return of appetite are the phenomena which was observed in conjunction with the diminution of the cough. In contrast with Bac., Tub-a. has considerable cough and little dyspnea. It has an acute, irritating cough, such as one meets with in acute diseases or sub-acute disorders in young people. A cough which fatigues and which leads to enfeeblement and loss of appetite, a suspicious cough. Dr. R.E.S. Hayes made the following statement: “My experience has led me to select the Tub. Bovinum for patients presenting more pronounced localizations in the meninges, abdomen, skin, glands or joints. But the Tub. Aviare for patients who were affected by a more evident depreciation of quality in the entire person at the same time, such as occurs after influenza or similar crises. This observation is purely clinical. “Recurrent influenza with long continued cough. Long continued, annoying, teasing cough remaining after the active symptoms of bronchitis or influenza, in a good many instances Tuberculinum aviare put an immediate end to this cough any related discomforts. Aviare has the usual characteristics of Tuberculinum plus its affinity to influenza and to nerve elements, both sympathetic and cerebro-spinal.” RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Bac., Bac-ts., Tub., Ars-i. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke

name: Tuberculinum Bovinum
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better open air, cool wind. Better dry mountain air, pineforests. Better dry, warm weather. Worse from close room. Worse change of weather, before a storm, cold, damp, drafts. Worse motion, slightest exertion, standing. Worse noise and music. Worse periodically. Worse after dinner, evening, night, when beginning to sleep. Worse on waking, early morning, after sleep, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. Worse in the mornings, much purulent expectoration, sickness and nausea, loss of appetite, thirst, fatigue. Worse or better at seashore..

keynote: PHARMACY - tub. Tuberculinum bovinum. Tuberculosis nosode. Tuberculinum bovinum of Kent. Tuberculinum of Koch. Nosode is prepared either from tubercular abscess or from a glycerine extract of pure cultivation of human tubercular bacillus. Dilutions. Historical dose: Tincture and…
full:
PHARMACY - tub. Tuberculinum bovinum. Tuberculosis nosode. Tuberculinum bovinum of Kent. Tuberculinum of Koch. Nosode is prepared either from tubercular abscess or from a glycerine extract of pure cultivation of human tubercular bacillus. Dilutions. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Acne. Albuminuria. Allergies. Appendicitis. Asthma. Bedwetting. Bones, decay. Breast, tumors. Bronchitis. Broncho-pneumonia. Catarrh. Chilblains. Chilly. Colds. Cornea, opacity, ulceration. Coughs. Dentition. Diarrhea. Dysmenorrhea. Dyspnea. Ear, infections. Edema. Emaciation. Epilepsy. Erysipelas. Erythema. Glands swollen. Hematuria. Hemoptysis. Headache. Heart, disorders. Hyperactivity. Influenza. Leprosy. Leucorrhea. Lungs, disorders. Lupus. Mania. Menses, early. Nephritis. Neurasthenia. Night sweats. Night, terrors. Paralysis. Pleurisy. Pneumonia. Throat, sore. Tonsillitis. Tuberculosis.

HOMEOPATHIC - Clarke found no appreciable difference between the action of Tub. and that of Bac. His own impression was that they are practically identical and that one will answer to the indications of the other. The first provers were tuberculosis patients and only pathogenetic symptoms are recorded. Tub. 30c was used. Tub. affects the mind, lungs, head, occiput, glands and larynx. When symptoms are constantly changing and well-selected remedies fail to improve. Relapsing states. Patient always tired, motion causes intense fatigue, aversion to work, wants constant changes. Tubercular miasm. In tuberculosis where the symptoms are constantly changing and begin suddenly, ceasing suddenly or of obscure nature. Early stage tuberculosis. Always tired, motion causes intense fatigue. Increasing exhaustion and lowered vitality. Weakness, emaciation with good appetite. Rapid breakdown of health. General exhaustion. Nervous weakness. Neurasthenia. Fainting. Trembling, quivering. Epilepsy. Nervous children. Mentally deficient children. Tendency tocatch cold easily, on slightest exposure, which ends in diarrhea. Diarrhea in children running for weeks, extreme wasting, bluish pallor, exhaustion. Chronic, enlargement of the glands, adenoids. Enlarged tonsils. Kidney disorders, chronic cystitis. Bruised pain throughout the body. Bones painful. Formication. Skin affections, acute rheumatism. Arthritis. Clothes feel very damp. Very susceptible to changes of weather. Very sensitive mentally and physically. Sensitive to music. MIND - Changing moods. Dissatisfied and restless, always wants a change. Desire to travel, does not want to remain in one place long. Deep feeling of being unfulfilled. Romantic longing to find inner contentment. Wants to do something different or even to find a new doctor. Restlessness. Needs stimulating experi- . enees. Constant fight against boredom. Compulsiveness. Desire to break things. Impulse to run. Reckless. Every trifle irritates, worse when waking. Anxious. Anxiety during fever. Children awake screaming with restlessness. Whimpers when spoken to. Whines and complaints with very little ailment. Precocious children. Contradictory behavior, changing moods. Insomnia and sopor. Depressed, melancholy. Hopeless. Weary of life. Sensitive to music. Fear something will happen. Fear of animals, particularly averse to dogs and cats. Aversion to mental work. Confusion, everything in the room seems strange. Ritualistic. Superstitious. Mania and melancholia. Maliciousness behavior and destructiveness. Abusive. Fits of violent temper, wants to fight, throws anything at anyone even without a cause. Destructive fantasies. Desire to use foul language, curse and swear.

Head - Meningitis. Periodical headaches. Intense pain, as of an iron band around head. Deep violent head pains, tears hair or beats head with fist. Dashes against the wall or floor, worse motion. Shooting from over eyes (right) through the head to back of ear (left) or from right frontal protuberance to right occipital region. Headaches students, worse study or even slight mental exertion. Brain feels loose. Sensitive scalp. Plica polonica (Vine.).

Eyes - Sore, bruised eyeballs, worse turning them. Eczema of margins of eyelids. Meningitis with squint.

Ears - Persistent offensive otorrhea. Perforation in eardrum with ragged edges. Sticking pain from pharynx to ears. Great aching in ears and teeth. Tinnitus. Rushing in ears with heavy head.

Face - Old looking, edematous, pale. Black blisters on lips. Slight swelling and itching of lips. Aching in malar bones.

Mouth - Dryness, stickiness. Black blisters on lips. Grinding of teeth in sleep. Teeth sensitive to cold air. Sensation as if the teeth were all jammed together and there were too many teeth. Delayed dentition. Nose - Nose and lips somewhat swollen. Sweat on nose. Crops of small boils, intensely painful, successively appear in the nose.green, fetid pus. Watery pimples, which, suppurating, form scabs. Dryness of posterior nares. Soreness inside of nose. Colds ending in diarrhea.

Throat - Hoarseness, better talking. Enlarged tonsils. Hawks mucus after eating. Adenoids. Dryness of the posterior sinuses. Vertigo - Vertigo with obscuration of eyes, is obliged to lean on something. Vertigo with palpitations, nausea. Vertigo with headache, in morning, after dinner. COMMENTS - Generally a history of tuberculosis in the family. Suppressed acute infections. Tendency for sore throats, colds, and upper respiratory infections or bronchitis. Swollen glands and big tonsils. Sore throats, swollen glands, start losing weight. Recurring tonsillitis in children. Similar to Bac., but more chronic and more severe. Colds that go into the chest (Phos.). Asthma, associated with frequent colds. Intercurrent for severe, chronic lung disease. Lingering coughs, pneumonias. Coughs where well-indicated remedies don’t work. Rapid emaciation with a good appetite (lod., Cina.). Emaciation associated with lung diseases. Rickets. Fatigue, faintness, and profuse debility. Great weakness in the limbs, after dinner. Paralysis. Disturbed circulation, chills and flushes alternating. Extreme exhaustion with sweat. Night sweats and weight loss (Med.). Night terrors. Insomniafrom overexcited state and overactive mind. Children grind their teeth during sleep. “Shivering when beginning to sleep.” “Cold feet in bed.” Low vital heat. Fontanelles that fail to close. Hydrocephalus. Meningitis. Characteristic desire to hit their head against the wall. Pressure in the head. Insanity. Hair growth in unusual and new places (Syph., Thuj.). Ringworm, particularly in children (Bac.). Voracious craving for ice-cold milk. Desires sweets, chocolate, fats, smoked meat, pork, bacon, exotic foods and spicy foods. Craves variety in food. Diarrhea. Better in the mountains, in pine forests. Desire for open air, particularly with respiratory conditions. Better motion, activity, exercise (Rhus-t.). Worse cold, damp with cold hands and feet. Hyperactive children. Children seem to have two personalities, one very sweet, nice and apologetic, the other destructive, obstinate, and argumentative. Tantrums, behavioral problems. Can be snappy, irritable, peevish, over-reactive (Cham., when due to pain). Very intelligent, but learning disabilities. Too much energy, can’t slow down to learn anything (Med., because they can’t focus). Easily bored. Very excitable. Active and very restless. Always needs something new. Strong desire to travel. Sense that there is something missing (Calc-p.), but they don’t know what it is. Discontent. Passionate, driven and dissatisfied. Deep feeling of unfulfillment, emptiness. Very romantic, yearning and longing, pining. Falls in love easily and deeply, can be easily grieved (Nat-m.). Easily upset. Hard to please, capricious. Malicious, conscious intent to do harm or to disrupt their environment (Med. is unconscious, more confused). Characteristic desire to break things. Can bite or mutilate themselves. Insanity. Fear of wasting their life, their time, of not accomplishing something significant before they die. Fear of dying or despair over their recovery. Dislike of dogs and cats, severe allergies to cats. Nebel used Tub. in exactly the same way as Burnett; others have used Bac., on the indications Burnett laid down and with Burnett’s results. In 1892, Arnuphy began giving Tub. 6x and 8x trituration in acute and chronic tuberculosis cases, with encouraging success, but with undesired aggravations at times. These were avoided with 12x and 30x. In one case, originating in influenza, both apices were affected, the right one breaking down and abundant pleuritic effusion on the left side. Six weeks’ treatment with Tub. brought about recovery. When seen a year later, the patient was quite well except for retraction of the left side. Arnuphy frequently used Tub. for bronchitis, catarrhal pneumonia, lobular pneumonia, tubercular pleurisy, parenchymatous nephritis and influenza. He gave two cases of acute lobular pneumonia with characteristic symptoms and high temperatures quickly resolved by Tub. One case concerned a boy, 3, who received the 12x; the other was a man, 78, who suffered from chronic bronchial catarrh. The latter was taken with influenza, pneumonia developed and he was in a very serious state. Tub. 30x made an almost immediate change for the better and recovery followed. Arnuphy related that, in this case, an abundant perspiration took place (the skin had been dry) during the night and he observed this in all cases of pneumonia when Tub. acted favorably. Clarke found Tub. 30c, 100c, 200c and 1000c the best general antidote to the chronic effects of influenza poisoning. A curious use of Tub. was made by Jau- regg of Vienna in a case of insanity. He had observed that cases of insanity are always benefited by an attack of an acute infectious disease, especially if it is accompanied with high fever. The idea then occurred to him to utilize the fever produced by Koch's Tuberculinic injections. He tried it on some patients and though the favorable symptoms soon disappeared after the fever subsided, there remained a steady clearing of the confused sensorium. Insanity is very frequently a manifestation of the tuberculosis miasm and there is something more than a pyrexial power in Tub. RELATIONS - Vaccinosis may block the way of action of Tub. until Thuj. has been given. When Tub. fails Syph. often follows, producing a positive reaction. Compare: (1) Bac., Phos., Sil. (2) Tub-a., Form-ac. Stann., (3) Psor., Lach. (4) Teucr-s. - tuberculosis, garlicky odor of all secretions and breath. Complementary: Bac., Phos., Calc., Chin., Bry. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Murphy. Phatak.

Stomach - All gone hungry sensation (Sulph.), which drives one to eat. Cramping pain in stomach. Belchings and sensation of fullness over stomach. Flatulent dyspepsia. Nausea with pains in umbilical region with diarrhea. Nausea before breakfast, with sudden diarrhea. Vomiting.

Abdomen - Inguinal glands indurated and visible. Drum belly. Spleen region bulging out, stitching pain in sides after running. Stitching pain in sides after running. Tympanites. Tabes mesenterica.

Rectum - Constipation, stools large and hard, then diarrhea. Chronic diarrhea with excessive sweat. Early- morning, sudden diarrhea (Sulph.). Brown, foul, watery stools, discharged with much force. Diarrhea of children running for weeks with wasting, exhaustion and bluish pallor. Tearing pain in rectum on coughing. Tearing in rectum on coughing. Sensations - As if the brain were squeezed with an iron ring. As if the teeth were jammed together and were too many for the mouth. Mucus in the throat of a tumor in the throat. Pressure in stomach going to throat as if the clothes were too tight. As if the clothes on the back were wet (Bac.).

Female - Burning in genitals. Amenorrhea. Menses too early, too profuse, long- lasting. Menses soon after childbirth. Dysmenorrhea, pains increase with the flow. Severe pain in breast at beginning of menses. Benign breast tumors. Retraction of nipples. Food - Loss of appetite, especially in morning. Aversion to all food, particularly meat. Ravenous hunger at night, driving out of bed. Craves alcohol, delicacies, sweets, cold milk. Strong craving for smoked meats and fats, bacon, ham, pork. Extreme thirst, day and night.

Chest - Heat in chest. Sore spot, pressure in chest. Sticking pain on both sides of chest in back. Constitutions - Tubercular constitutions. Lax fiber, low recuperative powers, very susceptible to changes in the weather. Mentally deficient children. Adapted to light complexioned. narrow-chested people. Coughs - Hard, dry cough during sleep. Hard, hacking cough with profuse sweating and loss of weight, rales all over chest. Cough with chill and red face, worse evening.

Heart - Heaviness and pressure over the heart. Palpitations on taking a deep breath after evening meal.

Back - Tension in nape of neck and down spine. Chilliness between shoulders or up the back. Pain in the back with palpitations. Sensation as if damp clothes on back. Breasts - Severe pain in breast at the beginning of menses. Breast tumors, benign. Retraction of nipples. Causations - Tuberculosis.

Limbs - Acute articular rheumatism. Hands and arms feel lame, unable to write or raise a cup or a glass. Fingertips brown. Sensation of fatigue in limbs. Cold feet in bed. Limbs feel weak or as if paralyzed worse dinner. Rheumatism. Pains in ulnar nerve. Wandering pain in limbs and joints. Lungs - Shortness of breath. Sensation of suffocation, even with plenty of fresh air. Longs for cold air. Asthma. Pneumonia after influenza. Tuberculosis. Deposits begin in apex of lung. Broncho-pneumonia in children. Profuse bronchorrhea. Hard, hacking cough, profuse sweating and loss of weight, rales all over chest. Dry, hard cough, more during sleep, worse dyspnea with chill and red face, worse evenings, worse raising arms. Thick, easy, profuse expectoration. Thick yellow or yellowgreen sputum. Mucus rattle in chest without expectoration.

Sleep - Insomnia and sopor. Overpowering sleepiness in daytime. Shuddering sensation on falling to sleep. Grinding of teeth during sleep. Night, terrors. Nocturnal hallucinations, wakes frightened. Screaming in sleep. Nightmares. Child wakes screaming. Awakes in horror. Night sweats. Poor sleep, restless, wakes early. Overpowering sleepiness in daytime. Distressing, vivid dreams. Dreams of shame. Dreams frightful.

Skin - Skin easily tanned. Dry, harsh, sensitive. Acne in tuberculous children. Ringworm. Measles. Psoriasis (Thyr.). Bran-like scales. Chronic eczema. Intense itching, changes places on rubbing, worse at night. Itching in cool air, better heat of stove. Itching worse undressing, bathing.

Modalities - Better open air, cool wind. Better dry mountain air, pineforests. Better dry, warm weather. Worse from close room. Worse change of weather, before a storm, cold, damp, drafts. Worse motion, slightest exertion, standing. Worse noise and music. Worse periodically. Worse after dinner, evening, night, when beginning to sleep. Worse on waking, early morning, after sleep, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. Worse in the mornings, much purulent expectoration, sickness and nausea, loss of appetite, thirst, fatigue. Worse or better at seashore.

Kidneys - Must strain at stool to pass urine. Sticky urinary sediment. Bedwetting.

Perspiration - Clammy sweats. Sweat stains yellow. Offensive, of chest, axillae, palms, nose and feet. Profuse night sweats. Sweats from coughing, from slightest exertion. Sweats on hands, on upper parts.

Temperature - Remittent fever. Loquacious during fever. Profuse sweat, easy, cold, clammy. Sweat on upper parts, on hands, worse coughing, stains yellow. General chilliness. Chilliness between shoulders or up back. Chilly, at beginning of sleep. Chilly, yet wants fresh air. Shuddering like a chill seems to go from brain down spine. Heat on cheek of affected side in spots. Burning in genitals. Flushes of heat, worse eating. Wants covers on in all stages of fever.

full:
PHARMACY - turq. Turquoise. Gemstone. Hydrous copper aluminum phosphate. CuA16(PO4)4(OH)8, 5H2O. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Asthma. Backache. Cramps. Coryza. Cough. Diarrhea. Faintness. Fractures. Headache. Heat, flushes. Influenza. Injuries. Leucorrhea. Vertigo

HOMEOPATHIC - Injuries after falling from a height. Injuries to bones, fractures. Sharp pains. Internal or external squeezing pain. Sharp pains. Internal trembling. Accelerated pulse. Tension. Faintness on rising. Weakness, lassitude. Emaciation. Influenza. Worse in the morning, afternoon, 1 to 4 p.m., after midnight, 3 a.m. Worse from waking. Coldness in the morning, in bed. Heat flushes, at noon. Heat aggravates. Better from the moon. MIND - Fastidious. Industrious. Creative. Memory, active. Dullness, slowness of mind. Difficult concentration. Aversion to mental work. Forgetfulness. Discouraged. Cheerfulness. Excitement, exhilaration. Laughing, quickly followed by weeping. Alternating moods. Horrible news, sad stories, affect profoundly. Sadness. Grief. Homesickness. Weeping. Despair. Impatience. Irritability, waking aggravates. Irritability before menses. Confrontational. Censorious. Hatred. Angry, toward husband. Averse to husband. Aversion to company. Anxiety, during cough. Vivacious. Confidence increased. Amorous disposition. Clairvoyance. Foreboding. Tranquility. Relaxed feeling. Persistent thoughts. Delusion that she is betrayed. Delusion of being old. As if in a dream. Time passes too slowly, appears longer. Detached. Sensitive to noise, light. Starting during sleep. Restlessness.

Eyes - Dryness, irritation. Heaviness, tired sensation. Swelling. Scratching sensation. Pain, as if from sand.

Ears - Clear discharge. Noises, especially in the left.

Nose - Obstruction at night, wakes him. Obstruction, morning. Coryza in the morning, with fluent discharge. Clear discharge. Sneezing in the morning. Acute sense of smell.

Face - Discoloration, red flushes. Greasy. Wrinkled skin. Dry lips, posterior nares. Peeling, rough lips. Herpetic eruptions, painful, suppurating. Eruption on lower lip, around mouth. Acne, on forehead. Pimples.

Mouth - Metallic taste. Numb tongue. Pain, biting in the tongue. Roughness inside lip. Swelling gums.

Throat - Pain. Itching. Thick sensation. Voice rough. Vertigo - Vertigo with headache, during sleep. Vision - Acute or blurred vision. COMMENTS - One of the first gemstones to be mined, turquoise has long been prized for its intense color, which varies from sky blue to green, depending on the quantities of iron and copper within it. Turquoise symbolizes laughter, humor, confidence, and purpose. Turquoise is said to strengthen eyesight and even cure blindness. Strengthens and calms the mind and body. Stimulates tissue regeneration. Revitalizes blood, nervous system. It is said to be beneficial for circulation, bowel cramps and the chest area including lungs and respiratory system. Throat, lungs, asthma. Tones and strengthens entire body. Good for internal cleansing. Infections. Headache. High blood pressure. Anorexia. Teeth, jaw ailments. Hearing disorders. Like amethyst, it protects and detoxifies from alcohol, poison, pollution, x-ray/sun radiation. Induces enthusiasm. Encourages family bonding. Promotes trust, love, kindness and innocence. Empowers artistic traits. Provides discipline, attention and understanding. For fear, depression. RELATIONS - Compare: Amethyst. Amber. Ruby. REFERENCES - Murphy. Rowe.

Stomach - Appetite diminished, easy satiety. Appetite increased. Thirst. Tension. Noises, gurgling. Eructations at night. Nausea, with chill, headache. Vomiting.

Abdomen - Distension. Abdominal pain, better from diarrhea or vomiting. Cutting. squeezing, cramping pain, during diarrhea.

Rectum - Constipation, ineffectual urging. Diarrhea. Frequent hard or soft stool. Bloody stool. Flaky stool.

Female - Profuse clotted menses, frequent, too early, too soon, too short. Cramping pain in uterus, during menses. Leucor- rhea, lumpy. Itching vagina. Pain, burning vagina. Perspiration - Scanty sweat.

modalities: Modalities: Pains in pylorus worse by pressure. Lumbago worse standing. Drinking causes belchings. Worse from walking. COMMENTS - Kuchenmeister and five others took substantial doses. Urethritis with yellow discharge. Hansen gave the indication “Acute or chronic gonorrhea, yellow or white, thick discharge.” Crawling in urethra, jerking in spermatic cord and drawing in right testicle are additional symptoms of the proving. Rosenberg gave some experiences. The first concerned an extremely violent gonorrhea, penis swollen, painful, emission of urine extremely painful, mixed with blood, patient feverish and restless. Tus-p. was given in water. There was a great aggravation of all symptoms in thirty- six hours. The remedy was discontinued and marked amelioration followed. Resumed again, much diluted, rapid cure followed. The remedy was used externally as well in this case. A second case was a chronic ophthalmia, the result of gonorrhea “cured” with turpentine. Tus-p. restored the discharge and then cured. Rosenberg referred to a writer who said of the plant that if it is macerated in water, the water will not spoil even if kept for years. Tussilago petasites grows on river-banks that are little trodden on. The roots are an admirable medicine in the worst kind of fevers with boils or buboes.” A medicinal plant, it was used as a diaphoretic in the middle ages. Its pharmacological action is sudorific, diuretic, emmenagogue and anti-asthmatic. It has been used for uterine cramps, coughs, hoarseness and urinary disorders.

CLINICAL - Boils. Burns. Chilblains. Constipation. Deafness. Hemorrhoids. Herpes. Inflammations. Malnutrition. Ophthalmia. Pain. Sore throats. Syphilis. Ulcers. Wounds.

HERBAL - Slippery elm is an herbal diuretic, emollient, and demulcent. A decoction of the viscous inner bark is used as a poultice for painful inflammations. It may be used as such in all cases of weakness, inflammation of the stomach, bronchitis, etc. The coarse powder forms the finest poultice to be obtained for all inflamed surfaces, ulcers, wounds, burns, boils, skin diseases, purulent ophthalmia, chilblains etc. It soothes the part, disperses the inflammation, draws out impurities, and heals speedily. The finely powdered bark makes an excellent gruel or food, and in addition possesses as much nutrition as oatmeal. COMMENTS - In a case in which the mucus membrane of the rectum was dry and extremely painful, Burnett relieved the sufferings with 20 drop doses of the tincture. Cooper mentioned that the triturated bark gives much relief as a snuff in old vascular deafness with tubal obstruction. He could not speak too highly of this remedy, and are confident there is nothing to equal it in the world for its mentioned uses. Inflammation in the bowels of infants and adults has been cured, when all other remedies have failed, by an injection into the bowels of an infusion of 1 oz of powdered bark to 1 pt of boiling water, used while warm. Slippery elm is also used in lozenges to relieve irritation of the pharynx. The food or gruel should be made as follows: Take a teaspoonful of the powder, mix well with the same quantity of powdered sugar and add 1 pt of boiling water slowly, mixing as it is poured on. This may be flavored with cinnamon or nutmeg to suit the taste, and makes a very wholesome and sustaining food for infants. REFERENCES - Clarke. Cooper. Murphy. Potter’s Cyclopedia.

The inner bark and the root contain similar properties, but the inner bark is preferred over the root, because stripping the bark does not kill the plant. It is reputed to enhance immune functions, increase energy and stamina. An ideal tonic forthose who are mentally, emotionally and physically exhausted from overwork or excessive stress. Helps against viruses, radiation, chemical toxins and chemotherapy effects. COMMENTS - Hank, age 53, suffered from partial urinary blockage due to an enlarged prostate for over two years. After drinking three cups of cat’s claw tea daily, using one teaspoon full of the powdered herb per cup. He reported that his symptoms dramatically diminished after three days. REFERENCES - Murphy.

CLINICAL - Asphyxia. Backache. Conjunctivitis. Eye, pains. Hangnails. Headaches. Palpitations. Sexual, excess. Styes. Tetanus. Vision, disorders.

HOMEOPATHIC - Upa. is obtained from a Strychnos and must not be confounded with Antiaris toxicaria, the concocted juice of which forms the "Upas antiar" poison of the Javanese. S. tieute is a climbing shrub. Pitet made a courageous proving of it, carrying it to the length of producing tetanic symptoms. Upa. produces tonic spasms, tetanus and asphyxia. A large proportion of the symptoms occurred in the head and eyes. A remarkable headache, “superficial drawing pain traverses left temple from before backward and ceases at outer angle of orbit, the part is hot and painful to touch.” Pressure in the eyes, feeling of a foreign body under the eyelids. Severe pains in orbits inflammation of the conjunctiva of the lids. Distorted vision. “Every morning weakness of the eyes with lachrymation, the lids being so heavy that they close involuntarily as if from drowsiness.” Drowsiness. Pressive and lancinating pains. Pain in the left side of the throat as from a splinter on swallowing. Pain in left Upas tieute sciatic nerve in left iliac fossa. Chiefly affects the left-side. MIND - Irritable. Disinclined for mental work.

Head - Dull headache deep in brain.

Eyes - Dull, sunken eyes. Pain in eyes and orbits with conjunctivitis. Styes.

Mouth - Herpes on lips. Burning on the tongue. Pain in mouth, as from a splinter (Nit-ac,). Sensations - As if the brain were rudely shaken. As if a foreign body in eye, as if sand in eyes. As if a splinter in throat on swallowing. As if a foreign body in esophagus preventing swallowing. As if an iron hoop around waist preventing breathing. As after sexual excess. COMMENTS - Keynote sensitiveness. Irritability, crossness, moroseness increased sensitiveness to cold, the least irritation brought on spasms, pressing in throat causing feeling of suffocation. Vertigo, ending in pressing headache. Twitching in brain and orbits. Pulsative headache with throbbing all over body. Great exhaustion after convulsive seizures. Itching in patella. Sexual function depressed. Distressing symptoms after sex, as occur after sexual excess. Left half of face red and hot, right half pale and cold. The tongue is coated white so thickly that it can be scraped off. Aversion to meat and eggs, the very thought of them causes nausea. Smell of manure in nose. Sallow complexion. Severe symptoms in the liver and from the right lung to the liver (cutting as with knives). RELATIONS - Antidote: Cur. Compare: (1) Upas-a., Ox-ac. (2) Upas when Bry. fails (typhoid). REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Male - Desire increased with loss of power.

Chest - Sharp pain throughout right lung toward the liver, stopping breathing.

Heart - Violent palpitations, sensation of heaviness in stomach.

Back - Dull backache, as after excessive sex. Causations - Sexual excess.

Limbs - Hangnails inflamed, itching and redness of nail roots. Numb hands, feet.

Modalities - Better after rising. Better evenings, after dinner. Headache better in open air. Pain in left iliac fossa worse by touch. Throat worse pressure. Worse by motion, walking. Worse morning, afternoon and evening.

PHARMACY - uran-n. Uranium nitricum. Uranium nitrate. Uranyl nitrate. Solution in distilled water. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Anal, itching. Ascites. Backache. Bedwetting, nocturnal. Bronchitis. Constipation. Debility. Diabetes mellitus. Diabetes insipidus. Dropsy. Duodenum, ulcer. Dyspepsia. Edema. Emacia- tion. Enteritis. Gastric, ulcer. Glycosuria. Impotency. Insomnia. Malassimilation. Milk, secretion. Nephritis. Nephrotic, syndrome. Neuralgia. Ophthalmia. Peritonitis. Phosphaturia. Seminal discharges. Stomach, ulcers. Stomatitis. Styes. Ulcers. Urine, incontinence. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - Uran-n. belongs to the chromium group of elements. Uran-n. was proved by E. T. Blake, his monograph forms part of Hahnemann’s Materia Medica. Blake’s proving was suggested by the observation of an old-school experimenter, Leconte, who found sugar in the urine of dogs slowly poisoned with Uran-n. Blake was not very successful in producing sugar, but his proving is not any less valuable on that account and clinical use has filled out the picture. Uran-n. causes glycosuria and increased urine. Produces nephritis, diabetes mellitus and insipidus, degeneration of the liver, high blood pressure and dropsy. Its therapeutic keynote is great emaciation, debility and tendency to ascites and general dropsy. Excessive thirst, nausea, vomiting, excessive appetite. Dry mucus membranes and skin. High blood pressure. Burning in the stomach, gastric ulcer. Incontinence of urine. Burning in urethra while passing urine. Impotency with nightly emissions. Backache and delayed menses. Menses suppressed during diabetes. The left side was more affected than the right. MIND - Ill-humor, not feeling well all day. Depression.

Head - Head heavy on waking. Heaviness of head with general languor. Dull, heavy pain. Heavy, burning, in right side of vertex. Shooting from right orbit extending to occipital protuberance, in evening. Frontal headache. Dull aching in right temple. Pain in forehead, over left eye. Pain in left temple, with feeling as if he had taken cold. Severe pain, at posterior edge of right and left temporal bones. Aching at occipital protuberance. Fullness of head. Sensation of blood flowing to head, before eating. Neuralgia on posterior edge of left temporal bone.

Eyes - Styes in left upper lid. Edema of lower lids, worse than usual. Lids inflamed, agglutinated. Shooting from right orbit to occipital protuberance in evening. Pain over left eye.

Nose - Itching in nose. Left nostril stuffed. Dry coryza. Nostrils sore with purulent acrid discharge. Chronic scabbing of inner nostril.

Mouth - Painless ulcer with one elevated side in mouth, opposite left anterior upper molar, worse evening. Acid saliva. Ulcers in mouth, with copious salivation.

Throat - Hawking of tenacious mucus. Contracted feeling in throat. Vertigo - Vertigo, faint, flushing of upper part of body during menses. Vertigo, worse in evening. Vertigo with heaviness of head. Vertigo with debility and cold feeling. COMMENTS - Many cases of diabetes have been relieved orcured by Uran-n., usually in the lower potencies. Diabetes with excessive thirst, polyuria and dry tongue. Glycosuriais by no means an essential part of the indications for Uran-n. Diabetes concomitant with indigestion, belching, burping, and heartburn. Urine with bile and sugar in it, can smell fishy. Kidney disease with protein in the urine, nephrotic syndrome. Stomach ulcers. Very weak (Ph-ac.), debilitated, tendencies toward dizziness. One case, involving a married woman, was cured with 5 grain doses of Uran-n. 2x. She was weak and emaciated, vomited mucus mixed with blood and coffee-ground matter and passed dark, tarry stools, sensitive and tender over region of pylorus. Dr. Choudhury noted a case of diabetes in a middle-aged man. The patient had progressive weight loss, weakness, and great weariness in the legs with edema. His tongue was coated white, severely dry mouth. Pale, looked haggard with dark circles. Neither Chin, or Phos-ac. helped. Uran-n 30c cured. The patient needed no insulin after treatment. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Elemental relatives, gastro-duodenal affections, Chrom. and Kali-bi. (2) Diabetes, Phos., Ph-ac., Syzyg., Thyr., Lac-def., Lac-ac. (3) Sinking immediately after meals, Ars., Cina, Lyc., Sil., Staph. (4) Craves tea, Sei. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Mur- phy-

Stomach - Constant faintness at stomach, even after a hearty meal. Indigestion in afternoon. Dyspepsia, flatus after food, acidity, pain. Tasteless, putrid belchings. Sinking at pit, with acid eructations, flatulence and copious urination. Boring pain in pyloric region. Burning pain. Gastric and duodenal ulcers. Recurring hematemesis. Nausea and vomiting.

Abdomen - Abdomen bloated. Borborygmi. Flatus. Sharp colic with tenesmus and raw feeling in rectum. Enteritis andperitonitis with meteorism and great prostration.

Rectum - Borborygmi. Constipation. Urging in rectum and bladder. Soft stool, twice in one day. Anal itching. Sensations - As if blood were flowing to head. As if he had taken cold with headache.

Male - Complete impotence with nocturnal emissions. Organs cold, relaxed, sweaty.

Female - Pale, anemic. Menses suppressed during diabetes. Flushing of upper body during menses, with giddiness and faintness. Excessive flow of milk. Food - Malassimilation. Ravenous appetite. Eating followed by flatulence. Excessive thirst with intermittent vomiting or with emaciation (diabetes). Loss of appetite during menses. Craves raw ham, tea, sweets. Intense thirst from sensation of dryness in mouth and fauces. Excessive thirst at night.

Chest - Intermittent pain, radiating from left side to ensiform cartilage, worse fasting.

Back - Pain at lower angle of left scapula, worse deep inspiration. Tenderness of spine near and extending to kidneys. Breasts - Excessive secretion of milk.

Limbs - Stiffness in loins. White vesicles on arms and legs with red areolae, burn and itch. Lungs - Bronchitis with copious mucus expectoration and much emaciation. Chronic colds. Hydrothorax and congestion of lungs. Lung infiltrated with gray tubercle.

Sleep - Restless, with shivering and heat. Extreme languor, on rising from bed. Feeling as if he had taken cold. Great drowsiness and prostration during menses. Restless at night during menses. Sleeplessness.

Skin - White vesicles on hands and legs, with red areola. Burning and itching. Ecchymo- sis. Epithelioma. Lupus exedens.

HOMEOPATHIC - On general indications, Urea, has been used in medicine by both schools. Merck mentioned that it is diuretic and is used in cirrhosis of liver, pleurisy, kidney calculus. The failure of the kidneys to eliminate urea from the blood leads to uremic intoxication, delirium, convulsions and coma. Tuberculosis. Lumps. Enlarged glands. Kidney dropsy with symptoms of general intoxication. Albuminuria, diabetes, uremia. Urine thin and of low specific gravity. Constant urging, much sediment in urine. Intolerable sensa tion in abdomen, with burning skin. Gouty eczema. General uneasiness, felt ill, poisoned. Urea acted as a nervous tonic in tuberculosis patients. Urea is a hydrogogue diuretic in the treatment of dropsies. 10 grains every 6 hours.

Eyes - Itching and profuse watering of eyes.

Abdomen - In right hypochondrium, a steady, dull sensation. Intolerable sensation in abdomen and burning of the skin.

Kidneys - Constant urging to urinate, beginning at root of penis. Profuse diuresis with rapid diminution of dropsy. Albuminuria, bloody urine, general dropsy. COMMENTS - Burnett used both Urea 6c and Ur-ac. 6c in gouty eczema, “where the gouty eczema has been the cutaneous outlet for the constitution.” Burnett gave Urea in gouty cases where the urine was thin and of low specific gravity, “it thickens the urine and gives great relief to the patient.” Allen cited from Mauthner two cases of kidney dropsy with symptoms of general intoxication in which Urea, 2 grains., divided into three doses and given two hours apart, cured brilliantly. Arthur Buch related cases of tuberculosis cured, on the plan originated by Harper of Nottingham, with Urea in 20 to 30 grain doses three times a day. Underthe treatment, lupoid nodules disappeared, tuberculous glands disappeared, tuberculous joints improved. No ill-effects of the treatment were noticed, “on the contrary, the action has evidently been in many cases that of a nervous tonic.” Villers examined the urine of an intensely neurasthenic woman, suffering from severe asthma and found 4.5 percent of urea instead of the usual 2.5. In order to find out the effect of Urea, on the healthy, he took for five days Urea. 15x., five drops thrice daily. He was then compelled to stop by the severity of the symptoms. He gave the same dose to a patient, a woman. She begged after a short time to be allowed to discontinue the medicine, as it affected her so painfully, causing constant urging to urinate, much sediment in the urine intolerable sensation in abdomen and burning of the skin. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Ur-ac. - gout, gouty eczema, rheumatism, lipoma. (2) Urt-u., Tub.,Thyr. (3) Urin., Ur-ac., Thiosin., Urt-u. (4) Diuresis, Thyr. (5) Tuberculosis, Tub., Bac. REFERENCES - Allen. Boericke. Clarke.
