PHARMACY - verin. Veratrinum. Veratria. Veratroidia. Viridia. Melanthiaceae. An alkaloid obtained chiefly from seeds of Saba- dillaandrootsofVeratrum album. Trituration. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Cohc. Diarrhea. Dysentery. Dysuria. Esophagus, stricture. Intestines, catarrh. Jaw, snapping. Neuralgias. Pain. Paralysis. Spasms. Spine, neuralgia. Tetanus. Twitch- ings. Vomiting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Verin, is both a paralyzer and a great pain producer. It causes a sensation like electric streams in nerves, shooting Veratrinum pains like electric-shocks in veins, muscles and joints. Verin, causes tetanus, which Farrington distinguishes from the convulsive action of Nux-v. in that Verin, causes purgation and vomiting with the spasms and that general paralysis does not take place from exhaustion as with Nux-v., but from devitalization of the muscles. In large doses, it causes violent sneezing and great gastro-intestinal irritation, vomiting, purging and symptoms of collapse. The pulse is rapid, small and irregular and often involuntary muscular tremors come on. A peculiar creeping and prickling sensation in skin generally accompanies these symptoms. Externally applied to the unbroken skin it has no marked action. If rubbed on with some fat, it passes through the epidermis and causes first irritation and then paralysis of the ends of the sensory nerves and producing a prickly and creepy sensation, succeeded by numbness. This effect is produced whether applied locally or taken internally. Brunton noted this irritating action in the sensory nerves is also observed if it is inhaled through the nose, where it causes violent sneezing, which also occurs after absorption through the stomach. COMMENTS - Subsultus tendinum, fibrillary twitchings are marked. Startings and tremors occur in limbs previously affection by paralysis or pain. The pains are tingling, sparkling, prickling, burning. Twitching of facial muscles. Snapping, closure of lower jaw. Drawing pain along the spine. Shocks in head. Sensations of oppression in head, suffocation of boiling water running over the back. As if a stream of warm air or drops of hot water issued from various parts. As if a frozen atmosphere around feet to knees or cold water poured on them. “Dull pain afterwards burning in lower part of spinal column, followed by pain in bowels and prepuce, accompanied with jerking in lower limb.” RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Coffee mixed with a little lemon-juice. Compare: ( 1 ) Sabad., Aeon., Con. REFERENCES-Clarke.

Worse wet, cold weather, change of weather. Worse at night. Worse exertion, touch, pressure. Worse before and during menses. Worse before, during or after stools. Worse fright, during pain. Worse injured pride or honor. Worse opium, tobacco chewing..

full:
PHARMACY - verat. Veratrum album. White hellebore. White-flowered veratrum. N. O. Melanthacae of the Liliaceae. Alps and Pyrenees. Tincture of the rootstocks collected early in June before flowering. Historical dose: All potencies, first to thirtieth potency.

CLINICAL - Amenorrhea. Anemia. Anguish. Anasarca. Angina pectoris. Asthma. Bronchitis. Cholera. Colic. Collapse. Coma. Constipation. Convulsions. Coprophagia. Coughs. Cramps. Deafness. Debility. De- hydration. Despair. Diarrhea. Dysmenorrhea. Eclampsia. Emphysema. Epilepsy. Esophagus, stricture. Fainting. Fevers. Gastric, catarrh. Head injury. Headaches. Heatstroke. Hernia. Hydrocephalus. Hy- drophobia. Hysteria. Influenza. Insanity, religious. Intermittent fever. Intussusception. Labor, constipation. Lips, cracked. Liver, hyperemia. Lockjaw. Lungs, edema. Mania. Measles. Melancholy. Meningitis. Menstruation. Neuralgias. Nyctalopia. Paralysis. Peritonitis. Pernicious fevers. Pneumonia. Pregnancy, imaginary. Ptosis. Rheumatism. Salivation. Scarlatina. Shock. Sleep, whining. Spleen, swollen. Strokes. Sunstroke. Throat, sore. Toothache. Typhoid fever. Vertigo. Water brash. Whooping cough. Yellow fever.

HERBAL - In his Helleborism of the Ancients, Hahnemann showed that Verat. was the principal agent used at Anticyra and other places in Greece to produce the evacuations which were regarded as an essential of the “cure.” Spring was deemed the most favorable season and autumn the next. The herbal treatment was employed in diseases including “mental derangements, epilepsy, spasms of the facial muscles, hydrophobia, ptyalism of the pancreas, diseases of the spleens, goiter, hidden cancer,” etc.

HOMEOPATHIC - Verat. profoundly affects the mind, nerves, abdominal, heart, blood, blood vessels, respiration, vertex and diges- tive system. Fainting, from emotions, least exertion, slight injury with hemorrhage after stools, vomiting. Progressive weakness and emaciation in acute diseases, whooping cough, ague, etc. Sudden sinking of strength. Paralysis after debilitating losses. Profound prostration, collapse with extreme coldness, blueness and weakness. Post-operative shock with cold sweat on forehead, pale face, rapid, feeble pulse. Cold perspiration on the forehead with nearly all complaints. Vomiting, purging and cramps in limbs. Profuse, violent retching and vomiting. Breath, tongue, cold as ice. Effects are violent and sudden. Copious evacuations, vomiting, purging, salivation, sweat, or urine. Excessive dryness of all mucus surfaces. Burnings. Blood seems to run cold, blood sepsis, pyemia. Carphology. Tonic spasms or cramps in chest, bowels, hands, fingers toes, soles of feet with diarrhea. Convulsions caused by religious mania or excitement, also of children. MIND - Melancholy with stupor and mania. Head hangs down, sits brooding in silence, wants to be alone. Sits in a stupid manner, notices nothing. Sullen indifference. Amativeness. Haughtiness. Remorse. Busy restlessness. Deceitful, never speaks the truth. Despair about position in society, feels very unlucky. Delusions of impending misfortunes. Malingering. Anguish, fear of death. Imaginary diseases. Thinks herself pregnant. Nymphomania, embraces everybody even objects. Kisses everybody, before menses. Puerperal mania. Religious mania. Despairs of her salvation. Imagines the world on fire. Prays, curses, shrieks in turn. Frenzy of excitement, shrieks, curses. Cursing, howling all night. Insanity. Violent mania alternates with silence and refusal to talk. Sings, whistles, laughs. Runs from place to place. Delirium with violence, driving to madness, loquacity or lewdness during pain. Mania with desire to cut and tear things (Tarent.). Aimless wandering from home. Talks about the faults of others or scolds. Swallows his own excrement.

Head - Cold sweat on forehead in all complaints. Sensation of a lump of ice on vertex. Violent pain driving to despair, better cold. Headaches with nausea, vomiting, pale face, diarrhea, diuresis. Vertex itches during headache. Rubs forehead. Contracted features. Neck too weak to hold head up. As if cold wind blowing through head. Hair bristle, painful.

Eyes - Surrounded by dark rings. Eyes dull, clouded, yellowish. Staring eyes, turned upwards without luster. The eyeballs are turned upwards. Pain, as if the eyeballs were bruised. Lachrymation with redness. Dry, heavy lids.

Ears - Shootings in ears. Pressure and constrictive sensations in ears. Alternate sensation of coldness and heat in ears. Deafness, as from obstruction in ears. Humming with sensitiveness to noise. Roaring in ears, especially when rising from a seat.

Nose - Icy coldness of tip of nose andface. Nose grows more pointed. Smell before nose. Nosebleed from right nostril, only at night in sleep.

Face - Face very pale, blue, collapsed, cold. Features sunken. Deathly pale, on rising, bluish, pinched or distorted, frowning cold, terrified look. Cheek red (left), as if burnt. Tearing in cheeks, temples and eyes. Jaws cramp on chewing. Lockjaw. Lips blue, hang down.

Mouth - Dry in center not relieved by water. Salty saliva. Water tastes bitter, like peppermint. Toothache, teeth feel heavy as if filled with lead. Grinding of the teeth. Tongue, cold, pale, cool sensation as from peppermint. Speech lisping, stammering or as if tongue too heavy.

Throat - Hoarse, weak voice. Loss of voice. Dry, scraping or roughness. When drinking water, it seems to run outside, not going down the esophagus. Vertigo - Vertigo, especially when walking. Vertigo with cold sweats on forehead with loss of vision, sudden fainting. Vertigo from opium, abuse of tobacco and alcohol. COMMENTS - Copious discharges, stools, vomiting, urine, salivation and sweat. Discharges drain the tissues. Exhausting discharges, causing vertigo, blackness before the sight, fainting and collapse. “Rapid sinking of forces, complete prostration, cold sweat and cold breath.” Useful for collapse with icy cold sweat (Carb-v.). Fainting from emotions, from the least exertion, from retching, or from stool. Sinking feeling during hemorrhage. “Skin blue, purple, cold, wrinkled, remaining in folds when pinched.” “Face hippocratic, nose pointed.” “Hands icy cold.” “Face and legs icy cold.” “Coldness of the whole body.” “Coldness running over whole body soon after taking it.” “Continued rigor in back and over arms.” “Cold feeling in abdomen.” Coldness predominates in fever, but there is also “heat and redness of face and hands.” “Feeling of internal chill ran through him from head to toes of both feet at once.” Cold sweats, especially on the forehead. Cardiac debility, following acute diseases. Thread-like pulse. Low blood pressure. Blood loss, hypovolemic shock. Faints in morning, face red when lying down or sitting up, deadly pale, hands cold, clammy. J. S. Mitchell considered it one of the best heart stimulants in homeopathic doses. Dryness and burning felt in the nose, mouth, palate, and throat. Pneumonia. Tickling deep in trachea and bronchials. “Tickling in chest, as if it would provoke cough in middle of sternum.” Severe dehydration (Chin.), often associated with heatstroke or sunstroke. Sun headaches or sunstroke. Extreme hunger, craving for cold food and refreshing things. Craves unripe fruit, ice cold drinks, ice cream (Phos.). Great thirst for ice-cold water, during both the chill and heat of fever. Copious stools. Cholera (Camph. and Cupr.). Rice-water stools. Watery diarrhea in infants. Green vomit, stool, or urine. Characteristic diarrhea, frequent, greenish, gushing, mixed with flakes. Cutting colic with cramps commencing in hands and feet and spreading all over. Prostrating after fright, worse least movement with vomiting, cold sweat on forehead during stool followed by prostration. “Violent vomiting with profuse diarrhea.” Characteristic constipation without desire. Large, hard stools, in round black balls from inactive rectum. Frequent desire felt in epigastrium. Painful constipation in infants, children, and women after confinement. Cramps, convulsions, can be tetanic with lockjaw or epileptic. The eyes are particularly convulsed or the lids paralyzed. There may be vanishing of sight, sparks before the sight, or night-blindness. Neuralgic pains, dysmenorrhea, or migraines, accompanied by diarrhea, vomiting, cold sweat, fainting or prostration. Delirium and prolonged sleep during fever. Violence in delirium. “Fury: tears his clothing, bites her shoes to pieces and swallows the fragments, cursing, stamping, wants to run away, makes a great noise.” Mental alienation. Insanity. Delusions of personal identity. Exalted, religious or sexual mania. Puerperal mania. Nymphomania, mania for kissing everybody. Delusion that she is pregnant, and she gets physical symptoms from it (pseudocyesis). Destructive mania. Despair and hopelessness, “bowed down with great grief.” Hahnemann said that it has the power “to promote a cure of almost one-third of the insane in lunatic asylums (at all events as a homeopathic intermediate remedy).” One of the symptoms taken by Hahnemann from Grading is “He swallows his own excrement.” Goullon verified this in a case of his in which a child had a craze for eating its own feces or dung lying in the street. Verat. 2c. three times daily, cured in a month. E. F. Watts had the case of Mrs. C., who had severe nervous headaches for years. Any over-exertion, like riding or working on hot days, would excite them. They frequently began in occiput, settling sometimes in one eye, sometimes in the other. Spig. and Sil. gave no relief. One day. Watts noticed that the brow contracted and the eyelids nearly closed with the intensity of the pain. Verat. was given and relieved at once. Gee cured, with one dose of Verat. 200c, the case of Mrs. L., a widow, 43. She had sciatica for four years. Pain sharp, transient, darted upwards and downwards and from both sides to center. Heat, worse “the cooler the better.” Cold sweat with the attacks. Headache from both temples to base of brain, worse by heat. Vertex itched during attacks. Pain compelled her to move about, but no better from motion. RELATIONS-Antidotedby: (Poisonous doses) Strong coffee, Camph. (pressive pain in head with coldness of body and unconsciousness after). Aeon, (anxious, distracted state with coldness of body or burning in brain.), Chin, (other chronic disorders from abuse of Verat. e.g., daily forenoon fever.), Staph, (most cases. Teste). Antidote to: Ars., Chin., Cupr. (colic), Op., Tab., removes the bad effectsofopium and tobacco. Compare: ( 1 ) Chin., Verin. - alkaloid from seed of Sabad. - electric pains, electric shocks in muscles, fibrillary twitchings. (2) Cho. - cramps in calves. (3) Camph., Cupr., Ars., Cupr-ar. - intermittent, cold, clammy sweat. (4) Narc-po. - gastro-enteritis with much griping and cutting pain in bowels. Fainting, trembling, cold limbs, small and irregular pulse. (5) Trychosanthes - diarrhea, pain in liver, dizziness after every stool. (6) Agar-em. Agar-ph. Follows well: Ars., Am., Chin., Cupr., Ip., Camph. (cholera), Am-c., Carb-v. Bov. (in dysmenorrhea with vomiting and purging). Lyc. and Nux-v. in painful constipation of infants. Followed well by: Puls., Aeon., Bell., Cham., Rhus-t., Sep., Sulph. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke. Mutphy.

Stomach - Painful, burning at pit of stomach. Hiccough after hot drinks. Cold water brash. Copious vomiting with nausea, aggravated by drinking and least motion. Vomits or belches froth. Violent retching. Nausea while eating, cannot get food down without retching. Cold feeling in stomach. Gastric irritability with chronic vomiting of food. Vomiting, worse drinking and least motion. Great weakness after vomiting.

Abdomen - Sinking and empty feeling. Cold feeling in abdomen. Epigastrium painful. Pain in abdomen preceding stool. Painful retraction of abdomen during vomiting. Abdomen sensitive to pressure, swollen with terrible colic. Cutting colic as if bowels were twisted in knots with cramps in limbs and rapid prostration. Peritonitis. Intussusception. Reversed peristaltic action. Sensation as if hernia would protrude (Nux-v.). As if hot coals in abdomen.

Rectum - Diarrhea from drinking cold water on hot days. Constipation from inactivity of rectum with heat and headache. Constipation of babies and when produced by very cold weather. Large stools with much straining until copious and forcibly evacuated, followed by great prostration. Evacuations of cholera morbus and true cholera when vomiting accompanies the purging. Cholera morbus. Cholera infantum. Stools, thin like ribbon, flat. Watery, green, odorless or colorless (rice water) stools, or in large masses with straining, until exhausted with cold sweat. Sensations - As if he had a bad conscience or had committed a crime. As if she would have to fly away. As if in a dream. As if head would burst. As if heat and cold at same time on scalp. Hair as if electrified. Distress over heart and epigastrium. As if something alive running from stomach into throat. As from ravenous hunger, pain in stomach. As of knives cutting bowels. As of hot coals in abdomen. Sinking, empty feeling in abdomen. As if pregnant or in throes of childbirth. As of knives cutting bowels. Electric pains occur in various parts.

Female - Menses too early, too profuse, suppressed. Dysmenorrhea with coldness, purging, cold sweat. Faints from least exertion. Menorrhagia with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. Nymphomania, before menses, from disappointed love, unsatisfied passion in lying-in women. Eclampsia. Puerperal mania. Food - Thirst for cold water, but is vomited as soon as swallowed. Craves ice water, wants everything cold or sour, drinks, juicy fruits and salt. Voracious appetite, gnawing hunger in spite of nausea and vomiting. Averse to warm food. All fruits disagree, causing painful distention. Potatoes and green vegetables disagree. Better eating meat and drinking milk.

Chest - Spasmodic contraction of muscles of chest. Oppressed chest, with pain in side during an inspiration. Sensation of fullness in chest, which induces frequent belchings. Constitutions - Suited to the extremes of age, children and old people. For lean, choleric or melancholy persons. Young people and women of a sanguine or nervo-sanguine temperament. People who are habitually cold and deficient in vital reaction. Persons of gay disposition, of fitful mood. Anemic persons.

Heart - Palpitations with anxiety and rapid audible respiration. Visible palpitations with chorea. Weak, cutting at heart. Intermittent, feeble, slow, thready pulse. Intermittent action of heart in feeble persons with some hepatic obstruction. Tobacco heart from chewing. Blood runs like cold water through veins.

Back - Neck so weak, child can scarcely keep it erect, worse whooping cough. Pain crampy between scapulae better motion. Bruised feeling in sacral region. Causations - Post-operative shock. Shock of injury. Ill effects of fright, disappointed love, injured pride or honor. Suppressed rashes. Opium, tobacco, alcohol.

Limbs - Brachial neuralgia, paralytic and bruising pain in arms. Fine burning in arms, right to left. Arms feel full and swollen. Tingling in hands and fingers. Feet icy cold. Cramps in calves during stools. Sciatica, pains like electric flashes in legs, must sit up and let legs hang down out of bed. Soreness and tenderness of joints. Difficulty in walking, like paralysis from debility. Pains in feet or knees as if heavy stones were tied to parts, must move about. Lungs - Air seems too hot. Asthma, worse in damp, cold weather, better bending head back. Tickling down throat into lungs. Rattling in chest. Much mucus in bronchial tubes that cannot be coughed up. Coarse rales. Chronic bronchitis in the aged (Hippoz.). Continuous violent cough with retching, worse cold drinks. Neglected whooping cough with complication. Barking cough with belchings, worse warm room. Involuntary urination with cough. Cough on entering warm room from cold air (Bry.). Hollow cough, tickling low down with blue face. Urine escapes when coughing.

Sleep - Wakes at night trembling. Starts as if frightened. Yawning. Nocturnal sleeplessness with great anguish. Sleep, long, uninterrupted, heavy, too profound. Sleeps with the arms passed over the head. Dreams with frightened waking and a fixed idea that the dream is true, of quarrels. Dreams are anxious, of being bitten by a dog and cannot escape, of being hunted of robbers.

Skin - Blue, cold, clammy, cold as death. Skin flabby and without elasticity. Wrinkling of skin of hands and feet. Cold sweat. Skin feels scorched. Dry tetters. Measles, tardy and pale. Nettle rash. Scarlatina in hot weather.

Modalities - Children feel better when carried about quickly. Better from warmth, covering, hot drinks. Better lying, walking. Better eating meat, milk. Worse from drinking, cold drinks. Worse wet, cold weather, change of weather. Worse at night. Worse exertion, touch, pressure. Worse before and during menses. Worse before, during or after stools. Worse fright, during pain. Worse injured pride or honor. Worse opium, tobacco chewing.

Kidneys - Scanty, red brown urine. Thick, greenish, suppressed, involuntary during cough.

Temperature - Chill with extreme coldness and thirst. General coldness, icy, on vertex, nose tongue, mouth, limbs, sweat. Internal heat with cold surface, when drinking. Fevers showing external coldness only.

full:
PHARMACY - verat-n. Veratrum nigrum. Dark-flowered veratrum. N. O. Melanthacae. Austria and Siberia. Tincture of fresh leaves and succulent flower-stalks. Historical dose: All potencies.

HOMEOPATHIC - Cooper gave a few observa- tions for Verat-n. The plant, he said, has much the same botanical characters as Verat, but the flowers are dark-colored. It is native to Austria and Siberia. Verat-n. has headaches, protracted menstruation. Tinnitus aurium.

Head - Constant headache when attempting to move or exert the brain. Fierce headache threatening acute mania. REFERENCES - Clarke.

Ears - Constant buzzing of left ear for two weeks with tenderness of meatus and intense sensitiveness of the head to the motion of an omnibus with beclouding of the brain and pain in nape of neck.

Female - Period continually returning, sometimes light-colored and slight in quantity and sometimes profuse with weak feeling in back.

name: Veratrum Viride
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from rubbing, lying with head low. Better eating. Pain in head better by pressure. Closing eyes and resting head helps vertigo. Worse from raising up, lying on back. Worse cold, sunstroke, going from warm to cold. Worse morning, on waking, evening. Worse after confinement. Motion aggravates, sudden motion causes faintness and blindness. Walking causes blindness. Lying down aggravates headache, breathing..

CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Amenorrhea. Asthma. Bunions. Carphology. Cecum.…
full:
PHARMACY - verat-v. Veratrum viride. American hellebore. Veratrum helonias viridis. Indian Poke. N. O. Melanthacae of the Liliaceae. Tincture of fresh root gathered in autumn. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Amaurosis. Amenorrhea. Asthma. Bunions. Carphology. Cecum. Chilblains. Chorea. Colds. Convulsions. Delirium. Diplopia. Diaphragmitis. Dysmenorrhea. Eclampsia. Esophagitis. Esophagus, spasms. Erysipelas. Headaches. Heart, disorders. Hiccoughs. Hyperpyrexia. Influenza. Malarial fever. Measles. Meningitis. Menses, suppressed. Muscle, pains. Orchitis. Pneumonia. Proctalgia. Puerperal, convulsions. Puerperal mania. Pupils, dilated. Sleep, dream filled. Spinal, congestion. Spleen, congested. Strokes. Sunstroke. Typhoid fever. Uremia. Uterus, congestion.

HERBAL - Growing side by side, Verat and Verat-v. are scarcely distinguishable when not in flower. Millspaugh, however, said that though much like Verat. in its minor points, Verat-v. is strikingly different in general appearance. Verat-v. having a much more pointed leaf, panicles looser and more compound, the racemes of Verat. being more compact and as a whole cylindrical, those of Verat- v. scattered, compound and craggy. Verat. flourishes in mountain meadows, Verat-v. grows in swamps and wet meadows and along mountain creeks from Canada to the Carolinas. Through this confusion, an accidental proving of the latter has been included in the pathogenesis of Verat-v. The plants belong to different orders, though it must be admitted there is a close resemblance in their effects. The root of Verat-v. contains Veratrine and the other alkaloids found in the root of Verat., but in different proportions.

HOMEOPATHIC - Burt proved Squibb’s liquid extract of Verat-v, and said he found no other preparation satisfactory. Hinsdale noted that it is known clinically that such diseases as Tiegel’s contracture, Thompson’s disease, athetosis and muscular paralysis present a symptomatology quite like that produced by Verat-v. upon muscular tissue. Verat-v. produces violent congestive conditions, base of brain, medulla, lungs with nausea and vomiting and weakness. Stomach, heart and capillaries are also affected. Congestions, especially to lungs, base of brain with nausea and vomiting. Congestive stage and early manifestations of hepatization in pneumonia. Twitchings and convulsions, here and there during sleep, jerking and trembling, threatened with convulsions. Chorea, twitching, contortions, unaffected by sleep, froth about the lips. Lies with head low. Continuous jerking of the head, sexual excitement. Spasms with violent shrieks, opisthotonos, before and after menses. Children tremble as if frightened and on verge of spasm. Furious delirium. Muscular prostration, pseudo-hypertrophic muscular paralysis. Great prostration. Sudden effects. Sudden fainting, prostration, nausea. Fainting, nausea. Erratic motion, staggering. Lowers blood-pressure. Numbness. Uneasy sensation in the whole body. Effects of sunstroke. Burn- Veratrum viride ing in different places tongue, pharynx, gullet of skin which is cold with prickling. Zigzag of temperature. As if damp clothing on arms and legs or clothes would not fit him, seemed as if they were scratching him somewhere. Especially adapted to full-blooded and plethoric persons. Bloated, lividface. Rheumatism of heart. Paroxysms of auricular fibrillation. Induces fall of both systolic and diastolic blood pressure. General pulsations. Eclampsia. Verat-v. has a pronounced action on the esophagus, it causes a sort of ruminating action or reversed peristalsis. The least food causes vomiting. Red streak down the center of the tongue. Farrington noted it for esophagitis. Uremia. MIND - Loquacity with exaltation of ideas. Suspiciousnature.Fearofseeingherphysician, of being poisoned. Quarrelsome. Delirium, furious, screams, howls, strikes incessant muttering. Mania, puerperal. Carphology.

Head - Head retracted. Pain from nape of neck, cannot hold head up. Congestion intense, almost apoplectic. Hot head, bloodshot eyes. Bloated, livid face. Hippocratic face. Sunstroke, head full, throbbing arteries (Bell., Glon., Usn.). Aching on vertex and between eyes. Strokes. Pain up occiput with dim vision and dilated pupils. Constant jerking or nodding of the head (chorea), throbs on raising up. Meningitis, basilar.

Eyes - Wild, staring during delirium. Blood shot. Pupils dilated. Vision of red spots, purple, on closing eyes, unsteady. Double vision.

Ears - Deafness from moving quickly with faintness. Cold and pale.

Nose - Pinched and blue. Rapid and con tinued sneezing with warm biting feeling in mouth.

Face - Face flushed, livid turgid, but becomes faint on sitting up. Convulsive twitching of facial muscles (Agar.). Tension across malar bones. Chewing motions of the jaw.

Mouth - Taste like musty odor. Odor from mouth like chloroform or ether. Foul. Increased saliva. Mouth feels as if scalded. Drawn at one corner.

Throat - Burning in gullet, esophagitis. As if as ball rising in.

Stomach - Gastritis. Burning in stomach and esophagus. Stomach seems to press against the spine. Constrictive pain increased by warm drinks. Hiccoughs, excessive and painful withspasmsofesophagus. Nausea and vomiting. Vomiting, violent without nausea. Smallest quantity of food or drink immediately rejected.

Abdomen - Pain above pelvis with soreness. Cutting at navel to groin. Pain in bowels runs into scrotum. Enteritis with high fever.

Rectum - Tenesmus and burning in rectum, better during and after stools. Sensations - Confused feeling in head as if head would burst. Tongue as if scalded. As if a ball rising into esophagus. As if stomach tightly drawn against spine. As of a load on chest. As of galvanic shocks in limbs. As if damp clothing on arms and legs. As if boiling water poured over parts. As if ankles distorted.

Female - Menstrual colic before the appearance of the discharge with strangury. Suppressed menstruation with congestion to head (Bell.). Rigid os (Bell., Gels.). Puerperal fever, convulsions with mania or mania continues after convulsions have ceased. Food - Very thirsty, drinks little, which ameliorates for a short time.

Chest - Burning in chest. Constitutions - Suited to full-blooded plethoric persons.

Heart - Constant, dull, burning pain in region of heart. Valvular disease. Beating of pulses throughout body, especially in right thigh. Pulse slow, soft, weak, irregular intermittent. Rapid pulse, low tension (Tab., Dig.).

Back - Aching pain in back of neck and shoulders. Cannot hold the head up. Opisthotonos. Causations - Sunstroke. Suppressed menses, lochia.

Limbs - Acute rheumatism. Severe pain in joints and muscles. Violent electric-like shocks in limbs. Cramps in legs, feet, soles, fingers toes. Convulsive twitching. Pain about the condyles. Pulsation felt in thighs. Restless hands during delirium. Vesicles on hands. Lungs - Dyspnea. Difficult breathing. Slow and heavy breathing, as of a load on chest. Congestion of lungs. Pneumonia, with faint feeling in stomach and violent congestion. Croup. Violent cough from very start.

Sleep - Sleeplessness. Dreams of drowning of being on water. Coma.

Skin - Hot sweating. Tingling and prickling in skin. Cold, clammy, bluish. Erysipelas with brain symptoms. Erythema. Itching in different parts better rubbing.

Modalities - Better from rubbing, lying with head low. Better eating. Pain in head better by pressure. Closing eyes and resting head helps vertigo. Worse from raising up, lying on back. Worse cold, sunstroke, going from warm to cold. Worse morning, on waking, evening. Worse after confinement. Motion aggravates, sudden motion causes faintness and blindness. Walking causes blindness. Lying down aggravates headache, breathing.

Tongue - Tongue, white as if bleached. Tongue dry with red streak down center. Vertigo - Vertigo with nausea and sudden prostration, better closing eyes and resting head. COMMENTS - Hale was instrumental in introducing Verat-v. to homeopathy, using it in fevers and particularly in pneumonia. Burt made a heroic proving of the liquid extract and his infant daughter (twenty-one months) very nearly died from taking a few drops of the tincture from a phial. In two minutes she began vomiting. Coffee and camphor were given as antidotes. In five minutes her jaws were rigid, pupils widely dilated, face blue, hands and feet cold, no pulse at wrist. Her abdomen and back were rubbed with camphor, when she went into spasms with violent shrieks. These spasms were frequently repeated, a hot path being most effective in relaxing the muscles. Vomiting ropy mucus kept up for three hours. Pulseless, hands and feet shriveled. After three and a half hours she slept quietly and soundly and next morning was well but a little weak. The congestive symptoms and also of nausea and vomiting, form one of the leading indications of Verat-v. in a great variety of cases. Sensations of fullness. “Head feels full and heavy, rush of blood to the head, face flushed, buzzing in the ears, chest constricted or oppressed as from a heavy load,” point to the congestive tendency. Congestion at the base of brain, chest, spine, stomach. Slowing of the heart’s action is a leading effect of the provings (from its action on the heart muscle and cardiac ganglia Dig. on the pneumogastric). Violent pains attending inflammation. Head full, throbbing of arteries, sensitive to sound, double or partial vision. Chorea, “twitchings during sleep.” “Constant jerking or nodding of the head, jerking and trembling. Threatened with convulsions,” are other leading symptoms. Puerperal convulsions, Verat-v. has only succeeded when nauseating doses have been given. Used locally and internally in muscular and joint rheumatism, and in chorea an application to the spine of the tincture, diluted with spirit, has proved a serviceable adjunct. Verat-v. has been used to “knock down” fever in the same way as Aeon. Nash pointed out that there is some risk in this. When Ve- rat-v. was first introduced he used it largely and successfully in a number of cases, but in one case which appeared to be going on favorably, the patient died suddenly. This he attributed to the Verat- v. D. McLellan was sent for in the middle of the night to see an old woman Whom he found sitting up in bed gasping for breath and blue. Rapid congestion of the lungs had occurred. The attack had come on suddenly. Verat-v. quickly rescued the patient from a condition of imminent peril. Clarke with the 30c, cured a man, 56 of dim sight as if scales over it, numbness, pain in head as if a tight band were around it, rush of blood to head, sleeplessness. Dreaming about water is a characteristic which he has confirmed. RELATIONS - Antidoted by: Hot coffee. Antidote to: Strychnine, use fluid extract, 20-40 drops. Compare: (1) Puerperal convulsions, Gels, has dull, drowsy state of mind. (2) Verat-v., apoplectic condition between the fits, face red, eyes congested, violent convulsive twitches. (3) Congestions, Ferr-p., Bell. (4) Plethora, Aeon. (5) Chorea, Hyos. (6) Pneumonia with engorgement, Sang. (Verat-v. more marked arterial tension). (7) Scalded tongue, Sang. (8) Tetanus, Nux-v., Hyper. (9) Rheumatic fever,Bry., Sal-ac. (lO)Sunstroke, double or partial vision. Glon., Gels. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Kidneys - Cystitis with fever. Urine scanty with cloudy sediment.

Temperature - Hyperpyrexia or rapidly oscillating temperature with sweat. Cold clammy or hot sweat. Cerebrospinal, suppurative, acute rheumatic, fever. Fever high in the evening, below normal in the morning. Suppurative fevers with great variation of temperature.

name: Verbascum Thapsus
author: Murphy
modalities: Modalities: Better from taking deep inspirations. Worse touch, pressure. Worse cold, drafts, change of temperature. Worse from stooping, walking, talking. Worse sneezing, biting hard (inferior dental nerve). Worse 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., twice a day, at same hour..
constitution: Anus, itching. Bedwetting. Colic. Constipation. Cough. Deafness. Ear, pain. Hemorrhoids. Hoarseness. Neuralgia. Prosopalgia. Tumors. Urinary, incontinence.
keynote: PHARMACY - verb. Verbascumthapsus. Mullein oil. Verbascumthapsiforme. Oleum mullein. Great Mullein. N. O. Scrophulariaceae. Tincture of fresh plant at the commencement of flowering. To prepare mullein oil, fill a bottle with the blossoms from the Verbascum thapsus, cork it tight…
full:
PHARMACY - verb. Verbascumthapsus. Mullein oil. Verbascumthapsiforme. Oleum mullein. Great Mullein. N. O. Scrophulariaceae. Tincture of fresh plant at the commencement of flowering. To prepare mullein oil, fill a bottle with the blossoms from the Verbascum thapsus, cork it tight and hang in the sun for four or five weeks. By that time there will be an oily liquid distilled. Mix with ten percent of alcohol. Tincture of the whole plant beginning to flower. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Anus, itching. Bedwetting. Colic. Constipation. Cough. Deafness. Ear, pain. Hemorrhoids. Hoarseness. Neuralgia. Prosopalgia. Tumors. Urinary, incontinence.

HERBAL - The Treasury of Botany said, “The thick woolly leaves of Verbascum thapsus, the Great Mullein, have a mucilaginous, bitter taste and a decoction of them is employed in domestic practice in catarrhs and diarrhea. “The leaves are also used as emollient applications to hard tumors and in pulmonary complaints in cattle hence one of its popular names is Bullock’s Lung-wort. It is also called Adam’s flannel from its flannellike leaves.” Among its traditional uses Gerarde mentioned it as a remedy for hemorrhoids and as applications for itching hemorrhoids or anal itching. An ointment is made of the tincture. Gerarde said that the oil of the yellow flowers is also curative in hemorrhoids. The flowers contain, according to Millspaugh, “A yellow volatile oil and fatty acid, free malic and phosphoric acids and their ate salts of lime, a yellow resinous coloring matter and the general plant constituents including an uncrystallisable sugar.” An oil prepared from the flowers has been found useful locally in cases of deafness or earache.

HOMEOPATHIC - Verb, has a pronounced action on the inferior maxillary branch of the fifth pair of the cranial nerves, on the ear and respiratory tract and bladder. Catarrhs and colds with periodical prosopalgia, spasmodic effects, neuralgias. Nervous and bronchial coughs. Urinary irritation. Tearing, stitching, cramping squeezing, crushing, paralyzing pains. Intermittent pains.

Eyes - Pains in eyes, as from contraction of the sockets with burning in eyes. Sight confused, as if directed through a veil.

Ears - Earache. Numbness in left ear. Otalgia with a sense of obstruction. Deafness from getting water in, as in swimming or as if stopped by a valve. Dry, scaly condition of meatus (locally).

Nose - Profuse coryza from frontal sinuses with hot, burning, profuse lachrymation. Sensation of stoppage of larynx and ears.

Face - Neuralgia affecting zygoma, temporo-maxillary joint and ear (Meny.), particularly of left side with lachrymation, coryza and sensation as if parts were crushed with tongs. Talking, sneezing and change of temperature aggravate the pains, also, pressing teeth together. Pains seem to come in flashes, excited by least movement, occurring periodically at same hour in morning and afternoon each day. Food - Mawkish taste with fetid breath. Hunger without relish for food. Insatiable thirst.

Mouth - Copious accumulation of salty saliva in the mouth. Root of tongue brown. Tongue of abrownish yellow color, loaded with viscid mucus in morning and after dinner.

Throat - Very severe pain in throat on swallowing. Hoarseness, voice deep, harsh, sounds like a trumpet, “bassoprofundo.’’ Sensation of obstruction in the larynx. Vertigo - Vertigo when pressing one cheek while supporting the head. Vertigo sudden, as from pressure on whole head. COMMENTS - Mullein oil is used, locally, for earache and dry, scaly condition of meatus. Also for teasing cough at night or lying down. Bedwetting, five-drop doses night and morning Cushing introduced this now rather well- known remedy to the medical profession in 1884. He wrote “My father’s house was the home for all poor tramps, as well as ministers, etc. He fell into the river, got water in his ears and was quite deaf for months. “A blind man had called, heard loud conversation, asked the cause, etc., then said for kindness received he would tell us how Verbascum thapsus to make something that would surely cure him and it was worth a thousand dollars in New York City. “We made the oil, put it in his ears at night and he was well in the morning. For years we kept a bottle of it and it traveled all around the towns and did wonders. That was when I was a youngster.” Hering, in “Hearing and Ears,” noticed “In Germany flowers of Verbascum thapsus put in a dark-colored bottle, hung up in the sunlight, give in two or three weeks an oily fluid which has cured many old people and children.” Hahnemann proved Verb, and his proving confirmed many of the old uses. It produced neuralgic pains of very great intensity, pressing and sharp and especially in the facial bones, navel and limbs and a peculiar cough. Chronic dermatitis of the external meatus and drumhead or exfoliation after furuncle. Catarrhal inflammation of the tympanum Suppurative disease of the tympanum. Accumulations of debris in the case of perforation, scarred eardrum. Chronic inflammation of the eyes. Chilblains. Burns. Nash described a “Cough, deep, hollow, hoarse in sound like a trumpet.” He cured many cases and always used it low. It is more especially a night cough. It occurs in children during their sleep. Mullein was used as a popular specific for tuberculosis, the leaves being boiled in milk, which was then strained and given warm. W. B. McCoy gave several illustrations. According to him Verb, (i.e., the “oil”) has a “soothing effect on the entire nervous system in many cases acting as a soporific.” In summer diarrhea he gave one to four drops in two ounces of warm water, a teaspoonful every hour. In bedwetting or dribbling of urine one-drop doses in warm water three or four times a day. Among his cases were those of two boys who had become deaf from getting water in their ears when swimming. They were cured by having three drops of the oil instilled “in each ear alternately night and morning.” O. S. Laws cured a youth of 16 of bed-wetting with fifteen drops of the oils three times a day. The oil plainly acts on the indications of the proving and may be regarded as an alternative preparation to the official tincture. It might be called Verbasci oleum. Mr. Kemmis spent a large amount of money treating with various physicians for what they pronounced a rose cancer and without any relief. An Indian woman told him to use mullein oil. He distilled it (by sun exposure) and for a short time bathed the cancer with the oil. The growth of cancer was permanently checked, but it was not healed. Mr. K. lived, perhaps, forty years after the treatment was used and the cancer never again bothered him. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Rhus-a., Caust., Plat., Sphing. - pain in zygoma. (2) in neuralgia. Plat. - pressure, Stann. - gradually increasing and decreasing. (3) Deep cough, Cor-r., Dros., Spong., Sulph. (4)Sheep-dung stools, Mag-m. (5) Cough from tickling in chest, Verat. REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke. Clarke. Murphy.

Stomach - Aching of stomach. Sensation of emptiness at pit of stomach, which disappears with a rumbling below left ribs. Frequent hiccough. Regurgitation of insipid serum. Empty or else bitter risings with nausea.

Abdomen - As of a lump or twisting around navel. Incessant gurgling and rumbling beneath left ribs. Inflation of the abdomen, violent and painful pressure on navel. Pinchings and gripings in abdomen.

Rectum - Many bowel movements a day with twisting about navel. Feces hard like sheep-dung and expelled with effort. Fearful diarrhea. Hemorrhoids, obstructing stools, itching and inflamed. Inflamed and painful hemorrhoids. Pain extends deep down, causing contraction of anal sphincter. Sensations - As if everything would press out at forehead. As if temples were pinched and crushed. As if ears were stopped up. As if something had fallen before ear. As if left ramus of jaw were pressed against upper jaw. As if nose and larynx were stopped up. As if intestines were adherent to wall of abdomen and were being torn away. As of a twist around navel. As if cold water were poured over side of body from shoulder to thigh.

Male - Pollutions without lewd dreams.

Chest - Shooting in chest, sometimes with oppression and obstructed respiration. Stitch :s in the chest. Red nodosity near xiphoid cartilage, painful when pressed upon.

Back - Lancinations in the back and shoulder blades. Sharp intermittent stitches in left scapula. Backache worse from pressure.

Limbs - Stitching in the limbs. Stiffness and soreness ofjoints of lower limbs. Lower limbs feel heavy. Cramp-like pain in soles, right foot and knee. Neuralgic pain in left ankle. Thumb feels numb. Lungs - Asthma. Catarrh with hoarseness and stuffed chest. Frequent attacks of deep, hollow cough with sound like a trumpet, better deep breathing. Soreness in pharynx, cough during sleep. Dry, hoarse cough worse at night. Cough, nervous without waking.

Sleep - Strong disposition to sleep after a meal. Disturbed sleep, at night with tossing. Short sleep at night, lasting only until 4 a.m. with anxious, frightful dreams of wars and dead bodies.

Modalities - Better from taking deep inspirations. Worse touch, pressure. Worse cold, drafts, change of temperature. Worse from stooping, walking, talking. Worse sneezing, biting hard (inferior dental nerve). Worse 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., twice a day, at same hour.

Kidneys - Increased urine with pressure in bladder. Burning urination. Constant dribbling. Bedwetting, at night, worse coughing.

Temperature - Internal coldness of whole body of hands and feet, perceptible also externally. Shuddering, especially on one side of body, as if it were bathed in cold water.

name: Verbena Hastata
author: Murphy
constitution: Depression. Epilepsy. Insomnia. Intermittent, fever. Mental, exhaustion. Poison oak.
keynote:
PHARMACY - verbe-h. Verbena hastata. Blue Vervain. Ironweed. Vervain.Tincture of entire fresh plant. N. O. Verbenaceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Depression. Epilepsy. Insomnia. Intermittent, fever. Mental, exhaustion. Poison oak.

HERBAL -…
full:
PHARMACY - verbe-h. Verbena hastata. Blue Vervain. Ironweed. Vervain.Tincture of entire fresh plant. N. O. Verbenaceae. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Depression. Epilepsy. Insomnia. Intermittent, fever. Mental, exhaustion. Poison oak.

HERBAL - Verbena, in the form of a tea as a diuretic drink, is used by Vannier to aid elimination in tuberculosis cases. In epilepsy it must be continued for a long time.

HOMEOPATHIC - Verbe-h. affects the skin and nervous system. Nervous depression, weakness and irritation and spasms. Promotes the absorption of blood and allays pain in bruises. Passive congestion. Epilepsy, insomnia, mental exhaustion. In epilepsy, it brightens up the patient’s mental powers and helps the constipation. Intermittent fever. Poison-oak. Vesicular erysipelas. COMMENTS - Anshutz reported “An extract from a paper by Dr. J. N. White, Queen City, Texas, detailing at length the case of a five- year old boy, who after six weeks of whooping cough, developed epileptic symptoms, having as high as twelve spasms in twenty-four hours. “After two months of treatment with such remedies as Sol-c., Sulfonal, Hyos., Cann- i., Calomel, Zinc., etc. with no results, the cases was given Verbena. “Another doctor was in consultation and we quote: I told my friend (the Doctor) that when he became satisfied with the zinc treatment, I wanted to try another eclectic remedy. (The Doctor was an allopath). He was perfectly willing and I put him on Verbena hastata tincture, twelve drops, every four hours, skipping the dose at midnight. “After we both took the case we decided, as there were no curative properties in the sulfonal, we would drop it and not use anything to control the paroxysms. Consequently the boy seemed to get worse to the parents, as now he would have several falling spells a day. “From the first dose of the Verbena hastata the boy began to improve. He would have contractions of the muscles of the arms and legs and look wild for a minute or more for the first week, but after that he never had another symptom. We kept him on the medicine, as above, for six weeks and now he takes twelve drops three times a day. “He has not had any symptom in over two months and all that wild vacant look is gone and he plays, eats, sleeps, etc., as if he had never been troubled with epilepsy.” REFERENCES - Anshutz. Boericke.

name: Veronal

full:
PHARMACY - vesi. Vesicaria communis. N. O. Cruciferae. Alyssineae. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Albuminuria. Bladder, pain. Cystitis. Dropsy. Gleet. Gonorrhea. Gravel. Hematuria. Kidney, pain. Prostatitis.

HERBAL - According to the Treasury of Botany, Vesicaria is a genus of Cruciferae, natives of the Northern Hemisphere, distinguished by the globose or oboid inflated pouch with hemispherical valves and numerous seeds (generally four to six) in each cell. They are herbs, sometimes shrubby at the base with oblong or linear entire or ripened leaves and terminal racemes of yellow flowers. The Vesicaria communis tincture is prepared from the whole plant collected fresh. It has been an old home remedy in various parts of Germany for various forms of urinary troubles attendant on gonorrhea, gravel, cystitis, nephralgia, prostatitis etc.

HOMEOPATHIC - George R. Shafter found nephralgia, acute cystitis, irritable bladder, following acute cystitis, and chronic cystitis. particularly amenable to Vesi. Its main indication is a great burning and smarting in urethra with a frequent desire to pass urine. Marked strangury (Thlaspi., Berb., Sars., Chim. and Canth.). COMMENTS - Shafter recorded many cases, including that of T. S., age 67, who suffered from kidney pain, for which he had received morphine injections in former attacks. Vesi. in 15 drop doses every fifteen minutes, gave marked relief in two hours, which in six hours was complete. S. B., age 57, had cystitis from cold, high fever, eating, burning pain on voiding urine, which was drop by drop. Vesi. tincture in 10 drop doses, cured in two days. A woman, age 39, had pain in her back, brick-dust sediment in urine, hands and feet swelling so she could hardly close her hands or walk. Vesi. tincture cured. Man, age 65, with an irritable bladder, had to rise twenty to thirty times in the night. Vesi. tincture in 20-drop doses, relieved quickly and cured in six weeks. C. M., 89, chronic cystitis, passing large quantities of mucus, pus. The bladder was at first washed out with boric acid solution, then Vesi. tincture 20 drops every two hours, were given. Improvement followed and in two hours the boric acid washing was stopped and Vesic. given every four hours. This finally cured. Gonorrhea with smarting and burning on urination and thick creamy discharge. Vesi. tincture a drachm every four hours, soon cured. Gonorrhea, female after being treated for two weeks with injections, was cured in seven days with Vesi. tincture in drachm doses. Cowperthwaite succeeded in causing albumen to disappear from the urine even in cases of actual Bright’s disease. He added that “it is necessary to use only the imported [i.e., European] tincture, 15 drops every four hours” (There are several Vesicarias native to North America). A. L. Davison treated Mrs. P. for general dropsy of a year’s standing, was in uremic spasms when first seen, the kidneys having ceased to secrete urine. Vesi. tincture was prescribed, 15 drops in a teaspoonful of water every hour until urine was freely secreted, then three times a day. The second day the kidneys were pouring out urine and watery stools were passed. In a week all dropsy had disappeared. Bancroft treated Mrs. T. for irritable kidneys and bladder with polyuria. After a time the urine became bloody with occasional thin clots. Previously there had been for some months a thick, yellow sediment. Vesi. tincture, 6 drops four times a day and later 15 drops three times a day, taken persistently, effected a cure. Halbert reported the case of Mr. H., a young man whose occupation involved much outdoor exercise and who contracted a chill and had lumbago in consequence. Under an “orificial” surgeon his rectum was operated on and the sphincter stretched. Thereafter he had fever, rigors and acute prostatitis. Urination was painful and difficult and soon hematuria ensued. The pain and nervous exhaustion were so extreme that he was put into hospital and for a time only relieved by injections of morphine. The urine contained albumen, blood-clots, much pus. Urine was only passed by means of the catheter and defecation was extremely painful. Vesi. lx was given hourly and great relief followed. The painful tenesmus was alleviated and he was soon able to pass urine without the catheter. In three weeks he was able to go home. Shafer gave Cact. and Thlaspi. in a case of dropsy from heart disease in a woman, age 48. These gave little relief. He then gave Vesi. in combination with the others. There was marked relief in twenty-four hours and in ten days the dropsy had disappeared. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Thlaspi, Berb., Sars., Chim. and Canth. (2) In Gravel, Coc- c., Urt-u., Thlaspi. (3) Hematuria, Chin-s., Fic., Phos. (4) Prostatic affections, Hydrang., Solid., Sabal. (5) Cystitis, Chim. Compatible: Cact., Thlaspi. REFERENCES - Clarke.

PHARMACY - vesp. Vespa crabro. Wasp. Vespa maculata. Vespa vulgaris. European hornet. Giant hornet. Yellow-jacket. American hornet. N. O. Hymenoptera, Sub-order Vespidae. Tincture of the insects. Historical dose: All potencies.

CLINICAL - Abscesses, multiple. Alopecia. Bee stings. Bedwetting. Boils. Cervix, ulcerated. Chemosis. Edema. Erythema. Fainting. Flushing. Glottis, spasm. Indigestion. Ophthalmia. Ovary, pain. Quinsy. Tongue, swelling. Uterus, ulcerated. Vertigo.

HOMEOPATHIC - The symptoms are mostly the results of stings although Berridge proved Vesp. 30c on three persons. The symptoms included low spirits, pain in right ear, nausea Vespa crabro with faint feeling and trembling, pain in left side of the neck on waking. Stinging, burning pains, as if pierced with red hot needles. Stinging piercing deeply, as if a hook were pulled out. Sudden stinging and burning in cheek. Burning of the part, then swelling, red with burning pain. Sudden tearing. Indurated feeling. Cutting like electric shocks through all joints. Arm, head and face swollen. Eyes red and twitching. Red lines along absorbents. Itching over whole body. Insensibility. Vasomotor symptoms of skin and mucus membranes. Nerve and muscular excitement. Trembling, quaking with chattering of teeth. Convulsions, loss of consciousness, does not answer when spoken to, looks into space, has no recollection of the attack. Dizzy, better lying on back. Faintness, all day with trembling and nausea. Numbness and blindness. Pulse slow, heart’s action scarcely perceptible. Feeling as if dying at night. Heat especially overpowers him. Feet were cold except in summer, when they burned uncomfortably. Perspiration on parts laid on with itching. Axillary glands swollen with soreness of upper arms. Nausea and vomiting, followed by creeping chills from feet upward. Cramping pain in bowels. Frequent urination. Weakness with bedwetting. Pain in sacrum extending up back. Disorders of left ovary with tenderness. MIND - Terrible anxiety. Low-spirited. Insensibility. Unconsciousness with inability to move.

Head - Fainting and loss of consciousness. A violent heat came over him, felt sick, then turned giddy and spun around and around like a top until he fell, staggered to the house, got into a chair in a moment, fell out of it, almost fainting, dashed water into his face, at length was able to lie down on his bed. Headache. Face and head swollen and inflamed. Alopecia.

Eyes - Injection of right conjunctiva. Chemosis of conjunctiva. Inflammation of right eye with baggy swelling of conjunctiva. Itching of right lid in evening with swelling afterwards pain in lid and ball. Erysipelatous inflammation of lid, whole side of face painful and swollen.

Ears - Sticking deep in right ear. Purulent catarrh of middle ears.

Face - Pain in cheek as if pierced with red- hot needles, suddenly awakening him from sleep and recurring periodically. Painfill and swollen. Erysipelatous inflammation of lids. Swelling of mouth and throat with violent burning pains. Face livid. Face smooth, dark red, bloated. Anxious look.

Mouth - Tongue swollen and tense, swelling below chin, between that and hyoid bone, pain in a point in middle line of tongue, swollen, red, rounded, filled the mouth, immovable, could not speak, only mumbled, swallowing was painful and difficult. Swelling of palate with inflammation. Peculiar taste, as when a nest of wasps is disturbed, worse heat. Sensations - As if a harpoon were sticking deep in and were drawn on. As if pierced with red-hot needles. As if a cutting instrument were piercing all joints like an electric shock. Cold, chilly sensation around sting. As if left shoulder joint were sprained. As if about to suffocate. As if dying.

Throat - Swelling of throat, soreness, heat of throat. Hypertrophied tonsils which secreted a cheesy matter. Pharyngeal varicosis. Vertigo - Fainting, loss of consciousness. COMMENTS - W. Rowbotham was stung on the right cheek. The next day, about 4 a.m., he was suddenly awakened by burning, stinging pain in cheek, “as if pierced with red- hot needles” and soreness and smarting along the lymphatics. After bathing the face he got to sleep and was again suddenly awakened by the pain two hours later, which recurred periodically in paroxysm, throughout the day. Burnett observed a case of a sting on the tongue in a woman. The tongue entirely filled the buccal cavity. The patient’s appearance was exactly like one suffering from severe synanche. The swelling was diffuse and deep- seated. There was not much redness. Berridge demonstrated that the poison of the hornet and the wasp may answer to each other’s indications. He cured with Vesp. 100,000c. (Fincke) a symptom produced by Vespa vulgaris, namely, chemosis of the right eye. Mr. X. age 66, had his right eye inflamed for six days. When seen there was redness of right lower lid, baggy swelling of conjunctiva partly covering the cornea when pressed upward, lachrymation of right eye worse in open air, right lids adhere in morning. Vesp. three times daily cured in a few days. E. T. Blake cured with Vesp. face swollen and puffy, skin transparent and blanched, scalding urine followed by itching, itching of right arm. Blake also related the case of Miss C. J., who at the age of thirty-one was stung on the left thumb, through some calico and . was never well after, dying at the age of thirty-eight. She was prone to constipation all her life and at twenty-three had “congestion of the left lung.” Most of the abdominal, urinary, ovarian and uterine symptoms were hers. Among the latter was an irritable ulcer. RELATIONS - Antidote: Semp., locally. Antidoted by: Apis, Led., Camph., salt water, vinegar. Compare: (1) Scorp. - sahvation, strabismus, tetanus, Apis. (2) pains as if pierced with red-hot needles, Ars., Apis. (3) Ulcers around os uterus, Mitch., Eup-pur., Apis., Hydre. Incompatible: Arg-n. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Cold feeling in stomach. Heat in stomach. Indigestion with flushing. Belchings. Nausea in evening after coming indoors with weight in stomach with faint feeling and trembling. Vomiting with swelling of head.

Abdomen - Uneasiness in abdomen.

Male - Swelling of scrotum and penis.

Female - Menstruation, preceded by pain, pressure, depression and constipation. Menses intermittent, sometimes brown, accompanied by pain and flatulence, preceded by mental depression, pain, pressure and constipation. Left ovary markedly affected with frequent burning, urination, sacral pains extending up back. Erosion around external os. Pain in left ovarian region. An irritable ulcer surrounded os tincae. Irritation, worse in groin, passing into pudenda.

Heart - Aching in heart. Slow beating of heart, almost imperceptible. Pulse rapid and small, feeble, with violent beating of carotids.

Back - Pain in left side of neck, waking her at night, preventing her from turning it to left side, felt least when lying on back, best on right side. Pain in scapula with soreness.

Limbs - Pain in shoulder, axillary glands swollen. Sprained pain in left shoulder joint on moving it, worse lifting arm or twisting it. Aching in hand and arm. Lungs - Dyspnea. Respiration hurried. Hoarseness. Voice lost. Spasm of glottis (after application of diluted ammonia to tongue), face pale, drops of sweat on forehead, arms thrown out to gasp for air, he got out of bed, sank back on bed, face livid, breath and pulse stopped.

Sleep - Night restless. Sleepless all night.

Skin - Erythema intense itching, burning. Boils, stinging and soreness, relieved by bathing with vinegar. Wheals, macules and swellings with burning, stinging and soreness. Erythema multiforme.

Modalities - Better from cold washing of hands. Cold water first relieves then aggravates. Skin better by bathing with vinegar. Worse from hot stove, in a closed room. Worse after sleep, after eating. Worse by motion. Open air aggravates lachrymation.

Kidneys - Marked tenderness to deep pressure in kidney region. Remittent dysuria with backache. Burning pain with urination, also itching. Burning urination in women. Hematuria. Incessant bedwetting.

HOMEOPATHIC - Viagra, used for male impotence, works by dilating blood vessels in the penis, allowing the inflow of blood needed for an erection. Viagra causes erections only during sexual excitement. It does not work in the absence of arousal. Heart attack, stroke, heart irregularities, dangerous surges in blood pressure, and sudden death have all been reported after use of Viagra, usually in men with existing cardiac risk factors, and typically during or shortly after sex. Allergic reactions. Chills. Dizziness. Drowsiness. Fainting, falling. Muscle ache. Joint disease. Bone pain. Numbness. Coordination problems. Slow reflexes. Tremors. Seizures. Strokes. Flushing. Rising causes fainting, nausea and dizziness..
constitution: After-pains. Cough, pregnancy. Cramps. Dysmenorrhea. Ears, painful. Epididymitis. Headaches. Hysteria. Labor, Viburnum opulus false. Labor, pains. Lumbago. Menstruation, painful. Miscarriages. Ovaries, pain. Paralysis. Uterus, pain.
keynote: PHARMACY - vib. Viburnum opulus. Cramp bark. High cranberry. Bush cramp. Bark water elder. N. O. Caprifliaceae. Great Britain. The Gueldres Rose or Snowball-tree is the cultivated and sterile variety. Tincture of the fresh bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all…
full:
PHARMACY - vib. Viburnum opulus. Cramp bark. High cranberry. Bush cramp. Bark water elder. N. O. Caprifliaceae. Great Britain. The Gueldres Rose or Snowball-tree is the cultivated and sterile variety. Tincture of the fresh bark. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - After-pains. Cough, pregnancy. Cramps. Dysmenorrhea. Ears, painful. Epididymitis. Headaches. Hysteria. Labor, Viburnum opulus false. Labor, pains. Lumbago. Menstruation, painful. Miscarriages. Ovaries, pain. Paralysis. Uterus, pain.

HOMEOPATHIC - Vib. is a remedy for general cramps. Colicky pains in pelvic organs. Conscious of internal sexual organs. Prevents miscarriage. False labor-pains. Spasmodic and congestive affections, dependent upon ovarian or uterine origin. Paralytic conditions after convulsions. Violent, spasmodic, nervous effects, especially in females, dependent upon the ovarian or uterine origin. Pains make her so nervous, she cannot keep still. Sick feeling all over in pelvic complaints. Hemorrhages. Left sided symptoms. MIND - Very nervous and irritable.

Head - Head dull and sluggish. Throbbing in head. Terrible crushing pain worse left parietal region with a sensation as if head opening and shutting. Severe pain in temporal region. Head hurt by every cough.

Eyes - Sclerotica streaked with blood. Sensation of sand in eyes. Pain in right eye with congestion. Burning and lachrymation. Sore feeling in eyeballs. Sore feeling on closing lids. Heaviness of eyes.

Ears - Stabbing in ears. Pains in bone waking at night. External ear sore as if bruised.

Face - Flushed and hot. Face swollen and congested. Swelling about right eye with induration. Face and lips pale, dark circles under eyes. Lips dry.

Stomach - Constant nausea, relieved by eating. Vertigo - Vertigo, feels as if falling forward, worse descending stairs. Feels faint on sitting up. COMMENTS - The first Vib. provings were by H. C. Allen, assisted by eleven provers, male and female with the tincture and first and 30c dilutions. Dr. Susan Fenton of Oakland, proved Vib. on six provers. One of the six took the tincture up to drachm doses without obtaining a single symptom. One pro ver was cured of a number of symptoms, but developed no new ones. All took potencies at first witfiout eliciting any symptoms. Taking the tincture all had these symptoms with variations: severe backache going through to the front or around the abdomen to uterus. Cramping pelvic pain. Temporal headache. Three had nausea with pains. All had “sick feeling all over.” One had omission of a period, two had menses early. One case was cured; Miss F., 25, a housekeeper, medium height, rather slender, blonde, sanguine, was strong until she had severe pelvic congestion and was fifteen months under treatment and most of the time in bed. In June, 1892, a double oophorectomy was performed with great relief, but attacks of pelvic congestion with severe pain still persisted, at first every two to four weeks, later less frequently, causing impairment of general health and strength. Symptoms included excruciating pains through lower abdomen with bearing-down sensation and a feeling as if the body from the waist to lower part of pelvis would collapse, an indescribable sick feeling all over with severe aching in rectum, great depression of spirits, symptoms better when lying down. Vib. tincture was taken in three-drop doses thrice daily. After taking it for three days she lost all her symptoms and felt “perfectly well for the first time in over four years.” It is evident that “sick feeling all over” in connection with pelvic complaints and “worse from movement, better by rest” are keynotes of Vib. RELATIONS -Antidotedby: Aeon, (epididymitis), Verat. (Diarrhea). Compare: (1) Vib-p. Cimic., Caul., Sabin., Sep., Thlaspi., Xanth. REFERENCES - Clarke. Hale.

Abdomen - Excruciating crampy colicky pain. Heavy aching, hypogastrium, better menses. Sudden cramps and colic pains. Tender, worse pressure about umbilicus.

Rectum - Stools large and hard with cutting in rectum and soreness of anus. Sensations - As if she could not tell where she was or what to do on awaking. As if she could not live, sick feeling at stomach. Emptiness, as if stomach hollow. As if body from waist to lower pelvis would collapse. As if urine continued to flow after urinating. As if menses coming on. As if pelvic organs were turning upside down. As if parts would be forced through vulva and she must support the part. Left side as if strained or bruised by over-lifting.

Female - Heavy aching feeling or excruciating cramps in pelvis, better from menses. Bearing-down pains before menses. Menses too late, scanty, lasting a few hours, offensive in odor with crampy pains, cramps extend down thighs (Bell.). Spasmodic and membranous dysmenorrhea (Bor.). Leucorrhea, thick, white, blood streaked worse during stools. Leucorrhea, excoriating. Smarting and itching of genitals. Consciousness of internal sexual organs. Pelvic organs turning upside down. Aching in sacrum and pubes with pain in anterior muscles of thighs (Xanth.). Pains from back to loins and womb worse early morning. Uterine pains extend around the pelvis often extending down the thighs. Ovarian region feels heavy and congested. Uterine hemorrhage. Frequent and very early miscarriage, causing seeming infertility. False labor pains. Violent persistent after-pains. Faint on attempting to sit up. Food - No appetite. No desire to eat, stomach feels full. Indigestion, food lies heavy.

Chest - Feeling of oppression over whole chest. Sensation as if muscles of chest failed to act, causing dyspnea. Shooting over left sixth rib near sternum. Constitutions - Suited to tall, slender, dark or fair haired hysterical subjects.

Back - Bruised feeling in back as after severe exertion. Tired backache, better pressure. Lumbago, better walking with a cane pressed, arms across the back. Pains in the back end in a cramp in uterus or go down the thighs.

Limbs - Stiff, sore feeling in nape of neck. Feels as if back would break. Sacral backache. Lower limbs weak and heavy. Cramps in calves, before menses. Lungs - Suffocative spells at night, worse cold, damp. Infantile asthma. Cough during pregnancy.

Skin - Tettery spots on cheeks, arms etc. Sleep - Very restless sleep, felt sick all over. When asleep, sensation of falling and awakened frequently with a start.

Modalities - Better by pressure, resting. Better in open air. Worse from motion, sudden jar, lying on left side, lying on affected side. Worse evening and night. Worse in close room, warm room. Worse cold, snow, air. Worse from fright. Worse before menses. Straining at stool aggravates headache. Stooping causes dizziness. Rising causes fainting, nausea and dizziness.

Kidneys - Frequent urging. Frequent, profuse urination during headache, menses, hemorrhages etc. Dysuria, spasmodic. Copious, pale, light-colored urine. Cannot hold water on coughing or walking.

full:
PHARMACY - Vib-p. Viburnum prunifolium. Black haw. An American species. N. O. Caprifliaceae. Tincture of fresh bark gathered in October and November from trees grown in open situations. Phares. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - After-pains. Dysmenorrhea. Infertility. Menorrhagia. Menstrual disorders. Miscarriage. Morning sickness. Tetanus. Tongue, cancer. Uterine, disorders.

HERBAL - Hale quoted his experiences showing a close resemblance between Vib-p. and Vib. with some additional uses of Vib-p. Viburnum prunifolium is a uterine tonic. Useful for habitual miscarriage. After-pains. Menstrual irregularities of infertile females with uterine displacements. Morning sickness. Cancer of the tongue, obstinate hiccough. Phares said of it, “Vib-p. is particularly valuable in preventing abortion and miscarriage, whether habitual or otherwise, whether threatened from accidental causes or criminal drugging.” COMMENTS - Phares noted the case of Mrs. W. had never gone to full term, had several children at eight months, all of them dying one month after birth. Frequent pregnancies and hemorrhages had seriously impaired her health. When next pregnant Vib-p. was ordered and at the eighth month when pains set in vigorously with copious bloody discharge, Vib-p. was given freely and she went to term, giving birth to a healthy boy, who survived. He also recorded the case of Mrs. L., married eighteen months, had miscarried and suffered long and much in consequence. Being again pregnant, Phares gave her Vib-p. tincture, a teaspoonful thrice daily. At the third month, she was severely injured by a fall from her carriage. Strong uterine contractions ensued, but were arrested by Vib-p., which had to be given freely for several days, the dose being gradually diminished. For nearly a week, miscarriage was threatened whenever Vib-p. was too long suspended. The patient went to term and gave birth to a large boy. Hale used the tincture in threatened miscarriage, dysmenorrhea and spasmodic uterine pains. It entirely antidotes the effect of Goss., which is much used for procuring abortion in some of the States, one pint of a strong decoction of the cotton-root being sufficient. Vib-p. when taken regularly completely neutralizes this. E. P. Fowler cured two cases of cancer of the tongue with the decoction of Vib-p. bark, used topically. Phares thinks it perhaps “the best remedy in the world for tetanus.” RELATIONS - Antidote to: Goss. REFERENCES - Clarke. Hale.

He considered hypochondriasis an indication for Vib-t. Deafness with sufferings in lower segment of abdomen and dysmenorrhea, erosions about the os uterus. Cramp in diaphragm. Horrible headache all over head, worse on right side with right-sided deafness, coming on at 7 a.m. and 11 a.m. and4 a.m. and 7 p.m. with great sinking in pit of chest. Waking at 4 a.m. with horrid depression of spirits that lasts until noon with a weight on chest and back, has to hold herself up to breathe. REFERENCES - Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - vichy-g. Vichy aqua. Vichymin- eral springs. Grande grille. Springs at Vichy, France. Vichy springs containing carbonicum acidum, muriaticum acidum, sulphuricum acidum, silica, phosphoric acidum, arseni- cum acidum, ferrum oxidatum, natrum, kalium, calcium and magnesium. Arsenicums. Oxygenums. Silicas. Dilutions. Historical dose: Tincture and all potencies.

CLINICAL - Bladder, catarrh. Constipation. Diabetes. Gallstones. Gout. Gravel. Heartbum. Indigestion. Intermittent, fevers. Liver, disorders. Neck, stiff. Rheumatism. Salivation. Skin, disorders. Uterus, disorders.

HOMEOPATHIC - The springs of Vichy are alkaline, both hot and cold. Croserio proved Vichy, taking the water and triturations of the salt and dilutions. Constantin James noted that the springs are used in a large number of maladies, especially diseases of the digestive tract, diseases of the liver with or without stones. Abdominal engorgements consequent on paludal fevers, chronic engorgements of the uterus, catarrh of the bladder, gravel, gout and rheumatism, diabetes mellitus, skin diseases. Among the most prominent symptoms were stitches below mastoid in chest in right loin and in heart. Across the chest there was a sensation as of a bar impeding breathing. Sinking sensation and sensation as if about to be sick. Burning flatulence. In the nose there were illusions of smell, corpse-like odor, odor of cucumbers. After sex there was excessive weakness as if from hunger. Modalities - Worse from cold, drafts of air. Worse when seated. Worse after sex. Worse after eating, when eating. Uneasiness is better by dinner. RELATIONS - Compare: ( 1 ) Nat-m. (2) Stitching pains, Kali-c. (3) Bar sensation, Haematox., Ars., Ox-ac. (4) Worse from sex, Kali-c., Kali- bi., Staph. (5) Illusory smells, Anae. REFERENCES - Clarke.

full:
PHARMACY - vine. Vinca minor. Lesser periwinkle. N. O. Apocynaceae. Grows in woods and shady places. Tincture of whole fresh plant. Historical dose: All potencies, first to third potency.

CLINICAL - Acne. Alopecia. Diphtheria. Crusta lactea. Eczema. Favus. Hemorrhages. Neck, stiff. Nose, redness. Plica polonica. Seborrhea. Throat, sore. Toothache. Uterus, bleeding.

HOMEOPATHIC - Vinca was proved by Rosenburg on four healthy persons, who took the tincture in 20 to 60 drop doses. It produced a deep impression on the organism and tissues. Weakness and prostration. “Weakness as if he would die.” Inclination to stretch. Trembling and tendency to start, especially on exciting the mind. Trembling in all the blood vessels. Uterine hemorrhages, followed by great debility. “Toothache better from warmth of bed.” Diphtheria. Empty, all gone sensation in the stomach and chest. Distention of abdomen after stool. Stool caused exhaustion. Skin affections, eczema. Plica polonica. Marked affects on the tissues. The left side was most affected.

Head - Tearing pain in vertex, ringing and whistling in ears. Corrosive itching of scalp. Irresistible desire to scratch. Spots on scalp, oozing moisture, matting hair together, plicapolonica. Bald spots covered with short woolly hair. Hair falls out and is replaced by gray hair.

Eyes - Itching and burning of lids, which become red. Eye dry, on getting snuff into it there was so little secretion he was obliged to wash it out. Foggy vision while reading, at times also while walking.

Ears - Ringing and whistling in ears with feeling of cold wind, especially the left.

Nose - Becomes red on becoming the least angry. Tip gets red easily. Moist eruption on septum. Seborrhea upper lip and base of nose. Stoppage of one nostril. Sores in nose. Frequent nose bleeding.

Face - Bloated face with pimples. Dry lips. Swelling of upper lip and corner of mouth. Tearing in malar bones.

Mouth - Increased secretion of saliva. Insipid taste in mouth to all food. Aphthae. Tearing in teeth better by warmth of bed.

Throat - Cutting in lower esophagus, which provokes swallowing. Diphtheria. Ulcers. Frequent hawking. Difficult swallowing. Vertigo - Whirling vertigo with flickering before eyes. COMMENTS - Vine, has a wide range in passive uterine hemorrhages. This case is related in Ind. H. R. (ix. 113): uterine hemorrhage, blood dark red, flow copious, uninterrupted with extreme debility. Chin, and Helon. failed to relieved, Vine, lx effected a rapid and permanent cure. Frequent nosebleed. The nose “becomes red from the slightest cause, when the least bit angry.” Scabby eruptions about the nose and on the septum, which are part of the general skin effect of the remedy. Corrosive itching of the skin provoking scratching, moist spots and burning in ulcers. The most characteristic effect is on the scalp, where it produces a condition having many features of crusta lactea, favus and plica polonica. Clarke cured With Vine, “sore spots on the scalp” in a young woman. A number of symptoms were produced in the throat and esophagus. C. M. Bogerrecordedthecaseofawomen, 31, who had a cutting sensation in lower part of esophagus while swallowing food and continuing after. Empty faintness in stomach better by eating. Stomach sore to touch or pressure of clothing. Constipation from induration of feces. Hemorrhoids constantly sore, smarting after stool. Vine. 41,000c (Fincke) cured. RELATIONS - Compare: (1) Olnd., Staph. (2) peevishness with repentance, Croc. Crusta lactea, Med., Melit, Mez., Jug-r., Olnd. (3) Viol-t. - with strong-smelling urine. (4) Lappa - glands swollen, axillary glands even suppurate. (5) Staph. - sickly children, pale face, dark rings around eyes. (6) Ust. - filthy eruptions, part of hair comes out, part matted. (7) Alopecia, Bac., Phos. REFERENCES - Boericke. Clarke.

Stomach - Emptiness in stomach. Gastric disturbance. Empty belchings after drinking beer and generally worse from taking liquid. Nausea after coffee. Violent, bitter, copious vomiting of yellowish-green liquid.

Abdomen - Abdomen full, tense but painless. Griping. Rumbling and gurgling with passage of much offensive flatus. Distention after a stool.

Rectum - Urging to stool. Stool first hard, then soft. Stool exhausting with burning in anus. Sensations - As if he would die from weakness. As if a hammer were beating from within outwards in vertex, cold wind in ears. As if something sticking low down in esophagus. As if a weight lying on cervical muscles.

Female - Menses, profuse, flowing like a stream without interruption with great weakness, at menopause. Passive uterine hemorrhages (Ust., Trill., Sec.). Menorrhagia, continuous flow, at menopausal (Lach.). Bleeding fibroids. Food - Hunger alternating with loss of appetite before the hunger has been satisfied. Scarcely any thirst.

Chest - Pains in chest with sticking and dyspnea. Stitching in sternum. Pressure on sternum with feeling of emptiness in chest.

Back - Painful tension and stiffness of cervical muscles with an illusive sensation as if a weight were lying on them. Causations - Anger. Mental exertion.

Limbs - Inclination to stretch limbs. Tearing pains in limbs. Arthritic tearing in bones. Swelling and stiffness of first joints of fingers with burning pain in the nails. Cramp-like drawing in feet and toes. Lungs - Hoarseness. Tenacious mucus in trachea. Spasmodic cough with little tickling in larynx. Rapid respiration.

Sleep - Frequent yawning. Sleeplessness and restlessness at night. Lascivious dreams.

Skin - Eczema of head and face. Corrosive itching. Great sensitiveness of skin with redness and soreness from slight rubbing. Pustules, itching, burning and offensive odor. Hair matted together. Weeping ec - zema intermingled with foul, thick, crusts. Corrosive itching.

Modalities - Worse after swallowing, walking, stooping, moving. Worse anger. Worse reading. Worse in open air. Drinking aggravates, liquids (especially beer) causes belchings, coffee causes nausea.

Kidneys - Diminished secretion of urine. Urine pale yellow.
